title: 100 Gram
content:
About
The 100 Gram is a G Squared Yoyos throw weighing just over 100 grams, pitched as a heavy practice yo-yo for building technique. It shipped with G20 pads, a G2 Ripper bearing, and a diamond-blasted finish.

title: 1to1
content:
From One Drop:

"This project started with a simple concept:  what if we made a yo-yo that had the exact same width and diameter?   A yo-yo that was square in it’s proportions. 53 x 53mm to be exact.

This proportion makes the yo-yo really wide.  On average these days, the width tends to be 70% - 80% of the diameter.  A very average example is the SK at 75%. On the wide side, the Sugar Glider comes in at 84%.  And on the narrow end, the Deep State is 50%.

What is really interesting is that if you just look at the 1to1, the width appears to be a bigger dimension than the diameter.  It’s almost like an optical illusion. Put two of them next to each other, one standing up (see photo), and you can see that those dimensions are exactly the same.

In play, it’s very stable and has a huge catch zone which inspires confidence.    The spin time is surprisingly long. It feels different.

Ships with Ultra Light Side Effects and starts at $59 for solids."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)
meta.yya_weight: 63g (65.5g with aluminium Ultra Light Side Effects)

title: 2018 WYYC Souvenir Yo-Yo
content: Commemorative yo-yo for the 2018 World Yo-Yo Contest hosted by Auldey in Shanghai. Straight profile with WYYC logo. Clear plastic body with anodized aluminum cowl and wings. Limited commemorative release.

title: 2019 WYYC Ambrosia Maple
content:
History / About
The 2019 WYYC Ambrosia Maple is a limited edition fixed-axle created by Fallen44 exclusively for the 2019 World Yo-Yo Contest in Cleveland, Ohio. Hand-turned from an Ambrosia Maple body with a Hard Maple axle, it was available in two stained finishes — Dark Walnut and Oak. Sold through YoYoSam as a contest collectible at $29.99.

title: Custom Polyester String
content: 24K Whips Custom Polyester String is the brand’s core product: hand-spun, made-to-order polyester string available in any color combination, thickness, and length. The signature offering is the faded string — a two-toned design where two colors twist and fade seamlessly across the strand’s length, producing a visually dynamic string during play.Orders are fully custom. Thickness ranges from thin competition-style to fat beginner-friendly profiles. Extended lengths are available for advanced players who prefer more string. Color-matching to specific yo-yos or custom splash/fade combinations is offered on request. All strings are made to order by Daniel Kessler directly, with orders placed through the brand’s Instagram and Facebook.A custom 24K Whips string matched to each colorway was included in the 2019 Rain City Skills × 24K Whips Retro Rocket package, introducing the brand to a wider audience through the collaboration release.

title: 2Evil
content:
History / About
The 2Evil is MonkeyfingeR Design’s spiritual successor to their debut throw, the Evil-Yo. Sharing the same core dimensions (52.5mm × 42mm), the 2Evil refines the H-shape geometry and drops 1g in weight to 65g. Like the original, colorway names reference the three mystic apes. Released February 9, 2016, and made in Canada, it was available through specialty retailers and Walmart simultaneously.

title: Bishop
content: About the BishopThe Bishop was released in early 2015 and reviewed as a versatile, well-rounded "jack of all trades." US-made with hand-testing on every unit for quality control. The V-shape features rounded edges and uses a thicker-than-standard axle. Designed to excel across fingerspins, horizontal tricks, speed play, and regenerations, making it an excellent daily driver. A set of NFL franchise-themed colorways was released, as well as a rare "Great White Shark" colorway. The Bishop sits in the core of the 2SickYoYos catalog as a do-everything performance throw.

title: Blitz
content: About the BlitzReleased July 21, 2016, the Blitz was 2SickYoYos' second bi-metal, continuing the brand's signature sandwiched stainless steel rim construction introduced with the Knight. At 54mm it is slightly smaller than the Knight, with a featherweight organic profile that delivers speed without sacrificing stability. US-made with a bead-blasted grind-friendly finish and simple engraving. Described as providing "insane speed" with serious spin time and strong horizontal play capability. A "Celestial" colorway limited to fewer than 10 pieces exists as one of the rarest 2SickYoYos variants. Priced at $150 at release.

title: Blockade
content: About the BlockadeReleased in 2019, the Blockade is an aluminum and steel bi-metal with a slightly organic but still sharp profile. Despite its appearance it plays noticeably more floaty than expected, with long spin times and strong stability. A slightly chalky but grindable finish suits talon grinds and technical play. Community colorways include "Unicorn Sneeze," "Supercharged," "Tide Pod," and a "Sneezy Unicorn Edition," indicating close community engagement around this model.

title: Crusade
content: About the CrusadeReleased in June 2020, the Crusade is a competition-geared bi-metal with a wide-set profile, large catch zone, and thick steel rings producing optimal weight distribution for maximum stability and spin power. The inverse curved profile minimizes string drag for excellent horizontal play performance. Plays bouncy and fast on the string. Initial production was limited to approximately 30 units. Colorways include Orange/Blue, Sneezy Unicorn, and Emerald (teal with rainbow rims).

title: En Passant
content: About the En PassantReleased September 29, 2017, the En Passant is a plastic/steel hybrid that bridges the gap between the all-plastic Pawn and the full aluminum bi-metal lineup. The machined polycarbonate body is fitted with stainless steel rings positioned slightly inward from the outer rim — not at the outermost edge — for a more even feel and superior maneuverability. This positions the weight distribution for a smooth, forgiving play character while delivering the stability and spin of a metal-ringed throw. Available in a wide variety of colorways.

title: Flank
content: About the FlankReleased in early 2019, the Flank is a performance-oriented 6061 aluminum monometal that reviewers noted plays on par with bi-metals in feel and stability. Fun and comfortable while delivering serious competition-level performance. Suited for all play styles. Available in multiple colorways including Cotton Candy Carnival, Grapeseed, Fire Lily, Rose Gold, and Black. Retailed in Europe at approximately €49.

title: Gambit
content: About the GambitThe Gambit was the launch product for 2SickYoYos, founded by Joey Serrano. Released in October 2013 in a limited run of approximately 50 units across five colorways, the Gambit emerged after Serrano shared an early prototype on the YoYoExpert Forums and received strong community support. It was produced in both a standard 6061 aluminum version and a premium 7075 version, each tuned for a different feel: the 6061 is fast, floaty, and agile, while the 7075 is solid and rock-stable. Rim-weighted for stability, the Gambit was designed to handle competition-level play while staying fun as a casual throw. Bearings were supplied by Buddha Bearings. Priced at $90 (6061) and $100 (7075) at launch.

title: Grandmaster
content: About the GrandmasterReleased April 19, 2019, the Grandmaster pushes into oversized territory at 59mm while maintaining a light, floaty feel thanks to stainless steel ring placement. The organic-leaning shape with flared design provides a generous catch zone suited to all trick styles. Despite its size the Grandmaster plays extremely light while delivering strong stability and powerful spin. The 59mm diameter supports long spin times without adding bulk. Name continues the chess-themed convention at the highest rank.

title: Guardian
content: About the GuardianReleased March 26, 2024, the Guardian is 2SickYoYos' first 7075 aluminum yo-yo. It delivers "unparalleled comfort, prolonged spin times, seamless performance, and robust durability" per the manufacturer, with a wide 48.03mm catch zone suited to all trick styles. The Guardian is explicitly marketed for 5A play due to its outstanding balance and resilience — uncommon for a primary product release. Priced at $50. Available in multiple colorways including Blue/Pink Fade, Gunmetal, Green Acid Wash, Red, Pink/Purple/Green Acid Wash, and Dark Blue/Light Blue/Orange Acid Wash.

title: King
content: About the KingThe King was the second model from 2SickYoYos, released in July 2014. Designed as the "ultimate competition level yo-yo that is still fun to throw when you're just hanging around," the King features a curved V-shape with massive rim weight for exceptional stability and long spin times. The cup includes a "2Sick Spin ring" for fingerspin performance, a signature 2SickYoYos design detail. Bead-blasted for a smooth grind finish. Available through YoYoExpert. A new run featuring six new colorways was released around November 2014. Bearing supplied by Crucial.

title: Knight
content: About the KnightReleased December 1, 2015, the Knight was 2SickYoYos' first bi-metal and introduced the brand's signature construction: stainless steel rings "sandwiched" into the rim of the aluminum body rather than placed at the outermost edge. This approach gives the Knight a distinctive look and feel compared to conventional bi-metals. The angular V-shape profile includes the "2Sick ring" in the cup for fingerspins. Bead-blasted finish for grip-friendly grinds. US-made and priced at $150 at release. Pro colorways were produced for team members Adam Czapla and Samuel Lee (both stainless steel ring variants). Later runs also included a brass ring option, and Blaise Becker and Shockwave pro editions were documented.

title: Paladin
content: About the PaladinReleased in 2022, the Paladin is a collaboration between 2SickYoYos and Thesis YoYos. Thesis took the iconic 2SickYoYos Knight as their starting point, scaling the shape up to a full-sized yo-yo, then added Hypothesis-style rings for maximum power and competition-level performance. Priced at $99.99. All Paladins shipped in a green double-layered pouch. Considered one of the most competitive throws from both companies. Collab partner Thesis YoYos is not currently in The Yoyo Archive.

title: Pawn
content: About the PawnThe Pawn was 2SickYoYos' first plastic yo-yo, notable for being fully machined from polycarbonate rather than injection-molded — an uncommon production method for plastic throws. This machined approach results in minimal vibration and a smooth feel uncommon in the price range. Rounded profile with good weight distribution. Impressive spin times for a plastic. Available in a clear/red hub colorway and a stars-and-stripes American-themed version, among others. Restocked at YoYoExpert on May 31, 2017.

title: Promotion
content: About the PromotionReleased October 22, 2018, the Promotion is a competition-oriented bi-metal continuing 2SickYoYos' chess-themed naming convention. The 6061 aluminum body is fitted with substantial stainless steel rings for powerful spin and excellent stability while maintaining a nimble, non-fatiguing feel in play. Smooth and fast. Reviewed as delivering competition-grade performance at a $100 price point. Designed to continue the lineage of the Knight and Blitz while refining the formula.

title: Queen
content: About the QueenThe Queen is a well-rounded V-shape from 2SickYoYos designed to handle all trick styles while remaining competition-ready. It received multiple restock runs with new colorways through 2016, attesting to its popularity. A rare 7075 aluminum variant known as the "Galaxy" colorway was produced in limited quantities. Joey Serrano himself appeared in promotional video content for this model. The Queen is considered one of the core models of the early 2SickYoYos era and is frequently found in collector lots from this period.

title: Rook
content: About the RookReleased February 27, 2016 in a limited run of 50 pieces, the Rook was 2SickYoYos' first titanium yo-yo. US-made and redesigned from an earlier prototype before going to production. Described as "stable, long spinning, dead smooth" with the characteristic ringing tone that titanium throws are known for. Available through the 2SickYoYos site and YoYoExpert at release. Priced at $280–$300. Features multiple anodized color options.

title: Serenity
content: About the SerenityReleased in December 2019, the Serenity is the signature model for 2SickYoYos team member Devin Jones. A high-performance 6061 aluminum monometal built around Jones' preferences, with a generous 47mm width for a large catch zone. The Serenity reached broader mainstream distribution than earlier 2SickYoYos models, available through Walmart and Amazon in addition to specialty retailers. Available colorways included Rose Gold and the signature "Sneezy Unicorn" edition.

title: Tempo
content: About the TempoReleased December 8, 2016, the Tempo is a collaboration between 2SickYoYos and Radical Seas. It combines the Oracle shape from Radical Seas with 2SickYoYos' signature sandwiched weight ring construction, setting the rings at the outer rim for maximum rim weight. The standard version uses brass rings; an alternate version with stainless steel rings was also produced. 6061 aluminum body with a bead-blasted finish. Described as fast with unstoppable stability and powerful spin. US-made.

title: 2WEI
content:
History / About
The 2WEI is an oversized yoyo based on our classic the E1NS. When throwing it, you immediately feel the 2WEI’s powerful spin. It weighs in at 67g that are carefully distributed to allow for the mentioned super spin times while keeping the floatiness alive. While 67g are definitely more on the heavier side, the large dimensions of the 2WEI make good use of the mass. It does not feel chunky and slow, it feels powerful and chilled. It will put a smile on your face from the moment you land your first trapeze.

Production Runs

Pre-Production #1 (March 2010) — 10 units, Silver; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 68.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Pre-Production #2 (August 2011) — 9 units, Purple/Silver; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 68.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: CandyBlast.
Pre-Production #3 — 6 units, Purple; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 68.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (August 2011) — 65 units, Pearl; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 68.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: CandyBlast.
Special #1 — 15 units, Blue; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 68.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #2 (February 2019) — 20 units, Azure; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 67.00g. Bearing: C. Finish: Soda Blast.
Run #3 (July 2019) — 28 units, Lush Green; D56.15mm / W46.30mm / 67.00g. Bearing: C. Finish: Soda Blast.

title: 3AM
content:
History / About
The 3AM is Fallen44’s unresponsive wooden yoyo, expanding the brand beyond fixed-axle play. Hand-turned by Kevin Markie from exotic hardwood with a Size C concave bearing, it maintains the lightweight, organic character of the Sixth Sense while delivering fully unresponsive performance. At 53g and 55.5mm diameter, it is compact and agile for a wooden throw.

title: 3D Printable Cambium (Prototype)
content: The 3D Printable Cambium is a digital fixed-axle derivative of MikeMonty’s wooden Cambium. Mike printed and tested the design in 2022, then documented a public Thingiverse upload on April 30, 2024 so players could manufacture their own examples.The design was publicly released but not confirmed as a conventional retail physical product, so this archive record carries the Prototype suffix. Exact filament, dimensions, weight, gap, axle construction, download URL, and license have not been recovered.

title: Accent
content: AboutThe Accent is a full-size H-profile acrylic model released around 2012, featuring a deep center hub and more rim weight than earlier 3YO3 designs. Available in black, white, Half-and-Half (Black/White), camouflage, and dyed variants. Uses General-Yo Thin Hat Pads for response. The Accent represents 3YO3's refined H-profile approach applied to a full-size diameter.

title: Acme
content:
History / About
The Acme is part of 3YO3's handmade small-batch lineup produced by founder Landon Balk, continuing the brand's tradition of individual craftsmanship and wide material experimentation — acrylic, delrin, aluminum, and titanium.

title: Acrylic Steamroller
content: AboutThe Acrylic Steamroller is a collaboration between XCube (France) and 3YO3 (Florida) in which XCube's radical aluminum Steamroller shape was adapted into hand-machined acrylic by Landon Balk. The result is nearly as wide as it is tall — an extreme undersized H-profile suited for chopsticks tricks and intricate string manipulation. At 59 grams it is approximately 5 grams lighter than the aluminum original. Each unit shipped in an XCube-branded canister with extra string and two pinback buttons. XCube is not currently in the Yoyo Archive database.

title: Acryllion
content: AboutThe Acryllion is a step-straight acrylic model similar in overall dimensions to the Cosmo but with edges that round off into the rims rather than running straight. It uses an axle system inspired by older Dif-e-Yo models. At $59.99 it is the most affordably priced acrylic in the 3YO3 lineup, using General-Yo Thin Hat Pads for response.

title: AL5
content: AboutThe AL5 is an aluminum version of the Ti5, released August 3, 2013 at 10 PM EST via YoYoExpert. Created in response to overwhelming demand after the Ti5 sold out immediately, the AL5 brings the Ti5's acclaimed profile to a dramatically lower price point. Shares the Ti5's organic mid-wall shape and overall dimensions in standard machined aluminum.

title: Bassline
content: AboutThe Bassline is 3YO3's debut metal yo-yo, machined at One Drop's manufacturing facility in Oregon. It takes the organic round silhouette of the FreeHand Zero (FHZ) and interprets it in modern precision-machined aluminum, with a contemporary large bearing gap and smooth, floaty play character. Anodized in various finishes, including a special One Drop × 3YO3 collaboration colorway produced alongside the main run. The name continues the TB-303 / bass synthesizer theme of the brand.

meta.yya_response: Flowable Silicone / One Drop pads (Pyramatte finish)

title: Bassline 2
content: AboutThe Bassline 2 is the last known product from 3YO3, released June 13, 2014 at 8 PM EST. It retains the Bassline's original dimensions but completely redesigns the weight distribution for a smoother, more floaty character — "built for comfort, not speed." It introduces One Drop's Side Effect axle system with custom Bassline-style hub Side Effects, allowing players to swap hubs for different feel and weight. Each unit ships in a custom wood and leather box, a premium packaging upgrade from the original Bassline. No further 3YO3 releases have been confirmed after this date.

meta.yya_axle: One Drop Side Effect (swappable; custom Bassline hub Side Effects)

title: Capella
content: AboutThe Capella is 3YO3's first dedicated Delrin model and shares its profile with the Ceephax, substituting POM for acrylic. The response area is shaved slightly thinner than the Ceephax to reduce sleep loss, giving Capella a more responsive feel suited to both casual and competitive play. Heavier than the Ceephax by approximately 4.7 grams due to Delrin's higher density relative to acrylic of the same volume. Available in blue/green, white/black, and black/white colorways as well as dyed and 2010 Worlds editions.

meta.yya_response: Thin Hat Pad (shaved for reduced sleep loss)

title: Ceephax
content: AboutThe Ceephax is named after British electronic musician Ceephax Acid Crew, reflecting the TB-303 synthesizer theme running through the 3YO3 brand. Released in May 2010, it is an undersized acrylic model with material gouged from the sides to push weight outward toward the rims. It features an integrated IRG (Inverted Rim Grind) groove for thumbgrinds. Early production runs offered customizable bearing size options (A, C, or D), making it one of the more versatile early 3YO3 throws. Released in clear dyed finishes and a special 2010 Worlds edition.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (also offered in A and D in early runs)

title: CMA
content: AboutThe CMA (Chris Moss Acid) was designed in consultation with 3YO3 team player Chris Moss. It takes the full-size diameter of the Collabricon and combines it with the wider gap dimensions of the Ceephax, topped with a massive integrated IRG groove. Despite being machined from acrylic, reviewers noted it plays "like a metal" in terms of weight and feel. Limited production run with minimal documented specifications.

title: Collabricon
content: AboutThe Collabricon is one of the rarest items in the 3YO3 catalog — a collaboration between General-Yo (Ernie Kaiser) and 3YO3 (Landon Balk) in which Ernie Kaiser designed the shape and Landon hand-machined all 20 units from acrylic. Only 20 were ever produced, each individually numbered. The General-Yo AIGR (All In Good Reason) bearing and General-Yo's Gen-Pads were used for the response, reflecting the collaborative nature of the project. It is one of the most sought-after 3YO3 collector pieces, with secondary market records at $120.

title: Cosmo
content: AboutThe Cosmo is the first yo-yo Landon Balk ever sold under the 3YO3 brand, launched in fall 2010. It features a straight (step-straight) profile — the only straight shape in the 3YO3 lineup — hand-machined from acrylic on a manual lathe. Each unit requires approximately 50 minutes of hand-machining. Despite its unconventional material, the Cosmo delivers a soft, comfortable catch and stable play through its blasted clear finish. Released in an unusually wide range of colorways including a special 2010 Worlds edition.

title: Grind King
content: AboutThe Grind King is widely cited as the world's first yo-yo commercially produced from Teflon (PTFE — polytetrafluoroethylene). PTFE has one of the lowest coefficients of friction of any solid material (0.07), making it ideal for finger grinds, arm grinds, and any trick requiring the string or body to slide along the player's skin. Dense for its undersized diameter, the Grind King delivers exceptional grinding performance while remaining competitive for standard 1A play. It won 1st place at the 2010 World Yo-Yo Contest Mod Contest (credited as 2011 entry), cementing 3YO3's back-to-back Mod Contest victories.

title: Hammerhead
content: AboutThe Hammerhead is the widest and largest-diameter acrylic in the 3YO3 catalog. Its full-size, wide H-profile provides an exceptional catch zone suited to players who prefer extra room on trapeze. An optional variant featured a light-up FHZ (Freehand Zero) board modification. Hand-machined from acrylic like all non-metal 3YO3 products.

title: Hour Glass
content: AboutThe Hour Glass is the most unusual product in the 3YO3 catalog — a functional hourglass built into a yo-yo body. Sand travels through a hollow thick axle from one half of the yo-yo to the other as it spins, creating a visible and measurable timing effect. Each unit takes approximately 3.5 hours of handwork to produce, the most labor-intensive model in the lineup. Two sand types are included: coarse blue sand (default) and fine brown sand for a different flow rate. The Hour Glass earned 3rd place at the 2010 WYYC Mod Contest and is the rarest and most expensive acrylic model at $174.99 USD.

title: Omnicron
content: AboutThe Omnicron is 3YO3's first model to use threaded inserts and a smaller axle to prevent stripping — a structural improvement over earlier releases. Its angular H-profile concentrates weight in the gouged-out wings for increased rim weight and stability. At 71.5 grams it is the heaviest acrylic in the 3YO3 lineup. Available in a clear blasted standard finish and special color variants machined from yellow, amber, pink, and multi-color acrylic billets.

title: Omnicron X
content: AboutThe Omnicron X is the CNC-machined aluminum evolution of the acrylic Omnicron, co-designed with community member CJ Atkinson. It carries forward the Omnicron's angular H-profile into metal, adding a spiked hub for matador tricks. Available in an unusually wide range of finish options: Pyramatte (standard), bead-blast (Special Edition), nickel-plated, powder-coated, anodized black and silver, a VsNYYC "The Works" custom anodization, and a Jason Wong custom anodization — the most elaborately finished model in the 3YO3 metal lineup.

meta.yya_response: Flowable Silicone or Hat-Pad sized pads

title: Savannah
content: AboutThe Savannah is the Delrin (POM) adaptation of the Cosmo, released concurrently with 3YO3's acrylic debut in fall 2010. Sharing the same straight-profile mold as the Cosmo, it substitutes acrylic for Delrin, offering a different surface feel and slightly altered play characteristics. The name, like Cosmo and Luce, reflects the Mazda rotary engine naming theme Landon Balk originally considered for the brand. Very limited documentation exists for this model as it was an early, transitional release.

title: Sigma
content:
History / About
The Sigma is one of 3YO3's handmade small-batch aluminum yo-yos. Landon Balk's 3YO3 brand specializing in yo-yos made from acrylic, delrin, aluminum, and titanium produced the Sigma as part of an expanding lineup of precision machined throws.

title: Ti5
content: AboutThe Ti5 is 3YO3's titanium flagship and one of the brand's most prized collector pieces. Hand-machined from titanium billet by Landon Balk, each unit is individually numbered and engraved. Released July 16, 2012 at 10 PM EST via YoYoExpert at $345 USD. The mid-region weight distribution and thin outer walls create a floaty, stable play style unusual for a titanium throw. The Ti5 arrives packaged in an electrical box that requires the included screwdriver to open — a signature unboxing experience. As with all titanium yo-yos, the Ti5 creates sparks when struck against pavement.

title: Volume
content: AboutThe Volume is the Delrin (POM) companion to the Accent, sharing the same H-profile and dimensions but substituting polyoxymethylene for acrylic. Slightly heavier due to Delrin's density. Released in blue, purple, and green/purple blend colorways alongside dyed variants. Like all 3YO3 Delrin models, it offers a distinct surface texture and feel compared to the acrylic lineup.

title: 44 Sticker
content:
About
44 Sticker is a sticker from Throw-Yo Threads. Die-cut matte sticker of "44 Bird", the Throw-Yo Threads mascot. Price: $3. First a Patreon sticker (May 2026).

title: 44CLASH (10th Anniversary)
content:
About
The 44CLASH yo-yo is the first original model produced under the 44CLASH brand name — not a collab colorway but a fully custom design commissioned to celebrate the contest's 10th anniversary in 2018. Produced by Mowl, with specs coordinated by Yo-Yo Studio Llama, laser-etched artwork by Hibari, and packaging designed by AA Yoyo Club. The stepped H-profile bimetal combines a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims for a smooth, powerful feel. Limited edition; retailed at $149.99 and available in Gold, Black, and Green colorways.

title: Feather Origin
content:
History / About
The Feather Origin is the result of a collaboration between 44EMPORIUM designer Evan Cui and Wayne of Layer Infinity. It represents Evan's original pre-production Feather prototype concept — refined through over 50 iterations of 3D printed prototypes — brought to retail form. The 3D printed body is reinforced with aluminum inner rims, making it competition-viable. The yo-yo debuted competitively at Evan Cui's ECR Preliminary performance.

title: Monogram Feather
content:
History / About
The Monogram Feather is a micro-run titanium variant of 44EMPORIUM's Feather design. Of 15 total units produced, two were reserved for Evan Cui and co-designer Yejune, leaving only 13 for public sale at $330. Each unit came with a numbered certificate and a Layer Infinity Capso Noir case.

title: 4mm Ywet
content: 10 of these were made, and 2 ended up lost. YWET with a 4mm gap. Sonny made these and gave them to his friends that played tug-responsive yoyos. The blue and orange are a different shade than what is on the production YWET, and there are no engravings on them.
The 5050  is a throw by Patrick Dressel, which he created before the Dressel Design brand.

From One Drop:

"The 54 is the first full size release from One Drop. It is named after the diameter which is 54mm. It is designed to be floaty and is the first yo-yo to use the Side Effects axle system. You will get aluminum spikes as pictured as well as brass domes. We'll have many more available in the future that you can use with this yo-yo."

The 54's innovation of Side Effects has had a huge impact on yo-yo design, with many other companies licensing out usage of the system. There is a huge assortment of Side Effects available today in many different styles, materials, and colors.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: 54 Gen 2
content:
From One Drop:

"The original 54 was released in 2010 and was the first yo-yo to feature the Side Effects axle system. Side Effects are something we are really proud of and they have stood the test of time. They are a genuine system for modding your yo-yo and nothing wears out. We adorably named it the “54” because it was the biggest diameter we had made to date - at the time, it was considered oversized but not so much now. 

With that in mind, the Gen 2 obviously needed to retain the 54” diameter, be a Side Effect yo-yo, and ship with an extra set just like the original did (in this case, clear aluminum Ultra Lights are installed and brass Micro caps are Included). Our idea was to imagine if we could simply hold both ends of a 54 and pull to stretch it out to be considerably wider. We feel like the Gen 2 pays excellent homage to the original while bringing the look and play up to modern standards."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

content:
From Dressel Designs:

"We started our designing journey in 2020, striving for the unordinary. In 2025, the equation has changed, and we've had to push through even further.

This isn't just another throw. It's a recalibration.

65 pieces.

Say hello to the 6060!

The 6060 was a silly idea from years ago that found life as a limited edition April fools style mystery yoyo. Playing off my first yoyo ever designed, the 5050, this yoyo features a 60x60 body but retains the 60g weight of the 5050. With it's oversized body and light weight, this yoyo is unlike anything you have played before! Limited to 65 pieces and the shiny emerald color found in our original prototype, get yours while you can!"

title: 66percent 66-STEP1
content:
About
The 66percent 66-STEP1 is a notable departure for the 66percent sub-brand: rather than miniaturizing another manufacturer's yoyo, it scales down SpinGear's own Step 1 looping yoyo to 38mm. It is also the first 66percent model designed for 2A looping play, marking SpinGear's return to looping within the miniature format after a long gap.
Made from aluminum with a K-size bearing and SpinX proprietary response system. Available in StarBurst-Gold, StarBurst-Black, Raw, Red, and Blue colorways. Priced from ¥10,600 to ¥12,100 depending on finish.

title: 66percent 888
content:
About
The 66percent 888 is a miniaturization of the iconic YoYoFactory 888 — one of the most celebrated competition yoyos of the 2000s, famous for its hubstack system. The 66percent version reproduces the hubstacks at 38mm scale using NSK micro hub stack bearings, making them fully functional. Available in two material options: stainless steel (64.3g) or brass (62.8g), each with distinct weight feel and aesthetics.
The 3.65mm gap and Size A bearing (5×10×4mm) are matched to the miniature format. Available in stainless steel raw, black anodize, and gold plated finishes.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size A (5×10×4mm) with NSK micro hub stack bearings

title: 66percent Barracuda
content:
About
The 66percent Barracuda was the very first model released under SpinGear's 66percent sub-brand in 2017, launching simultaneously with the Haymaker. The 66percent concept — conceived by SpinGear founder Taka Hasegawa — takes iconic yoyos and reduces them to approximately 66% of their original size, machining each unit entirely in Katsushika-ku, Tokyo.
The Barracuda is an officially licensed miniaturization of the Duncan Barracuda, reproduced as a stainless steel monometal at 37mm diameter. The first production run of exactly 66 units was sold without laser-engraved logos — these "Raw" units are collector's pieces. Subsequent runs introduced the PinkGold Edition with anodized accents. Despite its tiny size, stainless steel construction provides powerful spin and strong gyroscopic stability.
SpinGear recommends short thin strings for best performance at this scale.

title: 66percent Edge Beyond
content:
About
The 66percent Edge Beyond is an officially licensed miniaturization of the YoYoFactory Edge Beyond — the throw Evan Nagao used to win the 2018 World Yo-Yo Contest 1A title. Scaled to approximately 37mm (technically described as ~69% rather than strict 66%), it is produced as a bimetal with a 6061 aluminum body and either stainless steel or brass outer rims, machined in Tokyo.
Weight varies by rim material and plating: stainless steel rims, brass rims, and 18k gold-plated brass rims each yield different play characteristics. Multiple colorway combinations are available across the rim and body. One of the most sought-after 66percent models due to its contest-winning pedigree.

title: 66percent Haymaker
content:
About
Released alongside the Barracuda at the 66percent sub-brand's launch in 2017, the Haymaker is an officially licensed miniaturization of the Duncan Haymaker. It takes a bimetal approach (aluminum body with stainless steel rims) and comes in at just 44.4g — very light for the category. At 38mm diameter, it is slightly larger than a true 66% reduction of the original Haymaker, reflecting manufacturing constraints at extreme miniature scales.
Available only in blue. Minor vibration inherent to the small scale is acknowledged by SpinGear. The yoyo features a Japanese cartoon character aesthetic in its design language.

title: 66percent PYRO 66
content:
About
The 66percent PYRO 66 is the 8th model in the 66percent series, released in 2020. It is inspired by the classic H-Spin PYRO — a celebrated bimetal from the defunct Swiss brand H-Spin, which ceased operations around 2012. Since H-Spin is no longer active, no formal licensing was required.
The bimetal construction uses an aluminum body with brass rims. Three colorways were produced: Red/18k Gold-plated rim, Black, and Gold ("Flow to Love Edition"). Uniquely, the gold "Flow to Love Edition" intentionally retains a slight vibration as a stylistic choice — an homage to the character of hand-machined small-run production. Priced at ¥12,000.

title: 66percent Shutter
content:
About
The 66percent Shutter is an officially licensed scaled-down version of the YoYoFactory Shutter — Gentry Stein's World Championship-winning throw — reproduced at approximately 37mm diameter in stainless steel. Machined in Katsushika-ku, Tokyo using an NSK micro precision bearing at Size A.
Following an initial release, the model was re-released in 2023 in two colorways: Raw (¥9,900) and Gold (¥11,000). SpinGear recommends concave/center-track bearings and short thin strings to optimize performance at this scale.

title: 4Hunna
content:
About
The 4Hunna is a large/oversized monometal throw from A-RT.

title: BRICC
content:
About
The BRICC is a collaboration between A-RT and At Design Lab (Tokyo). Final drop occurred in October 2025.

title: DK
content:
About
The DK ("Door Knob") is a collaboration between SF Yoyos and A-RT, known for its novelty doorknob-profile shape. Released in Silver, Pink, Black, Gold (blast), and Light Pink colorways.

title: Holy Yogurt
content:
About
The Holy Yogurt is a Delrin (POM) reinterpretation of A-RT's earlier Grail model.

title: Inhaler
content:
About
The Inhaler is Charles Haycock's signature model, featuring a grooved inner rim that produces a distinctive resonant sound during play.

title: Yokel
content:
About
The Yokel is a compact, sub-50mm monometal throw from A-RT.

title: A10
content: AboutThe A10 commemorates AceYo's 10th anniversary (2023). Features stainless steel rings sandwiched between an anodized aluminum body and machined POM rims, combining the spin power of a bi-metal with the floaty soft-touch feel of POM. Available in Silver/Blue Ring, Light Blue/White Ring, Pink/Black Ring, and Black/White Ring.

title: Blue Angel
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the Blue Angel (Series 1, 1999) as a butterfly-shaped plastic ball-bearing yo-yo with an original delta centrifugal cam auto return system and a side cap showing a woman with blue hair. It is listed at 56 mm by 37 mm and 59.31 g, with a US$10 retail price. In 2000 the design was replaced with a text-only "Mythical Blue Angel" cap and starbursts were replaced with response pads.The YoYo Wiki says about 5,000 were made, and that the graphic was too much for some retailers selling to children.

title: Rad 3
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Rad 3 in the Black Mamba line and marks it unreleased.

title: Rad 5
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Rad 5 in the Black Mamba line and marks it unreleased.

title: Inferno
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki says the Inferno was produced by Abbe Toys as Dave Schulte's signature yo-yo, an auto-return with a four-armed cam system and a ball bearing axle, with metal balls under the side caps. A total of 4,416 were produced and sold between 2002 and 2004; the mold was then lost. The Yo-Yo Museum, from Schulte's collection, confirms the 2002-2004 production.

title: PhatYo Black Mamba
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum says the PhatYo line was made and sold in Australia by Abbe Toys, makers of the Black Mamba. The PhatYo Black Mamba is a redesign of the original with a new "cookie" response system, a rubbery recessed pad with teeth, and "Yo-Matic" branding for the centrifugal cam auto-return.

title: PhatYo Blue Angel
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the PhatYo Blue Angel as a concave version of the original Black Mamba with the cookie response system and some additional rim weighting, branded Yo-Matic for the centrifugal cam auto-return. The YoYo Wiki notes the Blue Angel was first made as a Black Mamba and later remade as a PhatYo.

title: PhatYo Mythical Blue Angel
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum says the Mythical Blue Angel was one of the high-performance PhatYos, with response cookies offering 120 settings and a concave axle sleeve over the bearing. It is similar to the Trick Assassin but lighter without metal weight rings, at about 60 g. It was briefly imported into the U.S. before sales were stopped because of alleged patent and trademark violations.

title: PhatYo Shadow Glider
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki PhatYo page lists the Shadow Glider among Abbe's PhatYo yo-yos. No further details were found.

title: PhatYo Trick Assassin
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki says the Trick Assassin began in the Black Mamba line and continued under PhatYo in the early 2000s, with a slimline butterfly profile, metal rims, cookie pads (120 response settings) and a concave plastic sleeve over an ABEC-5 bearing. It was briefly imported to the U.S. before being stopped over patent issues. The Yo-Yo Museum lists 68-70 g and a 2.25 in diameter.

title: PhatYo Velvet Hammer
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki PhatYo page lists the Velvet Hammer among Abbe's PhatYo yo-yos. No further details were found.

title: Regeneration
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki says the Regeneration was released in May 1999 and is a ball bearing yo-yo without the centrifugal cam, which let players do intermediate tricks. The Yo-Yo Museum records a Series 1 Regeneration 2000 with a take-apart design and ball bearing axle, 58 g, US$6, in a regular edition and a limited edition with an all-black body and gold foil imprint.

title: Rolling Thunder
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Rolling Thunder as an auto-return yo-yo released in May 1999 in the Black Mamba line, using four-armed quads weighted with steel balls and a steel ball bearing axle (the five-star equivalent of the Voodoo Guru). It is listed at 56.69 g.The Yo-Yo Museum records an approximate sleep time of 20-45 seconds and a US$11 original retail price, and says it is virtually identical to the five-star Black Mamba apart from name and packaging.

title: Steel
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the Mamba Steel as an anodized opal aluminum ball bearing yo-yo with high-grade steel components and aluminum for weight reduction, a mirror-like black finish, take-apart design and starbursts, originally US$25 (1999). The YoYo Wiki says it was meant to compete with the ProYo Cold Fusion and Tom Kuhn SB-2.

title: Stone Cutter
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Stone Cutter as a transaxle looping yo-yo released in the Black Mamba line in 1999 or 2000, touted as comparable to a modded Yomega Fireball and essentially the three-star Regeneration.

title: Voodoo Guru
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Voodoo Guru as released May 1999, with a four-armed quad cam system and an acetal transaxle sleeve. The Yo-Yo Museum records it as a Series 1 1999 model weighing 66 g, with an approximate sleep time of 10-25 seconds and a US$7 original retail price, virtually identical to the three-star Black Mamba apart from the name and packaging.

title: Yo-Matic Black Mamba
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki calls the Yo-Matic Black Mamba Abbe Toys' most well-known product. It uses a centrifugal cam rather than a clutch and was made in a 3-star version with an acetal transaxle sleeve and a 5-star version with a ball bearing. It was imported into the U.S. by several distributors during the late 1990s boom.The Yo-Yo Museum records the 3-star as a 1998 model with a plastic transaxle and an original retail price of US$7. A PhatYo version released in the early 2000s replaced starbursts with cookie response pads.

title: Abel
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re incredibly thrilled to bring you the latest instalment in our featherweight organics design line.

Meet Abel.

SPECS

Dia 54.3mmWidth 48.4mmWeight 63.2gMaterial 6061 AL

The Abel is easy to introduce.

Its antecedent, the Noah, began as a project in making an unapologetically light and round, blank-canvas organic that leaned fully into characteristics of the form factor. It had no bias for rim weight, a bubbly-wide and comfortable frame, and an incredibly fun lightness.

The Noah took off in ways we didn’t imagine, and became one of our own favourites.

The Abel extends that project of making our version of a fundamental, purist’s organic, and takes another step towards simplicity.

It has endless curves, and lines only where strictly necessary.

The most obvious difference is that the Abel isn’t compatible with Side Effects, a design feature that is core to the Noah.

It’s not really addition via subtraction here; the Abel isn’t intended as an upgrade over the Noah. It’s more of a 1a) and 1b) sort of deal.

Some players deeply enjoy customisation and control over the way a yoyo plays; some others enjoy the ease and intuitiveness of playing it as they come, and find tuning an additional effort.

The Noah is for the tinkerer; the Abel is for the player who doesn’t need to fiddle.

On that note, the Abel is one of the smoothest designs we’ve manufactured. This thing is just glass.

The Abel is machined out of 6061 aluminum bar stock, a switch from the 7068 alloy that the Noahs used.

We apportioned some of the extra material along the cup to give it an even, if slightly center-biased distribution.

We also added a tiny nub in the center of the cup – a homage to Flat Caps and the original Side Effects compatibility of its forebear – that many observed.

We enjoyed its subtle disruption of the otherwise unbroken curvature of the hub. It’s similar to the little “halo” groove that marked our initial line of organics, beginning with the Cloudberry and most recently in the Goji – an understated, light touch that we enjoy.

This nub is also featured on a few designs we have in the oven, and we can’t wait to show you more in due time.

The Abel clocks in at 63.2g, which is less than a gram heftier than the Noah in its lightest configuration.

The Abel’s weight distribution sits between a Noah with AL Ultra Lights installed, and another fitted with AL Flat Caps. It plays that way, too. It’s got a bit more body and presence than a Noah at its most featherweight form, but retains every bit of its light touch.

The Noah was originally designed as a miniaturised blend of the Goji and Pomelo (anyone who has played these two would understand this comparison), and the Abel shares that lineage. It’s endlessly boppable, light, and 63.2g of relaxed fun in a midsized frame.

The name Noah refers to a sense of restfulness and calm that we hoped to capture in its design and play. Abel translates to breath and vapor – a fitting name, we think, that encapsulates a sense of airiness and tranquility.

The Abel comes with a matte, ceramic-like blast that allows the colors on these to pop.

We masked the inmost portion along the schmoove step to keep it entirely unblasted and smooth, so as to reduce friction between the string and the matte surface. We also hand-process each Abel with various fabrics to further mute surface friction.

A handful of Abel prototypes were sent out to a list of friends and supporters of Atmos earlier in the year, as a way of expressing our gratitude for the incredible support we’ve received, and also to ask for feedback on the Abel. It was a wonderful exercise in testing on a scale we had never done before.

The Abel is the Noah’s slightly reserved but self-assured twin brother.

Smooth, airy, and easy, and it does everything with a light touch.

You know what you’re getting every single time.

title: Absurdity
content: AboutReleased exclusively through YoYoExpert on January 9, 2020, the Absurdity draws design DNA from the Monocle and Float — the two most popular models Jordan made under his previous brand Smashing YoYos. A high-performance monometal machined from 7068 aluminum, it shipped with an NSK DS Platinum bearing and Airetic string. Limited to 30 individually numbered units.

title: AbysmAL
content:
From ILYY:

"We ventured to cosmic ends, gazed even deeper into the everlasting darkness and saw… light.Delve deep into the black and emerge with eternal bliss through the white horizon.

The AbysmAL is the full aluminum representation of the crushing Abyss inheriting its comfortable and sophisticated shape and fingerspin abilities. We beefed up the rims to retain the powerful spin and stability.

The AbysmAL comes in two vastly different colorways.

First up: The ever so fitting Einstein-Rosen-Bridge edition (ERB for short) for all your time traveling wormhole needs.

There is also a second edition of the AbysmAL: Dinosalat. This color-way has first been used for the inner cup of the DR3I."

There were 20 ERB (Silver/Black) yo-yos made and 23 Dinosalat yo-yos made in the initial run of the AbysmAL.

title: Abyss
content:
From ILYY:

"Dominik’s view into The Abyss.

Oversized powerhouse, hubless, ready for fingerspins."

Run #1

Release: April 2016Diameter: 57mmWidth: 43.50mmWeight: 63.50gBearing: CResponse: 15x22x2 pads

The initial production run of Abyss consisted of 10 units in a black colorway with a Soda Blast finish.

Run #2

The second production run of Abyss consisted of 20 units in a black colorway with black rims and a Soda Blast finish.

title: Acadia BTM (Bimetal)
content:
History / About
The bimetal sibling of the Acadia, featuring stainless steel outer rims that significantly boost stability and spin time. Despite being a lightweight competitor, it delivers a deeply stable sleep that belies its weight. Jeffrey matched and pressed every ring by hand using a Delrin negative to prevent warpage — a standard he held across all his bimetal releases. The final run in January 2023 added a special TiAlN-coated version with white ceramic bearings.

title: Acadia (Monometal)
content:
History / About
Jeffrey Pang’s self-described “signature yoyo” — a performance-oriented evolution of the 2015 Evora. The design process focused relentlessly on removing material from the hub: smaller hub area, thinner wall thicknesses, shorter axle and nipple. The diameter was increased from 54mm to 56.5mm, inspired by the One Drop Citizen, bringing dramatically improved stability and spin time. Multiple runs were produced between 2021 and 2023; the final run came on January 31, 2023, and included a TiAlN-coated version with white ceramic bearings and white matte response pads.

title: Accelerated
content:
From Motion:

"Introducing our next model in the Motion Lineup - Accelerated (Motion)

All three of the models before this were slightly “oversized” by what I would consider “normal” standards. We are taking a dive into a YoYo that is a bit more undersized in nature. The organic nature of this bell shaped YoYo helps with the comfort aspect of throwing.

Immediately you will recognize some of the characteristics that you will find in all the Motion lineup, from the sunken dome, to some of the most gorgeous cuts you will ever see on a YoYo.

Our value promise has always been not only do you get a YoYo that preforms well above its value, but will also look the part. Motion has offered yo-yos with unique design characteristics on every release, one of the most unique we have done was the rim design on Centrifugal, which has been reengineered on this YoYo.

As always only the best materials are used: 7068 aluminum body with stainless steel rims. This combination of premium materials and limit-pushing design gives you a presence on the string unlike anything you have played previously. We truly believe this fills a niche that hasn’t been tapped.

@hesperaux and I were chatting one evening, talking about YoYo design and what we would like in a new throw. We discussed the existing Motion lineup and we felt as if there was a gap in our lineup that Accelerated would fill. @hesperaux and I went over the CAD many times trying to tweak and design it. The goal: that it would not only play exponentially better than it looks but also look amazing doing it.

One design decision was made by @gaitesk13. He felt as if we should add some flair to the rims and create a “bump” on the edge that is both for aesthetic and design purposes for weight distribution. He was right, it was the right move. This design feature makes the yoyo feel slightly smaller but play bigger. It's one of the unique things about this design that we love.

The collective effort of all of my proto team has lead to one of our favorite designs to come out of the Motion shop.

The body cuts have been brought back, the unique rim has been revamped, and an updated, more unique design for the dome which will further set our brand apart.

We feel like once again we have set the bar higher for existing products and we encourage you to experience what the difference is - this is Motion. 

So don’t let the specs fool you, this YoYo is a performer, it’s wide stance and undersized body play like a full sized yoyo. The spin time is something that I personally like to focus on, and this one is no slouch, it is designed to spin longer than any of our current lineup, one could say it has been “accelerated” from our other models.

We've also been pushing the limits of machining. @fpm_yoyomanufacture has been an amazing partner, allowing us to confidently shrink the wall thickness and create elaborate and beautiful stainless steel ring profiles not usually seen with these materials. The wall thickness of accelerated is about twice as thin as previous designs, but the ss rings work together with the body to create a durable and powerful design. One of the motion design goals is to push limits and advance yoyo design norms.

The YoYo loves to fly through each combo, with a strong presence on the string. Regens are a breeze and brings the YoYo back to life after short or long combos. At no time are you left wanting any more power. Even when the YoYo becomes exhausted, it still has energy to roll back to your hand in a snap.

Stability and long spin times were the goal here, and we far exceeded anything that we could have imagined."

title: Ace of Aces
content: AboutDescribed as "one of AceYo's most luxurious models," the Ace of Aces features broad stainless steel rings on a titanium body for optimal weight distribution. Debuted at the 2023 World Yo-yo Contest. Arrives in a premium wooden presentation box. Released in Raw finish.

title: Ace of Aces X
content: AboutThe Ace of Aces X is an aluminum and stainless steel bi-metal counterpart to the titanium Ace of Aces. Features wide straight geometry described as "a great all-arounder." The first production run features large intricate laser engravings in the cup. Available in Pink/White Flowers, Raw, Blue/White Wave, and Green/White Wave.

title: Acorn Full Size (Delrin Prototype)
content:
About
“It's the Acorn Mini but not mini.” A Delrin-bodied prototype variant of the Acorn Full Size, running a standard C-size bearing instead of the metal edition's bearing, unresponsive, using TK hex hardware. Low stock at release.

title: Acorn Mini
content:
The Acorn Mini began as a joke. In February 2026, YYE forum regular Slestak75 (Steve) teased a new fixed axle design he claimed would take the community "deeply by emotion" — then revealed the Acorn and Acorn Mini to be literal acorns that had fallen from the oak tree behind his house. The thread immediately took on a life of its own.

Andy (AudreySickburn) of Return Bottoms was the first to take the gag seriously. Within hours of the reveal, Andy had modeled the acorn shape in CAD and 3D-printed prototypes in wood-blend filament, complete with a glued-in stainless steel axle and MR85 pads. After testing and iterating on the geometry to address balance issues, Andy and Steve agreed to take the design to the machine shop. The production Acorn Mini was specified in solid copper — a material chosen for its density and heft in a small package — at 40.6mm diameter and 30.5mm width, running an MR85 bearing. Proceeds above production cost were designated for the Social Work fund of Salem VA Hospital.

Each Acorn Mini box is a 3D-printed tree stump. A pop-up squirrel, Throw-Yo Threads gummy Acorn counterweight, and a few stickers are pack-ins.

title: Acronym
content: Tony Šec's founder signature monometal. Named "acronym" (/ˈæk.rə.nɪm/). Drawing design cues from the Sympathy, the Acronym evolves that profile into a more aggressive, competition-ready monometal. Machined from 7075 aluminum — a higher grade than most production monometals — for exceptional durability and precision. Tony has been a core figure in the Bohnice Prague yo-yo scene since the brand's founding. Also released as the Acronym 이학제 colorway for Korean player Hakje Lee (이학제) in Polished Baby Blue with an engraved ZG-style logo, and a Bogdan Bezuglyi half-swap colorway.

title: Acrylic Echelon
content:
About

There were only 2 Acrylic Echelons made, different weights and diameters. These were made by Landon Balk of 3Y03 yoyos. These two yoyos were sold at VA States in January 2014, the first OhYesYo yoyos to be produced and sold.

title: Action
content: History / AboutProduction model followed an explicitly labeled pre-production release and offers a conventional compact plastic string-trick format.

title: Activated
content:
About

Activated is a V-shaped bimetal yo-yo from Motion YoYo, featuring a 7068 aluminum body and stainless steel rims. Motion first listed it on its internal timeline as a prototype. Preorders opened on October 5, 2026, in five new colorways, including a matte purple and a gold-rimmed (not brass) blue variant. Motion's Jeremy Ayers noted that a version of this design was done on Perpetual, the company's very first yo-yo, of which only two exist.

title: ADDICTION
content: About the ADDICTIONThe ADDICTION is sOMEThING's entry-level model, offering access to the brand at a significantly lower price point than the flagship aluminum throws. The plastic/metal hybrid construction follows the approach of Hiroyuki's YoYoJam-era signature models. Available in standard and Splash colorways. ~¥4,400 JPY (~$29 USD).

title: ADHD
content:
History / About
Signature monometal for Nam Donghun, Korean National 1A Champion (2017-2019) and 2023 Worlds 1A finalist (6th place). Large 58mm frame supports big sweeping-movement tricks at high speed.

title: Adrenaline
content: The Adrenaline is Blaise Becker's signature model — the 2024 NER 1A runner-up and W1LD USA team member. Described as "small but wide," it reduces diameter relative to the Wilderness while maintaining an outsized width, with stainless steel rims accounting for roughly two-thirds of total weight in a tri-material construction. The Adrenaline combines the Wilderness aspect ratio with the Wild-Trio's PC plus SS structure, designed specifically for competition.

title: Adrenaline SS
content: The Adrenaline SS is a solid stainless steel variant of the Adrenaline, making it the densest and most compact throw in the W1LD lineup. The extreme weight density of full stainless construction delivers tremendous spin power from a small frame. Available in a Size C no-logo version and a Size D bearing AP Limited configuration.

title: Aerodynex
content:
History / About
The Aerodynex is the signature model of mowl ambassador Hayato Itani, developed after two years of design work and six prototype configurations — two monometals, two bimetals, and two titanium variants. The name combines "Aero" (reflecting Itani's mastery of horizontal tricks in the air) and "Dynamics" (the aggressive, unpredictable movement of his tricks). The wide body creates a sensation of soaring through the air while maintaining unwavering stability to support Itani's high-speed, aggressive competition style. First pre-released as a no-logo version at the 2023 World Yo-Yo Contest in Osaka. A polycarbonate variant (Aero) with midship rims was also produced.

title: Aerodynex Ti
content:
History / About
The full titanium flagship of Hayato Itani's Aerodynex series, pre-released as a no-logo version at the 2023 World Yo-Yo Contest in Osaka where Itani used it on stage during competition. After two years of development through six prototype configurations (two monometals, two bimetals, two titaniums), the Aerodynex Ti delivers the ideal balance of agility, spin power, and maneuverability for Itani's aggressive horizontal and aerial style. Standout feature is innovative two-color laser engraving on the inner rim — a cutting-edge visual technique that makes the titanium release visually unmistakable. Itani described it as "An ideal yo-yo combining the agility and spin power of a bimetal with great maneuverability."

title: Aerodynex Ti V2
content:
History / About
The second generation of the Aerodynex titanium flagship, released in 2025. Refines the design of the original Aerodynex Ti with updated proportions and performance improvements to meet the evolving demands of Hayato Itani's competition career. Maintains the wide-body titanium construction and aggressive styling of the original.

title: Aether
content: About AetherThe Aether is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo designed for players stepping up from plastic. Balanced performance with smooth spin and responsive handling for string tricks.

title: Aethon
content:
History / About
The Aethon is a bimetal from GWAY Throws combining a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims. The wide catch zone provides forgiveness on harder tricks, while rounded rims minimize string wear and keep handling comfortable during extended sessions. Rim weight contributes spin power and durability. Available colorways include Open Ocean, Olive Panthenon, Rainbow Road, Tyrian Dreams, and Acid Wash Rainbow Nightmare.

title: AfterLife
content:
History / About
The AfterLife is one of G2's core modern-era models, released in 2023 and receiving consistent new colorway drops throughout 2023–2025. The AL7 AfterLife variants use higher-grade aluminum for a more powerful spin character. The model was included in the 2024 "Totality" solar eclipse special colorway drop — one of multiple G2 models given themed colorways for that event.

title: Aftermath Apocalypse
content: AboutThe Aftermath Apocalypse is a limited collaboration between Zeekio and Twisted Stringz, built on Zeekio's Aftermath platform. The yo-yo features a custom "Meteor Shower" anodized finish by Grunt Bull Anodizing and ships with Twisted Stringz's Trifecta bearing — a 10-ball Size C bearing with a dual-curved groove designed for unresponsive play and horizontal tricks. A Twisted Stringz string is included in the box. The h-profile shape targets horizontal play and finger spins.

title: Aftershock
content:
History / About
The Aftershock is G2 taking the Quake and enlarging it — a trend popular in the scene at the time (CLYW's Gnarwhal→Sasquatch, YYF's 888→DNA). The profile is a larger Quake in every way: same scalloped catch zone, same H-shape, same stepped rim design. Reviewer Brett Grimes found the larger diameter actually suited his larger hands significantly better than the original Quake. The Aftershock remains one of his all-time favorite G2 models. The AL7 edition was produced in extremely small numbers — Sour Apple (8 total) and Blue Steel (5 total) — making them among the rarest G2 pieces.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (BOSS Wrath and BOSS Rage, both included)

title: Agate
content: History / AboutDistinct model documented in Rewind's museum catalog.

title: Ai
content: About the AiThe Ai is the signature model of six-time World 5A Champion Takeshi Matsuura, featuring a revolutionary double-stepped round body shape developed to optimize stability for freehand play. Brass rims on an aluminum body provide dense edge weighting at 70.3 grams. Mirrored stepped outer caps are removable, and a shim-based adjustable gap system allows fine-tuning of response characteristics.

title: Aibou
content: AboutThe Aibou is JIGUN's entry-level competition throw, with "Aibou" (あいぼう) meaning "partner" or "buddy" in Japanese. Released in 2022 as one of the brand's first products, it is machined from 7068 aluminum to mainstream Japanese competition specifications. Available through the LEP store at $25 and at international retailers. Some retail packaging includes Sochi Company pads and hardware as a co-branded edition. Colorways have included Blue, Pink, Light Olive, Purple, Orange, Tiffany, Green, True Love, and Black.

title: Air King
content: AboutThe Air King was JT's flagship offstring model released in 2018. Its POM body is combined with an aluminum alloy rim precisely placed for maximum stability, and it uses a Size D (H-Spin) bearing — larger than the standard Size C — for an extra-wide gap of 64mm catch zone. Multiple rim color options were available on a standard White body, as well as a Green/Orange rim colorway.

title: Aire
content: AboutThe Aire is the signature model of Bryan Figueroa, six-time concurrent US National 4A Champion. Released in fall 2016, it was developed as an updated Kamui designed to meet modern 4A performance standards. Easier to use than the original Kamui, it was available in a standard version and a "Japan Edition" colorway.

title: Aitch
content:
From One Drop:

"The H (Aitch) shape yo-yo seems to be under-represented.  Even if you look at One Drop history, the H is rare. When we have done it (Benchmark Series) in the past, we kept it only mildly H. We decided that it was time to do a proper H shape.

The main idea of it being “proper H” is that the profile would need to be as extreme as possible without compromising how it played. The diameter is on the large side at 55.88mm. In order to make everything work, it needed to be a touch on the narrow side in relation to the diameter: the width is 39.62mm. We also wanted it to have Side Effects and to ship with a new style which is the Mini Spike. We feel like we achieved the goals and hope you agree."

title: Akura MG
content:
History / About
Luftverk’s first magnesium model, released January 2024. Development began in 2021 but was cancelled due to performance issues. The project was revived after Jeffrey gained knowledge from developing the plastic lineup — magnesium’s low-density characteristics behave similarly to plastic, and the techniques learned from the Plastic Fulvia unlocked the path to making it work. The raw version oxidizes quickly, developing blotches that Jeffrey considers a beautiful natural process; a ceramic-coated version is available for those who prefer a stable, protected finish. Despite feeling soft and light in hand like a plastic, the spin power and torque are unmistakably metal.

title: Akura TI-7068
content:
History / About
Released to celebrate 10 years of Luftverk, the Akura TI-7068 is an aluminum-and-titanium version of the Akura originally produced in magnesium. It carries forward the bold “brutalist” design aesthetic first introduced with the 2015 Evora. The key engineering innovation is a hollow air pocket inside the titanium rings — rather than solid rings pressed against the body, the titanium contains an internal void that modifies weight distribution and contributes to a uniquely floaty feel while preserving the chunky, visually striking rim aesthetic. Required extensive creative problem-solving since the proportions of the magnesium original could not be directly translated to heavier materials.

title: Albatross
content:
History / About
The Albatross is G2's very first release and the foundation on which the entire brand was built. Designed by Jacob Gross and Brett Grimes, it debuted in early 2012 to extraordinary acclaim. YoYoSkills' Dr. Yo-Yo (Chris Allen) described it as "one of the best flagship yo-yos I have ever had the pleasure of testing, but one of the best yo-yos I have ever tested period." The Albatross features a rounded V-shape profile with a clever split weight ring design — an equal amount of weight placed at both the rim and the halfway point. The slightly raised hub lifts the core, effectively widening the gap and catch zone. It came with a One Drop 10-Ball bearing and clear flowable silicone response. The success of the Albatross secured G2's reputation immediately; they went on to win YoYoSkills' New Manufacturer of the Year at the end of their debut year.

title: Alebrije
content:
From ZGRT:

"This project is the result of many hours of work, trials, testing, R&D, and many other stuff that are probably missing in the number of things we explored while developing this project.

When developing this project we had one thing in mind: creating a yoyo with an interchangeable bearing seat to accommodate different bearing sizes and widths. We started playing around with few concepts to more or less understand if this idea could become in a potential project.

Having that feature in mind, we went ahead and prototyped this system with aluminum body material and with few different type of shapes just to have an idea about the possibilities in using this modular system.

By playing around with the design and the different prototypes, the idea of incorporating it into a wooden throw blew our minds as this would be the perfect candidate to also bring another element or functionality to the system: fixed axle.

Having the experience in designing El MiJo, we decided to also bring such versatility to this design and make this wooden throw capable to use fixed axle and ball bearings.

The concept finally started to have a better shape of what we were looking to accomplish originally. The Alebrije then was born.

Alebrijes are surreal creatures from an oneiric (dreaming) world conformed

by physical elements of different fantastical/mythical and real animals. The creatures typically have the four classical elements as part of them: earth, water, air and fire. Around that idea, we wanted a throw to have different elements such as: wood, aluminum, different bearing sizes and types.

One of the characteristics of alebrijes is their multicolour designs and the way we wanted to express that is by adding different colours to the bearing seats and to the outer caps to contrast the beautiful tones of the natural wood.

Due to the nature and characteristics of the wood, the process of making this throw required the utilization of CNC to accommodate the modular bearing seat system as precise as possible.

The effort and resources invested in this throw were out of our original scope but the final result was worth the effort.

We are planning to bring the Alebrije to life for Fixed Axle February. At this point we will be only able to accommodate approximately 50 units. More information about when and how to order will be available at our site, IG or by DM.

Hope you enjoy this throw as much as we do.

Let nothing hold you down!"

title: Alive
content: AboutThe Alive is Veronika Kamenská's bi-metal signature and her second collaboration with AceYo. Features a small fingerspin hub. Kamenská won the European Championship using this model. Described as "really fast and stable." Available in Blue and Red.

title: Allegiance
content:
History / About
The Allegiance is G2's newest major model release as of May 2026, priced at $150. The "Trust Jake" colorway — named after Jacob Gross himself — is a direct personal statement from the brand founder. Three colorways were released in the initial drop: Trust Jake, Rainbow Galaxy, and Pacific Storm. Full material specs not yet widely documented at time of research.

title: Alliance
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"The Alliance is a collaboration yoyo between Yoyofriends and Damian Puckett.

The body is made from titanium and features the One Drop Side Effects system and NSK bearing. Optimizing the use of titanium resulted in a long spinning, stable yoyo. The performance combined with its comfortable shape can handle anything from a laid back session to the most intense combos.

The shape of the yo-yo and how it feels in the hand is also very important for us. Comfort was the driving factor when making the shape. The Alliance met all of our goals."

title: Flying Disk
content: HistoryAlox Manufacturing Company began in 1919 in St. Louis, Missouri, as a shoelace maker, later adding kites, marbles and jump ropes, and entered yo-yo manufacturing in the 1930s. YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's collector guide, says Alox bought yo-yo halves from other manufacturers and painted and assembled them, selling pegged models at 10 cents and one-piece free-spinning models at 15 cents. The Flying Disk is listed as one of Alox's two yo-yo models.

content: HistoryAlox Manufacturing Company began in 1919 in St. Louis, Missouri, as a shoelace maker, later adding kites, marbles and jump ropes, and entered yo-yo manufacturing in the 1930s.
