title: Alpha
content:
The following story was taken from ILYY's website.

After exploring performance-oriented design aspects with the Numen we took a step back and thought about what we love most about yoyos and which elements capture the essence of fun.

Out came the Alpha.

Slightly undersized at 53mm, it is a quick and snappy player. The smaller diameter combined with the massive outer stainless steel rings enables Alpha to perform like a full size yoyo without the compromise of kickback during throws and binds. It is an agile player with higher RPM while still retaining powerful spin. We carefully tweaked inertia to land in this goldy-locks zone.

The overall shape inherits the best elements of other ILYYs:

The Numen’s gap profile unlocks monstrous fingergrinds and gets out of the way during horizontal tricks. At a modern 45 mm width paired with its wide catch-zone, Alpha takes care of those difficult to hit (horizontal) tricks. The 4.5 mm gap takes in all string layers tech tricks bring to the table.

In addition, it allows for Numen’s fingerspin-hungy convex inner cup design guaranteeing flawless fingerspins at any time. The beautiful rounded-off central spike adds crucial milimeters to the overall axle length yet does not pose any danger of hurting the player.

Structural integrity was also considered and the upped AL-wall thickness of the Numen was incorporated into the design. Deformation from floor-hits is reduced, Alpha will retain its smoothness longer.

Alpha features blasted and electroplated stainless steel rims for great spintimes and grinds. The slick surface effectively works against spin loss during accidental touches.

The ring-body-intersection again features our rounded-off design for a more aesthetic impression.

We modified the profile to improve on rejection tricks giving the string a distinct edge segment to snap over.

The inner cup extends beneath the entire ring and finds its conclusion in an IRG lip allowing for amazing thumbgrinds. The steel ring sits on a wide base further strengthening the overall integrity.

The Alpha is our take on a Jaqueline-of-all-trades yoyo. It can do it all, but in a fun and motivating way.

Initial Run

The initial run of the Alpha came out in October of 2025 and was 25 pieces in the Inferno colorway with a Soda Blast finish.

title: Alpha Crash
content: C3's first injection-molded plastic yo-yo, designed for the 44CLASH competition in Japan. Based on the Berserker's step-straight platform with a lowered edge, it offered intermediate-to-advanced performance in an affordable plastic shell. Despite the plastic construction, it delivered stability competitive with full-metal contest releases of that year. Available in Turquoise/White, Purple/Yellow, Red/Yellow, Yellow/White, Red, and Grey. Price: $19.99.

title: Alt Bastet
content: History / About7075 reinterpretation of the original Bastet organic profile, using a smaller-diameter D bearing for tighter centrifugal feel.

title: Alter
content: AboutThe Alter is the signature model of Sora Uchihashi (Japan National 1A Runner-up), released in 2025. An A7075 aluminum body is paired with a high-weight, wide stainless steel rim for the combination of delicate trajectory control and breathing space during performance. JT's description for the Alter centers on the philosophy of "from imitation to transformation." Available in Silver/Matte Black Rim.

title: CAPPED INERTIA
content:
About
The CAPPED INERTIA is an evolution of the INERTIA in which the polycarbonate rims extend inward to form the caps rather than terminating at the outer edge. The diameter is reduced by 1mm to 55mm compared to the standard INERTIA. The aluminium weight distribution was reworked for the new geometry, resulting in a more technical play profile. Pre-released at WYYC 2025 Prague via the Spinkult booth. Released in Silver/Clear and Purple/Purple colourways at $65.

title: CAPPED INERTIA – AMBER UNIVERSE 2
content:
About
The CAPPED INERTIA - AMBER UNIVERSE 2 is the second collaboration between "alternatives" and SENSE in the Amber Universe series. The aluminium body features a magma-like gradient anodise, while the transparent polycarbonate caps are treated to show watermarks and dye traces creating a misty effect. Released as an early limited run with a larger production anticipated. $70.

title: INERTIA
content:
About
The INERTIA is "alternatives" first aluminium-plus-polycarbonate hybrid design. The PC rims are press-fit to the 6061 aluminium body, distributing weight towards the edges for longer spin times while keeping the price accessible at $65. Released in six colourways: Black AL / Neon PC, Blue AL / Pink PC, Clear AL / Clear PC, Grey AL / Tiffany PC, Red AL / Red POM (POM substituted for PC in this variant), and Red AL / Black PC.

title: INERTIA – AMBER UNIVERSE
content:
About
The INERTIA - AMBER UNIVERSE is a collaboration between "alternatives" and SENSE. The polycarbonate rims use advanced dyeing and surface treatment to create amber-coloured caps with air-bubble inclusions that evoke the look of ancient amber with suspended debris. The first release in the Amber Universe collection. Released at US Nationals 2025. $70.

title: INERTIA – VOLT
content:
About
The INERTIA - VOLT is a special colourway release of the INERTIA, debuted at US Nationals 2025. The neon-volt polycarbonate rims use an advanced dyeing process to achieve brighter colour saturation, particularly under stage lighting. Specifications are identical to the standard INERTIA. $65.

title: INERTIA – ZAFRAN
content:
About
The INERTIA - ZAFRAN is a signature colourway release for Zafran Aqil, two-time Malaysian National Champion (2014–2015) and "alternatives" team member. Released at US Nationals 2025. Specifications are identical to the standard INERTIA. $70.

title: KEY
content:
About
The KEY is the signature yo-yo of Karthik Devaraj, 2023 Malaysia and Thailand National Open Champion and "alternatives" team member. The stainless steel rims are pressed directly into the 6061 aluminium body rather than inserted via a conventional ring, a construction rejected by multiple factories before one agreed to produce it. The flat hub design keeps all weight at the rims. Development began May 2024 and took ten months. Designed for Karthik's WYYC 2025 debut. Released in Dark Coral, Emerald Green, and Raw (uncoated mirror finish) colourways at $150. The Raw variant requires periodic polishing to maintain its mirror appearance.

title: LACRIMA
content:
About
The LACRIMA is the signature yo-yo of Lam Nguyen, 2023 Vietnam National Champion and "alternatives" team member. Built for "pure power and precision without gimmicks," it uses 7075 aluminium — stronger and denser than 6061 — combined with stainless steel rims. Finishing is split between blasted (Maroon, Midnight Blue, Silver) and glossy (Sky Blue, Lilac) colourways to cater to different aesthetic preferences. $110.

title: re:inertia
content:
About
The re:inertia is a D-bearing variant of the INERTIA platform, built around the premise that a D-bearing yo-yo had to be executed perfectly to be worth releasing. The diameter is reduced from 56mm to 51mm, and the polycarbonate rims curve inward to the caps, enabling finger spin tricks. Released in Pastel (Blue/Cherry Pink) and Silver colourways at $65.

title: re:inertia – yejune
content:
About
The re:inertia - yejune is a signature colourway collaboration between "alternatives" and 44EMPORIUM for Yejune. Pre-released at AP Open 2026 Singapore. Specifications are identical to the standard re:inertia. $70.

title: UNLOCK
content:
About
The UNLOCK is the second signature yo-yo for Karthik Devaraj, developed after WYYC 2025 to support his new trick set. It uses a tri-material construction combining 7075 aluminium, stainless steel rims, and polycarbonate caps — an unusual combination engineered specifically to minimise vibration issues common in tri-material designs. The wide 52.5mm width was chosen for forgiveness on stage. Released in a Volt (Silver/Volt) colourway at $130.

title: American Metal SpinGadget
content:
About
The American Metal SpinGadget (アメリカンメタルスピンガジェット, #アメガジ) is a collaboration between SpinGear and One Drop YoYos, released on April 4 (Japan National Yo-Yo Day). SpinGear's Metal SpinGadget design was licensed to One Drop Manufacturing in the USA, who produced it using their machining facility. It is the first SpinGear design to be made outside Japan.
The collaboration introduces One Drop's iconic Side Effects axle system to the SpinGadget platform, allowing players to swap the axle assembly for different weight/feel characteristics. It ships with custom Ultra Light LEGO Side Effects (U.L.L.E.S.) at just 2.6g. The bearing was changed from the standard model's D-size to a C-size NSK Flat bearing, which SpinGear notes gives a "more friendly play feel."
Available in Clear, Gunmetal Black, Buddy Orange, White Cerakote, Pink Cerakote, and Blue (prototype) colorways — Cerakote finishes commanding premium pricing.

title: All American Jeweled (Prototype)
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The Yo-Yo Museum lists the All American Jeweled as a special prototype with a natural maple finish and a jeweled flag logo. The museum owner says Bill Cress told him the company planned an "All American Spinner" and had 12 prototypes, and he learned this example existed only when Cress sold remaining old stock in 2018.

The Collector series came out in 1990 in metalflake finishes, with a profile the Yo-Yo Museum says resembles the Russell Coke yo-yos. Catalog numbers recorded by the museum include BS-307 (deep blue sea), JG-306 (jade green) and RB-302 (candy apple regal blue). It was packaged in an American Spinners "Yo-Yo Garage" with a white cotton string and retailed for $15; the BS-307 example measures 59.7 mm diameter, 32 mm width and 49.65 g.

title: Diamond Spinner
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The YoYo Wiki lists a Diamond Spinner among the company's models. The Yo-Yo Museum describes a "Diamond Special" as the only model more expensive than the Rhinestone Spinner: $20 for 28 hand-set rhinestones, added to the price of the chosen catalog model. The museum does not confirm that the two names refer to the same item.

title: Pocket Rocket
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The Pocket Rocket, from around 1988-1990, was a one-piece wooden yo-yo that the Yo-Yo Museum says was actually made in Sweden by Halvorsen, the same company behind many wooden yo-yos sold in Canada in the 1960s and 1970s; its shape matches the Canadian National Olympic and National Pro Tournament models. The seal reads "Sweden" and the museum rates its quality below the Standard and Collector models. Original retail price was $4. The YoYo Wiki calls it a Swedish beechwood import.

title: Rhinestone Spinner (RS-1000)
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The Rhinestone Spinner (RS-1000) was a customized Standard in Shocking Pink (SP-105) with 12 rhinestones, six per side, per the Yo-Yo Museum. It came in an American Spinners yo-yo garage, retailed at $12 ($7 for the basic model), and measures 59 mm diameter, 32 mm width and 42.74 g. The YoYo Wiki says the jeweled models had rhinestones added after painting and were hand made by Bill Cress on special order.

title: Standard
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The Standard was the company's mainstay line: a bulge-face one-piece maple yo-yo painted in several color schemes by a company specializing in race-car paintwork, now sought by collectors. The museum's Standard (VR-104) in vermilion red is dated 1990 with an original retail price of $7. The Smithsonian National Museum of American History holds a black example with a red, yellow and green speckle design in clear oval packaging reading "American's Best One Piece Wooden Yo-Yo" (object nmah_1335505).

title: Venice Beach (Prototype)
content: History / AboutAmerican Spinners was founded in 1988 by Bill Cress and made one-piece wooden yo-yos with exotic finishes, according to the YoYo Wiki, which says the line was still produced as late as 1999. The Yo-Yo Museum says the company began during the late-1980s boom from the Smothers Brothers Yo-Yo Man routine, seeking a high-quality one-piece yo-yo like those of the golden age, and that all models except one used the same standard blank, with a raised logo face. The Venice Beach series, announced in 1990, was a prototype series of one-piece maple yo-yos with paint drips and splatter; the Yo-Yo Museum says it was never put into full production and sold, though many one-of-a-kind test pieces were made and occasionally appear for sale or auction. The museum's white example measures 59 mm diameter, 31.5 mm width and 50.16 g and came in a Yo-Yo Garage; the Collector price of $16.50 is cited for it.

title: Ample
content: AboutThe Ample is an ultra-wide 1A yo-yo released in 2025, available in polycarbonate and POM variants. At over 60mm wide — more than 10mm wider than most standard yo-yos — it provides an exceptionally large catch zone while JT designed the grip to feel more compact in hand than the size suggests. Despite the large dimensions, it maintains a familiar standard string trick feel. Available in PC Translucent Pink, White POM, Clear Yellow, Black POM, PC Translucent Light Blue, and PC Translucent Blue.

title: Amulette
content: AboutThe Amulette is JT's flagship offstring model, redesigned from the ground up as a "new flagship." Suitable from basic practice through soloham-level play, it offers a 76mm diameter with a 64.46mm width for reliable catches. Available in multiple hub color options: White/Red Hub, White/Silver Hub, Yellow/Pink Hub, and White/Blue Hub.

title: Amulette Pro
content: AboutThe Amulette Pro is the advanced-player variant of the Amulette, with the diameter reduced approximately 4mm and the width widened approximately 2mm. JT describes it as "designed for advanced players and people with smaller hands." Available in Black Hub, Purple Hub, and Green Hub colorways.

title: Amusing
content: AboutThe Amusing features a wide organic profile for an extremely comfortable catch with high-performance rim-weighted design. The faceted cup features a laser-engraved smile. Versatile all-around suitable for various skill levels. Available in Shiny Red, Shiny Silver, Shiny Mint Green, Matte Light Blue, Silver/Blue/Red, and Silver/Red/Pink.

title: Amusing 2
content: AboutThe Amusing 2 features an increased diameter over the original while maintaining the same organic rim-weighted design. Available in Mint Green, Purple, Red, Orange, Black, and Grey.

title: Amusing 3
content: AboutThe Amusing 3 is a 2024 makeover of the Amusing line with softened edges for a more comfortable, elegant feel while retaining the width and stability of its predecessors. Available in Blue, Purple, Green, and Red.

title: Amusing MAX
content: AboutThe Amusing MAX is a bi-metal upgrade of the Amusing series, adding a stainless steel ring to the wide organic profile for enhanced rim weight. Described as "a great all-arounder." Available in Dark Rainbow, Black/Pink/Blue, Green/Blue/Silver/Orange, and Black/Silver/Orange.

title: Anarchy
content:
History / About
The Anarchy was released in 2017 as a signature model of mowl founder and producer Eiji Okuyama — a two-time World 4A Champion and recognized innovator of the 4A division. It was mowl's first and for many years only offstring yo-yo, reflecting Okuyama's competitive background. A notable entry in the 4A category given that Okuyama's championship pedigree directly informed the design.

title: ANAX
content:
History / About
ANAX is Takumi Yasumoto's first signature model, released September 19, 2026. It inherits the core component design of YYR's ANOTOGASTER at a smaller scale, purpose-built for string play in venues where off-string isn't allowed. Available in two body materials, PC and POM, with roughly an 8g weight difference between them.

title: Anceps
content: The Anceps is the signature model of Seung Jae Hwi, 2024 Korean National 1A Champion and 4th place finisher at the 2024 World Championships. A heavyweight 7075 bi-metal at 68.3g, the Anceps combines power with precision for advanced string tricks and horizontal techniques at the highest competitive level.

title: Anceps Bloom
content: The Anceps Bloom is an oversized variant of Seung Jae Hwi's Anceps, expanding both the diameter and width significantly for a different play character while maintaining the same competition-level bi-metal construction. At 59mm diameter and 55mm wide, it is among the largest throws in the W1LD lineup.

title: Anceps Ti
content: The Anceps Ti is the titanium version of Seung Jae Hwi's Anceps signature, machined from TC4 Grade 5 titanium for a premium competition experience. It retains the wide bi-metal silhouette of the original Anceps in a full monometal titanium construction.

title: ANGLAM
content: About the ANGLAMThe ANGLAM is sOMEThING's inaugural model and one of the most influential bi-metal yo-yos in the history of competitive play. Released in 2012 alongside the brand itself, it established the template for the ANGLAM line that continues over a decade later. The body profile derives from the earlier ANGLE model; titanium weight rings are positioned at the rim for maximum spin power and stability. Hiroyuki Suzuki's signature is laser-engraved on the catch zone.Multiple colorway runs were produced throughout its initial production period, including Yellow/Orange, Yellow, Pink, Emerald Green, Blast Silver, Red/Blue, Pink/Black, Gold/Blue, Blue/Gold, Yellow/Silver, Blue, Silver, and Black.

title: ANGLAM 7075
content: About the ANGLAM 7075The ANGLAM 7075 carries the same body profile as the original ANGLAM but is milled from aerospace-grade 7075 aluminum (super duralumin) for significantly increased durability. Weight distribution is adjusted to match the standard version's feel while the tougher alloy adds resilience against impacts. Available in Pink, Red, and Blue.

title: ANGLAM CC
content: About the ANGLAM CCThe ANGLAM CC is a signature edition designed with sOMEThING team member Christopher Chia, a competitive player from Singapore. Chia modified the ANGLAM's shape and weight distribution to suit his style; the proprietary weight ring material is described as reducing manufacturing costs without sacrificing performance. The ANGLAM logo is engraved on one side, Christopher Chia's autograph on the other.Available in Purple and Light Blue. Bearing upgraded to CBC Center Trac Size C.

title: ANGLAM OG
content: About the ANGLAM OGThe ANGLAM OG is a reissue of the original 2012 ANGLAM flagship, restoring the titanium rim construction that the ANGLAM2 series replaced with stainless steel. Near-identical specs to the 2012 original with minor dimensional refinements. A return to sOMEThING's roots for players who prefer titanium's feel over stainless steel.

title: ANGLAM ONE REMASTERED
content: About the ANGLAM ONE REMASTEREDThe ANGLAM ONE REMASTERED revisits the original 2012 ANGLAM, updating its construction with stainless steel rims in place of titanium and shaving 1 gram from the overall weight. Shape and inner rim weight design are tweaked to "maximize performance and playfeel." Colorways: Emerald/Rainbow Rim, Black, Emerald Green, Pink, Blue.

title: ANGLAM PINNACLE
content: About the ANGLAM PINNACLEThe ANGLAM PINNACLE returns to titanium rims after the ANGLAM2 series used stainless steel. It is based on one of the final ANGLAM prototypes from 2012 — a shape that was never released during the original production run and held until 2019. "Light and powerful" feel: heavy at throw, then lightens considerably during trick execution. $259.99 USD.Colorways: Black × Blue Matte, Silver × Red Matte, Silver; limited Leopard Gunmetal edition.

title: ANGLAM TiSS
content: About the ANGLAM TiSSThe ANGLAM TiSS ("Titanium and Stainless Steel") debuted at the World Yo-Yo Contest 2015 in Tokyo. The titanium body enables extremely thin walls and precise weight placement; thin stainless steel weight rings are positioned on the inner lips of the rims, mirroring the original ANGLAM's approach in a far more exotic material pairing. The interior is hand-polished matte black with a polished exterior optimized for grinding.At approximately $900 USD at launch, the TiSS was one of the most expensive production yo-yos ever made at the time of release.

title: ANGLAM ZERO
content: About the ANGLAM ZEROThe ANGLAM ZERO is a full-titanium monometal built on the Anglam2 body shape. Wall thickness is calculated to exploit titanium's unique weight-to-strength ratio and maximize the material's performance benefits across the full body profile. First available at WYYC 2015 in Tokyo, it quickly became one of sOMEThING's most prestigious releases. Priced at approximately ¥66,000 (~$440 USD).

title: ANGLAM ZERO APOGEE
content: About the ANGLAM ZERO APOGEEThe ANGLAM ZERO APOGEE combines a titanium body with outer stainless steel rings. Ultra-thin body walls divert maximum weight to the rims for impressive spin time without sacrificing balance. The titanium body enables wall thickness that aluminum cannot achieve, pushing rim-weighting to its practical limit. Priced at approximately $1,000 USD.

title: ANGLAM ZERO VER.CC BEAU NOIR
content: About the ANGLAM ZERO VER.CC BEAU NOIRThe ANGLAM ZERO VER.CC BEAU NOIR is a full-titanium signature model for sOMEThING team member Christopher Chia, finished in Beau Noir ("Beautiful Black") — a titanium black surface treatment that also increases hardness and durability. "Powerful and beautifully stable," built specifically for the competition stage. $829.99 USD.

title: ANGLAM2
content: About the ANGLAM2"The Anglam design has been refined and polished over the past three years." The ANGLAM2 is the direct successor to the 2012 ANGLAM, switching from titanium to stainless steel rims and reworking the weight distribution for a lighter, faster feel. The updated profile reflects three years of competitive feedback. Hiroyuki Suzuki signature.Colorways: Yellow, Silver, Blue, Light Blue.

title: ANGLAM2 7075
content: About the ANGLAM2 7075The ANGLAM2 7075 is identical in spec to the standard ANGLAM2 but uses 7075 aluminum for the body, providing greater durability and a firmer playing feel that experienced players will notice. The harder alloy makes it more resilient against impact damage while maintaining the same profile and weight distribution.

title: ANOMALY
content:
History / About
ANOMALY is Minato Furuta's 3A signature, released November 18, 2025. Its aluminum body with a stainless-steel inner rim extending to the outer edge established a new bi-metal design standard for 3A that other brands later adopted; the structure is still used across YYR's own 3A lineup.

title: ANOMINA
content:
History / About
ANOMINA is Minato Furuta's dedicated 3A follow-up to his Anomaly signature, released July 11, 2026. It widens the body to 45mm from Anomaly's 42.5mm while keeping the same aluminum/stainless-steel bi-metal construction.

title: Another Eagle
content: AboutThe Another Eagle is a molded offstring released in 2014 as an accessible version of the Eagle Eye. The mold was derived directly from the machined Eagle Eye shape, maintaining its wide catch zone and H-profile. Designed for fast tech and regeneration combos, it was later released in another iteration with an aluminum/stainless steel rim (+S) variant for enhanced stability at approximately 5.5g added weight. An Another Eagle 2 follow-up was also produced.

title: Anotogaster
content:
About
Anotogaster is Takumi Yasumoto's signature model — the yoyo he used to win the 2020 Japan National 4A title. Slightly downsized from the Supercell he used to win nationals in 2017, with a revised shape combining the power to withstand intense speed play with maneuverability for a variety of regenerations. Aluminum hubs have a mortar-shaped slope, making it well-suited to finger spin tricks — unusual for an offstring model.

title: Anthelion
content: The Anthelion features a plastic body with copper rim weights in an H-profile shape. Modular center-unit compatible for hubstacks or LED upgrades. Delivers performance comparable to full-metal throws while maintaining affordability. Bind-required for unresponsive play.

title: Anti-PRO I
content:
History / About
Anti-PRO I marks the first release in MonkeyfingeR Design’s Anti-PRO series — Ray Smith’s vehicle for unconventional, rule-breaking designs. Each Anti-PRO model is a one-run release: once a colorway or model is done, it’s gone permanently, no restocks. The series format is intentional — designed to get ideas from Ray’s head into physical form without commercial compromise.
Described as "an absolute beast — odd, bold, aggressive" with a play character that "throws like a punch in the chest." The 2021 release was the birth of the concept, all designs hand-sketched by Ray before being pulled into CAD. The number of Anti-PRO models planned is undisclosed — Ray has said he’s sketched them all, but won’t reveal how many.

title: ANTiFRAGILE
content:
About
ANTiFRAGILE is Yoyofriends' flagship crystalized grade 5 titanium yo-yo. Crystalized titanium is made through a special heating process that changes the material on a molecular level, achieving an "ice cracking" visual effect. The design is based on the SlipStream with a modern spec, and the axle is increased to 8mm for better durability.

title: Antipodal Point
content: A C3yoyodesign × hSpin collaboration in 7075 aluminum with polycarbonate rings. Combines both companies' precision engineering philosophies. Price: ~$90–$110.

title: Air Rider
content: History / AboutThe Air Rider is listed among the yo-yos produced by AnY, the maker formed in 2005 by Korean and Taiwanese yo-yoers specializing in low-volume, high-end metal yo-yos made in South Korea. No specifications, release year or description could be verified from available sources.

title: Free Rider
content: History / AboutThe Free Rider is AnY's first release with more than 200 units produced. It has fewer aesthetic features than AnY's usual intricate laser engraving. Its profile is similar to the Duncan Freehand Zero, and AnY's site showed how well Freehand Mg sidecaps fit it. It has a thumb/finger grind lip and AnY's top-on hub, and is sand blasted for a low-friction finish. It uses a bearing comparable to the YoYoJam large bearing and a recessed AnY pad.

title: MiRoC
content: History / AboutThe MiRoC is the first mass-produced yo-yo with side-cap bearings and the third yo-yo released by AnY, after the QuickSilver 1 and 2. A total run of 100 was made, 35 sold through YoYoNation after an agreement with YoYoJam over the O-Pad response technology, a variation of YoYoJam's patented o-ring. It is the first in AnY's four saint beast series. The side bearing helps matador-style tricks, but some owners reported loose side bearings and side caps that flew off during tricks.

title: MiRoC 2
content: History / AboutThe MiRoC 2 follows the original MiRoC. Bearing caps on the sides let the player grab the yo-yo during play to change the plane of the axis or ripcord it into a spin. AnY was the original company to feature yo-yos with bearing caps as standard. The MiRoC 2 caps are concave to be easier to hold, unlike the flat-faced originals, and the yo-yo has removable weight rings that screw on or off the body halves.

title: QuickSilver
content: History / AboutThe QuickSilver was the first yo-yo released by AnY and was available only directly from the manufacturer or through non-US retailers, because of the O-Pad response, a variation of YoYoJam's patented o-ring technology. The QS1 was released in very limited numbers and quickly replaced by the QS2, both sold at Spingear or directly from AnY. The QS1 had a shape similar to the YoYoJam Night Moves, resembled Dif-e-Yo yo-yos with rings in the sides and an o-ring in each side for weight, and had a clear coat over the aluminum. AnY briefly considered a QS3 and posted pictures but closed the line.

title: Ultimate 3X
content: History / AboutThe Ultimate 3X is a high-end metal yo-yo from AnY released in June 2009. It has a finish combining blasting and anodization for grind efficiency, aluminum hubstacks for changing the plane of axis or ripcording into a spin, and an interchangeable rim system. It comes with two sets of aluminum rims, small and large, that screw on and off the main body, and the feel depends on the rims fitted. It uses the usual AnY pad and C bearing set-up.

The YoYo Wiki lists the Aoda Super Wheel among Aoda's counterfeits of Auldey's Super Yo-Yo line, described as a clone of the Duncan Wheels (via the Hyper Wheels); the Aoda version is said to be identical to Auldey's except for markings.

title: Thunderbolt Heroes
content: History / AboutAoda Toys is a Chinese toy maker that the YoYo Wiki characterizes as a producer of low-priced yo-yos whose designs resemble products of larger yo-yo makers. The YoYo Wiki lists the metal Thunderbolt Heroes (霹雳双雄) with no further details.

title: AoE
content: AboutThe AoE is Yoyofriends' first injection-molded polycarbonate yo-yo, designed as a low-budget, high-performing option for players at any skill level. Available in both unresponsive and responsive configurations with interchangeable axles and bearings, it delivers surprising performance at an accessible price point. The clear polycarbonate body showcases colorful fade finishes.

title: Aotus
content:
History / About
The Aotus is MonkeyfingeR Design’s signature model for Will Hahn, named after the Aotus (night monkey) genus — a nod to Hahn’s habit of playing both day and night. Hahn was heavily involved in the design process alongside Jesse Kazemeck. The comfortable hybrid shape supports both his 1A and 5A work, offering enough stability for technical sequences while remaining maneuverable for counterweight play.

title: Apathy
content: Keiran Cooper's first signature model, machined entirely from stainless steel — a rare choice in the modern yo-yo market. The high density of steel delivers exceptional stability and a uniquely powerful play feel unlike any aluminum or bimetal throw. Engraved with the æ logo and individual serial number. Described by the community as a stainless steel powerhouse.

title: Ape-X
content:
History / About
The Ape-X is MonkeyfingeR Design’s competition-focused flagship, 100% made in Canada. Released in January 2014, it sold out within days and never received a second regular production run, making it a sought collector piece. The limited “Tiki” edition — 10 units with tiger wood anodization — was a Zoo member exclusive. Elements from the Ape-X outer profile carried forward into the later G-Squared Co-Lab and Tri-B designs. A limited 7075 alloy variant (the Tiki Edition) was produced alongside the standard 6061 run.

title: Apollo
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"When it comes to yoyos, Dressel Designs studies the past to shape the future. Apollo is our second yoyo machined from POM, and our first non-hybrid plastic design.

Our team grew up with plastic yoyos, when throwing rancid milks and hourglass combos reigned supreme. There’s something special about that early feeling of yoyos, when your favorite staple tricks were being innovated left and right.

We opted to build Apollo with POM (Delrin) plastic. It is tough to use POM with complex construction like fixed caps or bimetal rims, and even moreso when the materials are slippery like POM. But there is an undeniably buttery-smooth texture that comes with POM that is difficult to recreate with other plastic materials, and most closely matches the feeling of those old plastic toys. While we love Polycarbonate and value how much easier it can be to build a multi-piece yoyo, we chose to avoid cutting corners to stay true to our goals for Apollo.

But yoyos aren’t just toys anymore. They’re built to perform.

Apollo builds a balance between these distinct epochs of ideals and play, melding together into one beautifully precision machined model that doesn’t compromise on what you value.

Looking for a trendy shape and wide catch zone for your biggest tricks and highest clicks? Apollo makes them riskless.

Looking to explore the intricacies and sensation of plastic that make your favorite players’ nostalgic? Apollo guides you there on every throw.

How about something that stands out visually from the rest of your collection? You won’t believe the unique engraving technique we used on our caps until you feel it for yourself.

Apollo isn’t just a yoyo. It’s a bridge between worlds.

More details imminent"

title: Aquarius
content: About the AquariusOriginally released in 2002 as the signature yo-yo of Hironori Mii, discontinued briefly, then re-released in 2004 after market demand. Its size and weight were optimized for the landing catches and orbital tricks that define 4A play. It remained a benchmark offstring yo-yo for years and helped legitimize the style at international competitions.

title: Aquilegia
content: HistoryAquilegia is a high-performance titanium model in the lineage of Hydrangea's first model, Laurus. Aquilegia aims for the best balance between spin time, stability, and responsiveness. The titanium construction provides durability and consistent weight distribution for competitive play.

title: ARAZU
content:
History / About
ARAZU is the off-string/4A signature of Yuki Uchida, 2021 Japan National Champion, released May 28, 2026. YYR describes it as having the smallest diameter and widest width of any off-string model in the brand's history. Early purchasers received a limited-edition art book.

title: Gemstones
content:
About the Gemstones

The Gemstones is Arc1's debut yoyo, released September 2022, and the first modern Dutch-made unresponsive throw. Its name derives from the shape created when two brilliant-cut gemstones meet at their culets — the form that defines the yoyo's profile. The design was developed in collaboration with Mark Diehr of MK1 YoYos, who contributed CAD work and the interchangeable spin-top cap design.

The body is polycarbonate, left unpolished from the lathe to preserve grind-friendliness. Aluminum hubs anchor the assembly, while stainless steel rings carry the majority of the weight — nearly two-thirds of the total — outward to the rim. At 40mm diameter and 40mm width, the Gemstones is intentionally undersized and pocket-portable. Weight varies by cap configuration: 60g without caps, 64g with flat or finger spin caps, and 65g with spin-top caps.

The cap system is the defining feature: flat caps, finger spin caps, and spin-top caps press-fit by hand and are removed with approximately 12 BAR of air pressure through an included air needle. The spin-top caps allow the yoyo to balance upright on a palm or flat surface. Each unit carries minor machining marks and slight vibe due to the multi-material construction — Arc1 considers this intentional, making each piece unique. The package includes a replacement bearing, air needle, five strings, two flat caps, two finger spin caps, and a set of spin-top caps.

title: Arctica
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

Say hello to the latest installation and the first plastic model in our Weatherman Line – the Arctica.

SPECSDiameter 58.6mmWidth 53.0mmWeight 66.6gMaterial machined polycarbonate

The Arctica began with a nostalgia for past eras of yo-yos. 

Plastic designs have a special place in the industry – not just for the fact they occupy a more accessible price bracket than metal contemporaries, but also because they form a part of a player’s experience that is unique and wholly distinct from performance metals. 

a duncan freehand zero — a kind gift from jayson, a tenured member of the local scene in singapore.

We grew up in the scene on a steady diet of plastics. even though now metals dominate the narrative in performance and design, we’ll always have an affection for the way plastics feel, play, sound – and how they exist in every collector’s case, and every player’s rotation.

The business case for plastic yoyos today is narrow, unless you’re injection-molding them in the thousands. today, plastics cost just about the same to machine as aluminiums, but take a lot more thought and engineering to get them in the same ballpark in terms of precision, smoothness, and play capability. We say this in appreciation for the many small brands and outfits in our community that still make small-batch plastic designs as a matter of passion, in a world where they’re becoming less and less of a sensible pursuit. 

For that very reason, we insist on plastic designs having their time of day in our product lineup. Practicality says to maximize for trends and margins; we intentionally resist those instincts so we can pay attention to things that we feel matter.

The Snowberry was our first plastic release – and also our love letter to plastic designs in general. It speaks to our love for the material, and that special feeling that comes with designing for fun and joy. 

If the Snowberry is a Delrin reimagination of the Cloudberry, the Arctica – clearly – is a polycarbonate incarnation of the Ari, the sophomore release of the Weatherman Line. The Ari is a wide, W-shaped titanium that became favored for its quick, light and floaty play, despite its relatively large size. It was also Side Effects-compatible, which made it a tinkerer’s dream. The Ari also took Duncan-spec caps, which were CNC-machined for an incredibly precise fit, and allowed a player to take on the hollow-body feel of older, nostalgic designs, if they so desired. This unique stack of product features made the Ari a favorite amongst the Atmos faithful, and a core design in our lineup.

At heart, the Ari is a big, light, floaty W-shaped titanium that promises hours of fun.

The core concept of the Arctica was to lean into the essence of the Ari and what made it special, and to craft a plastic version that tapped on years of nostalgia, fun, and feel.

We toyed with the idea of using Delrin, but eventually opted to go with polycarbonate. More on this later, but given the early design blueprints of the Arctica, we needed to work with material that had a high degree of rigidity. Delrin is beautifully smooth to the touch, but is also relatively soft, which can make it a challenging material to work with when designing for a multi-part model, since there can be some give in the fit between parts. Polycarbonate is a lot more rigid than Delrin, and when designed and machined for precise fit, can be used for more complex assembly. 

And – speaking purely from an aesthetic perspective – frosted polycarbonate just has a look to it.

the arctica is possibly the most over-engineered plastic yo-yo in circulation. it’s made up of an assembly of 12 discrete precision-machined polycarbonate and aluminum parts. for context, an injection-molded plastic has, on average, 6 independent components; a regular monometal has just 4. it generally follows that having more moving parts in a dynamic object such as a yo-yo results in more overall flex, give and imbalance, which can lead to vibe – but the arctica was designed and machined to outstanding degrees of precision.

the arctica comes with a level of smoothness that is generally not associated with plastics – especially if they are injection-molded.

following a method we pioneered with the snowberry, we designed for the aluminum spacer construction to sit embedded in the plastic hub, which conceals it for a purer, uninterrupted facade. the dimensions here were further altered and optimized for an even tighter and precise fit, which contributed greatly to the arctica’s smoothness and quality. 

the plastic hub, which packs a significant amount of mid-to-outer rim mass, is then concealed by a cnc-machined cap, similarly styled to the batch we produced for the ari.

the internal complexity of the arctica is concealed by its minimalist, and understated external features – you’d never guess what went under the hood.

note: while it is physically possible, we strongly recommend not removing the caps on the arctica.

the first prototype we machined came in at 64g, but it felt a touch too weak. we went back to the design blueprint and re-machined another prototype, which was more than 2g heavier in the mid-section, and it turned out feeling perfectly full and whole. 

it has that beautiful float and feel of a hollow-body plastic, while simultaneously having the stability of an ultrawide design. it felt closely reminiscent of the signature playfeel of the ari, and we knew we were on the right track.

the arctica is a real big boy at 58.6mm (diameter) and 53.0mm (width), but experientially, those numbers feel a lot less bombastic, and actually natural and comfortable in play. the string gap is a wide, forgiving chasm, and has a gap width that can take on multiple layers in more complex tricks.

in a similar vein, the arctica weighs in at 66.6g, but the density of polycarbonate and its overall diameter makes that number deceptively large. for reference, in terms of pure “feel”, we personally find it feels more akin to a 64g design.

it’s incredibly light, stable and floaty, and it’s massive fun. you’ll feel right at home with whatever style of play you throw at it. it’ll go wherever you want to take it.

the working title of the arctica was “polyari” all through prototyping and production – a literal description of its design concept – but it came too close to the polaris, which was released just before it. it eventually evolved to arctica, in reference to its icy, frosted appearance, while paying homage to the weatherman naming convention of taking after natural terminology, and also embedding “ari” in its name.

come enjoy the arctica.

title: Stomp 2
content:
History / About
The Stomp 2 is the updated edition of the Stomp, Ardeus' wide-profile fixed axle throw. The flared, wide body is designed for comfortable palm catches and stable looping. The 2026 revision reduces the diameter marginally and upgrades the axle to a 1/4" hickory peg, consistent with improvements made across the updated Ardeus lineup. Made to order in 3D-printed PLA filament with the brand's 8-hole tic-tac response, available through the YoYoExpert Buy/Sell/Trade forums.

title: Stride 2
content:
History / About
The Stride 2 is a revised edition of Ardeus' original Stride, a narrow fixed axle design intended for classic looping and string trick play. The diameter was reduced from the original 64mm for improved control, and the axle was upgraded to a 1/4" hickory peg. Like all Ardeus models, it is 3D-printed to order and features the brand's 8-hole tic-tac response system. Available in standard and UV-reactive filament through the YoYoExpert forums.

title: Stroll 2
content:
History / About
The Stroll 2 is Ardeus' revised take on the original Stroll, one of the brand's earliest 3D-printed fixed axle designs. The update shrinks the diameter slightly for a more controlled feel while retaining the wide, comfortable profile. It ships with a 1/4" hickory axle and the brand's signature 8-hole "tic-tac" response system. Sold through the YoYoExpert Buy/Sell/Trade forums, each Ardeus throw is made to order in the Philippines and available in standard, UV-reactive, and glow-in-the-dark filament options.

title: Area 51
content:
History / About
The Area 51 was released in late 2025, named in the UFO/government conspiracy tradition consistent with G2's diverse naming across creature, military, and pop culture themes. Priced at $145, it sits in G2's premium monometal or entry bimetal tier. Four colorways released across 2025–2026.

title: Ares Star
content: The Ares Star is the first signature model for Marcus Koh, 2011 World 1A Champion. Features an "inverse rounded" profile designed to excel at horizontal rail combos. Metal propeller axle detail. Limited run of approximately 1000 units, available in pink and blue.

title: Ari
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

Introducing – the Ari.

SPECSdia 57mmwid 48mmweight 65gmaterial Grade 5 Titanium

—

The Ari continues what our first non-organic model, the Khuno, began.

The essence of the Khuno, conceptually speaking, is the intersection of customizability and performance. its essence, in terms of its playfeel, is in stability, power, and an easy pace.

The same constitutes the soul of the Ari, which began as a project aimed towards being a consolidation of those parameters within a simplified frame.

What we’ve adapted from the Khuno is fairly clear – the tri-stepped W profile, the Side Effects compatibility, and its general measurements. Those variables felt core to the form factor, and so we’ve kept them constant in this iteration. What we’ve overhauled is more subtle, and requires a closer look.

To be clear, not every design needs a titanium analog. Certain designs are made such that titanium versions of its aluminum counterparts can be a bit gratuitous – for instance, a titanium Goji, while interesting as a concept, might not really be compelling in its play. Given its character as a material, titanium lends a flexibility where a design needs to be optimized in certain extremes – such as parking a disproportionate amount of mass in an area relative to the rest of its structure.

Where the Ari surfaced as a compelling concept was in the possibility of achieving that same intersection of customizability and performance in a simplified, monometal physique.

To maintain a degree of performance (read: spin, stability) while allowing for a variable mid-weight, the Khuno compensates for this with generous rim weight. Stainless steel rings serve to increase rim weight perfectly well, but add another variable in machining, construction, assembly, and more importantly, tuning for the user. Any Side Effect design requires tuning; throwing bimetal construction to the mix adds to that experience.

Given its unique density and strength properties, titanium allowed us to simplify our construction while advancing that sweet convergence between adaptability and performance.

the ari sports a full frame, coming in at 57mm and 48mm.

The lightest version of the Ari, with Aluminium Ultra Lights installed, clocks just 65g.

The seeming consensus with Khuno players is that it feels lighter than its weight suggests, and is surprisingly sprightly and fast. My addition to that sentiment is that it paces well – it’s not sluggish as typical of its weight, and it’s also not frenzied and uncontrolled. It moves easy and matches your pace.

This also applies to the Ari, which accelerates and decelerates precisely on the dime, despite its full frame.

Heavier options are available out of box, for those who prefer a heartier diet. The included Brass Ultra Lights take the Ari up to 67.1g; with caps, you have the option of going up to ~72.5g (AL ULs) or ~74.7g (Brass ULs).

The heavier setups might seem indulgent – but my favored configuration is actually with the AL ULs and caps installed. I never thought I’d gravitate towards a 72.5g throw, but it moves effortlessly.

On that tangent – caps are a core component of this form factor that we’ve also updated with the Ari.

The Khuno (as did the Gravity) featured injection-molded blank caps, which were produced primarily for plastic Duncan models. These blank caps came with a tiny stub where the piece breaks off the mold. For most use cases this little stub isn’t an issue – there generally is enough flex in a plastic body to accommodate tiny imprecisions, and so the caps can be pressed in, albeit with a tight fit.

However, the titanium and aluminum bodies of the Gravity and Khuno are rigid, and are less tolerant to imprecisions in the cap structure. The solution for these caps so far have been tool-processing the stub and the entire circumference of the cap by hand, with every cap then being hand-tested with a Gravity or Khuno halve for a tight fit. Still, hand-processed injection-molded plastic bodies are far from precise. Where a multi-part design is concerned, precision is essential.

For the Ari, we machined polycarbonate caps for precise fit and balance. These new caps are an absolute ease to install and remove, and play incredibly smooth.

These machined caps are backward compatible with Khunos.

They will be included with future batches of Khunos and other cap-enabled designs, but we’ve also made additional quantities available for current Khuno users to purchase.

Small detail here – we also altered the flat rim of the Khuno for a rounder finish. This allows for more mass at the rims, while providing a more comfortable catch. We also think it looks great.

Going from Khuno to Ari was a process of advancement by simplification, and we’re proud of how it turned out.

The Ari is unreservedly our best performing design to date.

It’s distinct from our relaxed, fun-oriented designs like the Pomelo and Goji, or more purist, organic slants in the Noah, but it’s also an affirmation of our tinkering in the performance segment of design. It’s the latest culmination of many thoughts we’ve had about the W shape, what we find interesting and significant about that design space, and where we could go with it.

It’s been heavily tested by Yuji, our newest team addition, who’s found it a “contest killer”. If you’ve seen him in action with it, well… I take his word for it.

https://www.instagram.com/tv/CZhQTkWg6JH/embed/?cr=1&v=14&wp=1080&rd=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.atmosprojects.com&rp=%2Fprojects%2Fari#%7B%22ci%22%3A0%2C%22os%22%3A1609%2C%22ls%22%3A841%2C%22le%22%3A1605%7D

The etymological roots of Ari are multiple – in Persian it means “to bring rain”; in Greek it gestures towards a “high” nature, of superiority; in Hebrew it means “lion”. Given Khuno draws its name from the Incan God of Storm, Ari feels fitting for its conceptual successor.

Aris come equipped with premier kit in Yoyorecreation’s NSK DS Platinum Bearing, Saturn Pads, and Zipline Strings’ Case Study #50s.

One Drop’s Aluminum Ultra Lights come installed, and we also include an additional pair of Brass Ultra Lights.

We also include a cap removal tool. (It screws onto both Side Effects, and pops the caps off through the holes.)

Note : We hand-tune each Ari for smooth play before we send them out, but as it is with any Side Effects design, players should expect that, should faint vibe occur, some degree of tuning is part of the game.

Thank you for sticking to the end of another of our design write-ups. We hope you enjoy the Ari as much as we did making them.

title: Aria
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

this the Aria.

SPECS

Dia 57mmWidth 46mmWeight 68.1gMaterial titanium

Shortly after the release of the Ari in February 2022, we began dreaming up concepts that would be fitting for an Ari Pro. This began early with talks with Evgeniy getting his Ari – incidentally his first Atmos design – he loved the feel, the width, and the light but powerful play of the Ari, but also mentioned he desired a bit more mass. We started sketching up a few concepts, and had a few in queue while we focused our developmental attentions to other projects in our pipeline, such as the Abel and Snowberry.

We returned to the concept shortly after, armed with feedback from Ari users. The Ari is and has always been a tinkerer’s model; it has a very light base weight, and was designed to accept One Drop Side Effects, Freehand-sized caps, and even rubber o-rings, which allowed a user to construct his own build, up to north of 70g. The only drawback with adding more moving parts on a precision design was that tuning became a necessity.

In our view, tuning isn’t something to be avoided – its a useful skill in yoyoing, similar to being able to correct string tension. It’s easy, and frees one up to enjoy SE-enabled yoyos without unnecessary frustration.

But the larger point for those who had played the Ari was that there was desire for a version unencumbered by the need to customize, assemble, and calibrate. There were calls for a high performing design in the format of the Ari, but even further simplified. Players loved the Ari’s physique, the full-frame form factor, and our use of titanium; but they were requesting play-readiness, and a sharper focus on high performance. That felt aligned to the Pro designation we were thinking about for the next iteration of the Ari form factor.

This brought us back to our conversations with Evegeniy about weight, and after some back and forth, we decided to move into the realm of heavier concepts.

We’ve generally kept our designs below 65g. One design that has broken that soft rule is the Snowberry, oddly enough our heaviest design to date, which clocks in at 65.6g. We’ve mostly been able to do creative things with width and weight distribution in achieving light power without piling on the pounds – case in point, the Snowberry, which is also arguably our fluffiest design in our lineup. For our design purposes the 62-64g space mostly suits us well.

But with this overt dip into heavyweight territory, what we were hoping to achieve in playfeel was akin to the handling and feel of performance cars with low ground clearing – that of torque, gravitas, balance, and the ability to turn tight corners at speed with supreme handling and full, fine control.

68g can sound extreme to some, given there are 66g designs that play sluggishly. The playfeel that players dread is the thudding rock on the end of a string that resists all types of movement. With the Aria, the idea was to design something with considerable mass but distribute it well enough across the Ari’s large 57mm and 48mm frame, so that it would feel substantial and balanced, but not unwieldy and reluctant.

This was one of the earlier prototypes we made of the Aria, machined on aluminum stock for feasibility testing – it had a stepped hub and an even more pronounced nub. We made multiple early prototypes, but they were all condemned by vibe and never made it past testing phases; the weight distribution was too extreme.

Eventually we simplified the wall design, and reduced the overall width from 48mm to 46mm – which, interestingly, makes the Aria our narrowest design to date.

The Aria also has significantly thicker rims than the Ari, giving it a lot more power. Crucially, we graduated the mass bias from the center to the outer rims, which gives the Aria a powerful, but very smooth acceleration and handle.

The Aria is deceptively deft and nimble for a 68g yoyo; it has that low-center-of-gravity smoothness, superb control and pace, and a powerful stability. It’s difficult to throw it off kilter. It stops on a dime. Once it gets moving, it plays lighter than 68g might suggest it would, and has all the spin you need – and then some more, and then some more… and then some more.

It’s everything we were hoping to achieve in an Ari Pro.

The Aria comes equipped with premier kit in Black Stratos Pads, Atmos Type I Concave Bearings, and Zipline Strings’ Case Study #50s.

title: Armadillo
content: HistoryThe Armadillo (Prototype v1) was released December 21, 2024 as a limited prototype run of just 10 units, sold exclusively in the US through the ZipLine store. The O-shaped design in 7068 aluminum plays with a characteristic float on a moderate toss that transitions to aggressive spin under power. ZipLine noted the units were not extensively test-throw tested to preserve surface condition, so minor vibe at the limits is possible. Bronze anodization. Priced at $75.

title: Armageddon
content: AboutThe Armageddon is Yoyofriends' full-sized competition monometal built for speed and width. Machined from 7068 aluminum, it delivers signature acceleration with an unusually wide 52.82mm catch zone — one of the widest monometals in the Yoyofriends lineup. It marks a new direction in competition monometals for the brand.

title: Artifact
content:
From One Drop:

"The Artifact is a collaboration with our long time friend Alex Whitney, formerly with Yoyocommunity.

Here is Alex’s description:

“I’m proud to introduce the Artifact, One Drop’s first small-bearing yo-yo. 

The Artifact was originally released as a collaboration between myself and Yoyocommunity in 2013, taking inspiration from Japanese designs of the late 2000s and early 2010s. Back in 2013, small-bearing yo-yos were less common than they are now (which considering that they’re still uncommon nowadays says quite a lot); this made the Artifact incredibly unique for the time but also presented its challenges. There was no standardized response pad for a small bearing yo-yo, and overall yo-yo manufacturing and design quality hadn’t quite reached the levels it has today. I’ve always felt this design could achieve more, which ultimately left the project feeling incomplete for the past 12 years. 

Small-bearing yo-yos have a unique feel on the string compared to the industry standard Size C bearing which makes them quite enchanting to play with. Because the bearing diameter is smaller, the string will actually wrap around the yo-yo more times when you wind it up. This means when you throw it, the yo-yo is going to spin faster, and you’ll be able to bind even at low RPMs. The difference in play is simultaneously subtle and striking and makes for a refreshing change compared to many of today’s other models. 

I approached One Drop — who live 1.5 hours South of where I grew up and have watched me go from an awkward teenager to a full-fledged adult over the last decade — about releasing an updated version of the design built to modern standards. Something that could go toe-to-toe with today’s designs performance-wise while maintaining the small bearing size. Suffice it to say, I was absolutely ecstatic when they agreed to partner on this project! Building from an unreleased prototype from before Yoyocommunity shut down, we aimed to stay true to the original design and kept the V-shape profile, mid-step rim, and of course the Size D bearing. We tweaked the hub design, increased the diameter slightly, boosted the alloy to 7075, lowered the weight, and fitted it with new response pads from our friends over at Freshly Dirty. 

The end result is one of my favorite playing yo-yos ever. I hope that this yo-yo sparks a newfound sense of wonder and adventure in your tricks, and can show people what a small-bearing yo-yo is truly capable of. Much like the name suggests, the Artifact is a true gem, and I’m excited to get it into everyone’s hands!”"
