title: Artifice
content: The following is archived directly from Yoyofriends' website:'The Yoyofriends' Artifice is the first signature yoyo of James Heder. We first scouted James at the 2024 National Yoyo Contest when he was 12 years old. He was using a Shortcut at the time, and was a fan of Yoyofriends. He showed us some of his tricks, and the entire Yoyofriends player team was instantly blown away. We then contacted his parents and officially offered him a sponsorship at the World Yoyo Contest 2024. James then proceeded to improve at an exponential rate, through his dedication and talent. He placed well in both the ANTE 2024 and PNWR 2025 contests. We realized James had potential to excel on the world stage, so we decided to make him a signature yoyo to help him further succeed in the yoyoing scene. Ante Yoyo Cup 2: https://youtu.be/TK5ie1oxfyI?si=Ml9omU4RsUTlTByZPNWR: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OKDyn4oZhXkIn the same way that Matthew Wallsten's signature, Replicant, came to fruition, team leader Philip and James got on Discord and talked for hours about yoyo designs, specifications and expectations. We discovered James is really smart--even at such a young age, he already had a great concept of the attributes he wanted in a yoyo. These included yoyo width, diameter, and weight distribution. He specifically requested a monometal so it would be less expensive to produce, making it more affordable for everyone. James' competition yoyo at that time was the Netrunner. He also was able to try Matthew's signature, Replicant, at PNWR, and he loved it. Both of these yoyos are all-out competition bimetals. Matching or coming close to their performance would be a monumental task.  (Picture of the Netrunner and Replicant)With the dimensions set by James, we started brainstorming the design ideas. First was the shape--James really liked Replicant, which has an organic element to add a splash of fun. Analyzing James' trickset and competition routines, we concluded he needs a yoyo with high pacing and power. Since the yoyo would be a monometal, the ratio of the V shape and O shape needed to lean more towards V. To get that golden ratio, team leader Philip's signature, Overclock, came into play. The Artifice profile is based on Replicant (simplified Graviton series) with the Overclock V/O ratio.  (Profile of Replicant, Artifice, and Overclock side by side) James requested a high level of power and stability in the yoyo. To achieve that, we implemented Stingray's undercut rim design in the Artifice. We found this undercut rim design enhanced the overall rim weight distribution, somewhat mimicking the feeling of a bimetal.  (Side by side picture of Stingray rim and Artifice rim)For the center cup design, we wanted something that slightly adds weight for acceleration. After looking through multiple designs, we decided to use the Raytracer center cup. This gives the yoyo a unique look while adding modest weight towards the center.  (Side by side picture of  and Arifice cup) James also requested the center response area to be polished for a crisp bind, like that of the Ultracut.  (Polished response area of Ultracut and Artifice)Combining all these design elements into one was a challenge, but we succeeded and the prototype was made.  (Picture of Artifice prototype)James received the prototype a couple weeks before US nationals and he instantly loved it. We found that this yoyo, despite being monometal, had a surprising amount of stability, even achieving the level of our flagship bimetal lineup! The overall specifications, weight distribution and undercut design came together to make this happen. Despite our suggestions, James immediately switched over to his prototype for the US national yoyo contest. He then proceeded to place 6th in the 1A finals division! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oEB20qi2S_AAfter consultations with the players and the manufacturing team, we decided to greenlight the yoyo for production without any changes. James then went on to use his prototype at the World Yoyo Contest and placed 16th at the 1A finals division! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=462wGu3KtKEJames decided to name this yoyo Artifice. Artifice means a clever or artful skill. It communicates what James aims to achieve in his yoyo performance--both high-level technical skill, and artistry that gives the audience a memorable experience. (Logo of Artifice)Artifice is the signature of James Heder and our ultimate monometal flagship. It combines the essence of multiple Yoyofriends' designs into one. Artifice redefines the performance of a monometal yoyo in terms of stability and usability, and challenges our flagship bimetals' performance in every aspect.

title: Ascension
content:
History / About
The Ascension is G2's 2025 titanium monometal, continuing the brand's occasional forays into premium titanium production alongside their core aluminum lineup. Named to convey a sense of elevation and achievement consistent with the competition-focused identity of G2's titanium releases.

title: Ascent
content: AboutThe Ascent is OFFSET's entry-level polycarbonate, designed for players learning from the ground up. It ships in responsive configuration out of the box and includes an unresponsive bearing upgrade so players can convert it when ready. The design incorporates a fingerspin hub for DNA tricks and supports conversion to bind play via a long axle. Available in glow-in-the-dark colorways, the Ascent was positioned specifically for learners targeting viral trick styles.

title: Ashiru Kamui
content: AboutThe Ashiru Kamui is a molded Delrin offstring, released in 2011 as the production successor to the original machined Kamui. The name means "new god" in the Ainu language. It retained the Kamui's performance character at a significantly lower price while maintaining Delrin construction. Multiple production runs updated the specs slightly; current production measures 79.60mm diameter, 50.35mm width, and 69.5g, with a 19mm silicone slim pad response.

title: Ashiru Kamui Light
content: AboutThe Ashiru Kamui Light is an injection-molded polycarbonate/ABS offstring released in 2012 as an entry-level option below the Delrin Ashiru Kamui. Lighter and less expensive, it brought the Kamui design to beginners. A 44CLASH Limited Edition colorway was produced for the 44CLASH contest.

title: Asora
content:
Asora Prototype 01/02

From Suspense:

[after the Fuwa 2] " ... I removed the weight ring concept, it was too much effort to design around a weight ring and caps, along with trying to control the weight and weight distribution, too many features caused for the stock bare bone design to be forced into a play that I did not like.

That’s when Asora 01 and 02 were born. These were the first designs I sold. Both were ordered at the same time (received Jan 2023).

Asora 01 was sold on March 2023. Asora 02 was sold after 01 sold out, in December of 2023. 02 sold out a few months later. 30 units for each, there’s a couple extra 02 floating around somewhere with family members and things of that nature. One of each is also with One Drop for their playable museum."

Asora Prototype 03

The Asora 03, which would eventually become the Production Asora, released at Worlds 2024 on July 31st.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bCnIQPGVxa4

Production Run

The production Asora released on October 11, 2024. It is identical to the 03.

The Asora released in five colorways: pink, clear, blue, black, and a lime green. Each comes clear Ultra Light Side-Effects, except for the pink which comes with red.

title: Aspen
content:
From Dressel Designs/Edition:

"Introducing the first TC4 Titanium 7068 Capped bimetal. Signature of Adrian Velez with a CAD design collaboration with Editionyoyo and Dressel Designs.

A yo-yo for a friend, made possible with the help of friends, with artwork by friends.

With TC4 we were able to construct a rim which incorporates traits from our favorite extended rim bi-metals, while still retaining the capped feel of some of our favorite "fun" yo-yos. This unique combination results in a design which excels at daily casual play with the power, stability and control you would crave in order to hit your tech routine if asked to!

We hope you enjoy this special project as much as we all have making it!"

Preorder Bonus

Those who preordered an Apsen got their throw in a 3D printed carry case and also received a signed photo from Adrian.

title: Assassin
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"When creating the Assassin the goal was to keep the spirit of their previous 5050 release alive in a smaller, pocketable, and more serious design. The stainless steel gives it a unique and premium feel in the hand and on the string without a premium price tag. The organic profile is still front and forward, but with an opening in the gap that reduces friction and adds stability without compromising any comfort or fun. The D bearing adds to the unique feel and gives you a tight bind every time with impressive spin power.

The Assassin is the last EDC yoyo you will ever need. Perfect to play anywhere with a blend of comfort and performance you won’t find even in your most competition focused throws!"

title: Assassin v2
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Don't call it a comeback. Assassin V2. The retirement run.

Slight changes to the design, only visible difference is a new cut in the cup.

Raw and black on our third year anniversary, 3/31."

title: Asterisk
content: A yoyo designed by Mk1 and @EOS44

title: Astraea
content: A contest-ready bi-metal inspired by four C3 predecessors: Bastet, Radius, Atomic Crash, and Fingerspin. Designed for power, long sleep, and stability through its tall bi-metal construction. Signature player Hobbit Wen is C3's Women's division champion. Available in Light Blue, Pink, Silver/Gold Rim, Black/Gold Rim, splash variants, and a Shibuya Edition. Price: $99.99.

title: ASTRO REMIX
content: About the ASTRO REMIXThe ASTRO REMIX pairs a 6061 aluminum body with Celcon (POM/Delrin) outer rings — a bi-material combination offering "the solid feel of metal with the softer touch and unique response of plastic." Designed for everyday sessions and casual play over pure competition use. Relaxed but capable playing style. $89.99 USD. Colorway: Midnight Navy / White.

title: Astro
content:
History / About
The Astro is sOMEThING's monometal designed with a focus on comfort and versatility. Its rounded, ergonomic shape offers a soft, effortless feel in play rather than specializing in one performance area. Suited for both newcomers to metal yo-yos and experienced players seeking a relaxed, approachable everyday throw, the Astro performs across various trick styles without demanding the precision of higher-end bimetal models.

title: Cephas ES
content:
History / About
The Cephas ES marks Atmos Projects' return to one of their most well-regarded designs. Building on the foundation of the original Cephas, the Essential Series designation signals a focused refinement rather than a reinvention — retaining the character players loved while tightening tolerances, redistributing rim weight for improved stability, and pairing the throw with Atmos's in-house Type II Concave bearing and Stratos response pads. Shipped with Cloudweave Micro string.

title: Contact
content:
History / About
Contact is a collaboration between atmos projects and SGMNT44, released June 30, 2026 as the brand's most aggressive, competition-oriented design to date. It carries an over-52mm-wide profile for a large landing zone on simple mounts while keeping the diameter compact so it doesn't feel bulky — a brutalist, performance-driven form factor shaped by input from technical competitive players.

title: DSG_017
content:
Coleman Weimer's Second Signature
DSG_017 follows Smoke as Coleman Weimer's second signature with Atmos Projects, again built around a jumbo polycarbonate organic shape that favors loose, flow-driven play. At 61.7mm across and just under 71 grams, it offers a big, forgiving catch zone while staying light enough to carry momentum through long freestyle combos.
It ships with Atmos's own Type I concave bearing and Stratos response pads installed.
Sold as an early-access preorder through the Atmos secret store under its DSG codename, ahead of a wider release under a name yet to be announced.

title: DSG_019
content:
A Rounded, Rim-Weighted Cap Design
DSG_019 takes the rounded profile Atmos established with the Butterball and rebuilds it as a capped, full-aluminum throw with weight pushed out to the rims. At 54.1mm diameter, 46.8mm width and 67.7 grams, it is aimed at stable, controlled 1A play.
Body and caps are both machined from 6061 aluminum, and it comes fitted with the Atmos Type II concave bearing and Stratos response pads.
Sold as an early-access preorder through the Atmos secret store under its DSG codename, ahead of a wider release under its eventual retail name.

title: DSG_020
content:
An Atmos x Project Cosmos Collaboration
DSG_020 is a joint design between Atmos Projects and Project Cosmos, combining the geometry of the Cosmos Procyon with cap construction borrowed from the Atmos Ari. At 55.5mm diameter, 48mm width and 67.2 grams, it is built for quick direction changes while keeping enough stability for technical combos.
Finishes include beadblasted solids and a two-tone stonewashed body with glossy caps. It runs Atmos house parts: Type II concave bearing and Stratos response pads.
Sold as an early-access preorder through the Atmos secret store under its DSG codename, ahead of a broader release.

title: DSG_021
content:
Vladimir Glazkov's Third Signature
DSG_021 is Vladimir Glazkov's third Atmos Projects signature. It revisits the H-profile shape of the Hamr in 7075 aluminum at a 54mm diameter and 54mm width, aiming for a lighter, more agile feel.
At 67.5 grams with rim-focused weight, it is tuned for accessible catch zones and quick maneuvering in technical 1A play. It runs the Atmos Type II concave bearing and Stratos response pads.
Listed as an early-access preorder in the Atmos secret store under its DSG codename, ahead of naming and general release.

title: Atmosphere
content: About the AtmosphereThe Atmosphere is the signature model of 2004 5A World Champion Makoto Numagami, designed for the counterweight play style in which he excelled. Despite its undersized 51mm diameter, it weighs a hefty 72 grams, concentrating mass in the nickel-bronze rims for extraordinary spin stability. The Solid Spin Axle system and silicone O-ring response make it reliable for advanced 5A and 1A play alike.

title: Atomic Crash
content: The bi-metal evolution of the Gamma Crash (POM hybrid). The Atomic Crash applies full aluminum + stainless steel bi-metal construction to the Gamma Crash's H-profile shape, with a titanium axle for extended sleep and a contest-ready character. Available in Light Blue, Black Rainbow, Rainbow, Pink, and splash colorways. Price: $99.99.

title: Anuran
content: History / AboutAnuran is the second model in Sync by Aufheben and the signature mono-metal model of Russian player Leonid Nemchik. At about 69 g it is a heavy yo-yo that is described as easy to move and reverse, with a moderate size suited to both technical and large tricks. Barrel-polished surface.

title: Aporia
content: History / AboutAporia is the third Sync by Aufheben model, the signature of Bae Ji Hoon. Like Nurture it is based on Aufheben's Shelter but designed with a different approach. It is slightly small, light and controllable, per Yoyostore Rewind. Barrel-polished surface.

title: Bufo
content: History / AboutBufo is Leonid Nemchik's second signature model, started after he asked for a new yo-yo because Anuran could not withstand his new tricks. The shape is Anuran stretched, about 9 mm wider overall. The body is A6061 aluminum with a large outer stainless steel rim and a very small midship rim near the step, following the concept of Dyad. Titanium axles are standard on Leonid's colorways; the Riku Araki Edition ships with a stainless axle and so differs slightly in weight.

title: Chiral
content: History / AboutChiral is the fourth Sync by Aufheben model, the signature of front-style player Takumi Shirasaki. It has a narrow width and small diameter with a small size D bearing, and large stainless steel rims protruding from the body for spin and stability. Barrel-polished, with minor vibration noted as a product characteristic.

title: Dyad
content: History / AboutDyad is Aufheben's first wide bimetal model aimed at competition. In addition to the outer rim, it embeds a thin stainless steel rim near the step, distributing weight both outside and inside for strong spin with easy handling and stability. Barrel-polished, with minor vibration noted.

title: Eureka
content: History / AboutEureka was the first model released by Aufheben, a Japanese yo-yo brand. Yoyostore Rewind describes it as a 7075 ("super super duralumin") mono-metal model; its shape was carried into Oxymoron (a larger, wider alternate version) and Eureka RM (re-mastered, about 2 mm wider). No standalone product page was found.

title: Eureka RM
content: History / AboutEureka RM (RE:MASTERED) is a renewed version of Aufheben's first model, Eureka. Like the original it is a mono-metal yo-yo machined from A7075 aluminum, an alloy harder and tougher than that commonly used in metal yo-yos. The appearance matches the original Eureka, but the width is about 2 mm greater to improve mount success. Yoyostore Rewind describes the feel as light and quick yet with a firm response, retained from the original.

title: Freeze
content: History / AboutFreeze is Aufheben's fifth release, developed around the theme of "the original pleasure of the yo-yo." It is small in diameter, wide, and light. Its distinctive feature is a multi-step rim that hollows out the inside of the rim to distribute weight. Rewind describes a rounded shape with smooth handling and strong spin duration despite the low weight.

title: Nature
content: History / AboutNature is Aufheben's first titanium yo-yo. It was developed from Shelter to approach the ideal feel of owner and designer Kazuki Morii; the aluminum version, Nurture, came first. A single-material titanium body would have needed dangerously thin rims, so an ultra-light A7075 wing is fitted to the outer edge. The body shape is identical to Nurture, but Nature emphasizes mobility and stability. It followed a long development period.

title: Nurture
content: History / AboutNurture is the first release of Sync by Aufheben, Aufheben's premium line produced at a higher-grade factory. It is the signature model of Aufheben owner Kazuki Morii. A mono-metal design, it is described as combining bimetal-like spin and stability with mono-metal directness, and is based on Aufheben's Shelter. Surfaces are barrel-polished, so small marks are part of the finish. The Aufheben store lists it as its newest item.

title: Oxymoron
content: History / AboutOxymoron was developed as an alternate version of Aufheben's first model, the 7075 ("super super duralumin") Eureka. The shape is largely carried over, but size and weight differ: it is larger overall and slightly heavier, and the width is increased by more than 3 mm, making it a wide-style yo-yo. Yoyostore Rewind notes it ships with an hkmt equipment grip-C pre-installed.

title: Poser (Jensen Kimmitt collaboration)
content: History / AboutPoser was developed jointly by Aufheben and Jensen Kimmitt, the 1A World Champion. It has an A7075 body covered by an A6061 hollow rim, a mechanism that was Jensen's idea, designed from his sketch. It was originally planned for release in 2022 but was put on hold when Jensen left the yo-yo scene, and the project stayed dormant because name and artwork had not been decided. Years later Tyler Vienneau found Jensen's artwork made for A-RT and gave it to Aufheben; the name Poser comes from that artwork. The response is snow-tire size, but it is silicone-filled to follow Jensen's original intent. Barrel-polished.

title: Shelter
content: History / AboutShelter is an earlier Aufheben model. Yoyostore Rewind texts state that Nurture and Aporia were developed on the basis of Shelter, that Nature was developed from Shelter, and that Sublation combines Unparalleled's Corruption with Shelter's side face. No standalone product page was found.

title: Sublation (Aufheben x Unparalleled)
content: History / AboutSublation is the first collaboration between Aufheben and Unparalleled. It is a full-metal yo-yo that combines Unparalleled's Corruption with the side face of Aufheben's Shelter. Diameter was slightly reduced to the 54 mm range; width is 44 mm; weight is about 64 g, in 7075 aluminum (super super duralumin). The focus is casual everyday play. The name is the English equivalent of the German "Aufheben," used to mark the collaboration.

title: Upcycle
content: History / AboutUpcycle joined Aufheben's regular lineup after roughly four years without a new regular model. It is a mono-metal yo-yo with a light, quick feel and strong braking: per Yoyostore Rewind it accelerates easily and stops precisely where intended.

title: Auldey Looping Yo-Yo
content: Designed by 2A specialist Yi Chenghao, the Auldey Looping Yo-Yo features an innovative bearing-lock system that adjusts starburst height. Six ultra-thin washers enable fine gap tuning. Wider gap than typical loopers, optimized for wrap combos. Polycarbonate construction in clear yellow and pink variants.

title: Autoscopy
content: AboutThe Autoscopy is the signature of Hajime Miura, who has won more World YoYo Contest titles than any player in the sport's history (9 as of 2025). The original AE line bi-metal at 56mm × 43mm × 66.5g grew into a full signature ecosystem: the MN Autoscopy (mono-metal, 67g), Mini Autoscopy (smaller diameter), Blur Autoscopy, and Liminal Autoscopy (2023 tri-material). The RE Autoscopy (2025), released to commemorate Miura's 9th title, is the current signature.The Autoscopy's 56mm diameter and moderately heavy 66.5g weight reflect Miura's preference for a stable, powerful throw that can sustain the long, precise combos that have defined his Championship-winning routines.

title: AUT(OS)COPY – Offstring
content:
About
The offstring counterpart to Hajime Miura's Autoscopy, developed simultaneously with the bimetal 1A/3A version to mirror Miura's dual-division mastery (he won both 3A and 4A at the 2018 World Championships). Slightly smaller than other models in YYR's offstring lineup while retaining stability, suited to general offstring tricks/regens as well as two-handed SOLOHAM-style play.

title: Avocado V2
content: About the Avocado V2The Avocado V2 is a compact, high-performance budget aluminum yo-yo with a wing-shaped profile for good weight distribution and long high-speed spins. High-end laser-etched graphics on a shiny anodized surface gave it visual distinction. A KK concave bearing centered the string for clean trick execution. Priced at approximately $10.99 USD, it represented one of MagicYoYo's most affordable aluminum performance options. Now discontinued.

title: Axiom
content: About the AxiomThe Axiom represents a landmark in YoYoJam's history as the company's first venture into full-metal yo-yo production, departing from their signature composite formula. Its wide round body with a relatively small diameter creates a unique weight distribution, and optional side caps allow players to fine-tune weight. The silicone O-ring response system was developed alongside the Meteor.

title: EX
content: AboutThe EX is Axis YoYos' second bimetal, distinguished from most bimetal designs by its internal stainless steel weight rings rather than the conventional outer-rim placement. The severe V-profile with an inner rim step optimizes the EX for horizontal (sideways) play and fingerspins. Six colorways — Violet, Tiffany, Scarlet, Raven, James, and Jade — were each packaged individually with unique presentation. At $114.99 it sits at the same premium tier as the original Pulsefire.

title: Mixtape
content: AboutThe Mixtape is Axis YoYos' first monometal and budget offering, released in early 2016 at $39.99. Its H-profile 6061 aluminum construction delivers solid unresponsive performance at an accessible price point. The hubs feature a distinctive "play button" engraving. Available in red, green, blue, blue/silver splash, purple/silver splash, and black/gold splash colorways.

title: Pulsefire
content: AboutThe Pulsefire is Axis YoYos' debut product and the throw that put the brand on the map. Crowdfunded via IndieGoGo and shipped November 2015, it features a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rims in a distinctive quasi-multi-step profile that concentrates weight distribution in novel ways. Yuki Nishisako — introduced to Axis by Yoshihiro Matsubara of Japan Looping Solutions — used the Pulsefire as his primary competition throw. Available in Bubblegum, Midnight, Midnight Azure, Midnight Cotton Candy, and Spitfire colorways, with engraved YG Blue variants also produced.

title: Pulsefire Ti
content: AboutThe Pulsefire Ti is Axis YoYos' Grade 5 titanium model, released in close proximity to the bimetal Pulsefire in 2015. At approximately $200–215 USD it was positioned as one of the more accessible titanium yo-yos of its era. Machined from titanium with a Trifecta Stainless Steel Size C bearing and IrPads response, it delivers the firm, distinctive spin character expected of titanium construction in a compact undersized package.

title: SAL-Ti
content: AboutThe SAL-Ti is Axis YoYos' first titanium model produced under the Axis brand (as opposed to the Pulsefire Ti, which launched at the same time as the original bimetal). A step-round undersized design at 54.37mm diameter, it delivers the firm, responsive bind and extended spin time characteristic of titanium machining. Released at $249.99 with M4×6mm axle and Dimple Bearing, the SAL-Ti was one of the brand's final releases before going inactive.

title: Azure
content: The Azure is the signature model of W1LD team member Ryo Igarashi. Built with a tri-material construction featuring polycarbonate rings and stainless steel rims on a 6061 body, the Azure is available in multiple polycarbonate color options that give each version a visually distinct character while sharing the same competition-ready specs.

title: Babbit
content:
History / About
The Babbit is MonkeyfingeR Design’s signature model for John, a comedian and performer. Designed as an approachable intro throw rather than a competition instrument, it shipped with hubstacks, a solid bearing, and a beginner-friendly responsive setup. Colorways at release were light blue, dark blue, green, and red.
The name is a nod to Babbitt, a small town in Minnesota where John’s grandmother grew up — a quiet, personal reference woven into what the brand describes as a “pocket-sized souvenir from a night of laughter and loops.”

title: Backstage Pass
content:
History / About
The Backstage Pass is MonkeyfingeR Design’s signature model for Nick Diffatte, 1.5 years in development. Diffatte brought an organic, casual shape concept; Jesse Kazemeck and Ray at MFD added performance refinements. The result is described as “smooth, confident, and show ready” — from sticker art to play feel, the whole package was given close attention. Released July 16, 2021.

title: Bad Decision
content: The Bad Decision was the second entry in Werrd's Decision series of aluminum/Delrin hybrid designs. The metal body is significantly larger than the Split Decision, at 59.5mm × 46.62mm, while the Delrin rims were redesigned for a stability boost over the Split Decision's interchangeable variants. The added rim mass generates longer spin times.

title: Bakemono
content:
History / About
The name means "monster"/"shapeshifter" in Japanese. An ultra-oversized bimetal that Sengoku describes as eclipsing even the Masamaxx in size, yet light for its size.

title: Ballom
content: History / AboutYuki Sakamoto signature evolved from a heavier hidden Stellar IX prototype, reduced in size and tuned for stronger center/rim feedback and control.

title: Balloon
content: AboutOPYOYOS's oversized "fun" throw, the Balloon features an enormous 66mm diameter, making it one of the largest performance yo-yos in the modern era. The narrow catch zone supports regens and unresponsive fixed-axle-style tricks while wide rims provide stability and a soft catch. Debuted at the YYF Hangout before the 2022 US National Yo-Yo Contest. Ships with HKMT Equipment Toru string in a matching pink pouch. Engraving artwork by Anne Marijn.

title: Accel Boost
content: AboutThe Accel Boost is the fifth model in the Hyper Yo-Yo Accel line, released in 2025. With the widest body of any Accel model at 43.35mm and the heaviest weight at 71.4g, the Boost is designed for players who want more spin stability and string trick real estate. The step-straight body profile differs from the Origin/Wing/Round shapes. It uses an original pad-type response system (not starburst) and a custom axle design. The wide Accel Discs overlap the body for a distinctive silhouette. MSRP: $29.99.

title: Accel Grab
content: AboutThe Accel Grab is the fourth model in the Hyper Yo-Yo Accel line, released in 2025. It features an H-profile body with large Accel Discs that extend to overlap the edge of the yo-yo body. The oversized discs are designed specifically for "grab and spin" tricks — DNA and sideways DNA variations — in which the player grips the spinning disc directly while the yo-yo continues to rotate. At 55.75mm diameter it is the narrowest of the Accel models, allowing for more precise disc-grab mechanics. Uses the same three-bearing Accel System. MSRP: $24.99.

title: Accel Loop
content: AboutThe Accel Loop is the sixth model in the Hyper Yo-Yo Accel line, released in 2025 as the dedicated looping variant. Unlike the Wing/Round/Grab/Boost models, the Accel Loop uses a Size K bearing (the same as competitive looping yo-yos like the Loop 720) and has the strongest response in the entire Accel lineup — designed so even beginners can catch the yo-yo reliably during Loop the Loop. The Accel Disc is intentionally smaller than other Accel models, reducing the risk of the disc slipping from the palm during catches. At 50.8g it is the lightest of the Accel models. MSRP: $21.99.

title: Accel Origin
content: AboutThe Accel Origin is the inaugural product of Bandai's fourth-generation Hyper Yo-Yo revival, released in Japan in July 2024 as the launch model of the Hyper Yo-Yo Accel line. The Accel System — patented in both Japan and the US — uses two large independently rotating "Accel Discs" on the sides of the yo-yo: by gripping the discs and pulling the string sharply, the player generates spin without throwing. This makes yo-yo play accessible to children who struggle with traditional throwing technique. The yo-yo uses three metal bearings in total. Six colorways were available at launch (Dragonic Red, Gaming Black, Heroic Blue, Hip-Hop Yellow, Cosmo Purple, Punkish Green), with additional colors released through late 2024. MSRP: $16.99 / ¥1,980.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size A ball bearing ×3 (1 main + 2 Accel Disc)

title: Accel Round
content: AboutThe Accel Round is the third model in the Hyper Yo-Yo Accel line, released in Japan in December 2024. It features a traditional rounded/modified body shape (as opposed to the Wing's butterfly profile) with the full Accel System. Heavier than both the Origin (56g) and Wing (65.7g) at 66.5g, the Round is specifically weighted for sleeping trick performance. Three colorways at launch: Crimson Ouroboros, Dark Monster, Sapphire Blade. MSRP: $24.99 / ¥2,860.

title: Accel Wing
content: AboutThe Accel Wing is the second model in Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo Accel fourth-generation line, released in Japan in October 2024. It is a wing-shape version of the Accel Origin — wider gap reminiscent of the Duncan Butterfly — with the full Accel System of independently rotating Accel Discs. At 65.7 grams and 58mm diameter it is heavier and larger than the Origin, providing more stable spinning and longer sleep times for attempting tower and rock-the-baby string elements. Three colorways at launch (Techno Purple, Classic Ivory, Twilight Blue); additional colorways in December 2024 (Scarlet Condor, Sunshine Phoenix, Sparkle Pegasus). MSRP: $19.99 / ¥2,530.

title: AceLash
content: AboutThe AceLash (also sold as "Ace Rush") is the 2013 Hyper Yo-Yo version of the YoYoFactory Loop 1080, using the same tiny 4×8×3mm Size K ball bearing found in the Mighty Flea and Loop 720. It is signed by Shu Takada, who placed 2nd in the 2A (looping) category at the World Yo-Yo Contest, making it the most competition-pedigree looping yo-yo in the third generation lineup. The standard body shape with tight response gives it the fast, snappy characteristics needed for professional-grade 2A looping. Oil injection required for bearing maintenance.

title: AstroFly
content: AboutThe AstroFly is a 2013 intermediate string trick model in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. It features the UFO-type (Center Trac) bearing specifically to keep the string centered on the axle for improved stability during tricks. The weight — 69.6 grams, one of the heaviest plastic string-trick models in the lineup — was intentionally increased over comparable models to improve spin times. Requires double-wrapping the string around the bearing for responsive return; intermediate players who have mastered basic string tricks will find it the natural next step after the GalaxyFly.

title: CrossDragon
content: AboutThe CrossDragon is the 2010 Hyper Yo-Yo version of the Yomega X-Brain, released for the third generation lineup. Its auto-return system — a four-part centrifugal clutch mechanism — automatically returns the yo-yo to the player's hand when spin drops below a threshold, making it the key learning model for beginners building their throw. Heavier than the Wild Claw (61.2g vs 58.8g) due to the four-part clutch assembly. At 60.55mm diameter it is the widest model in the Gen 3 beginner tier. A CrossDragon Ninteiten SE official certified-store limited colorway was released separately. Disassembles for maintenance.

title: DialMars
content: AboutThe DialMars is the Hyper Yo-Yo version of the YoYoFactory Velocity, released in Japan in 2011. Its defining feature is the Dial System — a knob on the side of the body that adjusts the response system's responsiveness. Turning the dial clockwise tightens the response for looping play; counter-clockwise extends sleep time for advanced string tricks. This made it the most versatile yo-yo in the third generation lineup, marketed as "the yo-yo that grows with you." H-profile shape with large trapeze width (37mm). Signed by John Ando in promotional materials.

title: Divault
content: AboutThe Divault is the highest-performing yo-yo released in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup, designed in collaboration with YoYoFactory and endorsed by world champion John Ando. It combines the heavy rim weighting of the YYF Northstar with the domed side cap profile of the YYF Protostar, adding an aluminum alloy rim for exceptional spin stability. Bind-required — it will not return on a simple tug — making it intended for players who have mastered 2nd High Level tricks and are ready to enter unresponsive yo-yo play. The Center Trac bearing with smooth coating finish makes it the most technically demanding model in the lineup.

title: FlamEWing
content: AboutThe FlamEWing is a 2010 Japan-exclusive version of the Duncan Dragonfly, released for the third Hyper Yo-Yo generation as the first Duncan string-trick model to enter the lineup. The wing-shaped body suits complex string maneuvers such as Stop and Dash, and the brake pad response with ball bearing delivers extended sleep times for stringing together advanced trick sequences. Described as "lightweight" with "good return," it sits at an approachable weight (52 grams) for a wing-shape model. Also branded as "FlameWing" in some regional listings.

title: FreezeWyvern
content: AboutThe Freeze Wyvern is a 2012 string trick yo-yo in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup, an OEM of the Shinwoo Techno 2. Its H-profile body has a notably low-profile edge — a new design feature for the Hyper Yo-Yo line at the time — that makes it well-suited for Eli Hops and juggling trapeze moves, as the low edge prevents the yo-yo from listing to one side during off-axis catches. The large Size C bearing provides extended sleep times for beginning through advanced string combinations. Eligible for official Hyper Yo-Yo certification.

title: GalaxyFly
content: AboutThe GalaxyFly is the 2011 successor to the StarFly, sharing the same H-profile body design but upgrading from a plastic bearing to a full metal UFO (Center Trac) bearing. The concave UFO bearing keeps the string centered on the axle, reducing tilt-induced spin loss and enabling significantly longer sleep times than the StarFly. Glitter-colored body halves distinguish it visually. At 67.2 grams it is one of the heavier plastic models in the third-generation lineup, further aiding spin stability. Suited for 1A, 3A, and 5A play styles.

title: GrindSaturn
content: AboutThe Grind Saturn is a 2012 string trick model in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. With a 53.26mm diameter it is the smallest-diameter yo-yo in the Gen 3 lineup, but its step-straight body profile and wide width (39.68mm) optimize it for finger grinds — the smooth, uninterrupted surface allows the yo-yo to glide along the finger for extended grinds, the naming "Saturn" evoking a planet with rings. Bind-required (no response on a dead string), targeting players who have progressed past beginner models. Size C bearing with slim pads provides unresponsive play.

title: Hyper Brain
content: AboutThe Hyper Brain is a Japan-exclusive version of the Yomega Brain, the world's first auto-return yo-yo. Licensed to Bandai and released in June 1997 as part of the inaugural Hyper Yo-Yo lineup, the Hyper Brain became the gateway model for a generation of Japanese players. Its patented centrifugal clutch mechanism automatically snaps the yo-yo back to the thrower's hand when spin speed drops below a threshold, making it virtually foolproof for beginners. Retailing at ¥2,200, it shipped with Hyper Yo-Yo branded sidecaps in place of Yomega's standard caps.

title: Hyper Comet
content: AboutThe Hyper Comet is the launch product of the third Hyper Yo-Yo series, released in 2010, and is described as "the first yo-yo released in the 2010s incarnation of the Hyper Yo-Yo range." It is Bandai's adaptation of the YoYoFactory FireDog — a simple, non-disassembling beginner model with a nylon spool axle that provides longer sleep times than a fixed-axle design. Before its official release, it debuted as the Hyper Comet Type-0, distributed exclusively at the 2010 World Hobby Fair. The body is a rounded-modified shape, cannot be disassembled, and requires no maintenance beyond string changes. Packaged with blue string and a trick/maintenance booklet.

title: Hyper Dragon
content: AboutThe Hyper Dragon is a modular, customizable yo-yo produced in collaboration between Bandai and Matsushita Electric (now Panasonic) and released in Japan in December 1998 as a tie-in with the manga/anime Chousoku Spinner (超速スピナー). Described as "a Hyper Yo-Yo born from Matsushita Electric Group's material processing technology, sophisticated design technology, and shaping technology," the Hyper Dragon's modular system allows the user to swap Frame Caps, Core components, and bearing types to configure the yo-yo for different play styles. The Dragon Tool (included) locks and unlocks components without standard tools. Retailing at ¥2,200 — the same price as the Hyper Brain — the Hyper Dragon was the centerpiece of Bandai's late-1998 marketing push. It remained in production through 1999 with the Fire and Aqua variants.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Interchangeable (nylon, non-slip, or metal bearing sets)

title: Hyper Dragon Aqua
content: AboutThe Hyper Dragon Aqua is the string-trick variant of the Hyper Dragon series, released in Japan in June 1999 alongside the Hyper Dragon Fire. Where the Fire uses the standard Dragon body, the Aqua ships with the solid black wing-shaped String Play Type Body, making it the recommended configuration specifically for string tricks. Its fiberglass-reinforced frame caps depict swirling tidal waves and are identical in construction to the Fire's caps — solid black without an aluminum frame, reducing weight by approximately 2 grams versus the original Dragon. Fully modular and Dragon Tool compatible.

title: Hyper Dragon Fire
content: AboutThe Hyper Dragon Fire is a variant of the Hyper Dragon released in Japan in June 1999. Its Frame Caps are made of solid black fiberglass-reinforced plastic without an aluminum frame, making them sturdier than the standard Hyper Dragon's caps and reducing total weight by approximately 2 grams. The caps depict eight blue fireballs swirling counter-clockwise around the lock mechanism — a visual contrast to the Hyper Dragon Aqua's tidal-wave motif. Like the standard Dragon, it is fully compatible with the modular Hyper Dragon component system and Dragon Tool.

title: Hyper Dragoon Pro
content: AboutThe Hyper Dragoon Pro is the final release in the original Hyper Yo-Yo lineup, released in Japan in April 2000. Designed as a simplified, tool-free version of the Hyper Dragon, the Dragoon Pro uses a different fastening mechanism that allows it to be taken apart and reconfigured without the Dragon Tool. In its standard configuration it features a transaxle sleeve with a pair of metal spacers. It is compatible with many Hyper Dragon parts, bridging the original Dragon's high-end modular system with accessible usability. The Hyper Dragoon Pro and Standard together mark the end of Bandai's first Hyper Yo-Yo generation.

title: Hyper Dragoon Standard
content: AboutThe Hyper Dragoon Standard is one of the final two releases in the original Hyper Yo-Yo lineup, released in Japan in 2000. It is a simplified, beginner-oriented derivative of the Hyper Dragon, designed to be more accessible to younger players. Unlike the Hyper Dragon, it can be disassembled and reconfigured without the Dragon Tool, making customization easier. The Standard version ships in a transaxle configuration, giving it responsive return suitable for learners. It represents Bandai's attempt to broaden the Dragon's appeal at the close of the first Hyper Yo-Yo era.

title: Hyper Fireball
content: AboutThe Hyper Fireball is a Japan-exclusive version of the Yomega Fireball, released by Bandai in July 1997 for the first Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. The Fireball was arguably the most iconic model of the 1997 Hyper Yo-Yo boom — far more familiar than the competition. It introduced the nylon transaxle to mass-market Japanese consumers, giving far longer sleep times than fixed-axle competitors. The rounded modified shape is versatile for both looping and basic string tricks, and the non-disassembling body requires no maintenance beyond string changes. Original string and cork pads on vintage examples may have degraded after 25+ years.

title: Hyper Infinity
content: AboutThe Hyper Infinity is the most unusual product in the entire Hyper Yo-Yo catalog, released in Japan on April 2, 2011: it is the only known motorized yo-yo ever sold on the mass market. An internal AAA battery-powered electric motor drives a gear box that keeps the yo-yo spinning continuously without the player needing to throw it. A plastic gear bearing connects to the motor assembly; the battery cover is removed via screwdriver for battery access. An adjustable plastic tube on the response string allows the player to tune how easily the yo-yo returns. The Hyper Infinity was marketed as a way for children to experience yo-yo play without mastering throw technique.

title: Hyper Loop
content: AboutThe Hyper Loop is a yo-yo manufactured by Playmaxx and released by Bandai in Japan in February 1998. It is the Hyper Yo-Yo rebrand of Playmaxx's popular ProYo II. The yo-yo features a modified body shape with laminated holographic pogs, a circular wooden axle sleeve, and came in numerous translucent color combinations. The original 1998 packaging erroneously labels the manufacturer as "ProYo II" rather than "Playmaxx." The wooden sleeve is not suited for long sleepers but delivers strong responsiveness for looping and two-handed play. Available in glow-in-the-dark variants as well.

title: Hyper Millennium
content: AboutThe Hyper Millennium is the first yo-yo in the Hyper Yo-Yo line developed entirely by Bandai rather than being a rebrand of another manufacturer's product. Released in Japan in October 1997 and manufactured in China, it features mirror-like metallic weight pogs inside each half, an aerodynamic profile suited for looping (including the circular "Loop the Loop" technique), and a responsive transaxle system. In 1998, a promotional lightweight variant was distributed — identically shaped but shipped without the internal weight pogs, reducing mass by approximately 6 grams. The Hyper Millennium represents Bandai's first step toward building an original yo-yo rather than relying on licensed designs.

title: Hyper Neo
content: AboutThe Hyper Neo is a yo-yo manufactured by Duncan and released by Bandai in Japan in March 1997 as one of five launch models of the first Hyper Yo-Yo line. It is technically a variant of the Duncan Imperial, sharing the same narrow fixed-axle looping form, but molded in bright solid neon colors rather than the translucent colors typical of the Imperial. The narrow string gap and fixed axle make it highly responsive, suited for basic looping and two-handed play. As a launch product it helped define the Hyper Yo-Yo brand identity alongside the Hyper Brain.

title: Hyper Papillon
content: AboutThe Hyper Papillon is a Japan-exclusive version of the Duncan Butterfly, released by Bandai in 1997 as part of the first Hyper Yo-Yo line. "Papillon" is French for butterfly, chosen for the Japanese market. The wide flared butterfly shape makes it significantly easier to land string elements compared to the looping-oriented Imperial-family models also in the lineup. As one of the earlier wide-gap yo-yos available in Japan, it introduced a generation of players to string trick play.

title: Hyper Raider
content: AboutThe Hyper Raider is a yo-yo manufactured by Yomega and released by Bandai in Japan in April 1998 as the flagship ball-bearing model of the first Hyper Yo-Yo line. Retailing at ¥5,000 — roughly $50 USD at the time and one of the most expensive models in the lineup — it was among the first yo-yos available in Japan to feature a full ball bearing, enabling sleep times far beyond any fixed-axle or transaxle model. The packaging reads "Yomega-Bandai 1998 Made in USA Hyper Raider." Its rounded modified shape, starburst response, and cover-type spacers deliver a responsive looping feel. Team High Performance Japan members used the Hyper Raider in demonstrations, cementing its status as a prestige model during the yo-yo boom.

title: Hyper RB II
content: AboutThe Hyper RB II is a yo-yo manufactured by Yomega and released by Bandai in August 1998 for the first Hyper Yo-Yo line. It is the Hyper Yo-Yo version of Yomega's RB II — a modified-shape yo-yo without side caps, featuring a metal ball bearing transaxle system. The minimal cap-less profile reduces mass to approximately 44 grams, making it one of the lightest models in the lineup, and its bearing enables considerably longer sleep times than fixed-axle siblings. Intended for looping and general play, it sat at a mid-range price between entry models and the flagship Hyper Raider.

title: Hyper Russell Professional
content: AboutThe Hyper Russell Professional (also known as Hyper Russell Pro) is a yo-yo manufactured by Russell in South Korea and released by Bandai in Japan in December 1998 as part of the first Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. It is the Hyper Yo-Yo rebrand of Russell's Professional model — a looping yo-yo molded in clear polycarbonate with flat bulged sidecaps featuring concentric rings, typical of Russell's heavyweight yo-yos from the 1990s. The fixed wooden axle provides strong response for looping tricks, while the 53-gram weight — heavier than its sibling the Hyper Russell Super by 9 grams — allows noticeably longer sleep times. A Hyper Russell Super variant (weighing ~44g, diameter ~56mm) was also produced.

title: Hyper Viper
content: AboutThe Hyper Viper is the original Hyper Yo-Yo off-string model, manufactured by Henrys and released by Bandai in Japan in October 1998. Produced under license from German yo-yo maker Henrys, the Viper's defining feature is its large rubber-shelled body: the rubber absorbs impact, allowing the yo-yo to bounce off hard surfaces without damage — an essential quality for off-string (4A) play in which the yo-yo is intentionally thrown from the string. The aluminum hub houses an adjustable-gap Quicktrick system for dialing in responsiveness, and the ball bearing provides extended spin times. Compatible with Henrys Viper and Cobra replacement shells. At 65.55mm diameter it is one of the largest yo-yos in the Gen 1 lineup.

title: Hyper Wasp
content: AboutThe Hyper Wasp is a yo-yo manufactured by Playmaxx and released by Bandai in Japan in September 1998 for the first Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. It is the Hyper Yo-Yo adaptation of Playmaxx's Turbo Bumble Bee — one of the most coveted string-trick yo-yos of the late 1990s. The ball bearing axle enables long sleep times, while the rare cork star brake pad response system gives it unique feedback characteristics. Like the Hyper Loop, the 1998 packaging erroneously labels the manufacturer as "ProYo II." The tight gap and aggressive response make it better suited for experienced players or collectors. Type 6 polyester string is recommended over original cotton string on vintage examples.

title: Hyper Wheels
content: AboutThe Hyper Wheels is a yo-yo manufactured by Duncan and released in Japan by Bandai in April 1997 as part of the Hyper Yo-Yo line. It is based on Duncan's Wheels model — a butterfly-shaped yo-yo with distinctive tire-shaped hubcap-style weight pogs on each side. The pogs add significant rim weight, giving the Hyper Wheels notably longer sleep times than the lighter Hyper Papillon or Hyper Neo. It was marketed toward players wanting to learn string-based tricks such as Trapeze, and remains one of the heavier fixed-axle models in the Gen 1 lineup.

title: HyperCluster MB2-S3 String Loop-D FlashFenrir
content: AboutThe HyperCluster FlashFenrir is a looping-type HyperCluster yo-yo released in Japan on July 21, 2012. Its disc-shaped body features a high edge and narrow string gap for strong responsiveness. Uniquely among HyperCluster models, the FlashFenrir uses a string-based response system rather than starburst ridges or response pads, giving it distinctive return characteristics optimized for looping trick flow. The MB2 designation indicates the upgraded second-generation metal bearing.

title: HyperCluster King Cluster
content: AboutThe King Cluster is the largest yo-yo ever released in the Hyper Yo-Yo lineup at 66.89mm diameter — roughly the same size as the Hyper Viper from 1998, but a full HyperCluster modular model. Despite its oversize dimensions, the light weight (58.3g) and standard gap width make it deceptively manageable, and it is particularly noted for excelling at looping tricks like Planet Hop — unusual for a yo-yo of this size. The package includes two King bodies, star-type cores, metal bearing, spacers, customization guide, trick sheet, and string — a complete HyperCluster kit.

title: HyperCluster Legend Cluster
content: AboutThe HyperCluster Legend Cluster is a rare limited-edition looping yo-yo from Bandai's HyperCluster series, released in 2012 and inspired by the Japanese TV drama "Hyper Yo-Yo Burning." It is the most premium model in the HyperCluster lineup: the ball bearing uses special ceramic balls rather than steel, making the Legend Cluster noticeably smoother and quieter than any other looping yo-yo in the lineup. The pads are specially formulated for superior looping responsiveness. Sold out immediately upon release and commands collector premiums on the secondary market.

title: HyperCluster Legend Coro Dragon
content: AboutThe HyperCluster Legend Coro Dragon is a 2012 special-edition HyperCluster model released in conjunction with Coro Coro Comic magazine and related TV Drama promotions. The round-body HyperCluster features the modular component system but in a specially configured preset rather than the user-customizable kits. At 64.6 grams and 56.17mm diameter with a wide 39.84mm body, it sits in the performance string-trick tier. Sold out quickly due to limited production tied to the Coro Dragon media property. Oil injection required for maintenance.

title: HyperCluster PB Pad Loop MachPhoenix
content: AboutThe HyperCluster PB Pad Loop MachPhoenix is one of the launch products of Bandai's HyperCluster modular customization system, released in Japan on April 23, 2011. The HyperCluster system consists of three interchangeable components: Body (determines play style), Core (contains axle and response), and Bearing. The MachPhoenix body is 5g lighter than other HyperCluster bodies and features glow-in-the-dark sidecaps. The PB (Plastic Bearing) and Pad Core configuration delivers strong looping response. The modular architecture recalls the original Hyper Dragon from 1998 but with a simplified, no-tool swap system.

title: HyperCluster MOB-S3-HMW Meteor Bahamut
content: AboutThe HyperCluster Meteor Bahamut is the heaviest production yo-yo in the HyperCluster line, released in 2012. Its body is nearly completely covered by an enormous mid-ship aluminum alloy weight ring that brings the total mass to 72.5 grams — extraordinary for a plastic yo-yo. The weight ring creates significant rim weighting, dramatically increasing spin stability and sleep times for advanced string tricks. Uses the inner-diameter support spacer system and requires binding. A Certified Store Limited Version with exclusive colorway was also produced.

title: HyperCluster MB2-S3 Laser Wing-H ThunderDrake
content: AboutThe HyperCluster ThunderDrake is the first HyperCluster model to feature a light-up function, released in 2011. Its hexagonal wing-shaped body is a new departure from the round and straight bodies in the lineup — the hex profile provides aggressive catch zones and a bold visual identity. The light-up laser core requires four LR41 button batteries (not included). The MB2 designation indicates the second-generation metal bearing upgrade over the original MB bearing, providing extended spin for high-level string trick practice. At 70.4 grams, the ThunderDrake is heavier than most HyperCluster predecessors, contributing to spin stability.

title: MetalBullet
content: AboutThe MetalBullet is the 2011 upgrade to the Woodbullet, a Duncan yo-yo licensed for Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line. Where the Woodbullet uses a wood fixed axle, the MetalBullet adds a metal ball bearing and friction pad response, significantly extending sleep times and enabling progression to Hyper Levels 1–2 certification tricks. At 46 grams it is slightly heavier than the Woodbullet (43.8g) but lighter than most bearing models. Disassembles for maintenance; oil injection supported.

title: MonsterShell
content: AboutThe MonsterShell is a 2010 Japan-exclusive re-release of Yomega's All-Star under the third Hyper Yo-Yo umbrella. Its fixed metal axle gives it a strong, snappy return response ideal for beginners learning Forward Pass and Breakaway. The non-disassembling body needs no maintenance beyond string replacement. Available in multiple colorways including Clear Red and Pink/White, the MonsterShell was notably used by competitive player Ryuji of the Top Spinners group. Packaged with red string and a certification-eligible instruction manual.

title: SpinPhoenix
content: AboutThe SpinPhoenix is a 2010 Japan-exclusive version of Yomega's Fireball, re-released under the third Hyper Yo-Yo umbrella. Maintaining the beloved Fireball body shape and transaxle mechanism, the SpinPhoenix adds glow-in-the-dark sidecaps as its visual upgrade. The lightweight plastic bearing creates a very light, free-spinning feel suited for intermediate players advancing to Super and Hyper level certification tricks. Disassembles for maintenance; oil injection supported.

title: SpiralJaguar
content: AboutThe SpiralJaguar is a 2012 looping yo-yo in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. Its standout feature is a three-spacer tuning system: the package includes six spacers in three thicknesses (purple, black, orange — two of each). The purple spacers produce tighter gaps for fast looping; the black spacers open the gap for longer sleepers; the orange spacers (factory default) provide a balanced middle ground. Players can combine spacers of different thicknesses to create custom response characteristics, making the SpiralJaguar one of the most tunable looping yo-yos in the Gen 3 lineup.

title: StarFly
content: AboutThe StarFly is a 2011 entry-level string trick model in the third Hyper Yo-Yo lineup. Its H-profile body with wide gap makes it easier to land string elements for players just beginning to learn string tricks — the wide trapeze width (30mm) catches the string without difficulty. Heavy for a plastic model at 64.9g, the weight helps sustain spin. It was later upgraded to the GalaxyFly (2011) which replaced the plastic bearing with a full metal UFO (Center Trac) bearing for improved performance. Oiling recommended as vintage examples age.

title: StormTiger
content: AboutThe StormTiger is the 2010 Hyper Yo-Yo version of Yomega's Raider, released in Japan in November 2010 for the third generation lineup. Its small metal ball bearing (Size K) provides high-speed performance and allows linking of looping tricks with regenerations — the ball bearing sustains spin long enough to chain multiple Loop the Loops. Described as "good for both looping and sleeping tricks," the StormTiger was endorsed by Top Spinner Ryuji as his go-to looping model. Bearing requires periodic oiling with Hyper Vaseline. A StormTiger Ninteiten SE special certified-store colorway was also released as a collector variant.

title: Super Yo-Yo Hyper Warp
content: AboutThe Super Yo-Yo Hyper Warp is an anime tie-in variant of the Yomega Hyper Warp, produced by Bandai to promote the Super Yo-Yo (超速スピナー) anime series. It is mechanically identical to the Yomega Hyper Warp — a robust modified-shape looping yo-yo praised for stability and long sleep times — but features side caps depicting the anime's main protagonist, Shunichi Domoto. The Super Yo-Yo anime aired on TV Tokyo from November 30, 1998 to September 6, 1999. A heavier variant, the Super Yo-Yo Hyper Warp Heavy, was also produced with a weighted body for extended sleep. The anime tie-in helped extend the Hyper Yo-Yo brand's reach into Southeast Asia, where localized dubs of the series were broadcast as late as 2005.

title: WildClaw
content: AboutThe WildClaw is a 2013 beginner auto-return yo-yo in the third Hyper Yo-Yo line. Like the CrossDragon, it uses a centrifuge clutch system — but with a simpler single-piece clutch rather than the CrossDragon's four-part assembly, making it lighter and less complex. Weak throws return the yo-yo immediately; strong throws allow it to sleep at the end of the string until momentum fades. Triple-wrapping the string around the axle is recommended for optimal performance. At 58.8 grams it is slightly lighter than the CrossDragon (61.2g). Suited for very young beginners first learning to throw.

title: WindOrbit
content: AboutThe WindOrbit is Duncan's second product released for the third Hyper Yo-Yo line (2010), a Japan-exclusive version of Duncan's Speed Beetle. Its looping friction sticker response system delivers strong, reliable returns, and the ball bearing gives it the spin times needed for multi-loop tricks. Lighter than the StormTiger at 47 grams, it is described as "slightly more geared towards looping tricks than the Woodbullet" with an easy-to-grasp form factor. Available in clear and opaque colorways.

title: Woodbullet
content: AboutThe Woodbullet is a Duncan OEM version of the ProYo, fitted with custom Hyper Yo-Yo sidecaps as a Japan exclusive for the third Hyper Yo-Yo line (2010). Its distinguishing feature is a wooden axle — giving it a notably smoother feel than a plastic-axle model. The wooden axle requires a brief break-in period (wrap the string approximately 10 times before first use), and replacement wooden axle sets are sold separately. Notably used by professional player Top Spinner Rei, the Woodbullet precedes the MetalBullet (2011) in the beginner-to-intermediate progression. At 43.8 grams it is the lightest model in the Gen 3 line.

title: Bandalo:re
content:
From Bandalore:

" Before we explain why we chose the name 「Bandalo:re」 for this product, allow us to take you back to a time before “Yo-Yo” became the official name it is known by today.

As some of you may not know, between the 17th and the 19th centuries, the term “BANDALORE” was referred to a toy made of wood, a spool or wheel attached to a string. It was an early version of the yo-yo, serving as a precursor to the modern design we recognize today. The user would wind and unwind the strings to perform various tricks, or just simply throw and retrieve the toy. It gained popularity in Europe as a French term for a type of spinning toy before spreading to the United States, where it played a key role in the evolution of the modern yo-yo.

We were deeply inspired by this fusion of history, merging the classic and old-fashioned yo-yo style with our personal favorite modern yo-yo, the “DK” by SF Yoyos, which sparked us the inspiration for this design. And so, with this combination,「Bandalo:re」 was born. A perfect harmony that bridges the evolution between eras, honoring the past while embracing the future, hope to igniting a new wave of creativity and inspiration. 

Also, just so you know, the “:re” in the name symbolizes “remake, redo, and refresh.” These are the ideas we wanted to capture both when the yo-yo first appeared and when it’s in your hand."

title: Bangarang
content:
About
The Bangarang is Lathed Back Design's first production yo-yo and the foundation of their mini modular titanium line. Designed to utilize titanium to its maximum potential despite its compact size, the Bangarang ships with three bearing configurations — a wide unresponsive centering bearing, a narrow semi-responsive bearing, and an anodized titanium fixed-axle blank — plus a set of 3D-printed Delrin expansion rims, O-rings, string, a size-A bearing removal tool, and a custom 1980s-style boom-box themed 3D-printed packaging case.
The rim system expands the core from mini to full-size dimensions, offering six distinct play configurations out of the box. An optional OST Module expansion (press-on titanium rims for spark play) was also offered. Each colorway was produced in limited runs of approximately 100 pieces; once sold, a colorway was permanently retired. All anodizing was performed in-house by the brand, one piece at a time.
Colorways
Standard retail colorways included Raw Machined, Black Cherry Cola, Rainbow Sherbet, Stardust, and Wildberry Meltdown. The YoYoExpert launch run (November 19, 2021) featured Fractured Royalty, Rippled Cobalt, Stardust, Spike, Plot Twist, and Blue Raspberry Cola. Artist's Proof editions — unique 1-of-1 or small-run custom anodize pieces — included Copper Fission AP and Wild Berry Fission, among others.

title: Banshee
content:
History / About
The Banshee is the model that cemented G2's reputation as a serious competition brand. Jacob stated that it was the first time G2 committed to keeping competitive play as the number one design goal — previous models balanced competition and casual use. Four prototype versions were developed before the design was finalized. G2 increased the rim weight compared to prior models to find the right balance of stability, spin time, and agility. The initial drop debuted with solid colors in the G2 Diamond blast finish, June 12, 2016. The Banshee became a long-running design platform — the "TiShee" (Titanium Banshee) was produced in 2019 as a raw titanium version limited to 100 pieces, signed by Jacob Gross. The Banshee 22 (2022) and Banshee T52 (2025, 6061 body with titanium rims) continue the lineage. The DireWolf was produced as a larger-diameter Banshee variant in honor of the final season of Game of Thrones.

title: Banshee 18
content:
About
Banshee 18 is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2018. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Banshee 22
content:
History / About
The Banshee 22 is the 2022–era update to the legendary Banshee platform. G2 expanded the Banshee into multiple material configurations simultaneously — a standard 6061 version, an AL7 (7075) for more powerful spin, and two exotic bimetal variants using titanium as the body material: the TiBr (titanium body with brass weight rings, "Foundry" colorway) and the TiSS (titanium body with stainless steel rims, "Gunmetal" colorway). This represented G2's most ambitious material experimentation on a single design platform.

title: Banshee
content: AboutThe Banshee was Huatian's flagship bi-metal yo-yo, machined from 7075 aluminum with stainless steel #304 rims. Its compact 52mm diameter and rim-weighted bi-metal construction deliver a stable, long-spinning, competition-oriented feel.

title: Banshee SS
content:
About
Banshee SS is a 6061 aluminum with SS rims yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2019. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Banshee SS FS

About

title: Banshee T52
content:
History / About
The Banshee T52 is one of the most exotic entries in the Banshee platform — using titanium weight rings on a 6061 aluminum body. Titanium is lighter than stainless steel but denser than aluminum, landing between the two extremes in terms of rim weight impact. The T52 designation specifically indicates the titanium ring configuration. Available in EDC Gray, Slate Black, and Rainbow Galaxy colorways.

title: Bapezilla
content:
The Bapezilla was the 3rd Anti-Yo release, releasing on July 4, 2006.  The name was influenced by the Japanese clothing company, A Bathing Ape.  It was an updated eetsit.  Having a smaller gap, and new colors Grass Green and Candy Blue.  Although it's retail price was only $80, they quickly became highly sought after with some people paying as much as $200 for one!  Someone reportedly, never verified, paid $400 for one!  In the box with the Bapezilla's were packaged little toys and stickers.

June 29, 2006 YoYoNation post by Kiya:

"Some how the number of supporters we had went from a small number to a huge chunk of the yoyo community in a matter of weeks after the release of the eetsit.  We got quite a few emails from people praising the eetsit, we got people wanting to buy multiples of it, we got some people that had issues with it, we had people wanting more of it.  In the end we realized that itwould be sad to let the eetsit live with only one release. So we tweaked the design of the yoyo a tiny bit, which decreases the gap by a millimeter or so, changed the colors, and went with a flat bearing.  The Bapezilla is about Spring, happiness, and colors so bright that it¹s hard to resist wanting to eat the yoyo.  Where the eetsit was about subtlety, the Bapezilla is about turning it all up to 11.

The pricing of the yoyo was supposed to be $90, but we reduced it by ten dollars because the yoyo is shipping with a flat bearing instead of a Konkave (I'd like to note that Anti-Yo is taking the monetary hit on this price reduction).  We love Konkave bearings; I personally put them in all the yoyos I can get them into.  Some people take them out of the yoyos they use and use flat bearings.  A Konkave will fit in the Bapezilla if that's what you want.   Regardless, the reason the Bapezilla is not shipping with a Konkave is because we couldn't get them fast enough because the demand for the bearing is so high at the moment.  Just in case anybodyis wondering, we plan to release our next yoyo with a Konkave bearing.

Preorders start on July 1 at most stores, the yoyo should start to ship from stores around July 7.

More info and specs will be posted on www.anti-yo.com shortly.

In the very near future we have the first skate deck from Paul Escolar, a new Anti-Yo t-shirt inspired by the 1A UK Champion Anti-Team member Simon Welch, and our next yoyo YWET.

Love and Kisses,Kiya + Sonny"

Platinum Bapezilla

The platinum Bapezilla was a 1 of 2 limited edition. One of these was sold to raise funds for the California State YoYo Championship.  The auction sold for $760.

From the Auction:

"This is One of Two Auctions. Both items are pictured below. Item specific pictures in the gallery.First is a 1 of 2 Platinum Plated Ended BapezillaThe Bape was:Ended by Anti-Yo themselves Polished Nickel plated Polished Again Platinum Plated (completely) Polished Again Again (outer rim only)These are Anti-yoThis is an ended BapeThis is ultimate swagger .All funds go to the California State Yo-Yo Championship.Thank you Sonny, Kiya, and Anti-Yo for sponsoring the California State Yo-Yo Championship!"

title: Bare Bones
content:
History
The Bare Bones was the model that made Dif-e-Yo a household name in the competitive yo-yo world. When it launched in 2005, most wide-format yo-yos were plastic — the Bare Bones proved that a full-metal throw could be wide, stable, and competition-ready at a price players could actually afford. Its satin exterior gave excellent grinding capability; the small internal groove served double duty for both weight ring retention and thumb grinds.
Sponsored player Dave "Dazzling Dave" Schulte set the AYYA Eli Hop world record of 120 consecutive hops on a Bare Bones at the 2005 World Yo-Yo Championships — an achievement that cemented the model's status in yo-yo history. The Bare Bones became Dave's signature throw and remained the most recognizable Dif-e-Yo model for the duration of the brand's life.
In May 2024, two months after Frank Difeo's death, Beyond YoYos released a tribute reissue of the Bare Bones (see Bare Bones 2024) alongside the Bimetal Cross Bones as a memorial to Frank's legacy.

title: Bare Bones 2024
content:
History
The Bare Bones 2024 was a tribute reissue released on May 10, 2024 — approximately two months after Frank P. Difeo's death on March 3, 2024. The release was a collaboration between Beyond YoYos, a Massachusetts yo-yo retailer with whom Frank had a close personal relationship, and the Dif-e-Yo estate.
The 2024 version is slightly larger than the original (54mm vs. 53.34mm diameter; 42.5mm vs. 41.15mm width) and updates to a standard 19mm slim pad response and Size C bearing rather than the KonKave — making it accessible to a wider modern audience while honoring the design that Dave Schulte rode to a world record in 2005. Available in Blue, Green, and Red anodize at $54.99.

title: Baroness Blend
content:
About
The Baroness Blend is an annual Throw-Yo Threads special. Once a year, the maker's wife walks into the thread room and picks, with no brief and no spec, and whatever she wants gets wound and named for her. The 2025 edition is an Ink-type string from the SOLUTIONS line, described as slippery in play with killer speed, long life and a slightly coarse feel. It first appeared to Patreon subscribers as the November 2025 "Baroness Blend #1" and was listed on the public store on March 20, 2026.

title: Barracuda
content: AboutThe Barracuda is Rafael Matsunaga's signature model and one of the most decorated yo-yos in modern competition history, used to win 8 National and World titles. It was unveiled at the 2012 World Yo-Yo Contest and debuted as a winner the same day — Brazilian player Hank Freeman used it to take 1st place in the 3A Division. The Barracuda's aluminum H-shaped Inverse Round body keeps the string clear of the inner walls during play, and it shipped with a Monkey Weight counterweight for 5A flexibility. The aesthetic — clean anodized colorways, angular profile — became the visual template for the Screaming Eagle premium tier.

title: Barracuda Jr.
content: AboutThe Barracuda Jr. is an undersized derivative of the full-size Barracuda, shrinking the diameter to 53 mm while preserving the Matsunaga-designed weight distribution and profile character. At 63 g and 53 mm it is a fast, snappy throw suited to players who prefer undersized yo-yos for speed-focused combos. Duncan positioned it as a natural companion to the Barracuda for players who wanted the same DNA at a smaller scale and a lower price.

title: Barracuda X
content: AboutThe Barracuda X represents the fourth major revision of Matsunaga's signature design, taking the foundational Barracuda geometry into bi-metal territory. Constructed from 7075 high-strength aluminum with stainless steel rims for extreme rim-weight distribution, the use of 7075 alloy — rather than the more common 6061 — provides improved strength-to-weight ratio, allowing thinner walls for more precisely placed mass. Limited quantities were sold at the 2019 US National Yo-Yo Contest before wider retail release.

title: Baryon
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Baryon is the special 6th anniversary yoyofriends yoyo. It has compact size with no compromises in performance.Following the footstep of the Vulture, Baryon features a 15g+ stainless steel inner ring that adds power and stability even in its compact form. Baryon is the everyday carry that can handle all you tricks with ease.

Baryon is a composite subatomic particle. Which aligns with the size of the yoyo. Baryon also participates in strong interaction, the strongest of the four fundamental forces. This aligns perfectly with the performance of the yoyo.Finally as a thank you to the yoyo community for the amazing support, Baryon's pricing is as low as possible. Cheers to yoyofriends 6th anniversary and cheers to more years to come!"

title: Basilisk
content:
From ZGRT:

"Basilisk lizards are proficient water runners that defy gravity, regularly dashing across bodies of water to evade predators. Studies have shown that static stability during locomotion is possible only when the center of mass remains within a theoretical region of stability. Running across a highly yielding surface could move the center of mass beyond the edges of the region of stability, potentially leading to tripping or falling.

They produce greatest support and propulsive forces that play with their body weight that dynamically stabilize them while running on water.

We wanted to recreate the qualities of this amazing lizard into a yoyo and came up with a very agile but powerful throw made out of 7003 aluminum.

The aluminum used in this throw allowed us to design thinner walls and to bring that weight in key areas to improve performance and stability.

We wanted this yoyo to be capable to perform as many tricks as possible, and just for added fun, we added a fingerspin hub, that in our opinion, is a beauty!

The Basilisk has a stylized V-shape with an almost unoticeable concave feature that brings more comfort to the hand and helps pushing few grams towards the rims."

title: Basilisk-D
content:
From ZGRT:

"One of the main characteristics of the first version of Basilisk was its traditional V-shape with a hint of U-shape that allowed moving some weight towards the rims and, at the same time, reduced friction between the string and cup.

The new Basilisk-D keeps such characteristic and its incredible finger spin capability. The dimensions of the finger spin hub and the shape remain identical. The two additional features we added this time are stainless steel rims and size D bearing.

One of the additional benefits that the stainless steel rims bring is having a wider cup area which facilitates finger spinning even more."

title: BassBoost
content: BassBoost was an early Double-Take Industries metal yo-yo designed and manufactured by Mike Montgomery. It was publicly documented in May 2010 and reached retail production after several design revisions. The name and cup-inspired form referenced a pair of subwoofers.The best-documented final revision, commonly called BassBoost V2, reduced weight and removed an inner-rim-grind lip to address vibration seen in earlier prototypes. It used Double-Take Industries’ square O-ring “Onion Ring” response. Exact production dimensions, alloy, bearing, axle, colorways, and launch price have not been recovered.

title: Bastet 2

title: Bully
content: History / AboutBig Brother Yo-Yos was created in January 2009 by Douglas Spence (Prototypeguy) in Woodbury, Minnesota, per the YoYo Wiki, and the Yo-Yo Museum describes it as an obscure, short-lived boutique brand. The Bully was its first yo-yo, with an angular profile and large spikes. The wiki lists it as a butterfly of 53 mm diameter, 42 mm width and 68 g with a size C bearing and flowable silicone response.

title: Juvenile Offender
content: History / AboutThe Juvenile Offender (JO) was reviewed by users in July and November 2010. One reviewer lists a diameter of 55.90 mm, width of 44.00 mm, gap of 4.50 mm, a weight of 69.5 g, a size C bearing and flowable silicone response, and describes its anodized finish and spiked edges used for matador tricks. The YoYo Wiki lists it among Big Brother's models.

title: Swirly
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Swirly among Big Brother Yo-Yos models. Forum posts describe it as a distinctively shaped yo-yo, now discontinued, with silicone response that can become unresponsive when damaged.

title: TT
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the TT among the Big Brother Yo-Yos models. A forum thread asking about the TT and Wedgie suggests they were announced around the time of the Bully, before they were available to buy. No specifications could be verified.

title: Wedgie
content: History / AboutThe Wedgie was the second release from Big Brother Yo-Yo Company (Douglas Spence). The YoYo Wiki lists a butterfly with a 50 mm diameter, 39 mm width, 65 g and a size A bearing. The Yo-Yo Museum describes a version made for the June 2009 Oklahoma State Yo-Yo championship, one of two, in 6065 aluminum with rubber O-rings; other editions used flowable silicone response.
