Released in January 2016, the Blizzard is Andrew Maider's first signature model and the first bimetal yo-yo from Caribou Lodge. Designed in close collaboration between Maider and CLYW owner Chris Mikulin, the Blizzard pairs an aluminum body with stainless steel rims for a light, fast, and powerful competition-oriented throw. The design draws aesthetic inspiration from the Arctic Circle 2 while delivering a distinctly modern string feel.

title: Bonfire
content: AboutThe Bonfire is the full-sized spiritual successor to the Campfire (2009), designed by Chris Mikulin and released in March 2014. A V-shaped organic profile aimed at flowing, intuitive play over competition performance. It became one of CLYW's longest-running and most beloved models, remaining in continuous production as of 2025. Current retail: $84.99–$90. A bimetal variant, the Wildfire, was released in April 2019.Current ColorwaysBerry Maple Drip, Mandarin Maple Drip, City of Champions, Forever Summer, Ferdico Fade.

title: Borealis
content: AboutThe Borealis is Zach Gormley's third CLYW signature, released December 15, 2015. It is the yo-yo Gormley used to win the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest in Tokyo — and it was designed entirely to his personal specifications, making it one of the most player-driven designs in CLYW's catalog. H-shape. Released alongside the Orca (Harrison Lee's signature).ColorwaysDugong, Sarsaparilla, Hulk Smash, Clareview Station Blizzard, Frozen Mammoth.

title: BOY
content: AboutBOY is the first CLYW signature for Ayumu Harada, released December 17–18, 2019. Described by CLYW as the "next evolution of the Arctic Circle family" — drawing from Zach Gormley's wide, powerful, floaty design lineage while being refined and adapted for Harada's distinct technical style. Mid-sized at 56mm, with a 44.5mm width and a centering bearing for modern unresponsive play.

title: Campfire
content: AboutThe Campfire was CLYW's smallest metal yo-yo at the time of its release (~2009–2010). At 48mm diameter it was designed as a compact, fun throw rather than a competition piece — a concept Chris Mikulin revisited years later with the full-sized Bonfire (2014), which shares design DNA and naming. The Campfire was short-lived in the lineup but is notable as the seed of one of CLYW's best-loved models.

title: Canopy PC
content: AboutThe Canopy PC is a collaboration between Caribou Lodge and Atmos Projects, currently in production. An oversized polycarbonate throw at 58.7mm × 49.1mm, weighing 68.2g — a large but surprisingly nimble design. Uses 19mm slim pads rather than CLYW's Snow Tires, reflecting Atmos's design input. $50 retail. Colorways: Black and Clear.

title: Canvas
content: AboutThe Canvas is Jensen Kimmitt's second signature model (following the Wooly Marmot), released around 2011. Named for the flat, slightly concave face profile that CLYW used as a literal canvas for painted and anodized artwork — making it the brand's most aesthetically expressive model at the time. Features a novel response area with a V-groove separating high wall from low wall. A "Final Edition" was released in October 2013, marking the end of production. At 54.61mm it sits between CLYW's undersized and full-sized offerings.

title: Chief
content: AboutThe Chief is CLYW's bestselling and most iconic model. Released in 2011, its prototype was rejected in 2010 before the design was refined. The defining feature is a distinctive extra inner groove that redistributes rim weight closer to the center of the body, striking a balance between power and maneuverability that competitors struggled to replicate. Drawing design cues from the Canvas and Avalanche, the Chief was kept in continuous production for years and re-released multiple times through the 2010s and 2020s.The Leaf (2022) is considered its spiritual successor, modestly widened and updated for modern play styles while preserving the Chief's character. The Chief arguably defined CLYW's second era — if the Peak established the brand, the Chief cemented it.Notable Colorways"28 Stories," "Clareview Station," "Hulk Smash," "Sasquatch Attack," "Salmon Fade," "Blueberry Cheesecake," and dozens more across its production history.

title: Cliff
content: AboutThe Cliff is the signature model for Czech & Slovak National Champion Petr Kavka, released in 2012 with a second run in February 2013. At 59.5mm diameter it is one of the largest yo-yos in CLYW's history — an oversized competition throw designed around Kavka's preference for powerful, stable performance. Kavka went on to have two more CLYW signatures: the Scout and Advance Scout (2014).

title: Compass
content:
History / About
Released December 2016, the Compass is Petr Kavka's signature model — his first with Caribou Lodge. Kavka, a multi-time European champion from the Czech Republic, collaborated with CLYW on a design that blends the DNA of the Chief, Bonfire, and Scout. The result emphasizes a super grinding surface for horizontal finger balancing, optimized rim weight, and an enhanced inner gap for extended spin time.

title: Ditch
content: AboutThe Ditch is CLYW's compact everyday carry metal, released in April 2022. At 50mm diameter it brings the Gorge's narrow high-wall silhouette concept down to pocket size — Chris Mikulin's description: "canyon → ditch." Full machined aluminum despite its tiny frame. Supports responsive play. $40–$50 retail, making it one of CLYW's most accessible metal options. Current colorways: Wolf Lake, Salmon Fade, Hulk Smash, Light Blue, Orange, Army Green, Horsehead Nebula.

title: Dune
content: AboutThe Dune is Anthony Rojas's first CLYW signature, released in February 2017. Named for CLYW's broader design philosophy of flowing organic shapes. At 68g it is one of the heavier models in the CLYW catalog, designed to provide Rojas with the power and stability his style demands. A Dune 2 was released in 2024–2025 with scaled-up dimensions and increased weight (69.4g).

title: Dune 2
content: AboutThe Dune 2 is Anthony Rojas's second CLYW signature, a scaled-up evolution of the original Dune (2017). Dimensions grow to 56.5mm × 44.4mm, and weight increases to 69.4g — making it one of the heavier throws in the current CLYW catalog. Designed for maximum power and stability to match Rojas's demanding style. $90–$95 retail. Colorways: Electric Bacon, Forever Summer.

title: Everyday
content: AboutThe Everyday is Steve Brown's second CLYW design — a responsive, slim pocket metal aimed at casual play and accessibility. At 54mm × 32.5mm it is narrow enough for slim-fit jeans and lightweight at 62.5g. Uses a half-spec bearing for a responsive (non-unresponsive) setup, making it approachable for players at any level. $40–$45 retail.A collab version with the punk rock band Hot Water Music was also produced at $45, featuring the band's fire/water logo anodized into the throw.

title: Glacier Express
content: AboutThe Glacier Express is a CLYW original model (non-signature) released in 2012, named after the famous Swiss train route. Its defining feature is a bold deep-carved undercut profile — aggressive machining that enhances both aesthetics and spin time by pushing rim weight outward while maintaining a relatively compact footprint. Described at launch as "small on the mid-sized end, but with unbelievable power." Re-released in 2024 with a new production run and current colorways (Salmon Fade, Tiffany Mint, Coffee Splash, Murky Summertide). Current retail: $75.99.

title: Gnarwhal
content: AboutThe Gnarwhal was CLYW's attempt to synthesize the best characteristics of the Bassalope, Bear vs. Man, and Wooly Marmot into a single undersized package. Released in 2010, it shares design DNA across those three earlier models while standing apart with its own weight distribution. Named for the narwhal. Succeeded by the Gnarwhal 2 in November 2013, which expanded both diameter and width for improved performance while retaining the undersized character.

title: Gnarwhal 2
content: AboutThe Gnarwhal 2 is the redesigned successor to the Gnarwhal, released November 22, 2013. The update added approximately 1mm in diameter and 5mm in width over the original while retaining the undersized character that defined the model. The additional width improved weight distribution and gave the catch zone a more forgiving profile. Released alongside the Arctic Circle 2 on the same date.

title: Gorge
content: AboutThe Gorge is a Chris Mikulin–designed CLYW original released in December 2016. An oversized bimetal at 59.5mm with a narrower-than-usual profile at 38.3mm, it deliberately evokes early round/high-wall yo-yo design language while using steel ring bimetal construction for modern performance. The narrow width combined with oversized diameter creates an unusual power-to-agility balance. The Ditch (2022) revisits this silhouette concept at a compact 50mm diameter.

title: H5 × Chief
content: AboutThe H5 × Chief is a collaboration between Caribou Lodge Yo-Yo Works and C3yoyodesign. C3 contributed the H5 body profile and manufacturing; CLYW contributed the double-rim treatment from the Chief. The resulting yo-yo combines C3's oversized H-shape with CLYW's signature weight distribution approach. The packaging featured a panda (C3's mascot) and a grizzly (CLYW) giving each other a high-five. A collector's piece from both brands' collaborative period.

title: Igloo
content:
History / About
Released November 2016, the Igloo is Michael Kurti's debut signature return top and the second bimetal from Caribou Lodge. Designed closely with CLYW owner Chris Mikulin, it takes a BVM2-inspired profile and fuses it with a powerful bimetal construction engineered for the longest spins and maximum stability. The Igloo was built to handle extended, demanding trick combinations at the highest competitive level.

title: Klondike
content: AboutThe Klondike is a collaboration between Caribou Lodge and SUS YOYO MECHANICS, released July 27, 2023. Based on the Wildfire design with a W-shape / inverted profile, stainless steel rings are added for heightened hardness and competition performance. Produced in collaboration with SUS YOYO MECHANICS (not currently in the archive). From $124.99.ColorwaysClareview Station with Blue Rings, Bip Bop!!, Hulk Smash, Tiffany Mint.

title: Kodiak
content: AboutThe Kodiak is the signature model for Tessa Piccillo, 2014 Women's World Champion and CLYW team member (and drummer of the band Badvril). Released as a bimetal on October 15, 2016, it was CLYW's first bimetal signature model, drawing design cues from the Manatee and Arctic Circle. The 2023 monometal re-release reworked the design with modified specs, removing the steel rings and adjusting the aluminum body for a lighter, more accessible throw.Current ColorwaysConfetti Cannon, Hulk Smash, Clareview Station, Clear. From $90 current retail.

title: Leaf
content: AboutThe Leaf is considered the spiritual successor to the Chief (2011) — CLYW's all-time bestselling model. The update is deliberately minimal: slightly increased width, a different hub profile, and a subtle weight redistribution for more contemporary play feel, while preserving the Chief's fundamental character. From $84.99–$85 retail.A collab variant, the Maple Leaf ($130), was released in collaboration with Crucial, combining Crucial's manufacturing expertise with the Leaf profile and featuring a Crucial Bearing v3.Current ColorwaysClareview Station, Hulk Smash, Deep Purple, Root Beer.

title: Manatee
content: AboutThe Manatee is the first signature model for Riccardo Fraolini, debuted at the Bay Area Classic on June 16, 2016. Two firsts for CLYW: the widest full-sized throw in the catalog at the time, and the first CLYW full-sized model at a budget price point (~$65 vs. the typical $115+ for metal). Also one of the first CLYW models manufactured in China rather than Canada. Step-straight shape with an extremely wide profile for a massive catch zone — Fraolini's stated goal was consistency for "nearly impossible tricks." Succeeded by the Minitee (2023), which shrank the diameter while expanding the width even further.

title: Maple Leaf
content: AboutThe Maple Leaf is a collaboration between Caribou Lodge and Crucial, applying Crucial's manufacturing approach to the Leaf profile. Specs are similar to the Leaf but uses a Crucial Bearing v3 and is 64g (68g capped). At $130 it is priced above the standard Leaf, reflecting the collab production and Crucial's contribution. Colorways: 28 Stories, Pure, Hulk Smash.

title: Metal Yeti
content:
History / About
Released in January 2019, the Metal Yeti is Caribou Lodge's aluminum reimagining of the Yeti line — their most challenging project ever. After two plastic iterations, CLYW decided the shape and feel were too good to abandon and returned to precision metal manufacturing. The result preserves everything players loved about the Yeti's distinctive feel while delivering the smoothness and performance of a machined aluminum return top. Released alongside the Akita.

title: Minitee
content: AboutThe Minitee is Riccardo Fraolini's second CLYW signature (following the Manatee, 2016), released in August 2023. Where the Manatee was already unusually wide, the Minitee takes the concept to an extreme: the diameter is shrunk to 44mm while the width is expanded to 50mm, making it wider than its own diameter. The oversized catch zone concept is preserved — but now in a pocket-sized package. Designed in Canada, manufactured in China. $60–$80 retail.ColorwaysSnowcone Fade, Horsehead Nebula, Dark Blue, Deep Purple.

title: Orca
content: AboutThe Orca is the first signature model for Harrison Lee, released in late 2015 alongside the Borealis. Shares the Avalanche's basic profile but with added width — at 45mm it is 2mm wider than the Avalanche while matching diameter nearly exactly. A stable, flowing model suited to Lee's style. Harrison Lee's second signature, the Otter (2021), evolved the Orca concept with a 1mm diameter reduction and collaboration input from Jeffrey Pang.

title: Otter
content: AboutThe Otter is Harrison Lee's second CLYW signature (following the Orca, 2015), released in April 2021. Co-developed with Jeffrey Pang, it retains the Orca's shape, weight, and width but drops 1mm in diameter for a more precise feel. Lee is a 3× Canadian National Champion. Designed in Canada, manufactured in China. CLYW described it as "fat, comfy, beefy and stable enough for average humans to complete ~45% of Harrison's tricks." Current retail: from $89.99.

title: Peak 2
content: AboutThe Peak 2 was released December 19, 2016 to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the original Peak (2006). The silhouette is faithful to the original, but the bearing seat, response area, and weight distribution were redesigned for smoother, floatier play befitting modern technique. A second production batch followed February 9, 2017. The Pixel Bearing — CLYW's proprietary centering bearing — made its debut here.Colorways28 Stories, Black Bip Bop, Ash Berry, Snow Cone, Confetti Cannon. ~$100–$115 at release.

title: Pickaxe
content: AboutThe Pickaxe is CLYW's undersized take on the Chief's double-rim design, released in 2018. At 52mm — significantly smaller than the competition-standard 55mm+ — it was designed for fun and casual play rather than competition performance. Where the Chief is a stage instrument, the Pickaxe is a pocket companion. Current retail $84.99; available in Orange, Dark Green, and Dark Blue.

title: Puffin
content: AboutThe Puffin is the first signature model for Palli Gudmundsson, the Icelandic champion, released around 2012–2013. It merges the organic peaked profile of the original Peak with the Chief's double inner rim design, creating an unusually wide catch zone at 46.9mm despite the moderate 54mm diameter. Succeeded by the Puffin 2 in January 2014, which featured a shortened hub for fingerspin tricks and a low response wall optimized for horizontal play. A further "new Puffin" re-release appeared in 2017.

title: Puffin 2
content: AboutThe Puffin 2 is Palli Gudmundsson's second signature, released January 24, 2014. Two key changes from the original Puffin: the hub was shortened to enable "grindwinder" fingerspin tricks, and the response wall was lowered and optimized for horizontal play. Dimensions are similar to the original but with these targeted refinements. Colorways include "28 Stories," "Salmon Fade," and "Hulk Smash."

title: Sasquatch
content: AboutThe Sasquatch is the signature model for Alex Berenguel, released in 2010. It sits at the larger end of the CLYW lineup at 55.48mm and is considered the direct forerunner to the Avalanche, sharing similar design philosophy with more rim weight and a faster, more powerful spin. Also released in a redesigned form in 2014 and again in 2022 as an oversized lighter throw. Colorways include "28 Stories," "Hulk Smash," and others from CLYW's colorway palette.

title: Scout
content: AboutThe Scout is Petr Kavka's second CLYW signature (following the Cliff), released in November 2014. It introduced a notable first: CLYW's "Advance Scout" — a limited production run of the exact prototype versions Kavka used to win the 2014 Czech & Slovak National Championship. Only 214 of the planned 300 Advance Scout units were made available, and CLYW stated they would never be remade, making them among the most sought-after CLYW limited releases. The regular Scout is the production-refined version released to the wider market.

title: Swan
content: AboutThe Swan is the first signature model for Michael Ferdico (CLYW team member and drummer of Badvril), released November 14, 2024. Inspired by the Manatee silhouette — CLYW's wide-catch-zone design — but at a compact 52mm diameter with steel rings for bimetal construction. Designed for "tight maneuvers and intricate string tricks." From $124.99.ColorwaysFire Blizzard, Gold with Black Rings, Zach Gormley Edition, Maiderade Fade.

title: Wildfire
content: AboutThe Wildfire is CLYW's first bimetal based on the Bonfire silhouette, released April 25, 2019. Where the Bonfire is a flowing organic, the Wildfire is engineered for competition — body weight is carved out and redistributed to the stainless steel outer rims for maximum spin stability. Prototypes were sent to the 2018 World Championship in Shanghai. The result is a lighter, more powerful throw that retains the Bonfire's familiar profile.

title: Wish
content: AboutThe Wish is Zach Gormley's fifth CLYW signature (preceded by Arctic Circle, AC2, Borealis, and Big Dipper), released in 2020–2021. A bimetal — 6061 body with stainless steel rings — but uniquely mid-ship weighted rather than rim-heavy, giving it a floaty character unusual for bimetal construction while retaining the power of steel rim weighting. Gormley used it at the 2020 Japan Yo-Yo Cup International Online. Current retail: from $124.99.ColorwaysSalmon Fade, Frozen Mammoth, Hulk Smash, Gold with Black Rings, and more.

title: Wooly Marmot
content: AboutThe Wooly Marmot is the first signature model for Jensen Kimmitt, released in 2009. Kimmitt's performance with it at the 2010 World Yo-Yo Contest in Prague — where he won the 1A title — brought both him and CLYW to global prominence. Undersized at 50.26mm, with a silhouette sharing design DNA with the Peak but optimized for Jensen's fast, technical style. The "28 Stories" colorway became one of the most recognizable anodizations in the hobby.SuccessorThe Wooly Marmot 2 (2014) expanded the dimensions while preserving the undersized character. Jensen's Canvas (2011) was his second signature.

title: Wooly Marmot 2
content: AboutThe Wooly Marmot 2 is the redesigned Wooly Marmot, released in 2014. Like the Gnarwhal 2 update, it added 1.4mm in diameter and 5mm in width over the original while deliberately preserving the undersized feel that defined Jensen Kimmitt's play style. New colorways included Northern Lights, 28 Stories, and Hulk Smash. Jensen's previous signatures were the Wooly Marmot (2009) and Canvas (2011).

title: Yeti
content: AboutThe Yeti was CLYW's first plastic yo-yo, released in 2013 and discontinued by 2015. An oversized polycarbonate throw at 58.75mm, it brought CLYW's design sensibility to an accessible $45 price point — dramatically below the brand's metal lineup. Discontinued in 2015; the Yeti 2.0 (2016) followed with a refined plastics formulation addressing issues with the original mold. Notable as the proof-of-concept that CLYW could produce a viable plastic.

title: Yeti 2
content: AboutThe Yeti 2 is the redesigned successor to the original Yeti (2013), released in 2016. The original Yeti was discontinued in 2015; the Yeti 2 addresses known issues with the original polycarbonate formulation and mold, producing a more consistent and durable throw. Specs are largely similar to the original Yeti. CLYW's continuation of accessible plastic at the ~$45 price point.

title: Carp
content:
About
The Carp reimagines yoyofriends' popular Koi design using machined polycarbonate for a more approachable, everyday yo-yo. The rounded silhouette carries over directly from the Koi, with no sharp edges to catch against during a catch. Construction combines a polycarbonate body and cap with a 6061 aluminum core and spacer, landing at 66.66g to offset the natural power loss from moving away from metal.

title: Carpfin
content:
About
Carpfin is a full-size monometal yoyo with a wide-arc trapeze profile at over 90% max width, built as an affordable performance model.

title: Cascade
content:
From One Drop

"Our new yo-yo, the Cascade, had some interesting design goals: Wide, Curvy/Organic, Mid-Size (53 mm), Side Effects

It went through three different iterations. Version 1 was a source of contention here at the shop. Everyone disagreed about liking it and some vigorous debate took place. However, we did all agree that it needed changes but we were on the verge of scrapping it.

Justin "Vendetta" Lotempio was visiting us at the time and convinced us to at least try a revision. Version 2 was much improved and everyone agreed it was an awesome yo-yo that really felt and played different.

Mark Montgomery really liked it and suggested a couple of small tweaks which resulted in version 3. For this revision we smoothed out some areas of the cup and added a touch of rim weight. We went to production with version 3 and are really excited to get this beautiful yo-yo out into the world. It ships with Dome Side Effects."

title: Case File 001
content:
History / About
Case File 001 is an experimental yoyo featuring a fingerspin dimple similar to Mike Marshall's previous signature model, and using G2's undercut design to shift center weight toward the rim for improved playability. Released Friday, May 26, 2017 at 5pm EST as a strictly one-run-and-done item.

title: Case File 002
content:
History / About
The 002 is a big organic yoyo with an undercut and fingerspin dimple, a team favorite. Machined in China; anodized, assembled, and tested in Ohio. Released as a strict one-time run via two windows on Wednesday, October 18, 2017 — a primary 6pm EST release plus an unannounced mystery drop later that evening. 50/50 swaps were not offered.

title: Case File 003
content:
History / About
Case File 003 is an undersized stepped organic bimetal, described by G2 as the most unique of the finger-spin-focused Case File yoyos. 100 units were produced; roughly 70 passed QC. Deep Purple and Steel colorways released Thursday at 8pm EDT following the announcement, joining an earlier Royal Blue contest-exclusive colorway and a fourth colorway released later that summer.

title: Catalyst
content: AboutCatalyst is a 50/50 blend of invisible nylon and Maxi-Lock stretch nylon in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Bouncy disposition and brisk velocity with a lasting shelf life and soft feel — a responsive, lively string suited to fast, dynamic play. Available in Azurite, Red Mercury, and Luteolin colorways alongside monocolor.

title: Celestial IX
content: History / AboutPhysical evolution of Stellar IX using 7075, a polycarbonate middle ring, and stainless outer rim in a large ultra-wide competition format.

title: Cenote
content:
One of Turner Return Tops' most popular releases, the Cenote has seen two production runs, the first released on September 15, 2023 and the second released on July 12, 2024.

The currently released colorways are as follows:

Sugar Sand (Micro Arc Oxidation aka Moon Rock)

Secrets of the Seas (Blue with limited art series engravings)

Clear

Beach Sand (with "I Spy" engraving)

Red (with Hibiscus engraving)

BRO Splash (Blue-Ringed Octopus)

Final Frontier (Black with limited art series engravings)

title: Centrifugal
content:
From Motion:

"Our second installment - Centrifugal (motion). Continuing off of the success of our flagship yoyo, Perpetual (motion), we have stayed true to what we said we would do: never compromise aesthetics for performance, and vice versa.

In designing this yoyo we decided that “less is more.” We wanted a very smooth body with minimal cuts. From each angle you will be able to see the calculated and distinct cuts we wanted on this yoyo.

We aren’t the first, or only company to use a dome in the cup, but we feel like this is a design aspect that truly catches your eye. Lastly something very unique to our yoyo is, once again, the rims. The large W shape has a very pronounced inverted M shape on the outer surface, which not only strengthens the SS rim and helps to keep from bending, but it also retains a “slimmer” feel in the hand without compromising any of the weight used to push on the outermost part of the yoyo.

We really think through each design to not only appeal to serious players, but to also give a timeless piece you could display on your shelf.

This is Motion."

First Run (Q2 2022):

68 yoyos were made in production, in 4 colorways:

18 BiFröst

18 Adeline's Jewel

14 Ice Bow + 3 extra*

18 Slytherim

* 3 extra Ice Bow were later obtained from the factory and were distributed to the community for pay-it-forward, a giveaway, and to reviewers.

Second Run (Q3 2023):

27 Dark Side of the Moon

40 Corliss's Inferno

title: Centrifugal 2 (Prototype)
content:
About
Centrifugal 2 (v2.0.2) is an in-development second-generation revisit of Motion's earlier Centrifugal model, marked "Prototyped" only on the brand's timeline, with no retail-release evidence found. Distinct name from the original Centrifugal already in the archive.

title: Centripetal
content:
From Motion:

"Say Hello to Centripetal (Motion)

Centrifugal was one of the most popular YoYo designs we have done, and over here at Motion we do things a little backwards from most brands. We typically focus a majority of our products toward the bi-metal market, however, we have been exploring the mono metal designs much deeper.

When we release a mono metal yoyo we want the characteristics to not only reflect Motions characteristics but also perform at the highest levels of anything else available In the market.

At Motion we are enthusiasts first and sales last, when we make a product we want that product to fill a specific gap somewhere. Centripetal does just that.

So what inspired the design?

The design was inspired largely by Centrifugal.

There are some traits on this YoYo that we wanted to achieve, as always, and aesthetics can never be ignored and need to remain just as closely tied to performance.

The YoYo is designed in a way that the rim weight is not compromised by being a mono-metal design, we were able to manipulate the body to not only carry similar rim to body ratio as the bi-metal model it was designed after but also give a similar feel.

What actually transpired was a mono-metal version of the YoYo that surpassed its bi-metal counterpart. The double rim design helps balance some mid-weight while the overhanging rim allows for functional thumb grinds and extra weight on the furthest point of the YoYo but moved down closer to the center.

Wider yo-yos have become more of a trend in the last few years and Centripetal is no exception, while broadening the gap and effective trapeze width of the YoYo you will find the characteristics of much wider yo-yos while maintaining a manageable width for hand feel. The overall delivery you will find is unsurpassed in the Motion lineup to this point.

We wanted to make sure that our second monometal YoYo was as large of a hit as the first one, and we think this design is about as close to perfect for the shape as it gets."

title: Cephas
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

After months of teasing, we’re thrilled to finally present the Cephas.

SPECS

Dia 54.3mmWidth 48.4mmWeight 65.2gMaterial 6061 AL

In case you’ve missed it, we wrote a bit about our Design Lines as of 2023 — in short, they represent different design pursuits in what we do here at Atmos Projects.

To that point, the Cephas is the newest installment to the Classic O’s line, which collectively focuses on minimalist organics, and is the latest iteration of the Noah and Abel.

Most immediately, the Cephas takes inspiration from forebears that share its flat capped visage. The foremost of the group is likely the SPYY Pure, which was released in 2009; the genre is also populated by others such as the Turning Point Bacchus, Core Co. Diesis, and most recently, the Duncan Freebird 3. The SPYY Pure in particular holds sway in the conversation for its unique manufacturing processes. As far as we know, the hub and the cap were separately machined, assembled, and then further machined on the lathe to render the already microscopic gap between the individual pieces invisible. This gave the Pure — very aptly named, we think — an iconic uninterrupted, solid-piece look.

The designs of the Bacchus, Diesis and Freebird 3, on the other hand, emphasize the point of assembly, rather than hide it. The “rims”, which encroach on the main body, somewhat resemble the Yoyojam-era of hybrids, or even how modern outer-rim bimetal rims look like.

Our intent with the Cephas was to recreate this former sense of purity and minimalism within our organic form factor. 

In the prior designs mentioned, none featured a strictly organic silhouette – their inner walls feature straight lines extending towards the rims, even if the outer hubs eventually rounded off. Where the flat caps provided a simple, austere look, the side profiles were slightly busier, with harder lines and faux rims.

We were compelled by the notion of an extremely round, organic model combined with the simplicity of a flat cap feature, with no visual hints at joinery, or discontinuation between body and rims – the Cephas thus builds on the Noah and Abel’s physique, which features clean lines and round, uninterrupted curves, and the integration of its capped design gives it a monolithic, solid feel.

But beyond mere visual difference, a thicker, more powerful, hollowed-body version of the Noah and Abel was, to us, an interesting marriage of different design concepts.

The cap conceals the hub, the primary site where we overhauled the base weight distributions of previous designs. To begin, we carved out mass from the center portion of the hub, giving it a cavernous hollowed-out body, and also to allow for a disproportionate concentration of mass closer to the rims.

The Cephas weighs in at 65.2g, which is the heaviest of the Classic O’s line — the Abel clocks only 63.2g, and the Noah an even lighter 62.3g. A majority of this additional mass lies in the caps, which actually weigh 8g each — that’s about a quarter of its overall weight in the caps alone. 

The effect of this adjustment is obvious – where there was nearly zero bias towards rim weight in the Noah and the Abel, this new weight distribution makes the Cephas the longest spinning and most stable installment of the Classic O’s.

This is assisted by a familiar schmoove-groove, which is less pronounced than those in the Fruitbowl Line. We made minor tweaks in the Cephas’ schmoove-groove for an even smoother play experience.

It still feels bubbly and extremely comfortable in hand, and features a familiar relaxed, agile playfeel, but it also has a steadier, more even presence compared to its two brothers.

The Cephas sits in a lineup of featherweight organics characterized by light, floaty playfeel – and it distinguishes itself in that company by its solid, grounded presence. 

To that end, the name Cephas – etymologically connected to “Peter”, both of them loosely translating to “rock” – playfully overstates that relative heft. Where “Noah” gestured towards “rest”, and “Abel” towards “breath”, the name Cephas is a reference to its relative stability and solidity.

For those more literally inclined, don’t fret – it doesn’t actually play like a stone on the end of a string. 

The Cephas joins the Classic O’s as a perfect everyday throw, best suited for relaxed, flowing play, and provides enough power and stability for uncompromised hours of pure fun.

title: Cerberus
content: About the CerberusThe Cerberus is the signature model of Yoshi Mikamoto, featuring an above-average 59.63mm diameter that creates a wide and forgiving catch zone for high-difficulty string trick sequences. The Solid Spin Axle system and straight body profile with aluminum rims deliver competitive spin times. A championship edition was produced for the 2012 World YoYo Contest.

title: Chaku
content:
From Alchemik:

"Enter the Chaku–the signature model of Ty McClellan, perhaps better known as @beverchakus. Drawing inspiration from the 2010s, Ty set out to create the perfect 3A titanium throw, something with deliberate heft—stable, powerful, and built to hold its ground through the longest, most demanding combos.

Its 72.5-gram frame offers rock-solid stability without sacrificing flow. The finely machined inner ring grind cavity is unlike any IRG you’ve felt before, making thumb grinds simpler, smoother, and more stable. A Matador-style spike invites advanced maneuvers and adds a distinctive edge to its profile.

Every curve, cut, and gram of the Chaku reflects Ty’s approach to yo-yoing: confident, precise, and unapologetically bold. Whether you’re chasing clean, high-speed 3A tricks or savoring the feel of a throw that channels the best of a bygone era, the Chaku is ready to deliver.

title: Champion
content: HistoryThe Champion line was Cheerio's flagship wooden yo-yo, produced throughout the 1930s–1950s. Multiple variants exist, with some featuring decorative medallions and gold-leaf finishes. Highly sought by collectors.

title: Champion Eagle Medallion
content: HistoryDecorative variant of the Champion line featuring an embedded eagle medallion. Produced around 1950, these models are now highly collectible and rarely appear on the market.

title: Hardwood Yo-Yo (The Art of Yo)
content: History / AboutChannel Craft of Charleroi, Pennsylvania makes authentic American toys, games and puzzles and offers a vintage-style maple wood yo-yo. According to YoYo Wiki, the yo-yo can be customized with a buyer-chosen logo for corporate use, and each comes in an individual clear display with 'The Art of Yo' history and trick booklet. The Yo-Yo Museum documents a 2024 example bought at the Sundance Mountain Resort gift shop: a three-piece (two halves plus axle) hard rock maple, book-matched and balanced, with a clear finish and 100% cotton string, with an unmarked body and a 16-page booklet dated 2009. Original retail price was $12.

title: Charm
content:
History / About
The Charm is Recess's 2018 competition bimetal, distinguished from the Weekend and Vacation by using inner-fitted stainless steel rings rather than outer rim placement. The broad inner rings provide precise weight distribution that creates a light feel on the string with a seriously powerful spin — capable of carrying through any competitive routine effortlessly. At 55.10mm diameter and 46.70mm wide, it is noticeably wider than the Weekend and Vacation, giving it a modern, generous catch zone. The "lucky charm" naming follows Recess's fun theme. Tyler Severance announced it in a Recess blog post on February 12, 2018 with the note: "Charm is the perfect yo-yo for all situations."

title: Charon
content: AboutThe Charon is JIGUN's oversized aluminum competition throw, released in 2025 at $85. At 71mm diameter and 78.5g, it uses a longer M4 × 16mm axle to accommodate the oversized body. Available in White.

title: Chaser
content: About the ChaserThe Chaser features an inverse-round body shape — YoYoJam's first — that reduces string-to-body friction for cleaner trick execution. An internal aluminum weight ring boosts spin momentum while the Solid Spin Axle system allows gap adjustment between responsive and bind play. Designed with input from Hiroyuki Suzuki, it prioritizes speed and efficiency.

title: Cheatcode
content: AboutThe Cheatcode is co-designed by Brandon Vu and Jeffrey Pang (Luftverk). Its defining feature is the Auto Orientation Technology: a Delrin (POM) fingerspin cap with an angled dimple that gyroscopically forces the yo-yo into fingerspin position regardless of the angle it is contacted. It eliminates the precision required for traditional fingerspins, making the trick accessible at any skill level while remaining competition-ready for advanced players. Developed after extensive field testing with competitive players, available in eight colorways.

title: Crown Royal
content: History / AboutChemtoy was a yo-yo manufacturer based in Cicero, Illinois. The YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's Collector's Guide to 20th Century Yo-Yos, says it produced three plastic, unpromoted yo-yos and that all were blister packed with a 1972 copyright date. The Yo-Yo Museum says Chemtoy was founded in the 1940s by Henry and Stanley Cohen in Chicago, began with bubble solution and bubble toys, licensed a Chemtoy Shark for the 1975 film Jaws, and was later acquired by the Strombecker Corporation. The Crown Royal, model 2072, dates from 1972-1974 per the museum and was Chemtoy's top-of-the-line model. It has a classic tournament-shaped translucent dark-green plastic body with the name and logo hot-stamped in gold foil, a metal fixed axle, starburst response and a cotton string. It was sold shrink-wrapped on a card for an original retail price of $1.

title: Mark V
content: History / AboutChemtoy was a yo-yo manufacturer based in Cicero, Illinois. The YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's Collector's Guide to 20th Century Yo-Yos, says it produced three plastic, unpromoted yo-yos and that all were blister packed with a 1972 copyright date. The Yo-Yo Museum says Chemtoy was founded in the 1940s by Henry and Stanley Cohen in Chicago, began with bubble solution and bubble toys, licensed a Chemtoy Shark for the 1975 film Jaws, and was later acquired by the Strombecker Corporation. The Yo-Yo Museum lists the Mark V as model 2071, a 1970s U.S. model and one of the other two models in Chemtoy's lineup alongside the Crown Royal. No specifications are recorded.

title: Number 1
content: History / AboutChemtoy was a yo-yo manufacturer based in Cicero, Illinois. The YoYo Wiki, citing Lucky Meisenheimer's Collector's Guide to 20th Century Yo-Yos, says it produced three plastic, unpromoted yo-yos and that all were blister packed with a 1972 copyright date. The Yo-Yo Museum says Chemtoy was founded in the 1940s by Henry and Stanley Cohen in Chicago, began with bubble solution and bubble toys, licensed a Chemtoy Shark for the 1975 film Jaws, and was later acquired by the Strombecker Corporation. The Yo-Yo Museum lists the Number 1 as model 2070, giving the era as the 1950s, while the YoYo Wiki says the company's yo-yos are from the late 1970s with a 1972 copyright. No specifications are recorded.

title: Chik!
content:
From One Drop:

"This is the signature yoyo of Igor Korzhev. When we asked Igor what he wanted for his signature yoyo, he gave us the following criteria: similar to the Burnside, add Side Effects and ship with spikes, make it lighter, add some Projection Profile grooves, competition ready.

This is now our largest diameter Side Effect yoyo. The Projection Profile was placed in the middle facet of the catch zone - just in the correct spot for finger grinds. The play is stable and smooth."

title: Chiyome
content:
History / About
An early-release model sold physically at the World Yo-Yo Contest (WYYC) 2026. Sengoku's own store lists it as "product for sale physically at WYYC 2026 — online release and retail price TBA." Named for Mochizuki Chiyome, a historical female ninja (kunoichi) leader of the Sengoku period — a notable naming departure from the brand's usual convention of naming models after male warlords.

title: Chocolate Mint
content:
History / About
Chocolate Mint reassembles into a replica chocolate-mint-ice-cream shape when disassembled/inverted. The product copy mentions, as an aside, a historical Akagi Dairy x Shin Ultraman ice cream promotion the designer once ate — this is flavor-text trivia, not an actual collaboration or licensing tie for the yoyo itself. Sold in recurring summer-limited lots, most recently May 20 - September 30, 2026.

title: Chopsticks Gorilla
content: AboutThe Chopsticks Gorilla is the signature of Hirotaka Akiba, 2019 Japan 1A Champion. Akiba earned the nickname "Chopsticks Gorilla" for his extensive use of chopstick formations — a trick subcategory requiring precise, repeated string manipulation between the fingers. The 53.9mm × 43mm bi-metal, at 65.2g, is compact enough for the fast string transfers Akiba's style demands while delivering full bi-metal spin stability. A smaller sibling, the Chobi Gorilla, was released subsequently.

title: Chroma Slate
content:
The Chroma Slate is the first release from True arc.

The Prototype

The prototype for the Chroma Slate was released in February, 2024. There were 5 units produced in a "Slate Blue" colorway.

The Production Run

The Production run of the Chroma Slate was released on September 15th 2024 with 20 in "Void" and "Red Shift" colorways and 10 in "Blood Moon".

title: Ciel
content: AboutThe Ciel is a Delrin offstring designed to meet the needs of offstring players at every level. At 2g heavier than comparable JT models, it spins more powerfully and stably. A standout feature is its adjustable return spacing — replaceable spacers sold separately allow players to tune the response feel. Colorways include Red/Black Hub, White/Hot Pink Hub, and White/Gray Core.

title: Hero
content:
About the Hero
The Hero was Circle City YoYos' step up to 7075-T6 aluminum for their second release (~2019), giving the throw a more competition-oriented feel relative to the 6061 debut Muse. The design features a large dimpled cup area optimized for finger spins and a substantial inner-ring grind (IRG) contact surface. A limited 2019 Worlds Edition Gold/Purple Fade colorway was released in conjunction with the World Yo-Yo Contest that year.
Multiple forum reviewers cited the Hero as one of the smoothest throws they had encountered in its price range. The package includes a Lifeline string and a zippered pouch.

title: Muse
content:
About the Muse
The Muse was Circle City YoYos' inaugural release, launched September 1, 2018 — the brand's first day in business. Founded in Indianapolis, Indiana by a hobbyist known as Bradd, Circle City named the throw after the Greek Muses; each of the three colorways is named for a specific muse and represents someone significant in Bradd's life. The design philosophy was to blend an old-school organic feel with contemporary competitive geometry, resulting in a smooth 6061 aluminum monometal suited to players across skill levels.
Lifeline Strings partnered with Circle City to offer a Muse bundle pairing the yo-yo with ten Radioactive strings. Community reception was warmly positive, with reviewers praising the throw's smoothness and approachable feel. Each Muse shipped with a pouch.

title: Odium
content:
About the Odium
The Odium is Circle City YoYos' fifth and final documented release, a full signature model for team rider Cody Diehl. It uses 7068 aluminum — the same alloy as the Warhawk P40's body — in a monometal design sitting in diameter between the smaller Warbird and larger Hero. Diehl's aesthetic influence is visible throughout: the six colorway names lean into adversarial vocabulary (Abhor, Rancor, Enmity, Ire), and each colorway uses acidwash, etch, or splash anodizing finishing. The package includes Bad Wolfe Co strings and Badwolf stickers.
The Odium appears to be Circle City's last release before the brand went on extended hiatus; the official website subsequently went offline. As the brand's concluding statement, it demonstrates continued investment in premium alloy choices and player-driven design.

title: Warbird
content:
About the Warbird
The Warbird was Circle City's first player-signature release, conceived in collaboration between team rider Kyle Pearson and machining specialist Nathan Joseph. It is smaller and lighter than the Muse and Hero, with a profile tuned for high-speed 1A competition play. The cup geometry was specifically engineered to create a seamless finger-spin catch zone, and the shape sits comfortably in the hand for extended sessions.
Colorway names — Yak-3 and A6M3 — honor World War II fighter aircraft, a theme the brand would carry forward into the bimetal Warhawk P40. The Warbird was machined from 7075-T6 aluminum and shipped in a zippered pouch. It was Circle City's third overall release.

title: Warhawk P40
content:
About the Warhawk P40
Named for the Curtiss P-40 Warhawk WWII fighter, the Warhawk P40 is Circle City YoYos' fourth release and their most technically ambitious design. It uses 7068 aluminum — a harder, stronger alloy than either 6061 or standard 7075 — paired with stainless steel rings for enhanced rim-weighting and extended spin time. The response is hand-poured flowable silicone, giving each unit individual character.
The package is unusually comprehensive: in addition to the yo-yo itself, each P40 includes two additional Size D bearings, .1mm and .2mm shims for gap tuning, a tube of extra flowable silicone, Bad Wolfe Co custom strings, and a custom Throwbags pouch. A YoYoSam-exclusive "Scrap Metal" colorway was released as a retail limited edition. Reviewers were highly positive; the Casual Throw review called it "tough to speak too highly of" and named it one of the best yo-yos of 2020.

title: Cirrus
content: AboutThe Cirrus is the signature model of Koyo Hashimoto, the 2024 Japan National 4A Champion. Released in 2024, it features a balanced shape and weight distribution designed to support customization via spacers, pads, and string combinations. JT describes it as suitable for beginners through competition-level play. Available in Red, Yellow, and White.

title: Citizen
content:
From One Drop:

"In 2010 we released our first titanium yo-yo, the Sovereign. Five years later we have tackled this amazing metal and produced a yo-yo that we feel is our best work to date: The Citizen.

A lot has changed in these 5 years. Yo-yos tend to be bigger than they used to be and high walls have gone by the wayside. As an industry and as a community we have all figured out what shapes, weights and weight distributions work better. As a yo-yo manufacturer we have improved our knowledge, skills and equipment an immense amount. All of these improvements played a role in the creation of the Citizen.

Titanium allowed us to take this shape and create a weight distribution simply not possible in aluminum; moving material to the rim while reducing overall weight. This gives it a light airy feel with incredibly long spin times.

Each Citizen was made with many hours of labor, love, and attention right here in-house in Eugene, Oregon, USA. Every single minute of machining was monitored, measured and scrutinized. Every half was hand polished. They have been checked, and re-checked. We could not have put more effort into assuring these were the most amazing yo-yos we could possibly make. There are one hundred and seventeen numbered Citizens in this run (there will not be another run)."

title: CLASHcube
content: AboutThe CLASHcube was designed around a single concept: 44mm. Diameter, width, and trapeze gap are all 44mm — a direct reference to the 44CLASH annual contest that yoyorecreation organizes in Yokohama. It also marked the brand's first use of a Size D bearing, making it one of very few YYR models to step outside the standard Size C spec. Distributed exclusively at the 2010 44CLASH event, the CLASHcube was never sold through retail channels and remains extremely rare among collectors.

title: Classic
content:
From Layer Infinity:

"Classic is a very simple return top reminiscent of the toys from a few decades ago.

It sleeps. It comes back with a tug. You can loop with it, if you're good enough. You can land it on a trapeze, if you're good enough.

Its aesthetic is inspired by vintage Russell yoyos. With a modern axle system, the two side caps can be detached and swapped for different colours and designs!

Classic shares its bearing and response system with its older brother Kasm, so it is compatible with everything in the Kasm parts kit (not included).

Special shoutout to the YoYo Boomers Club for suggesting the "Jazz" colourway (white/purple/teal) for those who miss the 90's 😂"

title: Clemency 2
content: AboutThe Clemency 2 is a unique all-aluminum design using contrasting-color 7075 rings against a 6061 body to achieve bi-metal-like stability at a lower cost than steel-ring designs. Fast play suitable for advanced tricks. Available in Silver/Green Rings, Green/Gold Rings, Black/Green Rings, Green/Red Rings, Blue/Gold Rings, Black/Green+Red Spade, Purple/Green Ring, Pink/Blue Rings, and Silver/Pink Ring.

title: Clique
content:
From One Drop:

"The goal:  Make the best mini unresponsive yo-yo we can using standard Flow Groove response and a standard C size bearing.  A mini is never expected to play quite as well as a full size so we wanted to see how close we could come. This is the Clique.

The challenge:  The reason most modern yo-yos end up with diameters in the range of 50-65mm is that anything outside of that range presents certain difficulties because play characteristics don’t scale.  However, these difficulties can be overcome. If you go bigger, the yo-yo tends to develop “kick back” and starts to move really slow and laggy. We feel we did a pretty good job manipulating the weight distribution with the Par Avion as it has minimal “kick back” and is actually quite nimble.   If you go smaller, you will either have a lighter yo-yo (possibly way too light), or you add thickness to make up the weight and then the yo-yo tends to feel like a rock on a string. One solution is to use a higher density material as a way of “hacking” the scaling problem - the increased density makes up for the lost weight.

The solution: For that reason, we choose 303 Stainless Steel.  Stainless is close to three times as dense as 6061 aluminum alloy.  This allows us to use a lot less material, but have the total weight be in the range where it still plays well.  We have also found the total weight should scale down a but from the standard range of 60-70 grams. For the Clique, the total assembled weight is 58.4 grams.

The finish is Stone Washed.

We will be releasing them in small batches and direct only from our site."
