Stay Sharp. Own Your Game - With CTRL"

title: Cura
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re proud to present — the Cura.

Our sophomore entry in our Artist Edition Line, the Cura is inspired by old school design, and takes its essence from In Hyeok Choi’s play philosophy that focuses on nostalgia, playfulness and joy.

Designed by In Hyeok Choi and Atmos Projects.

SPECS

Diameter 54.4mmWidth 43.2mmWeight 66.3gMaterial 6061 Aluminium

The Artist Edition is one of our favorite design lines to work on. The initial idea behind the lineup was to work with special players and individuals in the community to co-create designs that represented their unique philosophies, tastes, and ideas.

In December 2024, we released our first Artist Edition model — the Noma., in collaboration with Tsukasa Takatsu. The Noma. was soft, ultralight, and sensitive on the string — a real embodiment of Tsukasa’s philosophy — that is, a deep regard for simplicity, form, and feel.

This year, another name we deeply admired surfaced in team conversations — In Hyeok Choi.

In Hyeok is one of very few players in the community that exudes an extremely effortless style and grace in his play. In our personal opinion, he occupies the rare “your favorite player’s favorite player” air, and holds significant cultural influence despite not participating in the usual competitive circuits. It speaks not only to his tricks, but also to the artistic depth and complexity behind his play style.

We have been big fans of his style, approach and philosophy for years, and naturally we were incredibly excited when he said yes to working on something together.

In Hyeok is a current member of the Aufheben player team — we’re extremely grateful for the blessings Aufheben extended to us to work with In Hyeok on this project.

Right off the bat, In Hyeok dove into his artistic inspirations — and most of them surrounded the art form of pottery. This was an instantaneous point of connection, since form study in pottery had been a key influence in our design approach. In Hyeok sent me many references on textures and tones in porcelain and ceramics, including Helen Frankenthaler’s particular glaze and surface aesthetics.

Another moment of alignment happened early in our conversations, when In Hyeok sent me this:

We’ve always been hesitant about the min-max, meta approach to design.

In an age of complex and complicated design construction, the freedom to pursue simplicity and nostalgia in a physical object was something we were grateful for.

In Hyeok also cited multiple classic designs that he felt were particularly inspiring — amongst them the 2007 YoyoFactory 888, the SPYY Addicton, the Yoyofactory GrindMachine 2, and the Shinwoo Zen Rebuilt.

After multiple conversations, we circled around the idea to create a subtly curved, organic-feeling silhouette with high inner walls. Feel-wise, we wanted to go for a balanced, even-keeled weight distribution, ala the mid-2000s playbook of design and feel.

We would also pay special attention to curvature, lines, gradients and layers — the same way a potter would in giving form to clay.

We drew up four versions of the Cura, and ultimately prototyped three of them.

The first, original design (V1) took inspiration from the Shinwoo Zen Rebuilt, and sported a 54.4mm diameter, 43.2mm width, and we targeted a weight of roughly 66g. The playfeel on this version was very unique — extremely soft and comfortable, and very sensitive.

The third design (V3) had similar specs, but sported a design change that In Hyeok made specifically to the cup and rim design:

This changed the look of the V2, but the changes in mass also gave it a lot more spin power and stability. It added a solidity and smoothness that In Hyeok liked, and became the canvas for the fourth and final version of the Cura.

At In Hyeok’s request, we inserted a subtle countercurve near the inner walls of the Cura. It’s a nice, understated feature that is unique to V4, and adds a little bit of a pop on the spin.

This version — ultimately the one that made it to production — just has a feel about it.

In In Hyeok’s own words,

“The philosophy about Cura is the same as my approach to yoyo. It’s totally for fun. It’s not for competition. I focus on the feeling of being playful in yoyoing. It is necessary for me to take a distance from placing with high scores on stage — the thought somehow makes me feel like I should be recognized in a certain way. Cura comes from this distance. Its old school design and ordinary dimensions will bring you back to the early eras of yoyoing, which was an era of pure joy.”

The name Cura is especially meaningful — Cura is a figure in Roman mythology that formed the first human from clay, and in Latin literally translates to “care” — the fundamental spirit with which we design, craft and create things.

From In Hyeok:

“The name comes from my recent interest in pottery. I had the chance to work on some pottery, and I was captivated by the feeling of clay and forming it into shapes. It did require patience and time, which I think is the same methodology as making tricks. That was when I decided to name this yoyo after this idea — there were a few words that captured this essence, but Cura had a good feeling to me. It has its special echoes.”

The Cura occupies a very unique position in Atmos’ design lineup. It’s not a shape we usually work with, and there are design features in the Cura that aren’t found in any of our other projects. At the same time, it’s such a wonderful embodiment of In Hyeok’s philosophy that we find a deep resonance with.

We’re proud of what we’ve created alongside In Hyeok — we hope the Cura is something you enjoy, too.

title: Curry
content:
From Diverse Animals:

"The Curry is the classiest yo-yo you will ever have the opportunity to lay eyes on. It features a wooden body matched to aluminum weight rings and the Diverse Animals SPR system. The axle threads into steel inserts that are press fit into the wood to prevent stripping. The wooden body is polished to a gloss finish and protected by a wax coating.

The development process was the longest for any Diverse Animals yo-yo. The Curry has gone through numerous prototypes, 18th months of development, and four design iterations."

title: Curvy Donut Man
content:
About
The name came from a late-night design session where hungry designers made questionable naming choices — and they kept it. The Curvy Donut Man is a conscious departure from the formulaic H-shape designs dominating the market in 2016. Its curved, stepped profile and unusual cup geometry give it a bouncy, fast feel with high maneuverability that plays nothing like a conventional competition throw.
Pre-released at PNWR on February 20, 2016 and made available online March 24, 2016. YoYoExpert described it as "a step away from all the typical cookie cutter yo-yo shapes." Eternal Throw noted on the forums that the design was partly a reaction to the lack of shape diversity in the hobby at the time.

title: AXL
content: HistoryThe AXL was Custom Yo-Yo's 1998 debut and the company's first CNC-machined aluminum yo-yo. Designed to resemble the Tom Kuhn SB-2 in profile, the original version shipped with a size G (tiny) ball bearing and an optional metal fixed axle — no response pads were included in the first run. The yo-yo came in a square plastic display box with foam inserts for the yo-yo and strings, and the engraved name carried a superscript trademark symbol with no circle around the "CY" logo.A second production run (circa 2008 and later) updated the bearing to the larger Size A, added Performance Ring response pads, revised the font style and added a registered trademark symbol, and repackaged the yo-yo in a round metal can with a foam insert. The second version is slightly slimmer than the original, measuring 56 mm diameter × 23 mm width against the original's 57 mm × 27 mm, and lighter at 48 g versus 55 g. Both versions retail around $38–$60.The AXL was a popular candidate for "beefcaking" (stacking two bearings) because the original G-bearing left enough room inside the gap to accommodate a second bearing, widening the string gap for more advanced string tricks.

title: AXL Elite
content: HistoryThe AXL Elite is a Butterfly (concave)-shaped counterpart to the Modified AXL, first released in 1998 by Custom Products of Arizona. Where the AXL was designed for looping and general play, the Elite's slimline Butterfly profile was optimized for string tricks. The ultra-thin halves give it a notably low weight of roughly 42–43 g — lighter than most mini yo-yos of the era and lighter than any rim-weighted model Custom produced — achieved not through rim-weighting but by minimizing material throughout the body.As noted in a 2007 review, the design reversed conventional wisdom: rather than adding rim weight for spin time, Custom reduced the energy needed to maintain rotation by stripping mass. In practice the Elite spun well out of the throw but lost momentum faster than heavier rim-weighted alternatives, partly due to its narrow gap and grippy Performance Ring pads.The original run shipped with a tiny G-sized bearing; from 2008 onward all Custom yo-yos, including the Elite, were updated to the larger Size A bearing. The Elite retailed at approximately $40 and was produced in Red, Silver, Green, Purple, Bronze, Blue, Black, and Gold anodized colorways. The YoYo Museum records a Mint-in-Package specimen from 1998 in Red/Black anodize, Display Boxed.

title: AXLerator
content: HistoryThe AXLerator (stylized AXLerator) is Custom Products' dedicated looping yo-yo, introduced around 1999. Unlike the butterfly-shaped AXL and AXL Elite, the AXLerator uses a traditional Imperial (rounded) profile designed specifically for 2A-style looping play. Despite appearing substantial, the body is hollow — constructed from interlocking inner and outer aluminum shells — making it deceptively light and responsive.The AXLerator originally shipped with the same tiny G-sized bearing as the rest of the Custom line; from 2008 onward it was updated to a Size A bearing. It uses the Performance Ring response system and retailed at approximately $40. The YoYo Museum records a Mint-in-Package Bronze anodized specimen from 1999, display boxed with the same packaging style as other Custom products.

title: Chain Reactor
content: HistoryThe Chain Reactor occupies a pivotal place in Custom Products' history: it was the first production model to incorporate their ball-bearing axle and Performance Ring response system together, and it was developed directly from a player modification. Eric Wolff had converted a fixed-axle Reactor into a ball-bearing machine using Rubbermaid no-slip bathtub tread strips as improvised response pads. Custom Products formalized this design as the Chain Reactor and eventually rolled out Wolff's response concept across their entire lineup.In recognition of this contribution, a black Eric Wolff Signature Series Chain Reactor was produced. The Chain Reactor was very popular in the late 1990s yo-yo boom; Custom Products was subsequently sued by Playmaxx/ProYo over patent infringement related to the ball-bearing and response system design.The Chain Reactor shares the AXL's overall profile but in a compact mini form: 50 mm diameter × 26 mm width and 48 g weight, making it suitable for both looping and string tricks. Colorways: Red, Blue, Purple, Green (standard), and Black (Eric Wolff Signature). Retail ~$25–$34.99.

title: GoldenEye
content: HistoryThe GoldenEye is a Custom Products AXL with a 24-karat gold electroplate finish, billed at release as "the yo-yo industry's first and only 24-carat gold-plated yo-yo and yo-yo stand." The yo-yo itself sold for $80, with the matching gold display stand available separately for $40, making the full set $120. It shipped in a plastic case with a royal blue velvet carrying bag and two strings, and included both ball bearing and metal fixed axle options.The debut run lacked face engraving — a distinguishing detail from later manufacturing iterations. The gold plating is extremely delicate and collectors are advised to use only a soft polishing cloth. The GoldenEye uses a Modified shape (like the AXL), while its butterfly-shaped counterpart was released as the GoldenFly. Both products are long discontinued. A "Very Rare" variant exists without the "24k" stamp engraving on the body, noted as extra rare by collectors.The original manufacturer is listed as Mesa Custom Machining Corporation in Gilbert, Arizona — the parent company behind the Custom Yo-Yo and later Custom Products brand.

title: GoldenFly
content: HistoryThe GoldenFly is the Butterfly (concave)-shaped counterpart to the GoldenEye, featuring the same 24-karat gold electroplate finish on the AXL Elite body. Like the GoldenEye, it was sold with a matching gold display stand and came packaged in a presentation case with velvet bag and strings. The GoldenFly was described as "one of the smoothest yo-yos to ever hit the market" in retailer copy.The GoldenFly is long discontinued; retailer listings explicitly warn that the product will never ship and exists only for historical reference. It shared the same Performance Ring response system as the rest of the Custom Products lineup.

title: MAG 5-Star
content: HistoryThe MAG 5-Star is one of two Series 1 models (alongside the Cyko) that launched Custom Products' MAG line in 1998. The MAG series was conceived to bring an entirely different aesthetic to performance aluminum yo-yos: rather than smooth machined surfaces, each model featured intricate rotationally symmetrical cutout designs machined through the sides, making the yo-yo appear to have "no connection between the axle and the rim" when spinning — an optical illusion one museum contributor described as "exotic and beautiful."Series 1 models (5-Star and Cyko) used a tapered gap for response rather than the Performance Ring pads introduced in later series. Both shipped with a G-sized ball bearing, a plastic carrying case, a velvet bag, and two strings. Limited-edition black "Special" anodized matched sets of Series 1 pairs were also released at the end of each production run. Retail price was $50. The 5-Star's side cutout design features five radially arranged holes.

title: MAG Avenger
content: HistoryThe MAG Avenger is the first of two Series 2 MAG models, released from February 1 to April 30, 1999. Like Series 1, the Avenger uses friction from a narrow tapered gap for response rather than Performance Ring pads — the Avenger is one of the last Custom yo-yos without pads before the company introduced them across the line. The side design features five radially-arranged holes similar to a Lamborghini Countach wheel, and some dealers received units with different-colored halves, which was assumed to be a manufacturing error; however, matching same-color specimens were also produced.The Avenger "sold out fairly fast" upon release at $50. A limited black special edition was released at the end of the run. The YoYo Museum records a purple anodized specimen in Mint-in-Package condition, collected by Rick Brough. Retail: $50; general vintage unit via YoYoSam $58.

title: MAG Cyko
content: HistoryThe MAG Cyko is the second Series 1 model in Custom Products' MAG lineup, released from May 1 to August 31, 1999 (though some sources place Series 1 at 1998; the YoYo Museum records a blue Cyko acquired August 6, 1999). Like the 5-Star, the Cyko uses a tapered gap and G-bearing — no Performance Ring pads. Each MAG Cyko came in a display box with a bag.A limited black "Cyko Special" edition was released at the end of the colored production run. The serial-numbered black Special sets (Cyko Special + Predator Special) share matching serial numbers; Custom Products allegedly produced 200 units of each Special model, though higher serial numbers have been documented suggesting the run was larger. Retail: $50 standard, $75 for serial-numbered vintage units (via YoYoSam).

title: MAG Predator
content: HistoryThe MAG Predator is the second Series 2 MAG model, released alongside the Avenger in 1999. Like the Avenger, it relies on a narrow tapered gap for response and does not have Performance Ring brake pads — the YoYo Museum explicitly notes "Does not have 'performance rings' (brake pads) like the later models." It features a "sleek and narrow shape good for all kinds of looping tricks" per retailer descriptions.A serial-numbered black "Predator Special" limited edition was released at the end of the production run, matching the Cyko Special in serial number (both share the same number on matched sets). Custom Products allegedly produced 200 units of each Special, though the true run may have been larger. Retail: $50 standard; $75 for serial-numbered vintage units.

title: MAG Stiletto
content: HistoryThe MAG Stiletto is "the last model released in 'The Mag' Series" (per the YoYo Museum) and one of two Series 3 models alongside the Turbine. Series 3 was a significant departure from earlier MAG releases: it was the first to incorporate Custom Products' Performance Ring response pads rather than relying solely on a tapered friction gap. The museum record notes it "came with the new 'performance rings.'" The Stiletto was designed as a two-tone Red/Blue model, though some retailers color-matched all halves to solid Red to avoid the mismatched appearance.The Stiletto and Turbine are notable for NOT receiving black Special limited editions — only Series 1 (Cyko/5-Star) and Series 2 (Avenger/Predator) had black variants. Released 1999, retail $49.99–$54.99. Colorway confirmed: Blue/Red (two-tone) and solid Red.

title: MAG Turbine
content: HistoryThe MAG Turbine is the second Series 3 MAG model, released alongside the Stiletto in 1999. Like the Stiletto, it was the second MAG design to ship with Performance Ring brake pads. The museum notes "This version of the MAG has performance rings. The rings function similar to the brake pads found on Playmaxx Bumble Bee yo-yos." The Turbine features a turbine-blade-style cutout pattern on the sides and came in a distinctive Purple/Green two-tone colorway.Like the Stiletto, the Turbine received no black limited edition — only Series 1 and 2 received Special black variants. Retail $49.99–$54.99.

title: Reactor
content: HistoryThe Reactor is Custom Products' entry-level mini aluminum yo-yo, first released around 1999. Billed at the time as one of the first precision-machined aluminum yo-yos available for under $20, it was described as a "miniaturized version of the Custom Axl Elite series" — sharing the concave Butterfly profile but in a significantly smaller 50 mm diameter × 26 mm width package and weighing 49 g.The original Reactor used a fixed axle in some configurations; the museum records a 1999 specimen with fixed axle and green anodize at $25 retail. The modern Reactor sold by YoYoSam is ball-bearing equipped with a Size A bearing and Performance Rings, priced at $29.99–$34.99. Colorways include Blue, Red, Green, Purple, and Black. The yo-yo is also referenced as an AYYA 2005 competition prize edition (Exhibit #3948 in the YoYo Museum).

title: CUT Limited Edition
content:
History / About
Limited player/team signature colorways of the base Cut, distinct from the standard release. Filenames tie colorways to HSpin team riders including Shinya Azuma. Exact release year unconfirmed; placed circa 2010 based on retailer restock records.

title: Cyber Crash
content: History / AboutReworked the Atomic Crash profile in 6061 without stainless rims for an all-level daily competition throw.

title: Cyber Crash 2
content: History / AboutUpdated the entry competition model with greater diameter and weight while retaining its approximately 43 mm width for stronger spin and 3A suitability.

title: Bulldog
content:
About the Bulldog
The Bulldog is Chico Yo-Yo Company's first production release, launched in 2010. A round-profile 50mm aluminum monometal machined by Pro2Pro Machining Services in Chico, it established the brand's identity as a locally manufactured, competition-focused company. Rim-weighted for stability, the Bulldog comes with two replacement response pads. Its name became the brand's mascot and anchor series, spawning the Bulldog 5 Alarm, Titanium Bulldog, and Bulldog 225 variants.

title: Bulldog 225
content:
About the Bulldog 225
The Bulldog 225 is Chico Yo-Yo Company's expansion of its debut Bulldog model into the full-size category, released in 2013. Growing from the original 50.64mm (approximately 2") to 56.88mm (approximately 2.25"), it retains the round profile and Bulldog DNA while moving into competition-standard size territory. The Bulldog 225 was later released as a 2017 USN Edition commemorative variant — CYYC's last known release.

title: Bulldog 225 — 2017 USN Edition
content:
About the Bulldog 225 — 2017 USN Edition
The Bulldog 225 2017 USN Edition is a commemorative release of the Bulldog 225, issued at the 2017 US National Yo-Yo Contest. Priced at $99.99 (vs. $109.99 for the standard edition), it features a contest-exclusive colorway while retaining identical specs to the production Bulldog 225. This appears to be Chico Yo-Yo Company's final known release before the brand went dormant.

title: Bulldog 5 Alarm
content:
About the Bulldog 5 Alarm
The Bulldog 5 Alarm is a limited variant of CYYC's debut Bulldog, released in 2010. Only 80 units were produced, each hand-anodized with a unique black, yellow, and red flame pattern — making no two pieces identical. The specs are identical to the standard Bulldog, and each unit ships with two replacement response pads.

title: Bulldog Prototype
content:
About the Bulldog Prototype
The Bulldog Prototype is Chico Yo-Yo Company's first machined yo-yo, produced in 2009 before the official Bulldog release. Approximately ten units were made by Pro2Pro Machining Services in Chico, California. It shares the round profile and 6061 aluminum construction of the production Bulldog but with slightly smaller dimensions and an unfinished appearance. Specimens are held in collector and museum collections.

title: delToro
content:
About the delToro
The delToro is Chico Yo-Yo Company's second production model, designed by Thad Winzenz and released in 2010. A step-round profile aluminum monometal with a matte blast finish, it was built for competition-level stability and chopstick play. Available in Purple/Black, Red/Black, and Purple/Red colorways, the delToro set the technical direction that subsequent CYYC designs would follow.

title: Flat-Top
content:
About the Flat-Top
The Flat-Top is an undersized aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011. Its round body features stepped sides that create a channel keeping string away from the yo-yo body during play. At 50.3mm diameter it shares the compact footprint of the T-Bone and Gull Wing from the same year, offering a distinct playing character via its round profile.

title: Flyer
content:
About the Flyer
The Flyer is an undersized H-profile aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011 as the brand's more accessible price-point option. Featuring a distinctive marble color treatment in deep purple and black, and an angled stepped-H profile, it includes a 10-ball bearing. Priced at $74.99, it was positioned as CYYC's entry into a more accessible competition metal.

title: Gull Wing
content:
About the Gull Wing
The Gull Wing is an undersized aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011. Its inverse-round profile creates wide, spread wings that push mass to the outer edges while keeping the center light — a construction suited to long sleep times and versatile competition play. The Gull Wing shares its 50.3mm diameter with the T-Bone and Flat-Top from the same year.

title: Heavy Hitter
content:
About the Heavy Hitter
The Heavy Hitter is Chico Yo-Yo Company's full-size H-profile competition throw, released in 2010. At 55.88mm diameter it is the largest CYYC model to that point, with an open H-shape designed for long sleep times and smooth competitive play. The Heavy Hitter series would continue through multiple iterations — the SUV (Sam Ungerer), MME (Mike Marshall), and Type S variants.

title: Heavy Hitter 2 SUV
content:
About the Heavy Hitter 2 SUV
The Heavy Hitter 2 SUV is Sam Ungerer's signature model for Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2012. An evolution of the original Heavy Hitter, it deepens the side steps, rounds the outer rim to reduce string friction, and applies a bead-blasted finish for finger grinds. Slightly lighter than the original at 66.4g, it also features a subtle undercut for inner-ring grinds. The SUV designation references Ungerer's player handle.

title: Heavy Hitter 3 MME
content:
About the Heavy Hitter 3 MME
The Heavy Hitter 3 MME is Mike Marshall's signature model for Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2012. A series of stepped side profiles enhances the H-shape appearance and shifts weight slightly inward relative to the SUV for a more controlled playing feel. The rounded outer rim facilitates smooth string catches and long sleep times. The MME designation references Marshall's player handle.

title: Heavy Hitter 3 MME — 2012 USN Edition
content:
About the Heavy Hitter 3 MME — 2012 USN Edition
The Heavy Hitter 3 MME 2012 USN Edition is a commemorative release of Mike Marshall's signature Heavy Hitter 3, issued at the 2012 US National Yo-Yo Contest. Specs are identical to the standard MME; only the colorway and artwork differ. The USN Edition reflects CYYC's tradition of releasing contest-exclusive colorways at national events held in their hometown of Chico, California.

title: Heavy Hitter Type S
content:
About the Heavy Hitter Type S
The Heavy Hitter Type S is Sam Ungerer's second signature model for Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2013 and described by the brand as the pinnacle of the Heavy Hitter series. Its H-profile construction produces exceptional spin times and stability, while the marble-like silver and light-blue finish is exclusive to this model within the CYYC catalog. Each unit ships with a CYYC logo sticker. A curved and groove bearing is included.

title: Kestrel
content:
About the Kestrel
The Kestrel is an undersized aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2012, positioned as a spiritual successor to the delToro. Its flat rim and concave side walls create a profile suited to both horizontal and vertical play, with a smooth blast coating enabling finger grinds. A raised axle point assists string alignment, and the response is compatible with flowable silicone. Available in green, red/black, and green/black colorways.

title: Lightspeed
content:
About the Lightspeed
The Lightspeed is Nate Dailey's signature throw for Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2015. A V-shape (inverse round) profile aluminum monometal, it is designed around Dailey's fast technical style: central weight distribution aids speed and smooth regenerations, while the wider-than-usual (for CYYC) 46.58mm width provides stability assistance on string mounts. The Lightspeed placed 3rd at the 2015 Bay Area Classic and was CYYC's last signature model release before the brand went dormant.

title: Manimal
content:
About the Manimal
The Manimal is an aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011. At 53.3mm diameter it sits between undersized and full-size, with an inverse-round profile that CYYC described as "all-around all-mighty." Sharing its dimensions with the XL, the Manimal offers a slimmer take on that model's bell-shaped design for a more compact catch zone.

title: Recurve
content:
About the Recurve
The Recurve is an aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2012. At 53.37mm it occupies the same diameter range as the Route 66 and Manimal but uses an H-profile with a distinctive inner undercut — a gouged cavity in the inner wall that concentrates rim weight and contributes to impressive sleep times. A smooth blast coating makes the Recurve grind-capable.

title: Route 66
content:
About the Route 66
The Route 66 is Chico Yo-Yo Company's third production release and the brand's first H-profile design, released in 2010. Larger than the Bulldog and delToro at 53mm, it adds an outer ring for increased rim weight and a slightly angled outer rim that makes string catches forgiving during competition play. Response is compatible with YoYoFactory Broad Slim pads.

title: SB-4
content:
About the SB-4
The SB-4 is a collaboration between Tom Kuhn and Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2014 as a continuation of the historic Tom Kuhn SB series. An inverse-round aluminum monometal, it ships configured for bind play but includes a shorter axle and thinner bearing for conversion to tug-responsive play — bridging fixed-axle heritage and modern unresponsive competition performance. The SB-4 represents CYYC's only confirmed collaboration with another manufacturer.

title: T-Bone
content:
About the T-Bone
The T-Bone is an undersized H-profile aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011. At 50.3mm diameter it is compact, but its thick outer rim — described as "a rim the size of a thick steak" — concentrates weight at the edges for exceptional spin duration relative to its size. The combination of compact dimensions and heavy rim mass makes the T-Bone a distinctive entry in the CYYC catalog.

title: Titanium Bulldog
content:
About the Titanium Bulldog
The Titanium Bulldog is a limited anniversary edition released by Chico Yo-Yo Company on March 8, 2012. Only ten units were produced, each serial numbered. Machined from titanium with approximately 1mm wall thickness and a large undercut for rim weight concentration, it carries a black laser-engraved CYYC bulldog logo. Released via YoYoExpert at $330 retail, the Titanium Bulldog is among the rarest pieces in the CYYC catalog and the brand's sole titanium production release.

title: XL
content:
About the XL
The XL is an aluminum monometal released by Chico Yo-Yo Company in 2011. Its most distinctive feature is its unusual proportions: a 53.3mm diameter matched by a 53.3mm width — making it as wide as it is tall. CYYC described it as "a mutation of the Manimal"; its bell-like shape creates a super-wide catch zone from one side while the small diameter keeps it maneuverable. At 73.4g it is the heaviest model in the CYYC catalog.

title: ZRO
content:
About the ZRO
The ZRO is Zac Rubino's signature yo-yo for Chico Yo-Yo Company, released in 2012 as CYYC's first 4A (off-string) model. Its construction combines an aluminum body with machined Delrin (Celcon/Juracon) plastic rims — a hybrid approach suited to off-string play's repeated impacts. At 76mm diameter and 80g it meets standard 4A competition specifications. The axle area is shaped for finger grinds during play. The ZRO designation references Rubino's player handle.

title: D Bearing 5050
content:
From latiendadelyoyo.com:

“The design for the 5050 came about from a love of mid-school organics like the 888 and Hatrick with the idea of accomplishing 2 things in the process; getting rid of the “rock” feeling that plagues most undersized throws and making it very easy to play and catch. He took the diameter of most throws from that mid-school and made it 1to1 after enjoying a smaller ultrawide yoyo called the qubit for a bit.

The light weight makes the 5050 easy to throw for a long time and brings a joyful and zippy presence that usually isn’t felt with smaller yoyos.

It’s surprisingly stable for its shape and size and the D bearing takes everything you love about organics and brings it to the next level!”

title: D-Phalanx
content:
History / About
D-Phalanx is a wide-bodied (46mm) Size-D monometal, with a narrower gap and lower edge than D-Starter, roughly 2g lighter than a comparable full-size model.

title: D-Starter
content:
History / About
D-Starter is a low-cost, YoYoJam Lateral Cap-compatible entry model with no weight rings, designed by the brand's regular designer "Usukino/Sussu" to prove out Size-D-bearing monometal performance.

title: D-Zi 7068
content:
History / About
D-Zi 7068 is a special edition made for the Hamamatsu Yo-Yo Contest, carrying an in-story fictional commemorative credit for a "2014 Yo-Yo Fist Champion." Ships with Storybook Vol.1 and 2 spare pads.

title: D1 GHZ
content: About the D1 GHZThe D1 GHZ was MagicYoYo's first dedicated looping (2A) yo-yo. Polycarbonate construction delivers high responsiveness — a gentle tug returns it immediately — while handling the repeated hard use of looping practice. Suitable across skill levels from basic through advanced looping tricks. Sold in pairs for 2A play. Includes 5 replacement strings, glove, and bag. Available in Red, Green, Blue, and Crystal variants.

title: D2 One Third
content:
About
D2 One Third is a budget beginner plastic yoyo with a narrow responsive bearing.

title: D2 V1
content:
From Edition:

"I am thrilled to announce the latest addition to our Edition project line - with the help of Jordan Blofeld from OP Yoyos. Together, we’ve created a more competitive-focused design that builds on the beloved features of our previous Reflection release.

In response to customer feedback, we’ve increased the ring weight from 14.97 to 16.3g per ring for a more powerful spin. We’ve also made some key adjustments to the diameter and width, reducing them by 1mm each to counterbalance any unwieldiness. With these updates, we were able to drop the weight by 1 gram and introduce a nipple-styled hub to push the weight bias into a more aggressive direction.

Since some of you also expressed concern about the short axle on the Reflection, the new upcoming project will feature a 12mm axle."

title: D2 V2
content:
From Edition:

"An Updated Design II has arrived!

Design II Version 1.0 has received some fantastic feedback and love from those who have had a chance to snag one or try a version at clubs/Nationals. It really brings me joy to hear folks are enjoying these projects. I am always thankful for those folks who support these projects and those who are taking interest to debate design improvements and concepts.

So whats the plan going forward?

Ideally this would have gone straight into production and you would have access to snag it. However, I want this to be something a National or World Finalist could pick up and go compete with on that level of stage with, so additional refinement is required.

What were some of these “problems”?

In terms of direct player feedback the main reoccurring design flaw was that the design lacked spin speed. While in theory you could technically milk out 1:30 second combos out of the play, and Adrian managed to hit a 1:57 once with careful play, this was not a realistic test since after about 45 seconds the speed would die down into a “limbo state”. This limbo state resulted in the yoyo still having another 45 seconds or more of stable play. However, binds became slippy and would only return about 1/2 way up the string. To me that’s unacceptable.

Additional critiques were in the lack of “heft”. And while the yoyo was not light by any means, the packaging of that weight made it present as lighter while in play.

What caused it?

After several conversations with Jordan and Mark from MK1 also taking the time to diagnose the yoyo, It was decided that the rim angle needed a change. The previous rim angle cause high amounts of stability but with the string interaction within the catch zone it would cause the speed scrubbing effect. With this, I also wanted to have Jordan use his favorite material of choice: 7068 AL.

The material change instantly allowed us to repackage how we wanted to present that weight. With the ring now being increased from 16.13g to 18.74, dropping the body down to 13.02g compared to the original 15.28g (per half). MOI was preserved between the two versions as almost the same.

Aesthetically this update resulted in a more aggressive visual presentation of the rim section however we were also able to bring more of the extended rim styling element into play with the design.

title: D3 Dawn
content: About the D3 DawnThe D3 Dawn is MagicYoYo's third-generation looping yo-yo. Its standout feature is "rotary locking technology" — the nut rotates with the body to a controlled degree, reducing the damage from over-tightening that causes body cracking common in looping yo-yos. An improvement over the D1 and D2 in structural durability. Designed for 2A looping practice at all skill levels.

title: D4 UFO
content:
About
D4 UFO is a butterfly-shaped beginner yoyo with a translucent dome "UFO" cap over a round base.

title: D5 Dark Sprite
content:
History
D5 Dark Sprite is a Delrin-bodied plastic yoyo with a machined aluminum weight ring and sanded sides for grinding.

title: D6 YoSpinner
content:
About
D6 YoSpinner is a drum-shaped 2A looping yoyo with a spinner-cap system that doubles as a fidget spinner/spinning top.

title: Da Vinci
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Introducing the da Vinci, signature of Tomoki Toyama. This signature model is imagined by Tomoki, based on his high standards in performance and specifications to bring him the most confidence in contests and everyday use. Da Vinci features dimensions that are easy to land techy tricks, larger gap width for multiple string stacking, incredible control and stability to give Tomoki more confidence in his freestyle on stage and off stage. The da Vinci name is inspired by Leonardo da Vinci. Tomoki's name is associated with being " versatile", and Leonardo is called " Genius of All Things" with multiple innovations and creations that frontiered the human culture."

title: Dahlia
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Dahlia is Freshly Dirty's most experimental yo-yo ever released. One of the goals of the Stem System was to open the door to new materials in yo-yo design, and the Dahlia is a perfect use case. It is a stainless steel yo-yo made with a cutting edge process known as DMLS 3D printing.

DMLS, or Direct Metal Laser Sintering, uses a bed of steel powder and a powerful laser to selectively sinter (almost like melting the powder but not quite) precise areas one layer at a time. Yo-yo designs using this new process are not limited by many of the constraints that traditional CNC lathed yo-yos are. We aimed to take full advantage of this process by designing a yo-yo that is visually striking but also highly functional due to the high percentage of weight at the rim. 

Please note that this process is still being refined and these early DMLS yo-yos might have a little more vibe than regular metal yo-yos and require a bit of tuning. All new products are pre-tuned out of the box and tested extensively with rigorous tricks but a little trial and error will be needed to keep your yo-yo spinning smooth throughout its lifespan."

title: Daizzy-Fly
content:
History
The Daizzy-Fly was the second Dif-e-Yo model, released in 2002 as another 55-unit numbered collector piece. Unlike the Daizzy-Yo, which was purely a proof of concept, the Daizzy-Fly introduced the feature that would define every player-grade Dif-e-Yo for the next two decades: removable rubber weight rings. The orange powdercoat finish and wider gap made it the direct design basis for the Dif-Fly.
Ten special units were produced in yellow anodize and housed in hand-lathed walnut wood containers crafted by Ed Davidson — among the rarest pieces in Dif-e-Yo's history. A standard version came in a display case as well. The Daizzy-Fly moved Dif-e-Yo from collector curiosity to performance-focused brand.

title: Daizzy-Yo
content:
History
The Daizzy-Yo was Frank P. Difeo's very first yo-yo product, released in January 2002 as a pure collector piece. Machined from billet aluminum with a stainless steel axle, only 55 serial-numbered units were produced. Frank never intended it as a player — it was a proof of concept and a statement of machining capability.
The Daizzy-Yo introduced Frank's grooved bearing concept: a ball bearing with a single string-centering groove machined into the inner race. This was the direct precursor to the patented KonKave bearing that would define Dif-e-Yo's legacy. The model established the 2 1/8" (54mm) standard diameter that Frank would use for nearly his entire lineup.

title: Damascus
content:
The story of the Damascus below is reposted from Yoyofriends:

The Story of Damascus

One of our goals for yoyofriends in 2022 is to continue to explore and master all kinds of materials that can be utilized in making a yoyo. Like the Magnesium Cloudstrike, Brass and Copper Hummingbird to Titanium rim Graviton this year. This time we will tackle our most expensive and hardest material yet, the Damascus Steel.

The first time we came in contact with Damascus Steel was in 2016, when yoyofriends just started, when the first iteration of hummingbird was still just in the prototype phase. A friend of ours came and brought a knife made out of Damascus Steel. We were deeply attracted to the pattern and the texture of the material, we thought it would be great if this material could be made into a yoyo. However during that time, yoyofriends just started, we had no establishment to even consider this project. 

We never give up this thought. We know It will be a huge success if we can make a Damascus yoyo.

Fast Forward to the beginning of 2022, due to the hard work of the yoyofriends team, we are at a point where we can start this exciting project.

The beginning of the design consists of the entire yoyo made of Damascus Steel, because it will showcase the pattern more and lower the overall cost, however after scouting all the shops and factories, there is no way to find Damascus Steel with a diameter of more than 50mm. We don't want to just make the yoyo super undersized, we want this yoyo to perform and showcase well. This problem has made us decide to go to the bimetal routh, circumventing the problem completely by adding material outside of the smaller damascus steel body to make the yoyo full size.

Now another question arises, which material do we pair with the Damascus Steel body? We first went to the tried and true Stainless Steel, but we realize both materials have extremely high density and hardness. Pairing them both would not work well. We then decided to use titanium rims, since titanium has almost half the density as Damascus Steel. We can make the yoyo full size while still having a good weight on the yoyo. 

Damascus Steel is a very dense material, if we want to make the yoyo weigh normally, we have to make the wall very thin, however this material is meant mainly for knives, so its hardness is incredibly high. Even with the immense manufacturing difficulty, we decided to make the wall lower than 0.6mm, similar to our TISS hummingbird. This is a new manufacturing experience for FPM, our manufacturing team.

While designing the yoyo, we realized how hard this project will be, we are tackling a never before used material while making it one of the thinnest walls for a yoyo at the same time, stacked on top of the high hardness and cost of the material. Damascus Steel is around 3 to 4 times more expensive than titanium and around 2 times harder. We decided to just do it, we really want this project to become a reality!

After multiple discussions and trials the design is done. 

Next, we started to purchase the material to make the prototypes. The material is extremely expensive, 3 sets costs almost 600 USD. We are worried about the loss if it does not turn out well and the prototypes fail. 

The material we received looks absolutely incredible, we were all fascinated by the texture on the surface. It's so beautiful it made us ignore the high cost of the material.

Like we mentioned above, the Damascus Steel has a very high hardness. We could not even find a suitable tool in our inventory that can even manufacture it. To solve this we decided to contact a specialized tool factory to customize a set of tools for us. Thus making the total cost astronomically high.

Who knows the tool that came will not work at all! We communicated with the tool factory on how to solve this problem, but they only have experience on manufacturing knives, not yoyos. We knew that all knives are polished after manufacturing to form a beautiful surface. Yoyo is not the same as knife. Yoyo will be unless if make like knife way.

At the end,We resorted to our own FPM manufacturing team. We purchased all kinds of tools (around 15!) that might make this work. We finally made it work and can start to manufacture the prototypes.

The prototype came out different than what we imagined, there were no cool looking patterns, the surface became smooth, like titanium alloy. While disappointed we soldiered on and made the 3 prototypes.

We didn't want to give up on the special pattern we were looking for, so we found a laser engraving engineer to make a pattern diagram, then engrave it onto the yoyo. The result looks great but it's rough to the touch by hand and unrefined, so we decided to look for another option.

Later, we visited a knife factory that specializes in Damascus under the introduction of our friend. We realize we might need a special formulated chemical solution to treat the surface of the yoyo. The chemical solution can also be obtained at many places. Knowing this we happily contacted the chemical solution factory, although we didn't find the exact solution we were looking for, but we found an alternative that could make it work.

Look！The texture and the pattern came out great, Exciting！we finally tackled this project on a manufacturing level. All the hard work and dedication has paid off.

Finally the Damascus yoyo is assembled and tested. We picked Philip and Tony, properly stress test the yoyo and gave us overall feedback about Damascus yoyo

Also Doctor Popular, who has years of yo yoing experience and a professional yoyoer. Here We want to specially thank Doctor Popular for giving us some valuable testing experience. After the yoyo passes various stress testing by all kinds of players, it is now ready for prime time.

Damascus plays light and flowy. It has a special feeling as the material of the Damascus is more dense than the outer titanium ring while being powerful. It also didn't lose that bimetal property of power and stability due to the large titanium rim design. A yoyo that is an art but completely functional and can handle all the tricks by professional players.

Making Damascus yoyo has been a rollercoaster of a journey for us much like the magnesium cloudstrike, but the end result is worth it. We will do whatever it takes to push the manufacturing boundaries of yoyos and will continue to innovate in the future.

I believe you guys will this Damascus, its patten, also this yoyo！

yoyofriends real leather bag（2 hole pack）

Damascus Certification X 1

The letter”Damascus”logo will on the rim

title: Damascus FS
content: AboutThe Damascus FS (Full Size) is Yoyofriends' second Damascus release, featuring the iconic Damascus pattern across the entire body with no rings or secondary materials. A balanced V-shape profile delivers fast, stable play with the distinctive weight feel of solid Damascus steel. Includes NSK concave bearing.

title: Duality
content:
Overview
The Duality is an organic-shaped bimetal from Damian Puckett, sold circa 2021. Community descriptions characterize it as a more relaxed, casual feel compared to Puckett's performance-oriented later releases. Full specifications have not been published.

title: Hollow
content:
Overview
The Hollow is a bimetal from Damian Puckett documented through secondary market listings from 2023 onward. Secondary market prices ranged from $60–$80. Full specifications have not been published.

title: Power
content:
Overview
The Power is a bimetal from Damian Puckett, released in early 2023 and sold through YoYoSam. The flat-rim profile is intentional: by removing curves at the rim, Puckett created maximum real estate for the inner weight rings — producing a stable, rim-heavy throw designed for competition-level spin times.
Like the Wingweaver, the Power was offered in both stainless steel and brass ring configurations, allowing players to choose their preferred weight distribution.

title: DANG
content:
From One Drop:

"This is the signature yo-yo of Paul Dang. The original Project, our first yo-yo, holds a special place in Paul's heart. For his signature yo-yo he wanted to capture some of the OG Project in an oversize yo-yo with some elements of the CODE1 in it along with Side Effects. It's sort of like a Project with big rims and Side Effects.

It ships with Ultra light Side Effects to nail the perfect weight for Paul: 63.2 grams."

title: DANG2
content:
From One Drop:

"In October of 2011 when Paul Dang was a young lad and fairly new to our team, we released his first signature yo-yo, the DANG. That was a long time ago. Those were the days when yoyo design started to transition away from high walls, small diameters and narrow gaps. The DANG might have been on the previous design era in that regard, but it’s still a fan favorite and different from anything else – much like Paul.

In the following 6 years Paul became the face of One Drop and evolved both as a person and yoyo player. Over a decade of throwing he developed a completely unique style and it was a really interesting process to see how his growth translated into the design of his new signature model. That experience and style is now reflected in the DANG2.

Our first impressions of a new yo-yo are influenced by aesthetics, and even though we might think about how it would feel in play, nothing compares to experiencing the first time it rolls off the string. This makes the design process tricky because every single change about the form affects the play. The two can’t be separated and the play is more about discovery then pure intention. We can’t tell you exactly what mix of looks and performance Paul was thinking about when he put forth his ideas for the DANG2, but we would imagine it happened much like his yoyoing.

When you watch Paul yo-yo it's obvious he’s on a mission of discovery.  We've seen him deep dive into a particularly complex mount simply to find out what’s there. He doesn’t have any specific intentions about what he might discover, but rather he digs and digs until he finds something no one else had. After that he works on dialing in the style and execution.

Designing the DANG2 was much like Paul’s digging. The first prototype is probably the most tested yoyo we ever had. He played it for months before coming up with revisions so the final form could be born. Even the second version was played for months before going into production."

title: Daredevil
content:
History / About
The Daredevil is GWAY Throws’ debut retail release, developed in collaboration with Anomaly Yo-Yo’s. Built on a Size D bearing with an undersized profile, it offers a compact, nimble feel distinct from the standard full-size competition market. Every unit shipped with a handmade Bad Wolfe Co string and an enamel pin.
Colorways included Purple, Turquoise, Hot Pink, Blue/Orange Half-Swap, Copper/Red Fade, and the Bloodsport Black/Red Splash edition.

title: Dark Magic
content: About the Dark MagicThe Dark Magic was designed specifically for André Boulay's ring grind techniques, featuring an aluminum rim with an inner lip ideal for thumb grinds. Its wide gap and generous catch zone made it forgiving enough for beginners while performing at a competitive level — a combination that made it YoYoExpert's flagship learning tool for years. The 2004 and 2005 US National Champions won their titles using this model.

title: Dark Magic II
content: About the Dark Magic IIThe Dark Magic II refined every aspect of the original with a Solid Spin Axle system for greater hub durability, improved silicone O-ring response, and two included bearings — a narrow bearing for responsive beginners and a Speed Bearing for advanced bind play. It became the most widely recommended learning yo-yo in the hobby, largely due to its prominent role in YoYoExpert's instructional video series with André Boulay.

title: Dark Sonic
content: History / AboutDistinct model documented in Rewind's C3 museum catalog.

title: Darkstar
content: History / AboutC3's second release; a straight low-edge competition monometal with optional fine O-ring weight tuning. The original predates the physically revised 2026 revival.

title: Darkstar 2026
content: History / AboutRetains compact original proportions and 7075 while revising internal distribution and gap for modern string; includes an internal silicone weight/noise-damping ring.

title: Daytona Slimline
content:
History / About
A responsive pocket slimline titanium yo-yo, the Daytona was made for players who wanted a full-titanium throw they could actually carry around and use responsively. Taking design cues from mid-school shapes, it is slim enough to sit comfortably in a pocket. Two bearings ship in the box — a flat Size C for fully responsive play and a Half Spec for a snappier, tighter feel. Non-numbered, making it one of the more accessible Luftverk titanium releases of the era. Released approximately April/May 2017.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C flat; Size C Half Spec (both included)

title: Dazzler
content: AboutThe Dazzler is the titanium signature of Tatsuya Fujisaka, marking yoyorecreation's first use of titanium as a material. At 54mm × 41.2mm and 63.8g, it combines a compact footprint with the unique density properties of titanium — lighter per unit volume than 7075 aluminum, allowing wall thickness to increase without the weight penalty. Priced at ¥59,800 (roughly $600 USD at the time), it remains one of the most expensive and sought-after YYR releases. Extremely limited production. The Seventh Heaven (2015) is YYR's second titanium model.

title: Death’s Head Butterfly Cap Sticker
content:
About
Death's Head Butterfly Cap Sticker is a sticker from Throw-Yo Threads. Thermal-printed sticker sized for Butterfly caps. Types: Holo, White. Price: $1.50-$2.

title: Decade
content:
About
Decade is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2022. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: DECO
content:
OUTSIDE IN by DECONSTRUCTION
DECO reverses the usual structural hierarchy of a yo-yo: the outer half acts as the body, the inner half as a cap, leaving it ambiguous which side is the "primary" component. A hidden double-rim structure inside — invisible without disassembly — gives the 56.5mm/65g yo-yo a soft, floating feel despite its full size. Finished in Vintage Coating.
Released in Silver and Black colorways at $120 each (per brand's own site at time of research; both listed sold out — not independently re-verified against a live Shopify JSON pull).

title: Count Dracula
content: AboutCount Dracula was designed with an unconventional shape that opens up kendama-like catches, grinds, and stalls alongside traditional 5A play. Per the brand: it "challenges everything you thought you knew about 5A." Released October 11, 2025 — delayed from its original date due to Michael Letsom's emergency surgery. Custom colors available on request for an additional charge.

title: DedNug
content: AboutDedNug is a 420-themed counterweight released on April 21, 2026, as part of a special two-product 4/20 holiday drop alongside the Twisted Tripster bundle. Available in purple and green colorways.

title: Elysium Counterweight
content: AboutThe Elysium Counterweight was created by Michael Letsom — before Dedhed Designs was formally established — as a custom matching counterweight bundled with the Few & Far Between Elysium yoyo. Not sold separately. Also included a string pick. This early collaboration confirmed Letsom's counterweight work predating the Dedhed Designs brand name.

title: The GnomeHed
content: AboutThe GnomeHed is a gnome-character counterweight that launched alongside the Nether Gnome HedStand in December 2023, a joint reveal with Mile High Yoyos. The concept was years in the making — the HedStand project began in 2018. The GnomeHed is the second-tallest weight in the lineup. The Nether Gnome Electric Berry colorway (matte neon green/blue/pink, UV reactive) was released August 2024 as a limited run of 3 units and sold out within 2 days.

title: Hed-In-A-Bag
content: AboutHed-In-A-Bag marked Dedhed Designs' return after a company hiatus, debuting August 9, 2025. Lighter than most Dedweights at 10.3 grams, it features a satin black glove design with matte purple and sulfur yellow accents at the teeth area. The Blood Jewel colorway uses a custom three-ink blend with a glossy drip aesthetic. The reduced weight makes it "much more agile than heavier counterweights."

title: PUGZUZU
content: AboutPUGZUZU is a demonically possessed pug counterweight inspired by Pazuzu possession films. Details include a concealed kitchen knife engraved with "good boy," bared teeth, an ominous X on the forehead, and a leash attached to a severed hand on a spiked collar. The companion HedStand contains a hidden three sixes Easter egg. The concept was contributed by Jack from Dirtbag EDC. First released August 30, 2024; sold out by September 7. Available in Nickelodeon Edition (sold out) and Satin Black.

title: PumpkinHed
content: AboutPumpkinHed is a seasonal Halloween-themed counterweight featuring a carved pumpkin face with vine details. First released November 11, 2022, in Classic Eve (rich orange + glossy black, 8 units) and Fluorescent Fiend Orange (neon semi-translucent, 2 units). The design returned in 2025 in Velvet Purple/Neon Orange (Halloween 2025 Edition), Cotton Candy (blue + hot pink), and Glossy Transparent Orange colorways, with a BOGO half-off promotion on Halloween.

title: Twisted Tripster (ShroomHed)
content: AboutThe ShroomHed counterweight depicts a mushroom creature adorned with gills and fungi clusters, featuring a tree frog and centipede with eerie details. Released April 21, 2026, as part of the "Twisted Tripster" bundle (counterweight + companion ShroomStand HedStand) during Dedhed's 4/20 holiday drop. Available in Spectral Slime Edition and Bape colorways.

title: The Ghoul
content: AboutThe Ghoul is the base character of the Dedweight line and the counterweight most closely associated with Dedhed Designs. Cast in semi-translucent resin, each piece is hand-painted with alcohol inks and sealed with Cerakote aviation-grade ceramic coating for scratch and chemical resistance. The translucent body shifts appearance under different lighting. The Ghoul has appeared in many colorways over the years, including Astro-Zombie (navy blue + orchid purple + silver, June 2022), Frost Zombie (YoYoTricks exclusive), Dragon Fruit Zombie, Limeade Green Zombie, and Poison Berry Zombie.

title: The Visitor
content: AboutThe Visitor is one of the core characters in the Dedweight lineup, depicting an alien with large, unsettling eyes. Like all Dedweights, it is cast in resin and finished with hand-applied alcohol inks and Cerakote ceramic coating. Released in multiple colorways including the limited Goosebumps Edition (green-to-purple ombré fade, UV reactive, matte semi-transparent Cerakote — 8 units, December 2023).

title: The Warlock
content: AboutThe Warlock is a collaboration between Dedhed Designs and Alchemik Yoyos, released May 1, 2026, as part of "5A May." The counterweight combines Alchemik's mystic aesthetic with Dedhed's horror-craft, rendered in translucent blue and purple resin with iridescent mica powder that catches and refracts light. The shape is notably distinct from previous Dedweights, developed jointly with Alchemik.

title: The Yeti
content: AboutThe Yeti brings 11 grams of sinister heft to the Dedweight lineup, balanced for 5A play. Hand-painted with a touch of madness and shielded with Cerakote, it embodies the brand's ethos of functional horror art. Released in Frost Yeti and Icy Blue colorways among others.

title: Zombie Counterweight
content: AboutThe Zombie Counterweight is a classic zombie-themed Dedweight described as "the Living Ded." A very limited production run released April 24, 2026. Among the lightest in the Dedweight lineup at 10.2 grams.

title: Dedweight Pro
content: A competition-grade counterweight featuring an integrated A bearing. The design includes smooth, contoured string holes optimized for bead work and bead-based tricks. Weighs precisely 10g with the bearing installed, providing excellent control and balance. Made from durable resin and finished with hand-polished beeswax.

title: Deep State
content:
From One Drop:

"We want as many people as possible to enjoy yo-yoing with a nice well made metal ball-bearing yo-yo. There is just something cool about the feeling of your own energy powering a spinning yo-yo. It feels alive.

One of the hurdles in this goal is that all of our yo-yos to date have been unresponsive and require a bind to get them to return to the hand. This is no problem (and expected) for experienced players, but some just want to throw the yo-yo, let it sleep and tug it back to the hand without any learning curve. It's meditative, stress relieving, easy to do, and for many it's nostalgic.  It can put you in a "deep state" of relaxation. 

We are helping to solve this by releasing a semi-responsive metal yo-yo that fits nicely in the pocket, comes with a standard C size bearing and Flow Groove pads for easy maintenance, and is equipped with Side Effects for customizing the look and feel. It's our vision of the yo-yo as a fidget toy.

The bonus is that it's also really cool for experienced yo-yoers as who want to play semi-responsive fixed axle style, have a nice pocket yo-yo, or just want to work on getting smoother. The challenge is enticing and rewarding.

The yo-yo is called the Deep State.  We designed it with flush response pads, a fairly narrow gap and it ships with a lubed bearing installed.

How are you going to play your Deep State?"

title: Deeper State
content:
From One Drop:

"We need to go deeper.

The Deep State released almost three years ago.   We wanted to have a One Drop yo-yo that was accessible to everyone to use without a bind.  Since it was our first semi-responsive yo-yo, we weren’t sure how well it would be received and how much demand there would be.  The Deep State has turned out to be one of our best selling models and still going strong.  Because of that we decided to make a new version.  

One of the “weaknesses” of the Deep State is that doing modern 1A tricks can be really challenging.   For anyone not used to responsiveness, 1A is going to be difficult, however, the narrow width and narrow gap also add to the challenge.  For the Deeper State we wanted to improve this aspect so you’ll find it’s a little bigger in diameter and a fair bit bigger in width.  Additionally the gap is narrow at the bottom of the catch zone to help with responsiveness, but unlike the Deep State, the top of the catch zone opens up wide.  These features make it easier to land string tricks and it’s more stable than the Deep State.  Even though it’s a bigger yo-yo, the overall weight is the same or lighter than the Deep State (depending on the Side Effects used).  Don’t get us wrong, it’s still going to be challenging to hit your string tricks, but things are much improved in that regard.

We decided to use a tapped axle instead of Side Effects on the Deeper State just to mix things up.  The cup has a really cool and unique look to it.

If you’re looking to just throw it and tug it back up, the Deeper State is amazing.  It feels so nice how it responds - a really smooth return."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Deepest State
content:
From One Drop:

"We knew we wanted to continue the “State” series of semi-responsive yo-yos and had various ideas in the works but no firm decisions had been made until we were approached by Deep State Superfan, Jeff Atwood (better known as @codinghorror on the forums). Jeff and his family are philanthropists who started a project called “Stay Gold, America” to keep the American Dream alive for everyone.

https://blog.codinghorror.com/stay-gold-america

They are dedicated to doing things where everyone wins. Jeff says, “Winning does not have to come at the cost of everyone else. That's just not true. We live in a time of incredible abundance, yet in this Second Gilded Age, more of the wealth is in the hands of fewer people than at any other time in US history.” 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QPKKQnijnsM

His family donated large amounts of money to various charities immediately, and as a longer term strategy, funded Guaranteed Minimum Income (GMI) studies in rural counties, providing direct cash transfer to those in need. By extension, they are helping to create and support local American manufacturing businesses. Specifically in the case of One Drop YoYos, they have contributed to the creation of the Deepest State and the whole yo-yo community wins: the Deepest State has become a reality faster than we originally planned and the retail cost of the first run will be lower than usual. The Deepest State is  a great example of how everyone can win if we have the will. We don’t have to accept the zero sum game idea that if someone is winning, someone else is losing. We can make choices where everyone wins and this is exactly what Jeff’s family is doing.

In terms of the design, we started talking to Jeff and as it turned out the ideas we had for it were similar to what he was thinking and wanting in a modern semi-responsive yo-yo. We both agreed the Deeper State was an improvement on the Deep State with its wider gap and more curvy catch zone. With that as a starting point, we decided to bring back Side Effects, make it wider and even more curvy with a bigger catch zone. We didn’t want to add too much to the width to keep it from becoming something like a Panorama. We wanted it to still be a narrow semi-responsive yo-yo that still felt okay in your pocket but had a larger catch zone to make it easier to play. In honor of Devo, a great band that spoke on related themes, we felt that shipping with Energy Domes was the move. There is a documentary about them on Netflix that Jeff highly recommends:

https://www.netflix.com/title/82052197

Jeff also supported Matt at YoyoStringLabs by funding a unique run of neon yellow/orange high visibility strings that evoke the glow of 'staying gold' - retaining those youthful ideals we were all born with for the rest of your life. Each Deepest State in the first run will include one of these. 

https://www.yoyostringlab.com

The first run has four solid colors:Gold (of course), Blue, Red and Clear. $59

Stay Gold, America (gold base with blue and red splash) to honor the American dream Spacious Skies (blue base with clear splash)$75

We fully support what Jeff’s family is doing to share the American Dream, which includes helping fellow Americans build businesses that proudly create unique, high quality products right here in the United States. It is a deep honor to do this collaboration with Stay Gold, America and to highlight their important work."

title: Big D Astronaut
content: HistoryDell Plastics Co. of Brooklyn, New York, known for plastic toy soldiers and flowers, entered the yo-yo market in the early 1960s with the Big D line, packaged in blister cards with a 1961 copyright. Per YoYo Wiki, Dell and Royal were sued by Duncan over the word yo-yo, which appeared on Dell's packaging but not on the yo-yos; Dell dropped the line rather than litigate. The Big D Astronaut No. 605 has plastic satellite rings and domed halves with a fixed metal axle and gold hot-stamp. The Museum says its profile resembles the Big D Fireball and Duncan's Satellite. Only a black and white example is known.
