title: Delrin Gamer
content: AboutThe Delrin Gamer is the plastic iteration of Rain City's most iconic design. Hand-dyed by Jeff Anderson for unique colorways, it includes both a half-C bearing for fully responsive looping and stall play, and a full C flat bearing for unresponsive performance. Ships with spare pads, bag, thick lube, bearing tool, sticker, trading card, LEGO minifigure, and LEGO fingerspin cups.

title: Deluge
content: AboutJordan Walker's signature model and Rain City's first venture into bi-metal construction. A W-shape combining a 7075 aluminum body (40g) with stainless steel rings (25g), balanced between speed and stability for horizontal play. Fish-themed packaging: arrives in a fish-shaped pouch. Colorways: Salmon Sashimi, Royal Starfish, Fiddlers Green, Coral Corruption, and Murky Abyss. Includes custom MFD Vines string.

title: Demon’s Fun
content:
The Demon's Fun evolved from the brass Pocket Watch prototype from Return Bottoms. A larger, aluminum prototype version was made, called the Tardy. The Demon's Fun is the titanium upgrade to that. A super-slimline throw that fits comfortably in the pocketwatch pocket of a pair of jeans.

Each Demon's Fun came in a 3D-printed, legally distinct Tardis box.

Machined by Rapid Direct. Blue is a PVD coating, not anodized. Blasted with #220 grit before coating.

title: DenniSS
content:
About
DenniSS is a striking love letter to the SPYY Punchline. It pairs a fully stainless steel body with an accentuated 6061 aluminum ring. The design borrows standard bimetal practice but applies it in a contrasting way: the aluminum ring frees up about 8g per half to use in the steel, an approach Dressel Designs calls "subtraction from addition."
That extra weight budget let the team design a much broader and thinner rim than a monometal stainless steel design usually allows. The result plays smooth and relaxed while staying very stable.

title: derti
content:
The following is archived from RSO's website:

THE ELUSIVE GENIUS

My son and I (left) and Russell Andert (right).

I first spoke to Russell Andert, the maker of the dert and its various iterations, in November 2020. It was challenging to get hold of him, given that he has (by choice) decided not to jump on the social media bandwagon like everyone else. He literally has zero online presence. With the help of Andre Boulay of YoYoExpert, I managed to contact Russell via email. After a few back and forths, a Zoom conversation followed.

Russell is a machinist himself and one hell of a genius yo-yo designer (more on this later). Back in the day, he machined his yo-yos using leftover metal bars using a CNC mill. Conversely, other brands tended to make their yo-yos on a CNC lathe. What is the difference, you might ask? Put simply, the cutting tool moves in a mill while the raw material moves in a lathe. With the raw material turning, it is much easier to make a perfectly concentric yo-yo. Making a playable yo-yo on a mill is a challenging endeavour; just ask One Drop (their first yo-yo, the Project was made this way.) Due to the lack of raw materials, derts were made in tiny quantities. People love them, and they rarely pop up for sale on yo-yo forums. Today, Russell is still a machinist pondering about unique ways to make yo-yos.

Russell agreed to collaborate with RSO on our first Zoom call, after I pitched to him my vision for the collaboration and showed him RSO’s past projects. He revealed that he had previously turned several people down. I was extremely fortunate! Collaborating with Russell was an absolute breeze. I felt he was unequivocal in his thoughts and direction for the project, and he never fails to meet the deadlines set.

We actually completed the our collaboration project at the beginning of 2021 but I had to release it later due to various RSO projects already planned.

BEAUTY IN SIMPLICITY

The design of the various dert releases, starting from the first 6061 aluminium dert in 2006, through the mini iterations of the dert (the baby, eli and KC, for example), to the legendary 7075 aluminium dert in 2008, had straightforward designs. They all had organic shapes with reasonably high walls, primarily inspired by the Duncan Freehand, one of Russell’s favourite yo-yos of all time. Being the inquisitive machinist Russell is, he had most recently meddled around with more unique designs such as the Pop-A-dert, a bimetal design that can open beer bottles. He talks about it in a YouTube feature with Doc Pop below.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ndHff0D9zI

The standard dert shape essentially consists of a single arc at the catch zone and another arc in the hub joined with a straight line at the rims. Even the signature dert nipple is a simple cylindrical shape. The dert logo engraving on the nipple is the stock RomanS font from AutoCAD, a program both Russell and I are very familiar with.

From the start, we were in agreement that we would do a titanium yo-yo and to stick to the minimalist design philosophy of the dert series. Choosing which model to remake in titanium took us a while due to the number of models he had made, but we eventually settled on the mid-sized OG dert.

The OG dert design went through multiple iterations (Russell himself cannot even remember how many). The OG dert started as a 6061 aluminium, 52 mm, 58.5g yo-yo. After a few refinements, it became what Russell thought was the “best” version made out of 7075 aluminium, with a diameter of 53 mm and weighing 68g. The 7075 version was also the biggest run he had ever made. This 7075 version was the starting point of the titanium dert (which we affectionately call derti).

The response groove had to be modernised. We also felt that some weight reduction (we decided on about 63g) would make the yo-yo play better. It merely took me 5 minutes to thin down the walls of the 7075 dert CAD Russell sent me to arrive at the derti design. Fun fact: Russell had himself made a small run of 4 titanium versions of the dert back in the day, but it weighed 72g and is unacceptable by today’s standards.

We were extremely pleased with the prototypes and did not make any design changes to the production version. The resultant yo-yo plays in a sweet spot between floaty and solid. I would go further and say that is the best playing RSO to date. You would have to throw it to realise the beauty in its simplistic design.

Engraving on the 7075 aluminium dert.

Engraving on the derti prototype. 3 prototypes were made.

THE ART OF EUPHEMISM

The customer base of RSO has always been slightly older. Both Russell and I wanted to do something more suggestive with the artwork for a more mature audience. We thought it was a fun idea to have a simple-looking yo-yo and artwork with mature innuendos, a play on the “derti” name.

There was only one person I had in mind to do the artwork - Jason Week. It took us a few weeks to brainstorm the different components of the artwork.

A box art look-n-find certificate comes with every derti - can you identify all of the words and their related art? Jason also added a few hidden “69s” in the artwork for good measure, so start hunting when you receive your yo-yo!

WHAT’S IN THE BOX

BOX ART LOOK-N-FIND Certificate of authenticity

DERTI ENAMEL PIN

A PAIR OF 19MM CYAN TYPE 50 LANDING PADS RESPONSE

BLUE STRING

Can you find them all?

What do you see?

title: Derty Mag
content:
The following story was posted on the RSO Website:

A SERENDIPITOUS DISCOVERY

Once upon a time in the wildly spintastic town of Gigglesworth, lived a boy named Spencer, who had a real knack for stringing people along — like his parents, who still held onto the faintest hope that he’d become a doctor. One glorious afternoon, while valiantly exploring the dusty wasteland of his dad’s attic, he discovered a box labeled “Top Secret.” Naturally, he opened it, because ignoring giant warning labels is what heroes do, right?

Inside, to his absolute horror (or delight, we’ll never know), he found an impressive collection of adult magazines—classics like “Playtoy” and “Hustler.” Just what every awkward teenager needs for some… spinfluence. Spencer’s face turned fifty shades of red as he slammed the box shut. But not before catching sight of something shiny nestled among the fine literature.

RIBBED FOR EXTRA STIMULATION

It was a yo-yo. Not just any yo-yo—this one was sleek, shiny, and cheekily named “Derty Mag.” Spencer chuckled. “Perfect! Just what my social life was missing, a yo-yo with more personality than my entire high school.” He slipped the string on his finger and gave it a whirl. To his surprise, it spun with more sass than half the adults he knew.

The yo-yo came with a rather… informative brochure, chronicling the life of its creator, Russell Andert, affectionately dubbed the “Hugh Hefner of Yo-Yos.” Apparently, Russell had a mission: to create the “dert” series of yo-yos that could deliver maximum sensation while keeping things oh so pleasurable.

First Derty Mag CAD.

His pièce de résistance? The Derty Mag, which, according to the brochure, had a 1mm smaller girth and a “special groove for extra friction and sensation.” That groove went through more trial and error than a bad haircut, until he finally nailed the perfect one for peak stimulation.

“D”

As Spencer practiced, the yo-yo seemed to gain a life of its own, executing tricks with a level of enthusiasm that made him feel like the star of some sort of talent show. “Skin the Gerbil” somehow turned into “Rub the Bean,” and “Split the Atom” evolved into “Split the Eve,” each trick sending the yo-yo on spins that felt a bit too saucy for a simple afternoon of yo-yoing. The real kicker? When Spencer unscrewed the yo-yo, he found it housed a “D bearing” inside—because, obviously, a basic C bearing would never handle this kind of action.

C bearing (left) and D bearing (right) Derty Mag prototypes.

Derty Mag (right) is 1mm smaller in girth compared to derti (left).

A NIGHT TO REMEMBER

One night, their nosy neighbor, Mrs. Kathy, decided she just had to investigate the commotion. Just as Spencer was mid-trick—probably throwing down with a “Double Entendre Loop”—the Derty Mag made a bold escape, landing squarely in Mrs. Kathy’s lap. She gasped, clutching her pearls like they were some kind of force field. But then, out of nowhere, she let out a giggle. “Well, I never!” she said, half-scandalized, half-impressed. “That yo-yo is certainly… stimulating.”

Spencer, emboldened by Mrs. Kathy’s newfound appreciation for the fine art of yo-yoing, decided to step up his game. Soon, he was pulling off tricks at school that made the girls swoon and the boys look on in envy. Moves like “Kama-sutra-kaze,” “Gyroscopic Flip,” and crowd-favorite “Knicker Twister” had everyone in stitches.

POPEYE THE YO-YO MAN

It didn’t take long for Spencer to become the town’s newest celebrity. His yo-yo hand got so jacked, people started calling him “Popeye the Yo-Yo Man.” The once-snooze-fest town of Gigglesworth was now buzzing with laughter and some highly questionable yo-yo tricks, all thanks to one nosy kid and a box of, let’s just say, unexpected discoveries.

WHAT’S IN THE BOX

DERTY MAGAZINE Certificate of AUTHENTICITY

POPEYE THE YO-YO MAN ENAMEL PIN

A PAIR OF D SIZED TYPE 50 RSO X YOYOLAB LANDING PADS

CREAMY WHITE STRING

title: Destiny
content: About the DestinyThe Destiny is the signature model of Takeshi Matsuura, multiple-time 5A World Champion, and includes a special counterweight designed by Matsuura's father. Its H-profile body with aluminum rims and 53.25mm diameter suits Matsuura's dynamic freehand play style. Both a narrow bearing and a Speed Bearing are included for convertible responsive and bind play.

title: Detergent
content: AboutDetergent is wound from 100% rayon in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Slick disposition, lethal velocity, and immortal shelf life make it one of the fastest strings in the lineup — built for players who want zero friction and nothing slowing the trick down. Available in Tidewater, Argentum, and Scheele's colorways alongside monocolor.

title: Deviant 5
content: AboutThe Deviant 5 widened the Deviant line to 55mm — 5mm wider than the Deviant+ — and upgraded the body material to 7075 aluminum for added stiffness. At launch it was OFFSET's widest monometal, positioned as the maximum-width option for players who wanted the catch zone of a wide bi-metal without the premium pricing of steel rims.

title: Deviant 6
content: AboutThe Deviant 6 pushed OFFSET's monometal line to 60mm width — the widest Deviant yet — while retaining 7075 aluminum for the stiffness needed to maintain stability at that scale. Achieving 60mm width in a monometal without sacrificing performance required the harder alloy; the result is a throw that delivers maximum catchability without bi-metal pricing.

title: Deviant Limitless
content:
About
Deviant Limitless applies the LIMITLESS shape philosophy to a 7075 aluminium monometal body, reducing string contact during long combos and horizontal play. It's positioned as an entry point into the LIMITLESS line for players not ready for a bi-metal price point. Brandon Vu signature.

title: Deviant+
content: AboutThe Deviant+ is OFFSET's monometal flagship — described internally as "an Outlier+ in 6061 aluminum." The 50mm width brings the same catch zone as the bi-metal flagship but removes the steel rims to hit a lower price point. It gained attention when team rider Xavier Ng used it to win 2023 Singapore Nationals, demonstrating that OFFSET's monometal could perform at the same level as the bi-metal line in the right hands.

title: Deviant Titan
content: AboutThe Deviant Titan is OFFSET's full titanium monometal, co-designed by Brandon Vu and Jeffrey Pang (Luftverk). Industrial brushed finish. It shares the Deviant+ proportions but the titanium body produces a feel and spin character unlike any aluminum version. Announced on October 30, 2024, alongside the Outlier Titan, limited to 50 units. The pair represented OFFSET's entry into the premium titanium segment.

title: D&H Cutlass
content: About the CutlassThe D&H Cutlass was the companion debut model to the Raptor, released by D&H Enterprises in 1999. Named for the four blade-shaped cutouts defining its H-shaped body, the Cutlass was CNC-machined from T-6061 aircraft aluminum and hard-anodized in a blue and silver two-tone finish. Like the Raptor, each unit was engraved with the model name, the 1999 year mark, and a unique serial number on the inner wall, with the run strictly limited to 250 units. The gap is adjustable via the same .006" and .014" shim system shared across the D&H lineup. The Cutlass and Raptor share the same axle and bearing construction — a precision ball bearing pressed onto a stainless steel stud with a rolled threaded axle hole.

title: D&H Hurricane
content: About the HurricaneThe D&H Hurricane was a prototype model announced by D&H Enterprises alongside the Sextant and Mag as a planned June 2000 release. Named for its three-spoke body design, the Hurricane was shown in a planned purple and silver two-tone hard anodized finish. It would have used the same CNC-machined aircraft aluminum construction, shim-adjustable gap, and serialized engraving system as the released Raptor and Cutlass. The company closed by early 2002 without the Hurricane entering production.

title: D&H Mag
content: About the MagThe D&H Mag was a prototype model announced by D&H Enterprises alongside the Sextant and Hurricane as a planned June 2000 release. The Mag was shown with a planned black and gold two-tone hard anodized finish, distinguishing it from the other planned designs. Like the rest of the D&H lineup, it would have been CNC-machined from aircraft aluminum with a serialized engraving and shim-adjustable gap. No full prototype photography has surfaced; only a text label was archived from the D&H website. The company closed by early 2002 without the Mag entering production.

title: D&H Raptor
content: About the RaptorThe D&H Raptor was one of two debut models released by D&H Enterprises in 1999. Named for the three piercing talon-like spokes defining its H-shaped body, the Raptor was CNC-machined from T-6061 aircraft aluminum and hard-anodized in a striking red and silver two-tone finish. Each unit was engraved with the model name, a 9-point star year mark with "9" at center (signifying 1999), and a unique serial number on the inner wall. The run was strictly limited to 250 units. The gap is adjustable via included .006" and .014" shims, allowing players to tune string layering and response. D&H also offered an OEM corporate logo engraving program, though no documented custom runs have surfaced.

title: D&H Sextant
content: About the SextantThe D&H Sextant was a prototype model announced on the D&H Enterprises website alongside the Hurricane and Mag as a planned June 2000 release. Named for its six-spoke body design, the Sextant was shown in a planned green and silver two-tone hard anodized finish. Like the released Raptor and Cutlass, it would have been CNC-machined from aircraft aluminum with the same shim-adjustable gap and serialized engraving system. The company ceased operations by early 2002 and the Sextant, along with the other planned models, never entered production.

title: Diamond Back
content: About the Diamond BackThe Diamond Back is the full-metal signature model of Eric Koloski, featuring YoYoJam's new proprietary diamond-pattern engraving on the rim and inner side edge for enhanced thumb grind and finger grind performance. The nickel-bronze rim on an aluminum body creates a dense edge-weighted feel for extended spin. Its low-edge profile increases gyroscopic stability during play.

title: Dietz
content:
From One Drop:

"The Dietz is the signature yo-yo of Daniel Dietz. It was designed to be an undersized, Side Effect, high level competition focused yo-yo and this is exactly how Daniel uses it. The shape is unique with lots of angles and feels great in the hand. It ships with a new Side Effect (Dietz Side Effect)."

title: Dif-Con 1
content:
History
The Dif-Con 1 was the last yo-yo Frank P. Difeo designed before his unexpected death on March 3, 2024. A multi-stepped H-shaped profile machined using his signature milling approach, the Dif-Con 1 featured deep .045" pad pockets capable of accepting both standard .555-size Dif Pads and flowable silicone. Ships with silicone Dif-Binder pads.
The Dif-Con 1 represents the final evolution of Frank's design philosophy — precision milling, adjustable weight architecture, and user-serviceable response — distilled into his most modern profile. The name "Dif-Con" was likely a nod to Frank's lifelong use of the machining conference format to develop new designs.

meta.yya_response: Silicone Dif-Binders (.555 ID, .045" pocket — accepts flowable silicone)

title: Gladiator
content:
History
The Gladiator was Frank Difeo's entry in the yo-yo mod contest at the 2004 World Yo-Yo Championships. An all-aluminum evolution of the Spike-Fly concept, it was produced in two versions: one with solid aluminum spikes pressed into side cups, and one with full bearings pressed into the spike tips for frictionless spin-top play. Both versions were custom made-to-order only — no standard production run existed.
In 2015, Frank revisited the concept with the Gladiator Slave, which reused the name and some design philosophy but replaced the spikes with a clean butterfly profile and modern response.

title: GTO
content:
History
The GTO — named "Get This One" to help customers decide between the Sportster and Wide Sport — was Frank Difeo's mid-tier player model, released around 2005–2007. A polished aluminum butterfly with removable rubber weight rings that added 8g to the rim, it sat between the narrower Sportster and the wider Wide Sport in both feel and weight range. Straightforward competition performance with the standard Dif-e-Yo adjustable weight architecture.

title: Juggernaut
content:
History
The Juggernaut was the first release in Dif-e-Yo's "Hard Knock" lineup, announced in 2010. Thick rims, deep black anodization, intricate graphic printing, and a small machined internal lip for thumb grinds gave it a look and feel distinct from any prior Dif-e-Yo. Players who reviewed it noted a similarity in hand feel to the YoYoFactory DV888 — smooth, competition-oriented, and more polished than earlier models. Priced at $104.99.

title: Orbiter
content:
History
The Orbiter was the third Dif-e-Yo aluminum yo-yo, released in 2003 as another 55-unit numbered collector piece. Inspired by the vintage Duncan Satellite series, it featured Frank's most intricate machining up to that point: two sets of internally-placed O-ring weights, positionable at center or rim position, all enclosed in a nickel-plated finish with laser-engraved text and logo. Frank described it as the most complex design he had undertaken.
Unlike earlier models that used bolt-on pogs or external weight rings, the Orbiter's O-rings were fully internal — hidden within machined cavities — giving it a cleaner external profile while retaining the adjustable weight architecture Frank had become known for.

title: Sportster
content:
History
The Sportster was a polished aluminum butterfly-profile yo-yo released around 2005–2006. A slimline evolution of the Wide Load design, it was narrower and lighter than the Bare Bones — positioning it as a more competition-slim option for players who found the Bare Bones too wide. At 58g base weight and 65.5g with O-rings, it was also lighter, with a 57.15mm diameter that sat slightly wider than the standard Dif-e-Yo. Described as a successor to the Dif-Fly in the player lineup.

title: Tank
content:
History
The Tank was the third release in Dif-e-Yo's "Dif Series" competition lineup, following the Bare Bones and Bone Chip. The redesigned profile pushed more mass to the rims than any previous Dif-e-Yo, and the machined rim groove enabled thumb grinds. A Tank-F variant with flush pad response was also produced.
The 2006 World Yo-Yo Championship edition was particularly notable: a green anodized Tank with detailed laser engraving commemorating the event. This limited run is among the most sought-after Dif-e-Yo collector pieces.

title: Dif-Fly
content:
History
The Dif-Fly was Frank Difeo's first production player yo-yo and the model that established Dif-e-Yo as a serious brand in the mid-2000s performance market. Evolving directly from the Daizzy-Fly, it introduced a slimline flat-rimmed butterfly profile with removable rubber rim weight rings — a system that would define the entire Dif-e-Yo lineup for years to come.
The Dif-Fly went through several distinct generations: the original ran a friction disc and Frank's grooved bearing precursor; a later revision swapped to the patented KonKave bearing; and a final flush-pad variant was designated the Dif-Fly-F. In 2022, Frank released the Rev-1 Dif-Fly as a 20th anniversary upgrade.

title: Diffraction
content: Mk1’s first yoyo design, with a cool fingerspin hub that’s not too easy but still pretty good at centering.

title: Diffraction 2
content:
From Yoyo Expert:

"The original Diffraction design was inspired by conversations online with Jordan Blofeld (of Smashing and OP YOYOs). Taking inspiration from the Smashing Interlagos yo-yo, Mark from Mk1 got some interesting ideas about fingerspin hubs. After a couple failed attempts he landed on something unique; concentric stepped circles to act as a fingerspin guide. The shape of these circles is reminiscent of laser diffraction patterns, something Mark had seen a lot as he worked in a laser-lab during his college years. This inspired the name of the yo-yo as well.

Mark took his design to the YoYoExpert Forums for advice and refined it into the Diffraction 1 which was produced in limited numbers and sold to friends and family. Later in 2019, Mark put together a plan to tweak the design just a bit (the Diffraction 2) and ordered a 2nd run with some different colors, including the green that couldn’t look better if it tried! A good friend drew up a new logo and the Diffraction 2 became a reality!"

title: Diffraction 3
content:
From MK1:

"The Mk1 Diffraction v3 is a monometal yoyo designed for comfort and performance, utilizing a smooth inverse-round shape and a unique fingerspin cup. It’s an updated version of the first yoyo that Mk1 ever released."

title: Diffusion
content: AboutThe Diffusion marked yoyorecreation's entry into plastic manufacturing in 2012. Injection-molded from PC/ABS, it offered a 56mm × 40mm competition profile at a fraction of the price of the aluminum lineup. The original Diffusion became one of the brand's most recognizable designs and remained popular enough to receive a significant update — the Diffusion v2 in 2014, which enlarged the diameter to 57.8mm and refined the weight. A POM variant (POM Diffusion) followed in 2016.

title: Diffusion v2
content: AboutThe Diffusion v2 expands on the original 2012 Diffusion with a wider diameter (56mm → 57.8mm), a slightly wider catch zone (40mm → 43.1mm), and marginally lighter weight. The PC/ABS construction remains the same. Where the original Diffusion was compact and dense, the v2 moves toward a more contemporary oversized feel while retaining the accessible price point that made the original significant.

title: Digamma Crash
content: History / AboutRetail Crash-series model documented separately from Gamma, Atomic, Mega, and Cyber Crash.

title: Dingo
content:
From One Drop:

The Dingo is a mini yo-yo that is truly pocket-size but also plays really well. It features the same axle system from the M1. Comes with a large bearing and flow groove response making it the first mini metal yo-yo to have modern standardized guts. We set out to finally make a great playing mini that is available in large quantities and a decent price and the result is the Dingo.

title: Dingo Gen 2
content:
From One Drop:

"Oh my. Where does the time go? The original Dingo was first released in November of 2009, when we were just 2 years into making yo-yos and this was our 5th model. We’ve now made 95 models (more if you count all the Benchmarks and an extra one for the Perspective).The original Dingo was a pocket size mini that played well and spun a long time. It had the round pressed nut axle system that we were using at the time. We did a few runs like that. In October of 2014 we released one more run but we replaced the pressed nut with a tap-through axle. And that was that.It’s now been 10 years since we made any Dingos and in recent years we have been getting lots of requests to make more. The Dingo enjoys lots of love out there (we appreciate you). Once we decided to go ahead with doing more, it seemed clear that updating the design was the play.The diameter is the same as the original: 46mm. We stayed with a tapped axle but changed the cup to have a flat floor. This allowed us to use the awesome Dingo stamp in the middle of the hub rather than off to the side. We then opened up the catch zone by smoothing out the curve and increasing the width a bit to make it easier to play and have more room for string wraps. Finally, we reduced the weight down to 57.8 grams (the original was a hefty 63 grams) to bring the weight into proportion with the small size. It feels more well rounded and modern now but still has the same pocket size mini charm."

title: Dink
content:
History / About
The Dink is the miniature stainless steel member of the Dunk family, with a name Jake had planned since the Dunk launched. As Jake explains: "I'm an avid fisherman, and in that world when you unintentionally catch a small fish — usually a bass — they are called 'dinks.' Fast forward to the Dunk becoming a real yoyo, Dink and Doink immediately seemed like perfect names for the lineup." Jake and CJ Atkinson quickly realized stainless steel was the right material for a yo-yo this small — there are plenty of undersized colorful chunky aluminum options, and that's not what they had in mind. SS allowed them to go extra thin on everything and create something that looks more like a precision tool or machine part than a toy. The raw stainless finish reinforces that aesthetic completely. The Dink retains the signature Dunk profile including the inner cup bump, making it clearly part of the family at a glance. In Jake's 20 years of yo-yoing, mini-sized throws always appealed to him but consistently ended up collecting dust — "they play noticeably worse than their big brothers and feel like a novelty." So the Dink was tested for nearly a full year — far longer than any other Jake Bullock release — before going to production. At contests, the common refrain when players tried it was "it actually plays so well!" Jake found himself using the Dink to learn 3.0 hooks one summer, noting the smaller size made them easier. He positions it as excellent for dense tricks and short string tech for advanced players, and as a chopstick learning tool and form calibrator for beginners: "it will let you know if your breakaway sucks."

title: Dinosaur in the Wild
content: The Dinosaur in the Wild is a collaborative yo-yo produced by C3yoyodesign and W1LD to celebrate C3yoyodesign's 15th anniversary. The design merges W1LD's signature Wilderness wide shape with the titanium rim concept from C3's Galaxy Dinosaur model, resulting in a premium 6061 aluminum bi-metal with raw titanium rims and special co-branded engravings. Released in two colorways: W1LD Gold body and C3 Purple body, both with matching raw titanium rims.

title: Diorama
content:
From One Drop:

"The Diorama is a 7075 aluminum alloy re-designed Panorama. We gave it the “Boosted” treatment.  7075 aluminum is heavier than 6061, but because of the re-design, the Diorama weighs less than the Panorama. What’s interesting is that the profile shape and basic specs are the same.The redesign is inside - you can’t really see it but it’s significant. We did, however, change the cup to look different so it’s easy to recognize the difference.

Tsukasa specifically requested we do this. He loves the Panorama, but was really curious to see how it would feel Boosted. He finds the Diorama to have a bit more control, but can’t decide which one he likes better because they are so different."

title: Diplomat
content:
History / About
The Diplomat is the signature model of Recess team member Colin Beckford — the same player who wrote Recess's 2015 Buyer's Guide and went on to place 6th at US Nationals and 4th at BAC. Machined from 7075 aluminum for added durability and a brighter, shinier finish that stands out on stage. The curved H-shape profile offers a wide catch zone suited to Colin's complex, risky trick style. From the first throw, reviewers noted the weight distribution felt perfect — achieving a powerful, solid throw and bind while remaining light, maneuverable, and fast in play. One of Recess's early signature model releases and the first 7075 monometal in the lineup.

title: Anima
content:
About the Anima

The Anima is Remy Baskin’s signature throw and the debut release from Dis. Designed to feel distinctive and playful while performing at the highest level, the Anima draws inspiration from the Turning Point 2, UNPRLD Suction, YYF Severe, and CLYW Akita. The press-fit aluminum cap construction adds visual character but can develop vibe if damaged; raw aluminum editions will acquire cosmetic marks with use. Packaging features a woodcut pomegranate illustration by Leonard Baskin.

The Anima was released in standard, B-Grade, hand-engraved Sean Thackeray, and artist-collaboration In Hyeok Choi editions. The In Hyeok Choi edition features original drawings laser-engraved on each side, documented in Choi’s film Beautiful World, shot in Osaka following WYYC 2023.

title: Obscura
content:
About the Obscura

The Obscura is Dis’s third release and first explicitly competition-oriented throw, again designed by Martin Koprna. Tri-material construction combines a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel outer rings and flush-inset plastic inner rings. Two inner ring variants were offered: polycarbonate (PC, lighter) and POM (heavier), resulting in a 1g weight difference between versions. Inspired by the Japan Technology Kagerou & Mirage, Empathy Noir, and YYR Liminal Autoscopy.

Koprna competed with the Obscura (POM version) at Czech Nationals Open Division, placing 2nd.

title: Sibyl
content:
About the Sibyl

The Sibyl is Dis’s second release, designed by Martin Koprna of the Czech Republic. Described by the brand as a versatile all-rounder for anyone and everyone, the Sibyl features clean lines, relaxed curves, and integrated POM rings that shift weight distribution toward the rims for a softer, more controlled feel. Available in 13 colorways.

One colorway — purple with white POM rings — was released as the Danny Severance edition, with half the purchase price ($40 of $79) donated equally to Mental Health America, MHA Delaware, and Wildflower Alliance.

title: Disaster!!
content:
From Diverse Animals:

"The Disaster!! is the second yoyo from the homebrew brand Diverse Animals. Designed over four iterations for optimum stability and agility, the Disaster is actually the first yoyo that Diverse Animals conceived. Feel this unique yoyo dash between your hands, careening through tricks like one of those fancy-shmancy 'trick yoyos.' Hand-machined Delrin halves, hand-machined aluminum spacers, flowable silicone response."

title: Ariel
content: AboutThe Doble Ariel is a handmade wooden fixed-axle yo-yo with adjustable brass lapper discs. Archived Doble product information describes a 0.078-inch music-wire axle, a conventional twisted-cotton string, and an approximate weight of 57 grams that varies with the wood and finish. Turning and moving the halves adjusts the string gap and the pressure between string and lapper discs, allowing the player to tune sleep and return behavior. Smooth string-contact surfaces were intended to reduce string wear.John J. McAvoy Jr. patented the design. The 1993 patent date does not establish the Ariel’s retail release date. Archived Doble copy and Ariel photographs via Doc Pop.

Doble Ariel photograph by Doc Pop

title: Callisto
content: AboutThe Doble Callisto is listed alongside the Ariel, Calypso, Titania, and Swallow as a Doble manufactured model. Detailed specifications, release date, and production history have not been documented in available sources.

title: Calypso
content: AboutThe Doble Calypso was the flagship model from American craftsman John J. McAvoy Jr., patented in 1993. Handcrafted from burled Western Broad Leaf Maple with a natural grain-filled finish and three coats of polyurethane, each pair of halves was balanced and matched. The Calypso used McAvoy's patented adjustable lapper disc mechanism — threaded knobs allowed the player to widen or narrow the gap between internal discs to control string friction, optimizing sleep time while retaining response.The Calypso held the world record for fixed-axle sleep time at 63 seconds and continued to be used competitively for over a decade after its release. It shipped with untwisted waxed string for maximum sleep, and an optional suede finger strap (also patented by McAvoy) addressed "yo-yo finger" discomfort. Retail price was $60.

title: Titania
content: AboutThe Doble Titania was an innovative transaxle yo-yo released in 1993. Its defining feature: two freely-spinning halves mounted on a solid axle post with threaded knobs at each end, allowing the player to grab the yo-yo by its hubs while it was spinning. This proto-hubstack concept predated modern ball-bearing hubstacks by nearly a decade. The heavy string — a thick cord tethered to a small free-spinning brass sleeve with a leather finger loop — was an integral part of the design.At 120 grams the Titania was exceptionally heavy for its era. The gap was narrow by modern standards, but the freely-spinning halves were a genuine mechanical innovation. Like all Doble models, the Titania featured McAvoy's adjustable lapper disc gap mechanism. It was never produced in a butterfly profile. John McAvoy held US Patent 5,254,027 (1993) covering the core design.

title: A-maze-ing Wooden Yo-Yo
content: AboutThe A-maze-ing Wooden Yo-Yo is a lightweight responsive yo-yo based on YoYoFactory's Legend Wing wooden body, featuring custom laser-etched maze artwork created by illustrator David Birkey. Sold through Doc Pop's store at $14, it was designed as an entry-level and novelty product.

title: Bolt (Original)
content: AboutThe original Bolt was Doctor Popular's signature yo-yo produced by YoYoJam, sold for approximately five years beginning around 2001. Doc Pop specifically chose dual O-ring response over the standard YoYoJam starburst response when reviewing the prototype. The Bolt became notable in the early modding community — Doc Pop published online instructions encouraging players to modify their units. The modern BoltXP (2022) is a spiritual successor to this model, recreating the same shape with updated specs.

title: Bolt Part 2
content: AboutBolt Part 2 is a collaboration between Doctor Popular and Hadrien Bennaceur, manufactured by C3yoyodesign. It revives the shape of Doc Pop's original early-2000s Bolt in machined Delrin with updated modern specs. A Kickstarter campaign ran in February 2018 with general release on June 1, 2018.The yo-yo features "cubby hole" side caps designed for horizontal finger spins and schmoove grooves on the catch zone. It shipped with a standard size C bearing for unresponsive play, with an optional slim half-spec bearing available for modern responsive play. Available in Yellow, Green, Blue, and Black; B-grade Black units were sold at a discount.

title: BoltXP
content: AboutThe BoltXP is a machined POM (polyoxymethylene) yo-yo that recreates the shape and feel of Doc Pop's original early-2000s Bolt with updated modern specifications. Like the original, it ships with a size C bearing; an optional half-spec slim bearing enables modern responsive play. The design retains schmoove grooves and removable side caps (pogs) from the Bolt Part 2 era.

title: Day Tripper
content: AboutThe Day Tripper is a collaboration between Doctor Popular and Jeremy Park of Zip Line Strings, released January 15, 2021. A slimmer, lighter follow-up to the Weekender, it was designed for daily carry with an emphasis on stalls and regenerations rather than long spin time. It shipped with Zip Line Strings' "Executive Class Lite" string.The Day Tripper was sold simultaneously through doctorpopular.com and ziplinestrings.com. A "Saturday Market" colorway was offered as a Patreon-exclusive edition.

title: D.I.Y. (Desert Island Yo)
content: AboutThe D.I.Y. (Desert Island Yo) is a collaboration between Doctor Popular and YoYoEmpire, based on YoYoEmpire's Notus shape with modifications by Doc Pop. The concept is simple: if you could have only one yo-yo on a deserted island, what would it be? The answer is a wide, floaty shape that excels at fingerspins and adapts to any play style.Available in a standard POM/aluminum version ($55) and a lighter polycarbonate "DIY Lite" version (56g, $49.50). A Superblack Patreon-exclusive edition was also offered. Multiple colorways across both variants.

title: Hesitator
content: AboutThe Hesitator was an ultra-limited run of hand-assembled yo-yos produced by Doctor Popular in 2007, using Spintastics Eclipse bodies as the base. Unlike the brass-ringed stock Eclipse, Doc Pop used aluminum weight rings, making each unit lighter. From 55 units started, approximately 40 were completed and sold; 15 were discarded.Each Hesitator was individually hand-painted by Doc Pop using nail polish, ink, spray paint, Sharpies, glitter, and even McFlurry lids. The interior features flames spelling out "HESITATOR." All units were numbered and signed, and included custom pog artwork. The name originated from customers requesting "hesitator" yo-yos.

title: PLTPS
content: AboutThe PLTPS (pronounced "platypus") is a modern-responsive counterweight yo-yo designed by Doctor Popular, featuring machined POM rims and 6061 aluminum hubs. High walls facilitate string stalls, a schmoove groove minimizes string friction, and optimized finger cups enable pull-starts. A POM counterweight (9.6g) is included.The design synthesizes elements from Doc Pop's earlier Pop Art, Weekender, and Day Tripper models. "Have Fun" is engraved on the interior walls of select colorways. Available in six color combinations at $75.

title: Pop Art
content: AboutThe Pop Art is a collaborative modern-responsive yo-yo designed by Doctor Popular and Rain City Skills (RCST). Its slimline profile features high walls for extended string stalls, aluminum hub inserts within a Delrin body, schmoove grooves, and "extra-wide gamer pads" to minimize string friction through the narrow gap. The initial release included a Rain City Skills Rain Drop counterweight (Base Bead edition) for freehand play.

title: Populist
content: AboutThe Populist is Doctor Popular's first bi-metal yo-yo — a 7075 aluminum body with interchangeable brass or steel weight rings, produced in partnership with Dressel Designs. The design was developed collaboratively with Doc Pop's Patreon community before being refined for production.A prototype "Moon Rock White" was offered exclusively to Patreon beta sponsors, followed by a general release in multiple colorways. A Superblack Patreon-exclusive edition features black steel rings and black anodize at a reduced price point. Available with polished brass or raw/polished steel rings depending on colorway.

title: Stoopid
content: AboutThe Stoopid is a collaboration between Doctor Popular and Toybania, released in late 2023. Doc Pop's edition features a purple fade anodize with a brain in the shape of a donut laser-etched in white on the side — artwork designed by Doc Pop himself. The 6061 aluminum construction and full-size C bearing support both modern-responsive and bind-return play.

title: Super Scientist
content: AboutThe Super Scientist was Doctor Popular's first signature yo-yo, produced by YoYoJam as a custom variant of their Super SpinFaktor. The yo-yo featured neon lime green coloring with dark blue side caps and brass-colored weight rings. The side caps bore Doc Pop's distinctive raised-eyebrow logo. Plays identically to the base YoYoJam Super SpinFaktor model.

title: Super Sellout
content: AboutThe Super Sellout was a limited self-parody sequel to Doc Pop's Super Scientist, produced by YoYoJam. Limited to 71 pieces, it featured an all-green colorway with brass rims. The side caps replaced Doc Pop's standard logo with dollar signs ($) in the eyes — a humorous commentary on the concept of "selling out." It is the final production run of the Super Scientist line.

title: The Thing
content: AboutThe Thing is a collaboration between Doctor Popular and Toybania, released in early 2023. The slimline design uses a machined POM body with titanium hubs, giving it a distinctly light feel well-suited to modern-responsive and counterweight play. The Doc Pop editions feature light blue or raw/silver titanium hubs depending on colorway.

title: Weekender
content: AboutThe Weekender is an ultralight modern-responsive aluminum yo-yo manufactured by One Drop Design (Eugene, Oregon). The design originated during a challenge Doc Pop set for himself: design a complete yo-yo from scratch in 48 hours while visiting One Drop's machine shop — hence the name "The Weekender."The initial design was later updated to add fingerspin cups to the inner bowl. A Kickstarter campaign ran in March 2019, closing in June 2019 with 120 backers raising $9,680. Special Patreon-exclusive "Fingerspin Fades" colorways (Pink/Grey and Brown/Grey) were offered as early-access editions.

title: Dogu
content:
History / About
Dogu (どぐう) is inspired by Jomon-period clay figurines ("dogū"), intentionally chunky for a "lump of earth" feel rather than pure performance optimization; its shape references the YoYoJam Counterattack.

title: Dogu Dry
content:
History / About
Dogu Dry (どぐうさんドライ) is a renewed, roughly 1.5g-lighter version of Dogu, marketed with intentionally morbid "cracks suggesting imminent deterioration" flavor text.

title: Dome
content: About the DomeThe Dome is an undersized organic yo-yo designed in collaboration with Korean player Park Jemin (@parkjeminnn), reflecting his preference for compact, comfortable everyday play.Originally introduced May 2025, the Dome was restocked in 2026 with new colorways including a limited signature edition with player In Hyeok Choi, titled 'Enlighten Your Way.'

title: Dome Side Effects
content:

title: DON
content:
History / About
DON is the 3A signature of Kim Dong Young, released July 11, 2026. It uses an aluminum/stainless-steel bi-metal outer-rim structure — an unusual choice for a 3A model — deliberately selected for added rotational power.

title: Dongwu
content: AboutThe Dongwu (动物 — "Animal" in Chinese) is an aluminum competition throw released in 2024 as a JIGUN Japan National contest item. Available in Red and Yellow colorways at $45. Sold out.

title: Donut Ti KOI
content: AboutThe Donut Ti KOI is a limited titanium take on the classic KOI, released exclusively through the Yoyofriends Facebook group community. Sharing the same dimensions as the standard Ti KOI, this version features the playful "Donut" colorway finish unique to this drop. Titanium construction delivers the signature organic KOI feel with added titanium character.

title: Donut XL Ti KOI
content: AboutThe Donut XL Ti KOI stretches the KOI platform to oversized proportions in full titanium, offering a dramatically larger 63mm diameter paired with a lighter 63g weight for a floaty, expansive feel. Like its Ti KOI sibling, this was a Facebook group–exclusive drop in the "Donut" colorway.

title: DOOMBOT
content:
History / About
DOOMBOT took two years, seven prototypes, and four machinists to develop. It has a V-shaped catch zone and a stepped profile, with brass rims for acoustic character and weight distribution. Canister art by Firdaus of Studio Moonchild, samurai/Gundam-themed. Sold in A-Grade, Battle-Grade, and several sold prototype revisions (V1/2, V4, V5, V6).

title: Dopamine
content:
About the Dopamine
Released in September 2023, the Dopamine is Ross Levine's signature yoyo and the flagship aluminum release from ilinx Toys (Hollywood Modern Yoyos). It continues the design lineage that began with the Recreational Revolution Freq. Wav and the OhYesYo × ilinx Freq.Mod collaboration, refining the shape into a smoother, swooping profile that shaves off a small amount of weight relative to earlier iterations while preserving or improving spin time.
The key mass feature sits just inward of the rim, concentrating power and gyroscopic stability for off-axis and horizontal play. The hub features a flat surface surrounded by a valley groove for finger spins and DNAs, plus a central dimple that allows fingernail pull-starts. The Dopamine is machined from 7075 aluminum and uses Hollywood Pads (19mm slim) for response. It was released through YoYoExpert, AllYoyo, and the modernyoyos.com storefront in Red, Yellow/Orange Fade, Clear, Blue, Blue/Green Fade, and Pink colorways. Price at launch was $59.99 USD.

title: Dork
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: The Dork (A YoYo)

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is the sequel to my yoyo The Ork, this is a more laid back smaller less bitey yoyo. 

Like the Ork It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/41RypW. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. This one is intended to be printed with 100% infill. 

In addition to being cute the face has an actual purpose and functions as the response system, what makes it go up and down. In this case the glasses are also slightly embossed on the inside to provide a more reliable response."

title: dotE1NS
content:
History / About
It has been over a decade since we cooked up the crazy idea of making our own little yoyo to enjoy. Back in the day, the amount of different shapes, sizes, weight, construction types etc. was limited and we felt there was a void regarding small but powerful aluminum yoyos. So we stuck our heads together and after many discussions came up with basic shape of our first yoyo – the legendary E1NS.
We went through many iterations throughout the years following its initial release with different weight distributions, colours, finishes, sizes (2WEI), guts and so forth. But each and every of these versions came with the distinct E1NS-feel.
Letting it shine once more after its 10th birthday was only a matter of ‘when’. From this extra time to think about the new E1NS we came up with the strong desire to combine old and new. We used our old sketches and blueprints to achieve an overall shape as close as possible to the OG from 2007. But then we turned the madness-dial all the way to superundersize and shrank the yoyo to a mere 45.6mm in diameter. To compensate the weight reduction we then replaced a part of the rim with steel inserts that retain the exact overall shape. For such a small yoyo to feel right, its weight needs to come down as well. The 59g are just right for the small guy.

Production Runs

Run #1 (August 2018) — 12 units, Black/Orange; D45.60mm / W37.30mm / 59.00g. Bearing: C. Finish: Polished.
Run #2 (November 2018) — 18 units, Grey/Orange; D45.60mm / W37.30mm / 59.00g. Bearing: C. Finish: Soda Blast.

title: Dove
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Delrin gives a unique soft plastic feel while still being able to come close to the weight distribution achieved with aluminum. The Dove has a nice curved H-shape profile with chunky rims that round down into the aluminum fingerspin hub. They kept the weight relatively low and evenly distributed for a pleasantly nimble feel in play that you just can't get with aluminum. It moves fast and smooth in play and responds to your slightest command with ease!

Named Dove for the crisp white Delrin prototype and the pleasant, peaceful feeling you get from each throw!"

title: Downbeat
content:
From One Drop:

"We wanted to return to the roots of the yo-yo and make one that was just about fun. A yo-yo that is happier going slow and taking it's time. A yo-yo that prefers old school funk and drives 1973 Van with thick stripes painted on it. A yo-yo that enjoys chilling out with it's friends. A yo-yo that stands alone in your case. A yo-yo with this much soul can only be called The DownBeat.

Many yo-yos recently, including ones we make, are focused on competition and speed. This is a noble cause and one we'll continue to pursue because pushing the limits of performance is important and desired.

This isn't to say we sacrificed performance. The DownBeat comes with Side Effects, performs to modern standards, and spins as long as your favorite DJ. What's different in the play is that it weighs 70 grams with Ultra Light Side Effects. It's not getting any lighter than that groovy 70g but it can go heavier if you're in need of extra chill. Its weight distribution is designed to slow your play down and we hope this slowness gives you the time to rediscover the joy of yo-yoing.

The yoyo is big and curvy with a nice comfortable organic shape. The catch zone has machined 70s racing stripes that feel surprisingly good in the hand and create a new and refreshing look.70 Grams. 70 Bucks.It's time to chill.DownBeat."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)
meta.yya_weight: 67.50g (70g with aluminium Ultra Light Side Effects)

title: Downbeat 20/20
content:
From One Drop:

"We are kicking off our 20/20 Hindsight Series with Downbeat.   The original Downbeat was created to be heavy, slow and chill. We made it exactly 70 grams with Ultra Lights which meant there was no way to make it lighter than that. 70 grams was a statement.  

The point of the 20/20 series is to re-imagine old models so we thought making a much lighter Downbeat would be a signficant change because the weight was key to it's essence.  We were able to do this without changing the size or the profile shape so it still feels like the same yo-yo in your hand. With Ultra Lights it comes in at 65.3 grams - almost 5 grams lighter than the original. They are all shipping with Ultra Lights, except for the Saturday Market which has Flat Caps and weights 66.3 grams.

It’s strange to type this: the Downbeat 20/20 is fast. But somehow it still retains it’s chill.

Limited to a one time run of 120 pieces.  New lower price starting at $59 for solids."

meta.yya_weight: 62.8g (65.3g with aluminium Ultra Light Side Effects, 66.3g with Flat Cap Side Effects)

title: DR3I
content:
From ILYY:

"From all the designs and crazy ideas we devised in our yoyo journey, one project has always stood out as the unholy mother of insanity: the DR3I

Initially planned for a 2017 release, we had to postpone the release due to the immense manufacturing difficulties that spawn from this most ambitious construction. Being a full blown tri-metal yoyo, it was clear from the start the DR3I will require all skills and manufacturing brilliance in our machinists arsenal…and then some.

At that time, we were not able to produce more than three prototypes that fulfilled our performance requirements at reasonable cost. As mitigation, we went from tri-metal to tri-material and came up with the DR3I.ii that replaced the titanium body with a polycarbonate shell. This change allowed us to produce a few more for a mini-run. But we knew, only the real deal with its titanium body will eventually fill the void the initial concept idea created in our minds.

Now at the end of 2021, four years later and with a lot more experience and confidence in our bags, we gave this another try. Countless obstacles during production from machining, fitting and selection had to be overcome but we kept pushing forward only thinking about the ultimate target: DR3I must live!After sky-high mountains of scrap material and vast fields of shattered dreams, 23 pieces persevered. We are finally able to release our opus magnum to the world!

Here it is, the killer of lifespans and crusher of spirits: DR3I"

"The yoyo features a meticulously designed titanium body for maximum strength yet minimal weight. The DR3I’s power is provided by massive brass rings with a carefully shaped wave that complements the overall design and allows for exact rim weight placement. The inner cup is made of 7068 aluminum and inherits its anti-cone shape from the amazing Abyss. Thanks to the hollow construction, the angle of the anti-cone could be increased which yields even better finger spin performance. When spinning it combines the classic sounds of thin titanium and old-school throws with caps. The DR3I is a high-rpm yoyo with a satisfying oomph when binding.

The ‘Dinosalat’ anodization of the aluminum cup uses squeezed dinosaurs spiced with pirate-boot-matured Scotch. The resulting colors vary depending on the species of the used saurian making every DR3I unique."

Prototype #1

Release: May 2017Diameter: 54mmWidth: 39mmWeight: 62.50gBearing: CResponse: 15x22x2 pads

The first prototype, years ahead of the first production run, had 3 units in a Polished Raw/Splash colorway.

Run #1

Release: ???Diameter: 54.6mmWidth: 46mmWeight: 65.7gBearing: LResponse: 15x22x2 pads

The production run of the DR3I had 23 units in the Soda Blast Black / Dinosalat colorway.

title: DR3I.ii
content:
History / About
The concept of the DR3I to incorporate 3 materials into the body construction (namely titanium, steel and aluminum) resulted in a great and unique yoyo that ranges amongst our greatest creations to date. However, since the machining and fitting these parts with respect to our tight tolerances results in a very complicated and expensive process, we are currently not able to provide more DR3Is to all those who were interested.
We tried something else in this concept area. Replacing the titanium body with machined polycarbonate. To accommodate the lesser density of PC, we increased the overall width of the body which allows for a greater curve in the cup for even easier centering during finger spins.

title: Draco
content: The Draco is W1LD's third anniversary model, realizing a design concept first conceived in 2018. A polycarbonate body paired with stainless steel rims in an H-profile configuration, the Draco delivers the spin power of a rimweighted bi-material in a primarily plastic construction, bringing a different feel and a more accessible price relative to the all-metal models.

title: Dragonfly
content: AboutThe Dragonfly is the Duncan-branded successor to the ProYo Turbo Bumble Bee GT, which Duncan acquired when it purchased Playmaxx's assets in the early 2000s. The original version used a ball-bearing axle and brake-pad response, making it one of the first mass-market string-trick yo-yos. The 2021 redesign replaced the bearing with a transaxle and updated the response to starburst, simplifying production while maintaining the wing shape. Interchangeable sidecap graphics remain a signature feature, allowing players to customize their throw.

title: DragonJam
content: About the DragonJamOriginally called the DragonFly, the name was changed to avoid a copyright conflict with Duncan. The DragonJam features an adjustable string gap, ball bearing axle, and a unique hole-type response molded into the body. YoYoJam considers it their longest continuously produced model.

title: Draupnir
content: AboutThe Draupnir is the cornerstone of the yoyorecreation lineup and arguably the most decorated competition yo-yo ever produced. Named for the Norse mythological ring that multiplies itself every ninth night, it features a 7075 aluminum body with outer stainless steel rims — placing mass at the farthest possible point from the axle to maximize spin time and gyroscopic stability. The prototype was shown in August 2013; full production began 2014.Team YYR players have used the Draupnir to win more World YoYo Contest titles than any other single model in history. It has been used by Iori Yamaki, Akitoshi Tokubuchi, and numerous other World Champions and finalists. Special editions include 44CLASH contest colorways. The Draupnir has remained in continuous production since its debut and is still available from yoyorecreation's official store.

title: Dreadnought
content: AboutThe Dreadnought is the signature of Shinichiro Ohnishi, 2008 West Japan Champion. Its 62mm diameter placed it among the largest all-metal competition throws available when it debuted in 2010 — a deliberate counterpoint to the undersized trend of the era. The DreadnoughtG, released alongside it, added 11g (to 79g) for maximum stability and spin power. Both share the same 62mm × 45mm profile.

title: DreadnoughtG
content: AboutThe DreadnoughtG shares the Dreadnought's 62mm × 45mm profile but adds 11g through denser machining and a silver finish, bringing total weight to 79g. Released simultaneously with the standard Dreadnought, the G version targets players who prioritize absolute spin stability and maximum momentum over agility. At 79g it remains one of the heaviest production yo-yos yoyorecreation has made.

title: DRI-YWET
content:
Anti-Yo's Story:

"Smell The Magic of the DRI-YWET. Whether it's L7 or Whodini, this yoyo is going to rock out and be magical. This is an upgraded version of the YWET with a wild coating that's never been done on a yoyo. We start with halves which have been treated to give it that classic Anti-Yo Slip Matte® finish then we do a copper coating over this finish, but not once, we do it twice. This yields a yoyo that looks like pure gold (literally) when new but ages over time to form a patina that darkens as it oxidizes. It even gives off a scent just as a copper penny would as it ages. Copper is such a heavy metal that it adds three grams to the weight of the yoyo, giving this one a slightly more solid feel. We released ten of these at US Nats and they sold out in two minutes, we thought we should do a proper release for something which garnered that much attention. We've also taken the Side Effects and anodized them blood red and engraved our own heart onto them. So cute, but still magical and ready to rock."

2011 Nationals DRI-YWET

10 DRI-YWET's released early at the 2011 Nationals. These had blank aluminum side effects, instead of the red hearts.

title: Driftline
content:
History / About
The Driftline is the long-awaited first mowl brand signature model for World 3A Champion Hank Freeman, released June 13, 2025. Development began in 2023 after Freeman officially joined mowl as an ambassador. Building on the Surveillance HPF, Freeman's goal was more spin power, improved stability, and longer sleep times — critical for 3A. The Driftline adjusts the HPF's shape and increases overall weight by approximately 2 grams, redistributing it strategically to the rims for stronger spin and enhanced stability while keeping the light, balanced feel of its predecessor. The result is the definitive 3A weapon from a three-time World Champion.

title: Droid
content:
The Droid is a collaboration between Yoyofriends and Round Spinning Objects.

The following is archived from RSO's website:

ANOTHER WORLD’S FIRST

The Doombot had many breakthroughs. It was the first titanium-brass bimetal yo-yo ever made. It has also remained the largest titanium bimetal yo-yo to date, with a diameter of 58 mm. Machining a titanium yo-yo of this size is complicated.

The Doombot had nearly discouraged me from making another bimetal titanium yo-yo, but the opportunity to make the world’s first titanium bimetal SE yo-yo made me want to challenge my limits.

I am proud to present to you, Droid.

OUTER RING TITANIUM BIMETAL DESIGN

RSO has been primarily making organic old school designs so far. A yo-yo made for competitive play was the number one request from the fans.

Given that Droid is to be a SE yo-yo, it is critical to have an outer ring design instead of an inner ring one - let me explain.

Due to the Doombot’s inner ring design, the diameter of its titanium body has to span the entire 58 mm. Such a large diameter increases the risk of warping of the yo-yo body during the machining process.

The titanium yo-yo body of Droid (without the outer rings) measures at a smaller and hence safer 54 mm, allowing the yo-yo to be machined more consistently. The outer rings make up the rest of the 57 mm diameter for Droid.

Droid ties with the MagicYoYo Rex, another yo-yo with an outer ring design, as the 2nd largest titanium bimetal yo-yo to date. Most of the titanium bimetal yo-yos that have been released are in the 56mm to 56.5 mm diameter rage.

Stainless steel was the only material I felt was suitable for the outer rings. An outer ring design necessitated a material that was durable enough as the rings would be in constant contact with the player’s hands. Brass was not an option as it is prone to discoloration, particularly with repeated hand contact.

POWER, SQUARED

Droid was mainly inspired by two yo-yos, the One Drop CiTizen and Turning Point Diaspora. The most apt way to describe it would be a bimetal CiTizen with a Diaspora rim.

Its general shape is similar to the CiTizen, one of my favorite yo-yos of all time. It is however a hair larger and wider than the CiTizen. Given Droid’s bimetal design, it has significantly more rim weight and torque. I was surprised that Droid does not have significantly kickback despite being a heavily rim weighted yo-yo.

The rim’s shape is nearly identical to the Diaspora, a 54 mm diameter signature yo-yo of world champion Shinji Saito. The lower walled V-shaped catch zone of Droid makes it geared more towards competitive play.

The Droid’s SE hub is similar to Gravity, with a circumferential groove transitioning to an up-sloping arc to its peak. RSO will be using this SE hub design for future models as I prefer it over the standard angular SE hub One Drop uses.

PRECISION ENGINEERED

Given the complexity of the Droid design, I knew I could not do it alone. Neither could a partnership with another company who does not machine their own yo-yos.

RSO has worked with a handful of machinists over the years and continues to use a few machinists at any one time, tapping on the strengths of each of them. For Droid, I turned to Fenghuida Precision Machining, also affectionately known as FPM. FPM has an in-house yo-yo brand called Yoyofriends.

On the Shenzhen subway train to Songgang.

Bouquet of flowers from the FPM team.

Fun fact: RSO’s first models, the titanium Bowl and Bowl 7068, were machined by FPM. In December 2018, I travelled to Songgang, Shenzhen, to meet the people behind the company and to finalise the design for Bowl 7068. The entire journey from Hong Kong to Songgang took about an hour and a half by train. Jacky picked us up from the train station and ferried us to the FPM headquarters. We were greeted by a fine lady holding a bouquet of flowers when we arrived, marking the start of a meaningful partnership.

The FPM team has undergone a facelift over the years but its owner, Jacky, remains at the helm. I insisted that he be on the cover art for Droid!

My wife and I (center) at the FPM old headquarters. FPM has since relocated. Jacky, its owner, is on the extreme left.

Machining a Droid half.

Polishing a Droid half.

The prototyping process for Droid was vastly different from the other titanium yo-yos I had made. FPM suggested machining the first prototype out of aluminum, to ascertain whether the design is smooth with SE installed. Using aluminium instead of titanium significantly reduces machine time and costs.

The thinnest portion of the Droid CAD measures about 0.65 mm. Testament to the machining prowess of FPM, the aluminum prototypes were smooth. We then proceeded to machine titanium prototypes.

Titanium prototype half on the left, and aluminum prototype half on the right.

Aluminium Droid prototype before assembly.

Aluminium Droid prototype after assembly.

No changes were made to the titanium prototype apart from increasing the size of the groove around the SE hub. The outer rings of the production Droid weigh 13g each, with both making up 40% of the yo-yo’s total weight. FPM took charge of the production of the yo-yo and they delivered brilliantly. They had also kindly agreed to take charge of the assembly and order fulfillment for Droid.

PERFECT SYNERGY

As with all RSO SE models, Droid is powered by original One Drop SE and premium Yoyorecreation NSK platinum Double Straight bearings.

RESHAPING THE SE HUB

The SE hub was the most challenging part of Droid to design. There were multiple back-and-forths between Jacky and me while working on the SE hub. The struggle was to find a sweet spot between what I thought was functional and aesthetically sleek versus what Jacky thought was machinable.

Before I explain my design considerations for the Droid’s SE hub, let us briefly delve into the history of SE yo-yos.

SE were first introduced in 2010 with the One Drop 54. The first SE yo-yo released by another company other than One Drop was the Anti-Yo YWET in late 2011. The SE hub of these yo-yos had a standard angular design. In late 2020, I asked David Metz from One Drop why they stuck to this design, and was told that it allowed the SE hub to have the “least amount of weight”.

Standard SE hub on the One Drop Benchmark 2016. Photo by Spingear.

The only yo-yo released by One Drop which had a different SE hub was the Yelets, which had significantly more material around the SE hub. Most recently, Atmos Projects has released a yo-yo called the Noah with a different SE hub. Note that the shorter SE hub in the Noah also results in more material at the center of the yo-yo. One can infer from these designs that these yo-yos are not made with a rim weighted play-feel in mind.

One Drop Yelets. Photo by One Drop.

Atmos Projects Noah. Photo by Atnos Projects.

SE yo-yos had all been made of aluminium until the RSO x Sonny Patrick YWETi MK I, the world’s first production titanium SE yo-yo which had the standard SE hub. With more experience gained from prototyping titanium SE yo-yos, I realised that the shape of the hub could be remolded, as titanium could be machined more thinly than aluminium.

The YWETi MK II, Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition and Gravity all had SE hubs that were thinner than the standard ones.

Truth to be told, the ideal way to remove rim weight from the hub of a titanium SE yo-yo is to thin down the walls such that you would have a tall vertical nipple and a horizontal platform around it. This design was adopted by the New York YoYo Club for the V2 prototype of their yo-yo.

New York YoYo Club yo-yo prototypes, V1 in the center and V2s at the sides. Photo by Will Chavez.

The most weight saving SE hub design. Picture from Mark Diehr of MK1 Yoyos.

For Droid, the rim weighted play-feel was one of my top priorities. I tried my best to remove as much center weight as possible, including from the SE hub. However, the appearance of the hub was also a key consideration - I did not want the hub to appear too bulky or long as it would not look proportionate to the rest of the yo-yo.For the production Droid, the arc (green arrow in the picture below) which forms the SE hub creates the illusion of a shorter hub. Weight was removed from the bearing side of the yo-yo (blue arrow in the picture below) and redistributed to the rim.

Comparison between the SE hub on the Droid (white) versus the “standard” ones seen on a majority of SE yo-yos today (red). The arc (green arrow) which forms the SE hub gives the illusion that the hub is actually shorter than what it really is. The weight which was removed from the bearing side of the yo-yo (blue arrow) was added to the rim.

I do not seem to have the best luck with titanium bimetal models. We had initially wanted to release Droid in October 2021 but a wrong type of SE (regular domes instead of energy domes) was made. Not wanting to delay the release further, the yo-yos were assembled with, and will ship with, silver flat cap SE.

WHAT’S IN THE PACKAGE

CNC machined BLACK delrin CAPSULE

Certificate of authenticity IN THE FORM OF A DROID REMOTE CONTROLLER

DROID ENAMEL PIN

CIRCUIT BOARD PROTECTIVE CLOTH

A PAIR OF MAROON 19MM TYPE 40 RSO LANDING PADS

ORANGE THICK STRING

content:

These Limited Edition Droids are the last yo-yos of the Droid line. There are two colorways of this final release.

The first is a “Droid X” colorway with rainbow iridescent stainless steel rings.

The second has jet black stainless steel rings and is named “Droid 9E”, a tribute to the black-plated BB-series astromech droid last seen in the Star Wars sequel trilogy.

The package includes the same delirium canister and accessories as the regular edition Droid.
