title: Cheerio Big Chief
content: AboutYoYo Wiki states the Big Chief (Big C) was produced briefly in the early 1960s, replaced an earlier model marketed only in Canada, and came in various two-color combinations. The word Sweden is stamped into the back half, indicating manufacture by Elfverson. Listed specs: 53 mm diameter, 29 mm width, 36.2 g, fixed wooden axle.

title: Cheerio Rainbow
content: AboutYoYo Wiki lists the Cheerio Rainbow as a blue and gold wooden yo-yo, 60 mm in diameter and 30 mm wide, weighing 53.7 g with a fixed axle. The wiki says Rainbow yo-yos are said to have been produced either by Elfverson in Sweden or by Mastercraft of Ontario; the documented example may be Mastercraft because it lacks the Sweden stamp. Elfverson's wiki entry says Cheerio outsourced production of the Rainbow and Big Chief to Sweden from 1958 to 1964.

title: Kalmartrissan
content: HistoryAccording to Elfverson & Co, the story began in 1926, when Gosta Elfverson started a company in England importing and selling Swedish glass. He received a yo-yo and had the idea of making them with his brother Olof Elfverson in Sweden, who owned Elfverson & Co. At first the yo-yo was made in glued parts; a few years later the foreman Ivan Pettersson devised a way to turn it from a single piece, and the Kalmartrissan has been made in roughly the same way since 1932.The yo-yo carries a foil-stamped print of Kalmar Castle on one side; early examples were pad-printed with a different logo, and the body was later slightly flattened to improve the print. The first yo-yos had a 1.7 mm gap, because string was thinner then. The gap was widened to 2.2 mm in a redesign, and to 2.8 mm in 1999 after competitors in the USA reportedly sanded their yo-yos to enlarge the gap. Elfverson says about 20,000 are made per year today, versus over a million yo-yos made for Parker Brothers in Canada in a single year in the 1970s. In the USA and Canada it was known as the Sweden Yo-Yo because of the Sweden marking on the back.

title: Super Sonic Yo-Yo
content: AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum documents the Super Sonic Yo-Yo, a signature model of professional yo-yoer Linda Sengpiel, dated 1972. It came on a large shrink-wrapped card with Festival-branded string, six World Yo-Yo Club membership cards, a trick and personal history booklet, pinback buttons and patches. The yo-yo itself is one-piece beechwood made in Sweden by Elfverson & Company, and the Museum states it is identical to Festival's Big Zapper model sold during the same period.

title: Elite
content:
History / About
The Elite was released in 2017, representing G2's competition-focused offering for that period. The name was revisited years later as the Elite 23 (2023, 6061 body with SS rims — an entirely different model). Full specs were not available in accessible sources at time of research.

title: Elite 18
content:
About
Elite 18 is a 6061 aluminum with SS rims yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2018. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Elite 23
content:
History / About
The Elite 23 is a competition bimetal revisiting the "Elite" name from G2's 2017 era, now with stainless steel rims on a 6061 body. A special "Brass Elite 23" variant (numbered #117) uses brass weight rings instead of stainless steel — giving it a dramatically different weight distribution and golden aesthetic. The Brass Elite 23 numbered #117 was released as a premium collectible alongside the standard colorways.

title: Elixir
content: AboutElixir is wound from 100% trilobal polyester in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Crisp disposition, fast velocity, and immortal shelf life define it as a competition-capable string. Elixir has been chosen as the bundled string for several notable collaborations, including custom colorways produced for the YYBCxG2 Workhorse and a 100-piece run for Return Bottoms. Available in Mauveine, Quicksilver, Bistre, Auric, Phosphor Bronze, and Monobath colorways alongside monocolor.

title: Elysian
content: AboutThe Elysian is the signature model of So Takase (JT team member with a strong 1A competition track record), released in 2026. An A7075 monometal with a step-round profile — softly rounded shape with a clean, uncluttered face — it transfers throwing force efficiently. JT describes it as offering "straightforward, predictable handling." Available in Shiny Gold.

title: E=mc²
content: AboutThe E=mc² is the signature of Hiro Irifune, known in the community as "Roan," and the companion piece to Tatsuya Fujisaka's Blink in the "Tatsuya vs. Roan" series. Where the Blink added a lip to the Stardust formula, the E=mc² went in the opposite direction — flat sides, a rounded outer shape, and a low edge, with 69g of weight for strong spin momentum. The E=mc² +2 followed with an additional 2g. Irifune would later develop the Tricklab responsive series for yoyorecreation.

title: Eminence
content: Signature model for Czech player Filip David. The shape draws inspiration from his previous Pharaoh signature (The Good Life) but with a wider profile and inner-positioned stainless steel rings for greater power. Jakub Dolejš won Czech Nationals 2024 with this model; Filip David won Czech Yo-yo Cup Prague 2024 with it. The inner ring placement creates a distinctive feel compared to conventional outer-rim bimetals.

title: Emollient
content: AboutEmollient is a 100% woolly nylon string in the Throw-Yo Threads Comfort family, developed in 2026 following a nylon sourcing shift. Built for players who prioritize tactile comfort, it delivers a plush, ultra-soft feel with moderate velocity — the softest entry in the Comfort lineup.

title: Emotion
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"This is Emotion!

Dressel Design's flagship monometal for 2023! Shortly after the release of the assassin they started thinking of what a more normal sized assassin would look like. They knew 7075 would be the way to go to retain some of that indestructibility that you would get with stainless steel. Dressel also knew they wanted it to be slightly wider and smaller while still sitting firmly in the full sized category.

To achieve the play that they wanted they went with a new style of cup/hub design for them to attain a more even distribution similar to steel. The results? A yoyo that has a fun pacing and play feel that is also controllable and performance focused.

How does it play? Natural and with Emotion!"

title: Empath
content: Empathy's first production monometal, developed through five prototype iterations. Inspired by older yo-yo designs with thicker rims and high walls, but with a fresh play feel. Debuted at WYYC 2023 in Osaka, Japan with team members Maty Držmíšek and Kryštof Nosek. A pre-production prototype (1/5) in matte light green was sold as a collector item. Also released as part of a limited oneLove pack bundled with the Bubble in December 2025.

title: Bubble
content: Empathy's first plastic yo-yo, created in collaboration with singer-songwriter and yo-yo enthusiast Faye Webster. Faye has hosted the Faye Webster Yo-Yo Invitational twice — a theatrical exhibition combining top-level performance with live music. The Bubble uses a POM (Delrin) body with a polycarbonate cap for a totally unique feel. The profile follows the Empath shape at a larger scale. Smooth, playful, and quietly special — but still with edge and power. A WYYC 2025 (Prague) black edition was produced exclusively for the event. Also released as part of a limited oneLove pack bundled with the Empath in December 2025.

title: Cloud
content: A remastered version of the klid, a classic monometal originally designed in 2012 by Czech brand Barely Legal. Empathy used the original CAD files with minor adjustments — slightly reduced diameter and added weight for increased spin power. The curved stepped profile retains the soft, rounded feel of the original while delivering improved performance. Comfortable in hand and excellent for complex string tricks.

title: Copper
content: Keiran Cooper's bimetal signature, built from tumbled 7075 aluminum with genuine copper rims. Copper has greater density than stainless steel, providing massive rim weight within a compact frame for exceptional spin stability through long combos. The copper naturally develops a patina over time through exposure to air, moisture, and handling — each yo-yo becomes unique with use. Can be cleaned with lemon juice and salt to restore the original shine.

title: Empty
content: A special collaboration between Empathy and Japanese brand YoYoRecreation. A deliberate tribute to the era of YoYoJam hybrid yo-yos that helped define modern yo-yo culture. "Shout out to YoYo Jam, we miss you." Combines a lightweight, floaty capped sensation with precision machining and a premium finish. Available in two body materials: POM and polycarbonate, each paired with 6061 aluminum caps. Available at WYYC 2025 in Prague ahead of the January 2026 retail release.

title: Sympathy
content: Empathy's most technically ambitious design, over a year in development. A three-piece construction featuring a 7075 aluminum body, 7075 aluminum rims, and a precision titanium center cap. Unlike a conventional bimetal where weight is at the rim, the titanium cap sits centered — producing a satisfying clink on binds and string hits. Incredibly refined, solid, and stable. The titanium cap also adds a striking visual contrast to the aluminum body.

title: Plastic Yo-yo
content: History / AboutEmpress was a Japanese yo-yo manufacturer of the 1960s, and the YoYo Wiki lists a "Plastic Yo-yo" among its two models alongside the Satellite. The wiki has no entry, description or specifications for the model, and the Yo-Yo Museum has no matching exhibit.

title: Satellite
content: History / AboutThe Empress Satellite is a reproduction of the Duncan Satellite from the Japanese maker Empress, with the word "Japan" stamped on the rim in black ink. The YoYo Wiki dates it to the 1950s-1960s and notes it uses a three-piece design where the Duncan original is one piece; most examples have halves of unequal size, though the colors are vivid and the logo is imprinted more legibly than on the Duncan models. The Yo-Yo Museum dates its cream, green and red example to 1962 and values it at $125.

title: EMPYREAN
content:
History / About
EMPYREAN is a titanium monometal released May 6, 2026, introducing YYR's new "Whizy System" — a wider gap designed for oversized Whizy strings.

title: Emulsion
content:
About
Emulsion is Throw-Yo Threads' seasonal limited-release string series — each batch uses a unique blend formulated for a specific season, event, or occasion. No fixed formula, no repeatable spec. "Mixed, slightly thick, named, and dated before it goes out the door." Each run is retired once sold out.

title: Amaterasu
content: History / AboutAmaterasu (天照) is the first release from the Japanese yo-yo brand en, which develops its yo-yos together with image characters. YoYoStoreRewind describes it as a full-metal yo-yo characterized by light direction changes and sleep endurance, easy to control throughout. Its A7075 (super duralumin) hardness lets it respond quickly without much force, suiting players who want snap and speed in their tricks. The 2026 re-release states that the original was about 45 mm wide.

title: Amaterasu (2026 Renewal)
content: History / AboutThe first en model, Amaterasu, returned in a renewed form in 2026. Per the en official store, its defining trait is strong spin paired with quick handling and easy direction changes, carried over unchanged. Changes from the original: the protruding face was replaced with a dome; chamfers were adjusted overall; overall width went from 45 mm to 46 mm; and a logo engraving was added. The initial colorway is Kadode (門出, a green/black/yellow/orange fade). A variant with the cadode logo was also sold in the official store.

title: Himuro
content: History / AboutHimuro (氷室) is an ultra-light mono-metal themed on snow, per the en official store. Its smooth, low-corner shape and A6061 feel are emphasized by a weight well under 60 g, giving a distinctive feel. The rim is cut much thinner than a typical mono-metal, yet clever weight distribution keeps the spin strong. The store positions it as ideal for casual play. A B-grade (氷菓) version and a Yukidoke (雪解) set with Konohanasakuya were also sold.

title: Hoakari
content: History / AboutHoakari (火明) is an en mono-metal aimed at competition use. Details here come only from en's later Hoakari: Yu release, which states that the Yu model changes the original Hoakari's material to A6061 and substantially revises the weight, and that its development concept was 'Hoakari x Himuro'. The original Hoakari's own specifications could not be found in the sources consulted.

title: Hoakari: Yu
content: History / AboutHoakari: Yu (火明:悠) is the second model of en's 'Yu' (悠) series, which reinterprets competition models with different materials and weight designs. It changes the base Hoakari's material to A6061 and substantially revises the weight; the concept was 'Hoakari x Himuro'. It is a mono-metal with a mid-size diameter and wide width: the width raises mount success while the restrained diameter keeps complex tricks nimble. Corners are rounded for softer catching and grip, and the rounded inner rim gives a gentle feel. It stays competition-oriented but is more all-round.

title: Kaguzuchi
content: History / AboutKaguzuchi (加具土命) is a high-end three-layer bi-metal: in addition to the usual outer stainless rim, it has an inner aluminum rim. The en official store says that although it resembles the structure of trending tri-material models, its design philosophy and purpose are unique. The aluminum rim sits inside to support the winged stainless rim from below, improving handling without sacrificing outer-rim spin power. Since it is all-metal and the parts mesh effectively, it disperses impact well and is more durable than typical bi-metals. Spin and stickiness come from the outer-rim weight distribution, and handling from the mid-ship rim.

title: Konohanasakuya
content: History / AboutKonohanasakuya (木花咲耶) is en's first mini-size yo-yo. The store notes that its 45 mm diameter and 40 mm width make it easy to grip and let power transfer on slow throws. A low-relief step-straight shape covers size-related mount misses, and concentrating rim weight outward sustains spin, with the A6061 handling giving an assured feel unusual for a mini.

title: Shinatsu
content: History / AboutShinatsu (志那都) is a lightweight A6061 mono-metal themed on 'wind'. It shares direction with the ultra-light Himuro but focuses on power: a large rim area gathers weight outward so the roughly 60 g body still spins strongly. The store describes a speed like wind and a combination of power-derived spin and mount presence with the stress-free movement of a light body.

title: Tsuzure
content: History / AboutTsuzure (綴) is the signature model of Yuto Sato (サトウユウト), an en player and national-championship 1A division finalist. It is en's first metal-rim model, a three-layer build of polycarbonate (PC) body, A6061 core, stainless steel rim and an outer A7075 aluminum rim. The PC body concentrates base weight toward the perimeter while the stainless rim is set slightly inside the outermost edge, giving near mid-ship handling with strong spin and fast response. Its step-straight shape is meant to be straightforward; the store pitches it for competition yet comfortable for everyday play. It ships in a special pouch engraved with the Tsuzure logo and includes no goods.

title: Wadatsumi
content: History / AboutWadatsumi (海神) is described by YoYoStoreRewind as the horizontal-specialized bi-metal that en considers ideal. The name derives from the sea imagery of the horizon. It is built to resist the spin loss common in horizontal tricks while remaining easy to move in other tricks, with attention to resisting tilt and posture stability. The actual weight is in the high 67 g range, giving a solid feel at rest and in motion with a moderately firm feel. Its bi-metal spin power is tuned into easy-to-handle specs.

title: Wadatsumi: Yu
content: History / AboutWadatsumi: Yu (海神:悠) turns Wadatsumi into a mono-metal and is the first model in the 'Yu' series, which rebuilds mainly competition-oriented models from another angle. The larger diameter gives solid spin from the throw and stable posture during play. Though large, the actual weight is not heavy and it moves lighter than expected. The inverse shape's spin stability is inherited from the bi-metal version, balancing resistance to tilting and ease of handling. It is meant to be easier to handle and reach more hands.

title: Encore
content:
History / About
The Encore was released in 2024, its name suggesting a return or second act — possibly a revisit of an earlier G2 design philosophy or profile. Available in Pacific Storm, Plasmaberries, and Reverse Rainbow Road colorways. Full specs not publicly documented at time of research.

title: Energy Dome Side Effects
content:
Energy Domes are available in:

Aluminum: Multiple Colors

Brass

title: Enigma
content:
History / About
The next flagship. Enigma. Full sized, heavily rimweighted and smooth like rising eagles in the morning.

Production Runs

Pre-Production #1 (September 2009) — 25 units, Titanium; D54.10mm / W40.90mm / 71.00g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (December 2009) — 95 units, Blue; D54.10mm / W40.90mm / 67.00g. Bearing: L. Finish: CandyBlast.
Pre-Production #2 (October 2010) — 5 units, Gold/Green; D54.10mm / W40.90mm / 67.00g. Bearing: D. Finish: Candodize.
Run #2 (April 2011) — 80 units, Gold/Green; D54.10mm / W40.90mm / 67.00g. Bearing: D. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #3 (August 2012) — 25 units, Orange/Red; D54.10mm / W40.90mm / 66.00g. Bearing: L. Finish: CandyBlast.

title: Enigmatica
content: William Chow's third C3 signature — a wide bi-metal designed for technical and horizontal play. Price: $100–$110.

title: Aurus
content: History / AboutAccording to YoYoExpert, Enjoy Circle is a new yo-yo company from Russia and the Aurus was its debut release (YoYoSam lists it from November 2024; YoYoExpert lists January 2025). It is a bi-metal made of 7075 aluminum with stainless steel rings and an H-shape profile with an open catch zone. Enjoy Circle states the goal was a quality, confident and strong bi-metal that keeps a unique feel. Each yo-yo ships in a custom box with a cotton pouch, 4 stickers, response pads, a concave bearing, 10 white and 10 yellow strings and a stat card. Designed in Russia.

title: Domain Expansion
content:
About the Domain Expansion
ENSO's Domain Expansion inverts conventional bimetal logic by using Grade 5 titanium as the primary weight-distribution element inside a 7068 aluminum body. The enlarged inner titanium ring generates powerful stability and effortless control. The design evolved from an unreleased prototype, refined with proportional adjustments to the ring for enhanced performance. Available in Raw with Rainbow Ring ("Unlimited Void") and Black with Raw Ring ("Infinite Night") colorways.

title: Dragon Quest
content:
About the Dragon Quest
ENSO's Dragon Quest is a tri-material construction yo-yo built from six precision-machined components: a Delrin/POM body, an anodized 6061 aluminum inner ring, and stainless steel outer rims. Inspired by the classic YoYoJam Quest, the design delivers fast, stable, powerful play suited to horizontal tricks, bangers, and DNA-style combos. The aluminum ring receives the same finish attention typically reserved for main throw bodies.

title: Equanimity
content:
About the Equanimity

The Equanimity is Enso Yoyo's 7068 aluminum adaptation of their original titanium release, the UI. Released in March 2022, it carries the same wide-body, compact-diameter profile into a more accessible price bracket. The 7068 alloy — stronger than the more common 6061 — allowed Enso to maintain thin wall construction while bringing the retail price down to $80.

The Equanimity later served as the direct predecessor to The Brolly (2026), which Enso describes as "an updated, wider version of the Equanimity."

title: Gear 5
content:
About the Gear 5

The Gear 5 is Enso Yoyo's first competition-oriented design, released in September 2024. A bimetal with dual stainless steel rims on both the inner and outer edges of a 7075 aluminum body, the Gear 5 delivers the rim-weighted stability and spin time demanded by technical competitive play. At 50mm wide, it prioritizes string accessibility for whips and hops without sacrificing control.

Team Enso member Marc Zuno, who reached the 1A finals at the 2024 World YoYo Contest (18th place), threw the Gear 5 throughout his 2024 competitive season. His Prism Paradise colorway — cherry blossom pink with iridescent stainless steel rims — was released as his signature edition. Levi White's Augusta Purple colorway was released simultaneously. The Gear 5 was later followed by the Gear 2, a smaller-diameter training variant of the same competition-focused lineage.

title: Metatron’s Cube
content:
About the Metatron's Cube

The Metatron's Cube is Enso Yoyo's Damascus titanium monometal, released in April 2024 at $750. Enso describes it as the first full-size Damascus titanium yo-yo ever produced. Damascus steel — a layered composite of multiple metal alloys folded and acid-etched to reveal a wave-patterned surface — makes each unit visually unique. At 61g the Metatron's Cube plays exceptionally light for its size.

The shape follows the same diameter and width profile as the original UI and Equanimity, placing the Metatron's Cube in a clear design lineage across Enso's first three yo-yos. No colorways exist; each unit's Damascus pattern is its own.

title: Ohio (Prototype)
content: AboutAn April 2023 collector sale documents a yo-yo identified by its owner as the Enso Ohio prototype. The owner described it as a heavy titanium prototype with some vibration. Manufacturer specifications, design history, production quantity, and any public retail release remain unverified.Collector listing, April 16, 2023.

title: UI
content:
About the UI

The UI was Enso Yoyo's very first product, released in April 2021. A Grade 5 titanium monometal, the UI broke from convention with an exceptionally wide profile relative to its diameter — a shape Enso had not seen explored in the titanium space. The design accommodated both tight technical play and broader string maneuvers, using titanium's density to concentrate weight at the rims without additional hardware.

Priced at $400, the UI was produced in a small run with several finish options: Raw Blasted, Polished, Aqua, Rose Gold, and Indigo. It later served as the shape foundation for the Equanimity (7068 aluminum, 2022) and, more distantly, the SSJ GOD MODE (2026). Team Enso member Marc Zuno has called the UI his all-time favorite throw.

title: Envy64
content: The Envy64 was a lighter-weight iteration of the Envy, produced shortly after in response to player feedback that the original ~70g was too heavy for competition. The identical H-profile geometry was retained in full; only the weight was reduced to 64g by removing material. Named directly after its weight. The Envy64 became the more popular competition choice of the two models, pairing the groundbreaking H-profile with a weight more suited to extended contest combos. Available in bead-blasted finish variants with "ENVY 64" laser engraving.

title: EOM
content: History / AboutPOM 4A competition yo-yo preceding the hybrid GJ signature successor.

title: EOS
content:
From Sputnik:

"The EOS yo-yo is named after the Greek goddess of dawn. It marks the beginning of a new day, just as our expertisetransforms raw, sophisticated materials into intricate designs. Like the first light revealing the world's finest details, we bring precision and artistry to the creation of EOS, unveiling beauty where complexity meets craftsmanship.

EOS is a powerhouse in a compact form - a premium slightly undersized stainless steel yo-yo built for players who demand both precision and punch. Crafted from high-density stainless steel, it delivers an intense spin with unmatched stability, defying its smaller profile. EOS is lightning-fast yet incredibly controlled, making it perfect for tight, technical maneuvers while still packing enough power for dynamic combos. Its finely tuned weight distribution ensures a satisfyingly strong throw, embodying the perfect balance between finesse and force. Whether you're pushing the limits of your creativity or mastering intricate tricks, EOS is a true statement of refined performance in a sleek, slightly undersized design."

title: Epiphanion
content: History / AboutDistinct retail model documented by Rewind; Shibuya/Lucky Bag versions are editions.

title: Equilibrium
content: Marcus Koh's third and final signature model, the Equilibrium features a step-straight profile combining the Magnum side face with the Ares Star body. Designed for horizontal and difficult-control moves, supporting exceptionally long sleepers. Made from 6061 aluminum.

title: Equinox
content: About the EquinoxThe Equinox is the signature model of 2005 4A World Champion John Narum, notable as the first offstring yo-yo to incorporate a midship metal weight ring, increasing spin duration without significantly raising injury risk on drops. It can also function as an oversized 1A yo-yo, making it unusually versatile.

title: ERCIM
content:
History / About
"ERCIM" stands for "Electro Retro Combobulator Interdimensional Machine." Special cone-shaped side caps allow external string mounting and fingerspins.

title: ERCIM Battle Grade
content:
From Rewind Worldwide:

"A full metal yo-yo the likes of which we haven't seen before. ERCIM makes possible some pretty nostalgic tricks!

Have you ever seen a yo-yo mount on the outside of the body? Back in the day, this mod used an extra long axle that extended out from the sides of the yo-yo (a little bit like onedrop's side effects), creating a new surface on which you could mount the yo-yo string. The ERCIM sports a set of special side caps that make this kind of trick possible. Not only can you mount the yo-yo normally, but with the unique body design, it's possible to mount on the string on the "outside" surface peeking from the side face. This design is different from the original long axles that were used, and this means there's plenty of potential for new trick development using the ERCIM. As an added bonus, this side face has another special property that makes it great for practicing a newer kind of trick: fingerspins. The cone-shaped cap zeroes in on your fingertip and centers itself immediately, so even players who have never landed a fingerspin before can hit it easily.

We're not sure how well this design would serve on a contest stage, but that doesn't seem to be its intended purpose. The ERCIM is a novel, unique yo-yo meant for casual play, trick development, and a fun exploration of the possibilities of yo-yo.

You might be wondering what the name means; it's an acronym for "Electro Retro Combobulator Interdimensional Machine." This design lets you play on several different planes, bringing back an old idea in a new and exciting way. Despite its gimmicky appearance, we think the ERCIM is going to leave a lasting mark on Sengoku's history.

*If you're having any difficulty opening up the ERCIM, be sure to use your palms to apply some pressure to the protruding side caps as you unscrew them. Otherwise they may seem to spin freely without coming apart."

title: Esper
content:
History / About
The Esper is GWAY Throws’ eighth release, revisiting the D-bearing monometal formula with a refined approach to the power-versus-agility balance. Like the Daredevil and Malivore before it, the undersized profile and D-bearing configuration produce a lively, responsive feel that distinguishes it from standard competition throws.

title: Essence
content: AboutEssence is a 50/50 blend of rayon and Maxi-Lock stretch nylon in the Throw-Yo Threads Comfort family. Normal disposition, moderate velocity, and lasting shelf life make it a dependable everyday string with a soft feel. Available in Cassium and Aqueous colorways alongside monocolor.

title: Current
content:
About
The Current represents Eternal Throw's late-era output: an unusually shaped wide throw that breaks from the rim-heavy performance philosophy of earlier models. Community reviewers in 2019 described it as "not much rim weight but wide, agile and fun" with a comparison to a large-format WM2 — a boutique-tier underrated throw oriented toward agility and comfort over raw power.
Distributed partly through a monthly yo-yo subscription club service. No dedicated launch announcement was found, suggesting a quieter release than the earlier Victory, Elysian, and Sesh drops.

title: Elysian
content:
About
Announced in September 2014 and used competitively at the 2014 Canadian Nationals before its public release — taking both 1st and 2nd place finishes — the Elysian was Eternal Throw's most technically refined design to date. Kyle Hedges also used it to win 5A at PNWR 2015.
Its most distinctive element is the cup geometry: an inner divot channels toward the axle hole creating a smooth bowl-like funnel, while a beveled contact point at the fingertip dramatically reduces friction during fingerspins. Early reviewers documented 30+ second sustained fingerspin holds. The steep curved H-profile pushes rim weight outward for max spin time and stability across long combo strings and horizontal play lines. Available in a Seattle Seahawks-themed colorway.

title: Sesh
content:
About
Designed for the kind of throw you pick up and don't put down for hours. The Sesh is a large, rim-heavy H-profile that prioritizes long spin times and stability over agility — power without sluggishness. Its oversized form factor fits snugly around the finger for comfort during extended play.
Eternal Throw worked through multiple prototype phases beginning in late 2015. A Halloween 2016 pre-release generated strong community response before the full launch on January 25, 2017. YoYoExpert described it as smooth performance that balances power with playability. Pre-release Halloween 2016; full online release January 25, 2017 at 8 PM EST.

title: The Sesh
content:
History / About
The Sesh was released by Eternal Throw on January 25, 2017 (with a limited pre-release around Halloween 2015). Designed to keep players going through extended sessions, its oversized profile fits snugly around the finger for a comfortable feel while the wide rim-heavy H-shape provides powerful spin and excellent stability.

title: Victory
content:
About
Conceived on the drive home from the 2011 National Yo-Yo Contest, the Victory was Eternal Throw's first product and the throw that put the Seattle brand on the map. Chad Sage and Free Hinton collaborated with One Drop Design to produce the mold, and every unit was machined at One Drop's facility in Eugene, OR.
The Victory ships with One Drop's Side Effect axle system — swappable weighted inserts pressed into the hubs — and comes standard with the lightweight mini-disc Side Effects that give the throw its characteristic floaty, maneuverable feel. The double-rim butterfly profile pushes mass to the outer edges for strong spin stability without sacrificing approachability for intermediate 1A players. It launched at midnight on October 27, 2012.

title: Ether
content: AboutEther is a 50/50 blend of trilobal polyester and spun poly in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Normal disposition with brisk velocity and lasting shelf life gives it a balanced performance character — slightly coarser than the soft-feel strings but fast and durable. Available in Crocoite, Folium, and Incarnadine colorways alongside monocolor.

title: Euphonious
content:
History / About
The Euphonious represents Anomaly Yo-Yos’ most technically ambitious solo release — a full stainless steel monometal with an organic catch zone profile. Nearly a year of prototyping preceded its release in late 2019. Full steel construction gives the Euphonious a distinctive play character: dense, glass-smooth, and described by players as “light and quick” and “peppy” despite sitting heavier than its compact dimensions suggest. Three finish variants were produced. The Euphonious was featured in the Monthly Throw subscription box (February 2020, Tier 2) and a promotional video was created featuring competitive player Pavel Shiyanov.

title: Evil-Yo
content:
History / About
The Evil-Yo is MonkeyfingeR Design’s debut product, establishing the company’s identity from its very first release. The design features a distinctive trumpet-like H-shape profile with concave inner steps — an unusual form at the time. The first three colorways were named after the three mystic apes: Mizaru (See No Evil), Kikazaru (Hear No Evil), and Iwazaru (Speak No Evil). Two official production runs were made.

title: Evolution
content:
History / About
The Evolution was released in 2024 and quickly became one of G2's most active models, with both a standard 6061 version and an AL7 Evolution using 7068 aluminum (not 7075 — G2 labels their 7068 releases under the AL7 banner). The AL7 Evolution has received a larger number of colorway drops than the 6061 base version, including Patreon-exclusive colorways (Frogger, Sea of Flames, Oceanic Detonation) distributed only to G2's Patreon subscribers.

title: Evolve
content: The Evolve is the signature yo-yo of Justin Dauer of Team Duncan. He used This yo-yo to win the 2024 US Nationals 1A division and place 6th in the 2024 World YoYo Contest 1A division. The Evolve was initially sold through Rewind Worldwide, before landing for sale on Justin's website.

title: Evora 2020
content:
History / About
A revisited version of the original 2015 Evora, updated for modern play standards. Exact specifications were not widely published. Appears in the Luftverk personal archive as a collectible item. Revisits the H-shape brutalist design language that started the brand, offering collectors a chance to own an updated take on the model that started it all.

title: Evora (Original)
content:
History / About
The first Luftverk release and the first production titanium yo-yo to feature an H-shape profile, inspired by Hans Asplund’s “Architectural Brutalism” style. Despite the H-shape, weight is evenly distributed across the edges and mid-sections rather than purely on the rims, allowing it to spin longer. The very limited AMS2488 Type II version used a fully ceramic C-bearing to eliminate rust and corrosion risk. Produced in extremely small numbers and sold for around $300 USD. Met with immediate success and positive reviews, launching Luftverk as a serious player in the premium titanium market.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (metal standard); full ceramic C-bearing on AMS2488 Type II version

title: Evora Ti 7075
content:
History / About
A bimetal redesign of the original Evora, first released September 2016. Where most contemporary bimetals used dense stainless steel rings, the Evora Ti 7075 uses titanium weight rings placed inset on a 7075 aluminum body — making it lighter and faster while still spinning powerfully. Even the axle is titanium, shaving weight at the core. The Bead Blasted Black colorway was made as a homage to the SPYY Radian Mk II, a legendary yoyo of the mid-school era. The result is a nimble, fast throw that balances power and control in a way heavier bimetals cannot.

title: Executive
content: The Executive was a prototype titanium looping yoyo. As far as I know, and have been told, only one of these was ever made. I do not have any specs on these, other than it used the B.S.P axle system.

title: Exia
content:
From MK1:

"The Exia is a favorite competition yoyo amongst the MK1 team. It looks good. It plays good. What more could you want?"

There were three runs of the Exia, the original Nov 2020 release followed by releases in Feb 2021 and Apr 2022.

B-Grades

One colorway, glossy clear with rainbow rings, was only available as a b-grade yoyo.

Yoyo Tricks Exclusive Colorways

Three different colorways of the Exia were exclusive to yoyotricks.com.

April 8th, 2023 Run

The third run of the Exia contained three signature colorways for EOS44, Luis Lizardo, and Connor Sheahan. There was also a  collaboration with Scales Collective to create a Scales Edition, and with YoyoExpert to create a YoyoExpert edition. Oh, yeah. There was also a pink one.

Scales Collective Colorway

YoyoExpert Colorway

title: Faceless
content: AboutThe Faceless (千面, meaning "a thousand faces") is EXPECTmake's budget-accessible model, released August 2024 in collaboration with TOP YO. A full polycarbonate design with thick walls and a wide H-profile, the Faceless features an interchangeable center piece that allows players to swap color combinations — the brand has indicated potential future shell shape variants using the same system. The recessed center dimple enables finger spins. Unresponsive; bind required. $19.99.Colorways: Clear Pink + Black, Clear Green + Blue, Clear Green + Black, Clear Yellow + Clear, and additional combinations.

title: Frozen
content: AboutThe Frozen is EXPECTmake's debut and flagship model, released in 2021 in collaboration with TOP YO. A bimetal with stainless steel rims and a 7003 aluminum body, the Frozen's defining feature is a hollow hexagram cutout CNC-milled into the aluminum side face — the cavity inlaid with a clear polycarbonate cap that prevents string contact while preserving the visual geometry, resembling stained glass. Removing mass from the sidebody center pushes weight concentration outward to the steel rims for strong stability and spin. Limited to approximately 100 units worldwide at $149.99.Colorways: Elegance (Navy/Pink/Silver), Frost (Blue/Silver/Silver), Royal (Black/Orange/Gold), Black/Rose Gold Rim. Includes a 5-cut bearing.

title: Frozen II
content: AboutThe Frozen II is the second-generation evolution of EXPECTmake's debut concept, released in 2024 in collaboration with TOP YO. Wider than the original at 46mm, it uses 6061 aluminum for the body (versus the Frozen's 7003) and retains stainless steel rims, now with polycarbonate covers on both the string contact area and the side face plate. Each colorway receives a uniquely CNC-milled pattern in the side face, making every variant a distinct design rather than a recolor. A recessed finger-spin center adds a play dimension absent from the original. $149.99.Colorways: Light Blue, Green, Gray, Magenta — each with unique milling.

title: FTY 138
content: History / AboutAccording to Fair Trade YoYos (via YoYoExpert), the FTY 138 is an homage to the team's punk rock upbringing and DIY ethos. The Misfits' "We Are 138" inspired the 51 x 38 mm dimensions and the name. The round shape was inspired by rounded steel roller skates, Misfits horror punk, and the oxy ti. The profile gap keeps a slight "schwall" as in earlier models, though less pronounced, with large rims rounded into the cup that provide ample rim weight. Designed in the USA, made in China.

title: Project Ti
content: History / AboutAccording to YoYoSam, Project Ti is modeled after the Fair Trade YoYos Project Y but made in titanium. It is described as a power-forward throw designed to take advantage of its weight placement, with a size and shape that fit comfortably in the hand. It was to be available in blasted and raw finishes.

title: PV44
content: History / AboutAccording to YoYoSam, the PV44 is the second release from Fair Trade YoYos. It has a slightly undersized diameter and a comfortable profile that blurs the line between organic O shape and hard H shape. The design focuses on float and ease of movement for a laid-back feel.

title: Skateboard Wheel
content: AboutThe Skateboard Wheel was the sole product released by Fakies, available in 24 graphic variants licensed from four skateboarding companies: Birdhouse, Blind, World Industries, and Speed Demons. The yo-yo was shaped and colored to replicate an actual skateboard wheel, with each unit printed with artwork from its respective brand.The line was developed with input from yo-yo player Brian Cabildo of the DXL Crew and manufactured in China. A Blind-branded variant is held in the collection of The Strong National Museum of Play (Rochester, NY, Object ID 108.3858).Variants24 graphic variants across four licensed brands. Confirmed designs include Birdhouse "Pyro," Birdhouse "Samurai Sword," Birdhouse "Jeremy Klein," Blind "Skeleton Skull," Blind "Stars & Stripes," and multiple World Industries and Speed Demons designs.

title: Falcon
content:
History / About
Falcon is the widest entry in the ILYY line. Full sized, rimweighted, dead smooth.

Production Runs

Pre-Production #1 (June 2009) — Red/Titanium; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 67.30g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #1 (October 2009) — 100 units, Red/Titanium; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 66.90g. Finish: Candodize.
Special #1 (December 2009) — 100 units, Red/Green; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 66.90g. Finish: Candodize.
Special #2 — 25 units, Blue/Titanium; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 66.90g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #2 (February 2011) — 52 units, Red/Titanium; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 67.50g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Special #3 — 25 units, Green; D54.00mm / W44.20mm / 67.50g. Finish: CandyBlast.

title: Fallen Angel
content:
History / About
The Fallen Angel is a collaboration between Anomaly Yo-Yos and an individual named Jordan, and is the smallest release in the Anomaly catalog. The undersized organic form factor and D-bearing configuration produce a fast, nimble play character suited to pocket carry and casual sessions. A titanium variant was reportedly produced in limited quantities alongside the standard aluminum version.

title: Fat Tire 20/20
content:
From One Drop:

"A 20/20 Retrospective Edition is when we make a small change to a model using hindsight to make it better. In this case, it’s the Fat Tire 20/20.

Controversial statement: Scientifically, the Fat Tire 20/20 is more Floaty than the original.

Conventionally, yo-yo play descriptors have generally been considered to be largely subjective. However, we happen to have a collaborator that you may not have heard of. If you were on the One Drop Forums back in the day, you might have come across a user called “Dirty Birdy”. He is a long time friend and creative collaborator for One Drop and his name is Chris Greiner.  Chris is a PhD Physicist who has been doing on-going research into the physics of yo-yos. The standard physics of a yo-yo have long been understood but Chris has taken it further and examined play characteristics that have been described by players. He has delved into being able to figure out just from CAD, if a yo-yo design is going to be more or less prone to vibe - this has been hugely helpful to us. Everyone who appreciates One Drop should know that Chris plays a big role in our design work. We are so blessed to be able to collaborate with him.

In this case we are talking about Floaty, a descriptor that has been around a long time. It means something along the lines of “FEELS light in play”. The actual weight of the yo-yo doesn’t seem to be as much of a factor in this feeling. As a matter of fact, the Fat Tire 20/20 is actually about a gram heavier than the original. Weight distribution is the key here. Chris examined yo-yos which were universally considered to be Floaty and was able to figure out what they all had in common through deep physics. 

Chris proposed this re-work to the Fat Tire to specifically make it more Floaty. Most of the change is to the underside of the rim where you will see that it looks quite different. The profile shape is still the same.  The re-work stems entirely from physics analysis. Normally our designing is done with a combination of  intuition/experience, play testing, appearance and physics so this is different and very cool.

Getting this yo-yo out in the world is a continuation of the science where we now get to see just how subjective the feel of Floaty is.  We are looking forward to hearing what people think. We are, of course, aware that by pointing this out we are probably influencing the results but either way we thought this would be a lot of fun and the Fat Tire 20/20 is awesome."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)
meta.yya_weight: 64.1g (67.4g with aluminum Flat Cap Side Effects)

title: FAY
content: AboutThe FAY is yoyorecreation's accessible entry point — an oversized V-shape plastic with removable side caps that allow the response system to be swapped between responsive and unresponsive configurations. Beginner players can start with responsive play and transition to full unresponsive at their own pace without needing a second yo-yo. A NC Empire × SPINNS collaboration edition in ivory colorway with pop-art side cap graphics was released in 2018. A Kumame-branded colorway edition also exists.

title: Feather
content:
The following is archived from 44EMPORIUM's website:

I don't even know where to start this off. It is 5 PM, Thursday the 19th, and I am sitting in front of my computer, just blankly staring at the monitor, overwhelmed with the amount of work.

I am from a small and remote city in Canada - it is about a 3-hour drive away from Toronto. In July of 2022 - I just impulsively decided to come to the YoYoToronto meetup. I craved a community of yoyoers since I only meet them at the big national contest maybe once a year or less.

I met a bunch of cool kids that now I become good friends with including... just everyone. I love this community.Long story short, I started showing up to their monthly meetup regularly - I don't think I missed a single one yet.This got me attached to the Canadian / Toronto community a lot.

44Emporium started as a store that sells a selection of yoyos that I love. Jeff helped me set up everything I needed to start off with; and I was like yeah, why not since there are no active yoyo stores in Canada.

What this allowed me was to help my local buddies get the yoyos they wanted a lot easier, and this was such a wholesome thing to do.I also sponsored local contests including 2023 and 2024 Canadian Nats.

To be frankly honest, if I did not feel this way I wouldn't have been kept doing 44emporium. I struggle just to break even as a small store compared to the list of stores there are right now. This was literally the only thing that made me inclined to just stick with this idea.

One random day - I bought this yoyo called the GBP from G2Yoyos. 48 grams, bimetal and it played surprisingly well and was pleasing for a light yoyo like this.

Fast forward, a year later, I needed money so I was clearing out my collection - and GBP was sold to Evan Cui at one of the random meetup days in Toronto.

This was literally the very start of the Feather project; because Evan loved it. Like he loved loved it at that time.Evan told me how he doesn't buy new yoyos because he just thinks they are all the same, but this time it was different.

This is when Evan saw the potential in lightweight yoyos that are under 60 grams.

He enthusiastically shared with me a bunch of 3D printed prototypes that are sub 60g that he wants to eventually machine. This was only one of the prototypes, he made like 10 different iterations so please go check out his blog if you are curious about it.

At that time, honestly, I didn't see the vision. They were still fun but that was about it. It died in 10 seconds, pulse vibes, just... everything bad you can imagine of.

But he proved me wrong with this one. The very first feather prototype which we didn't even have the name of at this point. That little thing engraved is a chicken. you know, Evan's Instagram tag is walk_the_chiken so...

Keep this in mind - Evan was still unsure of which brand to release this yoyo under at this point. Toronto people and I just made a joke about yeah just release it under 44emporium lol

Evan loved it, I also loved it. I love fun and unique yoyos. But we agreed that something is missing... Evan's main concern was the little cuts on the profile caught the string while doing horizontal tricks. My main concern was the yoyo was too weak.I have this strong ego when it comes to yoyoing. I don't want to release yoyo under my brand or for it to be associated with my name if it is not "cool". Sounds funny but I do wanna feel confident enough about the product that I sell, whether it is someone else's product of my original lineup. That is kind of a rough thought I had with the first prototype.

Then Evan made changes based on his liking and everyone else's feedback including mine, we just sent the second prototype. This was... this was good.I remember trying it and immediately going "Yup, let's release it under 44EMPORIUM."This must've been the point where I suggested the name "Feather". Lightweight, and it goes well with the current engraving / Evan's iconic Instagram username.

Evan optimized as much as he could yet still keeping the maneuverability of 55g yoyo.One last problem we had to tackle was the response area. It was a bit slippy. I don't exactly know what Evan did to fix this because I am not the designer, so again, please go read his blog if you are curious as to what actually happened between this one and the last prototype haha.

Anyways, this one just had all of our problems fixed and we were at a point where all the local Toronto people could say "Damn, I can compete with this.", and it still has the floatiness of its lightweight. It also features a nice little 44E logo which is kind of a secondary logo I use for 44EMPORIUM.

This is the one both Evan and I used for Canadian Nationals and Worlds this year. I didn't accomplish much competition-wise, but Evan got 2nd place at Nats.Also, lots of people tried this at Worlds and we received numerous positive comments which gives me some hope.

photo by jacky le

So here we are, the very first original model from 44EMPORIUM, the FEATHER.Evan is the one who designed this and made it possible. I am just riding along, so please give all the credit to Evan.

My goal with the original lineup is to release as many interesting signature yoyos as possible from fellow local buddies of mine to make their yoyo see the light of the world (2 different prototypes are in the works), so supporting this project helps us to grow and push out more interesting stuffs out to the yoyo world.

Thank you for spending time to read my spiel. I really appreciate it.

title: Feather Infinity
content:
From Layer Infinity:

"The 44EMPORIUM Feather was originally a 55g bi-metal designed by Evan (IG: @walk_the_chiken) to be super light and fast for competition. It now has a fully 3D printed plastic version!

The 3D printed Feather Infinity stays faithful to the bi-metal Feather's size, shape, and its most defining weight of 55 grams. Without metal rims Feather Infinity doesn't have the same rim weight, so the same 55g is more spread out throughout the profile. This makes Feather Infinity feel even lighter and faster than the bi-metal Feather. Of all the material variations in the Feather series, the Feather Infinity feels the lightest and the fastest, by far!"

title: Anser
content: The Anser is Featherspin’s homage to the Galactic Goose. Its design removes the predecessor’s rim divot and widens the profile to improve modern string play while keeping its playful character.Featherspin listed the Anser at $85. The brand describes it as a tribute to the earlier design; no collaboration with its original makers is claimed.

title: Ibis (Prototype)
content: The Ibis draws on the birds and Art Deco atmosphere of Wilmington, North Carolina, and on older YoYoJam designs. Its rounded profile combines a 7077 aluminum core with a POM outer shell and a hollow space between them.Featherspin named its colorways Wrack Line, Shell Island, and Mud Flats after Wilmington landscapes. The announced price is $85. The store currently labels the model “Coming soon.”

title: The Owl (Prototype)
content: The Owl is an experimental Featherspin design offered through its Aviary R&D Department. The Grade 5 titanium yo-yo has an integrated titanium spike, a 53 mm diameter, and a 46 mm width.The brand offered one of five prototypes through this listing at $280. A public production release has not been confirmed.

title: Vogelkop
content: Featherspin designed the Vogelkop around the courtship display of the Vogelkop bird-of-paradise. Flowing ridges and a broad profile give this compact yo-yo a strong visual presence.The brand offered three half-swap colorways: Courtship Display (blue and black), Lady in Waiting (brown and black), and Kopulation (blue and brown). The listed launch price was $85.

title: Featherweight Canary
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Featherweight Canary is the sequel to our 2018 collaboration with Radical Seas, this time reborn with a new bimetal design and ultra lightweight design. We wanted to maintain the playful spirit of the original while further pushing the specs away from the competition. With a 55g body and D bearing construction, the Featherweight Canary will bring out the new flows from within you that you have yet to discover."

title: Be-A-Sport Baseball
content: History / AboutA plastic baseball-shaped yo-yo from Festival's Be-A-Sport series. The Yo-Yo Museum says the series began selling in the late 1960s and continued, under at least five packaging redesigns, until the very late 1970s, and included a football, basketball, baseball, eight ball, tennis ball, bowling ball and golf ball. The earliest dated museum example of this model is 1968. After Festival closed, the molds resurfaced, and the museum notes Duncan appears to have acquired them for its 2003 sports ball line. Festival Toys was a division of Union Wadding Company of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, and was associated with Wilf Schlee Jr., owner of Cheerio and Hi-Ker.

title: Big Zapper
content: History / AboutThe Big Zapper was a one-piece beechwood yo-yo similar in size and shape to Duncan's maple Tournament, made in Sweden for Festival by Elfverson & Company. The Yo-Yo Museum documents a green model sold around 1967-1970 for 59 cents and later models (red, black) sold from about 1970-1974 for 69 cents; the card tagline reads the semi-pro-yo with trick string. The museum says Festival made Big Zappers for most of the company's run, in versions with imprinted logos or stickers. Festival Toys was a division of Union Wadding Company of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, and was associated with Wilf Schlee Jr., owner of Cheerio and Hi-Ker.

title: Dragonfly
content: History / AboutA plastic butterfly yo-yo in Festival's line, sold on a bubble card with a mail-in offer for Bob Rule's Yo-Yo Secrets booklet. The Yo-Yo Museum notes Union Wadding let the Dragonfly trademark expire after 20 years in late 1991; Playmaxx later used the name and Duncan now owns the Dragon Fly trademark. Dated 1971 in the museum catalog. Festival Toys was a division of Union Wadding Company of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, and was associated with Wilf Schlee Jr., owner of Cheerio and Hi-Ker.

title: Joe Namath Official Professional Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutA plastic, fixed-axle yo-yo made by Union Wadding Company and sold in the Festival line, mounted on a bubble card with a football graphic. A picture sticker of quarterback Joe Namath, then with the New York Jets, appears on one half. The card back included a coupon for a discount at the Joe Namath Instructional Football Camp, valid in the US until July 1, 1976. Dated 1975-1976 in the Yo-Yo Museum catalog; original retail price $1 USD.

title: Mickey Mouse
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum shows a blue, three-piece wooden Festival yo-yo, about 2 inches in diameter and 39 g, with a face view of Mickey Mouse carrying the Disney trademark, dated 1964. The museum says Festival made a number of Disney character yo-yos, some sold in Hallmark packaging through its chain of stores.

title: Official NHL Hockey Puck Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutFestival's Official NHL Hockey Puck Yo-Yo was made by Union Wadding Co. and carries a paper team sticker; the museum example is the Vancouver Canucks, using the stick-in-rink crest worn on jerseys from 1970-1978. A mail-in coupon for Bob Rule's Yo-Yo Secrets booklet that expired Sept. 30, 1973 dates the carded yo-yo to 1972-1973. The body is two black plastic halves forming a short cylinder; original retail price $1 USD. The museum notes the puck yo-yos were not part of the Be-A-Sport series.

title: Orange Bird Sunshine Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutThe Walt Disney Orange Bird yo-yo, known as the Sunshine Yo-Yo, was a promotional yo-yo featuring the Orange Bird, a character created by Disney with the Florida Citrus Commission. The Yo-Yo Museum dates it to about 1971-1973 and says it was made by Union Wadding Company, known as Festival Toys. It came in a tournament-style shape with a Have a nice day sticker and a butterfly shape with a Be happy...smile sticker; other sticker phrases exist. The reverse is hot stamped with a Walt Disney Productions credit. No confirmed original price was found.

title: Screamer
content: History / AboutThe Screamer was an all-metal, whistling yo-yo in the Duncan Tournament shape, with airholes in the rim that produce a whistling sound as it spins. The Yo-Yo Museum dates the first version from about 1967 to 1972 (card priced 69 cents) and a second pink-and-black version from about 1974 to 1976 (priced $1.00). Festival made two different Screamers and the museum calls Festival the last company to produce a tin whistler. Festival Toys was a division of Union Wadding Company of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, and was associated with Wilf Schlee Jr., owner of Cheerio and Hi-Ker.

title: Zapper
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes this blue Zapper with a white stripe as the first Zapper, with larger and smaller versions made later. It is a one-piece wooden yo-yo about 2 inches in diameter, made in Sweden by the Elfverson company (a Sweden mark is impressed on the back), dated 1970 in the museum catalog. Festival Toys was a division of Union Wadding Company of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, and was associated with Wilf Schlee Jr., owner of Cheerio and Hi-Ker.

title: Fever
content: About the FeverThe Fever is the signature yo-yo of Hungarian National Champion Balint "Vooper" Farkas, featuring an inverse-round body with a thick, flattened outer rim almost entirely covered by aluminum alloy rim material. This design gives it the feel of a metal-heavy throw at a hybrid price point. The compact 54.45mm diameter suits players who prefer a nimble, precise feel.

title: BatTisai
content: AboutThe BatTisai is Few & Far Between's first titanium yoyo and a tribute to the legendary VsNYYC Battosai. After completing the Inception, the FFB team wanted their first titanium throw to have a truly distinctive shape. Finding an original Battosai in their collection, they contacted VsNYYC's Heath, who gave his blessing to remake it. Patrick Dressel then refined the gap width and proportions for modern unresponsive play.Artwork by Luis Atilano (ATILA). Limited to 39 units. Ships in a custom soft-touch box with a silk purple pouch, ZipLine string, custom stickers, enamel pin, and a katana letter opener.

title: Elysium
content: AboutThe Elysium is Few & Far Between's debut yoyo, released October 2020. A full-sized organic designed to stand apart from typical O-profile throws through its flared rims — adding stability and power while maintaining the floaty, comfortable feel of a classic shape. Described as "smooth, floaty, yet powerful and stable." Designed with contributions from Patrick Dressel and artwork by Chris Francz.Each Elysium shipped with matching Airetic custom string, a Dedhed Designs counterweight and string pick made by Michael Letsom, an FFB enamel pin, face mask, stickers, RSO landing pads, and tokens — all in a custom box. Released in three colorways: Mars (red), Neptune (blue), and Earth (green).

title: Inception
content: AboutThe Inception is Few & Far Between's first bi-metal yoyo, marketed as "the first production 7068 aluminum + titanium rim bi-metal yoyo." The name represents "beginning; commencement." Designed by Jonathan Saelens, Patrick Dressel, and Moises Vidal, with artwork by Celen Garcia-Vidal.Released in two colorways: Light Blue with Raw (silver) titanium rims, and Silver with Gold titanium rims. Ships with ZipLine Stranger Strings Type 50, a matching spinning top (totem), silk pouch, enamel pin, stickers, and a custom box. Includes a stainless steel concave bearing; ceramic and gold bearings also provided.

title: Taijitu
content: AboutThe Taijitu is Few & Far Between's last released yoyo, dropped October 9, 2024, on YoYoExpert. An undersized 6061 aluminum organic "built for speed," excelling at technical mounts and chopstick-style play. The name references the Taoist yin-yang symbol; each side features a tree engraving. Released in three colorways — Yin Black, Yang White (Moon Rock / micro-arc oxidation finish), and Yin Yang Fade — with half-swap combinations available on request.

title: The Dreamer
content: AboutThe Dreamer is Few & Far Between's most technically ambitious release: a tri-metal yoyo combining a 7068 aluminum body with titanium outer rings and stainless steel inner rings. Designed by team member Christopher Cotton (@theycallmecotton), it was created in collaboration with the brand Unknown. Described as "unique and greatly powerful." This was FFB's final known product before the brand went quiet in 2024.

title: The Vow
content: AboutThe Vow is Few & Far Between's second yoyo, named to represent the love and passion the owners have for each other and for yoyos. A lightweight stainless steel organic with a comfortable profile and D-bearing configuration. Designed by Patrick Dressel and Moises Vidal.Released in four colorways, each with a distinct character: "Til Death Do Us Part" (black electroplated, includes metal shovel), "Not Perfect Just Raw" (silver/polished raw, includes white quartz), "Gold Digger" (gold electroplated, includes metal shovel), and "Love at First Sight" (rose gold electroplated, includes rose quartz). Each ships with ZipLine string, silk pouch, custom counterweight, enamel pin, stickers, and a custom box. Both a concave D-bearing and flat D-bearing are included.

title: FGAL
content: AboutThe FGAL is a 2024 monometal version of JT's past representative model, the Shakushain FG. Machined from A300 aluminum — the same alloy used in the FiReal — with a step-straight profile slightly wider than the original to match modern standards. JT describes it as "an all-purpose monometal with few quirks and a straightforward, responsive feel." Available in Red.

title: FGTi
content: AboutThe FGTi is Japan Technology's titanium monometal, released in 2021. A step-straight profile in a classic 55.5mm diameter, it was positioned as JT's premium titanium string trick offering at ¥$469.99. A precursor to the aluminum FGAL, the FGTi shares design DNA with the Shakushain FG lineage. Currently sold out.

title: Fides
content: History / AboutDistinct model documented in Rewind's current-release catalog.

title: Fiesta
content: About the FiestaThe Fiesta is the original 4A signature model of Bryan Figueroa, engineered with repositioned response holes for a gentler catch and improved spin retention during missed tricks. Its lightweight plastic construction minimizes hand fatigue during extended 4A practice sessions. YoYoJam marketed it as "the new standard for offstring yo-yos" at its release.

title: Fiesta TRES
content: About the Fiesta TRESThe Fiesta TRES is Bryan Figueroa's third and final Fiesta signature model, switching from polycarbonate to POM/Delrin for improved durability and a smoother surface feel. Despite a larger diameter than the Fiesta XX, it weighs 4 grams less, enabling faster aerial movements. An upgraded Lock & Bolt system consolidates the bearing lock, response pads, and spacers into a single durable unit. It was released in 2015 as one of YoYoJam's final products before closure.

title: Fiesta XX
content: About the Fiesta XXThe Fiesta XX updates the Fiesta's design with a heavier 81.1 gram build, the Solid Spin Axle system, and a standardized Size C bearing with silicone O-ring response. Bryan Figueroa's 2007–2012 US 4A Championship run coincided with this model's active production period. Championship editions were produced for the 2011 Nationals.

title: Filament (Prototype)
content:
About
Filament was a monthly Project Torsion blend from Throw-Yo Threads, offered only to Patreon subscribers in April 2026. No public retail release has been confirmed.

title: Fire Devil
content:
From One Drop:

"***Second run Ridgeback Edition released on 12/19/2019. 2 grams lighter, ridgeback grooves in the catch zone and new colors.  120 units made.***

We love doing collaborations for a lot of reasons. One of the reasons is that it pushes us creatively.  Every maker has their own style, approach and methods. It’s so interesting to let go of having full control of your own product and to incorporate new ideas.  The end result is always something that wouldn’t exist unless these particular worlds were meshed together.

This particular collaboration with Monkeyfinger (Ray) started at Pacific Northwest Regional Contest in 2016.   Ray asked if we could sit down at some point during the contest and talk about doing something together and that is how it began.   Given that both of the companies had busy schedules and plans, work didn’t really begin on this until sometime in 2017 and now we are finally releasing 3 years later from that first meeting.  This one is special and it is worth the wait.

The idea was that Ray was going to design the yoyo in general and that One Drop (Shawn)  would add the final touches. One Drop would then doing the machining and Monkeyfinger would do the anodizing, package design, naming and art and thus the Fire Devil was born.

Each one is hand anodized by Ray in Canada and they look amazing.  As an anodizer, he is a true artist and works in small batches so he has invested a large amount of labor and love into the finish and it shows.  Available direct from One Drop and Monkeyfinger.

Releasing on January 21st from both companies' websites.  $79"

title: FiReal
content: AboutThe FiReal (also written Fireel) was Japan Technology's first string trick yo-yo, released in 2014. Machined from A300 aluminum — a 7000-series alloy — it features a distinctive inverse-round, round, and straight design that affects weight distribution. A response separator minimizes sleep loss during complex string mounting, making it equally suited for 3A and 5A in addition to 1A. Made in Hokkaido. Available in light blue, deep blue, hot pink, deep red, yellow-green, raw aluminum, and additional colorways.

title: Firecracker (Original C Bearing)
content:
History / About
The Firecracker is Recess's modern responsive slimline — designed for players who enjoy a slim, tug-responsive yo-yo but want one capable of handling modern string trick complexity and multiple layers of string. As Recess puts it, "Firecracker plays both sides." The stock rubber-shielded lubed D bearing keeps lube in place better than standard metal shields. An unresponsive grooved bearing is also included for players who want to run it fully unresponsive. The D Bearing Firecracker (current, $50) uses a D-size bearing configuration throughout and comes in Bomb Pop, Archie Kiss, and Rainbow Trout colorways. Currently in stock on recessintl.com.

meta.yya_bearing_size: D-size (rubber-shielded lubed, stock responsive); grooved unresponsive bearing also included

title: Firefox
content: Firefox is Auldey's all-metal budget competition throw, featuring bright anodized finishes in red and blue. Parallel grooves on the inner surface reduce vibe. Unresponsive design for technical 1A play.

title: Firestorm
content: About the FirestormThe Firestorm is the second collaboration yo-yo from the Yomega and YoYoJam partnership. Like the Odyssey, specific production specifications are not widely documented. Both models represent rare instances of YoYoJam collaborating with an established competitor in the yo-yo manufacturing space.

title: First Base
content:
History / About
The First Base launched alongside the Joyride and Weekend at the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest, instantly establishing Recess as a full-range brand from beginner to competition. It was designed to be affordable, durable, and genuinely useful at any skill level — fitted with a slim bearing for responsive beginner play out of the box, with a Size C grooved bearing included to convert it to unresponsive. The polycarbonate body has a flat hub that helps with fingerspins, a wide catch zone, and a comfortable shape. Recess has used the First Base as the centerpiece of their outreach program — running yo-yo classes and school workshops using it to introduce yo-yoing to new players. It has remained in continuous production since 2015 in dozens of colorways and is one of the best-selling and most recognized Recess products. The "First Bass by Jake Bullock" artist edition (2024, $25) and numerous other collaboration and artist editions have kept the model fresh. Clear and Lilac colorways are currently in stock.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Slim bearing (stock responsive); Size C grooved bearing (included for unresponsive)

title: First Base — Artist / Signature Editions
content:
History / About
The First Base has served as the canvas for numerous artist collaborations, team editions, and special colorways throughout Recess's history. The most notable named collaboration is the "First Bass by Jake Bullock" (2024, $25), which gave the longtime Recess collaborator his own edition of the beginner plastic. Tyler Severance's connection to Jake Bullock (Tyler introduced Jake to factory contact CJ Atkinson) makes this collaboration a full-circle moment in the Recess story. The First Base continues to receive new colorways and editions regularly.

title: First Base — ZipLine Edition
content: HistoryThe First Base — ZipLine Edition was released May 19, 2023 as a collaboration between Recess and ZipLine Strings. Based on the Recess First Base polycarbonate platform, ZipLine's version featured exclusive artwork by Jeremy Park and shipped with two AlphaLine strings and a special edition sticker. Sold exclusively through the ZipLine Strings store at $20, it served as an accessible entry point for customers discovering ZipLine through their string catalog. Each unit came with a half-spec C bearing for responsive play and a full-size C bearing for unresponsive conversion.

title: First Yo
content: AboutThe First Yo is Duncan's toddler-to-child entry point, constructed from a soft, impact-absorbing silicone body that is safe for young children. It ships with a shortened string to match smaller throwing arms, and its auto-return mechanism brings the yo-yo back to the hand with minimal spin required. The soft body minimizes damage when it swings into furniture or walls. Available in four bright colors and targeted at children ages 5 and up.

title: Flail (Prototype)
content:
History / About
Flail is a 5A-oriented design from Lewi (Yoyos by Lewi), also usable for 1A, announced on the YoYoExpert forums on May 15, 2026. It uses a 7075 aluminum body with an inner-ring construction. At announcement, Lewi said a production run was undecided and would depend on expressed community interest; no source confirms a run ever happened or shipped.
