title: Flatrim Fullsize
content:
From #UNBRANDED:

"The Luxury of Spin Power. The Simplest Answer to Improvement

To you, who yearns to get better.

When challenging yourself with new tricks, do you ever find yourself thinking: If only it would spin a little longer, I could calmly land this mount. That feeling is not a mistake. In fact, beginners and intermediate players aiming to improve are the ones who need Spin Power the most.

Achieving Spin Power Rivaling Bi-Metals with a Mono-Metal Flat Rim Shape

To get long spin times, I have to buy an expensive bi-metal yoyo. This is a common belief, but there is a design approach that achieves this with mono-metal. That is the adoption of the Flat Rim shape. By designing the body’s rim to be extremely flat and thick, we can concentrate weight at the very edge of the yoyo’s diameter. This shape is the most efficient and functional design for maximizing the Moment of Inertia that creates rotational persistence.

The confidence that It’s Still Spinning accelerates your progress.

The intense spin power created by the Flat Rim gives you the peace of mind that it’s still spinning, so I’m okay. This removes the panic from your fingertips and grants you the margin to surely land tricks. We know you want to stack up as many I did it! moments as possible in your limited time. This yoyo is the partner that most efficiently supports your busy daily practice.

Recommended for

Those who want spin power but are afraid of dinging an expensive bi-metal yoyo, preventing them from practicing fully.

Players who want to focus on mastering tricks.

Those who often fail during long combos or new trick practice because the spin dies out mid-trick."

title: Flawless
content: Rei Iwakura's landmark offstring signature, based on the Neo Solar as a foundation and expanded by 5mm width and 21.5g. Incorporates a bump area from the Solar Series for impeccable Soloham trick control. Comes with 3 sets of spacers providing 6 different gap settings.The first gen weighed 103.5g; substantially refined over three major iterations. The 2020 version added metal rings and reduced weight to 84.1g with decreased diameter (77mm→73mm) and increased width (62.3mm→66.5mm). Used by Iwakura throughout his world championship runs. Price: ~$99–$130.

title: Flawless Air
content: A lighter and faster offstring variant of the Flawless flagship. Signature: Rei Iwakura (7x 4A World Champion). Positioned as a complement to the original Flawless for players preferring a lighter 4A throw.

title: Flex
content:
History / About
The Flex is a 4A offstring model designed for European 4A Champion Fery Procházka (František Procházka). mowl met with Fery after the 2018 44Clash event to begin development, spending extensive time discussing shape, weight, and multiple prototypes before arriving at the final design. Fery's input focused on a model optimized for his high-level competitive style. The Flex expanded mowl's 4A offerings beyond the founder's own Anarchy signature.

title: Astro Spin
content: AboutThe Astro Spin was part of Fli-Back's 1968 product lineup, leaning into the space-race enthusiasm that permeated American toy marketing at the time. Advertised alongside Thunderbird TV imagery and space ship graphics, the Astro Spin was one of Fli-Back's later models — produced under the company's second-generation ownership before the 1972 sale to Ohio Art. It maintains the fixed-axle hardwood construction that defined every Fli-Back yo-yo.

title: Champion Style 55
content: AboutThe Champion Style 55 is an undersized wooden yo-yo produced by Fli-Back in the mid-1950s. Its most recognizable feature is the two-tone paint scheme — one half blue, the other red — paired with a gold foil "55" seal on both faces. The undersized dimensions give it a quick, snappy feel compared to Fli-Back's full-size Tournament models. The Style 55 was sold as part of Fli-Back's broader lineup during the era when the company was at peak production and distribution in High Point, North Carolina.

title: Circled Eagle
content: AboutThe Circled Eagle is a wooden Fli-Back yo-yo from the 1960s, distinguished by its gold stamp depicting an eagle enclosed within a circle. One of the more visually striking models from Fli-Back's later catalog, it was produced during the company's ownership transition and continued to represent the brand's North Carolina manufacturing heritage. Available in red and blue colorways, the Circled Eagle retains the fixed-axle hardwood construction standard to all Fli-Back yo-yos.

title: Double Circle
content: AboutThe Double Circle takes its name from the two concentric circles embossed on its foil seal — a clean, geometric design that set it apart from earlier Fli-Back models. Produced during the 1960s as the company transitioned ownership, the Double Circle represents Fli-Back's output during their later years in High Point. Like all Fli-Back yo-yos, it is constructed from turned hardwood with a fixed axle.

title: Genuine Tournament Championship
content: AboutThe Genuine Tournament Championship was the finest yo-yo Fli-Back produced — their flagship competition model of the early 1950s. Built from turned hardwood, it carried a foil seal that appeared in either blue or red variations. Its balanced weight distribution and reliable return made it the yo-yo of choice for serious competitors and enthusiasts during the height of the mid-century yo-yo craze. Fli-Back sold the Tournament Championship worldwide at a time when the company employed several hundred workers in High Point, North Carolina.

title: Genuine Tournament Championship Swirl
content: AboutThe Genuine Tournament Championship Swirl is a late-1950s variant of Fli-Back's celebrated Tournament Championship model. Distinguished by its swirl-patterned foil seal, this version runs approximately 10 grams lighter than the striped Tournament — making it noticeably more nimble on the string. Like all Fli-Back yo-yos of the era, it is turned from hardwood with a fixed axle.

title: Flightech
content: AboutThe Flightech is a collaboration between YoYoFactory and Japan Technology, released in 2025. JT handled the design work using YoYoFactory's Flight as the base platform. Machined from Delrin (Celcon/Duracon), it is JT Spacer-compatible and includes a 1.45mm spacer. The collaboration emphasizes beginner accessibility without sacrificing the performance needed for competition. Available in Blue/Black Hub, White/Black Hub, and White/Blue Hub.

title: Original Tournament Jewel
content:
History
The premium offering in the Flores Yo-Yo Company lineup, the Original Tournament Jewel was produced circa 1929 and featured four faux diamond jewels embedded in each side of the yo-yo — eight total — as a prestige decoration. Pedro Flores is credited with inventing the jeweled yo-yo as a concept, and this model represented the high end of the company's three-tier pricing range (up to approximately $1.50 in 1929).
Like all Flores models, it employs one-piece hand-lathed wood construction with the defining loop-axle slip string that distinguished Flores yo-yos from earlier fixed-string bandalores. Its larger 2¼-inch (57mm) diameter placed it above the standard and mini variants in both size and perceived prestige.
Museum examples have sold in collector markets for up to $886. The tournament shape, jeweled decoration, and Flores provenance make it among the most sought-after antique yo-yos.

title: The Wonder Toy
content:
History
Pedro Flores's original production yo-yo, the first mass-produced yo-yo in the United States sold under the "yo-yo" trademark. Flores filed a DBA certificate in Santa Barbara, California on June 9, 1928 under the name Yo-Yo Manufacturing Company, introducing the Wonder Toy to the American market at 15¢ for the smallest size.
The defining innovation was Flores's loop-axle slip string — the string was looped around the axle rather than tied to it, allowing the yo-yo to spin freely at the string's end in the "sleep" position and enabling a range of tricks impossible with earlier fixed-string bandalores. The slogan became: "If it isn't Flores it isn't a yo-yo."
At its 1929 peak, the company operated factories in Santa Barbara, Hollywood, and Los Angeles, employed 600 workers, and produced over 300,000 yo-yos daily. The Wonder Toy was offered in a three-tier pricing lineup (15¢, mid-tier, and premium) with colorways including red, green, blue, pink, and purple, each stamped with the distinctive "Big F" ink mark. The brand and trademark were acquired by Donald F. Duncan Sr. in 1932 for an estimated $250,000–$750,000.
Original examples are highly collectible; graded specimens sell for $300–$975+ depending on color rarity and condition.

title: The Wonder Toy (Mini)
content:
History
The miniature sibling to the standard Wonder Toy, produced alongside it during the 1928–1929 peak of Flores Yo-Yo Company production. It shares the same one-piece hand-lathed wood construction and Pedro Flores's defining loop-axle slip string, which enabled the yo-yo to sleep freely at the string's end.
Museum documentation characterizes the mini as having "a very very thin gap," a consequence of its reduced diameter relative to the standard model. Colorways follow the same painted-wood tradition with ink-stamped "Big F" branding, including a noted gray-blue with blue ink stamp variant and a red with black ink stamp variant.
Among the rarest surviving Flores specimens; condition grade 7/10 examples have been valued by collectors at approximately $750.

title: Flow Trigger
content: AboutThe Flow Trigger is Hong Teng Long's signature yo-yo with AceYo. Built for the long-spinning stability needed for intricate, flowing combos, it features a wide catch zone, soft body contours, and 7075 aluminum construction. Available in Teal/Black Rims, Light Blue/Silver Rims, Silver/Rainbow Rims, Silver/Silver Rims, and Black Blue/Black Rims, with an optional signature engraving.

title: Fluchs
content:
The Fluchs (pronounced Flux) was released December 11, 2004, and was the first release for Anti-Yo.  They were limited to only 225 yoyos.

One of my favorite things about Anti-Yo is the stories.  Like the story for the Fluchs:

A guy walks into a bar and places a pink and black yo-yo on the counter.Bartender comes by, picks up the yo-yo and starts playing with it.

"Damn" says the bartender "This is one buttery smooth big bearinged beauty."

The bartender pours a shot glass of milk for the stranger, before continuing to play.

"This thing feels like it's made of magnesium, while staying attainably within my budget. What makes this thing feel so silky smooth on palm grind?"

"It's the process," says the stranger between sips of milk "The yo-yo itself is made from high quality aircraft aluminum. Then it is precision machined into a sleek retro winding double knob skill toy with a heavy emphasis on modern artistic design."

"Of course," the bartender remarked, "The Eames influence is obvious. But what gives this thing its smooth laminar flow against my calloused hands?"

"That's the final process. After the yo-yo is removed from the lathe, Anti-Yo applies the Slip Matte® Finish. This special coating assures a durable finish while giving the yo-yo its low viscosity.

The bartender seems to think about this for a minute then says, "Slip Matte I get it."

"Good, most folks wont." Says the stranger as he finishes his last sip of milk.

"What was the name of the company again?" asks the bartender as he places the yo-yo back onto the counter.

"Anti-Yo," responded the stranger " they are based out of San Francisco."

"Anti-Yo huh? That's edgy."

"Yeah" says the stranger, as he placed the Fluchs® Yo-Yo into his custom made Prada yo-yo pouch and wiped the milk mustache from his lips. "Edgy."

About

title: Fluke
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Fluke is the signature yo-yo of our very own Wes Shuck. It is his ideal design for laid back everyday use, while still retaining a spirit of creativity and flow. The design is entirely the vision of Wes, with the original prototype even being hand produced with Wes's assistance back in 2018 in his home state of Michigan. The Fluke comes in 2 versions, a blasted and a brushed finish. The blasted version features a split beadblast along our signature "sight lines" in the gap to minimize string wear and provide a nice visual contrast both inside and outside of the sight line."

Johnny Scrabble Edition

From Wes:

"Living in Boston you find many strange things and meet many different people. My journey to the national yoyo contest started after work, traveling through the millions of people downtown for the Celtics parade after their championship win this year. I eventually made it on the bus heading to Philly and sat next to this wonderful man named Johnny Scrabble!! 

He's a Philly native whose love for the Celtics runs so deep he had to be in Boston for the parade (decked out in the sickest Celtics merch). He has the name Johnny Scrabble because he teaches students across Philadelphia how to play Scrabble, working on improving literacy within the public school system by creating an after-school activity for kids to learn and hang out together. 

After having great conversations that lasted our whole ride to Philly we parted ways at the bus stop, and my national yoyo experience was off to a wonderful start! Johnny's selfless service to his community and passion for his mission impacted me and the entirety of the Freshly Dirty team with whom I shared his story. We decided to make a special edition color after him -- spreading the news of his great work! -Wes

To learn more about Johnny here's a link to a bio of him and his work. https://phillyasap.org/asap-hero-highlight-johnny-scrabble/"

title: Fly High
content: History / AboutDistinct 4A model documented by C3 and Rewind.

title: Flying Lemon
content:
From Spinworthy:

"I’d like to announce my latest unresponsive yoyo design - The Spinworthy Flying Lemon

50mm diameter yoyos, particularly organic ones, have always caught my attention. It’s a size and shape I really love to throw. As good as many are that I’ve tried, they have never felt quite right to me. They lack a certain feel and performance that I’m craving for. The Flying Lemon is my attempt to create the exact thing I am after.

I knew what had to be changed - the bearing. C bearings are just too big to get the most out of undersized yoyo designs. D bearings are significantly better, but stil don’t quite make the cut. A bearings are better still but are just a tiny fraction too slim. Enter the 4mm wide variant of the MR85 bearing: this is the key.

The MR85 bearing is something I’m familiar designing yoyos around. Mark from MK1 Yoyos and I have released a couple together (the RBC and the Harbinger).

The benefits of the MR85-W4 include:

Very smooth throw and return feel (greatly reduced ‘clunk’ at the end of the throw)

Tight winds and powerful regens (enhanced further with the RBC pads)

Good low RPM play and bind performance

For organic design, the bearing takes up less inner wall estate, aiding regens

Lower weight still allows powerful performance

smaller (bearing) size means flat bearing negatives are significantly reduced.

I think I’ve succeeded in what I set out to do. The lemon is fast, spins furiously, stable and feels fantastic in play.

The colours will include Lemon, and Lime (lime green/lemon fade).

I love it and I hope you will too."

title: Fora
content:
From Canopy:

"Designed in collaboration with Martin Koprna, Slovakian National Champion, the Fora is the first model in our regional series - where we collaborate with local designers and players highlighting their unique styles, stories and perspectives.

A comfortable, performance-friendly form factor with design cue nods to the original Canopy lineup. The plastic double ring ensures a soft catch by covering the entire outer rim - without sacrificing power - while also enhancing durability. Fora blends a soft feel with a sharp image: bold yet minimal, fast yet grounded. It strikes the perfect balance between control and expression, with just enough spontaneity to let you get lost in the groove."

title: Worldsfair
content: History / AboutForester produced a small line of wooden, unpromoted yo-yos in the 1960s, according to the YoYo Wiki. Its Worldsfair yo-yo caused some confusion because it was not made for a World's Fair but was identified as such by some dealers. The wiki states it is unrelated to the World's Fair yo-yos produced for the 1939 New York fair and others. The wiki has no separate page or specifications for the model.

title: Worldsfair Spinner
content: History / AboutForester produced a small line of wooden, unpromoted yo-yos in the 1960s, according to the YoYo Wiki. The wiki lists the Worldsfair Spinner as one of the company's yo-yos alongside the Worldsfair, but provides no description or specifications for it.

title: Forge
content:
History / About
Collaboration between Sengoku Yoyos, YoYoTricks.com, and 2015 5A World Champion Jake Elliott. Released late August 2016 (exact day unconfirmed) as a competitive 1A yo-yo with a V-type profile, soft blast finish, finger-spin cup, and a slightly narrower gap for consistent binds and tilt resistance. Sold in solid colors (~$100) and splash colors (~$110), later bundled in a "Forge Yoyo Pro Pack" ($129.99) with lube, a multitool, a ceramic Center Trac bearing, and 5 strings. Colorways included Red, Blue, Teal Speckle, Fire, Royal Splash, and Red/Purple/Gold Splash. Now permanently out of stock at YoYoTricks and absent from Sengoku's current catalog — effectively discontinued.

title: FORK
content:
History / About
FORK is Tetsuto Kato's signature and the first YYR model to ship with the new Whizy System, released February 7, 2026. Available in POM and PC plastic body variants with aluminum rims, it ships with a standard-gap spacer set, short axle, and one YYR Whizy String.

title: Forma
content:
The following was archived from Editions YoYoExpert Forums post announcing the Forma:

Forma came to be due to a conversation with @fradiger and our shared love for mid-school throws. We were reminiscing about mid-school and modern designs and got talking about blending a few designs into something different:

CLYW Chief

Ikimono Tomo

OneDrop Cascade

YYR x OneDrop SYFO

A few messages later, Frad dropped this photo with the following quote:

“Theres a good yoyo in there, somewhere, because i like all these yoyos.”

The first concept would feature a polycarbonate inner ring forming a double rim, paired with a TP x CLYW-inspired profile. However as the vision evolved—leaning more into the Cascade and SYFO influences—we scrapped it for a cleaner monometal approach that better fit the SYFO/Cascade direction: MMP-01

MMP-01 final renders prior to prototyping:

Sadly MMP-01 wasn’t it though. It couldn’t handle impacts and vibed slightly from factory, so we went back to the drawing board. Enter MMP-02, later named Forma.

Forma went through three rounds of prototyping across three different shops: one in the U.S. (@Lotaxi), one at FPM, and one at TopYo. Around that time, there was a lot of behind-the-scenes chatter about inconsistent lead times, machining quality, and communication issues with OEMs. It felt like the right moment to test the waters and get a firsthand look at how each shop handled the process.

Although we would go on to prototype in both 7068 and 6061, the 6061 version just felt right—durable, comfortable, and locked into that midschool-inspired vibe that put feel first. Let’s be real—this wouldn’t be an Edition yo-yo if it didn’t still pack performance as a mainstay trait.

The result?

Forma is about execution—pacing your tricks, constructing with intention, and feeling the flow in your play. It packs power so that it doesn’t demand perfection, but it shines when your execution is clean and your transitions are thoughtful.

Available now on the Edition Yoyo storefront with the following colors:

We hope you enjoy as much as we did putting this together!

title: Format:C
content:
From One Drop:

"The Format:C Challenge: design a 7075 yoyo for competition play from the ground up. The "C" stands for "Competition" or "Contest".

The testing process was intense with two rounds of prototyping going to every single member of our team for extensive play. The Format:C probably has the deepest "beta testing" of any yoyo we have made.

We had an unexpected extra challenge on the manufacturing side. We had to change and refine some processes to be able too make these consistently balanced. Shawn (The Machinist) was up for the challenge and was able to solve the problems. There was a point where we thought we may not be able to release this but now the Format:C is here."

title: Format:C Gen 2
content:
From One Drop:

"The original Format:C was released 10 years ago in late 2013.  It is time to revisit.

For Generation 2, the big visual update is to the hub which is now flat replacing the tap-through and slightly raised hub of the original for a much cleaner, sleek look. This change also reduces the center weight. You can also see that the Sightline is wider.

Less obvious to the eye is, but easy to see if you compare cross sections is that Gen 2 is different throughout. This could be summarized as a big change to the weight distribution and the overall weight - the Gen 2 is 3.75 grams lighter overall.  You will feel the difference in play."

title: Forte
content:
History / About
The Forte is MonkeyfingeR Design’s signature model for Mike Montgomery, Idaho State Yoyo Champion. The name references the musical term forte (strong, loud), reflecting Montgomery’s powerful, precise 1A style. The narrow V-shape with a distinctive stair-step inner rim was unusual for its era — the ~36mm width pushed well below the competition norm — while the slim profile was engineered for Montgomery’s smooth, flowy, intricate trick sequences.

title: Crystal Dumpling
content:
History / About
The Crystal Dumpling is ForYoSa's first CNC-machined polycarbonate yo-yo. A prototype was measured in September 2023 and the model went into mass production that November. The brand announced it available to Taiwan locals on February 5, 2024, with worldwide sales to follow. ForYoSa describes it as faster than the Stinky Tofu with an even wider catch zone, and it includes a finger-rest area. It was sold in crystal white (transparent) and black.

title: Oyster Omelette (Prototype)
content:
History / About
The Oyster Omelette is a 4A prototype from ForYoSa, shown on the brand's blog in November 2023. No retail release has been confirmed.

title: Re:DM
content:
History / About
Re:DM began as a polycarbonate-and-7075-rim prototype in 2023. ForYoSa founder Stephen Hung stated on March 3, 2026 that the Re:DM had been released locally in Taiwan, with worldwide store setup still pending at that time.

title: Stinky Tofu
content:
History / About
The Stinky Tofu (also written Tshau Tofu) was ForYoSa's first production yo-yo, announced as released on September 25, 2023 after a prototype shown in July 2023. It is a 7075 aluminum butterfly-shaped, unresponsive design that the brand describes as strong and stable with a wide catch zone, good tilt retention and long idle endurance without sacrificing speed. It was sold in gold and blue-green gradient colorways.

title: Fossil
content: AboutThe Fossil is Japan Technology's titanium monometal flagship, and the first JT yo-yo to use a 10mm axle. Artwork was contributed by Bryan Figueroa. The design was inspired by ammonite fossils — straight lines creating an organically curved form. JT engineered it for a "soft catch, gentle sensation on string" character, distinct from the harder titanium feel of many competitors.

title: Fractal
content: AboutThe Fractal is a bimetal released in 2022, designed by Kohei Nishimura (2023 Japan National 1A Champion). Featuring a step-straight profile with a stainless steel outer rim, JT describes it as offering "maneuverability with power" — a simple design that performs stably across trick styles. The Fractal's rim shape was later inherited by the Plactal and the Tesract/Zetica line. Available in Soft Blast Grandiorite colorway.

title: Fragment
content: AboutThe Fragment is the signature of Ryosuke Iwasawa, known in the Japanese competitive community as the "laceration master" for his extensive use of whip and laceration elements. The inverse-round profile and compact diameter were chosen to maximize string interaction speed. The Size D bearing — shared with the CLASHcube — is one of only a handful of YYR models to deviate from the standard Size C spec. The Uragment (2013) is a variant of the Fragment prototype, featuring a flattened straight rim where the Fragment has a curved one.

title: Collector’s Edition — Duncan Genuine
content:
About
The Large "G" Genuine Duncan is one of the earliest and most historically significant yo-yo designs in the Duncan catalog, originating in the 1930s. Franklin Mint reproduced it in 1994 as the third and final entry in their collector's subscription series of vintage Duncan yo-yos.
The reproduction features three-piece wood construction with a fixed metal axle (replacing the original's wooden axle), glossy black finish with a day-glo orange stripe, and shiny gold foil seals — a departure from the matte gold of original seals. On originals the stripes are often imperfectly aligned with the seals; on the Franklin Mint reproduction, stripes and seals are in perfect alignment, making identification straightforward. Came with a gold-finished metal display stand matching the other two models in the series.

title: Collector’s Edition — Duncan Imperial
content:
About
The Duncan Imperial debuted in 1954 and is the oldest Duncan model still in production today. The chevron-branded version (1954–1962) was selected by Franklin Mint as one of three yo-yos for their 1994 collector's reproduction series.
The reproduction is made from standard plastic rather than the original's tenite (an early cellulose acetate plastic), and includes a small clear jewel embedded in one body half — a detail absent from originals. The "Imperial" text on the label is slightly off-center compared to originals. Like all three Franklin Mint Duncan reproductions, it comes with a gold-finished metal display stand. The Imperial is the only plastic-body yo-yo of the three-piece set.

title: Collector’s Edition — Duncan Litening
content:
About
The Duncan Litening was produced from approximately 1956 to 1959 and is distinguished by its two-coat crackle painting process, which gives the surface a distinctive textured appearance. Franklin Mint reproduced it in 1994 as part of a planned 12-yo-yo subscription series honoring historically significant Duncan models. Only three models from the series were ultimately released due to poor initial sales.
The Litening reproduction is identifiable by its gold-background foil sticker seal with a green lightning bolt (the original had a silver background with a gold bolt) and a metal axle rather than the wooden axle of the original. It came with a gold-finished engraved metal display stand. Each piece is a fixed-axle wood construction, playable but intended primarily as a display collectible.

title: The LiV
content: History / AboutFree2Throw is a company founded by Tony Saffioti with a goal of creating unique and affordable yo-yos for all levels of play. The LiV was its first design. According to YoYoExpert, the team took inspiration from the childhood favorite television show Power Rangers: the LiV is named after the Power Rangers' ally Alpha 5, and the dimple inside the cup was designed to match the dimple on the robot's head. It is a lightweight bi-metal with an organic profile, available with stainless steel rings (56.4 g) or brass rings (57.9 g). YoYoSam describes the brass-ring version as the green "Rival Edition" and the stainless version as the gunmetal grey production colorway with red rings. Designed in the USA and made in China.

title: Freehand
content: AboutThe 2016 Freehand reboot updated the classic design with a larger diameter, a lower wall profile for improved stability, and 19 mm response pads replacing older friction stickers. It retained the narrow Size C bearing that keeps the yo-yo responsive — appropriate for 5A's counterweight style, where players need the string to disengage from the counterweight cleanly on release. It comes bundled with a casino-die counterweight and is positioned as an accessible all-plastic 5A starter for players wanting to learn the style Takeshi Matsuura pioneered before investing in the aluminum versions.

title: Freehand 1
content:
The Freehand 1 was designed by Steve Brown, originally for Freehand, or 5A, style of play. Released in 2001*, Red, Blue and Yellow were the first colors to be released. A number of other colors and special editions were released later. The goal here is to collect photos of all the original Freehand 1's, and have them displayed below. Special thanks to Brandon Jackson for allowing the use of his FH1 collection photos. If you have any FH1's that we are missing in the archive please contact us, thank you.

title: Freehand Delrin
content: At the 2023 World YoYo Contest Duncan released a machined Delrin version of the famed Freehand 1. This limited run yoyo had both body and caps machined from Delrin in a large C bearing yoyo. These were released in White, Black, Blue, Red and Green, all with white caps. Retail price of $54.99.

title: Freehand Mg
content:
The Freehand Mg was a magnesium bodied version of the Freehand. These were released in a powdercoat and anodized finish. It originally was packaged in a deluxe wooden box with a limited-edition silver/black (or white/black) Duncan character counterweight set for 5A play. It also has a ceramic ball bearing, take-apart design, spacers for adjusting the string gap, and Friction Sticker response (the yo-yo comes with a set of four stickers). In 2013 Duncan released a Barebones version, with just the yoyo and a black/white counterweight dice. The Barebones edition featured recessed pads. The Duncan Mg was produced from 2004 until 2014*.

title: Freehand NextGen
content: AboutThe Freehand NextGen represents a significant modernization of the Freehand concept, pairing a polycarbonate body with an aluminum hub insert for improved bearing seat durability. Released December 15, 2018, it uses a KonKave bearing for unresponsive performance and ships with a standard die counterweight. The semi-organic step-straight profile is a design departure from previous Freehand shapes. Multiple graphic cap editions — Flying Panda, Flying Squirrel, Mongu, Throw Monkey, and "Duncan = Love" among them — made it a fan-favorite collectible as well as a serious 5A competition plastic.
