title: Freq.Mod
content:
About

“The Freq.mod was born in the BST Ross Levine of Ilinx Toys and myself were in a post about what yo-yos we would love to see updated, reissued etc and we both agreed on the freq.wav. The Freq.wav comes from the now defunct Recreational Revolution, I learned of this brand at the National Yoyo Contest of 2012. Alex Lee, and Ernest Kahn were hanging in a corner throwing, I recall asking Alex what yoyo he was using and he handed me the Rojas Edition freq.wav, being a long time fan of Anthony Rojas I needed it. So fast forward a bit into 2013 and I managed to score one then two, and at one point I’d collected about 7 in total. It’s the yoyo that kept me playing for hours on end for years. So in early 2019 Ross and myself discussed making more of then but out of 7075 and modernizing the response system but keeping the play and the aesthetic the same. Ross handled all the CAD work between two Freq.wavs hand measuring every angle on them both, I was left with double checking the work and going forward into manufacturing. Now these are available to the world again and i hope this yoyo inspires others creativity in the same way it has for me. "

- Coffin

title: Fresh Milk
content: About the Fresh MilkAnnounced June 17, 2016, the Fresh Milk marked Crucial founder Paul Yath's return to yo-yo manufacturing after a two-year absence — nearly a decade after the original Milk. During his hiatus, Yath taught himself CNC lathe operation and machining, deepening his manufacturing capabilities. The Fresh Milk reflects that development: low walls for complex trick execution, an organic profile that recalls the original Milk, improved weight distribution, fingerspin-friendly hubs, and a smooth grind finish. YoYoExpert described it as "the culmination of everything Paul has learned designing and throwing yo-yos over the course of his professional career." Ships with Crucial's signature Grooved Bearing.

title: Mod44
content:
History / About
The Mod44 features a 6061 aluminum hub that accepts three sets of interchangeable Delrin (POM) rims: Supersport, Tuner, and Coupe & Cruiser. An O-ring system keeps the rims aligned and secure. Freshly Dirty also released open-source rim files for community 3D printing. Available in Size C and Size D bearing versions.

title: Traveller
content:
History / About
The Traveller is the yo-yo that put Freshly Dirty on the map. After founder Alex Morton launched the company in March 2015 with early fixed-axle attempts he described as "terrible," the Traveller was the design that resonated with the community. Built from Indiana-sourced hardwood, it gained exposure at the 2016 World YoYo Contest and led directly to the development of the Cardboard Dreamboat bearing model.

title: A BATHING APE × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
A collaboration between Freshthings and A BATHING APE (BAPE), sold through BAPE stores and the brand's website. Translucent polycarbonate body with Ape Head graphics in Blue, Green, and Red colorways. Round/classic body shape. Retailed at $39.00 USD.

title: Central American × Freshthings Metal Yoyo
content:
Overview
The aluminum extension of the Central American × Freshthings collaboration. Machined from A6061 on the same H-profile body used by sOMEThING for the Angle — set to tug response with a thin C-bearing stock; swappable to bind with an M4×8mm axle. Central American branding applied to the Angle body geometry. Sold through international retailers at $54.99 USD.

title: Central American × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Central American, a Japanese street/lifestyle brand. Classic-shape plastic with the Freshthings mouse illustration on one face and the Central American logo on the reverse. Metallic print finish. Retail: ¥1,100.

title: Central American × Freshthings Yoyo (Kemushi)
content:
Overview
The Kemushi (caterpillar) variant of the Central American × Freshthings collaboration. Same base geometry and construction as the standard Central American collab, but with a caterpillar character illustration on one face and the Central American logo on the reverse. Retail: ¥1,100.

title: CHALLENGER × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with CHALLENGER, a Japanese streetwear brand. Classic TYPE P shape with skull design on one face and a crown graphic on the reverse. White and Black colorways. Retail: ¥1,320.

title: Chunichi Dragons × Freshthings Yoyo (Doala)
content:
Overview
Official licensed merchandise for the Chunichi Dragons of Nippon Professional Baseball, featuring DOALA — the team mascot — on a classic-shape plastic yo-yo. Sold at Dragons-affiliated retail channels. Retail: ¥1,100.

title: Chunichi Dragons × Freshthings Yoyo (Logo)
content:
Overview
The team logo variant of the Freshthings × Chunichi Dragons collaboration, identical in construction to the DOALA mascot version but carrying the Dragons team crest rather than the mascot artwork. Retail: ¥1,100.

title: Freshthings Classic Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Freshthings Classic Yoyo is an entry-level transparent plastic yo-yo with the brand's printed logo, targeting beginners and casual players. Available in Blue, White, and Pink with a random string color included. Retail price ¥1,540.

title: Coca-Cola × Freshthings Metal Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Coca-Cola Metal Yoyo elevates the collaboration to a machined aluminum body — the TYPE X geometry in A6061, engraved with Coca-Cola branding. Released in three colorways (Gold, Silver, Red) with three logo engraving variants: standard Coca-Cola, Japanese Katakana logo, and French "Buvez Coca-Cola" script.
Ships tug-responsive with a thin C-bearing and M4×8mm axle; upgradeable to bind play with a standard Size C bearing. Retail: ¥5,500.

title: Coca-Cola × Freshthings Titanium Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Coca-Cola Titanium Yoyo is the premium tier of the Freshthings × Coca-Cola collaboration: a fully machined titanium X-shape with engraved Coca-Cola branding. Retails at ¥55,000, placing it alongside the Fragment and Freshthings own-label titanium releases. The same geometry as the Metal TYPE X series, elevated to titanium.

title: Coca-Cola × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Coca-Cola Yoyo is the cornerstone product of Freshthings' collaboration with The Coca-Cola Company, using the classic TYPE P geometry — a modernized Russell Yo-Yo shape with disassemblable halves and a Size K loop bearing. First released at launch in November 2016, the model was produced in an extensive range of colorways and logo variants over several years.
Colorways and Variants
Classic Color series (red/white Coke Logo and Coca-Cola Script); Glow in the Dark series (five designs: Red/Glow Laurel, Red/Glow Bottle, Red/Glow Logo, White/Glow Logo, White/Glow Wing; also available as 10-piece assort); Silver series (Black/Silver with three designs: 1886, Coke Logo, Katakana Logo; also 10-piece assort); ongoing colorways including Red (Girl), Red (Katakana Logo), Black (Katakana Logo), Orange, Pink, White, Red/Green/White.

title: Coca-Cola × Freshthings Yoyo (H-profile)
content:
Overview
The H-profile Coca-Cola Yoyo applies the Freshthings Première/Premiere geometry to the Coca-Cola collaboration — a wide wing body with Coca-Cola branding. Beginner-friendly; upgradeable from tug-responsive to bind with a standard Size C bearing. Released 2017.

title: Coca-Cola × Freshthings Yoyo (X-shape)
content:
Overview
The X-shape Coca-Cola Yoyo applies the outer-rim weighted TYPE X geometry to the Coca-Cola collaboration. Released in multiple design variants: "ICE COLD" text, Japanese Katakana Logo, and a clear green Bottle Color edition inspired by the classic Coca-Cola glass bottle. All share the same TYPE X specs with a thin C-bearing for responsive play upgradeable to bind.

title: #FR2 × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with #FR2 (Fxxking Rabbits), the Japanese streetwear brand by photographer Ryo Ishikawa, known for rabbit iconography and transgressive messaging. TYPE X H-profile plastic in Yellow and Black colorways. Retail: ¥3,300.

title: Fragment × Freshthings Titanium Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Fragment Titanium Yoyo is the third Freshthings × fragment design collaboration and the most premium: a fully machined titanium X-shape limited to 100 units worldwide. Released April 2021 and featured on Hypebeast. The satin-finish titanium body is engraved with outer rings reading "Fragment Yo-Yo" and fragment design's double lightning bolt emblem on the inner face.
Retailed at ¥55,000 (~$570 USD at release). Collab partner: fragment design / Hiroshi Fujiwara.

title: Fragment × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Fragment Yoyo was one of two products released on Freshthings' launch day, November 2, 2016. A collaboration with fragment design's Hiroshi Fujiwara — one of the most prominent figures in Japanese streetwear — the yo-yo uses the classic TYPE P geometry with fragment's double lightning bolt logo on the face. Responsive out of the box and convertible to unresponsive.
The launch was described at the time as "the biggest fashion/yo-yo design collaboration" to that date. Retail: ¥3,300.

title: Gallery 1950 × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Gallery 1950 (G1950), an interior and lifestyle shop based in Ebisu/Shibuya, Tokyo, known for collaborating with brands like PORTER and Nike. TYPE X H-profile plastic with metal ball bearing. Retail: ¥2,200.

title: GOD SELECTION XXX × Freshthings Metal Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with GOD SELECTION XXX, a Japanese fashion and music brand. Machined aluminum TYPE X geometry with the XXX logo engraved on the matte-finish body. Retail: ¥8,800.

title: Hatsune Miku × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Licensed collaboration with Hatsune Miku (Crypton Future Media). Classic TYPE P-adjacent shape with metal ball bearing. Two variants: Green (Miku silhouette design) and Pink ("01 HATSUNEMIKU" logo). Sold out quickly at ¥1,980.

title: Hotel Keychain × Freshthings Yoyo (TYPE M)
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Hotel Keychain brand on the TYPE M macaron geometry. Glow-in-the-dark plastic with Hotel Keychain logo. Same platform as the Sequence Hotels TYPE M collab. Retail: ¥2,750.

title: Hotel Logo Metal Yoyo
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Sequence Hotels (a Japanese hotel chain with locations in Tokyo and Kyoto). The same machined A6061 H-profile body as the Motion Logo and Central American metal models, applied with Sequence Hotels' logo in a smooth matte finish. Tug-responsive stock; upgradeable to bind with M4×8mm axle. Retail: ¥5,500.

title: Mark Gonzales × Medicom Toy × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
Released April 27, 2018, initially via the Medicom Toy web store. The triple collaboration brings together Freshthings, Medicom Toy, and legendary skateboarder Mark "The Gonz" Gonzales. One face carries Gonzales' signature angel character; the reverse features a skateboard wheel-inspired graphic. Available in Red and Yellow.
Retail: ¥3,300.

title: Motion Logo Metal Yoyo
content:
Overview
The Motion Logo Metal Yoyo is Freshthings' branded aluminum model, produced on the same machined A6061 H-profile body used for the sOMEThING Angle. It ships configured for tug response with a thin C-bearing and M4×6mm axle; swapping to an M4×8mm axle enables full unresponsive bind play. Features the Freshthings motion logo graphic.

title: Paris 2024 Olympic Yo-Yos
content:
Overview
An official licensed product for the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games: a set of four wooden yo-yos manufactured in France. Each carries distinct artwork; they are designed as display and collector pieces — the string is fixed and not intended for active play. Minor manufacturing variations may appear. Retail: ¥12,100 for the 4-piece set.

title: Peanuts × Medicom Toy × Freshthings Yoyo
content:
Overview
A triple collaboration between Freshthings, Medicom Toy, and the Peanuts franchise (Snoopy). The packaging and yo-yo face are designed as a four-panel newspaper comic strip. Each color represents a distinct trick: Red = Long Sleeper, Blue = Rock the Baby, Yellow = Walk the Dog. Retail: ¥3,300.

title: Première
content:
Overview
The Première is Freshthings' original H-profile plastic model, released alongside the Fragment collab yo-yo on the brand's launch day, November 2, 2016. The wide wing body is designed for strong spin on weaker throws, making it beginner-accessible out of the box with a responsive thin C-bearing setup that can be upgraded to full unresponsive bind play with a standard Size C bearing.
A 2017 additional production run (marked "AP") released further colorways on the same geometry.

title: Sequence Hotels × Freshthings Yoyo (TYPE M)
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Sequence Hotels (Tokyo/Kyoto). Glow-in-the-dark TYPE M macaron-shaped plastic with Sequence Hotels logo. Advanced players can upgrade with POM spacers and a short axle (sold separately at ¥550) for a different play feel. Also available with a collab logo pouch. Retail: ¥2,750.

title: Square Logo Yoyo (TYPE M)
content:
Overview
The Square Logo TYPE M is a macaron-shaped plastic yo-yo in Freshthings' own branding. Purple colorway. The TYPE M geometry is compact and ergonomic, designed to fit comfortably in hand. Metal ball bearing. Retail ¥2,750.

title: Square Logo Yoyo (TYPE X)
content:
Overview
The Square Logo TYPE X is an H-profile/X-shape plastic yo-yo in Freshthings' own branding. Yellow and Black colorways. The outer-rim weighted design enhances rotational force. Metal ball bearing. Retail ¥2,750.

title: Freshthings Titanium Yoyo
content:
Overview
Freshthings' own-label titanium yo-yo, machined in an X-profile with the brand's circle logo engraved. Limited production. Comes packaged in an acrylic display/storage case. Priced at ¥55,000, placing it alongside the Fragment and Coca-Cola titanium releases as a premium tier product.

title: TYPE M Glow
content:
Overview
The TYPE M Glow is Freshthings' standalone release of their macaron-shaped platform in glow-in-the-dark plastic. Comfortable ergonomic hand-fit shape. The TYPE M geometry has also been used for the Sequence Hotels and Hotel Keychain collaborations.

title: Yackle × Freshthings Yoyo (TYPE M Glow)
content:
Overview
Collaboration with Japanese music artist/producer Yackle. TYPE M macaron-shaped glow-in-the-dark plastic with Yackle branding and QR code stickers that unlock four original Yackle tracks, including the three-minute competition yo-yo music "D0uble 4" plus three shorter pieces. Retail: ¥2,750.

title: Fruitloop
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re proud to introduce our newest entry – a bobbing, popping, bundle of fun.

Say hello to the Fruitloop!

SPECS

dia 53.7mm

wid 47mm

weight 65.2g

material 6061 AL

The Fruitloop began with the desire to return to levity in throwing, and that process has resulted in the most fun design we've made to date.

Much of 2021 had been spent working on more technically challenging and performance-oriented designs. After months of poring over a thousand CAD revisions, we felt the need to disrupt our rhythm slightly, and just do something playful.

our aim from the beginning was to depart from the traditional organic form and design a rounded, ball-like model that would whizz, whip, run and roll through tricks. In other words, sacrilegiously unoptimised for the modern trickset, but something you couldn’t bear to leave home without.

Initial drafts of the first prototype were made under the working title, “Pebble”, conveying the sense of a small, compact, ball-ish object. It captured the essence of what it should feel like in hand; we also wanted it to feel more solid than what is usual of our organic lineup.

Our first prototype came back after some tinkering, and featured a thick 49mm width, 53.7mm diameter profile, with a majority of its mass packed in the hub. The mass bias was evened out by a ring-shaped machined aluminum cap, which was press-fit into the main body.

Having worked on the CAD, we knew how it would look, but having the physical prototype in hand for the first time – its unique profile reminiscent of a certain breakfast cereal – felt simultaneously amusing and inspiring.

Yoyo-ing can be self-serious at times. Holding an aluminium doughnut can be a good reminder that the ultimate substance of our hobby is having joy in play.

The first prototype was very interesting in motion. It was endlessly floaty, veered off-axis too easily, and required more constant application of movement and force than other designs we’ve made. At the same time, I felt myself gravitating towards hops, rolls, funky binds and odd whip-regens – the satisfying, frivolous stuff that are unapologetically my guilty pleasure.

Coleman, who tested and provided feedback for the prototype, mentioned he found it nimble and agile, ran faster than he expected, and floated with all the buttery smoothness anyone could want. He also enjoyed the effect of the Fruitloop rounding-off quick movements – a dampening that made movements feel gradual and natural that I experienced, too.

The prototype was promising – Evgeniy found it pure fun, but surprisingly capable for a “fun yoyo”, and gravitated to both its form and play – but we wanted to make a few tweaks .

The overarching sense was that the prototype had to be consolidated. It was a bit too wide (even by our standards), and played just a bit too airily – perhaps an unexpected criticism for such a concept – but the team agreed moving towards compactness and density felt right.

The second version (left, in lighter pink) came back perfectly aligned with our initial vision of how it should play and feel.

In probably a first for an Atmos design, we slimmed the overall profile – by just a bit. We also made the Schmoove-step less aggressive.

The most significant tweaks were made to the overall distribution of mass, primarily through the modification of the ring-caps. We increased its mass by roughly 10%, and altered its construction for a more secure fit with the rest of the body.

The new, slimmer and weight-adjusted Fruitloop retains the movement signature of the original prototype, which I think lends itself to redirects, and more rhythmic play. Additionally, it spins much better, has a cleaner gap width, and the unique dampening and rounding effect feels nicely paired with its new, fuller construction.

We’re usually conservative with releasing colorways, as we prefer to maintain a cohesive palette with each release.

The Fruitloop presents a unique (and wholly positive) challenge on this front, given its namesake cereal is characterized by what feels like a spectacle of colors.

As research (and breakfast) goes, I bought a box of the good stuff to dissect, and with some surprise figured there are, in truth, only six Frootloop colors – red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. I was considerably deflated, having operated under the grand illusion this number was something closer to 78.

We decided on a palette of eight to round off the set, and we’re in love with how they came out.

Short aside: this is not something we’re officially recommending, since it is vaguely equivalent to ripping rings out from bimetal designs, and may cause vibe, but – they do this.

For the more experimental and less precious amongst us – a colorway extravaganza awaits you.

The Fruitloop is not made for tech (although Evgeniy still finds a way to do elegantly complex things with it). It’s certainly not the yoyo to pick up if you’re into speed play or the latest competition meta. It’s actually even structurally biased against finger spins and DNA binds, and it won’t break any long sleeper world records. If you’re looking for a powerful performance beast, we genuinely recommend you to set your sights on other industry offerings.

However, if you’re like us – in need of something a bit different – perhaps in the search of a fun, boppy and rhythmic throw that will bring on hours of jamming fun, something unique to freshen your rotation, or something playful that might inspire the next shoot-the-moon-behind-the-neck-regen banger that will set the collective interwebs on fire, the Fruitloop might just be for you.

Note: Fruitloops come with a deep blast that feels similar to the one applied on the Noahs, but is smoother, and less aggressive. It gives the Fruitloop a lovely matte, clay-like finish.

We’ve tested the blast for string breakage risk with approximately 120 mins of play on a single string that is thinner than the average “fat” bulk spec with no resulting breakage issues.

However, we recognize some variance exists; should your string show premature wear, we recommend taking some time to lighten the blast on areas that make the most contact with your strings. You can do this by rubbing the inner walls with old denim or a leather belt to alleviate any abrasiveness. We recommend doing this for a few minutes, and it should be perfect for play after a good buffing.

title: Fruitloop ES
content:
History / About
Fruitloop ES, released July 27, 2026, is a rebuilt successor to atmos projects' original 2022 Fruitloop. It keeps the signature open "donut hole" body cutout but was reworked from scratch across five full prototype rounds — revisiting rim thickness, weight distribution, and donut-hole circumference — to add spin power and stability while rounding off response-pad grooves and edges for a softer hand feel. It's slightly narrower in width than the 2022 original.

title: Fruiture
content: The Fruiture was a limited WYYC 2013 midnight release designed collectively by the Werrd Alliance and Wrecking Crew team. After many prototypes, the comfort-focused shape prioritized smooth play and extended combo sessions. Released in four fruit-named colorways — Strawberry, Blueberry, Plum, and Apple — each with a distinct laser etching design on the cup face. $100 USD.

title: Fubar
content:
About
FUBAR is the offstring signature model of Takumi Hakamata. Its design is minimized to the bare minimum, with a slightly smaller diameter that increases rotational force and makes it easier to handle — control performance built to help with regeneration tricks and technical combos.

title: Fugaku
content: AboutThe Fugaku is JT's high-end offstring released in 2024, featuring a precision-machined polycarbonate body paired with a stainless steel rim. Named after the traditional name for Mt. Fuji (Fugaku), it balances spinning power, stability, bounce, and maneuverability. Available in Clear Pink with Silver Rim.

title: Fuji
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re very excited to present the Fuji, a pocket rocket that’s smooth, fluid and a perfect everyday companion.

It’s part of a three-model series, that serves as our love letter to Japanese culture and design philosophy.

SPECS

Diameter 52.7mmWidth 45.9mmWeight 66.5gMaterial 7068 AL & SS

Over the past five years of our existence, Japanese design philosophy has been a core pillar of inspiration and reference of what we do at Atmos Projects. In the early 2010s, before Atmos’ inception, we spent a significant amount of time in the suburbs of Kyoto. This season of life was extremely immersive, and sparked a young and early passion for design and making. Our time there gave us a vision and appreciation for design that is subtle and restrained, highly attentive to form, and yet joyous and relentlessly practical in the way they take shape in the world. This extended to an appreciation for fabrics and materials, even in other spheres such as pottery, construction, and architecture. Our experience did not give us an aesthetic to emulate, but rather convictions and values that resonated deeply with our own process of making.

In fewer words, our approach to design and making has been centred around an obsessive care surrounding the form of an object (teinei / 丁寧), minimalism and restraint (shibumi / 渋い and kanso / 簡素), everyday-ness (yo no bi / 用の美), and joy (tanoshisa / 楽しさ). The Fuji and the other two unreleased designs were designed to represent all of that.

We started on the Fuji design project in 2022, and made a first round of prototypes in 2023. It originally began as a Side Effects-enabled bimetal, and went through two iterations without the SE system. These were bimetal designs made with brass rims for maximum rim weight, with the hope it would push boundaries in terms of technical performance — our focus at the time.

Images of these prototypes have surfaced on the Internet, and Fuji prototypes have also been in circulation after we gave them away through our membership, SPHERE. Unfortunately, the initial prototypes didn’t meet the mark, conceptually, or technically. It didn’t capture the essence of Fuji that we hoped for, despite early promising feedback. Despite being far into development, the Fuji was benched for some time. We were clear we needed fresh insight and new inspiration to take the design where it needed to go.

Then, in 2025, we launched System_Refresh° on SPHERE — an internal design initiative to look at old designs or previously shelved projects, and the Fuji was top of the list of design projects that quite obviously deserved a fresh look.

We departed from the old approach of a heavier, thinner and more aggressive design to something smaller and wider — the current Fuji proportions are relaxed and comfortable, from an ergonomic perspective. Instead of pushing hard for a maximalist, performance-oriented design, our refreshed approach was to create something easy, comfortable, and appropriate for the everyday.

The walls take reference from the topological lines of the Weatherman profile, but the cup is a simple and minimalist arc that hides a weight distribution tuned for power. The understated exterior hides an oversized capability — the very restraint in design we previously referenced. To that end, we refrained from unnecessary angles and lines, keeping the form as clean as possible. Some designs shout, but we wanted the Fuji to exist quietly, and assuredly in what it was made to be.

The Fuji’s playfeel was where we wanted to most establish its essence of yo no bi / 用の美 — or, in the way we understand it, it’s everydayness. We wanted it pocketable, easy to toss in your bag and to bring around without second thought — but still retained a surprising seriousness in its performance. It had to be capable and fun, yet not fatiguing. Bimetals can sometimes feel either heavy and muddy, or conversely thin and sparse, depending on the design approach taken by its makers.

The Fuji leans towards a grounded, smooth and fluid feel. Its thick stainless steel rims give it sufficient power at its smaller size, but its intentional weight distribution mechanics preserve its fluidness in motion so it neither feels plodding and clumsy, nor sparse and thin.

It handles softly and gently, and gives you all the control you want and need.

The Fuji was built as a representation of our design philosophies and approach, which has evolved and been refined over the past half decade. There’s an obvious evolution if you trace our early work to what we do today — but there is also a clear line of what is worthy, unique and joyous design that runs across our body of work.

title: Full Metal Damascus
content:
History / About
The Full Metal Damascus represents one of the most unique yoyos ever created, combining performance with distinctive aesthetics through its layered steel construction. Each piece is truly unique — no two yoyos will be alike due to the nature of the Damascus steel pattern.
This yo-yo is engineered to handle complex tricks while maintaining extended spin duration for technical sequences. Enso positions it as a collector’s item and professional-grade instrument, representing their aspirational design vision since the company’s founding. The piece merges exotic material selection with precision engineering to deliver both functionality and visual appeal.

title: Fulvia 6061 (Monometal Aluminum)
content:
History / About
The Fulvia design returns in a monometal 6061 aircraft-grade aluminum edition — Luftverk’s first monometal aluminum model in eight years. Available in Raw and Matte Gray finishes, it delivers long spin times and impressive stability while opening the Fulvia design to a wider audience at a lower price point than titanium. Released in a busy late-2024 window alongside the Stelvia XP589 and Akura MG.

title: Fulvia BTM-R
content:
History / About
The bimetal sibling to the Fulvia R, released the same day — May 31, 2016. The BTM-R (Bi-Metal Titanium Rim) uses Grade 5 titanium body halves with Stainless Steel 316 alloy weight rings for significantly greater rim weighting, stability, and spin time. It was Luftverk’s first bimetal release and demonstrated Jeffrey Pang’s commitment to pushing material boundaries from the beginning.

title: Fulvia R
content:
History / About
Released May 31, 2016 alongside its bimetal sibling the Fulvia BTM-R, the Fulvia R was the first Luftverk model to use the LuftPAD response system — a proprietary silicone pad that would go on to be included in all future releases. Focused on higher RPMs rather than brute rim weighting, it is more forgiving and accessible than the BTM-R while still being competition-ready. Limited to 30 polished, numbered units.

title: Fulvia TI7068
content:
History / About
The Fulvia TI7068 is Luftverk's first bimetal flagship design, pushing the limits of bimetal construction by substituting titanium rings for the traditional stainless steel. The less-dense titanium ring improves the spin feel on the initial throw and reduces the kickback typical of aggressive steel bimetals. Designer Jeffrey Pang drew the cup profile from a "concave meniscus" aesthetic — a distinctive lip that imitates a cup sitting in water with an upward-pulling tension. Available in both raw and anodized finishes, with the anodized version being a limited run. The raw finish was discontinued due to surface consistency difficulties in production.

title: Fury
content:
History / About
Our first no compromise in your face H-shaped throw. This 2012 variant is 3g lighter than the original which gives it a lot more floaty goodness. Stability is not affected. This thing flies like on rails.

Production Runs

Proto #1 — 15 units, Orange; D56.00mm / W43.00mm / 71.50g. Finish: Candodize.
Proto #2 — 10 units; D56.00mm / W43.00mm / 67.00g.
Proto #3 (February 2010) — 20 units, Silver; D56.00mm / W43.00mm / 66.50g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (April 2010) — 160 units, Red; D56.00mm / W43.00mm / 68.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #2 (August 2012) — 15 units, Titanium; D56.00mm / W43.00mm / 65.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.

title: Fury (Dale Tubat)
content:
About
Fury is Dale Tubat's oversized 3D-printed competition throw, over 63mm in diameter. Dual-density construction pairs heavier rim material with a lighter body, concentrating weight outward for extended spin. A dedicated finger-spin seat at the center holds solidly for tricks like DNA. Available in Black w/ Green Accents and White w/ Blue Accents. Priced at $34.99.

title: Fusion
content:
The Fusion is a collaboration yo-yo between Damian Puckett and Dressel Designs. It features a comfortable profile shape and the most complex ring design on the market (for its time)! The hanging ring allowed for placement of more rim weight to help create the most powerful and stable yoyo for this shape!

Fusion w/Brass Rings

In June of 2022 Dressel Designs released a version of the Fusion with Brass rings instead of Stainless Steel. This added another 2g to the overall weight of the Fusion.

title: Fusion 2.0
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Fusion was the perfect bimetal yoyo for me. It captured the feel of some of my favorite yoyos from the 2009 era with more modern performance. After getting feedback from top performers on the stage, collectors who have tried them all, and everybody in between, we are proud to bring you fusion 2.0!

So what's changed?

✅ Bigger and Better Weight Distribution and Size

✅ Featherweight aluminum body and an overall lighter weight

✅ Enhanced comfort and performance

✅ 4 all new colors"

title: Futura
content:
History / About
Futura is part of yoyorecreation's Typeface series of monometal 6061 aluminum throws. Spinkult (Sweden) released an exclusive Dark Purple "Spinkult Ed." colorway of the model in 2019, sold through spinkult.com for $58.

title: FUWA
content:
From Suspense:

"My first design was named FUWA and there’s 5 in existence. One was sold to a friend who really helped give me the confidence I needed in the beginning. One was test plated at a local shop, it’s a 1 of 1 gold, and does not play very well. One was sent to One Drop for their playable museum, the last two are with me. I designed this one in 2021 and recieved months later in May of 2022."

title: FUWA v2
content:
From Suspense:

"The next version’s idea was to change the design to be modular. One thing for me was to push the design extreme in both ways to find the middle ground balance point.

The concept was to have rubber weight rings that allowed for a press fit cap design. This made sure the caps were locked in, and eliminated any chance for vibe (in theory). It also allowed for smaller caps like Butterfly XT caps to fit."

"This design was maybe too over engineered. The issue was that, it was far too hard to remove the caps once they were in. The yoyo also did not play well without weight rings inside, the stock bare bones setup was 57g, the yoyo was too light. Designing around all of these constraints was too hard, I would need to alter the design completely, likely ditching my original plan of an organic.

5 exist, one is with One Drop, one is with a friend, the other three are with me."

title: FYFO
content:
About
FYFO — “First YoYo From Oregon” — was YYR's first yoyo machined at their new US facility. A comfortable rounded V-shape profile with powerful spin and excellent stability, in a minimal-but-slightly-oversized mono-metal body for a light on-string feel.

title: G-Squared Co-Lab
content:
History / About
The G-Squared Co-Lab is a collaboration between MonkeyfingeR Design (Ray Smith) and G-Squared Yoyos (Jake Elliott). The name is a pun on "collab." G-Squared contributed the Triton floor and hub geometry while MFD brought the Ape-X outer profile and their in-house anodizing. At 69.3g, it stands as one of the heaviest throws MonkeyfingeR has produced. Accepts G-Grip silicone pads or Monkey Snot. A second run followed the initial release.

title: Construct
content:
History / About
Released in May 2026, the Construct is G Squared's take on the classic O-shape profile. Rather than reinventing the form, the goal was to perfect it — a no-frills, comfortable throw built entirely around the enjoyment of play. Machined from 6061 aluminum with a diamond blast finish, the Construct pairs a G2 Ripper V2 bearing with G20 response pads and a 10mm axle.

title: Gadol
content:
About the Gadol
The Gadol — Hebrew for "big" or "great" — is an oversized 7068 aluminum bimetal from Mr. Mazal Top's Yoyos, announced on September 28, 2022, with only 10 units available. At 73mm diameter and 70.7g, it is notably larger and heavier than a typical competition yoyo. The brand positioned it not as a novelty but as a genuine performer, emphasizing that its oversized format provides a large catch zone and high-mass stability while still playing competitively. The extremely limited production run of 10 units makes it one of the rarest releases in the brand's catalog.

title: Gaia
content:
From Alchemik:

"Evolving from our first release, The Tyrant, The Gaia represents a refined return to our origins—reimagined in Grade 5 titanium and fitted with a C Bearing for a smoother, more deliberate feel. More than an upgrade in materials, it’s a transformation in experience: Grade 5 titanium delivers a density, balance, and tactile presence that is immediately apparent—cool to the touch, solid in hand, and unmistakably premium. At the center of the cup, a precision-engraved logo is executed with tight tolerances and finished seamlessly into the surface, serving as a quiet signature of the machining precision and restraint that define The Gaia. Every interaction, from the first spin to prolonged play, reflects a level of intention and refinement designed for collectors who value nuance and uncompromising quality.

Why Titanium Grade 5?Titanium Grade 5 (Ti-6Al-4V) stands apart from other titanium grades because it is a true performance alloy. By combining titanium with aluminum and vanadium, Grade 5 achieves exceptional strength while remaining remarkably lightweight—far stronger than commercially pure titanium without sacrificing corrosion resistance. This unique balance of durability, precision, and longevity makes Grade 5 the gold standard for aerospace, medical, and high-performance applications where materials are expected to perform flawlessly under stress."

title: Gairyusen
content:
History / About
Gairyusen (凱龍閃, RY-011) is the storyline's final-boss yoyo, a "V5" free-spinning-outer-catch-zone design. Sturm Panzer's official page states the V5 system is used with permission of Team Pre King (Chen Jialin's yoyo design collective); this permission claim is first-party only and could not be independently corroborated. Bundled with Storybook Vol.11, which includes a Zoids retrospective.

meta.yya_bearing_size: CP-06 D9 center (Size D) + two Size-C flat bearings for the free-spinning V5 rim

title: Galactus
content: AboutThe Galactus is OFFSET's team model rather than a named-player signature. Marketed at launch as the world's widest bi-metal at 60mm, it features what OFFSET calls Extra Catch Technology: an angular inner body profile that guides string into the gap even on off-center hits, reducing rejections during technical tricks. Colorways are named for members of the OFFSET pro team — Allon Splash, Xavier Red, Brandon Splash, and Angel2Up Fade — making it a celebration of the full roster.

title: Galaxy Dinosaur
content: Galaxy Diver-shaped model featuring titanium rim rings — same shape as the Galaxy Diver but with titanium replacing stainless steel for a different balance of weight and feel.

title: Galaxy Diver
content: Wide-bodied 7075 bi-metal in C3's Galaxy series, delivering exceptional stability for off-axis and horizontal trick play.

title: Galaxy Diver 7075 v2
content: History / AboutPhysical alloy and weight-distribution revision of the wide Galaxy Diver platform.

title: Galaxy Surfer
content: Ultra-wide bi-metal Galaxy model with extended stainless steel rims for maximum spin power and stability.

title: Gamer AL Light
content: AboutThe Gamer AL Light is Rain City's aluminum lightweight take on the flagship Gamer design, developed after community feedback that earlier aluminum versions were too heavy for modern responsive tricks. Designed for stall-based play. Includes both a full C bearing and a slim bearing. Comes in a hard shell case.

title: Gamma Crash
content: C3's first composite/hybrid yo-yo and the founding model of the Crash series. In 2017, C3 reignited the hybrid yo-yo craze by combining POM plastic with a stainless steel weight ring — merging the soft catch of plastic with the spin power of metal rims. Delivers "the control and speed of top-end bi-metal yo-yos, with the soft catch of light plastic yo-yos." Available in White/Gold Rim, Black/Gold Rim, White/Silver Rim, Yellow, Red, Blue, Black/Silver, Green/Black, Black/Blue, Green, White/Rainbow Rim. Price: $69.99.

title: Gargantua
content: AboutThe Gargantua is an oversized injection-molded plastic designed for 1A play — not 4A offstring, despite its size. It pushes the maximum diameter boundary of competition-legal play, giving 1A players the largest possible catch zone while keeping the throw on-string. Iori Yamaki, one of yoyorecreation's elite team players, used the Gargantua in his semi-final performance at the 2015 World YoYo Contest, demonstrating that its extreme size was a competitive asset rather than a novelty. A POM variant (POM Gargantua) was released in 2016.

title: OG-OM
content: About the OG-OMThe OG-OM is the founding model of Gates YoYo and the design that established Jon Gates's reputation in the fixed-axle community. Each half is individually hand-turned on a lathe, resulting in subtle variations from unit to unit. The yo-yo features a weight-rim ply construction — concentric laminated wood layers that concentrate mass toward the rim for extended spin times. Originally discontinued, the OG-OM was relaunched with improved execution and continues to be regarded as one of the finest hand-made fixed-axle throws available.Spin time with good technique: 10–15 seconds. Capable of looping tricks, Boingy Boingy, and classic fixed-axle play.

title: Ohm
content: About the OhmThe Ohm is the ball-bearing evolution of Gates YoYo's popular fixed-axle OG-OM design. Built from laminated hardwood with a One Drop fresh bearing installed, it delivers unresponsive play with the warmth and character of hand-turned wood. Designed for intermediate to advanced players comfortable with bind response. Ships with Foxtail string, which is described as exceptionally soft once broken in and highly durable. Tested spin times exceed five minutes, making it suitable for competition-level 1A, 3A, and 5A play. Each unit is hand-made with slight individual variations.

title: OHM XL
content: About the OHM XLThe OHM XL is an enlarged iteration of the popular OHM model, adding diameter and mass for players who prefer a larger, heavier throw. Like all Gates YoYo products, it is hand-turned on a lathe from laminated hardwood with no jigs or molds, giving each unit a slightly individual character. Unresponsive with bind response, intended for intermediate to advanced players. Ships with Foxtail string.

title: Gaza-fury
content:
About
The Gaza-fury is a distinct mid-range offering from SpinGear that steps beyond the beginner SpinGadget line into bind-required unresponsive play. It uses SpinGear's proprietary SGX-SYSTEM response and is available in two materials: polycarbonate or POM. The D-size flat bearing and H-shaped profile support string trick performance. Available in Red/Blue, Black, Yellow/Blue, and Clear/Purple colorways.

title: GBP
content:
History / About
The GBP is described by G2 as "something special" — a 48-gram full-size bimetal yoyo, unique, fun, and playable. Preorders ran for a single 12-hour window on January 8, 2021, with remaining balances due upon shipment in early April 2021.

title: Gear 2
content:
History / About
The Gear 2 is a compact bimetal training yoyo designed as a miniature version of the Gear 5 competition model. Despite its smaller size, it features dimensions that completely change the feel compared to typical mini yoyos, delivering performance characteristics similar to full-size models.
The thick stainless steel rim contributes to stability and extended spin duration. Available in Prism Paradise (polished cherry blossom pink), Augusta Purple (matte plum), Dark Miku (polished teal), Goku (polished orange), and Alicization (matte royal blue), including signature editions for team riders Marc Zuno and Levi White.

title: GEEDORAH
content:
History / About
The GEEDORAH is GWAY Throws’ fifth release and first competition-oriented design, shaped by Sean Collins with box art and engraving by Danyllo Barbiero. The double-rim construction pushes more mass toward the outer edges, increasing momentum and stability for demanding technical sequences. Narrowly rounded rims keep the profile maneuverable despite the added rim weight.
The name and three-headed dragon kaiju artwork give the yoyo a distinctive visual identity. Colorways included Teal, Pinkish Red, Copper, Gray, Faded Dream (Pink/Gray Fade), and Ectoplasm (Purple/Green/White Splash).

title: Gelada
content:
History / About
The Gelada is MonkeyfingeR Design’s second release and the throw that established the company’s catalog identity. Named after the gelada (a large Ethiopian primate known for its distinctive mane), it features a classic butterfly profile with low-edge geometry. Developed internally as the "LUX" before launch, the Gelada introduced MFD’s practice of treating all throws with Buff polish — a standard carried through every subsequent release. Multiple colorway runs followed its initial drop.

title: Gelada 2
content:
History / About
The Gelada 2 is MonkeyfingeR Design’s follow-up to their flagship model. Retaining the butterfly geometry of the original, the Gelada 2 pushes the weight up to 66.6g and widens the gap to 4.5mm for a more assertive, stable play character. It became MFD’s most-requested model in later years, leading to the 2.1 revision and multiple re-releases. The Gelada lineage forms the core identity of the MFD catalog.

title: Gelada 2.1
content:
History / About
The Gelada 2.1 is a refined revision of the Gelada 2 — MonkeyfingeR Design’s most-requested throw. The geometry carries over from the Gelada 2 with a slight weight adjustment and the updated Tasmanian Tornado Hybrid bearing. Described by retailers as "the most requested throw even years after its original release," it received multiple re-releases and a YoYoNews giveaway colorway edition in 2016.

meta.yya_bearing_size: MFD REvolution (Tasmanian Tornado) Hybrid Size C

title: 5 Star
content: AboutThe 5 Star is General-Yo's second model and the company's first competition throw, featuring an hourglass profile shaped for hand comfort and a deeper recess for silicone response. The first run produced approximately 100 units.The 5 Star became one of General-Yo's most enduring models, released in a large number of special-edition colorways over the years: the 2009 Nationals Edition (10 made), the Christmas Collaboration (10 made), UK Edition (20 made), Germany Edition, Japan Edition, and USA Edition, among others. Current production runs ship with a string centering bearing and 19mm slim pad response. An ongoing classic in the General-Yo lineup.

title: Amplitude
content: AboutThe Amplitude was described at release as Ernie Kaiser's 15th unique design. A departure from General-Yo's signature organic shapes into a V-profile, the Amplitude is optimized for fast, technical play. Lightweight for an all-aluminum throw at 63.4g. The tumbled pyramatte finish provides excellent grind performance. Not a relaxed throw — purpose-built for speed and technical combos.Sold out quickly after its initial release. A second run was produced. Discontinued.

title: Atonement
content: AboutThe Atonement is General-Yo's first brass-ring bimetal, combining a 7075 aluminum body with brass rings for a distinctive heavy, authoritative spin character that differs from the stainless steel ring models. An organic-shaped bimetal powerhouse.

title: Banger
content: AboutThe Banger was built specifically for the General-Yo team, with design input aimed at players pushing 3A and 5A alongside 1A. Refined weight distribution targets control and balance across all play styles for long flowing combos.The Banger is notable for being the first General-Yo in 17 years to use non-proprietary response pads: One Drop 19mm pads, chosen by Ernie for their slightly softer feel and thinner depth compared to General-Yo's own HAT pads. This marks a significant milestone given the brand's long history of proprietary response systems dating back to their 2008 founding.

title: Entheos
content: AboutThe Entheos is General-Yo's first throw to depart from purely rounded shapes, introducing a straight body with flat rims that was unprecedented in the General-Yo lineup. The flat rim design produces noticeably longer sleep times. Named after the Greek word "entheos" (ἔνθεος) meaning "in god" or "inspired by god." Uses the kotinos (an olive wreath, symbol of glory and peace) as its logo engraving.Fewer than 150 units were produced. The Entheos was Ernie Kaiser's ninth design. Discontinued.

title: Essence
content: AboutThe Essence is General-Yo's synthesis throw, designed to combine the rims of the Hatrick, the catch zone of the 5 Star, and the weight of the Torrent into a single cohesive design. Only 88 units were released in the original 2011 run, making it one of the most collectible General-Yo models.The Essence was reissued in 2020 (Essence 2020) in new colorways including Red and Red/Black Half-Swap, retaining the same specs with a bead-blasted finish and string-centering bearing. The 2020 reissue retailed at approximately $69.

title: Hatrick
content: AboutThe Hatrick is General-Yo's third release and arguably their signature throw. An undersized, round-profile yoyo named with a play on "hat trick" — three successes. It became so popular that Ernie produced numerous subsequent runs with many limited colorways over the years.First run editions include: Production Gray/Blue (70 made), BadAss Edition (12 made), 2009 Nationals Edition (10 made), Christmas Collaboration (10 made), Blue/Red (89 made), Red/Black (41 made), UK Edition (20 made, yellow/silver), and USA Edition (20 made). The Hatrick 10th Anniversary was released in 2019 with the same specs in special colorways. The Hatrick line continues to the present day. See also: Hatrick 2 (2023 bimetal).

title: Hatrick 2
content: AboutThe Hatrick 2 is the bimetal evolution of General-Yo's most iconic model. The beloved organic undersized profile of the original Hatrick is retained while stainless steel rings dramatically extend spin times and improve stability. The body retains the same comfortable hand feel as the original while performing at a much higher competitive level.

title: KLR
content: AboutThe KLR is named for the initials of its three co-designers: Ernie Kaiser, Alex Lee, and James Reed. An aggressive modified V-shape profile in 7075 aluminum, designed to push stability and speed for competitive play. Very limited original production. Inspired later General-Yo designs including the Royal 1.The KLR was reissued in August 2024 in a slightly refined version with updated dimensions and color options (Black/Red Splash, Black/Red Fade, Powder Blue). The 2024 reissue retails at approximately $48.

title: Legato
content: AboutThe Legato is General-Yo's first bimetal yoyo. Built off the Prestige's profile, it adds stainless steel rings set into the cup for increased rim weight, delivering rock-solid stability and long spin times. Also notable as the first General-Yo designed in the USA but machined in China.The Legato introduced Ernie's string-centering K bearing — the first General-Yo to ship with this bearing type. Limited production. Discontinued. See also: Legato II (2022).

title: Legato II
content: AboutThe Legato II refines the original 2016 Legato bimetal, adding 1g to the stainless steel ring weight and widening the gap slightly for improved bind response. Maintains the V-shaped profile and rock-solid stability of the original.

title: Magnum
content: AboutThe Magnum is General-Yo's most experimental release and one of the rarest yoyos the company ever produced. Machined from magnesium and finished with nickel plating, the Magnum was one of only two production-quantity magnesium yoyos of its time (the other being the YoYoJam FH-MG). Development took over 10 months for Ernie Kaiser to master the magnesium-plus-nickel-plate machining process.The magnesium alloy allows approximately 30% more rim mass at the same total weight compared to aluminum, pushing spin performance and stability. Only 48 units were released, making it among the rarest and most collectible General-Yo throws ever produced.

title: Majesty
content: AboutThe Majesty is a landmark General-Yo release — the first to use 7075 aluminum alloy. Larger, wider, and more angular than any previous General-Yo model, it was purpose-built for modern freestyle competition in 2012. Far ahead of its time, the Majesty proved that General-Yo could compete directly with the V-profile competition yoyos that were dominating contest stages.Multiple production runs were made over the years. The Majesty 2020 reissue retained the same specifications in new colorways including Orange. The 2020 reissue retailed at approximately $68.99.

title: Mini Star
content: AboutThe Mini Star is General-Yo's fourth release and their first undersized competition throw, built directly off the 5 Star's profile at pocket-yoyo scale. It debuted at the 2010 USA Southwest Regional Contest. Extremely limited production. Includes a Purple Heart special edition among other colorways. Discontinued. See also: Mini Star 2 (2022 bimetal).

title: Mini Star 2
content: AboutThe Mini Star 2 is the bimetal successor to the original 2010 Mini Star, retaining its pocket-sized dimensions while adding stainless steel inner rings to push spin and stability far beyond what the original monometal could achieve. A compact powerhouse for competitive play.

title: Model 10
content: AboutThe Model 10 (also known as M10) is General-Yo's first step-straight-profile throw, breaking from the brand's tradition of organic rounded shapes. The name "Model 10" refers to it being Ernie Kaiser's tenth unique design. It debuted at the 2013 California State YoYo Contest and reached retail at YoYoExpert in early 2014.Known for a floaty, graceful feel despite its competition focus. The Model 10 has a notable story: a retail shipment was stolen from YoYoExpert in early 2014 and later recovered as police evidence. After a two-year court case, Ernie sold those exact units under the name "M10 Evidence" — a nod to the evidence tag placed on the recovered merchandise.

title: Prestige
content: AboutThe Prestige became General-Yo's best-selling model in 2016. It features the brand's signature engraved side face on a soft step-straight profile — a blend of their classic organic aesthetic with modern V-shape performance, machined from 7075 aluminum for exceptional smoothness.The Prestige was reissued as the Prestige 2022 with a raised hub for finger spins and new colorways — Lavender, Blue Dream (Alec Cecena's signature color), and Red Icon — along with a string centering bearing.

title: Prophecy
content: AboutThe Prophecy is a full-sized butterfly-shaped 6061 aluminum throw featuring a custom centrifugal hub designed specifically for finger spins and grinds. Ernie Kaiser described it as "a predestined shape that was meant to be." First shown as a prototype at the 2015 California State YoYo Championships. Limited release. Discontinued.

title: Royal 1
content: AboutThe Royal 1 is marketed as "the product of 12 years in the making" — Ernie Kaiser's synthesis of what he learned across the entire General-Yo catalog: the profile from the KLR, the cup design from the Majesty, and the weight distribution of the Model 10. A high-powered, stable, and smooth all-aluminum throw available at a relatively accessible price point. Colorways include Torrent Blue and Solid Clear (Crown Badass variant).

title: Torrent
content: AboutThe Torrent is General-Yo's first-ever release, launched in December 2008. Ernie Kaiser designed it before he could even perform modern string tricks — the result is a rounded, organic-profile throw built from first principles. Only about 60 units made it through Ernie's quality inspection on the first run, as he rejected the majority for vibe. That uncompromising standard became the defining trait of the General-Yo brand.The Torrent uses Born Crucial Ghost Pads on the original run and transitions to Hat-Pad response on subsequent runs. It remained in production through multiple small runs before eventually being updated as the Torrent II.

title: Torrent II
content: AboutThe Torrent II faithfully revisits General-Yo's founding throw with the same organic rounded curves, high walls, and thumb-grindable rims from the 2008 original. The primary update from the original Torrent is a modern 20mm HAT Pad response, replacing the older .555 / Ghost Pad format. Marketing emphasized "back after over a decade." Retailed at approximately $69.

title: Ghost
content:
History / About
The Ghost was released in 2017 as part of G2's expanding lineup during their mid-era. Named in keeping with G2's supernatural/creature naming theme (Banshee, Wolf, Ghost). Specific design details and full specs were not available in accessible archived sources at time of research — additional documentation may be available at gsquaredyoyos.com or in the G2 Nation Facebook group.

title: Ghost 24
content:
About
Ghost 24 is a plastic with SS rims yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2023. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Ghost IX
content: Sora Ishikawa's first C3 signature, designed for 5A counterweight freestyle competition. Price: $54.99.

title: Gladiator Slave
content:
History
The Gladiator Slave was Frank Difeo's return to active releasing after several years of quieter production. A tribute to the 2004 Worlds mod contest Gladiator — but without the side spikes — it was described as fusing "old school style with modern competition level performance." The wide, flat-rimmed butterfly shape carried an intricate carved cup design and precision weighted set screws.
The Gladiator Slave was notable for introducing the silicone Dif-Binder response pads, replacing the traditional Dif Pads that Frank had used since the early days. A gold acid wash variant was produced in limited quantities alongside the standard anodized options.

meta.yya_weight: 60g (61.5g with 2 O-rings; 63.5g with 4 O-rings; 70.5g with pogs + O-rings)

title: Gladius
content: About GladiusThrow Revolution's premium flagship bi-metal yo-yo. The Gladius represents the pinnacle of the brand's design philosophy, delivering uncompromising performance for championship-level string tricks.

title: Glanz
content:
History / About
Signature model for Sora Tahira, 2024 All-Japan 3A Champion. "Glanz" is German for "shine." Built primarily for 3A with stated versatility across 3A/5A/1A play, prioritizing spin time and agility for high-risk multi-yoyo tricks.

title: Gleipnir
content: AboutThe Gleipnir takes its name from Norse mythology — Gleipnir is the magical chain forged by dwarves to bind the wolf Fenrir, while the Sleipnir is Odin's eight-legged horse. The relationship between names reflects the relationship between models: the Gleipnir shares the Sleipnir's basic geometry but adds a rounder outer profile, 3g of additional weight (to 68.2g), and ships with a KonKave bearing. The result is stronger spin momentum with a slightly more organic feel in the hand.

title: GLHF
content: GLHF was a beginner-to-advanced convertible yo-yo sold through the MikeMonty store in 2021. It arrived responsive with a half-spec Size C bearing and short axle, while the box included a standard full-width Size C bearing, wider axle, bearing-removal keychain, and string for unresponsive play.The design included fingerspin cups and was offered in a documented Sky Blue variant for $15. Because the model is absent from Mike’s current retrospective and the old store described its catalog more broadly as made for, used, or endorsed by MikeMonty, its exact design and manufacturing attribution remains unresolved.

meta.yya_axle: Short responsive and wider unresponsive axles included
meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (half-spec responsive and full-width unresponsive included)

title: Glitterspin
content: HistoryThe Glitterspin featured jewels set in a square pattern across the wooden body, creating a shimmering effect. Premium decorative variant, contest models exist but are ultra-rare. Produced from 1947 onward.

title: Glory Insignia
content: AboutThe Glory Insignia is a 2025 competition bimetal with a wider-than-standard 52mm profile and 6061 aluminum body paired with stainless steel outer rings. Priced at $85. Available in Red, Silver, Champagne Gold, and Blue colorways.

title: Go Big
content: About the Go BigThe Go Big is Ben Conde's 4A signature model, featuring rubber-overmolded wings for enhanced durability and bounce-back on missed catches — a critical feature for extended offstring practice. The Solid Spin Axle system and size-appropriate bearing provide spin stability for the large aerial tricks of 4A play. It became one of the most recommended 4A yo-yos for developing players.

title: Aquila
content: AboutThe Aquila is God-Tricks' most technically advanced 4A off-string model, developed after applying 1A performance principles to off-string play. The adjustable gap system includes 8 pairs of spacers covering a 1.93–3.33mm wheelbase range. Designed for superior bounce, excellent idle ability, and fault-tolerant recovery. Built to professional rope standards.

title: Bomber
content: AboutThe Bomber features a distinctive S-shape profile. At ~70g, the thick outer rim generates substantial rotational inertia for extended spin during long combo sequences. Inverse-round shape suited to intricate string work. Available in Red, Purple, and Gold.

title: Bounty Hunter
content: AboutThe Bounty Hunter is God-Tricks' oversized full-metal model. Its step-straight body profile with rounded outer edges minimizes hand impact on catches — a practical consideration for aggressive play. The low edge design prevents tilting during trick execution. Suited for larger hands and capable of horizontal and rail tricks. Available in an exceptionally wide range of colorways including themed Halloween editions.

title: Cyclone
content: AboutThe Cyclone became one of God-Tricks' most popular models thanks to its unconventional wide-to-diameter ratio H-profile, pushing weight further from center than expected for the size. The result is impressive spin stability at a price that undercuts most comparable metals. Particularly popular with 5A counterweight players. Available in solid and blasted colorways.

title: Cyclone IV
content: AboutThe Cyclone IV is the fourth iteration of the Cyclone series, expanding the diameter to 59mm while keeping weight low at 63.7g. The larger catch zone and lighter construction push the series toward faster, more agile performance. Limited English-language documentation is available for this model.

title: Cyclone Mark 5
content: AboutThe Cyclone Mark 5 is the fifth generation of God-Tricks' flagship Cyclone series. The outer circle diameter has been adjusted for compatibility with additional trick styles, and the stability threshold has been raised to prevent inconsistencies during fast combos. Positioned specifically for speed-focused play at a reduced weight of 63.8g versus earlier iterations.

title: Cyclone Next
content: AboutThe Cyclone Next was designed as a synthesis of two God-Tricks staples: the original Cyclone's wide-gap maneuverability and the Return's rim-weighted power. The result is an H-profile full-metal described by the manufacturer as "superbly balanced." Uses CBC slim response pads. Available in Red, Purple, Blue, and Gold.

title: Cyclops
content: AboutThe Cyclops features a step-round profile that gives a characteristically soft, light feeling in the hand and on the string. Full-sized at 55.91mm with standard dimensions, it was positioned as an approachable first full-metal for players stepping up from plastic. American comic-inspired aesthetics. Available in Blue, Silver, Green, and Red.

title: Destiny
content: AboutThe Destiny was God-Tricks' first international hit and the model that established the brand globally. Lightweight and nimble, it features a shortened axle to reduce center weight and flattened sides for improved stability. Its inverse-round shape with low edges near the response area made it accessible for players at all skill levels. Sold on YoYoExpert from launch. A limited Chinese New Year Red edition followed in early 2011.

title: Destiny Mark 3
content: AboutThe Destiny Mark 3 is the third refinement of God-Tricks' flagship Destiny model. Described as "all-powerful," it offers improved stability and idle over earlier iterations while maintaining the balanced feel that made the original Destiny popular. Designed as a bridge yoyo for players developing their skill — stable enough to avoid the "out of control" feel of pure speedballs while remaining fast and responsive. Available in two-tone acid-wash colorways.

title: Eternal
content: AboutThe Eternal was the first flagship model under God-Tricks' premium GT·INFINITY sub-label. Heavier than most contemporaries at ~69g, it delivers greater rotational inertia for extended spin and improved stability in complex combo sequences. A lustrous finish adds visual presence in competition. Round body shape. Available in solid and acid-wash colorways including a Christmas limited edition.

title: Evolution
content: AboutThe Evolution is the second model in God-Tricks' GT·INFINITY premium series. Its H-profile silhouette with a thicker outer rim pushes weight toward the wings for greater power and stability. A slight concave cutout in the center wing adds visual distinction. Matte smooth coating. Available in striking two-tone colorways including a Chinese New Year black/red edition.

title: Exalted Perseus
content: AboutThe Exalted Perseus is the GT·INFINITY upgrade of the 2016 Perseus, using Korean 7075 aluminum alloy for the body and a stainless steel ring for rim weighting. The "Exalted" name references astrological terminology for enhanced elevation and power. Redesigned to address muscle fatigue issues identified in the original Perseus while preserving its core performance. Particularly accommodating for players with hand or shoulder injuries.

title: Fire Return
content: AboutThe Fire Return is the signature model of Su Chen Dong, Chinese 3A yoyo champion. Refined from the standard Return, it sheds 2g for improved control and responsiveness in double-handed 3A play. Strong stability supports complex paired-yoyo string tricks. Available in acid-wash two-tone colorways with silver splash.

title: Freedom
content: AboutThe Freedom was God-Tricks' first production yoyo, establishing the brand's mission of competition-capable metals at beginner-friendly prices. Its mix of round and straight body profile delivers a blended feel suited to chopstick and string trick play. Smooth anodizing minimizes sleep loss. Available in Blue, Gold, and Silver.

title: Freedom Mark II
content: AboutThe Freedom Mark II revisits the brand's debut model with updated dimensions and an H-profile silhouette. Both diameter and width are increased by approximately 2mm over the original Freedom, pushing the Mark II into larger mid-size territory. Straight profile with geometry changes that improve feel and power versus the original. Available in acid-wash two-tone colorways with silver splash.

title: Freedom Origin
content: AboutThe Freedom Origin is God-Tricks' 17th product and a spiritual relaunch of the brand's founding Freedom model for a new generation of beginners. Designed for speed, quick response, and steady performance, it was released as part of "Project 99Cash" — a brand initiative to offer high-quality entry throws at 99 RMB (~$15 USD) domestically. The "Origin" name references God-Tricks' founding mission of accessible performance.

title: Hercules
content: AboutThe Hercules is God-Tricks' titanium entry under the GT·INFINITY sub-label, constructed from TC4 (Ti-6Al-4V, Grade 5) alloy with post-processing for enhanced luster. Named for the twelve labors of Hercules, paralleling titanium's legendary hardness. Delivers stability and idle comparable to stainless steel rim bimetals with the distinctive resonant echo of titanium. Finger spin excluded from intended use. A late-career prestige release for the brand.

title: J-Power
content: AboutThe J-Power is a GT·INFINITY premium model featuring a distinctive two-tone striped anodize and a clean H-profile silhouette with low edge. Competition-focused design. Available in Blue/Red, Black/Yellow, Purple/Pink, Yellow/Green, and Silver/Green.

title: Justice
content: AboutThe Justice is God-Tricks' 19th product. At 69g it is heavier relative to its size, reducing fatigue in throws and catches during extended play. Designed so most trick styles complete even under ultra-low rotation. Emphasizes stability in complex structural trick combinations. Available in Black, Blue, Red, Purple, and Grey.

title: Kepler-11
content: AboutThe Kepler-11 is a GT·INFINITY premium sub-label model named after the Kepler-11 planetary system — a star containing six transiting planets discovered by NASA's Kepler mission. It continues the GT·INFINITY tradition of naming premium models after mythology and science. Limited English-language documentation is available; specifications are unconfirmed.

title: Mystery
content: AboutThe Mystery was God-Tricks' first venture into plastic construction for 1A play. Rather than injection-molded plastic, it is CNC-machined from Delrin (POM) — a harder, more precise material. The oversized inverse-round design with thick rim balances trick-landing ease with spin durability. A budget-accessible alternative to the brand's aluminum line. Available in Black, Blue, and Pink.

title: Pegasus
content: AboutThe Pegasus succeeded the Windforce as God-Tricks' dedicated 4A off-string model. Machined from hard Delrin (POM) plastic, its H-profile provides bounce and recovery for off-string techniques. Adjustable gap via included spacers accommodates different string gauges. Removable metal side caps (2.6g each) allow weight customization. Ships with four extra response pads in two thicknesses. Available in Red and Blue.

title: Perseus
content: AboutThe Perseus is the debut bimetal under the GT·INFINITY premium sub-label, first sold at the China YOYO Corporation Championship in 2016 after two years of development. Named after the Greek mythological hero, it combines a 7075 aluminum alloy body with a heavy stainless steel outer ring for extreme stability, spin capacity, and an "ultra wide effective line width." Five performance pillars: stabilization, lasting, accuracy, high speed, and power.

title: Return
content: AboutThe Return focuses on rotational power through a thick outer rim in an H-profile construction. Includes a 10-ball bearing for smoother spin straight from the box. Smooth finish. Available in Green, Red, Purple, Blue, and Pink.

title: Reverie
content: AboutThe Reverie was the first oversized model under the GT·INFINITY premium sub-label. Its inverse-round body features distinctive checkered laser etching. Designed for fast play and athletic body tricks while avoiding the sluggish feel typical of larger throws — at 69g it remains agile for its size. Horizontal-trick capable. Available in Blue and Silver.

title: SIP
content: AboutThe SIP (God-Tricks' 23rd product) is a CNC-machined polycarbonate yoyo with an innovative modular weight system. Interchangeable covers allow three distinct weight configurations, and players can substitute beverage can lids or coins for DIY aesthetics and customization. The high-toughness polycarbonate is more impact-resistant than POM, surviving drops that would dent metal. Particularly suited to 3A and 5A play. The concept was developed years earlier but shelved until the design matured.

title: Sonic Cyclone
content: AboutThe Sonic Cyclone (Cyclone Mark II) is the third entry in the Cyclone series. At 64.1g it is lighter than its predecessors, and its wider body with larger diameter enables faster, more agile play. The H-profile maintains the series' characteristic stability despite the reduced weight. Available in Light Blue, Gold, Light Green, Red, and Silver.

title: Tai Chi
content: AboutThe Tai Chi was a promotional exclusive released at the World YoYo Contest 2018, priced at RM 15 (Malaysian ringgit) — a subsidized contest price. Designed as a transitional throw for players upgrading from responsive to unresponsive play, it features hybrid response behavior bridging the two styles. Very limited distribution; sold only at the contest.

title: Trump
content: AboutThe Trump was God-Tricks' first bimetal yoyo, pairing an aluminum body with stainless steel rim weighting for improved spin power and stability. Designed for extended "constant rotation" rather than explosive initial spin, making it forgiving for practice while still delivering competition-capable performance. Thumb-grind and top-on capable. Available in a wide range of colorways including seasonal and acid-wash editions.

title: Venture
content: AboutThe Venture is a GT·INFINITY model with an unconventional construction: an aluminum inverse-round body paired with a metal-plated Celcon (POM) weight ring rather than a traditional metal rim. The result is a lighter, flightier feel compared to standard full-metals of similar dimensions. One side carries the GT·INFINITY logo; the other features character art. A Valentine's Day "LOVenture" variant substituted the GT·INFINITY logo for a themed design.

title: Windforce
content: AboutThe Windforce was God-Tricks' entry into the 4A off-string category. Machined from hard POM (Delrin) plastic, its inverse-round body offers durability for the impacts inherent to off-string play. The adjustable string gap via included spacer and washer set allows players to tune the throw for their string and style preference.

title: Goji
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

This has been a crazy month for us, having just released the Gravity with Round Spinning Objects. That was a whirlwind, and we’re incredibly grateful for all of your support.

All the same, we’re very excited and proud to announce something that has been in the works for a long time.

Say hello to the Goji.

SPECS

dia 52.5mmwid 49.7mmweight 63.5gmaterial 7068 AL

If you’ve been on this thread at all, you’d know that our design process always begins with some acknowledgement of history. That is usually where we begin, and our hope is that by the end of each design cycle we have added on to the body of work that has come before.

The Cloudberry was our attempt to saddle lightness and power and to find its place a long line of great organics; the Pomelo an oversized featherweight that pays homage to the fat, chunky designs of the 2000-2010s era.

The Goji begins with the lineage of great undersized organics. It is easy to call to mind which they are, because they’ve been and remained iconic throughout the years – Yoyofactory’s 888, Caribou Lodge’s Wooly Marmot, and Anti-Yo’s Bapezilla remain some of the most emblematic and enduring instances, and in my view, this lineage is continued today in wonderful designs in One Drop and Static Co.'s Parlay and Sudo, and A-RT’s Sparrow, amongst a few others.

The challenges for us in putting out something we felt could stand amongst such storied designs were in adapting the classical shape and specifications for modern play. Undersized designs are sometimes limited in spin power and stability. That “sensitivity” to off-axis movement is part of the joy that accompanies small and round return tops.

At the same time, we wanted the experience of someone using the Goji to be as thoughtless, free, and unexacting on the player as possible – something you could just comfortably jam with, without it requiring too much care and focus.

We wanted to take the intensity and intentionality of honing a player’s precision out of the experience, and provide something more fun, more effortless.

Our first prototype weighed in at 66.6g. It was a total spin machine.

Isaac Sams is someone we’ve had the privilege of helping us test early iterations of our designs. Of the Cloudberry, Thunderberry, Pomelo and the Goji, he wrote back saying the Goji was his favourite – that was quite an affirming moment for us.

Still, I personally felt it overpowered the Thunderberry, which was an interesting and exciting experience in itself – it could just go on and on. It reminded me of the Bapezilla 2, which felt thunderous in playfeel despite having an unassuming profile.

Power wasn’t an issue, but its nimbleness was.

An early design prompt that was core to the process of creating the Goji was that it had to feel like it could “run” on the string.

An early working title for the project before we settled on a final name was Peter Rabbit, which was meant to help us visualise the sort of liveliness it should have in play. If you’ve ever seen old videos of Jensen Kimmitt trick-shredding on a Wooly Marmot in that inimitable hop-style, you’d have a sense of what we were fixated on.

We took a month off design work to play and test the Goji, so we could find clarity in what we wanted to keep, and what we’d take off the board.

We liked the Goji’s profile, and so we retained its silhouette completely intact, but we eventually overhauled its entire weight distribution. After reconstructing its rim and cup, the design turned out 3.1g lighter, which is a significant mass for any return top, much less one this small.

Prototype II came back possessing that very litheness on the string. It isn’t as powerful as Prototype I, but still has enough juice to get through most modern tricksets.

It’s not meant for competition in the slightest, but if kicking back and jamming for hours is something that sounds like a good idea to you, you might just like the Goji.

This thing just sprints across string.

As always, thank you for getting to the end of another of these very long posts. If you have any thoughts or comments, I’d absolutely love to hear what you think!

·
