content:
History / About
Limited-edition colorway of the HandQuake 2, listed by the Yo-Yo Museum as a 2024 release. Exact date within 2024 unconfirmed.

title: HandQuake 2 – Working Breakfast
content:
History / About
Limited-edition colorway of the HandQuake 2. Yo-Yo Museum records announcement January 7, 2024 and shipping January 24, 2024.

title: Hanzo
content:
History / About
A monometal companion to the bimetal Hattori, carrying the same shuriken-inspired cutout body at about 4g lighter — a more affordable entry into the cutout concept.

title: Harmonic
content:
From Motion:

"Say hello to Harmonic (motion)

The motion lineup is strong, very strong. The market has had a lot of organics over the past couple of years. We decided to wait and make sure we got it right. Our motto is not to release anything unless it improves the game: Harmonic does this.

On first throw, you will notice that harmonic feels like throwing air, but the weight is there - you just don't feel it. It makes a beautiful sound befitting its name. A hollow bonging sound will play while you use this yoyo.

As you run through tricks, you will be surprised by the stability and spin power of Harmonic. The things that usually slow down an organic yoyo slow down Harmonic less. The undercut near the bearing, and the cuts along the slope going out toward the rim, all help to reduce string drag and the effects of the high wall design.

The aethetics of this yoyo are unbelievable. The light dances off the surface similar to Accelerated, but the cup has gentle slopes to remind you that this yoyo is for relaxing and enjoying your day.

Like all motion designs, the yoyo is lighter than average. The 55mm diameter is comfortable and accomodating of any size hand. "

title: Hatsukoi
content: AboutThe Hatsukoi (初恋 — "first love" in Japanese) is JIGUN's first titanium yo-yo, released in 2023 at $250. It features an elegant wing shape with a simulated diamond rhinestone set into the cup — a decorative touch reflective of the romantic name. Available in a raw titanium finish only. Sold out.

title: Hattori
content:
History / About
Modeled after a shuriken and named for ninja Hattori Hanzo. Features actual cut-out holes through the body — rare in yo-yo design — reducing horizontal-play air resistance while spinning. Not fingerspin-friendly; the maker warns long hair can catch in the holes.

title: Hawk
content:
History / About
The Hawk (2017) is a full aluminum monometal from G2's mid-era. It was revisited in 2025 as the Hawk (D Bearing) — the same basic concept updated with a D-size bearing for higher RPMs, showing continued relevance of the design. Full specs for the original Hawk were not available in accessible sources at time of research.

title: Hawk (D Bearing)
content:
History / About
The Hawk (D Bearing) revisits G2's 2017 Hawk model with a key update: a D-size bearing replaces the standard C-size, enabling higher RPMs and a faster, more agile feel. The D-bearing format has been gaining traction in the yoyo community (as seen in the Recess Joyride D, Firecracker D, etc.) and G2 adopted it here for the Hawk platform.

title: Haworthia
content: HistoryHaworthia is part of Hydrangea's expanding lineup of performance yo-yos. Following the botanical naming convention established with Laurus, Haworthia represents another evolution in the brand's design approach.

title: Haymaker
content: AboutThe Haymaker is a full-size monometal aluminum competition yo-yo combining a strong spin profile with wide catch zone dimensions optimized for elegant, forceful tricks. At 56 mm diameter and 45.16 mm width it sits in full-size territory and is positioned as an expert-level daily competition driver. This version is distinct from the earlier Haymaker OG bi-metal and Haymaker X bi-metal, representing the accessible monometal expression of the Haymaker design ethos.

title: Haymaker Beta
content: AboutThe Haymaker Beta was designed as an all-new monometal competition platform inspired by the community revival of monometal competition yo-yos in the early 2020s. Duncan recognized that bi-metal had dominated competition for years but that a new generation of players were returning to monometal for its more forgiving play feel and lower price. The Beta takes the Haymaker X's principles — wide, aggressive, powerful — and reinterprets them in a single-material format. At 48 mm wide it is one of the widest mono-metals in Duncan's lineup, making it unusually forgiving for complex string formations.

title: Haymaker OG
content: AboutThe Haymaker OG is the original Haymaker, unveiled at the 2016 World Yo-Yo Contest as Duncan's entry into the bi-metal competition category. At 52.75 mm it is deliberately undersized — described at release as "the little brother to Tal Mordoch's Orbital" — and its 61.4 g weight combined with stainless steel rim rings creates a fast, maneuverable bi-metal that prioritizes speed and agility over raw spin. It broke new ground for Duncan by demonstrating that the brand could produce a competitive bi-metal at a Worlds-level launch.

title: HaymakerX
content: AboutThe HaymakerX expanded on the Haymaker OG's bi-metal formula with a larger, full-size profile. At 57.21 mm diameter it is one of the bigger throws in Duncan's lineup, and the stainless steel rim rings push mass to the extreme periphery for long, grinding spin times suited to horizontal tricks and extended combos. The additional rim weight makes the HaymakerX noticeably more stable on horizontal throws, which was a specific design goal based on Team Duncan player feedback.

title: HD
content:
From MK1:

"The Mk1 HD is a competition-focused bimetal yoyo, and the signature design of Connor Sheahan. It’s designed for smooth comfortable play, ultra stable, and fast pacing without going out of control."

The first production of 190 units was released on June 21st 2024, at the US National Yoyo Contest.

title: Hearse
content:
About

The Hearse began as an IndieGoGo project to raise funds for a OhYesYo touring vehicle.

title: Heart of Engine
content: AboutThe Heart of Engine is a polycarbonate hybrid with a frosted clear body for grinding and an anodized hub assembly. Stainless steel rims increase rim weight within the body for playability that rivals full metal without excessive weight. Available in Clear/Black Rings and Clear/Rainbow Rings.

title: Heartbeat
content: History / AboutHigh-end 6061 competition model later followed by Heart Attack.

title: Heavy Cream
content: About the Heavy CreamAnnounced in August 2010, the Heavy Cream was Crucial's first all-metal yo-yo — a pivotal step for founder Paul Yath after establishing Crucial's reputation with precision-machined Delrin plastics. Drawing from the popular Milk design, the Heavy Cream translated the same profile into aluminum, featuring smooth spin, beautiful anodization, and laser engraving. It demonstrated that Crucial's design philosophy scaled naturally from plastic to metal and opened the door to the brand's later high-end metal lineup.

title: Helianthus
content: HistoryHelianthus continues Hydrangea's product line with a design focused on performance and value. The model maintains the company's high standards for precision and consistency.

title: HELIX
content: AboutThe HELIX is a budget 6061 monometal from Yoyofriends built for players who want solid performance without the premium price tag. Designed for practice sessions, casual play, and fingerspin tricks including the DNA, it punches above its $29.99 price point with good stability and catch zone geometry.

title: Helvetica
content:
History / About
Helvetica is part of yoyorecreation's Typeface series of monometal 6061 aluminum throws. Spinkult (Sweden) released an exclusive Dark Purple "Spinkult Ed." colorway of the model in 2019, sold through spinkult.com for $58.

title: Cobra
content:
About
The Cobra is the plastic-hubbed counterpart to the aluminum Viper, designed for string tricks and regeneration at a lower price point. Introduced in 1999 as part of the AXYS modular axle system, it features spring-elastic plastic half-shells with an extra-large diameter and lightweight plastic hubs. The AXYS system allows swapping between slider transaxle, fixed wooden, and Speed Explosion ball bearing axle configurations.

title: Coral Snake
content:
About
The Coral Snake was the first yo-yo released as part of Henrys' AXYS modular axle system in 1999, and serves as the premium aluminum counterpart to the plastic Tiger Snake. It features an anodized aluminum body with thick rubber outer rings and air-cushioned power rings for near-indestructible impact resistance. Designed for looping tricks with precision aluminum construction.

title: Lizard
content:
About
The Lizard is the entry-level model in the Henrys lineup, introduced in 1999 as part of the AXYS system. It features an H-profile plastic body with rubber rings on the rims for added stability and spin. Designed for beginners and casual players, the AXYS interchangeable axle system allows upgrades between fixed, transaxle, and ball bearing axle configurations.

title: M1
content:
About
The M1 was Henrys' first full-metal yo-yo, released in 2012 and representing a major departure from the brand's rubber-shell composite designs. Machined from lead-free aluminum alloy in an H-profile, it features a dry oil-free flat Size D bearing and Gecko Pad silicone response. Grooved half-shells accommodate thumb grinds. Fully unresponsive; bind required to return. A MaxGap Tuning Set was available separately to expand the string gap.

title: M2
content:
About
The M2 is a second production run of the M1 design, released in 2014 under a new model name. Lead-free aluminum construction with anodized finish, a grease-free bearing, and an extra-wide string gap designed for optimal unresponsive play. Functionally similar to the M1 with a slightly larger diameter.

title: Python
content:
About
The Python combines the aluminum-hub-with-rubber-rim construction of the Viper family in a shape optimized for 1A string tricks rather than offstring play. Introduced around 2010, it features an aluminum hub with a rubber power ring for enhanced spin and stability. Not compatible with the AXYS axle system. Designed as Henrys' premier unresponsive string trick model.

title: Tiger Snake
content:
About
The Tiger Snake is Henrys' dedicated looping yo-yo, introduced in 1999 as part of the AXYS lineup. It features air-cushioned rubber power rings for impact resistance and a lightweight plastic hub designed for fast, consistent loops. The AXYS modular axle system allows swapping between a standard transaxle for looping or a ball bearing axle for string tricks. An adjustable Quicktrick gap system allows fine-tuning of the string gap width.

title: Viper
content:
History
The Viper is Henrys' flagship yo-yo and one of the earliest purpose-built for offstring (4A) play. Introduced in 1998, it featured aluminum hubs with large removable rubber shells that allow the yo-yo to bounce safely when dropped — a critical design element for offstring freestyle. The original version used a Quicktrick gap adjustment system that rotated the halves to widen or narrow the string gap. A revised version released in summer 1999 added compatibility with the new AXYS modular axle system, allowing swappable fixed, transaxle, and ball bearing axle configurations. The rubber shells were also compatible with the American Playmaxx/ProYo Mongoose.
The AXYS-compatible version features an anodized aluminum hub with removable rubber shells and a Size D Speed Explosion ball bearing. Available in Black, Blue, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Purple, Sky Blue, Glow, and Ice colorways. Still in production as of 2025.

title: Viper Flux
content:
About
The Viper Flux is based on the Viper Neo platform but equipped with integrated Flux Axle hubstacks — spinning plastic caps on each end that can be grabbed or used for Z-axis tricks. The Flux Axle penetrates through the main axle and bearing. Features the same Gecko Pad silicone response as the Viper Neo and is equally suited for offstring and string tricks.

title: Viper Neo
content:
About
The Viper Neo is the modern redesign of the original Viper, introduced around 2010. It features a widened gap, lowered rim profile, and a silicone Gecko Pad response system replacing the original design. The hub uses a shim-adjustable axle system rather than the original AXYS platform. Well suited for laceration-type tricks and offstring play.

title: Viper Neo XL
content:
About
The Viper Neo XL is an extreme variant of the Viper Neo fitted with oversized micro-diabolo rubber shells, creating an unusually large yo-yo at nearly 80mm in diameter. The massive diameter and width were designed for a dramatically different offstring feel with a greatly enhanced catch surface. Discontinued around 2015.

title: Herdsman (Agent 002)
content:
History / About
The Herdsman, subtitled Agent 002 in the G2 product catalog, was released in 2022. It is part of G2's "Agent" internal naming system for certain designs. The design received a major upgrade in the AL7 Herdsman (2025/2026), which uses a 7068 aluminum body with stainless steel rims — transforming it from a monometal to a bimetal for significantly improved performance.

title: Heron
content:
From MK1

"The Heron is a collaboration between Mk1 Yoyos and yoyofriends, combining the design aspects and skills of both companies. Its primary features are a polycarbonate outer ring, softening the overall feel and play, and an aggressive lock-in fingerspin hub. The addition of steel weight rings pushes up the performance, resulting in a stunning all-rounder that you can take on stage or to your local yoyo club."

title: Honeypot
content: History / AboutAccording to Hesh Enterprises, the Honeypot is the second Hesh Enterprises yo-yo and is intended as a reimagining of the Petri, made smaller, wider and with more rounded edges to be less challenging and more comfortable to play. Brendan McGinnis designed it in January 2020 while working as a machinist, slightly modified the design in 2024, and had it machined by One Drop Yo-yos in Eugene, Oregon. It measures 54.5 mm in diameter and 38.6 mm wide and weighs 65 g.

title: Petri
content: History / AboutHesh Enterprises is described on its site as a sole proprietorship of Brendan McGinnis. The Petri was designed and manufactured at Performex Machining Co in San Carlos, CA. The maker's site notes that a blue/green half-swap run was sold at PNWR 2020 shortly before the COVID lockdown, engraved at a business in San Mateo, CA without interior engraving; later post-COVID versions were engraved by Brendan on his own laser engraver and add an interior engraving. YoYoExpert later sold a YoYoExpert Edition (half red, half black). YoYoExpert describes the Petri as a minimalist large-diameter design inspired by the A-RT Poupon and RecRev Reverb, with a narrow profile suited to unresponsive play and an optional responsive setup using a half-spec bearing and shorter axle. Its deep interior groove, called the "schmoove groove" by Doc Pop and the "moat" by McGinnis, keeps string friction low, and the wide flat cup is meant as a canvas for artwork, which inspired the name.

title: Heterogeneity
content:
History / About
The first signature model of mowl ambassador Kenta Kushiro, released in January 2022. The Heterogeneity specializes in smooth feel in play and tenacious spin — the name reflecting the diverse, boundary-pushing nature of Kushiro's style. The 4th anniversary edition released in January 2026 marked four years since the original production run. A titanium version (Heterogeneity Ti: 55.8mm diameter, 42.8mm width, 65.2g) was produced as a special 5th anniversary edition. Artwork on later runs was updated but the core design remains consistent.

title: Heterogeneity Ti
content:
History / About
The titanium version of Kenta Kushiro's signature Heterogeneity, produced as a 5th anniversary special edition. Shares the same core dimensions as the aluminum Heterogeneity (55.8mm diameter, 42.8mm width, 65.2g) translated into full titanium for a different play experience. Available in Raw and Bronze Engraving finishes. A limited production run made it one of the rarer mowl items.

title: Inca
content:
About
The Inca is a bi-metal yo-yo from HICOO featuring an aluminum body with brass rims, giving the finished piece an antique appearance. Designer Black Cement spent weeks researching ancient civilizations before settling on the logo design, which he completed in a single day. Laser engraving covers the catch zone, wall, response groove, and bearing seat. A sandblasted-then-anodized finish creates an effective grinding surface.
Approximately 130 pieces were made in the initial HICOO release. A subsequent collaboration version with Auldey Toys extended the model to a wider audience.

title: JOY
content:
About
The JOY is an aluminum yo-yo from HICOO released in early 2007. Detailed specifications and production figures are undocumented in publicly available sources; the model is known primarily through photographic records.

title: Khan
content:
About
The Khan is an evolution of the Mini 7, sharing the undersized profile while introducing changes aimed at longer sleep time and easier control. It was intended as an exclusive release through a well-known yo-yo store. Specific production details and specifications are undocumented in public sources.

title: LEO
content:
About
The LEO is HICOO’s exploration of the H-shape, taking design inspiration from the Hspin ENVY. It is machined from an undisclosed exotic lightweight alloy — a material identity that designer Black Cement deliberately kept secret at the time of release. The result is an H-shape yo-yo weighing just 47 grams, dramatically lighter than typical aluminum designs of the era. Rubber weight rings are included to push rim weighting even further.
The model was released in at least two colorways: a standard edition and a gold edition.

title: Mini 7
content:
About
The Mini 7 is an undersized aluminum yo-yo with deeply recessed friction-sticker platforms — a design choice that reduces string friction and enables reliable unresponsive play. Flowable silicone is a compatible alternative response. Only 54 pieces were produced, making the Mini 7 one of the rarest HICOO models.

title: Virus
content:
About
The Virus is a collaboration between HICOO and Auldey Toys, one of China’s largest toy manufacturers. A modified butterfly shape with H-profile characteristics and a deep thumb grind ring give the Virus a stable, versatile feel. The partnership gave the model wider distribution than HICOO could achieve independently. Released in blood red and graphite colorways, both featuring painted rim artwork.
Initially responsive out of the box, the Virus becomes fully unresponsive as the bearing breaks in, with a reliable tight bind.

title: West Uranium
content:
About
The West Uranium was HICOO’s debut model and a landmark in yo-yo history — the first high-end aluminum yo-yo ever produced by a Chinese manufacturer. Designed by Shu-Yu Chen (“Black Cement”), it was deliberately priced low so that players in mainland China could experience premium metal construction for the first time. Thick walls provide durability without sacrificing performance; the yo-yo ships with interchangeable O-ring weight rings so players can tune total weight to preference.

title: West Uranium Black
content:
About
The West Uranium Black is an evolved redesign of HICOO’s original model. Thinner walls redistribute mass to increase both diameter and width, producing a longer sleep time than the original West Uranium. Response platforms are deeply recessed in the same fashion as the Mini 7, enabling reliable unresponsive play with a smooth ultra-finish surface.
Two production runs were made: the standard black anodize run, and a “Run 2” Yoyonation exclusive with pinkish-purple color engraving, a scratchless anodize coat, and a wooden presentation case.

title: Hideyoshi
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"The Hideyoshi is a tri-metal design composed of a light 7075 aluminum body, a dense steel outer ring, and an even denser brass inner ring. The balance and weight distribution achieved through the combination of all these different materials gives the Hideyoshi a completely new feel unlike anything on the market. It plays fast, feels light yet really solid at the same time, and has an incredible spin time and stability that you need to feel to believe!

Sengoku is a company based in Nagakute, Japan creating some amazing high performance yo-yos with a cool story. The name Sengoku is an era in Japanese history when the country was in an internal war of samurai clans, finished only when Japan was unified by the Shogun. Keeping this history in mind, Sengoku is naming their yo-yos after the most notable Samurai leaders, and this is the Hideyoshi!

 Toyotomi hideyoshi was a preeminent daimyo, warrior, general, samurai, and politician of the Sengoku period, who is regarded as Japan’s second “great unifier”. He succeeded his former liege lord, Oda Nobunaga, and brought an end to the Sengoku period.

With Hideyoshi considered one of Japan’s Great Unifiers, it only make sense that the yo-yo bearing his name would bring together so many different materials to create one amazing new yo-yo!"

title: Hideyoshi Battle Grade
content:
History / About
A B-grade/outlet run of the trimetal Hideyoshi platform — cosmetic imperfections only, fully playable, not a prototype. Sengoku's own copy for the standard Hideyoshi calls it "the first tri-metal that was ever made," referring to the historical original this Battle Grade run shares its build with.

title: High Wall
content:
History / About
The High Wall PC was released on April 4, 2021 (Yo-Yo Day) as a reimagining of mowl's older aluminum High Wall model. Developed from the concept of "a model that recognizes the original fun of yo-yoing" — many players hesitated to throw expensive full-metal yo-yos outside, so mowl updated the design to polycarbonate so players would actually want to take it out. The new version is approximately 4mm wider in both diameter and width compared to the original, with a large 61.9mm diameter and thick PC rim for powerful spin. The same metal hub system used in the Hybrid and Surveil balances the overall weight. Artwork by KALON DESIGN STUDIO follows a "Life's Journey" theme through a series of sequential pieces. A High Wall SH variant (61.9mm, 44mm wide, 69.5g) was also produced.

title: Hipster Highlife
content: AboutThe yoyo that started Rain City Skills. Founder Jeremy McKay and his wife Andra conceived the brand after visiting One Drop's shop in Eugene, Oregon — a hipster-themed, machined-in-Oregon Canadian brand. Blending influences from the SPYY Punchline and CLYW Chief, the Hipster Highlife debuted in summer 2017 as a competition-capable organic shape with a distinctive LEGO-compatible hub nub. Anodized by Gruntbull. Original four splash colorways: The Foodie, The Beer Snob, The Starving Artist, and Herb. Later re-released in solid colorways with custom engraving. Packaged in a hemp bag inside a mason jar.

title: Hitman
content: About the HitmanThe Hitman is the signature model of 2003 World YoYo Champion Johnnie DelValle, whose winning freestyle using a super-wide gap, shims, and a KonKave bearing revolutionized competitive 1A play. Its undersized slightly-wide Butterfly profile with large aluminum weight rings delivers long spin times and stability. A Hybrid version featuring half O-ring/half starburst response was also produced.

title: HitMan Professional
content: About the HitMan ProfessionalReleased on New Year's Eve 2010, the HitMan Professional modernizes DelValle's signature design with the YoYoJam patent-pending Solid Spin Axle system for enhanced balance and hub stability. It retains the undersized profile and aluminum rim that define the Hitman line while upgrading to silicone pads from the original rubber O-rings.

title: Hitman X
content: About the Hitman XReleased in 2013 to celebrate the 10th anniversary of Johnnie DelValle's 2003 World Championship with the original Hitman, the Hitman X modernizes the iconic design with the Solid Spin Axle system and upgraded silicone O-ring pads. The profile is slightly wider than the original for improved stability. It serves as both a commemorative collector piece and a functional competition throw.

title: G-Yo Flower
content: History / AboutHolgate Toys has made wooden toys in the USA since 1789 according to the Yo-Yo Museum. In 1998 it released the G-Yo line of non-circular yo-yos, three-piece Northern hardwood (hard maple) with fixed axles, each sold display-boxed for an original retail price of $5 US. The shapes are covered by US design patents issued to Richard F. Bly of Kane, PA, all filed 16 January 1998. The Museum notes the G-Yo line is no longer manufactured.Maple yo-yo shaped like a six-petal flower with black logo. Patent: US Design D403,366, issued 29 December 1998.

title: Steiff 1932 Replica Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutHolgate Toys manufactured a replica of a 1932 Steiff wooden yo-yo, branded for Steiff. According to the Yo-Yo Museum it is not an exact replica: it has a yellow background with a swirl of red dots and letters, while the original has a second swirl in black or dark blue. It came in a black embroidered drawstring pouch with a rubber coaster, and was sold with the North American exclusive Steiff bear 'Hansel - The Baby Face Bear' around June 2006. The bear and yo-yo were each limited to 1,500 pieces.

title: Holiday 2 Neo
content: AboutThe Holiday 2 Neo is the second generation of Huatian's Holiday line. The original Holiday debuted in 2014 as a casual everyday throw built to make tricks easy, fun, and relaxed. The Neo refines that idea with a soft, forgiving feel in the hand and in play, a rounded V-shape profile, and a powerful weight distribution that balances performance and comfort — capable of complex, smooth play while still feeling relaxed to throw.

title: EX! 2
content: Modern rebuild of the Axis EX!Released September 5, 2026, EX! 2 is Hollywood Modern Yoyos' first bi-metal yo-yo. The company developed it with Axis founder and original EX! designer James Reed, preserving the earlier model's character while revising its width, hub, and weight distribution for modern competition play.The design moves from the original inner-ring construction to stainless-steel outer rims on a 7075 aluminum body. An undercut beneath the rims concentrates mass near the edge for stability. The entire exterior, including the rims, is bead blasted for lower friction during hand-contact tricks, while the gap interior is polished to reduce string friction.The stock 4.45mm gap can be widened with either or both included 0.075mm stainless-steel shims, producing 4.525mm or 4.60mm configurations. EX! 2 ships with a Size C bearing and Clear Shore 60 Hollywood Pads. Its launch price was $109.99 USD.

title: Honey
content: AboutHoney is a 75/25 cotton and silk blend designed for responsive play in the Throw-Yo Threads Luxury tier. The cotton-dominant formula produces slow velocity and a soft feel with a lasting shelf life — a luxury responsive string for fixed axle and responsive 1A play. Available in Thistle colorway alongside monocolor.

title: Honey Badger
content: HistoryThe Honey Badger was the first yo-yo produced by ZipLine Strings, created in collaboration with Justin Bui of Unspoken Yoyos. Released April 5, 2019, it introduced ZipLine to the hardware side of the yo-yo world, pairing Jeremy Park's string expertise with Unspoken's machining connections. The 6061 aluminum H-shape aimed for a versatile, competition-capable feel at an accessible price point.

title: Honey Badger 23
content: HistoryThe Honey Badger 23 (HB23), released December 15, 2023, was the first solo ZipLine Strings yo-yo, developed without the Unspoken Yoyos collaboration. The design revisited the Honey Badger in 7068 aluminum with a full re-spec: slightly larger diameter (55.97mm), wider catch zone, and thinner profile compared to the 2019 runs. Jeremy Park described it as feeling "lighter, faster, while at the same time being more powerful." Available in Space Grey, Winter Blue, and Metallic Sage at $67. Each came packaged with an Executive Class string, an AlphaLine string, and an HB23 sticker.

title: Honey Badger · 7068 V1
content: HistoryReleased December 6, 2019, the Honey Badger 7068 V1 was the third iteration of the ZipLine × Unspoken Yoyos Honey Badger collaboration. The switch from 6061 to 7068 aluminum — a denser alloy — allowed Jeremy Park and Justin Bui to thin the walls, reduce overall weight slightly, and redistribute mass toward the rims. The result played lighter and faster than the original while generating more spin power. Available in Commander Green, limited batch at $65.

title: Honey Badger · 7068 V2
content: HistoryThe Honey Badger 7068 V2 was a follow-up release continuing the ZipLine Strings and Unspoken Yoyos partnership into 2020. Like its predecessor, it used 7068 aluminum for a rim-heavy weight distribution and lively play character. The V2 represented further refinement of the 7068 platform before ZipLine ultimately developed the standalone Honey Badger 23 redesign in 2023.

title: Honeybee
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: The Honeybee Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"Oh look another yo-yo. This time it's honeybee themed. Includes original crayon drawing by yours truly. Beehive shaped yoyo with honeycomb that act as the response system to make it come back up. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/41RypW. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. Print this one at 100% infill. 

If yours doesn't want to come back up please add a drop of lube to the end of your string or some chapstick rubbed on it."

title: Hop King
content: About the Hop KingThe Hop King was King Yo Star's debut model, designed by Chen Jia Lin and Vong Kin Ian. A defining characteristic of KYS's early design philosophy was width exceeding diameter — the Hop King's 50.35 mm width dwarfs its 53.3 mm diameter, creating an enormous catch zone. An anti-vibration ring is embedded in the edge. Chen Jia Lin won 1st place at CYCC 2011 1A competition with the Hop King. KYS sponsored the BIYO 2011 (Bali International Yo-Yo Open) with this model.

title: Hop King 2 (BIYO 2011 Limited Edition)
content: About the Hop King 2 BIYO Limited EditionProduced exclusively for the Bali International Yo-Yo Open 2011 (BIYO 2011), this black limited-run Hop King variant was described as "dead smooth" and particularly suited to horizontal tricks. King Yo Star was a division sponsor at the event. Limited distribution; exact production numbers unknown.

title: Hornet
content: AboutThe Hornet is Duncan's purpose-built looping yo-yo for intermediate to advanced players, designed with an ideal center-to-rim weight ratio for smooth, consistent two-hand looping. First shown as a prototype at the 2012 World Yo-Yo Contest, the production Hornet ships with two sets of spacers — aluminum spacers for tighter loops and polycarbonate spacers for wider, competition-style loops — allowing players to tune the response to their style. The polycarbonate body provides rigidity and impact resistance, and the Size E bearing is standard for high-performance loopers.

title: Hour 2K13
content: The Hour 2K13 was a refined update to the 2012 Hour, maintaining the 7075 aluminum construction and Time Series identity while introducing subtle dimensional changes to the width, response pocket, and axle system. New bright colorways were added to the lineup.

title: Hourglass
content: This is the Hourglass a 3D-printed yoyo that is 106mm wide.

title: Antipodes
content: The Antipodes is the first signature model of Hadrien Bennaceur, four-time French Champion. Designed for his fast, intricate playing style, it prioritizes speed and maneuverability over mass. A "handtested and tuned" premium variant was released alongside the standard edition, with each unit individually assessed for optimal play performance (minor anodization imperfections retained but mechanical flaws removed). The standard version uses the D-size bearing while the handtested version was upgraded to a curved bearing. Colorways: Blue and Green. Price: $64.99 USD.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size D HSpin (curved bearing on handtested variant)

title: Envy
content: The Envy introduced the H-shaped profile to yo-yo design — machined from a single piece of aluminum to push weight as far to the outer rim as possible without adding secondary ring materials. The H-profile creates two deep catch zones and a pronounced inner rim step, concentrating angular momentum at the outermost edges. This became one of the most influential yo-yo shapes of the 2000s; HSpin's H-profile geometry is a direct precursor to modern competition yo-yo design used industry-wide. Initial production run of 500 units. Available in multiple bead-blasted finish variants.

title: H2O
content: The H2O was conceived at the 2008 European Yoyo Meeting in Vienna by HSpin's Christopher Kayatz and Italian brand Oxygene. The production split the work across countries: HSpin machined and anodized the aluminum halves and performed laser engraving in Switzerland; Oxygene produced the titanium axle system and performed shrink-fitting in Italy. Based on Oxygene's Oxy 4 model. An adjustable gap on a full metal yo-yo was extremely rare at the time. Remaining original 2009 production stock was offered via HSpin's relaunched website in 2024, exhibiting minor vibration characteristic of legacy inventory.

title: ICON
content: The ICON is the second Core Series model and the signature yo-yo of Stefan Benjamin (Magl33to), one of Europe's most respected players. Intentionally simple and round without "crazy gimmicks" — designed to be accessible for all skill levels while performing at a competition level. The bead-blast finish delivers excellent grind performance. Packaged in a sock with a replacement axle, four response pads, and a pair of socks. Price: $58.99 USD.

title: Little Evil
content: The Little Evil is a miniature stainless steel yo-yo derived from the Good and Evil series. Following HSpin's December 2013 closure, production was licensed to YoyoZeekio with HSpin actively participating in the manufacturing process. The use of full stainless steel in a miniature form gives it a deceptively heavy feel for its size. A Little Evil 2 variant followed. Sometimes described as a "Mini HSpin Good and Evil."

title: NVx
content: The NVx was a further experiment in HSpin's H-profile tradition, driving weight further to the rim edges while incorporating an "inverse round" body shape that minimizes string contact during tricks. The gap accepts a finger grip for controlled throws. The NVx introduced HSpin's AR (Axle and Response) 2.0 system, which featured a plastic/steel hybrid bearing (shieldless) — a first for HSpin. Available in Red/Purple and Green/Deep Green colorways. Price: $64.99 USD.

meta.yya_response: HSpin Slim (thin silicone pad + schmoove ring)

title: Phoenix
content: The Phoenix is the signature yo-yo of Polish champion Grzegorz "Plamek" Wojcik (2010 Polish Nationals 1A 2nd place). At 49.98mm diameter it is undersized, purpose-built for the complex string tricks that defined his intricate playing style. The Phoenix marked a significant departure from HSpin's typical D-size bearing, adopting the larger L-size bearing (ILYY/OXY5 specification) — a first for the brand. Includes a replacement axle and individual serial number. Price: $119.99 USD.

title: Pyro
content: The Pyro is one of the most iconic metal yo-yos ever produced and a defining moment in HSpin's history. It was the first yo-yo in history to feature laser engravings on the profile — the outer rim face, not the flat side. The matte anodized fire-red finish with flame engravings became immediately recognizable. Its radical 45.5mm width and 71.7g weight were unlike anything on the market; some described throwing it like "an unopened soda can." The matte surface excelled for grinds. A new axle system with very tight threads produced remarkable smoothness. Multiple production runs followed the December 2005 debut, with 2008 variants featuring updated response grooves. The Pyro's weight and width later prompted HSpin to develop the Pyro Light as a slimmer variant.

title: The Cut
content: The Cut was a radical aesthetic departure from HSpin's characteristic smooth organic curves. The body features a multi-stepped polygonal profile with angular steps cut directly into the sides — described by reviewers as having a "disco ball-like look." Originally released raw/unfinished, with anodized versions following in gold and silver. Called "a new start for HSpin" at its debut. Serial numbered. Standard and limited edition variants were produced, with the limited edition commanding a higher price. The M3 axle system provides solid thread engagement.

title: Doughnut Bite Size
content:
History / About
Doughnut Bite Size is Hubless Yoyo's second model, announced in a company blog post and YouTube video around December 21-22, 2018. It keeps the brand's signature hollow-center look but drops the separate center hub entirely — the two halves screw directly together — and adds a fingerspin cup. Marketed as a playable collection piece rather than a competition throw.Unverified/conflicting at import (Aug 2026): live hublessyoyo.com and its store were unreachable during research. Spec-table diameter/width (57.31mm / 42.48mm) conflict with the brand's own rounded marketing copy ("58mm" / "41mm") — spec-table figures used here. Exact string gap and axle spec not found in any source. Colorway list below (12 names with pricing) is sourced from a June 2019 archive of the company's own store; the current resale listing on en.yoyostorerewind.com shows a different, smaller subset of colorways plus some names (Blue and Orange Swirl, Green Swirl, Chocolate Glaze) not in the 2019 list — colorway offerings likely changed/rotated over the product's run and this list should not be treated as exhaustive.

title: Hummingbird
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"The Hummingbird is machined from 7068 aluminum with stainless steel rings and the design fully takes advantage of the materials. The lightweight body has one of the thinnest, if not the thinnest, aluminum walls in any yo-yo design. Paired with some thick stainless steel rims, We were able to push as much weight as possible to the very edges of the yo-yo for maximum spin power and stability.

The Hummingbird moves fast and nimble just like the bird it's named after. With a comfortable yet performance-driven feel on the string this is an excellent choice for any yo-yo player! "

title: Hummingbird Ⅱ
content:
The following is archived from Yoyofriends:

FInally, the long awaited sequel to Hummingbird is here. Hummingbird is one of the all time classics not only for yoyofriends, but also the yoyo community. Back in 2017, we went all out with a wrapped around ring concept on a lightweight bimetal. It was at that time, fast and powerful. It's performance was a standout among the yoyo community and we made multiple runs afterwards. 

(yoyofriends Hummingbird)

Making it a sequel to a classic is a daunting task. Yoyoing has evolved and changed drastically over the years since 2017, and specs are totally different then what it used to be. We have to walk a fine line of making this yoyo perform well in modern standard, while not stray away too much from the hummingbird feel. 

For our initial design, we first analyzed the iconic center hub that brings both aesthetic and center weight. We think this plays an essential role in the hummingbird's identity. To keep that feel and essence, we decided not to change the cup. The gap width is increased to 4.54mm to accompany the thicker strings. We want to increase the width without changing the profile too much. We decided 48mm width would be a good sweet spot. Not super wide that could drastically change the feel of the yoyo. For the outer ring, we decided to upgrade the original wrapped around ring. Based on Tomoki's second signature, Melzi. The ring slope is now a lot steeper for more extreme outer weight distribution. 

Finally for the weight. We first thought of making it close to the original's weight at around 63g. Then we felt that yoyo would clash with Melzi also at around 63-64g. To provide a more unique experience in our lineup, we increased the weight to around 65g to prioritize power and stability over speed. We gathered all these points and made the first prototype.

(Hummingbird II prototype 1)

The prototype one is made. There are some manufacturing issues. Although the yoyo plays great, the yield is not. It is not up to our utmost high standards.We then compare it to the original hummingbird side by side. No wonder the original Hummingbird is an all time classic. Although the new prototype plays great, we still feel it is missing something to truly warrant an upgrade.The project was temporarily put on hold. During this period, we communicated with many brand partners about material use. It became clear that 7075 aluminum is more widely favored by the market. Offering hardness and strength comparable to 7068. Therefore, we decided to use 7075 starting with Hummingbird.

The project was restarted in mid-2025, and we decided to use 7075 aluminum for the Hummingbird II.

Over time our manufacturer has mastered this material, making it possible to machine the walls almost as thin as 7068.  We felt the weight is at a great spot, but the weight distribution is not extreme enough. So we reduced the curvature of the center hub design, then proceeded to put the weight saved to the aggressive SS ring. Prototype 2 is made shortly after. 

(Hummingbird II prototype 2)

The yoyo finally hit the sweets pot. With the performance increase fully warrant an upgrade while not straying too far from the original. After multiple player's testing, we greenlit this design to production. 

(production Hummingbird II)

For the logo and naming, we decided to keep it simple. We still think highly of the original hummingbird and we want to keep the same elegance and pay homage to it.

title: Hummingbird Brass / Copper Ring
content: AboutA special bimetal variant of the classic Hummingbird, this version adds brass or copper rings to the outer rim for enhanced weight distribution and a premium aesthetic. Two versions were released: blackish green with brass rings (65g) and purple with copper rings (66.7g), each delivering a distinctive character while preserving the Hummingbird's legendary performance.

title: All Pro
content:
About
The All Pro is the primary mold of Humphrey Corporation and the shape collectors refer to as "the Humphrey style." Introduced when Humphrey entered the yo-yo market in 1975, it outlasted the company's two other molds — the Classic and the Monarch — to become the sole production shape in the brand's later years.
As an advertising specialty product, the All Pro was never sold at retail. Each unit was manufactured with a client's corporate logo, slogan, or artwork imprinted directly on the yo-yo body. Humphrey supplied thousands of distinct branded variants to corporations, small businesses, and organizations as promotional giveaways. The company produced over one million yo-yos per year at its peak and over 1,000 distinct branded variants annually.
The All Pro is a fixed-axle plastic looping yo-yo with a classic imperial profile, consistent with the advertising yo-yo category of its era. Collectors commonly encounter Humphrey All Pro yo-yos branded for a wide range of clients — oil companies, fast food chains, sports teams, and local businesses — making each branded edition a distinct collectible in its own right despite sharing the same underlying mold.

title: Classic
content:
About
The Classic was one of three mold shapes Humphrey Corporation offered when the company entered the yo-yo market in 1975. Like all Humphrey yo-yos, it was produced as an advertising specialty item — custom-imprinted with client branding and sold exclusively through distributors to businesses and organizations as promotional giveaways, never at retail.
The Classic was discontinued before the All Pro, which became the company's primary and eventually sole production mold. Specific dimensions, colorways, and technical specifications have not been documented in any public source.

title: Monarch
content:
About
The Monarch was Humphrey Corporation's butterfly-shaped yo-yo, one of three molds offered when the company launched its yo-yo line in 1975. Its wider catch zone distinguished it from the imperial-profile All Pro and Classic molds, making it nominally better suited to string tricks — though as an advertising specialty toy it was produced for promotional rather than performance purposes.
Like all Humphrey yo-yos, the Monarch was sold exclusively through distributors as a custom-imprinted corporate giveaway, never at retail. It was discontinued before the All Pro, which became the company's flagship and surviving mold. Specific technical specifications have not been documented in any public source.

title: Hybrid
content:
History / About
The Hybrid uses a polycarbonate body with Delrin (POM) rims — an unusual material combination that gives it a uniquely soft and comfortable feel distinct from standard plastic/metal hybrids. The POM rims provide a smooth, quiet play experience while still contributing rim weighting for stability. A Kenta Edition variant was produced in collaboration with mowl ambassador Kenta Kushiro. The Hybrid later served as a technical foundation for the Protostar Hybrid Ti collaboration with YoYoFactory.

title: Hybrid 5050
content: A hybrid aluminum/POM version of the 5050.

title: Hybrid Fulvia (Anodized)
content:
History / About
A hybrid material version of the classic Fulvia design in an anodized finish. Part of Luftverk’s expansion from purely titanium into mixed-material and aluminum territory during 2023–2024. Currently available at $55 on luftverk.com. Full material specifications not publicly documented.

title: Hybrid Hitman
content: About the Hybrid HitmanThe Hybrid Hitman retains the Hitman's aircraft-aluminum weight rings and proven profile but replaces the double O-ring system with a half-starburst/half-O-ring hybrid response, making the yo-yo less aggressive in its return. It bridges beginner-friendly responsiveness with competitive-level sleep times.

title: Hydrogen Crash
content: Based on the H-profile with a wide bi-metal design, the Hydrogen Crash delivers "astonishingly aggressive long sleep" at only 63g through its extended stainless steel rims. A paradoxical blend of lightweight operation with heavyweight-like power and stability. Price: $109.99.

title: Hyper Freehand
content:
The Hyper Freehands were made in the US by Duncan and licensed to Bandai for sale in Japan. 500 sold in the US in 2004, these were only available via Duncan's website. Differences between the Freehand 1 and the Hyper Freehand were: raised lip around the friction sticker and ultrasonically bonded caps. They were packaged in a clear clam shell and included a clear counterweight dice or matching clear dice for the translucent colors.

It is an official addition to the Hyper Yo-Yo line.

Shared by Steve Brown on the YoYoExpert forums

title: Hyper Russell Professional
content: History / AboutReleased in December 1998 through Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line in Japan, the Hyper Russell Professional was a tie-in with the anime series Chousoku Spinner (Super Yo-Yo). Made in Korea by Russell, it used translucent colored polycarbonate plastic — distinguishing it visually from the opaque Super — and was the heavier of the two Hyper Russell models at approximately 53 grams. It appeared in anime flashbacks depicting the character "Nakamura Meijin's" past. Packaged in a Japanese bubble card, complete examples are now rare in the collector market.

title: Hyper Russell Super
content: History / AboutReleased in 1998–1999 as part of Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line in Japan, the Hyper Russell Super was the lighter companion to the Hyper Russell Professional. Where the Professional used translucent polycarbonate plastic, the Super used opaque colored plastic and was approximately 9 grams lighter. Both models were manufactured in Korea by Russell and distributed by Bandai as tie-ins with the Chousoku Spinner anime. The Super came in multiple color options aligned with the anime's character colorways.

title: Hypercut
content: AboutThe Hypercut is Yoyofriends' first hybrid throw — a polycarbonate body paired with stainless steel rings — released as the 9th Anniversary model. Derived from the bimetal Papercut, it expands the body width, increases stainless steel ring weight, and raises overall weight for more powerful play. The transparent PC construction makes the internal stainless rings visible.

title: Hypernova (Aluminum)
content:
History / About
The Hypernova is the reissue of Tyler Severance's legendary pro model — originally developed through three generations at YoYoFactory before Recess brought it home. It combines elements of H, W, V, and Organic shape profiles with even weight distribution, resulting in a yo-yo that works for nearly every style of play. It won 3 US National Titles in Tyler's hands, multiple worldwide international titles, and multiple top-3 placements at the World Yo-Yo Contest — while simultaneously becoming a favorite of trick innovators and content creators because of its versatility. Tyler described it as one of the first throws capable of genuinely competing in 1A, 3A, and 5A without compromise. The aluminum Hypernova and its machined polycarbonate version (PC Hypernova) are both offered by Recess.

title: Hypocrisy Max
content: AboutThe Hypocrisy Max is a smaller-size bi-metal, described as "different from popular competitive size yo-yos." The compact profile provides a whole new experience compared to full-size competition models. Available in Silver, Gold, and Green.

title: Hypocrisy +
content: AboutThe Hypocrisy + is the bi-metal version of AceYo's Hypocrisy series, adding stainless steel rings to the V-shape competition-ready design.

title: Hypocrisy SE
content: AboutThe Hypocrisy SE features a modified V-shape with several cuts near the rim for comfortable profile in hand and fast play on string. Glossy cup with soft blast catch zone for grinds. Available in Black/Gold/Silver and Red/Yellow/Silver.

title: I – Aluminum
content:
From YoyoExpert:

"I ALUMINUM is built for those quiet sessions. The moments when the world pauses and it is just you, the string, and the rhythm of your throw.

Crafted in the exact same silhouette as its titanium counterpart, I ALUMINUM embraces the softer side of performance. The smooth, mild feel of aluminum offers a gentle response in hand, inviting long practice sessions and effortless flow. Tricks feel natural. Movement feels unforced. Your thoughts begin to clear as the spin settles into a calm, steady rhythm.

The iconic hub colorway and groove design pay tribute to the legendary BSP lineage, now reimagined with a modern cap structure. The flat rim profile, refined over generations, delivers clean spin power and stability within a lightweight 62 gram body. It is timeless design meeting present day precision.

A beautiful finish of vintage coating, the I ALUMINUM carries a subtle luxury that feels as good as it looks."

title: I – Titanium
content:
From YoyoExpert:

"I TITANIUM is for the challenger within.

Sharing the exact same shape as I ALUMINUM, this titanium edition transforms the experience through material alone. The higher density and rigid feel of titanium create a powerful, commanding presence on the string. Every throw feels intentional. Every landed trick carries weight and satisfaction.

To preserve balance and playability, At Design Lab engineered a hollow hub structure, maintaining the iconic BSP-inspired hub design while optimizing weight distribution. The result is a uniquely pleasant float paired with unmistakable titanium solidity.

The perfected flat rim shape maximizes spin efficiency and stability, all within a refined 62 gram profile. It is precise. Focused. Uncompromising.

The I TITANIUM stands as both a performance instrument and a collector’s statement."

title: Ibex
content:
From ZGRT:

"Ibex are goats that live in the peaks of mountains close to the clouds and can climb practically anything with the aid of their special split hooves.

Ibex have been seen defying gravity climbing massive dam walls in some parts of Europe, Asia and North Eastern Africa. They are able to make 1.8 meters or 6 feet jumps without a running start!

We got the inspiration from such amazing animals to design our second throw: the Ibex.

This is a V-O shape full-size mono-metal throw made out of aluminum 7068 with thin walls, good weight distribution with enough rim weight to provide long spin time and stability. With the Ibex you will be capable to perform as many tricks as you want due to its multiple features and blast finish surface."

title: Ice Cream
content:
About
Ice Cream is a remake of the first prototype created by Cold Metal, recreating one of the early milestones in Russian yoyo history. Originally released as a very limited drop in 2007 (contemporary accounts describe the original run as prototype-stage, with uncertain wider release status), SPUTNIK brought it into a modern form with the approval of the original creators. The original colorways and overall character are preserved, with the shape refined for modern comfort — retaining the dense feel and distinctive sound of late-2000s yoyos while adding a modern response system.

title: Ieyasu
content:
From Rewind Worldwide:

"Sengoku's first titanium model with all-out effort.

Sengoku, which has been tackling various new challenges such as the use of A7068, tri-metal designs, and even perforated metal, has finally released their first high-end titanium model.It adopts an H-profile shape with a polygonal, finely graded tilt angle. It has a modest diameter that fits nicely in the hand, but has tremendous horsepower. During play, you can always catch the center of the yoyo, and even when you are playing with a lot of momentum, you can control the yoyo firmly without losing sight of it.Both the bearings and string are specially made forÂ the Ieyasu. The high-precision V-shaped bearing keeps the string in aÂ centered position and keeps it in control during play. The thicker string that comes with the yo-yo is a special string handmade by a team member. The package is also handmade by the owner. There are no future plans for the string and package, making them rather collectible.This Ieyasu is also a one-time special production, with no plans for any future runs.This is the first titanium model, and is a high-end model that Sengoku has poured a lot of effort into producing."

title: Caffeine
content: About the CaffeineThe Caffeine was an early ilinx Toys yo-yo and predates the 2022 Melatonin, which the maker introduced as its second yo-yo. Contemporary community discussion describes the Caffeine as a stable, limited direct-sale model available through ilinx.Hollywood Modern Yoyos is the successor identity to ilinx Toys. Surviving sources do not provide dependable dimensions, weight, construction material, response specifications, colorways, or original price, so those details remain unrecorded.

title: Drop
content:
About the Drop
The Drop was ilinx Toys' (Hollywood Modern Yoyos') first 3D-printed yoyo, released in 2022. At launch it was widely recognized in the yoyo community as the best-performing 3D-printed yoyo available, praised for a wide catch zone designed to excel at horizontals, neck tricks, and body tricks. The design prioritized a fingerspin-friendly hub with a flat surface surrounded by a talon-grind-optimized valley.
The original Drop was printed in PLA plastic with a plastic bearing seat. While performance was strong, the PLA formulation was prone to chipping on concrete impacts and the plastic bearing seat could warp under stress—issues Ross Levine addressed directly in the successor model, the Drop 2 3D. The Drop was sold exclusively through the ilinx / Hollywood Modern Yoyos online store and served as proof of concept for the brand's 3D-printing line.

title: Drop 2 3D
content:
About the Drop 2 3D
Released in 2024, the Drop 2 3D is the improved second generation of ilinx Toys' (Hollywood Modern Yoyos') 3D-printed yoyo line. Ross Levine addressed every structural weakness of the original 2022 Drop: the plastic is now PETG—significantly stronger than PLA, capable of surviving multiple concrete impacts without chipping or peeling—and the bearing seat is now precision-machined stainless steel rather than plastic, eliminating the warping problems found on the original.
Performance was also pushed further. The Drop 2 stretches to 60mm width, a first for the Hollywood Modern Yoyos lineup, with a catch zone engineered specifically for horizontals, neck tricks, and body tricks that demand space and stability. The hub retains the flat fingerspin surface, talon grind valley, and central pull-start dimple from the original. The Drop 2 3D is available through the modernyoyos.com store at $30.00 USD in Pink, Teal, and Blue colorways. Hollywood response pads are included.

title: The Ruler
content:
About The Ruler
The Ruler is Hollywood Modern Yoyos' / ilinx's most experimental release to date, debuted at US Nationals 2025. At twelve inches (one foot) in width with a 3.52-inch diameter, it is widely recognized as the widest yoyo ever made and stretches the definition of what a yoyo can be. The unusual proportions produce a slow, powerful spin driven by extreme rotational inertia from the rim mass distribution.
Despite its scale, The Ruler is a functional unresponsive yoyo. It was refined through multiple prototypes to reduce vibration, and the final version features upgraded metal bearing seats drawn from the Drop 2 3D engineering work. Ross Levine introduced it publicly at US Nationals 2025 as a statement piece and conversation starter about the outer boundaries of yoyo design. It is sold through the modernyoyos.com store at $50.00 USD.

title: Imagine Breaker
content: History / AboutCurrent physical redesign of the Imagine Breaker platform, using a wide aluminum competition profile.

title: Immersive
content: AboutThe Immersive is JT's ultra-compact offstring released in 2025, available in both POM and polycarbonate versions. At under 60mm diameter, it is markedly smaller than typical offstring models, yet its wide 59.8mm width provides a secure catch zone. JT describes it as usable for 1A string trick practice and entry-level 5A as well as 4A. The POM version weighs 73.6g; the PC version is approximately the same dimensions at $59.99.

title: Imperial
content: AboutThe Imperial is the world's best-selling yo-yo and the model that defined American yo-yo culture for generations. Introduced in 1954 to replace Duncan's wartime wooden models, it was molded in Tenite plastic to replicate the dimensions of the classic wooden Model 77 in continuous production since 1929. Its narrow string gap and starburst response produce the snappy, reliable return loops that made it the standard yo-yo for beginners and seasoned loopers alike. The fleur-de-lis gold stamping on the face became an iconic visual identity for the brand. After Duncan's 1965 bankruptcy and Flambeau's acquisition in 1968, the Imperial mold was preserved and continues in production today, essentially unchanged.

title: Candy Club Yummy Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutA clear plastic yo-yo with each half filled with Willy Wonka's candy-coated Tart N Tiny candy, dispensed by using a coin to unscrew a plug in either half. The package notes the yo-yo must be balanced, with equal candy on each side. Item No. 7154, dated 1995 in the Yo-Yo Museum catalog. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: E-Z Go Ribbon Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutImperial's E-Z Go Ribbon Yo-Yo has plastic body halves with a cloth ribbon pegged to the axle and is essentially identical to the Duncan Yoffy, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, which also lists a similar Ribbon Spinnin' YoYo by an unknown maker. The yo-yo is imprinted U.S. Pat. No. 4290224, was made in Korea for Imperial Toy Corporation of Los Angeles, and is dated 1987 in the museum catalog (mid to late 1980s).

title: Hawaiian Punch
content: History / AboutA plastic butterfly yo-yo with a sticker of Punchy, the Hawaiian Punch mascot, on each side. The Yo-Yo Museum notes this butterfly shape was very popular during the late 1990s yo-yo boom despite its novelty status and average performance. Dated 1997 in the museum catalog; original retail price $3 US. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: Hi-Tech Professional Glo-Yo
content: History / AboutThe Imperial Toy Corporation Hi-Tech Professional Glo-Yo (No. 7249), circa 1985-1987, is a plastic, glow-in-the-dark, tournament-shaped yo-yo with a cotton string, fixed axle and starburst response, made in Korea. The Yo-Yo Museum says the glow version is hard to find today while the non-glow version of the same model is far more common. Original retail price was $1.50 USD. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: Hot Wheels All Pro Yo-Yo
content: History / AboutThe Imperial Toy Corporation Hot Wheels All Pro Yo-Yo (No. 7012), circa 1990, is a plastic modified-shape yo-yo designed to look like a wheel from a Hot Wheels toy car. The Yo-Yo Museum records a cotton string, fixed axle and starburst response, made in China, with an original retail price of $2 USD. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: Mountain Dew Bottle Cap
content: History / AboutThe outer perimeter of each yo-yo half is shaped like a pop bottle cap, with a Mountain Dew logo sticker applied to each side. The Yo-Yo Museum notes Imperial also made a version for Pepsi. Dated 1992 in the museum catalog; original retail price $2 US. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: Sonic Space
content: History / AboutThe Sonic Space yo-yo combined eight different electronic sounds with several multicolored LED lights, all activated when the player threw a sleeper. The Yo-Yo Museum records a metal axle and starburst response, dated 1995, and notes that by the mid to late 1990s Imperial yo-yos were considered novelty items. Original retail price was $3 US. Imperial Toy Corporation was founded in April 1969 by Fred Kort, and its yo-yos often carry a detailed imperial crown mark.

title: Impertinent
content:
Interesting in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: The Impertinent Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a print in place one piece yo-yo, just add string. It is styled after classic imperial shapes but has a chunk bit out of it at the bottom to allow for easy printing. It has 6 holes hidden in the gap create drag for response. 

Recommended to print at very low layer height (0.05 to 0.07) and 100% infill. Shown here printed in Prusament Linden Wood. "

title: In Decision
content: The In Decision completed Werrd's Decision trilogy of aluminum/Delrin hybrid designs. A more angular body than the Bad Decision at 59.7mm × 46.42mm improved performance on horizontal and off-axis tricks. The slightly larger gap also aided slack and whip techniques.

title: Inevitable
content: AboutThe Inevitable is the signature of Arata Imai, built on a curved body with flared stainless steel rims and spec'd with the NSK Double Straight (DS) angular-contact bearing rather than the standard Size C ball bearing found on most YYR models. The DS bearing's angular contact geometry reduces string friction and can improve spin efficiency at high-angle string formations. At 56mm × 43mm and 65.5g, it sits close to the Autoscopy in the modern YYR lineup.

title: Infiltrate
content:
History / About
The Infiltrate is the signature model of mowl ambassador Eric Tran-Ton, a Chicago-based professional player known for long, intricate combos with an artistic, efficient flow (finalist at both 1A and 3A World Championships). The Infiltrate was designed with Eric's preference for rounded edges in mind — rather than sharp modern edges, the soft contours allow players to maneuver through intricate string formations with ease and minimize catching the string during long combos. Despite coming in at 67 grams, the weight distribution makes it float through tricks. The first prototype was in 6061 aluminum, but at Eric's request the material was changed to 7075 to add the stability he needed for long combos. A titanium version (Infiltrate Ti) was released in 2025.

title: Infiltrate Ti
content:
History / About
The titanium edition of Eric Tran-Ton's signature Infiltrate model, released in 2025. This refined design maintains the lightweight feel of the aluminum monometal while expanding the width by approximately 2mm to cater to the demands of modern yo-yo players — the wider catch zone makes landing even the most challenging tricks easier. Available in a striking Polished Purple finish with a radiant polished face and blast-finished side, balancing brilliance with understated elegance. Designed for players who push the limits of long intricate combo play.

title: Yomega Saber RB II Infinite Illusions Exclusive
content:
History / About
Yomega produced this limited edition of the Saber RB II exclusively for Infinite Illusions, with a total run of just 240 units — 80 each in clear, semi-clear red, and semi-clear neon green. The Saber RB II is an auto-return ball-bearing yo-yo with the distinctive Saber Wing shape. The Infinite Illusions exclusive run was sold entirely through Yoyoguy.com and is now a rare collector's item.

title: Ink
content: AboutInk is a 50/50 blend of rayon and trilobal polyester in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Slick disposition, lethal velocity, and immortal shelf life make it the blend for players who want zero friction and maximum speed. The broadest colorway selection of any Performance string: Ceruse, Vitriol, Fuchsine, Malachite, Atramentum, Orchil, Gamboge, and Realgar alongside monocolor.

title: insomnia 7068
content:
About
The insomnia 7068 is the debut release from "alternatives," seventeen months in the making with direct input from National, Asia, and World Champions. The body uses 7068 aluminium — a stronger alloy than the more common 6061 — paired with stainless steel rims for maximum rim weight and spin time. The dual finish combines an inner blast to reduce friction with a glossy outer ring for aesthetic contrast. Debuted at WYYC 2024. Released in three colourways: Black, Green, and Silver, each priced at $150.

title: Inspire
content: About the InspireThe Inspire is John Narum's dedicated 1A signature model, featuring an inverse-round body shape that reduces string contact at lower spin speeds. The POM body with aluminum rim delivers a smooth, quiet feel characteristic of Delrin-composite construction. A championship edition was produced for the 2012 US Nationals.

title: Insulation Lithium
content: AboutThe Insulation Lithium (also listed as "Insulation MAX" on the LEP store) is a hybrid yo-yo with a 7075 aluminum body and patented polycarbonate outer rims — a budget alternative to the stainless-steel-rimmed Lithium W. The PC rim construction uses a proprietary joining method. Available in Silver.

title: Intercut
content:
About
The Intercut is the tri-material version of the Papercut, with upgraded material and width. A polycarbonate ring sits between the aluminum and stainless steel, adding fun and flow on top of strong performance.

title: InTernal Turmoil
content:
History
The InTernal Turmoil (IT) was the fourth release in the Dif Series and Dave "Dazzling Dave" Schulte's second signature model. Many players who owned multiple Dif-e-Yo throws considered it the smoothest the company ever produced. The deep 0.045" pad pockets accepted both standard .555-size Dif Pads (stacked .030 + .015) and flowable silicone — giving players a response option that was rare in a branded metal yo-yo at the time.
The aesthetic detail that set the IT apart was the contrast between its satin-finished catch zone and polished raw internal crossbones-patterned side panels. Available in anodized green and purple for the standard release.
A 2008 US Nationals special edition was also produced: colored body and laser printing with a black weight ring, sold at $134.99.

meta.yya_response: Dif Pads (.030 + .015, .555 ID) — pockets accept flowable silicone

title: Intro
content:
From One Drop:

"A long long time ago (December 2008), in a yo-yo community not so far away, we released our 3rd yo-yo and it was called the M1.  M1 meant “metal for everyone”. At that time, high-end yo-yos were rare, runs were small, prices were high and almost none of it was made in China.

As the new kids on the block, we looked at this situation of scarcity, and decided we would make a high-end yo-yo that was affordable and available.  Solid colors retailed for $60, many people were able to obtain their first metal yo-yo, and One Drop Yo-Yos had landed. There was some controversy because we had shaken up the market, but from that point forward, “budget metal” became a standard offering in the industry and eventually this lead to other brands moving their production overseas in pursuit of lower and lower prices and higher and higher availability.

Now, 12 years later, we are the only company of volume producing in North America.  Furthermore, we have always produced our yo-yos in our factory. This is our jam, we have stuck to our convictions, and we are a unique offering.  Thank you to everyone who supports us - it’s because of you that we are still here. It’s not easy competing against China.

We know we will never be able to get our price as low as our outsourcing competitors, but we are always striving to get close while maintaining the high quality that we are well known for. In the spirit of the M1, the Intro is our next “Metal for Everyone” but I think the phrase needs updating:  “Made in Eugene, Oregon, USA Metal for Everyone” is more accurate. Starting at $44 for solid colors, we want to have the most affordable model possible to INTROduce people to our brand and quality. Obviously, our current supporters might love it as well (especially those who first discovered us through the M1).    It’s great value for everyone with a little bit of nostalgia thrown in.  

Taking inspiration from the M1, the diameter nudges toward the pocket friendly side of things at 54mm.  Of course that is 4mm bigger than the M1, but still on the smaller side of things by today’s standards. The curves are simple and clean and the flat hub has two circles of ornamentation paying homage to the round nut axle system that most M1s had.  It’s a solid performer, pocket and wallet friendly, and made in the USA."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Balrog
content: AboutThe Balrog is Brazilian Yoyo's sole bimetal throw, released January 2016. A 6061 aluminum body is fitted with stainless steel weight rings on the outer rims for enhanced stability and spin time over the brand's all-aluminum lineup. At 58mm diameter and 67g, it is engineered for competition and daily unresponsive 1A play. A special Titi Freak Edition was produced in collaboration with the Brazilian street artist and yo-yo player Titi Freak (formerly of Duncan Crew Brazil), featuring a black body with Titi Freak engraving and artwork; this variant was pre-released at the Brazil Nationals Spring 2016 before wider retail distribution.

title: BRZ
content: AboutThe BRZ (a nod to Brazil) is Brazilian Yoyo's undersized competition model at 54mm diameter, released in 2014. Its H-shaped profile delivers strong stable spin in a more compact package than the Hover. Victor Sachelli won 1st place at the Brazil Nationals 1A division in 2014 using a BRZ. Available in splash-anodized colorways.

title: FNX
content: AboutThe FNX is Ioiô Fênix's flagship bearing plastic, originally released as the "butterfly" before being updated in 2010 with "FNX" branding, an engraved edge, a holographic sidecap, and a approximately 2mm wider gap. The hybrid response system — silicone O-ring on one side and starburst on the other — is similar to mid-2000s YoYoJam configurations. At 59mm diameter and 64g, it delivers satisfying performance for intermediate players. A special Titi Freak artist-edition was produced in collaboration with the Brazilian street artist and yo-yo player, featuring black body panels with Titi Freak artwork on the caps. Available in black, red, white, and yellow.

meta.yya_response: Hybrid: silicone O-ring (one side) + starburst (other side)

title: Hover
content: AboutThe Hover is the flagship model of the Brazilian Yoyo lineup and has held that position since its 2013 release. Its H-shaped profile allows the yo-yo to "float" between strings for technical 1A and 3A play. Brazilian National Champion Daniel Borges used the Hover to win the 1A title; Hideki Yassuda used it to win 3A — making it one of few throws to claim national titles in multiple play styles simultaneously. The first production run featured a glossy finish; the second run added a blasted surface for grinding capability. Available in a wide range of splash-anodized colorways.

title: Luka
content: AboutThe Luka is Ioiô Fênix's entry-level fixed-axle yo-yo and one of the brand's longest-running products. Its slimline profile differs from traditional bulge-face fixed-axle shapes, and multiple side-cap print designs — including the Luka Pitbull branded edition — have been produced over the years. The Luka has been a consistent bestseller in the Brazilian school yo-yo campaign market and is widely distributed through Brazilian toy retailers.

title: Mira
content: AboutThe Mira is Ioiô Fênix's mid-tier bearing yo-yo, designed by Marcio Alves and announced at the Fig Festival in Valinhos, SP in January 2010. Positioned for mass-market accessibility under R$20 at launch, the Mira targeted Brazil's school yo-yo campaigns as an affordable entry into bearing-based play. Its A-size concave bearing (dry, without shielding, US-sourced at launch) delivers consistent unresponsive spin. One silicone O-ring on one side provides smooth response; a second ring can be added to increase responsiveness. A "Novo Mira" (New Mira) update was released in subsequent years. Available in semi-translucent colorways.

meta.yya_response: Single silicone O-ring (one side); second ring optional for more response

title: Prime
content: AboutThe Prime is the first high-performance aluminum throw from Ioiô Fênix, initially developed as a Fênix-branded prototype around 2010 before being relaunched as part of the Brazilian Yoyo lineup for the 2012 division debut. The Prime's hubstacks (lateral side bearings) enable horizontal plane-change tricks and ripcord spin play not possible on conventional yo-yos. A "Prime by Marechal" signature edition was also produced. The Prime laid the groundwork for the Brazilian Yoyo premium aluminum catalog that followed.

title: Psy
content: AboutThe Psy was one of three aluminum competition yo-yos released simultaneously to mark the launch of the Brazilian Yoyo division in 2012, alongside the Prime and the Veloz. A full-performance machined aluminum throw aimed at the competition market. Exact specifications have not been publicly documented in available sources.

title: Sênior
content: AboutThe Sênior is Ioiô Fênix's professional fixed-axle yo-yo and the brand's core mid-tier product. Its lightweight ABS body and starburst response system make it ideal for classic responsive tricks including the sleeper, walking the dog, and around the world. Sold through major Brazilian retail chains including Casas Bahia and Ponto Frio, the Sênior is available in several sub-variants with different thematic designs: the Sênior Kraken (yellow and blue colorways) and Sênior Lhama (blue and green colorways), all sharing the same core specs. A reliable and widely distributed entry-level professional yo-yo in the Brazilian market.

title: Veloz
content: AboutThe Veloz ("Fast" in Portuguese) is one of Brazilian Yoyo's three inaugural 2012 aluminum releases. Its wing (butterfly) profile is paired with lateral side bearings that enable changing the plane of the axis mid-trick — allowing horizontal play and ripcord spin maneuvers similar to the Prime. A concave bearing and silicone pads suit unresponsive competition-level play. A "Veloz by Marechal" signature variant was also produced. Exact dimensional specs have not been publicly documented.

title: Irony JP
content: The Irony JP ("JP" for Japan) was a 7075 refinement of the original Irony, developed with input from Japanese freestyle players. The nubs from the original Irony were removed and the sides flattened, redistributing weight for improved balance and power output. The result was shinier than the later 2K13 version. Available in Red, Silver, Gold, and Acidwash (Green/Silver) colorways. $119.99 USD. This "Old Version" was followed by the Irony JP 2K13 in 2013.

title: Irony JP 2K13
content: The Irony JP 2K13 refined the Irony JP platform for elite Japanese freestyle demands. Key changes included a concave finger-spin cup, a soda-blast finish suited to grinding, and a Dif-E-Yo KonKave bearing. The negative-cut Irony shape was retained. A special variant for Carlos Braun (EYYC 2014 1A champion) weighed 65.6g with a fine polished finish in orange. Ships with Kitty String Type 6.

title: Irony JPX
content: The Irony JPX continued the refinement of the Irony JP for Japanese competition freestyle demands. Polished rims, a Dif-E-Yo KonKave bearing, and a concave finger-spin cup were carried over from the 2K13 version. Team rider Yoku Kato was featured in a 2015 promotion video; Brandon Vu appeared in the December 2014 teaser. The negative-cut Irony shape remained the foundation.

title: Isthmus
content:
TRT's second release. The Isthmus is available in the following colorways:

[Florida] Bay Fade

Beach Sand

The Isthmus is full-sized, yet slimline and pocket-friendly!

title: Itsy Bitsy YoYo
content: The Itsy Bitsy YoYo is an extremely small three-piece wooden souvenir yo-yo produced by Wallace Toy Company in Wallace, Idaho. Released in 1991, it was sold as a novelty and tourist item, with variants produced for different U.S. states. The yo-yo is unfinished natural wood or dark brown stained, and is roughly comparable in size to a YoYoFactory Flea — among the smallest wooden yo-yos commercially produced. It uses a fixed axle with a thin string pegged directly to the axle.

title: Iwakurarator
content: History / AboutDistinct retail model documented by Rewind, separate from Iwakura-branded color editions of other models.

title: IX
content: History / AboutThe original large, ultra-wide IX preceded the machined-PC Stellar IX and later Ghost IX.

title: Ixion
content:
History / About
The Ixion is GWAY Throws’ sixth release and first bimetal design.
