Combining a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rims, the construction concentrates mass at the outer edge for maximum spin stability and power. The move to bimetal marked a significant step in GWAY’s product line, targeting competition-level performance for the first time.

title: iYoYo 2
content: AboutFull aluminum aimed at beginners via a narrow bearing, shipping with a centering bearing upgrade for unresponsive conversion. Step round profile with a notable fingerspin cup. Responsive from the factory, fully convertible for advanced play without buying a new yo-yo.ColorwaysSplash (Blue/Yellow/Pink), Confetti, German Edition, Galaxy, Splash (Black/Blue), Splash (Black/Light Green).

title: iYoYo 2 Pro
content: AboutBimetal version of the iYoYo 2, adding 7075 aluminum rims to the 6061 body for increased stability as spin decreases. The heavier alloy rim weighting prevents wobble during complex trick sequences. Step round profile with a DIF-licensed KonKave bearing for smooth, centered string play.ColorwaysGreen, Galaxy.

title: AiR DiVE
content: AboutiYoYo's first offstring model. Compact 70mm diameter provides excellent maneuverability compared to standard 75–80mm competitors. Thick rim design minimizes bounce on missed tricks. Designed in collaboration with Ze'ev Yehuda. Predecessor to the iCEBREAKER and AiR DiVE lineage.ColorwaysLight Blue, White, Red, Blue, Yellow.

title: ANTARCTiCA
content: AboutTitanium + stainless steel (TiSS) bimetal based on the second-generation iCEBERG profile (46mm wide). "Hard control feel" with "lightness when force is applied" — handles like a monometal at will but with bimetal spin extension when needed. Prototype first shown December 2022; production release 2023.ColorwaysBlue, Silver.

title: BARBARiAN
content: AboutFirst collaboration between iYoYo and YoYoTricks.com (Throwback Skill Toys). Dense 7075 aluminum construction described as providing "a feeling of solidity." Very low first-contact angle makes it naturally suited for horizontal tricks. Easily accessible fingerspin cup. Multiple named edition colorways across production runs.ColorwaysYoYoTricks Edition, Crimson, Black/Purple Fade, UnKnown Edition, Surprise Me.

title: EXPLOSiON
content: AboutiYoYo's widest mid-ship bimetal at time of release (50mm wide). Competition-focused H-profile with 7075 aluminum body and stainless steel rings. "Unmatched string control and stability." Designed to inspire confidence for daring tricks under pressure. Released January 4, 2025.ColorwaysBlue/Green Fade/Silver Rings, Purple/Silver Rings, Silver/Blue Rings, Silver/Blue Rings No Logo.

title: FiRROX
content: AboutCompetition bimetal designed in collaboration with Ze'ev Yehuda, positioned as the aggressive counterpart to the HiDRA. Large stainless steel rims and an extreme bumped response area for reduced string contact. Also romanized as "Filox" on some retailer pages. Multiple production runs with expanding colorway options.ColorwaysRed, Silver (1st run); Black/Gold, Blue, Galaxy, German Edition, Midnight, Grey, Black/Light Blue Splash (later runs).

title: FiRROX 7075
content: AboutUpgrade of the original FiRROX using hardened 7075 alloy for the body, increasing durability and making it better suited for horizontal and competition play. Maintains the H-profile stainless steel rim design from the original with updated colorway options.ColorwaysBlack/Black Rim, Blue/Rainbow Rim, Silver/Rainbow Rim, Red, Green.

title: HEiSENBERG
content: AboutNamed after physicist Werner Heisenberg (and the TV show Breaking Bad). 7075 monometal with competition feel at a non-bimetal price. Developed from Carlos Braun's suggestion after testing the ANTARCTiCA at German Nationals. Described as "the 7075 version of the ANTARCTiCA." H-profile based on the iCEBERG family. Features the CLYW × iYoYo Pixel Bearing.ColorwaysIce Blue/Silver Logo, Clear/No Logo, Clear/Black Logo, Ice Blue/Black Logo, Dark Green/Silver Logo.

title: HiDRA
content: AboutiYoYo's accessible full-metal step-up model, designed in collaboration with Ze'ev Yehuda. Bumped response pads reduce string-body contact for extended spin times. H-profile with competition-capable specs at an approachable price. Multiple colorway runs across several years. The HiDRA NXG is the next-generation update with a wider profile.ColorwaysGreen, German Edition, Blue/Gold, Blue/Multi Splash, Black/Light Blue/Pink, Light Pink, Summer Fade, Rainbow, Blue/Pink/Yellow.

title: HiDRA NXG
content: AboutNXG (Next Generation) update to the HiDRA: several millimeters wider for improved string-placement success rate and maneuverability. H-profile 6061 aluminum with bumped response area carried forward. Features the Pixel Bearing, a collaboration between CLYW and iYoYo. Multiple colorways including iYoYo "German Edition" and a "Forest Edition" exclusive acid wash.ColorwaysRaw, Hot Pink, Green/Yellow/Blue Fade, Blue Lagoon, Forest Edition, German Edition, Pink.

title: iCEBERG
content: AboutSecond-generation iCEBERG, 3.5–4mm wider than the Classic for improved string catch consistency and faster, more dynamic play. Wide H-profile now standard. Fingerspin zone retained from Classic. Considered the current standard iCEBERG going forward; the original 2017 model is now referred to as the iCEBERG Classic.ColorwaysIce Blue/Blue Ring/Blue Hub, Dark Blue/Silver Ring/Silver Hub, Clear/Blue Hubs+Rims, Blue/Pink Fade/Black Rim+Hub, Clear/Rainbow Ring/Silver Hub, Dark Green/Silver Hub+Ring.

title: iCEBERG CLASSiC
content: AboutDescribed as "the plastic version of the iYoYo Steel." CNC machined polycarbonate body with stainless steel rings for maximum rim weight contrast against the ultra-light body. Custom concave hub for fingerspins. Launched the same day as the iCEBREAKER offstring. Named "Classic" retroactively once the wider second-generation iCEBERG was released in 2021. Extensive colorway range across many production runs.ColorwaysClear Blue/Silver, Black/Blue Rim, Black/Rainbow Rim, Clear Yellow/Silver, Translucent Purple/Gold, Translucent Purple/Silver, Glow Purple/Silver, White/Pink/Rose Gold, and many more.

title: iCEBERG New
content:
About
The iCEBERG New is an updated version of iYoYo's iCEBERG design, featuring a polycarbonate body with stainless steel weight rings. The bimetal-style construction uses the density differential between polycarbonate and steel to concentrate weight at the rims, producing spin times and stability that rival full-metal competition yo-yos. Following the original iCEBERG and iCEBERG CLASSiC, the iCEBERG New represents iYoYo's continued refinement of accessible performance yo-yo design.

title: iCEBREAKER
content: AboutiYoYo's second offstring and successor to the AiR DiVE. Based on the AiR DiVE body with an added bumped response area. Claims to be the first offstring with a fingerspin zone. CNC machined polycarbonate construction (vs. typical Delrin competitors) for greater precision. Adjustable gap via two included spacer sets. Designed with input from Ryan Connolly.ColorwaysClear/Blue, Clear/Silver.

title: iMPACT
content: AboutHigh-performance bimetal with polished stainless steel rims. 7075 aluminum stepped H-shape body. Artwork by Bryan Figueroa of the "Unknown" collective. Standard Pixel Bearing and iRiNGS response. Multiple rim color variants across production runs.ColorwaysTeal/Silver Rings, Red/Silver Rings, Silver/Blue Rings, Purple/Gold Rings.

title: INFiNiTY X
content: About"Inspired by Infinity Stones." Hybrid construction: POM body for smooth, dense performance with polycarbonate sloped fingerspin caps that guide the finger naturally to center. Wide H-profile. Available in a wide range of colorway combinations pairing POM body color with PC cap color.ColorwaysWhite POM/Blue Rim Dip, Green POM/Purple PC Cap, White/Orange Cap, White/Yellow Cap, White/Purple Cap, White/Red Cap, Black/Light Blue Cap, Yellow/Clear Cap.

title: INTENSiTY
content: AboutThin, wide stainless steel ring design positioned differently from the iCEBERG's outer-edge rings. Deep H-profile reduces tilt. Sandblasted stainless steel rings minimize string slip even with sweaty hands. Fingerspin spot standard. Wide profile for stable competition play.ColorwaysClear/Blue Rim, White, Purple.

title: iPPON
content: AboutCNC polycarbonate body with stainless steel weight at the outermost wing for "quick and sharp" play with excellent balance. Mild H-profile with straight silhouette. Standard fingerspin spot. Available in a wide range of solid and tinted colorways.ColorwaysClear Rainbow, Clear Blue, Clear Black, Black/Black Ring, Red, Blue.

title: KiCKSTART
content: AboutiYoYo's first injection-molded plastic, produced and molded entirely in Germany. Funded via an Indiegogo campaign in December 2015. H-profile polycarbonate designed in collaboration with Kyle Weems of Kyos Toys. Ships with two spacer configurations for responsive and unresponsive play. Each unit hand-tested by Dave Geigle before shipping.

title: KiCKSTART Pro
content: AboutCrowdfunded follow-up to the original KiCKSTART, adding a metal rim to the polycarbonate body for enhanced spin power. H-profile with clear-tinted body in various two-tone color combinations. Designed in collaboration with Kyle Weems / Kyos Toys.ColorwaysClear Red/Gold Rim, Clear Red/Silver Rim, Clear Blue/Gold Rim, Clear Blue/Silver Rim, Clear Green, Clear Yellow.

title: NiGHTMOVES X
content: AboutModern reimagining of the YoYoJam Nightmoves, created in collaboration between Dave Geigle (former YYJ player) and Jun Aramaki of Yo-Yo Store REWIND (also a former YYJ player). Wide body with stainless steel rim weighting and removable side caps for adjustable aesthetics. Full modern specs with Size C bearing and iRing response. A tribute to the YoYoJam legacy from two of its former sponsored players.ColorwaysWhite/Blue Rim, Teal Blue/Rainbow Ring, Purple/Gold Ring.

title: iYoYo
content: AboutThe debut model from iYoYo, released at the brand's launch in November 2015. A stepped H-shape 6061 aluminum with a fingerspin cup. Founded by 5× European Champion Dave Geigle, the iYoYo brand takes its name from this first release. Limited availability at launch; exact production specs not fully documented.

title: PASSiON
content: AboutEntry-level aluminum for beginners. Undersized 53mm diameter fits smaller hands more comfortably. Ships with both responsive and unresponsive bearing configurations for a full progression path in one package. H-profile construction.ColorwaysGalaxy, German Edition (Black/Red/Gold), Blue Lagoon, Green/Black Acid Wash, Fireworks.

title: iYoYo × hspin Pyro X
content: AboutModern version of the legendary hspin PYRO, officially licensed by hspin and designed in collaboration with Hadrien Bennaceur, the original hspin yo-yo designer. "Modern Legendary YoYo." 7075 aluminum for improved durability and performance over the original design. A tribute to one of the most influential throws in competition history.ColorwaysGreen/Purple, Orange/Red, Blue/Green, Blue/Orange, Purple/Grey, Black/Blue, Pink/Purple.

title: RiTTER
content: AboutNamed after the German word for "Knight." Angular, armor-inspired design in 6061 aluminum. Fingerspin dip. Floaty yet powerful feel. Artwork on the body by Bryan Figueroa of the "Unknown" collective. Priced as an affordable option within iYoYo's lineup.ColorwaysBlack/Light Blue Splash, Silver/Rainbow Splash, Black/Pink/Silver Splash, Black/Red, Light Blue/Red.

title: SHOOTiNG STAR
content: About"Full plastic version of the iCEBERG." Stepped H-shape CNC machined polycarbonate based on the iCEBERG profile. Metal fingerspin dimple. Ships with both a responsive narrow bearing AND an unresponsive Pixel Bearing for a full progression path in one box. Extensive colorway selection across many production runs.ColorwaysYellow/Blue Fade/Black Hub, Purple/Silver Hub, Orange/Black Hub, Translucent Light Blue/Black Hub, Yellow/Black Hub, Blue/Pink Fade/Black Hub, Rainbow Fade/Black Hub, Clear/Blue Rim Dip/Black Hub, Translucent Teal/Black Hub, Black/Silver Hub, Translucent Dark Blue/Silver Hub, Translucent Dark Green/Silver Hub, White/Black Hub, Solid Light Blue/Silver Hub, Translucent Blue Glitter/Silver Hub.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C Half-Spec narrow (+ Pixel Bearing included)

title: SKYLiGHT
content: About"The first offstring that can fingerspin like no other." POM/Delrin body with 7075 aluminum fingerspin hubs for reliable finger spin performance in an offstring context. Stable, fast, and bounces well for 4A recovery play. Designed in collaboration with Ryan Connolly. Adjustable gap via two included spacer pairs.ColorwaysWhite/Blue Hub, Green/Silver Hub, Blue/Pink Hub, Red/Silver Hub, Yellow/Silver Hub.

title: SONiC WAVE
content: AboutMore prototypes produced during development than most iYoYo models. Curved inner stainless steel ring creates "stable yet dynamic weight distribution." Bridges the slim and wide segments of the iYoYo lineup. All hand-contact surfaces are polycarbonate for a softer feel. Fingerspin hubs standard.ColorwaysRed/Silver Ring+Hub, Dark Green/Silver Ring+Hub, Yellow/Black Ring+Hub, Light Blue/Black Ring+Hub.

title: SPiNMASTER X
content: AboutPolycarbonate body with 7075 aluminum rings for fingerspin-focused play. Named as a spiritual homage to the classic YoYoJam SpinMaster series. H-profile with cherry-red polycarbonate body aesthetic.

title: SPiRE
content: AboutCollaboration offstring between iYoYo and YoYoTricks.com (Throwback Skill Toys). Claims to be the first offstring with an inner lip in the cup for thumb grinds. Also excels at finger spins and finger grinds. CNC machined polycarbonate construction to 1A precision standards. Successor to the iCEBREAKER lineage.ColorwaysClear/Red Hubs, Clear/Mint Hubs, Clear/Black Hubs, Clear/Purple Hubs, Clear/Blue Hubs, Black/Blue Hubs, Red/Black Hubs, Blue/Black Hubs.

title: iYoYo Steel
content: AboutThe bimetal that put iYoYo on the competitive map. 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims in an H-profile design, featuring a fingerspin spot on the side face. Power and stability through precise steel rim weighting. Multiple splash and solid colorways across several production runs.ColorwaysGalaxy, German Edition, Grey/Gold, Red/Gold, Blue/Gold.

title: SUNRiSE
content: About2A looping collaboration between iYoYo (Dave Geigle), YoYoFactory, and Bill de Boisblanc. Named after the YoYoJam Sunset Trajectory, a double-signature model by Dave Geigle and Bill de Boisblanc. The body is identical to the YoYoFactory Loop 720 but uses a custom spacer enabling a YYJ-size B bearing for a softer, more traditional looping feel. Origin story: Bill emailed Dave over breakfast at WYYC 2018.ColorwaysBlue/White Cap, Orange/White Cap, Edge Glow Yellow, Green/White Cap, Translucent Yellow/Aqua Cap.

title: TEQUiLA
content: About"A celebration of European yo-yo culture." Designed by Ze'ev Yehuda with artwork by Bryan Figueroa. Unconventional double-tequila-shot-glass shape — each cup measures approximately 20mL. Originally a WYYC 2020 Budapest surprise release. The unusual wide profile (65mm width at 50mm diameter) aids navigation through dense string formations. Ships convertible responsive/unresponsive.ColorwaysBlack, Red/Gold Fade (WYYC Edition).

title: TiGER
content: AboutFull titanium collaboration between iYoYo and ILOVEYOYO (ILYY), both German brands. Based on iYoYo's flagship model with design influences from ILYY's Torino. Released October 29, 2015. Comes in a specially designed aluminum storage and display case. A landmark release for the German yo-yo scene.ColorwaysGold, Raw titanium.

title: TiRROX
content: AboutiYoYo's second full titanium model. Complex curved multi-step shape with beveled grooves; thin titanium walls provide "absurd speed and stability." Packaged in a custom aluminum box. Designed in collaboration with Ze'ev Yehuda.

title: TiSSOX
content: About"HiDRA's final form." Combines a titanium body with stainless steel rims — iYoYo's premium bimetal at time of release. Designed in collaboration with Ze'ev Yehuda. TiSS construction delivers the lightweight agility of titanium with the spin-extension of dense steel rims.

title: TiTANiC
content: AboutFull titanium version of the iCEBERG profile. Fully polished titanium with engraved sinking ship artwork by Bryan Figueroa of the "Unknown" collective. Released December 17, 2019. Packaged in a custom metal box. Fingerspin dimple. Plays fast and stable with a pleasantly nimble feel. A 2022 Rainbow Edition reissue was also produced.ColorwaysGreen (original 2019), Rainbow Edition (2022 reissue).

title: UNLiMiTED
content: AboutiYoYo's first official pro signature model, designed for Ryan Connolly who became World Champion in 4A in August 2024. Follows the AiR DiVE shape but with a smaller diameter and wider build per modern 4A trends. Double rim construction without a separate weight ring. Adjustable gap via included spacers. One of the most-used 4A throws at WYYC 2024.ColorwaysYellow/Silver Hub, White/Blue Ring+Blue Hub, White/Blue Hub, Red/Silver Hub, Green/Silver Hub.

title: VERiTAS
content: AboutReleased October 27, 2016. Limited run of 100 units. Designed by 14-year-old German player Mathilde Witt, who produced full technical drawings and submitted the design as a State Science Fair project. Dave Geigle manufactured it from her specifications. Heavier than typical for power and stability, with excellent fingerspin performance. Sold out immediately at release.

title: VERiTAS Pro
content: AboutUpgraded commercial release of Mathilde Witt's VERiTAS design. Embedded 7075 aluminum weight rings and polycarbonate fingerspin caps minimize friction during finger spins. Horizontal-trick focused with a step straight profile. Signature collaboration with Mathilde Witt continuing her original Science Fair project vision.

title: Rainbow YoYo Jacks
content: History / AboutThe Ja-Ru Rainbow YoYo Jacks toy combined yo-yo and jacks in one toy. A transparent yo-yo housed a colorful jacks set; unscrewing the halves gave access to the jacks and ball stored inside. Released in 1999 with an original retail price of $3 USD, according to the Yo-Yo Museum, which also records a fixed axle and starburst response. Ja-Ru, Inc. was founded in 1961 by Bernard Selevan in Jacksonville, Florida, and named for his sons Jack and Russell.

title: Stunt Wheelie
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki lists the Stunt Wheelie as a Ja-Ru yo-yo with a tire shape in black and silver. Reported specifications are a diameter of 5.2 cm, a width of 3.9 cm, a weight of about 2.2 ounces, plastic and rubber construction, a size D bearing and a starburst response. The wiki leaves the release date blank.

title: Jackal
content:
History / About
The Jackal was released in 2024 as part of G2's expanding modern catalog. Featured in the "Jackal Prep" development log shared by G2 ambassador Fifth Mission in May 2024. Currently offered in Nebula and Ness Depths colorways at $139.

title: Jackpot
content:
History / About
The Jackpot is a 2025 bimetal from G2's modern lineup, priced at $135 with 6061+SS construction. The casino/gambling name joins G2's eclectic naming tradition.

title: Dunk Rebound
content:
About the Dunk Rebound
The Dunk Rebound is Jake Bullock's refined iteration of the original Dunk design, machined from 7075 aluminum with the same profile. It uses a D-size bearing and Freshly Dirty response pads. The yo-yo ships with custom packaging artwork and was available in Olive, Lilac, Black, Silver, Orange, and Easter Swap colorways.

title: Slap Junior
content:
About the Slap Junior
Jake Bullock collaborated with Jameson Larkins to create the Slap Junior, an undersized bimetal iteration of the Slappa. The diameter shrinks from approximately 58mm to 52mm while the stainless steel rims are thickened to maintain power — notably, the rims alone weigh more than the entire 7075 aluminum body and internals combined. The result is a pocketable, competition-capable slimline yo-yo at 59 grams.

title: Ti Dunk
content:
About the Ti Dunk
Jake Bullock's Ti Dunk is a full titanium execution of the Dunk profile, designed to take Dunk performance to its upper limit. The titanium construction provides exceptional durability and extended spin characteristics. It ships with a C-size KonKave bearing and Freshly Dirty response pads. Released in a raw titanium finish.

title: Janus
content:
From ZGRT:

"With every project we embark, new concepts and ideas come to us to  explore different designs, playability and versatility for future creations. Working on the KnuckleYo kindled a spark of imagination and inspiration leading us to the creation of the Janus: a slim line yo-yo that uses two removable coins to play.

The starting point of the design was around the dimensions of the coin itself.  Coins of this type can be used as worry or rolling coins and come in different dimensions that go from 30 to 45 mm diameter, 3 to 7 mm thickness and 10 to 40 gr. We started to explore all the multiple designs around those dimensions and see what would fit best.

The diameter

The ‘standard’ size of a manipulation coin is around 35 mm diameter. Having a diameter in that range was not the best fit for what we were looking for.  Although the main idea of this project was to design a yoyo that could be easily transformed into a coin, we always wanted the Janus to be a capable yoyo to play with.  Our goal was to find the best size of diameter that allowed the Janus to be playable as a coin as well as a  throw.  We found the sweet spot to be 45.5 mm.

The thickness

The next challenge we faced was to determine the coin’s thickness which is fully correlated to the performance, weight and width of the throw. A thin yoyo would compromise certain performance capabilities and functionality; whereas,  a thick coin would not be ideal to perform manipulations. With those two challenges to consider, we determined that the thickness was pretty much limited to be in the 7-8 mm range.  We used the thickness of El MiJo yoyo as a point of reference which is 12 mm, and our objective was to go no less than 60% of that dimension.

Due to the design of the Janus, the weight is proportionally correlated with the thickness and the size of the diameter. Although we had a range of 30 gr. to play with, the diameter that we established along with the width that we were aiming,  the weight became another factor that had to be considered. With all those elements on the table, we ended up with a thickness of 7.8 mm which gave us a weight of 23.7 gr. when in coin mode.

The incorporation of Side Effects

In order for this throw to be transformed into a coin, we needed a system that was suitable and functional for the Janus. We explored many options to adapt this idea. We went back a forth with different approaches, until we saw the potential that the Side Effects machined by One Drop could bring to the Janus.  One Drop’s Side Effects allowed the Janus for a complete removal of its axle and bearing seats and feel it more “coin like” when in coin mode. This also opened the possibility to use the Janus as a wearable coin.

The final design

Once all of the above elements were incorporated, we had two elements left to accomplish: performance and design.  The most suitable material for this concept was aluminum 6061. We needed certain wall thickness for the shape and design we envisioned.  We pushed the walls of the cup in a way that could work for coin manipulation and as a worry coin, and at the same time to allow a better weight distribution when played as a yoyo.

We do not consider the Janus to be a micro-yoyo by any means. The Janus is a small, fully functional pocket throw that can be played as a responsive and unresponsive yoyo that when disassembled yet it can also be used as a coin for coin manipulation tricks as well.

The name

In ancient Roman religion and myth, Janus is the god of beginnings, gates, transitions, time, duality, doorways, passages, frames, and endings. Janus is typically depicted as having two faces and was commonly embossed onto Roman coins.

The name reflects the dual nature of our creation and the various passage ways it may lead you while playing.  The throw’s mismatched sides of different colours and patterns further reflect the characteristic of Janus:  the double faced pocket throw that actually fits in your pocket.

We would like to thank our team members Jack Morris, Iñaki Diez and Jason Williams for al their input during the development of this project.

A special thanks and recognition to Chris Francz for his amazing artwork in the Janus that was used in both the logo and the engraving of this throw.

Let nothing hold you down!"

title: Shaqshine (2019 Layered)
content: The 2019 Layered edition of Japan Technology’s Shaqshine is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo with stainless steel weight rings. It has a C double-straight bearing and slim response pads. FIU’s June 21 listing refers to an Unknown edition; its count is undocumented.This 2019 Layered model is distinct from the original 2016 A300 model.

yya_gallery_images.title: Japan Technology Shaqshine yo-yo, Unknown edition

title: Jello
content: About JelloA polycarbonate yo-yo offering durable, budget-friendly play. Known for its translucent colorways and reliable performance in casual and intermediate play.

title: Jenos
content: History / AboutC3 4A retail model documented by the official catalog.

title: Jester
content:
The Jester is the inaugural release of Wickedyoyos, and released during Worlds 2024.

From YoYoSam:

"Introducing the WickedYoyos Jester, a yoyo designed for competitive play while still being a fun throw for any casual player. The Jester features POM caps for flawless fingerspin performance as well as a 7068 Aluminum body. This yoyo was designed by Owen Kroeger and Jordan Blofeld and is the pinnacle of yoyo design. At 66.5g, this yoyo is a beast on the string that can withstand any trick that you throw at it! The ultra smooth blasted finish on the Jester will allow for flawless grinds and long spin times."

title: Jet-Set
content: AboutThe Jet-Set is the retail production collaboration between sOMEThING and Japan Technology. It combines the H-profile of the Jet-Set EX with the cup design from JT's Amulette, resulting in easy, confident catches with a light feel that remains maneuverable between strings. Designed for players at all levels from beginner through competition. Available in White/Hot Pink Hub and Blue/Silver Hub colorways.

title: Jet-Set EG
content: AboutThe Jet-Set EG is a collaboration between sOMEThING and Japan Technology, released in 2017. Based on JT's JetSet EC, the EG features a redesigned shape and side face by Atsushi Yamada that — despite nearly identical weight and dimensions — significantly affects weight distribution to improve stability and regeneration sensation. A follow-up Jet-Set EG.W variant and the Jet-Set EG.W ONE limited edition were also produced, including a Hajime Edition.

title: JET SET EX
content: About the JET SET EXThe JET SET EX is a collaboration between sOMEThING and Japan Technology, designed as a signature model for 4A World Champion Michael Nakamura. It redesigns the JetSet EG with a W-shape profile that opens up the catch zone for greater offstring playability. Inner stainless steel weight rings provide power and precision. "Lighter and more powerful" than the EG.Colorways: White with Blue Hub and Silver Ring; Red with Silver Ring and Black Hub. Japan Technology is the manufacturer; sOMEThING is the co-releasing brand partner.

title: JET SET
content: About the JET SETThe JET SET is the latest iteration of the long-running sOMEThING and Japan Technology offstring collaboration series. H-profile full-POM construction is "sharp and responsive" on quick movements. Suitable for players from beginner through advanced offstring. $69.99 USD.Japan Technology is not currently in The Yoyo Archive. Colorways: White with Hot Pink Hub, Blue with Silver Hub.

title: Jewelled Satellite
content: HistoryThe Jewelled Satellite was Cheerio's premium decorative model featuring embedded jewels in a satellite pattern. Produced in the 1950s as a high-end collectible yo-yo.

title: AIBOU
content:
About
The AIBOU — Japanese for "partner" or "brother" — is the debut yo-yo from JIGUN, a Tokyo-based player brand, produced in partnership with Sōchí Company. Machined from 7068 aluminum with an 8mm axle, it was built to competition-level specifications and sold at an accessible $40 price point. The model ships with Sōchí response pads and was available in seven colorways: Blue, Pink, Light Olive, Purple, Orange, Tiffany, and Green.

title: MG Lithium
content:
About
The MG Lithium is a limited run of 100 pieces produced by JIGUN in collaboration with Sōchí Company, recreating founder Luckey Yulin Li's original Lithium signature throw in magnesium and stainless steel. The magnesium body delivers an exceptionally lightweight feel while the stainless steel rims provide the spin power and stability expected of a competition bimetal. Released in white, the MG Lithium requires drying after extended play to prevent corrosion inherent to magnesium alloy. It retailed at $180 USD and sold out quickly.

title: Josy-Ann
content:
History / About
There’s a lack of oversized yoyos. Josy-Ann fits that void perfectly. Extremely stable and smooth. Named after our girlfriends. A winner.

Production Runs

Pre-Production #1 (December 2008) — 30 units, Gold/Orange; D57.95mm / W37.45mm / 64.00g. Finish: Soda Blast.
Run #1 — 120 units, Gold/Orange; D57.95mm / W37.45mm / 64.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.

title: Journey
content: About the JourneyThe Journey features an adjustable string gap allowing beginners to start with a narrow, responsive configuration and gradually open it as skill improves. Packaged with a narrow C bearing for beginner-friendly response, it can be upgraded to a wider bearing for bind play. A later collaboration variant was produced with Yomega.

title: Joyride (D Bearing / Current)
content:
History / About
The D Bearing Joyride is the current production version of Recess's founding flagship organic monometal, updated from the v3 profile with a D-size bearing. Recess explains the reasoning: D bearings are wider (5mm inner width) than A-size small bearings (4mm), giving players the agility and RPMs of a small-bearing system without the narrow string gap that would cause friction and hinder modern trick selection. The result is a fast, agile Joyride with a full-width gap. One colorway (Riley Moore "Silly Goose") is a collaboration with Riley Moore of YoYo Memes fame — a half-swap yellow/aqua edition.

title: Joyride GT
content:
History / About
The Joyride GT is the anodized-finish variant of the Joyride v3, offering the same specifications in a different surface treatment. Where the standard Joyride uses a smooth blast finish, the GT's anodized surface provides a different grind feel and aesthetic. Offered alongside the standard v3 at the same price point, it gave players a choice of finish while maintaining identical performance.

title: Joyride (v1 / Original)
content:
History / About
The Joyride launched simultaneously with the Weekend and First Base at the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest, introducing Recess to the world with a complete lineup in one day. The Joyride was the flagship monometal — an organic-shaped 6061 aluminum throw that Recess describes as foundational to "a modern wave of organic yoyo design." At the 2015 Worlds pre-release, it stunned players with its power and stability for a monometal, making many rethink their preference for bimetals. The fingerspin hub and grind-friendly blasted finish made it practical for modern play. Colin Beckford's 2015 Buyer's Guide on YYE Forums rated it 9/10, calling it best for stability and power. The Joyride went through three major iterations: v2 (2017, 56.9mm/44.5mm/66.3g, updated hub) and v3 (2023, 56.72mm/44.7mm/66.16g, wider gap of 4.50mm, redesigned hub). The D-Bearing Joyride (current, $50) uses the v3 body with a D-size bearing for higher RPMs and is currently in stock.

title: Genertia
content: History / AboutGenertia is described by Japan Looping Solutions as its first full-metal looping yo-yo. It shares Loop Up's basic structure for continuously adjustable gap and ships with a titanium axle. The pull-back mechanism is a replaceable plastic starburst. Listed weight is 52.5 g and diameter 57.0 mm.

title: Genertix
content: History / AboutGenertix is a full-metal looping yo-yo with metal caps, a titanium axle for balance, and a metal spacer. Washers of different thicknesses and a custom 0.02 mm ultra-thin shim are included to set the gap. The caps are not glued but are not meant to be removed.

meta.yya_gap_width: Set with washers and 0.02 mm shim

title: LeveLRise
content: History / AboutLeveLRise uses metal caps for appearance and a sharp feel with stable looping. It has Loop Up's gap-adjusting mechanism, and the included metal spacer allows fixed-gap play. Contents: LeveLRise, metal spacer, suction cup.

title: Loop Up
content: History / AboutLoop Up is the looping model of Japan Looping Solutions, developed by Mino-Kamo, Gifu players together with competition players. Its distinctive structure allows continuously adjustable, fixable gap width, and the gap barely drifts in use. It is aimed at intermediate to advanced players and needs a 6 mm wrench for adjustment. Compared with rc2 the axle material grade was raised for durability and the body was adjusted to correct a loop trajectory that tended to run high. Per the maker, Loop Up won the 2A division at the 2019 Japan National, Asia Pacific and World championships.

title: Loop Up (Hiraku Edition)
content: History / AboutHiraku Edition is a Loop Up edition associated with JPLS player Hiraku Fujii, listed by Yoyostore Rewind in a standard version and a Metal Spacer version. Mechanics follow Loop Up (adjustable gap, polycarbonate body); the metal spacer version has the fixed-gap setup described for Loop Up (Metal Spacer).

title: Loop Up (Metal Spacer)
content: History / AboutThe Metal Spacer version of Loop Up comes with machined 7075 (super super duralumin) spacers preinstalled, one red and one blue per side, so no adjustment is needed, making it suitable for beginners. The gap was set after the setup of world champion (2008, 2013, 2014) Takuma Yamamoto, for Type 6 (50/50) string, and it also works with polyester strings. The body is identical to standard Loop Up, but the different axle means the adjustment nut cannot be fitted.

title: Loop Up rc2
content: History / AboutLoop Up (rc2) went on sale at stores from 14 December 2017, according to the Japan Looping Solutions site news. It is the earlier version of Loop Up, whose body was later revised because the rc2 loop trajectory was said to run slightly high, and whose axle material grade was later raised for durability. The project began when looping players in Mino-Kamo, Gifu, feared they would lose usable looping yo-yos; the first prototype took one month and the official release took nearly two years.

title: Jugemu
content: AboutThe Jugemu is a 6061 aluminum monometal released in 2023, designed to overturn the image of heavyweight models. Despite its 66.8g weight, it plays lighter in hand than the number suggests. Its wide 48mm H-profile body provides visual confidence for string-hitting tricks. A '24 update expanded the width to 52mm, and a 7075 ESD '24 variant was released simultaneously.

title: Jugemu ’24
content: AboutThe Jugemu '24 refreshes the Jugemu with an ultra-wide 52.2mm body, providing a massive catch zone well-suited to string-hitting trick styles. The iconic Jugemu side profile is maintained while the width is modernized. Available in Shiny Light Pink, Shiny Black, and Matte Purple colorways. A 7075 ESD '24 variant (68.5g) was also released alongside it.

title: Alpha Sapphire
content:
About
The Alpha Sapphire is July YoYo's first 7075 aluminum and stainless steel bimetal, establishing the flagship line that later produced the V2 and Mini. The harder 7075 body pairs with stainless steel rims for competition-level spin power and stability. Full specifications were not published by retailers; the V2 (2025) cites a two-year development cycle that implies the Alpha Sapphire originated around 2023–2024.

title: Alpha Sapphire AR
content:
About
The Alpha Sapphire AR is a hybrid construction — a 6061 aluminum body with a 7075 aluminum ring rather than the stainless steel rims of the standard Alpha Sapphire. The harder 7075 ring adds rigidity and stability without the extreme mass shift of a full bimetal, targeting players who want agile monometal handling with an extra layer of punch. Available in Green/Gold Ring, Red/Black Rings, and Ice Blue/Silver Ring. Priced at approximately $70.

title: Alpha Sapphire AR-Mega Evolution
content:
History / About
Alpha Sapphire AR-Mega Evolution is an evolution of the already-archived "Alpha Sapphire AR" (A6061 body / A7075 rim), enlarged and widened to match current trends. It exploits the slight density difference between A6061 and A7075 to shift weight toward the rim for powerful, long-lasting spin, while avoiding the abrupt "layered" feel of a true bimetal — described by the brand as retaining a smooth, unified single-metal feel. The enlarged size increases string contact area for stability on larger tricks.

title: Alpha Sapphire Mini
content:
About
The Alpha Sapphire Mini distills the Alpha Sapphire V2 into a 50.54mm compact format while maintaining the 65.2g weight through thicker stainless steel rims that compensate for the reduced body size. The 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rims preserves the powerful spin and solid stability of the full-size flagship. Available in Splash Black/Green. Retailed at $69.99 and sold out on launch.

title: Alpha Sapphire V2
content:
About
The Alpha Sapphire V2 is July YoYo's flagship competition bimetal, the product of a two-year development process with multiple prototypes. Designed by team player Zhang Yufu, the 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rims achieves a 49.59mm width — significantly wider than the original — in a 56.01mm diameter package. The inverse-curve H-profile targets crisp direction changes, extended spin stability, and aggressive power for competition freestyles. Debuted at the 2025 CYML Northwest China Contest. Available in Matte Splash Silver/Light Blue/Light Purple. Retails at $84.99–$89.99.

title: Axono
content:
About
The Axono is July YoYo's value competition bimetal, named after axonometric projection and co-developed with Korean team members. The 57.03mm body at 65.9g pairs a 6061 aluminum frame with stainless steel rims, with a 49mm width specifically chosen to maximize string-landing hit rates during competition. July positions it as "a bimetal built for competition at a price that defies expectations." Available in Matte Splash Purple/Blue/Black with Shiny Silver Rim. Retails at $54.99–$65.

title: Axono Nexus
content:
History / About
Axono Nexus is the flagship successor and next-generation evolution of July YoYo's bimetal "Axono," built after multiple prototyping rounds into a larger, wider, more powerful design. A thinner-wall 7075 aluminum body boosts explosive spin power and sustained horizontal-style rotation; width was expanded to just under 55mm with a revised edge angle for a larger string contact area. A small hollow section between rim and body fine-tunes weight distribution to resolve sluggishness and improve stability.

title: Axono Z
content:
History / About
Axono Z is an update to the cost-effective bimetal "Axono," developed by July YoYo's own team members in Korea (the name derives from "axonometric"). It was widened slightly versus the original Axono per competitive-player feedback. A stainless rim concentrates weight outward for powerful, low-decay spin through long combos, and the body supports string response for advanced tricks. Marketed as bimetal performance at an accessible price point.

title: Delta Stream
content:
About
The Delta Stream is July YoYo's compact competition bimetal, pairing a 55.45mm diameter with a wide 50.12mm body — a high width-to-diameter ratio that maximizes catch zone area while keeping the throw compact. The 6061 aluminum body and stainless steel rims deliver competition-grade spin power and maneuverability. Responsive trick transitions and strong finger-grip stability. Available in Matte Fade Blue/Silver with Matte Black Rim. Retails at $74.99–$79.99.

title: E-Stub (Pre-Production)
content:
History / About
E-Stub ("E" for "Extreme") is an enlarged evolution of July YoYo's long-running flagship "STUBBORN." It has a larger diameter and wider body than STUBBORN, increasing string surface, power, and anti-tilt stability for long, planted spins. Explicitly a competition-minded model, and the base from which the Park Sol signature "Solute" was itself derived. July YoYo labels this a pre-production model whose specs may change before official release.

title: EXORCIST.SE
content:
History / About
EXORCIST.SE is a 6061 aluminum monometal that, per July YoYo's own account, "earned strong support across China and South Korea." It is distinguished from an earlier, separate "EXORCIST" model. Its base shape was later carried over into the bimetal "Hailspire," built by player request as an explicit reimagining of this design. EXORCIST.SE's own listing is confirmed live on the Korean retailer YJYOYO Shop; its exact release date could not be independently verified and is estimated here.

title: Fleurtain
content:
About
The Fleurtain is July YoYo's widest model at 60.3mm — among the widest yo-yos in production. The tri-material construction combines a 6061 aluminum body for structural precision, stainless steel rims for spin power, and POM outer wings that extend the catch zone and add a textured, comfortable feel to string catches. The 58mm diameter at 66.9g. Available in Pink. Retails at $109.90–$109.99.

title: GALEWNG
content:
History / About
GALEWNG is built on the shape of July YoYo's "Special Lemon Honey," a multi-material model designed for more power. It carries a larger stainless rim ratio than the "Lunar Dance Tri," concentrating dense metal at the outer edge for immediate, powerful spin, while the 7075 hub keeps weight aggressive toward the wing tips. The polycarbonate body creates a felt contrast between heavy rims and light body for expressive handling, while retaining strong spin power and stability through long combos. Marketed toward power-style players wanting fast, uninterrupted combos.

title: Hailspire
content:
History / About
Hailspire is a bimetal reimagining of an earlier July YoYo monometal, the "EXORCIST.SE," built by player request. It carries over EXORCIST.SE's base shape with fine-tuned weight distribution for fast, sharp movement that stays level and stable at speed. Marketed on accessible pricing for a bimetal.

title: Invocaluna
content:
History / About
Invocaluna is billed by July YoYo as the culmination and full material upgrade of its "Lunar Dance" series. A dense 7075 aluminum hub and a further-thinned polycarbonate body expand the stainless steel rim's proportion of overall mass for greater rotational stability and longer spin, while the PC body preserves the series' light, nimble handling. An extra polycarbonate ring layered over the outside softens catch impact and adds a distinctive layered look. Positioned for horizontal/high-motion tricks as well as standard 1A play.

title: Lemon Honey
content:
About
The Lemon Honey is July YoYo's first bimaterial model and the launch of what became a full product line. The 6061 aluminum body is paired with a polycarbonate or POM rim that combines the rigidity and precision of metal with the softer, more flexible feel of plastic — reducing hand fatigue during extended competition practice. At 56.5mm diameter and 47.61mm width, the H-profile provides a generous catch zone. The Lemon Honey name and design concept spawned subsequent versions including the 1.5, Special, and V2.

title: Lemon Honey 1.5
content:
About
The Lemon Honey 1.5 is an intermediate revision between the original Lemon Honey and the V2, debuted at the 2025 CYML Northwest China Contest. Slightly larger in diameter (57.07mm) and width (47.95mm) than the original while maintaining the same 66g weight and bimaterial construction philosophy. Available in Could Shop, Glass Enamel, Rainbow, and Galaxy colorways — all sold out. Priced at $49.

title: Lemon Honey 2
content:
About
The Lemon Honey 2 is the second-generation bimaterial in July YoYo's flagship line. The 6061 aluminum body is paired with a polycarbonate rim that absorbs impact on catches, reducing hand strain during intensive practice sessions. JULY describes the character as combining "the flexible feel of a plastic yoyo and the rigid precision of metal." Multiple rounds of weight distribution refinement preceded the final spec. Available in Light Green with Light Green PC rim. Retails at $49.99.

title: LifEter
content:
About
The LifEter is July YoYo's large-diameter monometal, combining a 57.93mm diameter with an unusually wide 52.17mm profile for a monometal. The H-profile geometry concentrates weight at the rim to maximize spin power from single-material construction, while the wide body significantly improves string-landing success rates. Matte splash finish in Black/Blue/Green. Retails at approximately $39–$44.99.

title: LR Raid
content:
About
The LR Raid is the signature bimetal for July YoYo 5A team player Wang Ruitao. The aluminum body with stainless steel weight rings targets the specific demands of 5A freestyles — quick direction changes and maneuverability during counterweight tricks combined with the long, stable spin required for complex combinations. Available in Blue/Silver Rings and Blue/Green Fade colorways. Priced at approximately €70.

title: Lunar Dance Tri
content:
About
The Lunar Dance Tri is July YoYo's tri-material design — polycarbonate body for a responsive, nimble feel; stainless steel rims at the perimeter for spin power; and an aluminum hub at center. The combination targets sharp, precise play at high speeds that conventional single-material throws cannot match. The 56.92mm H-profile at 65g. Available in Blue. Retails at $54.99–$60.

title: Operetta
content:
About
The Operetta is July YoYo's lightweight bimetal, featuring internal stainless steel rings rather than outer rims to generate spin power while keeping the overall weight at 65.5g and maintaining an agile feel. The gloss finish is not grind-friendly but contributes to a smooth, polished aesthetic. Available in Silver and Silver/Blue/Pink acid wash. Priced at approximately €70.

title: Overelity
content:
About
The Overelity is July YoYo's polycarbonate-body bimaterial — inverting the usual formula by placing the plastic on the inside and the aluminum rim on the outside. The 57.83mm H-profile delivers a light, nimble feel with a gentle play character distinct from all-metal construction. Includes a fingerspin spot on the side face. Available in Clear body with Blue Rim colorway. Retails at $54.99.

title: Overlap PC
content:
History / About
Overlap PC is described by July YoYo as "the long-awaited polycarbonate version of the OVERLAP series," carrying forward the monometal Overlap's design philosophy in machined polycarbonate. Its H-profile shifts weight toward the outer rim for spin endurance and a crisper feel, and it includes a finger-spin spot for DNA-style tricks. Positioned as both a competent first-bind yo-yo and a casual throw.

title: Overlap.Pro
content:
About
The Overlap.Pro is July YoYo's in-house evolution of the TopYo collaboration Overlap concept, developed as a standalone model with a larger footprint and a distinctly floaty, agile character. At 57mm diameter and 51.8mm width, it prioritizes the floating feel over raw spin power. Described as combining "rock-solid stability with agile speed and control." Available in Light Blue, Dark Green, and Titanium Styling Brown Matte. Priced at approximately €44.99.

title: Precipice Blades
content:
About
The Precipice Blades is July YoYo's flagship model and the culmination of a four-year development arc beginning with a 2021 prototype. The 7075 aluminum body is paired with titanium rims — the highest-performance rim material available in yo-yo construction — delivering exceptional spin duration and stability. The 57.15mm H-profile at 65.7g targets high-speed technical play and complex combination sequences. Retails at $169.99.

title: Sharpness
content:
About
The Sharpness is the model that established July YoYo's reputation, becoming one of the best-selling budget metal yo-yos in the Chinese market. The sandblasted 6061 aluminum body with a polished inner cup delivers a distinct two-texture feel, while the wide H-profile with rim weighting provides a stable, forgiving play experience described as having "Japanese vibes." Available in Black and Blue/Silver/Pink acid wash colorways. A Sharpness 7075 variant was also produced in the same period.

title: Sharpness 7075
content:
History / About
Sharpness 7075 is a 7075 aluminum monometal variant of July YoYo's original 6061 aluminum "Sharpness," and a distinct SKU from both that model and the already-archived "Sharpness V2." It was sold through the Korean retailer yoyoboxstore.com, whose listing for this model is no longer live at time of research; confirmation instead comes from a May 2025 customer review and unboxing, dating the release to around that period.

title: Sharpness V2
content:
About
The Sharpness V2 is July YoYo's entry-level flagship — a 6061 aluminum H-profile designed specifically as a first metal yo-yo recommendation. At 55.87mm diameter and 47.5mm width, the forgiving catch zone and lightweight 65.2g construction minimize the learning curve for players transitioning from plastic. Available in a broad range of matte and shiny colorways including Matte Green, Pink, Ice Blue, Orange, and Black. Retails at approximately $24.99–$39.98.

title: Solute (Pre-Production)
content:
History / About
Solute is billed as Park Sol's first signature model — a tri-material build stemming from his run at the Korean Nationals, based on the "E-Stub" he used at that event. It adds stainless and POM rim components around the outer edge for more delicate control alongside the E-Stub's spin power and handling, with width held narrower than tested wide prototypes for precision control. July YoYo explicitly labels this a pre-production/pre-release model whose specs may change before official launch.

title: Special Lemon Honey
content:
About
The Special Lemon Honey upgrades the Lemon Honey concept to a tri-material construction: a 6061 aluminum body provides the structural core, stainless steel rims add spin power and stability, and a polycarbonate outer cover softens catches and reduces hand impact. The 57.85mm H-profile at 66g balances powerful spin with a comfortable, gentle feel. Strong slack and whip string control. Available in Black, Light Blue, and Galaxy colorways. Retails at $69.99–$90.

title: STUBBORN
content:
History / About
STUBBORN is described by July YoYo as "the flagship that July YoYo has refined over many years," long relied on by domestic and international team players as a top competition choice. It is the direct predecessor to the pre-production "E-Stub," which is explicitly built as an enlarged evolution of this model. STUBBORN's own dedicated retail listing is no longer live as of this research; its existence, specs, and role are corroborated by a May 2024 review and by references in the E-Stub product copy.

title: W/Z Shuriken
content:
About
The W/Z Shuriken is a limited prototype release from July YoYo — a 7075 aluminum monometal with ultra-thin wall construction enabling a 54.97mm width packed into a 57.91mm diameter body. The name combines Wave (spin stability) and Zap (sharp control response). The non-sticky smooth coating and extreme width create an unusually open catch zone for a single-material throw. Limited production run; retails at approximately $64.

title: K1
content: About the K1The K1 is MagicYoYo's foundational beginner plastic yo-yo. It ships responsive for easy returns and comes with an upgrade bearing for unresponsive play, covering the full learning progression in one package. Durable ABS construction handles the drops and rough play of a learner's practice. A K1 Plus variant adds Z-stack hubstacks for additional trick options. Sold in Dark Blue, Red, and other colorways. The K1 Classic and K1 Plus are the two primary variants.

title: K10 Behemoth
content: About the K10 BehemothThe K10 Behemoth lives up to its name: an exceptionally wide 53.72mm polycarbonate yo-yo with a metal weight ring for rim weighting. The width makes it one of the most forgiving catches in MagicYoYo's catalog, assisting string landing during trick learning. Unresponsive with accessible price. Available in Red and Blue colorways.

title: K2 Crystal
content: About the K2 CrystalThe K2 Crystal (also sold as K2 Plus) is an injection-molded polycarbonate yo-yo designed for beginner through intermediate players. Its extra-wide upper line assists string trick landing, an ultra-thick outer ring extends spin time, and a dedicated finger groove teaches finger spin entry. Ships with both responsive and unresponsive bearings. Available in Crystal Blue, Crystal Black, Solid Light Blue, Solid White, and Solid Pink.

title: K3
content:
About
K3 is the budget entry in MagicYoYo's K-series, with an elegant rounded V-shape body. Distinct from the previously catalogued K3 Aurora-P variant.

title: K3 Aurora-P
content: About the K3 Aurora-PThe K3 Aurora-P is a wide-body ABS plastic with a smooth bowl shape for a comfortable catch and a built-in fingerspin dimple for learning finger spin tricks. It includes both responsive and unresponsive bearings for a full progressive learning path. High-impact ABS construction handles the drops common in beginner play. The "Aurora-P" name distinguishes it from the metal Y02 Aurora model. Available in Blue/White and other colorways.

title: K5 Night Angle
content: About the K5 Night AngleThe K5 Night Angle is a slightly undersized, narrow step-round aluminum yo-yo featuring POM weight ring elements and one of MagicYoYo's most distinctive aesthetics: a clock-face graphic printed on each side. The 8-ball gold bearing and shining anodized finish give it a premium feel at a budget price. Plays fast and smooth with good rim weighting for its size.

title: K6 Bronze Saints
content: About the K6 Bronze SaintsThe K6 Bronze Saints is a compact butterfly-profile aluminum yo-yo with hubstacks for pinwheel and gyroscopic trick variations. Features a gold-plated 8-ball bearing and yellow silicone response. More compact than most K-series models at 52.98mm, with POM elements integrated into the design. Named with the martial/fantasy theme common to early MagicYoYo branding.

title: K7 Lightspeed
content: About the K7 LightspeedThe K7 Lightspeed is an aluminum-and-plastic hybrid yo-yo with a larger 56.52mm diameter for a forgiving catch zone. A slim bearing keeps it responsive for beginners learning basic throw technique and returns. One of MagicYoYo's more affordable entry-level hybrid models, bridging plastic and metal construction.

title: K8 Leopard
content: About the K8 LeopardThe K8 Leopard is an oversized butterfly-shaped hybrid aluminum/plastic yo-yo with a 59.51mm diameter that creates a very generous catch zone. Pronounced rims concentrate weight toward the outer edges for stability and spin time. Inverse-round profile for comfortable play. Unresponsive; bind required. A 10-ball bearing provides smooth, long spin. Available in multiple colorways.

title: K9 The King
content: About the K9 The KingReleased in 2014, the K9 The King is an H-profile aluminum yo-yo with flat hubstacks that allow players to place a finger directly on the hub for gyroscopic and pinwheel tricks. A 10-ball bearing and silicone pad response provide smooth unresponsive play. One of MagicYoYo's definitive hubstack models of the mid-2010s. Available in Gold+Blue, Cyan/White, and other colorways.

title: Kagerou
content: AboutThe Kagerou is Japan Technology's flagship bimetal, built on the Mirage shape with a thick and heavy stainless steel outer ring. JT designed it to combine powerful spin power and stability from the ring weight with a quick, light design feel — spin power without sacrificing speed. Players are advised to inspect strings frequently as colored steel rims may show minor blemishes with use. Special editions include a sOMEThING collaboration colorway (Brown), a Kohei Nishimura Edition (Gray/Black Ring), and an Unknown Edition.

title: Kagerou ’24
content: AboutThe Kagerou '24 is the updated bimetal flagship, evolved for the modern competitive scene. Width expanded approximately 2mm and weight increased over the original, with widened stainless steel rims that provide exceptional visibility of the yo-yo's position in play and deliver enhanced stability. Available in Royal Blue/Raw Ring, Red/Raw Ring, Matte Green/Gold Rim, Matte Hot Pink/Gold Rim, and Shiny Black/Rainbow Rim.

title: Kainer
content: AboutThe Kainer was developed as a sibling and successor to the original Kamui through rigorous testing. Its response system uses 19.6mm Joker Pads with Type80 pads included for players preferring weaker response. The design was refined specifically for grinding and regeneration combos in competitive 4A freestyle.

title: Kaiser
content: About KaiserThe Kaiser is a solid 6061 aluminum yo-yo built for competition and serious play. Known for consistent spin, stable flight, and responsive tricks.

title: Kaizoku
content:
From Sleeper:

"The Kaizoku yoyo, a perfect way to help support me while getting something in return as well! It's used in all my current tutorials so you can see what it's made of 💪🏼.

As well as supporting 2 of the artists who helped make this possible! The artist of the design is my good friend sheep.

And Kaiga Marine, another talented artist who helped make the engraving for this yoyo possible!

title: Kamui
content: AboutThe Kamui was Japan Technology's debut model, released in 2009. Machined from a solid block of Delrin rather than injection-molded, it eliminated seams and delivered metal-like smoothness in an offstring throw — unprecedented for its era. One of the most expensive 4A yo-yos of the time, it established JT's reputation for precision-engineered offstring performance.

title: Kamui Wide
content: AboutThe Kamui Wide is a 2019 renewal of JT's original Kamui in polycarbonate/ABS plastic. It adds approximately 10mm of catch zone width over its predecessor and was designed to be accessible to all skill levels — bouncing high with minimal required force. Available in Clear Blue, Clear Red, Deep Purple, Clear Orange, Clear Green, and additional colorways.

title: Kamuraiju
content:
From One Drop:

"The Kamaraiju is the signature yo-yo of team player Daiju Okamura. This is his description of how the yo-yo came to be:

'I designed this yo-yo so that it would be optimal when performing Skin the Gerbil. Taking inspiration from older One Drops like the Project, the Kuntosh and the Summit, I adopted the flat rim. This is a One Drop yo-yo after all! This choice wasn’t only about making a statement, but also to create an easy grip when holding and a unique feeling during play.  Of course I really like the way it looks.

I recommend throwing the Kamuraiju with a light touch. For me, throwing it with less force than usual really suits the way I play. I just want to take it easy. However, this yo-yo is designed so that you can throw it powerfully and you'll be able to do the same tricks, so use it at full power if you feel that is what you need.

My setup is Flat Caps, 10Ball Bearing and Flow Groove pad which all come standard in the box.  For string I use Cirrus Foam or Kitty Fat but it will ship with one One Drop basics string. Choose the string that works best for you.

For the box design, I used the kanji symbol "寿(Kotobuki)" that is used in my name. This kanji character means something like “Best Wishes” or “Long Life” and it is used frequently around New Years time. I give you Kotobuki and many thanks for supporting my signature yo-yo and I hope you really like it.'"

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blER00ddrR4

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)
meta.yya_weight: 61.20g (64.55g with aluminum Flat Cap Side Effects)

title: Kanto
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Our goal was to take a sub optimal shape for performance, and fuse as much performance into it as we can. It’s been given the nickname “Slimline Draupnir” by those who have been able to try it because of its unique play experience.

To avoid packing on endless rim weight, we decided to design the Kanto around the idea of making the weight, diameter and width add up to 151 as a tribute to the original 151 pokemon, and with 6061 aluminum to make it affordable for everyone. This made us get creative with the shape and design of the yoyo, most specifically with the schmoove groove portion of the profile. A tiny “bump” at the edge of the schmoove acts as another way to reduce tilting friction and keep the string centered with a comfy organic shape that is just so fun to play!"

title: Karasu
content:
History / About
The Karasu is the first yo-yo maker Lewi (forum handle Herelieslewi / "Lewiii") took to a real, if small, production run. Designed around 2021 and first shown publicly on the YoYoExpert forums in February 2022, it went through a purple prototype phase and a community color poll before the production run shipped in blue. Units were sold in small, informal batches directly through forum Buy/Sell/Trade threads rather than any retail storefront; Lewi tracked remaining stock down to single digits before selling out, and it has since circulated on the secondary market.

title: Karma
content: About the KarmaThe Karma is YoYoJam's second full-metal yo-yo to use a midship brass weight ring, sharing the Phenom's concept in an undersized aluminum body. Unlike the Phenom, it omits the mirror caps for a cleaner aesthetic. Its round body shape and compact 50.8mm diameter make it a collectible for players who prefer undersized full-metal throws.

title: Kasm
content:
Layer Infinity's second, most well-known, and loved release is the Kasm, a 3D-printed slimline return top designed for modern responsive (0A) play.

Dexter Edition

Dexter is a member of Team Layer Infinity...and also a cat. Dexter also has his own special edition of the Kasm, with caps featuring a "sleepy" Dexter, and "playful" Dexter on each side.

title: Katana 2
content: About the Katana 2The Katana 2 is the second MagicYoYo × SpinGear collaboration, redesigned from the original M06 Katana. At 62.2g it is lighter than the original while concentrating more weight in the stainless steel rims for a stronger spin. A V-shaped profile replaces the original's H-shape, with a small hub protrusion for extended axle thread durability. Updated logo design. Available via SpinGear and select specialty retailers.

title: Katharsis
content:
The following is archived from ILYY:

This yoyo is dedicated to everyone getting told they don’t belong. Because of how they look. Because of what they wear and who they love. Because of how they feel and who they want to be. Because of how they express themselves. You do matter. You do belong. You are not alone. You are strong and beautiful. Just the way you are.

In 2010, when budget mono metals were quite popular, we cooked up the Void filling a gap in our portfolio. With its basic angular design it was easy to machine and thus yielded a good A-grade ratio, very important back in the day, when a scrapped yoyo run would mean ruin to the business. But beside the engineering and economical aspects, it played surprisingly well. Inherent to this basic shape is a magic formula that just works perfectly for a yoyo. This can be seen on many well-regarded yoyos with such designs from the Draupnir to the Peregrine X.

It was time to again tap into this magic sauce and create a yoyo to clear the mind from daily stress and burden. A yoyo to immerse the player into the joy of this hobby without compromise and to feel re-newed and happy. We achieved Katharsis.

Katharsis inherits its overall body shape from the Void but adding modernized elements like low-walls, increased width, less weight, bi-metal construction and the ILYY fingerspin cup finished in a beautiful yet still moderate acid wash anodization.

The blasted and plated stainless steel rings are machined thin yet wide to maximize their mass moment of inertia. The rimweight is carefully chosen to offer massive spintime while still retaining snappy un- and rewinds. The increased width allowed us to push the rimweight even further than with the Numen while still keeping balance between inertia and RPM. The rings flare out making the cup diameter as large possible for easier fingerspin catches. This design gives Katharsis an aesthetically pleasing calm and airy appearance further adding to the concept. There are no unnecessary curves or slopes with Katharsis, just pure function doing its thing.

Katharsis is the new top performer in the ILYY line-up with unmatched spintimes and stability. Its 50mm width offers a large catch zone for modern meta while still being able to move through tighter technical maneuvers.

title: Kawa
content: AboutThe Kawa (川 — "River" in Japanese) is JIGUN's first offstring (4A) yo-yo, released in 2024. An oversized POM body with a Size D bearing for enhanced regeneration stability, it was priced at $55. Available in White/Blue Core, White/Silver Core, and Yellow/Black Core colorways.

title: KE
content:
History / About
KE is a titanium casual/daily-use monometal released November 6, 2025, designed personally by YYR's own representative (founder).

title: Kenshin
content:
The Kenshin is the first yo-yo ever made of the 7068 aluminum alloy.

From YoYoExpert:

"Uesugi Kenshin was a pioneer and one of the most powerful lords of the Sengoku period remembered for his prowess on the battlefield and famed for his honourable conduct and military expertise.

Sengoku, tasked with creating a yo-yo unique and powerful enough to live up to the Kenshin name, sought out a completely new alloy to create their latest design - 7068 Aluminum. 7068 Aluminum is an amazingly strong Aluminum alloy that actually has a better weight/strength ratio than grade 5 Titanium! This allows for weight distribution that feels similar to Titanium without the crazy Ti price tag.

The Kenshin is the first mono-metal yo-yo Sengoku has made and it fits perfectly in their lineup alongside all the high performance multi-metal designs. It plays fast, stable, and has a light presence on the string. Comfortable in the hand with a feel that just begs you to keep throwing, the Kenshin is a serious game changer!"

title: Kenshin Kiwami
content:
From Rewind Worldwide:

"Based on the Kenshin, with an undeniable power-up thanks to its bimetal design!

Based on Sengoku's monometal Kenshin, with the addition of a stainless steel outer rim, it has exactly the effect you'd expect: a major power-up in speed and stability.

The major point is "acceleration," which is especially felt at first throw and the moment you mount the string, but put on just a little speed and the smoothness will amaze you. The playfeel is very light and nimble, and can move quickly at your slightest command.

The actual weight is only 63 grams, making it a lightweight model to begin with with the deliberate decision to use the slightly less-dense 6061 aluminum body, to shave a wee bit of mass from the body, concentrating more force in to the weight ring. This is a great reliable throw."

title: Euler
content: AboutThe Euler is KenTech's debut and only original release, designed by founder Ken Luo in 2015. A compact bimetal throw with 6061 aluminum body and stainless steel rims, the Euler achieves exceptional spin stability and extended spin time at an unusually low body weight of 62.8g. The stainless steel rims concentrate mass at the outer edge without adding bulk, enabling precise maneuverability for 3A and fast 1A play. Priced at $229.99 and limited to a single US-manufactured run, the Euler sold out quickly and has been near-impossible to find at retail since. KenTech accompanied the launch with a "Technology For Champions" incentive: $500 to any US National Champion and $1,000 to any World Champion who won using a KenTech throw. Colorways: Black, Acid Wash (Blue/Yellow).

title: Euler (Yoku YoYo Design)
content: AboutThe Yoku YoYo Design edition of the Euler is a 2018 collaboration reissue of Ken Luo's 2015 design, produced in China and distributed by Yo-Yo Store REWIND. Slightly smaller in diameter (52.62mm vs 53.3mm) and marginally heavier (63.9g vs 62.8g) than the original, the reissue brings the Euler design to a wider audience at $69.99 — a significant reduction from the original's $229.99. Available in Black/Black Rim and four splash colorways: Yellow/Black/Purple, Orange/Blue/Black, Purple/Silver, and Light Blue/Yellow.

title: KEY – INHYEOKCHOI DAY
content:
About
The KEY - INHYEOKCHOI DAY is a collaboration between "alternatives" and South Korean artist In Hyeok Choi (@inhychoi), created as a token of appreciation for Karthik Devaraj. The DAY edition features a full-blast finish on both the aluminium body and both stainless steel rims, adding 0.1g over the standard KEY. $160.

title: KEY – INHYEOKCHOI NIGHT
content:
About
The KEY - INHYEOKCHOI NIGHT is arguably the rarest release in the "alternatives" catalogue: only four units exist. Created for Singapore Nationals 2025 as a collaboration with artist In Hyeok Choi (@inhychoi). One unit was made available through the website at an undisclosed time. $175.

title: Keyhole
content:
Interested 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: Keyhole Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a doorknob shaped yo-yo, it actually plays very well, and is surprising for it's shape. 

It is a challenging print and you will need a well tuned printer and you may need to do a temperature tower first to ensure you have the right temp for the overhangs. It took me a few failures before I got the overhang right. Settings that helped me succeed:

Enable dynamic overhang speeds

Slow perimeters (30 mm/s)

Extra perimeters on overhangs

Avoid crossing curled overhangs

Detect bridging perimeters

I included a 3mf file for MK4S MMU3 that has these settings in it for those with that printer. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/41RypW. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. If you want it to work well slice it to 54-60 grams weight. Honeycomb or cubic infill for best balance."

title: KG
content:
History / About
KG is the casual-line signature of Kensuke Goto, manager of Yoyo Shop NEST and a longtime YYR veteran, released July 18, 2026.

title: Khuno
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We released the Cloudberry, our first model ever, exactly year ago in September 2020. The original concept for the Fruitbowl Line, which the Cloudberry kickstarted, was to us something of a design study in the organic genre and what play experiences they would yield based on dimensional tweaks.

For our sophomore year, we’ve been looking to take a little bit of a different direction. A Season II of sorts. We’re still going to be working on organic designs, whether released under the Fruitbowl Line or not, but Year Two will feature us pursuing a distinct design angle under our Weatherman Line.

As the debut design of this line, we’re very proud to introduce the Khuno.

SPECS

dia 57.0mmwid 48.3mmbase weight with AL Ultra Lights 63.5g, (maximum stock weight of 71.7g)material 7068 AL · SSincludes AL Ultra Light SEs, Brass Ultra Light SEs, and blank Duncan caps

This is the first non-organic we’ve released. W shapes have been a space we’ve been interested in a long time. Personally, I find them a bit more intriguing than the pure V-profiles that generally occupy the competitive, performance-oriented space. Part of this is due to my experience with incredibly made W-shape throws – some of the best instances of these throws, in my opinion, are made by the elder statesmen of the return top design game. Zach Gormley’s Arctic Circle line and Mark Mangarin’s Akita by CLYW, the Kuntosh by One Drop, and the Summit by the two companies top my private list. One Drop’s Sugar Glider is also a sleeper winner that I feel is confusingly underrated.

These Ws offer the performance edges of a more competitive profile, but retain the comfort and feel of rounder shapes.

This was our first prototype of the Khuno.

The base concept we began with was that of a customisable, competitive W-shaped return top. The foundation of this concept centers on the view that player preferences on competitive features are not so monolithic, and that variability – a feature usually reserved for more casual designs – is favourable even in the performance space.

Having sufficient power is a given, but there is less of a consensus when it comes to weight and feel. One might perceive the general narrative to favour the floatier and lighter of designs, but there is fair presence of those who prefer a heftier ride.

I got to know Thawhir Iqbal, Singapore’s and Asia’s 3A champion, when I was working on the Gravity project, and his feedback on my designs and early prototypes have been illuminating.

The first time we met, he opted for the heavier of the few Gravities I brought to the shoot, and at a later session commented he felt the Khuno prototype (then outfitted with Aluminium Ultra Lights) was too light.

His preference is for throws in the 67g-69g range; he feels that the extra weight compensates for stage nerves. His experience has been that when a player is nervous, his jitters can make everything feel lighter, flimsier, harder to control.

Light and agile can be enjoyable in a casual setting, but the additional mass can be anchoring, grounding, when a player is competing on stage. He gestured towards the Turning Point Mustang ES as reference, his choice for competitions, which comes in at 68.7g.

The moonshot for us was to create a Side Effects-compatible bimetal, which would ideally combine high performance with the freedom to switch things up. The hope with the Khuno is that wherever your play preferences lie on that spectrum, its customisability gives you control to dictate your preferred feel on the string.

(Prototype I on left, Prototype II on right)

The initial prototype came back playing great, but had a few setbacks we had to address.

At its lightest setup, it was agile and had a nice floaty signature. At the same time, it lacked the aggressive power we felt necessary for a performance-focused concept. The curved ridge that bridges the inner wall and outer rims also made it slightly sharp on the catch.

For Prototype II, we added a touch of rim weight in the stainless steel rings, tweaked the mid weight in the aluminium body, filled out the curved ridge into a graduated slope, and rounded some edges. The new profile feels significantly better in the hand and has a nice, full presence on its spin.

One challenge of creating a Side Effects-compatible bimetal is in allowing for a meaningful range of weight while preserving sufficient mass in its stainless steel rims.

In other words, its lightest and heaviest configurations have to be actual playable weights. If the lightest configuration starts at 65g, it doesn’t leave much room in the upper ends of the weight spectrum for using other Side Effects or weights – it gets too heavy too quickly. Reducing too much overall mass to achieve a light frame (reduction is most efficient in the stainless steel rings, given its density) is not a solution either; to fulfil its concept, the lightest configuration of the Khuno still has to play like a bimetal.

This wasn’t easy for a throw with a 57mm * 48.3mm frame, but 7068 AL allows us to creative things with wall thickness and where we apportion weight. We ended up with a base weight of 58.8g for the gutless halves.

At its lightest, the Khuno comes in at 63.5g when fitted with Aluminium Ultra Lights. That mass is distributed over a relatively large and wide frame, and moves easy. It glides through string elegantly. This is the setup that will likely come stock.

We are also including Brass Ultra Lights to give users the option of adding more center-weight without having to purchase another set of SEs; this clocks a medium mass of 66.2g. The additional center mass gives you a bit more zip without slowing things down too much – a setup great for denser, more deliberate tech, I think.

The kicker is that the Khuno also accepts Freehand caps. The polycarbonate caps add roughly 5.5g – along with Aluminium Ultra Lights, the Khuno comes in at around 69g. This set up is an absolute beast in stability and power without being sluggish, and is reminiscent to me of the original YYF Severe. The white Duncan caps are an aesthetic I really appreciate – it calls back to early Freehand prototypes, which were fitted with the same blank white caps.

(Of course, the last permutation that is available stock is combines the Brass ULs with caps, which puts it at a slightly intimidating 71.7g. For those who need a bit more torque than the average player, this is available to you. Fair warning – it is slightly animalistic.)

These are configurations that are available out of box.

One technical difficulty to overcome in producing the Khuno was the possibility of vibe. Given that Side Effect axles are moving parts secured by a precise fit, SE throws can be more susceptible to vibe in comparison to tapped axles. The challenge is compounded by the addition of stainless steel rims, which are yet another independent component, secured by way of press fit, to the whole of a spinning body.

Given these considerations, the balance of mass and tolerances were areas we gave careful attention to. We are also using the famed Yoyorecreation NSK Platinum DS bearings in each Khuno. They are held to higher tolerances in manufacturing – the more precise fit with the bearing post allows for a smoother ride. If you’ve been around, you’ll know that the Khuno is fitted with top-of-line parts.

We hand-tune each Khuno for smooth play before we send them out, but as it is with any Side Effects throw, players should expect that some degree of tuning is part of the game.

The product of months of designing, prototyping, testing and iterating is Atmos’ first non-organic, customisable beast of a throw that caters to any of your preferences in performance play. We’re excited for you to meet this guy.

Thank you for reading! We’d love to know what you think.

·

As far as we know, this is also the first Side Effects bimetal to be made, but let us know if we missed a prior design.

·

Special thanks to Elvin of RSO for kind help rendered on this project. We’re happy to announce that the Khuno will come with Landing Pads, which we feel are some of the best in the field right now. Also, each Khuno will come with the same SE removal tool that we included with the Gravity.
