title: Kickflip (Prototype)
content:
About
Kickflip was a monthly Project Torsion blend from Throw-Yo Threads, offered only to Patreon subscribers in December 2025. No public retail release has been confirmed.

title: KickSide
content: About the KickSideThe KickSide is one of YoYoJam's most enduring plastic designs, featuring a Butterfly profile that balances accessibility with respectable performance. The hybrid response allows players to experience both responsive and semi-unresponsive play, making it a natural stepping stone. Its Celcon construction makes it durable enough to withstand the drops of developing players.

title: KILL SHOT
content: About the KILL SHOTThe KILL SHOT pushes outer-rim weighting to its extreme: an extra-thick stainless steel ring extends outward to form the body's actual outer edge profile, maximizing momentum and spin. "Impressive control in play" for advanced string trick sequences. Available in Pink with Black Rims, Yellow with Silver Rims, and Black with Silver Rims (Blasted). $209.99 USD.

title: Kinetic
content:
From Motion:

"After what we would consider two successful yoyo releases we are super stoked to dive even deeper into the “performance aspect” of throwing. Like the last two models we released, you will be more than pleased with the aesthetic and performance of this yoyo.

Immediately recognizable is the sunken dome that we intend to carry through our product line. We integrated very distinctive grooves to imitate a visual of sound waves moving across the cup of the yoyo.

One thing we always want to offer is a unique experience with each yoyo. You will find a really exclusive rim design that not only visually catches your eye, but also pushes the limits once again on molding stainless steel onto a 7068 aluminum body.

So why a V shape?

To be completely honest - we wanted a yoyo that was a no compromise, true V. It doesn’t seem to be common anymore for us to see a straight V yoyo come out of any of the shops. We are unsure exactly what the reasoning is behind that considering that we feel as if you can’t get this much performance out of any other shape.

The design we went for here is to pack in as much performance as we could. We kept the weight low, the power high, and the weight distribution highly pushed to the outer rims. The V shape allows for a gradual ramp up of weight across the body of the yoyo, while being strategic in the amount of material we leave between the catch zone and the outer rim.

You will find that Kinetic will rival any existing YoYo that finds itself in the performance category. Once again we raise the bar - this is Motion. "

60 Made in 4 colors:

15 - Moose Blue

15 - Winter's Heart

15 - Adeline's Ruby

15 - Molten Merlot

title: Kinetics Crash
content: History / AboutDistinct C3 Crash-family retail release with compact diameter and moderately wide competition profile.

title: King Sago
content:
From TRT:

"Is 65g too light for you? That’s ok, float isn’t for everyone! Weighing in at a solid 68.3g, exuding stability and spin power for eons, presenting the King Sago.

The King’s identical 7068 cups are crowned with rims of raw brass instead of stainless steel to increase the overall weight and performance of this royal edition of the Sago.

Classy competition ready.

Are you ready to kick it with the King?"

Colorways

The King Sago is currently only available green with brass rims.

What's in the Box

Each King Sago comes in a hand-stamped, numbered box, making every piece feel special. Included with the yo-yo is a Zipline ZS Air 100% nylon string, a TRT sticker, and a TRT Series #4 POG.

title: Kiss Side Effects
content:
Kisses are available in:

Titanium

Kisses are one of 4 different Side Effects to be made in Titanium by Brian Fellhoelter. They are made of Grade 5 Titanium, and 25 sets of each were made.

title: K!T
content: About the K!TReleased December 2013, the K!T (also written KIT) was King Yo Star's first model machined from 7075 aluminum. Designed with input from Chinese players He Jiajie and Tan Chang, it was reviewed as fast, smooth, and fairly stable. Promoted by Luckey Li, Zhao Chen, Jason Liu, and Rocks Tan. A wide gap was noted to produce loose binds with stock pads — reviewers recommended tighter response. Review scores: Stability 4/5, Smoothness 5/5, Response 2/5.

title: Kitchener 99
content: HistoryThe Kitchener 99 was a professional-grade wooden yo-yo, named after the company's home city of Kitchener, Ontario. Produced in the 1950s–60s as a premium offering.

title: Kitchener Knobs
content: HistoryThe Kitchener Knobs was Cheerio's original product, manufactured by Kitchener Buttons Limited starting in 1931. Made from wood with simple turned knobs, it represents early Canadian yo-yo manufacturing.

title: Klassm
content:
From Layer Infinity:

"Klassm is a hybrid bi-plastic modern responsive return top. The body is made of machined polycarbonate, and the caps are 3D printed with PLA.

Klassm is the result of combining two of Layer Infinity's iconic responsive return tops: Kasm and Classic. The profile is the same as Kasm, while the caps are identical and interchangeable with Classic. See here for a three-part series on how this was developed: Part 1, part 2, part 3.

Comes with Kasm's bearing locks that stop the bearing from spinning to allow for fixed axle mode. Also compatible with everything in the Kasm parts kit."

title: Dyna-Glo
content: History / AboutDyna-Glo was made by L.H. Knibb Co. of Chicago; the company was founded by inventor Leroy Hayes Knibb, and the YoYo Wiki lists the Dyna-Glo as the only model known to survive. GlowYoYo.com says it is believed to be one of the world's first glow-in-the-dark yo-yos, though the Corey Games Glo-Yo may have reached market up to five years earlier. The packaging read "Glows Red by Day, Blue by Night" and claimed it was "dynamically powered and balanced with steel rings for high speeds"; it sold for 49 cents. GlowYoYo.com dates it to 1952 and measures 57.4 mm diameter, 32.8 mm width and 43.9 g. The Yo-Yo Museum, which lists it as the Knibb Dyna-Glo Top, shows a plastic body with metal axle and separate glow sections embedded in the outer shell, in pink, glow, orange and blue; the museum is unsure of the date and gives 1958.

title: Dyna-Glo (Script Logo)
content: History / AboutGlowYoYo.com describes this as the rare Knibb Dyna-Glo featuring the script Knibb logo; its pale pink coloring distinguishes it from the brighter red plastic of the non-script version. The tent-card display packaging reads "Dynamically Powered. The Fastest Spinning Top of All - It Glows... Day or Night..." A Playthings trade-publication advertisement shows an early version with script lettering and the word "Disc" instead of "Top". GlowYoYo.com lists 1952, 57.4 mm diameter, 32.8 mm width and 43.9 g.

title: Knok
content:
About
Knok pairs a small diameter with a round, easy-grip shape for a catch that feels like it absorbs into your hand.

title: KnuckleYo
content:
From ZGRT:

"We have a tendency in wanting to turn everything we see into a yoyo. Some ideas from this tendency are, of course, kind of crazy but some others are kind of cool. One day, having this obsession in mind while looking at a knuckle roller, we asked ourselves our typical initial question: what if…

And here it is the KnuckleYo.

The KnuckleYo pushed our very own limits in creating a knuckle roller that is capable in turning into a yoyo—hmmm we are not sure now if it was the other way around: a yoyo that is capable in turning into a knuckle roller?

The initial challenge we hit right away was the weight and dimensions the KnuckleYo needed to have in other to be functional as a yoyo and as a knuckle roller. We played around with different dimensions, shapes and materials. Some worked perfectly, some just did not such as Titanium. One of prototypes we made out of titanium did not perform the best as a yoyo. The limitations of the dimensions and its density did not play well.

For such reasons, we ended up using only Stainless Steel, Brass and Copper. All of them have similar densities but different enough to have a different weight distribution for each material. In other words, although the weight is the pretty much the same, each material variation has a slightly different weight distribution.

The other challenge we had was in the designing part. We wanted to have thin walls with thick rims but the size of the cup prevented to use standard tooling. This of course led us to work with the machinist and create customized tooling.

The initial idea was to accommodate begleri as part of the features by using a 275 paracord that fit the M4 hole size no problem. It worked perfectly. The problem we had was that the axle was going through the cup side making the yoyo assembly a little bit frustrating. For such reason we ended up adding a stop to prevent the axle to go to the side of the cup, but that reduced the diameter of the ending part of the axle hole. For such reason, a <2mm diameter paracord could do the trick to turn the KnuckleYo in begleri.

For the engine of the yoyo, we did not want to use a mini bearing. We wanted instead to use a a bearing size that had a good performance and that was easy to find out there in the market. At the same time, we wanted the bearing to be concave to some how reduce the friction of the string with the pads. We ended up choosing an A size bearing and customized pads to properly fit the bearing and yoyo dimensions—by the way, our Throw Key (not included) can also remove this bearing if it gets stuck ;)

Playing with a mini yoyo is challenging. This is not the exception but definitely has great stability to perform complex tricks and to improve your yoyo accuracy. One element that definitely is key with this throw is the string, we tested several combinations in terms of materials, length and thickness along with Zipline to find the perfect match that suited the KnuckleYo not only from the performance perspective, but also from the winding up and binding perspectives.When not in yoyo mode, you can toss it in your pocket and start using it as a knuckle roller practically anywhere yo go.

This project made us connecting with different people with different skills to test the prototypes and to receive feedback after testing them. We would like to thank them all for their time and extraordinary response that helped us to develop this project.

As we always say, let nothing hold you down."

title: Koi
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"KOI showcases a different side of yoyofriends by focusing on flow and feel. It has an overall organic shape that still packs performance. KOI has an optimized center/rim weight distribution to give a relaxed experience when throwing normally. It also has optimized power and acceleration to handle all the tricks when pushed. KOI is the everyday carry that gives users a fun and pleasant experience no matter the situation."

title: Komodo
content:
History / About
The Komodo is the signature model of Recess team member Ahmad Kharisma, the Indonesian National Champion. Described by Recess as made "for fun play and that's it," it represents a more playful direction compared to the competition-focused Diplomat and Weekend. The 7075 aluminum construction gives it durability and a premium feel. Ahmad was also a key player in the Recess Vacation promotional videos (Singapore and California content). The Komodo's mid-size dimensions (54mm diameter) give it a nimble, compact character suited to Ahmad's style.

title: Kraken
content:
From One Drop:

"We are proud to be expanding our amazing partnership with independent game studio Re-Logic once again by bringing another yo-yo from the game of Terraria into reality: The Kraken.

As the name suggests, the Kraken is monstrous. Equipped with a beefy body and 60mm diameter, the Kraken is our largest yo-yo to date. With it's 1/200 drop rate in the game, only a handful of players all over the world can say they've tamed the beast. Be on your A-Game, because the Kraken demands constant control and finesse. If you fumble a bit during play, it'll come biting. Don't fret though, pick yourself up and go at it again. No one said it was going to be easy. You could call it an "H" shape but the transitions are so soft and bulbous that it kind of defies a label like this. Just because it's a beast, doesn't mean it's going to feel like a rock during play; strangely, almost magically, it feels agile and light.

In Terraria, the Kraken has "infinite spin". We honestly didn't think it'd be fair to other yo-yo companies to apply the "infinite spin" modifier to the real life Kraken, so we gave it just enough spin for you to pull off your favorite tricks.

While the virtual Kraken can only be found in a post-Plantera dungeon, the real world Kraken will be relatively easy to track down and in many of the colorways you've all come to love on the Terrarian, as well as a handful of new ones!

Hidden away from the world for far too long, we think it's time to finally release the Kraken!"

title: Kraken (Prototype)
content:
About
The Kraken V1 was a prototype from a G Squared Yoyos project with YYWS that never worked out. G2 described it as Marvel-inspired and a bit on the heavier side. Leftover stock was sold in a January 30, 2019 prototype drop.

title: Krapfen
content:
From ILYY:

"After successfully reviving some of our older designs we felt it was time to unleash something new and fresh for the ILYY line-up. Going through our models we realized there was no full-sized, medium width entry.

Full-size yoyos with a slimmer profile below 40mm always feel special when throwing them around. They ooze some kind of easiness and relaxing energy that wider yoyos usually lack.

It is named after a beloved German pastry, a jelly-donut without a center hole. Why? Simply because everyone who tried a Krapfen falls in love with it.

For our entry into this range we wanted something very ILYY-like that encapsulates our design language and philosophy in terms of playing style and understatement. We thus went with a very comfortable organic shape that inherits some of the Lio’s mojo but adds its own aesthetic style. We also decided this new yoyo should have a fade anodization, never seen before on an ILYY, but with grace and class. The Krapfen combines a fresh design with known and loved ILYY-aesthetics.

Weight was kept fairly low for the Krapfen at 62g due to the more compact design. It feels just right when throwing. With its beefy rims and carefully placed mass, the Krapfen is a great performer with plenty of spin time and power while still keeping the great feeling of easiness alive. We noticed a surprising effect when giving the Krapfen a few hours of undivided attention. It feels like becoming a standard issue of a yoyo. Something that would sit in an institute of standards. A yoyo that is used to compare bearings, pads etc."

Initial Run

The initial run of the Krapfen came out in February 2023. 39 Red/Orange fade colorways with Soda Blasted finish were made.

2nd Run

The second run of the Krafen arrived in December 2023. This time 39 yo-yos were made with a Rosé/Blue fade and a Soda Blasted finish.

title: Krown
content: Designed with Shinya Kido less than a month before the Japan National contest, the original Krown became one of the best-selling competition yo-yos of all time and launched C3 onto the global stage. Its design philosophy centered on three points: power, stability, and control. The release triggered a wave of Krown variants across the following decade.Machined from high-grade aluminum and anodized in-house by C3. Multiple colorways. The Krown series includes: Krown (2013), Krown 2019 reissue, Krown 7075, Krown.st bi-metal (2015), Krown.wst wide bi-metal, Krown Ti (titanium), Mini Krown, Krown 7068. Price: ~$85–$95 original; $64.99 on reissue.

title: Krown (2019 Reissue)
content: A redesigned reissue of the iconic Krown. Shinya Kido and C3 updated the dimensions and weight distribution while preserving what players loved about the original. Machined from 6061 aluminum and anodized in-house. More accessible price than original. Price: $64.99.

title: Krown 7075
content: The Krown in 7075 high-grade aluminum — a monometal variant offering a lighter, faster competition throw in the iconic Krown shape. Signature: Shinya Kido.

title: Krown.st
content: The bi-metal evolution of the original 2013 Krown, developed through years of player feedback. Stainless steel outer ring designed with a rounder shape without sharp edges. "Feels light and strong, with a strong sense of explosion and speed while spinning." Not easy to get out of control during high-speed rail combos.Multiple editions produced over the years including Krown.st 7068 (limited), Krown.st Shion Araya, Krown.st Kouhei Edition, Krown.st Limited Black. Price: $119.99.

title: Krown.st 7068
content: History / AboutRetail material revision of the Krown.st platform documented separately by Rewind.

title: Krown.st 7075
content: History / AboutRetail Krown.st revision documented separately from the original 6061/stainless model.

title: Krown Ti
content: The Krown executed in pure titanium — the ultimate version of Shinya Kido's iconic signature. Exceptional lightness and premium feel. Signature: Shinya Kido.

title: Krown.tri
content: History / AboutShinya Kido signature combining a 6061 body, functional polycarbonate middle ring, and stainless outer rim.

title: Krown.ws
content: History / AboutA development-stage accident judged important enough for retail production; widened the Krown concept to 48 mm.

title: Krown.wst
content: The wide-style bi-metal evolution of the Krown — expanded width for a massive catch zone and improved string layering capacity while retaining the competition DNA of the original. Signature: Shinya Kido.

title: Küntosh
content:
The Prototypes

There were around 8-10 proto Kuntosh's made. These were the only Kuntosh available Anti-Yo until years later in 2016 when One Drop partnered with Sonny to release finally release a production run of the Kuntosh (see below).

The Production

From One Drop:

"You may have heard whispers coming from the far corners of the internet or backrooms of your yo-yo club about the last(and unreleased) yo-yo from Anti-Yo. Legend has it that Sonny Patrick designed it and One Drop Yo-Yos built it. For years, only 10 of them have been in existence and are highly coveted by their lucky owners. It is rumored to grant it's owner special powers and good luck.

Now, years later, with a push from a powerful underground movement of hardcore yo-yo players, Sonny and One Drop have finally come together to bring you the Küntosh!

Sonny took inspiration from the poster of the Italian sports car he had hanging in his room growing up. The Countach was not comprised of the strictly purposeful lines of a vintage Porsche 911, nor the long sensual arcs of Ferraris of the day. Rather, it had abrupt surfaces and sharp angles that emphasize what we'll have to invent a new term for: 'Squariness". Yet somehow, the end result comes together in a way that you wouldn't expect and it takes your breath away. It just screams performance and of course it lives up to the look. Sonny was bold enough to think he could pull of a similar thing in yo-yo design. Anyone who has been lucky enough to try the Küntosh would tell you that he pulled it off... in a big way. In both aesthetics and performance.

The legend is about to be reality."

title: Küntosh 5000QV
content:
From One Drop:

"In 1985, Lamborghini released a limited version of the Countach. This special edition included a few changes to the body to account for the redesigned and upgraded engine, the addition of four valves per cylinder-quattrovalvole in Italian, gave birth to its name the "Countach 5000 Quattrovalvole" or "5000 QV" for short. We took inspiration from this and made changes with the approval of Sonny Patrick, designer of the original Küntosh and created the Küntosh 5000QV.

From afar, the changes aren't as noticeable without the trained eye of a previous Küntosh rider. There's a subtle groove driving along the rim as it meets up with the profile of the catch zone. It's a little more spacious around the floor of the cup surrounding the Side Effect area. More importantly, the Küntosh 5000QV features a 7075 aluminum alloy body. It's a more dense and heavy alloy than the 6061 aluminum used on the original. The resulting weight of the redesign is lighter on the scales, but this number doesn't really mean much by itself on this screen you're looking at. During play, you'll find the that the 5000QV has more of commanding spin than its older brother. Your handling will improve only if you spend the time to practice. Taking those sharp corners will be a breeze in no time; accelerate at a moments notice. And when you finally have it parked after hours of burning rubber, admire it's beauty and run your hands across the bead blasted finish.

The soul of the original Küntosh still resonates within the 5000QV, it's just going to have a little more horsepower.

First run features Desert Drifter, Racing Red, Streaking Silver and Burnout Blue. There will be 40 of every colorway released with no reruns for all runs."

title: Twin Twirler
content: HistoryYoYo Wiki says the Twin Twirler was introduced in the early 1950s at the New York Toy Fair, after Kusan arranged with the patent holder of a combination yo-yo and spin top. The Yo-Yo Museum notes the inventor was Wallace F. Darden of Springfield, Tennessee, granted US patent 2,614,364 on October 21, 1952. It came in several body styles, sold as the Falcon (finned faces), Flying Eagle (pointed halves) and Bat models. The wiki says they were produced for only two years; the Museum dates the Falcon and Flying Eagle to 1952 and the Bat to 1953-1961, with later versions by Marketoy and Coleman. Kusan was among the first manufacturers to use plastic for yo-yos.

title: Kutex
content: Auldey's flagship model, the Kutex combines an aluminum body with an inner titanium rim for optimal weight distribution. H-profile shape. Smooth matte finish with zero vibe. Supports 1A, 3A, and 5A play.

title: KWK
content:
History / About
KWK is Toru Miyazaki's titanium signature, released November 22, 2025. It inherits its small diameter from YYR's BAE for combo precision, paired with a wide 48mm body for stability.

title: Alph
content: AboutThe Alph was released November 2006 as Kyo's first 7075-aluminum model. Kyle Weems used the same bowtie butterfly profile as the TiPhiter 2, translating the harder and stronger alloy into a more accessible price tier. The flush-mounted Dif-Pads response and serial numbering continued Kyo's precision-manufacturing identity.

title: Cyclotron
content: AboutThe Cyclotron is a collaboration between South African brand Radiyoactive (designer Jaco) and Kyo. Jaco provided the design and Kyle Weems machined all 250 units, each individually serial numbered. Released in a burnt copper color with white accent lines, it was one of the first cross-continental, serialized limited-run collaborations in competitive yo-yo.

title: Death Robot Mg
content: AboutThe Death Robot Mg is the world's first magnesium and dual stainless-steel bi-metal yo-yo, announced April 7, 2016. Kyle Weems chose AZ31B magnesium for the body — aluminum-comparable strength at roughly two-thirds the weight — and 304 stainless steel for the dual rings, thermally fit at approximately 650°F. A ceramic coating protects the magnesium from oxidation while providing a smooth yet textured surface feel. Called "the culmination of over 15 years of yo-yo design experience," it was Kyo's first new production model in over five years at the time of release.

title: DNS
content: AboutThe DNS ("Do Not Stack") is a high-performance precision aluminum yo-yo from Kyo with a wide profile and concave shieldless bearing for unresponsive 1A play. The dual Vapor O-Ring response system and precise machining are consistent with Kyle Weems's manufacturing standards.

title: Immortalis
content: AboutThe Immortalis is Kyle Weems's first commercially sold yo-yo and the founding product of Kyo. A Freehand-inspired machined aluminum butterfly, it shipped in July 2004 — 80 units total, 50 sold through Infinite Illusions in anodized black and red. The hub accepted Duncan Wheels plastic side caps, and the body used standard response pads over a ball bearing axle.

title: Immortalis 2
content: AboutThe Immortalis 2 shipped February 8, 2006 as a second production run of the Metal Worlds Freehand design. Following high demand after the 2005 Worlds sellout, Kyle Weems revised the hub geometry and released this updated version. The machined aluminum Freehand format continued to be suitable for both 1A and 5A play.

title: Metal Worlds Freehand
content: AboutThe Metal Worlds Freehand is a machined aluminum adaptation of the Duncan Freehand, sold by Kyle Weems directly at the 2005 World Yo-Yo Contest in August. Fifty units were sold at Worlds; the remaining inventory moved through Infinite Illusions. High demand led to a follow-up second run, released as the Immortalis 2 with a modified hub design.

title: Phi
content: AboutThe Phi is Kyo's second production model, shipped May 11, 2005. Its geometry was mathematically derived from the golden ratio (φ = 1.618), and its inner concave rim was designed specifically for Inner Ring Grinds — a technique not yet mainstream at the time. The reversible spacer system, an original Kyo innovation, allowed three selectable gap widths. Stock configuration came with Paul Yath's Carbon Fiber Friction Stickers and a large bearing. 150 units were made; 125 sold through Infinite Illusions; all individually serial numbered.

title: Phi 1.618
content: AboutThe Phi 1.618 shipped December 7, 2005 as a refined successor to the original Phi. The teflon finish was dropped in favor of bare aluminum, making it popular for custom powdercoating. The profile was slightly narrowed, and the inner hub wall was thickened to accommodate a recessed response pad mod. A proprietary "super-bearing" with a non-stick coating was included to reduce lock-up risk. 203 units were produced; 200 sold; all serial numbered.

title: Senza Nome
content: AboutThe Senza Nome ("without a name" in Italian) is a precision aluminum yo-yo from Kyo, documented in community discussion around 2012 where it was compared favorably to the Anti-Yo Busin€$$ — a high bar for competition 1A throws of that era. Detailed specifications are not publicly documented.

title: Tinman
content: AboutThe Tinman is the world's first diamond-coated titanium yo-yo, announced in mid-2018. Loosely based on the YoYoJam Hitman profile, it is machined from 6AL4V Grade 5 titanium with an actual diamond coating — not DLC — applied by a U.S. coating company, described as "low friction, very tough, and very pretty." Machining was handled by FPM. The high walls and slightly undersized diameter produce a distinctive audible hum or "sing" during play that became a talking point in community reviews. Priced at $300 USD.

title: TiPhiter
content: AboutThe TiPhiter is only the second titanium yo-yo ever commercially produced and is considered the first highly playable, practical titanium throw in the hobby. Kyle Weems sold all 15 commercial units directly — never through Infinite Illusions — and they sold out within two hours of photos going online. The recessed .555 Dif-Pads response and wide bearing axle made it competitive with the best aluminum throws of its era at three times the price.

title: TiPhiter 2
content: AboutThe TiPhiter 2 is Kyle Weems's second titanium production model, featuring a bowtie butterfly profile that would become the direct template for the 7075-aluminum Alph released later the same year. Production details are not publicly documented.

title: TiRade
content: AboutThe TiRade is a numbered titanium production model from Kyo featuring a slimmer profile than standard competition throws of its era — described as similar to a YoYoFactory 888 but thinner. The Dif-e-Yo KonKave bearing and choice of silicone ring, flowable silicone, or O-ring response gave players flexibility. At least 28 serial numbers are documented in community forum records.

title: Kyoto
content:
History / About
The Kyoto is the second design in a three-part series celebrating Japanese culture and design philosophy, described as “a titanium incarnation of the Fuji.” It features exceptional fluidity and performance with an unusually light, flowing feel despite its 70-gram weight — reportedly playing “like a 64–65g yoyo.”
The design incorporates a W-shaped profile with hub curvature that distributes weight toward mid-zones rather than the rim, creating an “extremely agile and floaty” experience. Its 52.7mm diameter and 45.6mm width provide comfortable, pocketable proportions suited for everyday use while maintaining significant capability and power.

title: L3
content: Designed by Yicheng Luo for competition play. The L3 achieved a historic 4th place finish at the 2008 World Yo-Yo Contest — the best result ever from a Chinese player at that time. Features laser-engraved graphics and is hubstack-compatible. Marked Auldey's transition from clone production to original high-performance engineering.

title: La’Grange
content:
About
The La'Grange is the second yo-yo in Lathed Back Design's mini modular titanium line and the direct successor to the Bangarang. The brand describes it as "the brainchild of a fighter jet and a swiss army knife" — an aerodynamically-tuned, hardened competition platform in a pocket-friendly package. Like the Bangarang, the La'Grange uses a modular rim system: a Delrin competition rim set expands the core to 53mm diameter and 63g total weight, while a Delrin looping rim set yields a 52mm diameter and 59g total for 0A and looping play configurations.
All accessories are cross-compatible with the Bangarang modular system. The La'Grange performs best with thin string for 1A unresponsive play; thick string is recommended for looping configurations. As with all Lathed Back Design products, each colorway was produced in limited runs with in-house anodizing, and Artist's Proof editions feature unique 1-of-1 or short-run custom finishes.
Colorways
Retail colorways included Solar Flare, Berry Magma, Neutron Berry, and Unicorn Puke (via YoYoSam and YoYoExpert). YoYoTricks carried Disco Lemonfade, Flamingo Fade, and Misty Rainbow. Artist's Proof and short-run editions included Cthulhu's Madness (1 of 2), Modders Mayhem! (1 of 1), Cobalt Chaos (1 of 2), Subject 42, 86, and Cloud Chaser.

title: Lab Experiment #1
content:
From One Drop:

"Somewhere along the way during the Dietz development we did a small run of a particular prototype that was later rejected.

This particular version is narrower than a Dietz and weighs a touch more. The catch zone shape is also a bit different. We have 21 numbered but there also about a dozen out there floating around that aren't numbered. We thought it would be cool to make them available as it has quite a different play from the Dietz and makes for a cool collector item."

title: Laevateinn
content: History / AboutDeveloped from P.Wave, Accelerator, and Vanitas dimensions for fast 1A play and accessible bind learning.

title: Laguna
content:
From One Drop:

"Year: 1991City: Laguna BeachLocation: Club Post NuclearMusic: New Beat and Industrial

Laguna Beach is important and special in the history of One Drop because that is where the owners (Shawn and David) met way back in 1991. We happened to both be hanging out at Club Post Nuclear every Friday night and ended up being roommates and friends. It’s fair to say that One Drop started in Laguna Beach. It feels right to honor how this all came to be by calling this new yo-yo the Laguna.

What also started in 1991 was a life long friendship. The idea to start a business together happened not too long after meeting and becoming roommates. It took a decade for it to actually happen and One Drop Design was formed in 2001. We started making yo-yos in 2007. “They” say to not go into business with your friends, and while that is probably generally true, One Drop is fueled by our friendship and it just works. Pretty cool!

The first thing that happened in the design process was that we were able to buy blue Delrin in a reasonable quantity. Normally we can easily get black and white but other colors are usually really expensive and only available in large quantities. We jumped on it.

We made only two Delrin models previously: Cabal and Cabal Gen 2 and it was definitely time for a new model. The goal was to achieve modern specs and proportions without using a weight ring. Because Delrin is less dense than aluminum, it weighs less, so you need more of it to achieve a desirable weight. The first Cabal wasn’t very wide so it had to be really thick to achieve the weight without a ring. By making the Laguna much wider and lighter (10mm wider and 5 grams lighter than the Cabal), we were able to achieve the correct weight without it being overly thick. This also allowed us to push a ton of weight out to the rim.

Our trusty physicist and good friend, Dirty Birdy, crunched the numbers and the Laguna is well into the “Dark Side” which means it has large amounts of rim weight and spins forever. The overall feeling of machined Delrin in your hand is always nostalgic to the old plastic yo-yos, but the performance meets modern expectations. It’s a joy to play."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Laguna 67
content:
About
The Laguna 67 is a heavier, wider Delrin version of One Drop's Laguna, released in August 2026. At 67 grams, it moves more weight out to the rim without the need for a weight ring. It uses One Drop's custom machined insert and hub system ("Cabal Guts") with a 10-ball size C bearing and Flow Groove response, finished in Pyramatte.

meta.yya_axle: Custom machined inserts and hubs, 12mm (Cabal Guts)

title: Authentic
content: History / AboutAuthentic was developed as the first yo-yo of Laid Back Swing (LBS). To launch the brand, the makers wanted the most authentic yo-yo as a flagship, choosing a round, organic shape for the most retro feel from yo-yo history. The theme was "retro and modern", "never gets old to play with" and "blends in with a variety of scenes", refined through repeated prototyping. The artwork was inspired by the word Authentic itself, such as the Ivy League and American baseball.Rewind notes it weighs in the low 63 g range but has a soft yet substantial feel that carries itself, giving a casual play feel; the polish finish can show water-droplet-like color unevenness due to the manufacturing process.

title: Auto Pilot
content: History / AboutAuto Pilot is named for the automatic control system, and as a metaphor for a body that moves on its own or a habitual movement in yo-yoing. LBS says the face is based on a propeller airplane for a nostalgic look. The shop lists it at 6,600 yen, made in China, with a 10-ball concave C-size bearing, in Orange, Clear, Blue, Pink, Purple and Deep Green.

title: Genius
content: History / AboutGenius was developed to convey a soothing feel from the very throw, and is LBS's second flagship yo-yo. Its face design draws on the first flagship Authentic, sampling an American college T-shirt. It was named Genius so a player picking it up thinks "You're a genius!". The Quad Rim lets a 6061 aluminum body be thinner overall and spreads the center of gravity to reduce stress in the throw.

title: Nude Trump
content: History / AboutNude Trump is LBS's second yo-yo, built on the concept of the yo-yo's versatility. It draws on the U.S. Navy custom of bringing playing cards (with nude pictures) to sea, where cards were either played or simply viewed. The different ways to enjoy cards are expressed through two bearings, a flat bearing and a slim (C-minus) bearing, letting the player choose bind or responsive play.Rewind notes the very high edges (high wall) suit regeneration and modern-responsive stall tricks, an unusual advantage among metal yo-yos.

title: Nude Trump Type2
content: History / AboutNude Trump Type 2 is an alternate version of Nude Trump with the same playing-card-culture theme and bind/responsive bearing options. According to Rewind, the Type 2 is slightly heavier with a changed weight distribution, for more stability and a more secure feel during play (64.5 g versus 63.3 g).

title: Pomade
content: History / AboutPomade was developed around items used in daily life: inspired by traditional hair pomade, the team set out to make a yo-yo that looks like a pomade case, in line with the LBS concept of a yo-yo as interior decor. Two artwork designs were prepared, and two included weights plus a dedicated remover let the player adjust balance and feel. It comes with a 19 mm slim pad and a C-size bearing. Colorways at the LBS shop: Moss Green, Polish Black, Blasted Silver and Polish Silver, 11,000 yen.

title: Straight Jacket
content: History / AboutStraight Jacket is a Laid Back Swing x FuzzyEssence collaboration, introduced on the LBS shop as a completely handmade all-leather yo-yo. It is a responsive (return) model, and the shop warns that it may deform under strong force and varies slightly between individual units. Natural color; sold at 9,900 yen.

title: Laika
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: The Laika - Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is another 4mm stainless steel pin axle yo-yo. I use these. Add a drop of thick super glue gel into one axle hole, the axle, a drop in the other side, then press together and let dry. If you want it to work well slice it to 54-60 grams weight. 

I've also included a pocket teacup sized version but it will only work with heavy weight filament such as Proto-Pasta steel filled filament, bronze fill, etc."

title: Lamina
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

The Lamina is the first release in our new Research and Design lineup.

It’s smooth, wide and floaty — but beneath all the fun, the Lamina was crafted as an experimental design study in weight distribution and playfeel.

It comes in two variants: α and β, identical in shape, size, and material — except for its center weight, illuminating how small shifts in mass can transform feel.

SPECS

Diameter 51.9mmWidth 52.9mmWeight [α] 66.8g and [β] 65.5g (Δ = 1.3g center weight)Material 6061 AL

The Lamina was inspired by countless conversations around design theory and how small physical changes can lead to tangible shifts in playfeel. The community is full of these. The most iconic of them centers on the word “floaty” — a term that’s notoriously hard to pin down, not just in how a yoyo plays, but in what physical features might actually produce that sensation.

Designers and manufacturers we admire have chimed in from opposite sides of the aisle — and to us, the absence of conclusive agreement only makes the discourse more compelling.

It’s not straightforward to define playfeel, either. A player’s experience of a design is so subjective that it’s hard to map that objectively onto another person’s expectations. Specifications are also imperfect descriptors here — a 67g model could very reasonably feel like a 64g yoyo. 65g models can feel more reluctant than heavier alternatives. We’ve heard this countless times over our years spent in design and manufacturing.

Over that time, we’ve come to see playfeel more like tasting notes than a spec sheet, where many subjective descriptors (”reluctant”, “zippy”, “agile”, “hang time”) can help to paint an impressionistic picture of an experience. In many of the Design Notes that we’ve published in the past, we’ve tried to bridge that gap — to provide vocabulary of what a design might feel in your hands.

But without some shared baseline — both in language and in experience — it’s hard to map design variables directly to playfeel.

The Lamina was created to address that. Designed intentionally with two variants — α and β — it allows players to feel the difference that a subtle shift in centerweight can make, side by side. It’s also the first release under our Research and Design lineup — a space for experimental, potentially one-off projects and design exploration. As Coleman put it, this is us leaning fully into the “projects” part of Atmos Projects.

Rim weight is a lot more straightforward, and more easily understood — higher rim weight generally results in a sturdier, more powerful presence and spin. Center weight and mid weight, however, requires a much subtler view. From a “minmax design” perspective, centerweight is generally seen as purposeless — even subtractive — and does not help performance in any way.

Our personal stance is that weight distribution is a lot more nuanced than that, and that playfeel comes about by how the three mass categories harmonize with a design’s profile and size — each of these being vital levers for adjusting and creating a specific playfeel.

In musical terms — center weight can often feel like the missing bassline that makes an already wonderful acoustic set feel complete and whole. It’s not loud, but it has an incredibly grounding effect. When it’s missing, the musical experience feels somewhat empty.

We approached the Lamina like a controlled experiment, an A/B test — we fixed all design variables across the Alpha and Beta — except for center weight, where the Alphas pack an additional 1.3g in a slight dome hub. This additional mass is slight, but not insignificant — it isolates the effect of center weight as a sole variable, and allows us to observe its influence on feel.

The Lamina is wide enough for this subtle difference to feel real and observable, while keeping it stable in play.

The goal of this project isn’t to say that a specific design or playfeel is better than the other, but to provide a reference point for their own tastes and preferences. The Lamina exists to help players understand what playfeel speaks to them, and how to recognize it when it appears.

Our personal, subjective observations of the differences are as such:

“α / Alpha — Domed hub, with an 1.3g of additional center weight overall. Plays more rounded, bouncy and whole. A lot more gradual and smooth on directional changes.

β / Beta — Flat hub, base weight, and rim weight is proportionately more. Plays clean, light and agile. Very quick and amenable.”

For what it’s worth, A/B test and design theory aside — the Lamina is possibly one of the most fun designs we’ve made.

The name Lamina is Latin for layer — reflecting the tiered nature of design in a physical world. The suffixes, Alpha and Beta, draw from the Greek tradition of empirical observation.

We’re excited to hear if your experiences of the Lamina align with ours, and whether experiencing both versions together surfaces any realizations about existing models and designs.

—

The Lamina comes with a velvet texture blast. Bearing areas are masked and smooth, and will not affect string wear. Please note before purchase.

title: Laser
content: AboutThe Laser represents yoyorecreation's first use of bi-metal construction — a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel inner rings placed at the lips rather than the outer rim, a placement that differs from the later Draupnir architecture. The Laser was the competition yo-yo of Yasuki Tachibana at the 2013 World YoYo Contest. Its performance there directly influenced the development of the Draupnir, which refined the bi-metal concept further. Tachibana also later received the Triplet (2014) as a 3A signature.

title: Lateral (Prototype)
content:
About
Lateral (v0.6.1) is a narrowed H-shape bi-metal design on Motion's internal timeline, marked "Prototyped" only — no retail-release evidence found anywhere.

title: Laurus
content: HistoryLaurus is Hydrangea's first model, representing the brand's inaugural release. The name draws from botanical themes, consistent with the company's naming convention. Laurus was designed as a high-performance 1A model with balanced specs suitable for both casual and competitive play.

title: Circo
content:
History / About
Circo is Layer Infinity's first yo-yo designed for offstring (4A) play, made possible by a soft TPU body that absorbs the impacts of 4A tosses. Modular construction includes three parts: a TPU body with white rims, interchangeable gap spacers to switch between 1A and 4A modes, and side caps compatible with other Layer Infinity models.

title: Pizza Klassm
content:
History / About
Pizza Klassm is a limited variant of Layer Infinity's Klassm model, featuring pizza-themed 3D printed PLA caps on both sides while retaining the Klassm's hybrid polycarbonate/PLA construction and fixed-axle-capable bearing system. All specs and hardware are identical to the standard Klassm.

title: Laze
content:
From MK1:

"Jack Hudspath’s latest signature yoyo, the Laze is a comfortable yoyo designed to take you to your relaxed space."

title: AETHERIS
content:
About
The AETHERIS is LEAD's first monometal yo-yo, released on April 4, 2026 — Yo-Yo Day. Built from 7075 aluminum, the AETHERIS was designed in consultation with national champions in 3A and 5A alongside the brand's 1A expertise, resulting in a yo-yo intentionally suited for multiple play styles rather than optimized for one. At 57mm diameter and 48.5mm width it is larger than LEAD's bimetals, maintaining modern competitive dimensions while keeping the character of a pure monometal.
LEAD positioned the AETHERIS as an accessible entry point — priced at $57 USD — while maintaining high-performance construction. Released in Galaxy and Splash (Pink/Gold/Silver) colorways with worldwide express shipping at launch. LEAD's official online store opened May 5, 2026, alongside the AETHERIS launch period.

title: Lead Balloon (Prototype)
content:
About
The Lead Balloon was a G Squared Yoyos prototype built from an idea suggested by Patreon supporters: an organic-shaped yo-yo over 80 grams. A larger diameter and H-shaped profile keep the weight manageable on the string. A small batch was sold to Patreon supporters; it never entered full production.

title: New Vulcan
content:
About
The New Vulcan is LEAD's second mass-production yo-yo, released in 2026. At 55.5mm diameter and 43mm width, it trades the Protagonist's ultra-wide profile for a more moderate catch zone while maintaining bimetal performance and competitive-weight specs. Priced at $130 USD, it sits above the Protagonist in LEAD's lineup.
Released in Violet and Light Blue colorways through the yoyobox store. Sold out at launch.

title: Protagonist
content:
About
The Protagonist is LEAD's inaugural production yo-yo and the design that introduced the brand to the international competitive community. A compact 55mm diameter paired with a 50mm width delivers high operability and maneuverability for 1A string tricks without sacrificing stability. The bimetal construction — aluminum body with stainless steel rings — provides the weight distribution needed for competitive performance at the rim.
The Protagonist launched through the yoyobox store in 2025 and sold out across all colorways at release. The NYC Edition (Niigata Tournament Special Edition) was the first colorway variant, featuring an ice-blue surface with snowflake logo. All colorways have since sold out with no announced restock.

title: Protagonist Prime
content:
About
The Protagonist Prime is a limited-edition design sharing the Protagonist's overall form factor but built around a unique tri-material construction: an aluminum body with a polycarbonate ring set against the inner wall of a black electroplated stainless steel ring. The added polycarbonate element shifts the weight distribution to prioritize agility over pure stability — the brand described it as "a distinct product from the original Protagonist — brand new design, brand new experience."
Only 20 units were produced. The brand announced no mass production plans for this model. Debuted alongside 2025 NYC and 2026 RYC contests.

title: LED Light Up Yo-Yo Kanagawa
content: About LED Light Up Yo-Yo KanagawaThrow Revolution's LED light-up plastic yo-yo designed for casual play and visual appeal. Features LED glow effects for tricks under low light.

title: Legacy
content: About the LegacyThe Legacy is an all-plastic successor to the Dark Magic, sharing its iconic profile in injection-molded Celcon at a significantly lower price. It features silicone O-ring response in a fixed-gap design wider than the original Dark Magic's, making it immediately suitable for semi-unresponsive play. It became one of the most recommended budget yo-yos for intermediate players learning bind techniques.

title: Legacy 2
content: About the Legacy 2The Legacy 2 upgrades the original Legacy with aluminum alloy rims and the Solid Spin Axle system, bridging the gap between budget plastic and metal-rimmed performance. It ships with a thin bearing for beginner-friendly response and includes a Speed Bearing for advancing players. Championship editions were produced for 2011 Nationals.

title: Legacy 3
content: About the Legacy 3The Legacy 3 increments the Legacy 2 formula with thicker outer rims contributing an additional 3 grams of weight, improving gyroscopic stability without sacrificing playability. The Solid Spin Axle system and dual-bearing package (thin + Speed Bearing) make it convertible between responsive and bind play. It represents the final evolution of the Legacy line before the company's closure.

title: Legendary Terrarian
content:
"In Terraria, you need to kill the Moonlord to have a chance to get a Terrarian yo-yo.  That chance is exactly 11.11%, repeating of course. It’s the best weapon in the game, and the best version is the one that rolls with the “Godly” modifier.

We are still waiting for details, but the Terrarian might be unseated as the best weapon in the game by the Legendary Terrarian.  Keep an eye out for announcements from Re-Logic on that.

And as is now tradition, the Legendary Terrarian is also coming to the real world.  We are using the same technique as we did on the Seven Summits and the Kuntosh 5000QV:  the Legendary Terrarian is made from 7075 aluminum alloy (the original is 6061) and the weight distribution is changed so the total weight is less than the original, even though 7075 is more dense (weighs more).  What that means is it looks the same to your eye in play as the original, but it feels totally different. You will notice the visual changes in the cup. This procedure is now known as “Boosted”.

Are you ready for the next level?"

title: Leo Sniper Boost
content:
History / About
Leo Sniper Boost (SY-010B) succeeds the bestselling Leo Sniper line, with a 3-stage step inverse round profile and its stainless rim moved to the outside while retaining an inner-rim visual. Bundled with a revised Storybook Vol.10 (2nd ed., includes discontinued SY-010 blueprints). Yoyo performance duo SPINATION is referenced again in connection with this release, though as with SY-010 this is a storybook/promotional credit, not a confirmed design partnership.

title: Leo Sniper MK-II
content:
History / About
Leo Sniper MK-II is Sturm Panzer's best-selling model line, built on an OEM chassis credited to "Yo-Yo Laboratory," sold across several colorway lots from 2013 through 2016.

title: Leo Sniper MK-II 7068 Ver.
content:
History / About
The 7068 Ver. switched Leo Sniper MK-II to factory (non-handmade) production, using A7068 alloy for a sub-60g weight with a stiffer feel.

title: Leo Sniper (Pre-Release)
content:
History / About
The pre-release Leo Sniper was Sturm Panzer's first Size-D bimetal, built on an OEM chassis credited to "YOYO Laboratory" as their "A-01 Style."

title: Aibou
content:
About
The Aibou is an entry-level offering in the JIGUN by LEP line. At 56mm diameter, 43.94mm width, and 65g, the Aibou delivers competitive dimensions at an approachable $25 USD price point. "Aibou" means "partner" or "companion" in Japanese — fitting for a yo-yo positioned as a starting point within LEP's lineup. Available in True Love and Black colorways.

title: Bipolar
content:
About
The Bipolar is a wide-body competition bimetal from JIGUN by LEP, inspired by the concept of emotional highs and lows. Its 7075 aluminum body pairs with a stainless steel outer ring at 56mm diameter and 49.2mm width. An upgraded 10mm axle (in place of the standard M4) was chosen for enhanced stability at high rotational speeds, producing smoother spins and better control during complex tricks. Available in seven colorways: Turquoise, Green, Burgundy, Azure, Pink, Silver, and Black. Retail price: $90 USD.

title: Charon
content:
About
The Charon is JIGUN by LEP's second off-string yo-yo design, a successor to an earlier 4A model. The development process spanned September 2023 through May 2024 across multiple prototypes, refining stability during float through broader weight distribution and smoother internal construction. Stainless steel rings embedded at the edges provide rim weight for stability. Named after Pluto's moon Charon. Released in White. Retail price: $85 USD.

title: Dongwu
content:
About
The Dongwu is an entry-level model in the JIGUN by LEP lineup. "Dongwu" translates to "animal" or "creature" in Chinese. At 55.5mm diameter, 45.05mm width, and 65.9g, the Dongwu delivers competitive dimensions at an accessible $45 USD price point. Released in Red and Yellow.

title: Glory INSIGNIA
content:
About
The Glory INSIGNIA is Wayne Chung Cheng Hsun's third signature model with JIGUN by LEP. Wayne used the INSIGNIA to win his 9th consecutive Taiwan National Championship. The 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rings delivers competition-ready bimetal performance with an emphasis on consistency at the championship level. Available in Silver, Blue, Red, and Gold. Priced at $85 USD.

title: HANABI PC
content:
About
The HANABI PC is JIGUN by LEP's most accessible plastic model, priced at $11.99 USD. "Hanabi" means "fireworks" in Japanese. Available in White, Tiffany, and Clear colorways. An entry point into the JIGUN lineup for players newer to the brand.

title: Hatsukoi
content:
About
The Hatsukoi is JIGUN by LEP's first full titanium yo-yo. The name means "first love" in Japanese, and the design reflects that sentiment — an elegant wing profile with a simulated diamond rhinestone set into the cup. Full titanium construction enables precise weight distribution for powerful spin without added heft. Priced at $250 USD and released in Raw (unanodized titanium) finish.

title: Insulation Lithium MAX
content:
About
The Insulation Lithium MAX is a premium model in LEP's Insulation product line. Specific construction details were not publicly documented. Available in Green at $165 USD.

title: Insulator Lithium
content:
About
The Insulator Lithium is Yulin Li "Luckey"'s signature model developed through the collaboration between LEP and Sochi Company — the company founded by Luckey himself. The bi-material construction pairs an aluminum body with a polycarbonate (PC) covering over the inner profile, adding the tactile and acoustic properties of PC to a conventional aluminum platform. Released in a WYYC 2023 Purple colorway. Priced at $59.99 USD.

title: Insulator Pro Lithium
content:
About
The Insulator Pro Lithium is the premium upgrade of the Insulator Lithium, evolving the signature design of Yulin Li "Luckey" into a full tri-material construction. Where the standard model pairs aluminum with polycarbonate, the Pro version adds titanium rims for elevated rim weight and spin performance. The collaboration between LEP and Sochi Company produced both models for the same WYYC 2023 release window. Priced at $199.99 USD.

title: KAWA
content:
About
The KAWA is JIGUN by LEP's first off-string yo-yo, a 4A design constructed from POM (polyoxymethylene/acetal) plastic and anodized aluminum. Size D bearings were chosen over the standard Size C for improved regen stability during off-string play. During the KAWA's development phase, a member of LEP's team achieved third place at a South Japan Regional competition using the yo-yo. "Kawa" means "river" in Japanese. Available in four colorways: Yellow POM/Black anodized, White POM/Silver, White POM/Blue, and SAKURA (Silver anodized). Retail price: $55 USD (8,300 JPY).

title: Lithium W
content:
About
The Lithium W is the JIGUN signature model for Yulin Li "Luckey," the founder of Sochi Company and a multi-national yo-yo champion. The bimetal pairs 7075 aluminum with stainless steel rims at a competitive 56.5mm diameter and wide 49.2mm width. Released in Black with Black Rims and Orange Silver Acidwash. Priced at $94.99 USD.

title: Marina 4
content:
About
The Marina 4 is the third signature throw Wu Congcong released with JIGUN in 2022. Built on the structural foundation of the Martian, the Marina 4 replaces that model's polycarbonate cup with 7075 aluminum, yielding a full bimetal construction with substantial stainless steel rims. The brand emphasized its ability to deliver "smooth execution of any trick while boasting substantial stainless steel rim" with "powerful spin and explosive energy." Ships with Sochi Fat string included.

title: Marina9
content:
About
The Marina9 is JIGUN's 2025 competition flagship and the throw Wu Congcong used at Prague Worlds. Named after the Mariner 9 space probe, the Marina9 uses a 7075 aluminum body with frosted stainless steel rims and includes a convertible weight system: the base configuration is 66.8g; adding the included 3D rings raises total weight to 68.5g. "Insigne elements" appear in the design alongside the Mariner 9 reference. LEP released the Marina9 unannounced at Prague Worlds, where it sold out the following day. Priced at $99 USD.

title: Martian
content:
About
The Martian is the signature model of Chinese champion Hu Congcong and one of LEP's most technically ambitious early designs. The tri-material construction pairs a 7068 aluminum body with a polycarbonate (PC) cup and stainless steel rings, achieving wall thicknesses reaching 0.5mm at their thinnest point. The result is a powerful competition throw emphasizing spin time and stability while leveraging the flex and tactile properties of the PC component. Ships with a zippered protective case. Priced at $150 USD.

title: Martian+
content:
About
The Martian+ is a premium variant within LEP's Martian product line, priced at $270 USD. Specific construction details were not publicly documented. Available in Black and Grey. As with other Martian-line models, it sold out at release.

title: Martian.W
content:
About
The Martian.W is the competition throw Wu Congcong designed for the 2024 China National Championship, where he competed as defending champion. The model expands the original Martian's width from 46.82mm to 50mm, increasing the catch zone for "greater error tolerance" and improved stability during the high-difficulty sequences required at national level competition. Released in Triple GOLD, Silver, Silver+Gold Ring, and Gold+Raw Ring colorways. Retail price: $145–$160 USD.

title: Martis
content:
About
The Martis is an LEP model incorporating the brand's patented polycarbonate (PC) inner profile design, providing heightened tactile feedback during play. The PC element covers the inner profile of the yo-yo, enabling what LEP describes as "seamless transition between casual tricks and competitive execution." The Martis shares naming lineage with the Martian and Marina series. Available in Silver, Black, Pink, and Purple at $55 USD.

title: MG Lithium
content:
About
The MG Lithium is a limited collaboration between Sochi Company and JIGUN by LEP, recreating Sochi founder Yulin Li "Luckey"'s classic Lithium signature in magnesium alloy. Limited to 100 pieces, the MG Lithium achieves a 2.5:1 aspect ratio that delivers "heightened spin power and impressive hollow sensation" through the inherent low density and stiffness of magnesium. Priced at $250 USD and released in White. Considered by community reviewers among the standout designs of 2023.

title: Moonwalk
content:
About
The Moonwalk is LEP's anniversary release and first major collaboration, produced together with Sochi Company. Designed by Wu Congcong with visuals by Tan Chang, the Moonwalk uses a tri-material construction: a 7075 aluminum body paired with a glow-in-the-dark polycarbonate inner ring and stainless steel outer ring. The brand described it as delivering "a different kind of swing from the big loop yo-yos." Released in multiple colorways including a Czech Edition across two production runs.

title: New Moon
content:
About
The New Moon is one of LEP's most technically distinctive designs, featuring a patented POM (polyoxymethylene/acetal) rim system. Rather than conventional stainless steel rings, the New Moon uses POM rims to achieve appropriate weight distribution while optimizing wall thickness and tactile feedback. The brand described it as maintaining inertia "equivalent to stainless steel rims" through material geometry rather than density. The POM rims are visible from the side, giving the New Moon a clean two-tone appearance. Priced at $55 USD and released in three colorways: Pink/White POM, Blue/White POM, and Purple/White POM.

title: ONIGOKKO
content:
About
The ONIGOKKO is the founding product of Lab Exploration Program's JIGUN line and Wu Congcong's first signature throw with the brand. A stainless steel rim bimetal at 56.2mm diameter and 46.8mm width, the ONIGOKKO established LEP's design language and introduced the brand to the international competitive yo-yo scene in 2021. Its release marked the beginning of an ongoing series of signature models developed for Wu Congcong and other top competitive players.

title: ONIGOKKO 3
content:
About
The ONIGOKKO 3 is the third installment of JIGUN's ONIGOKKO line, originally Wu Congcong's first signature. The third generation shifts away from the original's bimetal construction to an aluminum monometal at 57mm diameter and 51mm width — dimensions that carry over the wide width of the Martian+ and styling elements from the Martis. Designed for 1A, 3A, and 5A play, the ONIGOKKO 3 was positioned as LEP's most versatile and accessible model at $35 USD. A limited WYYC 2025 (World YoYo Contest) edition was also released. Ten colorways were offered: Light Blue, Gray, Pink, Red, Violet, Navy, Orange, Yellow, Titanium, and Tiffany Blue.

title: PC Rumbling
content:
About
The PC Rumbling is the polycarbonate plastic version of JIGUN's Rumbling, sharing the same profile in an accessible plastic construction. Available in a wide range of colorways including Fluorescent Green, Clear, Red Pink, Blue, Pink/Clear, Blue/Clear, Pink/Blue, and a Czech Edition.

title: Rumbling
content:
About
The Rumbling is the JIGUN signature model for Zhang Suze. The bimetal construction pairs 6061 aluminum with stainless steel rims for competitive performance at a $60 USD price point. Released in five colorways: Silver with Silver Rims, Red with Black Rims, Purple with Silver Rims, Mint with Silver Rims, and Maroon Tan Acidwash with Silver Rims.

title: Ti Aibou
content:
About
The Ti Aibou is the titanium upgrade of JIGUN's Aibou model. At 54mm diameter — slightly smaller than the original Aibou's 56mm — the Ti Aibou uses full titanium construction for a precision, lightweight competition platform. Released in the Virus colorway. Priced at $220 USD.

title: TiSS Bipolar
content:
About
The TiSS Bipolar is the extreme-tier version of JIGUN's Bipolar, replacing the aluminum body with grade titanium and retaining stainless steel rims. Limited to 10 sets worldwide — the titanium body adds 29g while the stainless steel rims contribute 35g of the 66.2g total weight. The brand noted "extreme technical difficulty and low yield rate" in manufacturing. Each set includes a comparison aluminum Bipolar in titanium colorway. Released April 4 (Yo-Yo Day). Priced at $560 USD (88,888 JPY).

title: Vandal
content:
About
The Vandal is a mid-range model in the JIGUN by LEP lineup, priced at $20 USD standard and $25 for Artist Proof editions. The Vandal was notable for its wide colorway variety, released across multiple production runs and tournament editions including WYYC (World YoYo Contest) and NYC colorways. Standard colorways include Raw, Pink, Dark Green, Light Blue, Purple, Gray Blue, Green, Tiffany Blue, Black, and Colorful. Tournament editions added Blue Silver Splash, Green WYYC, Purple WYYC, and Black NYC.

title: Insulator
content:
About
The Insulator is a collaborative release from the Lab Exploration Program and Sōchí Company, serving as a signature throw for Sochi founder Luckey Yulin Li. The design pairs a 7075 aluminum body with a polycarbonate inner shroud that covers the inner profile to smooth string contact and alter the feel of the throw without changing the core metal geometry. It features a step-round profile with a matte coating and was released in a purple WYYC 2023 colorway. Also sold under the name Insulator Lithium in some markets. It retailed at $59.99 and sold out.

title: Insulator Pro Lithium
content:
About
The Insulator Pro Lithium is a tri-material upgrade to the Insulator, produced by the Lab Exploration Program and Sōchí Company. To the 7075 aluminum body and polycarbonate inner shroud it adds titanium rims for a significant increase in rim weight, spin power, and stability over the base model. Released as a WYYC 2023 special edition in purple, it targets competitive 1A players who want the Insulator's unique feel with maximum performance specifications.

title: Moonwalk
content:
About
The Moonwalk is a special release commemorating the first anniversary of the Lab Exploration Program, produced with Sōchí Company. Designed by China National Champion Wu Congcong with visual artwork by Tan Chang, it combines a 7075 aluminum body with a transparent polycarbonate center ring and stainless steel outer rims. The polycarbonate ring glows under UV light, adding a visual element to competition use. The stainless steel outer weighting delivers the spin power and stability expected of a competition-grade throw.

title: YOFO
content:
About
The YOFO is a patent-pending convertible yo-yo and spin top developed by the Lab Exploration Program in collaboration with Sōchí Company. By disassembling and flipping the halves, the YOFO reconfigures between standard string yo-yo play, fixed-axle ground spin tricks, and hand spin tricks — all from one piece of hardware. The bearing locks on both sides depending on configuration. Machined from 7068 aluminum with a polycarbonate element, it supports DNA tricks, gyro flops, and traditional spin-top techniques. Available in Silver and Black, retailed at $100. Sold out.

title: YOFO
content:
About
The YOFO is a patented novelty from the collaboration between Sochi Company and LEP. Bearing locks on both sides of the yo-yo allow the two halves to be disassembled and flipped, changing the configuration between yo-yo and spin top. In yo-yo mode the YOFO plays normally using a Size C bearing; in spin top mode it supports ground spinning, hand spinning, and DNA (freehand) tricks. The 7068 aluminum body with polycarbonate components keeps weight competitive at 64.6g despite the added hardware. Custom 18mm pads replace the standard 19mm response.

title: Lesula
content:
History / About
The Lesula is MonkeyfingeR Design’s compact undersized entry in their lineup. Named after the lesula (a species of monkey discovered in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2007 — one of only two new primate species found in 28 years at the time), it brings a traditional feel to MFD’s otherwise competition-oriented range. The tighter dimensions and 6061 construction give it an accessible, familiar play character distinct from the larger Gelada.

title: Lesula 2
content:
History / About
The Lesula 2 is MonkeyfingeR Design’s successor to their 2013 Lesula, revealed on a Christmas Eve 2024 livestream. The updated geometry expands the catch zone and improves spin times over the original, while maintaining the compact undersized character of the Lesula lineage. Eight colorways were available at launch through the MFD Shopify store.

title: Level 6
content: Designed as C3's budget-friendly alternative to the premium Krown, the original Level 6 was narrower, heavier, and machined more expeditiously to hit a lower price point. Despite the cost-cutting approach, it delivered exceptional spin retention and agility, earning high marks across the board in early reviews. Shockingly easy to control for a full-metal competition throw. Price: $49.99.

title: Level 6 (2018)
content: A modernized renewal of the original 2013 Level 6. Increased diameter and width by 1mm and reduced weight by approximately 4 grams, creating a lighter, faster monometal with the power and feel of a high-end bi-metal design. Retained the accessible price point. Price: $29.99.

title: Libero
content:
From ZGRT:

"The dimension, shape and material of this throw adds the desired power we envisioned the Libero to have.

This time we were fully focused in utilizing aluminum 7075 to balance the weight along with the shape we wanted to have for this throw. The base of the shape of the Libero is a V shape which combined with tall rims creates a hybrid V-H shape. This combination makes the Libero fall in between the Basilisk and the Qi, but the result is surprisingly unique.

We tested a handful of prototypes to reach the weight distribution, performance and aesthetics we wanted to have for the Libero. We made the rim wider to move certain part of the rim weight away from the outer diameter. That way, the Libero ended up playing more nimble without compromising spin time and stability.  We also wanted to have a wide catch zone to improve playability and land easier on the string.

Libero plays competitively due to its characteristics, weight and dimensions. Its stability and nimbleness makes the Libero easy to control and to perform combos quickly.  It is also capable to play horizontally and its spin time is impressive.

LIbero will bring freedom to your play.

Let nothing hold you down!"

title: Life
content:
History / About
Life is a collaboration between G2 and A Return Tops (a-rt.ca), designed by Jensen. G2 calls it "an absolute joy to play," and it features loose bearing posts that can be removed without tools (with a minor, acknowledged fingernail-vibe trade-off on some A-grades). Additional design context was published on the a-rt collaboration site. It was restocked December 15, 2019, and again referenced in later releases (Caribbean Sea Life, Sept. 2019; AL7 Life Nebula, Dec. 2021; Interstellar Life, March 2022).

title: Light Chaser
content: AboutThe Light Chaser is Chinese player Zhang Suze's signature yo-yo with AceYo. Features a matte finish with minimal engraving for maximum grindability, with a high polish on the string contact zone for off-axis tricks. Floaty touch with bi-metal stability for long competitive combos. Described as a "great all-arounder." Available in Blue/Silver Rims, Silver/Silver Rims, and Black/Gold Rims.

title: Lightning
content:
History / About
In our tribute series, we focused on the Air Rider by AnY HaPPY YoYo. The Lightning is an homage to the AnY Air Rider with even more power and stability. The pads are gone and have been replaced by our trusted Hot Red sILYYcone response system and the typical metric bearing.

Production Runs

Run #1 (April 2015) — 10 units, Titanium; D53.50mm / W37.10mm / 67.80g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.

title: Limelight
content: AboutThe Limelight is Duncan's light-up beginner looper, featuring a transparent polycarbonate body that houses internal LED lights which blink and shift through color patterns as the yo-yo spins faster. The rim-weighted design gives it respectable sleep times for a transaxle yo-yo, and the plastic sleeve reduces friction for smoother loops. It remains one of the most visible yo-yos in Duncan's catalog — literally — and is a popular choice for nighttime performances and introductory light-show routines.

title: Limitless
content: AboutThe Limitless is OFFSET's novelty and trick-innovation plastic. Three bearings total — one axle bearing and two outer shell bearings — allow the shells to spin freely while the body rotates. Players can grab, hold, tilt, and reposition the outer shell mid-trick without stopping the spin. At 75g it is the heaviest OFFSET plastic, and the design was conceived specifically for trick creation and shareable content. Marketed as a tool for pushing the boundaries of what is possible in play.

title: Linear
content:
From Motion:

"Say hello to Linear Motion

The YoYo that was never in the plan. When Motion was first started, I had only envisioned using bimetal yo-yos for all of our lineup, this was met with quite a few comments internally and externally from members of the community. James Underwood was one of the largest pushers to get a mono metal made and, being the stubborn person I can be, I kept refusing.  It was in discussions within the proto team that we finally determined we were going to move forward on a monometal yoyo, under one condition: it couldn’t be a compromise.

The ultimate goal of Motion is to always bring a top quality product into the customers' hands, and I didn’t want to just make a mono because it can be made cheaper. So to the drawing board David and I went, and we quickly found that designing a mono can be very challenging. We started at the place where we felt like we should: on our flagship YoYo, Perpetual. Using perpetual as a starting point, we were able to get a firm base from which to develop the design. What ensued exceeded our expectations, and upon first throw we knew that we hit the mark.

So why Perpetual as the basis for the mono?

Perpetual is the YoYo that we feel best represents our brand. It’s a blend of everything Motion set out to be. So with this being taken into consideration, what better platform to build on?

Perpetual is still one of our favorite yo-yos that we have done, being insanely stable and insanely powerful, we weren’t sure how much of this we could dial in without the rims to push that weight toward the outside. What you will find is a very thick outer wall that mimics the weight of having a bi-metal rim. The cut around the top edge of the YoYo is there to resemble the cut-back on perpetuals rim, one of its defining visual characteristics.  

Aesthetically, we pushed this YoYo to the extreme; each angle just blasts your eyes with elegance and beauty with every single strategically placed cut. The cuts not only help us control weight distribution but also present an interesting tactile and visually pleasing experience. 

One design characteristic you will notice is the double rim around our sunken dome which transplants some weight to the center to help balance, but also pops out at you aesthetically. 

We hope you can see that the time and attention put into this design was just as extreme as any of our bimetal offerings. And we hope this YoYo not only reaches our existing market, but allows more people an entrypoint into our brand. You will be getting the full Motion experience but not at the higher price of a bi-metal offering. 

This is Motion"

141 Made in 8 colors

Coral Burst - 15

Desert Coral - 19

Glistening Amethyst - 19

Periwinkle - 20

Sakura Seiun - 30

Interstellar - 18

Nationals Artist Proof - 18

1 of 2 Artist Proof - 2

title: LinkX
content: AboutThe LinkX was originally a 2017 injection-molded design, later relaunched as a precision-machined polycarbonate yo-yo. Its double rim structure distributes weight for solid spin, and a dedicated fingerspin hub enables fingerspin tricks. It supports responsive play conversion via thin bearing and axle upgrades sold separately. Includes a Konkave bearing. Available in Orange/Blue Hub, Emerald/Dark Teal, Red/Gray, and Blue/Light Purple.
