title: Lithium W
content: AboutThe Lithium W is the signature model of Luckey Yulin Li, a multi-national champion and JIGUN team player. A 7075 aluminum body bimetal with stainless steel outer rims, it features a wide 49.2mm width for a generous catch zone. Released in 2023 at $94.99. Available in Black with Black Rims and Orange Silver Acid Wash colorways. A premium magnesium variant, the MG Lithium, was released as a Sochi Company collaboration.

title: Little Evil 2
content:
History / About
Sequel to HSpin's Little Evil, released as a collaboration with YoYoZeekio (Zeekio), a North American yo-yo manufacturer. Multi-piece stainless steel construction with a concave )-( shape, fixed-gap silicone response. Packaged with a drawstring bag and polyester strings, originally retailed around $60. Yo-Yo Museum confirms a February 2016 release; the exact day is unconfirmed.

title: Little League
content:
History / About
The Little League is Recess's modernized undersized organic model, heavily influenced by the Dressel Designs 5050. It revisits the undersized concept first explored by the Snack but with an updated profile: wider (44.34mm) relative to its diameter, a more organic round shape, and a gap corrected from the original Little League which had been criticized for being too narrow. At 51.49mm it qualifies as undersized while the 44.34mm width gives it a disproportionately wide catch zone. Rewind's blog highlighted its utility for chopstick tricks, wrist-mounted hops, and tight-space maneuvers, and noted it's also comfortable for players with smaller hands or children. The Recess description: "it plays light but binds heavy" — distributed like the Triple Double.

title: Live
content: AboutThe Live is Veronika Kamenská's first signature with AceYo. Its V-shaped profile features a hidden fingerspin hub, emphasizing the concept of "mindfulness" — living in the present. Designed for difficult tricks. Kamenská is world vice-champion and multiple European champion. Available in Galaxy, Rainbow, Green/Gold/Orange, and Pink/Silver/Black.

title: LM Schneider
content:
History / About
LM Schneider is an off-roster, lighter and straighter variant of the Schneider, aimed at competitive tastes.

title: LM2
content:
History / About
LM2 is a collaboration tied to Takatsu Tsukasa's "Ultimate Yo-Yo" YouTube project, released November 25, 2025. The name "LM" was inherited from an old friend and renamed LM2 for this release. It features a distinctive extended hub on the face for top-spin/string-hub tricks.

title: Loadout
content:
History / About
The Loadout has become G2's flagship accessible model — a 7068 aluminum monometal priced at $119 that receives consistent new colorway drops more frequently than any other G2 design. It represents G2's "daily driver" tier: premium 7068 construction without the bimetal premium. The sheer number of colorways it has received since 2024 (Berry Storm, Snozberries, Plasmaberries, Ness Depths, Unicorn Storm, Sea of Flames, Kaleidoscope, Lavender Burst, Midnight Mist, Aquamarine, Rainbow Galaxy, and many more) makes it the most colorway-diverse model in G2's current catalog. A Loadout Wide Prototype was previewed in early 2026 suggesting an expanded-width variant is in development.

title: Loadout SR
content:
History / About
The Loadout SR is a bimetal upgrade of the Loadout monometal, using the same 7068 aluminum body but adding stainless steel rims manufactured by Safety Rims Inc. — whose branding G2 incorporates into the model name. At $105 it is priced below the standard Loadout ($119) while adding the benefits of bimetal rim weighting — an unusual positioning for a bimetal model. The "SR" suffix denotes the Safety Rims partnership.

title: Loadout Wide – Prototype
content:
History / About
Loadout Wide – Prototype is a limited 15-unit prototype release exploring a wider profile of G2's Loadout shape. Full specifications were not published by G2 at time of release.

title: LOCK
content:
About
LOCK is a mono-metal signature model for Karthik Devaraj, part of "alternatives"' signature lineup alongside KEY (bi-metal) and UNLOCK (tri-material).

title: Logic 2
content: AboutThe Logic 2 succeeds the original Logic with two significant upgrades: the body material moves from 6061 to 7068 aluminum for added stiffness, and width expands to 60mm — Allon's widest throw at the time of release. The inner ring bi-metal construction is retained, keeping the weight distribution that suits Allon's horizontal and technical play style. Allon used the Logic 2 to win back-to-back Australian Nationals and place 10th globally for the second consecutive year.

title: Logic Limitless
content:
About
Logic Limitless is Allon Chen's signature model in the LIMITLESS line, built for technical/string-trick players. Adds stainless steel inner rims to a 7075 aluminium body for added stability during dense trick sequences.

title: Logic
content: AboutThe Logic is the first signature yo-yo for OFFSET team rider Allon Chen (Australian National Champion). Unlike conventional bi-metals with outer rim rings, the Logic places stainless steel on the inner surface of the body, a weight distribution designed specifically for the horizontal trick styles and extended technical combos that define Allon's competitive play. Allon used it to win Australian Nationals and place 10th globally.

title: Lossless
content:
About
Lossless takes a standard-sized yoyo and shrinks down every part of it — width, diameter, weight, bearing, and even the response pads — while keeping huge (for its size) steel weight rings. Its profile shape borrows partially from Mk1's HD model, but with a larger drop into the profile and broader steel (and overall) rims. Ships with a yoyo string included. Solo Mk1 release.

title: Lotus
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: Lotus YoYo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"Fixed axle (no bearing) lotus flower shaped yoyo. This is a big one, I recommend slicing to end up around 60 grams. The axle is threaded on both ends and screws into the halves. 

For the axle infill density, shape, and filament type is very important. If you print with defaults or standard PLA the axle will break. I recommend using a strong filament such as HTPLA, PLA+, PETG, or carbon fiber. Infill should be 30-50% and one of the directionally strong infill types such as honeycomb, cubic, or triangles. 

I've included a 3mf file compatible with MMU3 so that you can do color versions."

title: Lotus
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"Introducing the Sengoku Lotus – A Monometal Marvel Sengoku, renowned for their innovative designs like the Tri-metal yoyos and the extreme rim-weighted Hattori, now presents the Lotus! This latest creation takes the concept of a metal yo-yo with cutouts to an entirely new level. The Lotus features a distinctive perforated shape, with a body divided into four interconnected parts resembling flower petals. Its unique shape speaks for itself, evoking a sense of disbelief that it should even work, but wow does it!

One of the coolest features of the Lotus is the captivating wind-cutting sound it emits when thrown. The resonance of the string hitting the body is uniquely characteristic, setting this yo-yo apart from any other. While playing on the string, you can feel the air resistance like a mini fan, which is truly something we had not experienced before. Despite its unique design, the Lotus surprisingly doesn't catch the string at medium to high RPMs, allowing it to be fully playable!

The Lotus's design not only looks stunning but also offers a unique throwing experience. Each yo-yo has been meticulously opened and tweaked, with shims added until the gaps are perfectly aligned, making it a true finished functional piece of art. While it is safer than previous models like the Hanzo and Hattori, it still requires careful handling. Tricks such as rejection or sidewinder-type tricks, where the string touches the body vertically, may result in the string catching on the body, leading to a sudden stop. Therefore, while it can ride on or slide along the string without issue, controlling it at an angle needs caution.

The Sengoku Lotus is not just a yo-yo; it’s a revolution in design and performance. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or a dedicated enthusiast, the Lotus promises to deliver an experience like no other. Embrace the future of yo-yoing with the Sengoku Lotus and feel the difference in every throw."

title: LP
content: About the LPThe LP is sOMEThING's dedicated 2A competition looping yo-yo. POM spacers provide an ideal gap width for looping response straight out of the box — no modification or tuning required for competition readiness. The second generation (shown here) refines the design further for match-day use. Available in Ghost White.

title: Lucency
content: AboutThe Lucency is a bi-material wedge polycarbonate yo-yo with stainless steel rings. Positioned as a competition-capable hybrid design.

title: Lucha Libre
content:
The Lucha Libre was the final release for Throw Down. According to team members, the prototypes had a number of concerns. There was a thick axle that was screwed directly into the Delrin and the bearing sat on the Delrin. There were changes to the production version, a spiked hex nut, a different bearing seat, but these changes were never tested by the team. Due to an error at the machine shop, the production run's bearing seat was machined too thin. This caused the Lucha Libre to break, sometimes just by returning to the hand. 80 yoyos were released in white or dyed colors. Most Lucha Libre's became unplayable shortly after playing for the first time. Throw Down never recovered from this and shut down.

Prototype halves - All Delrin, no spiked hex bolt

title: Be A Sport
content:
About
Be A Sport is a tin yo-yo series from Lumar featuring British sports themes lithographed onto the body. The Footballer (football/soccer) variant is confirmed; given the British market, additional sports variants are plausible. Also documented as “VINTAGE MARX BE A SPORT SERIES LUMAR YO-YO, FOOTBALL DESIGN.” Fixed axle; same two-piece tin shell construction as the Beginners models.

title: Beginners 33
content:
About
The Beginners 33 was the most common tin model in the Lumar range and the entry point for generations of British yo-yo players. Two-piece tin shells are crimped together, with the “GENUINE LUMAR YO-YO” trademark lithographed directly onto the body — a detail that collectors use to authenticate specimens. The model was produced across several decades, with significant colorway variation: examples are documented in green/yellow/black, red/yellow, light blue/yellow, and blue/yellow schemes. Fixed axle; no bearing or response pads, as standard for the era.

title: Beginners 34
content:
About
The Beginners 34 shares the same hollow two-piece tin shell construction and lithographed logo as the Beginners 33 but is significantly less common. Collectors consider excellent-condition specimens exceedingly rare. Known colorways include blue, black, red, and a red/yellow spiral variant. Fixed axle; no bearing or response pads.

title: Butterfly 77
content:
About
The Butterfly 77 is Lumar’s entry into the butterfly (wing/concave) shaped plastic yo-yo format. Its widened catch zone makes string tricks more accessible than the imperial-shaped models in the range. Impressed “LUMAR” branding appears on the sides. The blue body with orange caps is the documented colorway; other colorways may exist. One of the rarer production models in the Lumar line. Fixed axle.

title: Championship 99
content:
About
The Championship 99 is Lumar’s most-produced model and the plastic yo-yo most closely associated with the brand in the postwar decades. Its full name — “Genuine Lumar Yo-Yo Championship 99” — is raised in molding on the body sides. A composite construction combines a plastic shell with a thin internal metal sheet reinforcement for durability.
Production ran continuously from the early 1950s into the early 1980s under Louis Marx ownership and then under Dunbee-Combex after the 1967 acquisition. Stamp lettering width varies across production runs and is used by collectors to date specimens: the larger, wider “LUMAR” text indicates earlier manufacture. Known colorways include black, orange, baby blue, pink, yellow, red, and green. A 1950s pin badge (“Spinner Award” button) was sold as a companion accessory.

title: Deluxe 99
content:
About
The Deluxe 99 stands apart from most of the Lumar line in its use of wood construction — a material otherwise uncommon for the brand. Its elaborate full name, “Genuine Lumar Deluxe 99 Champion Yo-Yo Junior Express Competition Model,” reflects the competition-event branding Lumar used during its promotional yo-yo campaigns. Unlike the tin models’ lithographed artwork, the Deluxe 99 carries a printed paper sticker label. Fixed axle; no bearing or response pads.

title: Hi-KER
content:
About
The Hi-KER is a metal Lumar yo-yo from the 1950s distinguished by four decorative rhinestone (sparkle) inserts set into the body. Listed as “Lumar Hi-KER With Four Sparkles Master Yo-Yo.” Whether Lumar licensed the Hi-Ker name or applied it independently is unclear; the Canadian Hi-Ker brand (Hi-Ker Inc.) is a separate entity with no confirmed connection to Lumar’s version. Fixed axle.

title: Jewel 99
content:
About
The Jewel 99 is a prototype yo-yo recovered from the Lumar factory in Swansea after its permanent closure in 1981. The model was never mass-produced; only a single specimen is known to exist, found in the factory by yo-yo collector YoyoZee (Richie). It appears to have been conceived as a rhinestone or jewel-embellished variant of the Championship 99 format. The Jewel 99 represents the last documented design intent of the Lumar line before the factory closed for good.

title: Muppet Show Yo-yos
content:
About
The Muppet Show Yo-yos are a set of licensed plastic yo-yos manufactured by Lumar Limited, featuring individual characters from Jim Henson’s The Muppet Show (1976–1981). Each yo-yo in the set carries a different character’s face. Confirmed characters include Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and Monster (possibly Gonzo or Animal), with at least a fourth unidentified character also produced. Decorated with the Muppet Show logo and character artwork. Fixed axle.

title: Whistling Yo-yo
content:
About
The Whistling Yo-yo is a tin novelty model in the Lumar range, stamped “THE ORIGINAL LUMAR WHISTLING YOYO REGISTERED MADE IN GT BRITAIN.” Holes or slots in the tin body create airflow that produces a whistle sound while the yo-yo spins — a feature that made it a deliberate specialty alongside the standard models in the Lumar catalogue. The registered design designation indicates Lumar held design protection for the mechanism. Fixed axle.

title: Wombles Yo-yo
content:
About
The Wombles Yo-yo is a licensed product manufactured by Lumar Limited featuring characters from the BBC television series The Wombles, which debuted in 1973 and reached peak popularity through 1975. The Uncle Bulgaria character is confirmed; additional characters from the Wombles cast were likely included in the range. Plastic construction; fixed axle.

title: Luna
content:
History / About
The G2 Luna combines design elements from the Casefile 003, Triton, and Life, offering an organic feel with additional rim power not found in mono-weight designs. It launched Friday, August 26, 2022 at 7pm Eastern in the Pacific Storm colorway.

title: Lunar Eclipse
content:
From onedropyoyos.com:

"One Drop x OhYesYo Lunar Eclipse

First there was the Great Solar Eclipse and now, once again astronomical forces have aligned to bring One Drop and OhYesYo together to make a yo-yo where the sum is greater than the parts. Coffin Nachtmahr, Founder of OhYesYo, Frequency Wavelength Modulator, and Yo-yoing’s Modern Anti-Hero, tells the story of the Lunar Eclipse:

--how it came to be--

This Lunar Eclipse was born purely out of desire and not necessity. A random comment in a few threads online gave me this idea somewhere around 2019. If I could pinpoint its origin it was probably Andrew Swenson's idea. After the release of the Eclipse, lots of people asked me endlessly if we would release more or perhaps do an updated version in 7075. I kept hopeful about the idea but didn't want to rush into it without really figuring out what I'd like to change about it.

--how to revamp a yoyo--

I've never seen myself as one to desire a "signature yoyo", however there are clear design features that I've grown fond of in my decade of throwing. To update the Eclipse, which was designed to be a bit of a casual and solid daily yoyo, I approached the design from my trick knowledge and styling that I currently use. I then put the original Eclipse through its paces and picked it apart looking for what I would want to modify or change to get it up to speed with what I do now.

--what’s new--

I began with understanding what 7075 would do to the design, or rather, what the design could do better in 7075. So this quickly became a more battle ready eclipse as opposed to it's laid back original. Shawn and I decided to reduce the thickness of the mid-weight ring in the cup, invert the angle of that first step after the bearing seat and added a cut before the rim to pay homage to the yoyo that inspired the original Eclipse's design (Swenson said the Eclipse was a Nightingale variant and he wasn't wrong at all). Overall, the changes shift weight towards the rim just a bit more, but not so much that it feels dead on the string, but rather, that its still as maneuverable as its predecessor.

--why the long wait--

Well ya know the world was closed and now I'm a dad and things are changing but nothing rushed is ever worth the effort, so I appreciate everyone's patience in this weird transitional period we are all experiencing, and I'm happy to present you with the Lunar Eclipse."

Cerakote Raven Lunar Eclipse

From One Drop:

"We are honored to continue our collaborations with Coffin of @theohyesyo . The Lunar Eclipse was the 7075 follow up to the original Eclipse and there has only been one run so far. Both of them were heavily influenced by the Ohyesyo Nightingale. For a second run Lunar Eclipse, Coffin was again influenced by the Nightingale but this time by a specific coloway called Raven. Raven was a two-tone anodizing with black in the catch zone and purple in the cups. For this new run of Lunar Eclipe we are only releasing 40 units and they are all Raven. The difference from the original Raven is that this time the black is done with Cerakote."

Release Date: July 17th, 2024

title: M
content:
History / About
The M was mowl's first yo-yo, released in June 2016 and conceived as a high-end proof-of-concept for the brand's design philosophy. Produced by World Champion Eiji Okuyama, the M features a rounded H-shape profile that incorporates elements of both Butterfly and straight-shaped yo-yos — feeling like a Butterfly during sleep but straight and powerful during play. Eye-popping laser-engraved artwork reminiscent of street art made mowl an instant hot topic in the scene when high-quality player videos dropped alongside it. Development started in December 2014 with designers Dee (Shimizu Daiki) and 44nollie (Kawamura Yoshinori). The design goal was a yo-yo that still felt great five years after release — with particular emphasis on the slow, flowing feel without sacrificing spin power or stability. A minor update to the M was released on mowl's 6th anniversary in June 2022.

title: M-PCS
content:
History / About
The M-PCS debuted at the 2024 World YoYo Contest in Osaka, bringing the M's design DNA into a plastic/metal hybrid construction known in Japan as "kin rim" (metal rim). The polycarbonate body offers a refreshing, light feel while the stainless steel rims provide perfect weight distribution and spin power. The aluminum hub completes the tri-material construction. Each logo is meticulously engraved in Osaka for precision and care. Thoroughly tested by players worldwide before release with rave reviews, it makes the M series accessible at a lower price point than the full titanium M Ti.

title: M+
content:
History / About
The M+ is the bimetal evolution of mowl's debut flagship, the M. It takes the M's rounded H-shape and adds two stainless steel weight rings for dramatically more aggressive and powerful performance on the string. Compared to the monometal M, the M+ has a much more assertive character — more rim weight, more stability, and more competition-level punch. It retains the M's comfortable feel and distinctive design language while elevating its performance ceiling.

title: M Ti
content:
History / About
The M Ti launched in November 2024 as the titanium pinnacle of mowl's founding flagship series. Since mowl's founding, the M series has been at the heart of the brand's journey. The M Ti features a unique H-profile design that delivers the exhilarating feel and power of a straight H-profile while staying true to the unmistakable M shape identity. Became a fan favorite quickly after launch. Available in Jet Black and a Gold colorway with a two-tone logo released January 2025. At $549.99, it represents the premium tier of the mowl aluminum-lineage series expressed in titanium.

title: M001 Silencer
content: About the M001 SilencerThe M001 Silencer is widely regarded as one of the finest performers in MagicYoYo's catalog relative to its price. Its H-shaped profile with a smooth anodized finish and alloy inner weight ring creates near-perfect weight distribution for exceptional stability and long spin times. The stock KK (concave) bearing centers the string for clean trick execution. Frequently recommended in community discussions as the standout "best value" from MagicYoYo's metal lineup. Available in Black, Silver, Blue, and other colorways. Also available as a VIP Edition at selected retailers.

title: M002 April
content: About the M002 AprilThe M002 April (also referenced as M002 Heist in some markets) is a butterfly-shaped 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a sand-blasted finish that resists fingerprints and scratching. Praised in community reviews for impressive spin duration and balanced play character. Positioned in MagicYoYo's mid-range segment. Suitable for 1A, 3A, and 5A styles.

title: M003 Prophet
content: About the M003 ProphetThe M003 Prophet is a bead-blasted 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a narrower width profile than typical MagicYoYo throws. Compared favorably to contemporaries like the YYF Accelerator in community discussions. Good spin stability for 1A, 3A, and 5A play styles.

title: M004 Stealth
content: About the M004 StealthReleased as a limited run in November 2020, the M004 Stealth is MagicYoYo's accessible bi-metal entry in the M-series. A 7075 aluminum body provides rigidity and precision machining tolerance while stainless steel rims push weight to the outer edges for enhanced spin time and stability. Praised in community reviews as "a very capable bi-metal at an affordable price." Available in Blue with Gold Rims, Black, and other colorways.

title: M005 Magical
content: About the M005 MagicalThe M005 Magical was MagicYoYo's first bi-metal throw, designed by professional team player Junliang Tian (Jason Tan). The stainless steel weight rings on the rims weigh nearly 16 grams — a significant proportion of the 65.78g total — enabling stronger, longer spins than the all-aluminum M-series predecessors. A flat laser-engraved hub and CenterTrac bearing complete the package. Released in 2016, the Magical marked MagicYoYo's entry into the premium bi-metal segment. Available through gomagicyoyo.com and specialty retailers.

title: M06 Katana
content: About the M06 KatanaThe M06 Katana is a collaborative bi-metal yo-yo between MagicYoYo and Japanese specialty retailer SpinGear. It features a chiseled H-shape profile machined from 7075 aluminum with bold gold-plated stainless steel weight band rims and a bead-blasted finish. The NSK Gold bearing (a premium Japanese precision bearing) provided noticeably smoother spin than stock MagicYoYo bearings. An internationally notable collaboration releasing competition-grade design at an accessible price. All colorways are now sold out.

title: M07 Hotdiggidy
content:
About
M07 Hotdiggidy is Dylan Kowalski's signature yoyo, themed around his "Hotdiggidy" nickname (hot dog + likeness motif). Thick rims give a bi-metal feel at a mono-metal price.

title: M1
content:
From One Drop:

"For our second yo-yo release, we set out to create a high-quality aluminum yo-yo which is readily available at a reasonable price. The result is the M1. As you would expect from us, many months of prototyping and refinement went into the creation of the M1. We once again enlisted the help of the Portland Yo-Yo Club, Mark Montgomery and others to test the playability. All agree that it is, first and foremost, a solid player.

We paid close attention to the testers feedback and the features that they most wanted. In that regard, the M1 sports a recess groove that's deep enough to take flow-able silicone, an inner thumb grind lip, and tapered outer rims that provide plenty of catch-zone width (more than a Project in fact). The M1's profile and shape move us in a new direction, bringing a narrower width to the undersized yo-yo.

Because of the play, the price and the availability, the M1 is intended to be a true players yo-yo. One which you don't have to worry about throwing anywhere, anytime, over any surface."

title: M2
content:
From One Drop:

"The M1 was our second yo-yo model and was released in December of 2008 as the follow up to our debut yo-yo, the Project.

At the time, high-end yo-yos had higher retail prices than they do now and supply was limited. You could go to an online yo-yo store and 90% of the listings would be sold out. The Project was a strong entry into the market because of its unusual axle system, the “projection profile” and the soda blasted finish and it too was limited in supply mainly due the kind of machine we had then.

By the time we were ready for our next model, we had improved our machining capabilities and wanted to release a high availability and affordable yo-yo that was made in house. That yo-yo was the M1. The name meant “metal for everyone” and we tried to deliver on that. To this day, 17 years later, we still have customers that purchased an M1 and for many of them, it was their first high-end metal yo-yo. We feel so grateful and honored to have had this kind of support and love over the years. The theme of the M1 of being available, affordable and made in house has been a central driving force for our business ever since. It set the tone that has carried forward to the present.

We felt the time was right to do a follow up to the M1. The M2 is a scaled up M1 and maintains the same proportions of width to diameter. The diameter has gone from 50mm to 55mm and the width has gone from 35mm to 38.6mm. The other big change is to the axle system: the M2 has a 12mm tapped axle where the M1 had a pressed nut axle system. The pressed nut system was a predecessor to Side Effects but we decided in the effort of affordability that the M2 would have a tapped axle. Interestingly, even though the M2 is bigger than the M1, it weighs less, coming in at 64.4 grams where the M1 was 65 grams. This is achieved by changes to the weight distribution (more rim weight and thinner through the middle).

In play you can tell they are related, but the M2 has more rim weight and overall feels more modern with a 27% increase to spin inertia as calculated by our resident scientist, Dirty Birdy.

Solid colors start at $55."

title: MAD
content: The MAD is the signature model of W1LD team member Lee Jun Sang. A 6061 bi-metal with stainless steel rims, the MAD delivers a balanced competition feel with strong rim-weighted spin power. Available in multiple colorways.

title: Mad Minute
content: The Mad Minute is a compact everyday carry throw and spiritual successor to the Minute line. Its 55mm × 39mm step-straight 6061 aluminum body carries minimalist engraving on one side and a timepiece design on the other, continuing the Time Series aesthetic. At 65.4g it punches above its size. Available in Pink. $49.99 USD retail ($40 on sale).

AboutThe 5150 is MadHouse YoYos' debut product, released in late 2008 by founder Rick Kroytz. Named after the California police code for a mentally disturbed person (a fitting brand statement), it is undersized and lightweight with excellent weight distribution — an early hallmark of the boutique American yo-yo scene. The 5150 was sold primarily at the 2009 World Yo-Yo Contest. Two special colorway editions were also released in collaboration with YoYoGuy.com: the "Infinite Illusions Edition" and the "YoYoGuy Edition."

title: Compulsion
content: AboutThe Compulsion is MadHouse's fourth full-size yo-yo and their most technically ambitious release, designed by Rick Kroytz and Hans Baker. It debuted the brand's patented "fusion finish" — a process that permanently bonds full-color photographic-quality designs directly into the aluminum body, producing results indistinguishable from a high-resolution print but durable to the touch. Unlike paint or standard anodizing over a decal, the fusion bond integrates the color into the metal surface itself. The Compulsion features weighted rims for stability, a hub spike for matador tricks, and full butterfly shaping. At approximately $110, it was the brand's premium flagship.

title: EPIC
content: AboutThe EPIC is MadHouse's first hubstack yo-yo, released February 2011 at $118, designed by Rick Kroytz and Nick Pelham. Its defining innovation is the "TA-Ta" system — named for "Trajectory, Assimilation" — a large, cap-style hubstack that simplifies hubstack-based tricks and allows a single hand to simultaneously catch both stacks. The larger stack size makes grabs far more accessible than standard hubstack designs of the period. Slim response pads keep the gap clean for unresponsive play while the hubstacks open a secondary layer of technical tricks.

title: Lucky 7
content: AboutThe Lucky 7 is MadHouse's third yo-yo and first full-size model, released around 2010. Its defining feature is seven evenly-spaced holes drilled around the rim edge, which reduce weight while giving the throw a distinctly unconventional look. The body carries the same "Chalkboard" bead-blast finish as the UnKnown, with a polished area around the engraved side logo. A rare variant — the Lucky 13 Edition — was produced in a run of only 13 units with an acid-washed red/orange finish. The Lucky 7 was available in both Size C and Size A bearing configurations.

title: RAD
content: AboutThe RAD is MadHouse's final known release, launched in 2013 at approximately $99.99. An undersized companion to the Compulsion, it carries the same patented fusion color finish on a smaller, more compact body. The name and aesthetic lean into retro 80s culture — colorways include bold leopard prints and a heavy-metal plaid pattern the brand described as "radical cheetah print and heavy metal plaid." The outer surface is soda-blasted for grinds, while the center section is polished. Each RAD shipped with a MadHouse sticker. After the RAD, the brand went dark with no further releases confirmed.

title: UnKnown
content: AboutThe UnKnown is a limited-production redesign of MadHouse's original 5150, built for the 2009 World Yo-Yo Contest. Approximately 2.5 grams heavier than its predecessor, it features laser-engraved artwork by "IV" on the side and a distinctive "Chalkboard" bead-blast finish in brown/black anodization. The UnKnown's unconventional A-sized bearing — unusual for a full-performance throw of its era — was praised in reviews for its distinct spin feel and quick response characteristics.

title: Maestro
content: AboutThe Maestro is the signature of Naoto Okada, 4A World Champion in both 2009 and 2011. It marked yoyorecreation's first foray into offstring design, built from Delrin plastic in a step-straight profile appropriate for competition offstring play. The larger body offers ample catch area for re-catch tricks while the Delrin construction keeps bounce damage to a minimum. A second 4A plastic, the Aeronaut, was released the same year with a more flared profile.

title: PEAK
content:
About
PEAK is a tri-material competition yoyo built for Zhu Hangfeng, a member of China's champion "Hit" team. It pairs a 6061 aluminum body with 304 stainless steel rims and a PC ring, and uses a full stainless steel U-bearing for a wide, stable catch zone at high speed.

title: MAGN SAVAGE
content:
History / About
MAGN SAVAGE is a magnesium-body, stainless-steel-rim bi-metal variant of Ayumu Kasuga's Savage, released December 18, 2025, as a premium limited material run.

title: Magnum
content: Marcus Koh's second signature model, the Magnum features an H-profile shape wider than the Ares Star, optimized for horizontal and top-on tricks. Includes gilded ring detail on sides. Available in black, pink, and red.

title: Magpie
content:
The design is based on maneuverability and catchability. The yoyo is really wide and have a huge catchzone and gap width to make landing any sort of high tech and slack tricks easy. To combat the width we made the diameter under the midsize to keep the yoyo nimble and fast. Utilizing 7068 metal on this one to optimized weight distribution not just for pure performance and spin time, but also feel, floatiness and fun. Magpie is one of the smartest animal on the planet, they can recognize themselves in a mirror.

Featuring a widish body, smooth lines, super-strong 7068 aluminium, and a weight that feels just right, the Magpie is a super-durable, powerful and dead-smooth throw!

title: Magpie 2.0
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Magpie 2! We have used our experiences gathered throughout the years to fine tune the design. We have get rid of the fingerspin hub and moved the weight to the rim for more power and stability, rounded the rim off for better comfort, decreased the gap width for better bind, and increased the width to enhance the magpie feel and catchability."

title: Makisushi
content:
Makisushi is a special edition of the hugely popular Sushi yo-yo, based on the same CAD. Sushi ranks amongst my top RSO releases, not only because of its unique playfeel but also due to my love for the sushi delicacy and Japanese culture.

The yo-yo was intentionally designed to resemble a sushi roll, which is also known as “makizushi” or “makisushi”.

The anodized black cracked hard coat finish on Makisushi is reminiscent of the seaweed, or “nori”, used to wrap around the sushi rice. The “cracks” on Makisushi have a gold hue, in contrast to the ones on the Mecha-Viszilla SE Edition, which have a silver hue. Unfortunately, I could not make a larger run of Makisushi due to the high-risk nature of the anodization process.

Fun fact: Nori comes in different grades. As a general rule of thumb, the darker the colour, the better. Higher grades have a jet-black hue.

Makisushi will ship with the same components included with the raw Sushi run.

Note: Due to this yo-yo's anodized coating, the finish may wear if the caps and rings are repeatedly installed and removed. For the same reason, the caps and rings are also slightly tighter on Makisushi than its raw counterpart.

title: Malivore
content:
History / About
The Malivore is GWAY Throws’ fourth release. A mid-sized D-bearing monometal, it follows the undersized formula of the Daredevil while pushing the dimensions slightly larger. The design prioritizes an engaging, energetic play character described by the brand as “explosive fun.”

title: Mantis
content:
From One Drop:

"The Marquis was the first yo-yo Blind Box and it was awesome to see it so well received and that everyone had fun with the idea.  So let's do it again!  Time to crack boxes!

This time the run will be 600 units called The Mantis, featuring a selection of solid colors, classic fades, nickel plating and titanium.  They're sealed up just like the Marquis, so you won't have a clue what you're going to get until  you rip open that box!  We have increased the odds of getting a titanium over what it was with our first Blind Box (and increased the number of them from 5  to 10). We also increased the odds of getting a non-solid color overall.

Early civilizations believed the Mantis insect had supernatural powers.  We 're not much believers in magic, but we do think that if you spend just the right amount of time with your Mantis, that hopefully, it'll make your yo-yoing be much more on point.  The Mantis is machined out of 7075 aluminum (except for the Titanium version), and features an organic H shape profile.  It's a deceptive little bugger once you get your hands all over it.

The Mantis is always going to be on the hunt for its next prey and there's only one person that's going to help it get there, YOU!  Go find that bug net hiding back there, these Mantis aren't going to be lingering around for long!

*Titanium Mantis is redesigned to share the same specs and profile as it's counterpart. It features a more opened cup and takes our 19mm Flow Groove."

title: Marina 4
content: AboutThe Marina 4 is Wu Congcong's flagship competition bimetal, described as his "third signature model" from JIGUN. Replacing an earlier polycarbonate-component design with full 7075 aluminum and stainless steel construction, the Marina 4 was engineered for more powerful spin and enhanced stability to match Wu Congcong's 2022 China National Championship performance. Includes Sochi Fat string. Available in Blue with Silver rings at $89.99.

title: Marina9
content: AboutThe Marina9 is Wu Congcong's contest flagship for the post-2025 Prague Worlds season. A 7075 aluminum body bimetal with frosted stainless steel rims, it features a convertible weight system: a base configuration at 66.8g and a contest configuration at 68.5g via included 3D rings. Incorporates design elements from the Insignia line. Available in Silver and Black with Gold ring, at $99.

title: BRS x Markmont. edition Tellos
content:
History / About
The BRS x Markmont. edition Tellos is the fourth installment in the ongoing Markmont x Thesis Yoyos collaborative series (following the Markmont Shop x Thesis "Da Capo"). Co-released through Bladerunners Systems (BRS), a balisong/skill-toy hardware brand, the collab was framed as bridging the yo-yo and balisong communities. Sold in a yellow colorway via both markmont.shop and bladerunnerssystems.com, shipping with Markmont Formulas' hand-twisted nylon "Draken" string.

title: Markmont. Classic
content:
From One Drop:

"***The Markmont Classic is now handled by the Markmont Brand.  Please visit markmont.shop to inquire about it.***

Through the words of Mark Montgomery:

'The Markmont. Classic is the brain baby of this oldschool(ish) player mixed with the genius of more then 4 generations of yo-yo advancement and the build expertise of David Metz and Shawn Nelson. The idea was to make a yo-yo that could sit next to the throws of past and still hold its own weight as a 'classic'. To re-interpret the classic organic butterfly shape but meet the modern day throw play standards. Ultimately, this was a massive feat to accomplish that would eat up quite a bit more brain juice then anticipated, but in the end, the result is exactly as it was intended to be play wise and even aesthetic wise. A far departure from the original Markmont. and Markmont. Next throws, but still nodding to certain specific details like the flat outer faces of the rims and the stylized side effects to match the Markmont. Next to keep it in the family.'"

title: Markmont. Classic Magnum Opus
content: AboutThe Markmont. Classic Magnum Opus (MCMO) is a 7075 aluminum evolution of the original 2014 Markmont. Classic, machined by One Drop Design in Eugene, Oregon. While the outer profile is identical to the 6061 original, the MCMO features squared rim angle transitions and smoothed cup face angles — refinements that translate the Classic's floaty, open-format play style into a denser, faster alloy without sacrificing its expressive character.A Cobalt King prototype run of 15 units (10 sold) was also produced, distinguished by a deep blue finish and priced at $149.Colorways included Gunmetal Gray, Pink/Aqua Fade, Black/Clear Fade, Black, and Cobalt King (prototype).

title: Markmont. Crease
content: AboutThe Crease is a solid titanium yo-yo originating from One Drop Design's private trove of experimental concepts, produced exclusively for the Markmont. Shop. Its angular geometry is blended with rounded and flat areas to offer varied grip positions for aggressive or delicate play styles.Despite its compact size, the Crease carries what Mark describes as "solid heft for its size." Available in Raw Polished and Raw Buffed finishes, with custom color anodizing available through XKKnives.Variants: Raw Polished ($70), Raw Buffed ($65). Sold out.

title: Markmont. FRS Black Canon
content: AboutThe FRS Black Canon is the first entry in Markmont.'s Flat Rim Series — a collection of collaborations with One Drop Design that depart from the organic shapes of the Markmont. Classic. The Black Canon draws inspiration from the vintage Tom Kuhn Silver Bullet, scaling its proportions into a modern pocket throw with a reduced height for stronger in-play stability.The Side Effects axle system allows the throw to be configured responsive or unresponsive. Despite its compact dimensions, the flat rim profile delivers solid rim weight and a distinctly stable play character for its size.Colorways: Black/Silver Fade, Hyper Magenta, Gray/Silver Fade, Clear, Light Teal, Nickel Plated, Purple/Light Teal Fade, Black, Purple, Green Scene (B-grade).

title: Markmont. FRS Blunder Bus

title: Markmont. FRS Project 2
content: AboutThe FRS Project 2 is the second entry in Markmont.'s Flat Rim Series with One Drop Design, conceived as a modernized evolution of the original 2008 MarkMont Project. Where the original was compact and precise, the FRS Project 2 scales up to full competition dimensions with a distinctive catch-zone lip that reduces string gap rub during play.Like all Flat Rim Series throws, it uses One Drop's Side Effects axle system for weight customization, and is finished in Pyramatte for grip and longevity.Colorways: Green Pine, Orange Peel, Purple Opal (plus B-grades in Black, Yellow, Blue, Purple, Orange, Red, Clear, Green). Price: $85. Sold out.

title: MarkMont Next
content:
From One Drop:

"The MarkMont Next stays true to the original. The design imperative was to make the yo-yo that Mark wants. It has the same basic profile as the original with some small but important tweaks. The first difference is that it is made on a lathe whereas the original was made on a mill - the benefit here is improved concentricity. We added a little thickness in the middle so we could put in a Flow Groove response system (the original had pad response). We also added some rim weight to increase the spin time and stability. You'll notice the hub/cup area looks a lot different including a new axle nut that has a unique look not seen before. The finish is soda blasted and nickel plated."

title: Marquis
content:
From One Drop:

"The Marquis is our first yo-yo model to be released in a blind box. Limited to only 400 yo-yos, featuring a variety of finishes as well as five Titanium variants in the mix. They're all sealed up and randomized so even we don't know where they're all going to end up! Imagine picking up a pack of your favorite trading cards, but instead of cardboard, you get a sweet playing yo-yo. With an assortment of finishes, you're bound to find YOUR ultimate prize!

Remember when you thought all that math you learned in class wouldn't help you in life? Think again! Here are the different editions and your chances of scoring them:

The yo-yo itself pays homage to the Halifax prototypes of years back with it's undersized manner and angular design. The jewel-like look and feel inspired it's name. It's a nimble little gem, but with a profound presence on the string. It's small enough to slide into your pocket when you're going about your day, but big enough to shine when the moment is right.

Continuing our commitment to deliver great value, each sealed box will retail for $49. We understand how many hours of labor you guys have to go through to afford a new yo-yo. Your work doesn't go unnoticed. You deserve a little break and some fun while you're at it!

The anticipation in cracking one open is real. Will you be the one to own a Titanium Marquis? Only one way to find out. Good luck and enjoy!

*Titanium Marquis shares the same weight and profile as it's aluminum counterpart, but has a redesigned inner cup, and takes 19mm Flow Groove."

title: Martian+
content: AboutThe Martian+ (Martian Plus) is Wu Congcong's premium signature model under the LEP brand, an enhanced version of the tri-material Martian design at $270. It uses an aluminum body combined with polycarbonate and stainless steel components. Sold through the Lab Exploration Program store.

title: Martian.W
content: AboutThe Martian.W is Wu Congcong's 2024 China National Championship signature model — an expanded, wider evolution of the Martian design. At 50mm width it provides greater error tolerance and enhanced stability for high-difficulty competition tricks. Priced at $145–$160 depending on colorway. Available in Triple Gold, Silver, Silver with Gold ring, and Gold with raw ring.

title: Martis
content: AboutThe Martis is a Martian-series design using 7075 aluminum and patented polycarbonate rings instead of stainless steel — a mid-tier option bridging casual and competitive play. Priced at $55. Available in Silver, Black, Pink, and Purple.

title: Marvel
content:
History / About
The Marvel arrived with a degree of mystery — G2 requested a media embargo on photos during the review period, an unusual move for the era. High Speed YoYo noted it apprehensively but followed the embargo. The Marvel introduces design elements new to G2 at the time — a subtle organic V-shape profile with slightly rounded rims transitioning into the catch zone, whose walls round out partway down before reaching the gap. A departure from the more H-shaped Quake and Aftershock family. At 55mm diameter and 44.12mm wide it sits between the Quake (undersized) and Aftershock (full) in character.

title: Mary
content:
History / About
Mary is part of the signature project. Designed to fit raytsh’s style. 2009 version featuring schmoove rings and our brand new Candodize coating. Smooth and shiny. Candyness increment.

Production Runs

title: Masamaxx
content:
History / About
An extreme heavyweight, roughly 1.5x the weight of a standard yo-yo. Sengoku's own marketing copy explicitly states: "NOT for competition," "NOT for beginners," "throw at your own risk."

title: Masamini
content:
History / About
An undersized bimetal marketed as a mini version of the Masamune — stability that defies its small size.

title: Masamini 2
content:
History / About
Sengoku's own store describes it simply: "The popular Masamini is back with new colors!" A rerelease of the Masamini 2 platform.

title: Master Galaxy
content: One of the first ultra-wide yo-yos to establish the wide-body design standard. Features an H-profile with an impressively wide catch zone, delivering smooth and easy play comparable to the Capsule 2. Designed to balance speedy play with showy trick execution. Gave players confidence on both standard and off-plane tricks. Available in Splash (Blue/Purple), Splash (Gold/Green), and Splash (Black/Silver). Spawned the Re:Master Galaxy (2017) and Neo Master Galaxy lineage. Price: $99.99.

title: Matrixx-Cube
content:
History / About
Matrixx-Cube (SS-002) is a light-up square yoyo shipped partially disassembled as a build-it-yourself kit, with a light-up feature powered by two CR927 button cells and a magnetic on/off switch. Its name/logo are styled after YoYoJam's "Matrixx" as a homage, not a licensed collaboration.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C- thin (upgradeable to standard C)

title: Mecha-Bapezilla
content:
History / About
Mecha-Bapezilla is RSO's first-ever collaboration, a modern-manufacturing reimagining of the 1990s Anti-Yo Bapezilla with Sonny Patrick, keeping the original's 52x40mm dimensions while eliminating its vibe issues. 49 units: 29 Raw, 16 Gold electroplate, 4 Rose Gold electroplate (only 1 Rose Gold sold at retail).Distinct from the later 2021 "Mecha-Bapezilla Side Effects OG & Viszilla Editions" final-release SKU already in the archive, which uses a different bearing/response spec and a cracked hard-coat finish.

title: Mecha-Bapezilla Side Effects Edition
content:
The following is archived from RSO's website:

THE YO-YO

The non-SE Mecha-Bapezilla was RSO’s first collaboration and one that helped give the company the initial push it needed (this is something I will always feel indebted to Sonny for). Over the years, different versions such as the Mecha-Viszilla, OG Edition and Godzilla Edition were released and were exceptionally popular. Collaborations with Sonny also allowed RSO to experiment with SEs in the YWETi SE Edition MK I and II, the first SE titanium yo-yos ever made. With the Gravity, I had designed what I thought was the perfect SE titanium yo-yo.

The Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition halves were actually machined at about the same time as the YWETi SE Edition MK II in the fourth quarter of 2020. However, due to the limited availability of SEs and NSK DS bearings (I channelled what I had to YWETi and Gravity), the Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition has taken a while to see the light of day.

THE PERFECT MIX

The Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition comes equipped with premium parts including silver flat cap SEs from One Drop and platinum Double Straight C bearings from NSK.

This yo-yo is, in fact, the second SE version of the Bapezilla line. The first Bapezilla with SEs was the Bapezilla 2, a peculiar yo-yo. It was machined by One Drop and had a rough blasted finish called "Slip Matte Type III Hard Coat", which tended to cut strings. Players resorted to smoothening its surface by rubbing it on denim. Initially, it was not as well-received as the OG Bapezilla. About 400 pieces were made and sold in batches at retailers and eventually on Massdrop. Despite being heavily discounted, they took a while to sell. Recently, the demand for the Bapezilla 2 has increased, with people scouring forums for it.

The Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition has the revised more vertical nipple design like the YWETi MK II, staying true to the aesthetic of the OG Bapezilla. "If it ain't broke, don't fix it", people say. I believe that a SE version of the OG design would have done better. Models like the Static Responsives Co. Parlay and Sudo, essentially SE versions of the OG Bapezilla design with minor tweaks, have been fan favourites. The Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition is derived from the OG Bapezilla CAD and is the closest representation of what a SE Edition of the OG Bapezilla will play.

This is the last collaboration with Sonny. It has been an incredible ride with a meaningful friendship forged. RSO will be moving towards independent releases and original designs in the year 2022.

MECHA-BAPEZILLA SE EDITION

YWETi SIDE SE MK I

WHAT’S IN THE BOX

Certificate of authenticity IN THE FORM OF AN INSTRUCTION SHEET

ROCK THE BABY MECHA-BAPEZILLA ENAMEL PIN

A PAIR OF MAROON 19MM TYPE 40 RSO LANDING PADS

CUSTOM STRING BY ARLEQUIN STRINGS

title: Mecha-Bapezilla Side Effects OG & Viszilla Editions
content:
The following is archived from RSO's website:

These Mecha-Bapezilla: Side Effects (SE) Special Editions are the last yo-yos of the Mecha-Bapezilla line. No more Mecha-Bapezillas will be made. There are two colorways of this final release - an “Original Gangsta (OG)” colorway in the tribal blue and green of the original Bapezilla and a “Viszilla” colorway in a black cracked hard coat finish reminiscent of the Godzilla you see at the movies. The cracks on the latter can barely be felt by the hand. The package includes the same box and accessories as the regular Mecha-Bapezilla SE Edition.

meta.yya_weight: 67g With One Drop Flat Caps Side Effects

title: Mecha-Viszilla
content:
History / About
Mecha-Viszilla is an "Evil Sonny" box-art variant on the Bapezilla platform, with a Star Wars-themed certificate, made with Anti-Yo's Sonny Patrick. This is a standalone 2020 release, distinct from the cracked hard-coat Viszilla colorway included in the 2021 "Mecha-Bapezilla Side Effects OG & Viszilla Editions" already in the archive.

title: Cadet
content: HistoryThe Medalist line was distributed by Strombeck (Strombecker) Mfg. Co. of Moline, Illinois, in the mid-1960s after Duncan's bankruptcy. The Yo-Yo Museum says the Medalist line was identical in shape and profile to earlier Duncan models, differing in name, stamp and colors. The line sold the Cadet for 49 cents, the Trickmaster for 79 cents and the Trophy for $1; the Trophy was plastic and the other two wood. The Cadet (No. 1044) corresponds to the Duncan Beginner, with bi-colored halves. The Museum dates its carded example to 1967-1968.

title: Trickmaster
content: HistoryThe Medalist line was distributed by Strombeck (Strombecker) Mfg. Co. of Moline, Illinois, in the mid-1960s after Duncan's bankruptcy. The Yo-Yo Museum says the Medalist line was identical in shape and profile to earlier Duncan models, differing in name, stamp and colors. The line sold the Cadet for 49 cents, the Trickmaster for 79 cents and the Trophy for $1; the Trophy was plastic and the other two wood. The Trickmaster (No. 1077) corresponds to the Duncan Tournament, in striped and solid colors. The Museum shows one-piece examples dated 1965 and a three-piece carded example dated 1967-1968. A Strombeck family member told collector David Hall that Strombeck bought Duncan's yo-yos and machines as a favor during Duncan's bankruptcy and never planned to replace Duncan; the Museum also notes early stamps were of poor quality.

title: Trophy
content: HistoryThe Medalist line was distributed by Strombeck (Strombecker) Mfg. Co. of Moline, Illinois, in the mid-1960s after Duncan's bankruptcy. The Yo-Yo Museum says the Medalist line was identical in shape and profile to earlier Duncan models, differing in name, stamp and colors. The Trophy (No. 1400) is the plastic model, equivalent to the Duncan Imperial, in solid colors. Museum examples carry Boston Bruins and Boston Celtics logos stamped in gold foil and are dated 1967-1968; it likely used a metal axle.

title: Mediocre S (Abandonware)
content:
History / About
Mediocre S is a solid brass, Side Effect-format throw from Return Bottoms (also operating as Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop), sold in a 10-unit limited production run for $20 on the brand's Bigcartel store under the status "Abandonware." It uses One Drop-brand "OD Flow Groove" response pads and ships with included brass microcaps/flat caps.
"OD" in the listing refers to One Drop Yoyos as the maker of the response pad hardware used — not a collaboration or co-release with that company. The brand's forum history separately documents a killed project called "That B" after One Drop enforced IP control over its Side Effect axle/bearing system, but That B is a distinct, separately-archived product ($85, B-size bearing, silicone brake pads, 12mm axle) and is not the same item as Mediocre S.

title: Mega Crash
content: Originally designed as a special performance yo-yo for the Hong Kong-based Let's Yo team, the Mega Crash is the world's largest hybrid 1A yo-yo. The Gamma Crash design was scaled up 22.99mm in diameter to reach 80mm — matching a typical offstring yo-yo in size while remaining technically a 1A throw. Because of its extraordinary size combined with stainless steel rims, it generates immensely powerful spin. Solid POM colorways feel soft; clear PC colorways feel hard and lighter. Price: ~$80–$100.

title: Mega SpinFaktor
content: About the Mega SpinFaktorThe Mega SpinFaktor features nickel-plated bronze weight rings and a ceramic ball bearing for reduced friction and extended sleep times. Rick Wyatt used it to break the AYYA World Record for longest sleeping yo-yo in 2001. The model is housed in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History collection.

title: melatonin
content:
About the melatonin
The melatonin is ilinx Toys' first major production release, launched in March 2022. Founder Ross Levine drew design inspiration from the hormone melatonin and its sedative, soft effects. The rims pillow outward gently and the hub curves flow like a billowed sheet, giving the yoyo a smooth, organic silhouette. At 54.5 mm diameter and 39.8 mm width it sits noticeably slimmer than a full-size competition throw, yet the weight distribution and gap keep it fully trick-capable.
Levine cited the YYJ Speeder 2 and Recreational Revolution No. 9 as design references, incorporating grind-friendly surfaces and enough catch-zone width for string-intensive play. The melatonin ships with a Size C CenterTrac bearing and ilinx's own 19mm slim mouse-pad response. It was sold through YoYoSam and YoYoExpert in Clear, Clear/Red, and Red colorways. The melatonin is best enjoyed with a glass of warm milk.

title: Melzi
content: AboutThe Melzi is Tomoki Toyama's second Yoyofriends signature model, following the Da Vinci. Named after Francesco Melzi — Leonardo da Vinci's closest disciple — it features an aggressive wrapped stainless steel ring design for fast acceleration, high speed, and enhanced power. Wide at 48mm with a notably wide gap for modern trick sets.

title: Memento
content: Memento was MikeMonty’s 2020 aluminum release, named for the Stoic phrase memento mori. Its comfortable organic profile was informed by Mike’s experience with the One Drop MarkMont Classic and Basecamp Jackknife. Jordan “ChaosGow” assisted with the individual design work.The first run used a 4.6 mm gap and appeared in red, blue, gray, and a red/blue halfswap. A second run launched July 3, 2020 with a 4.4 mm gap and orange, purple, pink, Olive Branch, gray, clear, and documented halfswap variants. It retailed for $65 and included a ZipLine Skyline III string.

yya_gallery_images.title: Orange Mike Monty Memento yo-yo in side profile

title: Menehune
content:
The Menehune was Buzz-On's first undersized yoyo. Plastic body with inset aluminum weight rings. The first release had unengraved weight rings, while later releases had engraved weight rings. The Menehune and Element X were the yoyos that introduced the SPR system in Buzz On's yoyos. Original Menehune used a B sized bearing. The general specs for the Menehune's were. Original price was $29.99

OLYMPUS DIGITAL CAMERA

Dave's Skill Toy's edition included recessed SPR kits.

title: Menehune 2
content: Released in 2007, exclusively on YoYoGuy.com. Used an A bearing SPR kit, instead of the B sized SPR.

title: Menehune Pro
content: Limited edition version of the Menehune. Recessed SPR with a C bearing and flush mounted weight rings. 250 pieces made in white and black. The original price was $45. The red/orange version below, was featured on Buzz-On's website. Although it seems they were never released.

title: Meniscus (Prototype)
content:
About
Meniscus was a monthly Project Torsion blend from Throw-Yo Threads, offered only to Patreon subscribers in October 2026. No public retail release has been confirmed.

title: Mentsch
content:
About the Mentsch
The Mentsch — Yiddish for a person of good character — is Mr. Mazal Top's tri-material hybrid yoyo, released via pre-order in 2023 at $65 USD. It features an extremely thin-walled polycarbonate body (1.5mm wall thickness) paired with chunky stainless steel outer rims for rim-weighted stability, and a blasted-finish aluminum flat cup hub. The brand claims the weight distribution rivals bimetals priced over $100. A YoYoExpert community forum thread was created in May 2023 to discuss the design. Each Mentsch ships with a 30-pack of response pads, a premium ceramic hybrid bearing (pre-installed), a custom collector's hard case and velvet pouch, and wooly string and string rosin samples. Available colorways included pink and clear.

title: Mercy 3
content: AboutThe Mercy 3 is a wide-body competition bi-metal featuring oversized stainless steel rings that push weight to the outer rim for extended spin time. The stainless steel ring profile is comfortable on catch. Available in Blue/Silver and Silver/Green/Purple.

title: Mercy 4
content: AboutThe Mercy 4 is a "high performance outer ring bi-metal" with a competition-ready blasted surface and powerful spin times. Features an extensive colorway lineup including Ace Girl character options. Available in Pink, Navy, Turquoise, Lavender, Silver/Black/Pink, Silver/Red/Green, Red/Black Ring, Green/Black Ring, and more.

title: Mercy 5
content: AboutThe Mercy 5 is a fast and nimble competition-ready bi-metal with powerful stainless steel outer rings. A continued iteration of AceYo's outer ring competition formula.

title: Mercy 6
content: AboutThe Mercy 6 features what AceYo describes as "the most extreme design yet" — rings widened and flared outward for an improved rim weight ratio that delivers enhanced power, stability, and extended spin. The expanded V-shape profile is suited for competitive play and advanced tricks including horizontals. Features Ace Girl anime character engravings in the cup. Available in Green, Blue, Mint, Gold, Pink, Black/Gold/Blue, Black/Silver/Purple, Red/Silver/Light Blue, and Red/Silver/Gold.

title: Mercy 7
content: AboutThe Mercy 7 merges elements of prior Mercy iterations into a refined V-shape suited for advanced tricks and horizontal play. Thick stainless steel rims deliver stability and extended spin. Released in 10th anniversary colorways and extensive Ace Girl character options including Hinata and Konoka. Available in Gray (Ace Girl Hinata), Black (Ace Girl Konoka), Green, Shiny Silver/Black Rims, 10th Anniversary Silver/Orange/Teal Acidwash Gold Rims, Light/Dark Rainbow, Pink, and Black/Rainbow Ring variants.

title: Mercy 7075
content: AboutThe Mercy 7075 is a premium 7075 aluminum variant of the Mercy series, delivering stronger spin times and more extreme weight distribution than the standard 6061 model. Soft blasted with multicolor splash anodization. Available in Black/Red/Green, Black/Green/Blue, Black/Silver/Turquoise, and Black/Silver/Red.

title: Mercy 8 (Inner Ring)
content: AboutThe Mercy 8 inner ring version offers an alternative ring placement philosophy to the outer ring variant. Smooth, stable, and long-spinning. Released simultaneously with the outer ring version to give players a choice of construction approach.

title: Mercy 8 (Outer Ring)
content: AboutThe Mercy 8 outer ring version features extremely beefy outer rims on a wider-stance body, creating a stable, long-spinning, powerful throw. Well-reviewed as one of the best price-to-performance bi-metals in the series. Available in multiple colorways.

title: Meridion
content: Meridion is a 3D printed return top designed for unresponsive 1A/3A/5A play.

title: Messiah
content: AboutThe Messiah is the signature of Takahiro Iizuka, whose hyper-complex trick style drew international attention at the 2009 World YoYo Contest. At 49.5mm, it is one of the most undersized competition throws ever produced by yoyorecreation — a deliberate choice to match Iizuka's need for a fast, precise instrument. The step-round profile and 68g weight provide stability despite the reduced diameter.Iizuka would later receive the SIX (2014) as a second signature model. The Messiah 666 (2023) revisited the concept as a full bi-metal combining Messiah and SIX DNA.

title: Metal Ascent
content: AboutThe Metal Ascent is OFFSET's aluminum entry point, bridging the plastic Ascent and the competition-grade Deviant and Outlier lines. A dual-bearing switching system lets players swap between responsive and unresponsive configurations without tools, lowering the barrier for beginners moving off plastic for the first time. At 50mm wide it offers a substantial catch zone for learners.

title: Metal Capsule
content:
About
Metal Capsule reconstructs Dale Tubat's original 3D-printed Capsule in a 6061 aluminum body, done in collaboration with UNPRLD (Unparalleled), for improved precision, spin axis accuracy, and weight balance over the 3D-printed original. Retains the signature capsule-insert system for vertical floor-spin tricks. Engravings by @dad.father and @failureisunknown. Colorways: Red Race Car, Gold Brick, Green Teddy, Blue Battle, Black Unknown. Priced at $59.99.

title: Metal Drifter
content: AboutThe Metal Drifter was Duncan's original mass-market entry-level aluminum yo-yo, released in 2010 as a wide, wing-shaped unresponsive throw that made quality metal performance accessible at around $20. Every Metal Drifter includes a counterweight die, making it an economical single-purchase entry into 5A (Freehand/counterweight) play. The Metal Drifter introduced thousands of players to unresponsive aluminum yo-yos and remains in the catalog as a value offering.

title: Metal Drifter XL
content: AboutThe Metal Drifter XL is an oversized variant of the Metal Drifter, stretching the diameter to 65 mm — well above full-size — while retaining the same CNC aluminum construction and 19 mm response system. The larger diameter creates a cavernous catch zone ideal for players learning complex multi-layer string formations, and the heavier 69.9 g weight produces strong gyroscopic stability. It remains one of the few oversized metal yo-yos available at a mid-range price point.

title: Metal Harbinger
content:
From MK1:

"The Harbinger is a long-spinning aluminum yoyo perfect for the entire host of classic and responsive yoyo tricks. Designed by Mk1 Yoyos in collaboration with Spinworthy of Australia."

title: Metal Object_138
content:
About
Metal Object_138 is a yo-yo-shaped "object" for contemporary living spaces that can also be played as a yo-yo. Heavier and wider than a standard throw, it may behave unexpectedly during play.

title: Metal Racer
content:
A metal yo-yo first released at 44CLASH 2014 in Asia, followed by a 2015 release in North America.

Known for the plastic Racer Caps which are also compatible with other yo-yos that use Freehand Zero caps.

The yo-yo is also compatible with Duncan's Mod Spacers and Performance Rings.

title: Metal Skyva
content: About the Metal SkyvaThe Metal Skyva is the aluminum version of MagicYoYo's SKYVA collaboration with Jeffrey Pang of Luftverk. The machined 6061 aluminum body uses a very fine media-blast technique for a premium matte feel. A Delrin (POM) finger spin cup is integrated into the hub — chosen for its "buttery smooth," low-friction properties during finger spin tricks. The weight distribution differs significantly from the plastic SKYVA, providing more stability and spin time at the cost of some of the original's floaty character. Response is handled by the Luftverk LuftPAD. A Metal Skyva 2 followed with updated colorways. Available in Pink with Blue Cap, Purple with Yellow Cap, Green with Green Cap, and Red with Black Cap.

title: Metal SpinGadget
content:
About
The Metal SpinGadget is SpinGear's direct aluminum successor to the plastic SpinGadget, described by the brand as a "faithful metalization" — reproducing the same silhouette and feel in an aluminum shell. Positioned as an intermediate learner model, it ships with a D-size bearing for responsive play but can be upgraded with a KK (Konkave) bearing for bind/unresponsive play.
It has been released in over 30 colorways including Ti Color (premium anodize), Gold, Aqua Blue, Ice Blue, Raspberry, Olive, Snow, Khaki, Matte Indigo, Sakura, Red, Maroon, Gunmetallic, Black/Gold, and Gold/Black, as well as no-logo and outlet blemish variants at reduced prices.
A premium sub-variant called the MASTER PIECE was produced in limited Champagne/Black cap and Champagne/White cap colorways at ¥4,400.

title: Metal SpinGadget Pro
content:
About
The Metal SpinGadget Pro is a refined iteration on the Metal SpinGadget, shaving 5 grams from the standard model (56g vs. 61g) while maintaining the same diameter and profile. Compatible with SpinGear's SGHG Pad and SGHG Stainless Steel ball bearing accessories. Standard colorway is Red (¥4,800); outlet stock in Brown, Black, Pink, and Silver.

title: Metal Tornado
content: The Metal Tornado is the full-metal version of the Tornado, retaining the distinctive extended cover-cap design that wraps the rim and sides for mid-spin hand-catching. Duralumin construction throughout.

title: Metalhead
content: AboutMetalhead is Rain City's collaboration with Throws N' Brews, designed to be the brand's most performance-oriented throw since the original Hipster Highlife. Traditional rounded hub for fingerspins. Music-themed packaging. Includes two custom engraved guitar picks (0.5mm and 0.6mm) plus a random LEGO musician minifigure.

title: Meteor
content: About the MeteorThe Meteor is Hiroyuki Suzuki's first all-aluminum signature yo-yo, featuring slightly thicker rims than the Speeder series for enhanced stability and a smooth mirror-capped presentation. It was developed to achieve the spin consistency required for competitive-level play, and Suzuki used it to sweep the Japan Nationals in back-to-back years.

title: METEOR TYPE-Y
content: About the METEOR TYPE-YThe METEOR TYPE-Y is a tribute to Hiroyuki Suzuki's YoYoJam-era Meteor Type signature model, re-released under sOMEThING. The aluminum body with plastic caps retains the hybrid construction approach of the original. Accessible entry point in the sOMEThING lineup at $84.99 USD. Colorways: NY Green, Hot Pink.

title: Mg DIFFUSION
content:
History / About
Mg DIFFUSION is a magnesium-alloy remake of YYR's classic plastic Diffusion, released November 21, 2025. Per the listing, the surface may show uneven coloring or minor scratches due to magnesium processing.

title: MG Lithium
content: AboutThe MG Lithium is a collaboration between Sochi Company and JIGUN, designed with Luckey Yulin Li. A 100-piece limited run released in 2023 at $250, it uses a magnesium alloy body paired with stainless steel rims — recreating the Sochi Company Lithium design with premium 2023 materials. The 2.5:1 aspect ratio creates an extreme hollow sensation in play. Available in White only.

title: Mico
content: History / AboutShion Araya signature translating compact competition geometry into an unusually heavy full-stainless construction.

title: Micro Caps Side Effects
content:
Micro Caps are currently available in:

Aluminum: Multiple Colors

Brass

Titanium

Micro Caps are one of 4 different Side Effects to be made in Titanium by Brian Fellhoelter. They are made of Grade 5 Titanium, and 25 sets of each were made.

title: MicroMo
content: About the MicroMoThe MicroMo is the signature model of Dr. Mo (Mo Chavez), miniaturizing the standard YoYoJam construction to an extraordinary 44.2mm diameter while retaining a Size C bearing and silicone O-ring response. The nickel-bronze rims provide edge weight needed to keep such a tiny yo-yo spinning. Its compact size makes string tension management critical, rewarding players with highly developed technique.

title: Midship (Prototype)
content:
About
Midship is a G Squared Yoyos prototype notable for using two separate stainless steel rims for weight distribution and stability. It runs G19 pads.

title: MiLARGE
content: AboutThe MiLARGE (Large + Mirage) is an oversized version of the Mirage, approximately 6% larger in all dimensions. JT designed it to address a gap in the oversized market for a model with straightforward operability — it avoids the quirks typical of oversized designs while delivering the powerful, stable spin that comes from a larger yo-yo. Available in Matte Purple EZONE Special Edition and additional colorways. Also sold as part of the Mirage Box Set ($229.99) alongside a Blue miniRAGE and Gray Mirage.

title: Mild
content: The Mild is the signature model of Shuyun Tang, 2022 US Nationals International Open Division Champion. A 6061 bi-metal with stainless steel rims, the Mild is slightly more compact than the Wilderness with a precise, responsive feel tuned to Tang's aggressive 1A style. Sold with a Shuyun Tang photo card.

title: Milder
content: The Milder is Shuyun Tang's second signature model for W1LD, stepping up from the Mild with titanium rims in place of stainless steel. The result is a lighter, faster competition throw that retains the wide, powerful character of the Mild while elevating performance to the titanium tier. Limited availability; includes Tang photo card.

title: Mile Highbrid
content: AboutThe Mile Highbrid is the final yoyo from Mile High Yoyo Club, combining a Delrin (POM) body with 7068 aluminum rims in the same organic silhouette as The Gnome mold. Debuted at the Colorado State YoYo Contest on November 30, 2024; wider release via YoYoExpert on November 4, 2025. Each purchase included a "decision coin" with Good Guy and Bad Guy sides. Bobafret (Dave) noted at the YYE listing: "it has been a long fun ride" — confirming this as the brand's closing product.Early local colorways included Good Guy, Bad Guy, Mile High Sunrise, Hero, Villain, and Clear. The YYE-exclusive colorways were Logan (yellow POM / blue rings), Magneto (red POM / purple rings), and Bape (white POM / teal rings).

title: The Gnome
content: AboutThe Gnome is the signature throw of Mile High Yoyo Club — an undersized 7068 aluminum organic designed with a fingerspin dimple and undercut rims for thumb grinds. All editions share the same mold and specs; each drop introduced new engravings, colorways, or collaborator artwork. Sales were conducted exclusively through Instagram DMs and local club meets at PlayForge Games and The Rabbit Hole Café in the Denver/Littleton area.Editions1st Run — Higby Gnome (early 2023): Two colorways with art by legendary yoyo artist John Higby. Sold out immediately.Forge Gnome — Fire & Water (Spring 2023): Two colorways; exclusive to PlayForge Games, Littleton, CO.Buddha Gnome (Spring 2023): Peace/meditation theme with "Om Mani Padme Hum" engraving; art by Nathan Bottcher.Gnometrooper (Oct–Nov 2023): Stormtrooper-themed; nods to Dave's 501st Legion hobby; art by Nathan Bottcher. Released in black and yellow (Halloween) colorways. Sold through YoYoExpert and local meets. $69.99.Nickel Plated Gnome (Nov 2023): Nickel plating by Denver Metal Finishing.Nicky Gnome (Jan 2024): Bundled with the GnomeHed counterweight + HedStand in a collab combo with Dedhed Designs.DedGnome + ShroomHed (March 2024): Custom ghost engraving; bundled with Dedhed Designs' ShroomHed counterweight. Sold out immediately. Collab with Dedhed Designs.PokéNōm (April 2024): Pokémon-inspired double-sided engraving; art by Nathan Bottcher (yoyoretro). ~60 units. Released at PlayForge April 6 then online April 20.UNgnome (April 20, 2024): Final run of The Gnome mold. ~60 units. Released on 4/20.

title: Milk
content: About the MilkThe Milk is Crucial's original flagship yo-yo, released in 2008 by founder Paul Yath following eight years as a competitive player. It was among the first high-performance Delrin (POM) yo-yos ever produced and became widely cited as a landmark in precision plastic yo-yo design. Its organic, rounded profile influenced a generation of plastic throws and established Crucial as a leading voice in the art of machined plastic.

title: MINI AUTOSCOPY
content:
About
Mini Autoscopy is a compact entry in Hajime Miura's Autoscopy family — YYR's own copy ties its design to Miura's favorite Quad Four shape rather than a straightforward shrink of the full-size Autoscopy. Undersized throw retaining full-size performance, positioned as a technique/control challenge.

title: Mini Banshee
content:
About
Mini Banshee is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2022. This model has been retired. title: MiNi Hummingbird
content: AboutThe MiNi Hummingbird brings the legendary Hummingbird platform down to undersized proportions, packing extreme weight distribution and performance into a compact 47mm frame through brass rim rings for maximum outer density. Despite its small size, it retains the Hummingbird's signature character — aggressive, fast, and powerful.

title: Mini Krown
content: A miniaturized version of Shinya Kido's iconic Krown, designed as an undersized EDC while preserving the competition character of the original. Signature: Shinya Kido.

title: Mini Mo-Tu
content: About the Mini Mo-TuThe Mini Mo-Tu is an undersized Butterfly yo-yo designed for Dr. Mo (Mo Chavez), featuring a compact profile for intricate string work. Its removable side caps reveal an inner rim ideal for thumb grinds, giving it performance depth beyond its diminutive size. The brass rims concentrate weight at the edges for extended spin.

title: Mini Panzer
content:
History / About
Mini Panzer (SS-001) is produced under the Sturm Panzer SS sub-brand by former Team YoYoJam member ZhaoYuan Liu ("PHENOM"), marketed as the world's smallest playable/bind-capable production yoyo — smaller than a 1-yen coin/US penny — inspired by the YoYoJam Mini-Jam. It has gone through several generations: a 2020 original (with a limited "SECRET PROTOTYPE" bonus even smaller than the retail unit), a 2021 packaging/body update, a 2022 second generation with a more H-profile-leaning shape and anti-rust brass coating, and the current 2024 version adding a dual-thin-bearing setup and a new dedicated axle. A gold/silver-plated "SS-001DX Mini-Panzer EDITION" (on the 2020 body) was also released with a light-up display box and necklace chain.

title: Mini-Panzer Economy
content:
History / About
Mini-Panzer Economy (SS-001z) is a responsive, economy-tier variant of the Mini Panzer, shipping oil-injected and ready to play as a return top out of the box. Currently classified by the brand as a "novelty toy" with candy-store-style bonus stickers.

title: Mini Peregrine X
content: AboutThe Mini Peregrine X delivers full-sized performance in a true undersized 41mm body, using large stainless steel or brass rims for unprecedented power and stability at small scale. The unusual combination of tiny diameter and heavy rim weight enables long combos and horizontal string tricks that most undersized throws cannot handle.
