title: MINI Ti
content: AboutYoyofriends' MINI Ti is an undersized titanium yo-yo designed as an everyday-carry option, drawing weight distribution cues from the Hummingbird and Sunbird series. At 44mm and 58g, it is exceptionally light and fast for a titanium throw, yet remains stable and capable for serious tricks with rim weight pushed toward the outer edges.

title: Mini Ti KOI
content:
About
Mini Ti Koi takes yoyofriends' popular Ti Koi and shrinks it down into a genuinely pocketable form. To keep the smaller body from feeling underwhelming, it uses a smaller-diameter D-size bearing, delivering a throwing sensation close to a full-size model.

title: MiniJam
content: About the MiniJamThe MiniJam was remarkable for its extremely compact size, featuring the same composite construction as the SpinFaktor scaled down dramatically. It uses molded dimples rather than a formal response system. The signature model of Philip Travelant, released in 2001.

title: Mirage
content: AboutThe Mirage was released in 2019 and became an instant hit. A full-sized 6061 aluminum monometal, its mid-sized H-profile with a refined silhouette inspired by the LaPua design balances speed and power across 1A, 3A, and 5A play styles. Available in Gray, Gold, and Mint Green colorways. The Mirage line was subsequently updated in 2020, 2024, and continues in production.

title: Mirage ’20
content: AboutThe Mirage '20 is the 2020 renewal of the Mirage. Sized up approximately 2mm from the original while reducing weight, it maintains the same power output with improved versatility across hand sizes and skill levels. Positioned as an all-around performer and part of the ongoing Mirage line.

title: Mirage ’24
content: AboutThe Mirage '24 is the current-production Mirage, released in 2024 with an expanded width of approximately 48mm for improved maneuverability and string-trick confidence. The overall silhouette carries forward from the '20, updated to meet modern competitive standards. Available in JAPAN Edition, Light Green, Light Purple, Shiny Black, Shiny Gold, and Shiny Stone Blue colorways. A 7075 ESD variant (Mirage ESD '24) was also released simultaneously.

title: Mirage ESD ’24
content: AboutThe Mirage ESD '24 is the 7075 "extra super duralumin" premium version of the Mirage '24. At 68.3g it is approximately 2g heavier than its 6061 counterpart, with nearly double the strength and refined wall thickness for more precise weight redistribution. ESD variants have been released alongside the '19 and '20 Mirage generations as well. Available in Silver Blue and Super Light Yellow.

title: Mirage SB
content: AboutThe Mirage SB is a complete re-engineering of the Mirage chassis for a small/Size D bearing (5×11×5mm). The outer rim is thickened to compensate for the changed mass distribution, with a lightened center and adjusted diameter to achieve enhanced power and stability characteristics specific to small bearing play. Available in Matte Gray.

title: Miro
content:
About
Miro is Edition's compact bimetal design, built around the idea of "pocket-able performance." Wide extruding stainless steel rims make up almost two-thirds of the weight per half, concentrating mass at the rim to handle dense technical mounts and improve accuracy without sacrificing the feel of a larger throw.
Per-half breakdown: stainless steel ring 21.4g, 6061 aluminum body 9.6g.

title: Yoyogi
content: History / AboutMister Babache is a Switzerland-based manufacturer of juggling equipment founded in 1985, known for its diabolos. The YoYo Wiki states that at one point it produced its own yo-yos and lists the Yoyogi among them. No further specifications or dates could be verified.

title: Mk1 Brass Exia
content:
History / About
The original Exia was released in 2020 and had three production runs, making it the most popular Mk1 yoyo to date. The Brass Exia swaps out the Exia's steel weight rings for heavier brass rings, giving it more overall mass and power while retaining the Exia's wide wing shape, comfortable catch, smooth blast finish, higher-grade aluminum alloy, and 10mm axle.
The first run released June 30, 2023, in a limited batch of 120 pieces across 3 colorways (Lilac, Green, Blue). A second production run followed in December 2023 with 150 pieces across 3 more colorways (Clear, Rose, and a Black "signature edition" colorway for Mk1 team rider Elliot Ding). It is an unresponsive, bind-required yoyo aimed at advanced trick play.

title: Kyrios
content:
History / About
The Kyrios is the signature yo-yo of MK1 team player Max Choo. An aggressive and well-balanced bimetal, the Kyrios features a 6061 aluminum body with steel rims for a powerful, competition-ready throw. The collaboration between Max and MK1 resulted in a design that reflects his precise, technical playing style.

title: Penumbra
content:
History / About
An ultra-wide premium bimetal yo-yo with an incredible feeling of lightness and power. The Penumbra uses a 7068 aluminum body with stainless-steel rims for a combination of speed and stability that belies its broad 55mm width. Each colorway is the signature edition of one of the MK1 Yoyos team members, making the Penumbra as much a celebration of the team as a technical achievement.

title: Onda
content:
History / About
Onda — meaning "wave" in Portuguese — is a signature yo-yo MK1 designed for its Brazilian team player Bernardo (the "BMP" in the name). It pairs a 7075 aluminum body with One Drop's Side Effect axle system and a sweeping profile that flows from one curve to the next. The 7075/Side Effects combination makes it particularly durable, and swapping Side Effects lets players tune weight and looks.
Design Notes
In the designer's words, the goal was a yo-yo that feels comfortable in the hand while still solid and powerful when thrown — minimal, carry-anywhere, and robust in every throw. Colorways draw on fluid, dynamic themes: the ocean, lava, space, and air.
Colorways
Clear, Laserfade, Oilslick, Purple Nebula, Magma Drops, Ocean Wave.

title: MN AUTOSCOPY
content:
History / About
MN AUTOSCOPY is a monometal aluminum version of Hajime Miura's Autoscopy signature, released November 22, 2025.

title: Mo-vitation
content: History / AboutEarlier retail design whose shape contributed to Peter Pong's later P.Wave signature.

title: Mobile Gamer
content: AboutThe second release in Rain City's 2024 "12 months, 12 yoyos" initiative. A stainless steel micro slimline designed to fill a gap for tiny slimline throws. Default unresponsive; add lube for responsive play. Three colorways: Game Over (Black), You Win (Rainbow), Free Loot Box (Gold).

About

title: Mod 44
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Modular 44 is Freshly Dirty's first yo-yo design with interchangeable rims. By using a standard hub-to-rim interface that is compatible with all Mod44 products from Freshly Dirty, one yoyo can suddenly take on many different forms. The Mod44 uses an O-ring system to keep the rim aligned and spinning smoothly, even after extended periods of regular wear and tear.

For tips and tricks on how to remove and install rims, click here.

One of the most exciting aspects of the Mod44 is open source rim design. Throughout the prototyping process, 3D printing was used to develop new designs and test them in real time. Freshly Dirty supports community members who wish to design and print their own rims. For more information as well as file downloads, click here."

The Mod 44 comes in both C bearing and D bearing models, giving players even more choice about their Mod 44 play.

Mod 44 Rims

There are a multitude of rims available for the Mod 44, both for sale and available to print at home using a 3D printer. That doesn't include other home-made rims the community has come up with over the years. Before getting started with Mod 44 rims, it's important to know how to safely take of old rims and install new rims. Thankfully, Freshly Dirty has you covered in their tutorial video.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qcUMKGc02oc

Mod 44 Rim Removal

To remove a rim, first place your index finger along the inside of the rim as shown. Next, place your thumb on the “44” logo to create some leverage. While holding the other side of the yoyo with your opposite hand, simply pull the rim at a single point until the O-ring is visible. Some force will be necessary. Repeat this process 2-3 times around different points of the yoyo until the rim is no longer held in place by the O-ring. 

Next, pull the ring straight off of the metal hub. Be sure to pull the rim straight off the side of the yoyo and not at an angle to make this easier.

Mod 44 Rim Installation

First, align the ring on the body of the yoyo by snapping it onto the metal hub. The fit is snug to allow smooth performance. This is the same position your rim was in after releasing it from the O-ring.

Next, squeeze the rim over the O-ring at 2-3 different points around the yoyo. Try using your thumbs to press on the metal hub as shown while the rest of your fingers grip the outside of the rim. Some force will be necessary. Repeat 2-3 times around different points on the yoyo until the rim is securely fastened and the O-ring is no longer visible.

Retail Mod 44 Rims

There are a variety of Mod 44 rims available to purchase from Freshly Dirty or other retailers. These come in either POM or Delrin, and are the easiest way to switch up your Mod 44 play. These are:

Supersport

Coupe

Cruiser

Tuner

Big Rig

Hatchback

3D Printed Mod 44 Rims

There are many different types of Mod 44 rims available to print at home. Freshly Dirty provides a bunch, including templates for making your own, over at GrabCAD. They include the following notes about 3D printing rims:

"The Modular 44 supports 3-D printed rims. The link found above provides design templates as well as finished rim designs. Use these files to design and print your own custom rims for the Modular 44. Two types of rim designs are available- rigid and flexible rim models.The rigid models are similar to the POM rims included with the yoyo; these should be printed in PLA, PETG, Nylon, or any other rigid material.The flexible models use a different interface to connect to the hub. Use a TPU or FLEX filament to print these rims. Be sure to remove the O-ring on the hub before attaching a flexible rim.The rim templates are stored in a .dwg file; this is a 2-D file format that should be easier to modify with a wide variety of CAD softwares. Dimensions are in millimeters. The dotted line on the left side of the drawing is the centerline of the rim; this should be used to revolve the sketch into a 3-D model. The dotted line on the top of the drawing represents the center of width of the Mod44; use this to calculate the total width of the assembled yoyo.

Reducing vibe in your 3-D printed rims is a trial and error process. Some tuning will usually be needed to achieve smooth performance. If you are looking for a dead smooth yoyo, there are already a multitude of budget metal yoyos that will provide what you’re looking for."

title: Modular 44
content:
History / About
Modular 44 is Freshly Dirty's interchangeable-rim yo-yo, shipping with swappable Coupe and Cruiser POM weight rim sets around a 6061 aluminum body — an "open source" modular concept intended to let players tune weight distribution. Spinkult (Sweden) released an exclusive Clear "Spinkult Edition" colorway in 2021 for $85, alongside standard Black, Aqua, Orange, Caldera, and Nightshow releases.

title: Monarch
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"The Monarch is a hybrid yoyo inspired by classic yoyojam models but with modern design cues. It features a Polycarbonate body and Aluminum weight rings. Whether you're just spreading your wings or ready to rule the stage, Monarch is sure to help you achieve your goals."

title: Mongoose
content:
History / About
The Mongoose was released in 2022 and has proven resilient in the G2 catalog, receiving an updated "Mongoose 1.5" variant in 2025 with refined proportions. A stainless steel prototype (Mongoose SS V2) was also in development as of mid-2025, suggesting the Mongoose platform may expand further.

title: Monkey Flyer
content:
From ZGRT:

"MFD + ZGRT collab

A year before the release, MFD and ZGRT started the discussion to do a collaboration and the planning began. It was an extraordinary year of working together from the yoyo designing process, prototyping and finalizing the details. It took several months as both teams were involved in testing and input. It took several months as both teams were involved in testing and input.

The result was to make an organic throw that played floaty and nimble but with a beefy rim to add certain grade of performance.

We then played around with packaging, artwork, colour selection and the name before it all came together.

This has been such an epic journey and project that we have thoroughly enjoyed since the very beginning.

That being said…

We are more than trilled to introduce the Monkey Flyer!"

title: mono 50mm
content: About the mono 50mmThe mono 50mm is the smallest diameter in At Design Lab's MoNo series. At 50.3mm diameter and 61.8g it offers an undersize option within the same high-wall W-shape silhouette as the flagship 54mm. The brand references the YoYoJam Night Moves 5 as design context while engineering the mono lighter. Available colorways include Starlight/Silver (Smooth Ultimatte), an Aging Coating edition with slow-nickel patina finish, and a Snow Coating Edition (October 2023).

title: Mono 52mm
content: About the Mono 52mmThe Mono 52mm sits between the 50mm and 54mm in At Design Lab's MoNo series. At 52.5mm diameter and 62.5g, it is described as offering "improved controllability while maintaining stability." The design references the YoYoJam Night Moves 5 for size rationale. Available in Starlight/Silver half-and-half (Smooth Ultimatte) and a Snow Coating Edition released October 2023.

title: MoNo 54mm
content: About the MoNo 54mmThe MoNo 54mm is At Design Lab's first product and the flagship of the MoNo series. Released in autumn 2021 in a single production run of 100 pieces worldwide, it sold out in approximately five minutes at the brand's direct store and in one minute at Spingear Japan. Development involved five prototype stages, including 3D-printed verification models and aluminum prototypes.The design is a high-wall W-shape drawing inspiration from the CLYW Peak (rim weight structure) and YoYoJam Hitman (rim weight distribution). It is positioned for calm, leisurely trick execution rather than speed competition — a conscious choice the brand frames as an appreciation for flow over performance metrics. "MoNo" signals a single-material, single-form philosophy. Smooth Ultimatte Coating, in a Silver/Space Gray half-and-half finish, was the only colorway produced.

title: MONO 56mm
content: About the MONO 56mmThe MONO 56mm is the largest diameter in At Design Lab's MoNo series at 56.5mm. "Thick and stable rims with high walls designed for smooth trick execution at a moderate pace." The full-size profile provides more gyroscopic stability than the smaller variants while maintaining the same high-wall W-shape silhouette. Available in Starlight/Silver and a Snow Coating Edition (October 2023), the latter using a special resin finish that produces a more plastic-like playing feel.

title: MONO Signature
content: About the MONO SignatureThe MONO Signature is a multi-material evolution of the MoNo series, designed as a signature model for Junhong Mcintosh-Lee. The 6061 aluminum W-shape body is paired with stainless steel weight rings and POM (polyoxymethylene) outer rims — a three-material construction that departs from the pure monometal MoNo series. At 53mm diameter and 73.4g it is the heaviest and most rim-weighted model in the At Design Lab lineup, built for maximum stability and spin power. $101 USD. Colorway: Silver/Starlight.

title: Monolith
content:
From 44EMPORIUM:

"Monolith is the second original model from 44EMPORIUM, and a signature model of Junhong Mcintosh-Lee.

The concept of this yoyo from the beginning was to create something heavy and stable, but comfortable and maneuverable simultaneously; something Junhong loves.

73.4 grams of weight may sound heavy, but the large POM rings translate it into something enjoyable and pleasant.

The black version creates an illusion - resembling a full metal yoyo with midship SS rings, whereas this Silver version highlights the clean-looking white POM on top of 2 different metals.

After two prototypes; we have found the ideal yoyo for Junhong's taste, and it is ready to see the light of the world.This heavy yet maneuverable yoyo brings the throwers a unique experience that they haven't felt before.

Thank you for your continued support."

title: Monsoon
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"Dressel Designs takes on the oversized concept with their latest creation, the Monsoon. Serious in performance yet full of playful character, this yo-yo captures the fun of dancing in the rain while delivering the power and control of a true storm.

Inspired by the classic A-RT 420, the Monsoon brings a fresh approach to oversized yo-yos. Instead of following the trend of making the throw wider they have decided to push the envelope with the diameter instead. Despite its 63mm diameter, it plays incredibly light and fast on the string, weighing in at just 63.9 grams. The result is a yo-yo that feels nimble and effortless, offering a big presence without the sluggish feel often associated with oversized models.

Each Monsoon features the incredible artwork of Aspen Troutman, adding a personal and artistic touch to every throw. Available in a range of stunning colorways, each Monsoon (except the unengraved Silver with Dark Gray Splash) features a smooth bead-blasted finish for clean grinds and a premium feel. "

title: Moonwalk
content: AboutThe Moonwalk is a collaborative release from LEP (Lab Exploration Program) and Sochi Company for LEP's one-year anniversary, with visual design by Tan Chang and design lead by Wu Congcong. A tri-material construction combines a 7075 aluminum body, a translucent polycarbonate inner ring, and a stainless steel outer ring. The translucent PC inner ring glows and catches light at certain angles — the "moonwalk" effect. Available in Clear with Red Rings. A Czech Edition was also produced.

title: Gold Atom 7000
content:
About the Gold Atom 7000

The Gold Atom 7000 is the third and final model in Moose's Series 2 reflective line, released around 2001. A reflective gold plastic yo-yo, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through Australian toy retailers. It was the highest-numbered model in Moose's entire yo-yo lineup.

title: Power Glow 3000
content:
About the Power Glow 3000

The Power Glow 3000 is the third model in Moose's Series 1, made from glow-in-the-dark plastic. Released during the late-1990s Australian yo-yo craze, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through Australian toy retailers.

title: Silver Bullet 6000
content:
About the Silver Bullet 6000

The Silver Bullet 6000 is the second model in Moose's Series 2 reflective line, released around 2001. A reflective silver plastic yo-yo, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through Australian toy retailers. Not to be confused with the Tom Kuhn Silver Bullet, an unrelated American performance throw.

title: Thunder Bolt 5000
content:
About the Thunder Bolt 5000

The Thunder Bolt 5000 (also marketed as the Black Thunderbolt 5000) is the first model in Moose's Series 2 reflective line, released around 2001. It features a reflective black plastic body, black string, and a metal disc insert, packaged with a trick instruction booklet.

title: Tornado Glitter 4000
content:
About the Tornado Glitter 4000

The Tornado Glitter 4000 is the fourth and final model in Moose's Series 1, featuring glitter suspended inside a clear plastic body. Released during the late-1990s Australian yo-yo craze, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through Australian toy retailers.

title: Ultrasonic Chrome 2000
content:
About the Ultrasonic Chrome 2000

The Ultrasonic Chrome 2000 is the second model in Moose's Series 1, featuring a chrome finish on a plastic body. Released during the late-1990s Australian yo-yo craze, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through Australian toy retailers.

title: Vapourizer Scent 1000
content:
About the Vapourizer Scent 1000

The Vapourizer Scent 1000 is the entry model in Moose's first series of novelty yo-yos, produced during the Australian yo-yo craze of the late 1990s. A scented plastic yo-yo packaged with a trick instruction booklet, it was sold through Australian toy retailers alongside the other three models in Series 1.

title: Mori
content: Mori was MikeMonty’s second advanced yo-yo. Mike asked designer Jordan “ChaosGow” for a V-shaped model that could help him develop horizontal and off-plane play; an existing design was adapted with a minor outer-hub change. MagicYoYo manufactured and anodized the production run as a vendor, not a co-brand.The run arrived in April 2021 in Blackberry, Emerald, Sienna, Burgundy, Indigo, and Marigold. A-grade units launched at $65 and B-grades at $35. Official archived specifications list a 56 mm diameter, 46.8 mm width, 64.5 g weight, 4.4 mm gap, Size C bearing, and M4 × 10 mm axle.

title: Morning Star (Prototype)
content:
History / About
Morning Star is a 1A signature design proposed by Lewi (Yoyos by Lewi), publicly introduced on the YoYoExpert forums on March 30, 2025 as a tri-material build with a 6061-T6 aluminum body, stainless-steel outer rims, and polycarbonate inner rings. Lewi stated there were no plans for a full release unless roughly 20-25 buyers expressed firm interest; a later January 2026 forum post mentions a "new Variant" preorder, but no source confirms the model ever actually shipped.

title: Morpheus
content: About the MorpheusThe Morpheus appeared throughout 2015 as the primary competition throw for several King Yo Star team riders, including Jordan Shen (featured in "Renewal," December 2015), Trent Knighton (October 2015), and Josh Yee ("Morpheus x Pun," November 2015). Specifications were not publicly documented by KYS. A "King Yo Star Morpheus x Benedict" colorway was referenced on yoyoskills.com.

title: MOUNT
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"MOUNT is a standard-sized aluminum yo-yo designed to balance comfort, control, and performance. Carefully tuned weight distribution delivers smooth spin, strong power, and dependable stability without feeling demanding on the string. It handles regens with ease, responds cleanly to player input, and maintains control through longer combinations.

Built for both everyday throwing and high-level play, MOUNT feels natural in the hand and confident in motion. It is bold without being overbearing, refined without feeling fragile, and designed to move as a true extension of the player. A well-rounded first release that sets a strong foundation for Sputnik’s lineup."

title: Mountain Man
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"After well over a year of prototyping and development, Alex Curfman's signature yoyo - The Mountain Man - is finally ready to embark on the trail ahead!

When we took a look at the Freshly Dirty team of misfits, it was clear that Alex was more than deserving of a signature design. In his flagship division of 3a, Alex has competed on the world stage multiple times, and earned top 3 podium positions at the National Yo-yo contest. His style combines technical expertise with flow and creativity in a way that pushes those around him to innovate and try to keep up.

Alex wanted a yoyo with uncompromised stability. Clocking in at 59mm diameter, the design may seem large on paper but after one throw its clear that big diameter = extreme stability. Combined with a moderately narrow profile, the Mountain Man has the endurance to survive even the most challenging 3a, 1a, and 5a tricks while still providing excellent control and maneuverability on the string. The grooved profile and complimentary engraving pay tribute to the mountains that made Alex's yoyo career possible. We hope that this offering will be as much fun for you to throw and enjoy as it was for us to help Alex bring it to life!"

title: M.O.V.E.
content: Designed to stand out among full-metal yo-yos by focusing on fingerspin (top-on) style tricks. C3 took their know-how from the Movitation and applied it to the M.O.V.E., rounding out the side face to create perfect conditions for finger-spin technique while also delivering long steady spin comparable to the Level 6. Suitable for both competitive and casual advanced play. Multiple splash and solid colorways. Price: $54.99.

title: Move Apex
content: History / AboutCurrent retail evolution of C3's M.O.V.E. design family, combining an aluminum body with a polycarbonate cap.

title: High Wall SH
content:
History / About
The High Wall SH is a collaboration between Mowl and KALON DESIGN STUDIO. It deliberately revives the high-wall aesthetic at a time when low-edge competition shapes dominate the market. The 61.9mm diameter polycarbonate rim provides extended spin times, while balanced metal hubs reduce player fatigue. The design emphasizes responsive, technique-oriented gameplay over pure unresponsive competition performance.

title: Mowl M Plastic
content:
History / About
A collaboration between Luftverk and Japanese yo-yo company Mowl, producing a plastic version of the Mowl M design. Currently in stock at $60 on luftverk.com. Represents Luftverk’s continued expansion into the collaborative plastic market and its growing ties to the Japanese yo-yo scene following Jeffrey’s move to Osaka.

title: Mr. Butcher
content: AboutThe Mr. Butcher is the 5A freestyle signature of Hiroyasu Ishihara, 5A Japan National Champion in 2004 and 2005. Purpose-built for counterweight play, the 67g weight and 7075 construction balance the momentum demands of 5A — enough mass to maintain spin under the repeated impacts of counterweight play without the excessive bulk that would slow trick execution. It is one of the few yoyorecreation models explicitly designed for a non-1A play style.

title: MRL-04
content:
History / About
The MRL-04 is the first in the MRL series — a unique triple collaboration between mowl, Yo-Yo Studio Llama (Aomori, Japan), and REWIND Shibuya store manager Shingo Terada (2001 World Champion), featuring a modular hub-and-shell system that allows the shell (body) to be swapped for a completely different feel. This particular release features CLYW team member Petr Kavka (known for his Chief, Sasquatch, and Avalanche preferences) and is based on his Cliff signature model — large diameter with a double rim design and deep inner carving. The artwork is by Titifreak. Comes with a limited glow edition of Petr's signature Candy Dice Pro PK counterweight.

title: MRL-05
content:
History / About
Released the same day as the MRL-04 (December 23, 2021), the MRL-05 is a collaboration with SF Yoyos and their team member Tony Šec, based on Šec's Statement signature model. The wide shape and competitive profile give it a nimble, agile feel on the string. The key innovation over the MRL-04 is the addition of the first metal stainless steel rim weight in the MRL series for added stability and power. Like the MRL-04, artwork is by legendary artist Titifreak. Part of the same MRL modular platform.

title: Musashi
content:
History / About
A minimalist design with no centering finger groove or cosmetic lines, inspired by the Masamune and the profile of a katana blade. The 7068 alloy allowed a sharper carve than 7075 permitted.

title: Musubi
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Introducing Musubi: a signature model for Bachi that takes inspiration from the YYR acrophobia and a unique take on plastic aesthetics on performance monometals.

From Bachi:

Musubi is an AL/PC design with a double rim and PC sandwiched in between the rims. Musubi is also one of my favorite snacks, the sandwiched plastic in the rim reminded me of them, and I wanted to make a colorway inspired by it.

Last year Patrick and I started talking about details for this yoyo, sharing my favorite yoyo designs and what characteristics I enjoy. I wanted something fun that didn't lack power for my favorite tricks. We went through different CAD drawings and added things I originally didn't think about at the time. The 1st prototype was a hit! It was perfect from the start and didn't want to change the way it felt. It has a soft, bouncy feel on string with 'float' in all the right areas and time. I really hope you enjoy it as much as I do!"

title: Musubi SS
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Musubi SS. A steel cut signature yoyo for Bachi.

SS has more pronounced speed and power than the regular Musubi while being a smaller diameter."

title: Mystery Gift
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"We took the well loved Kanto shape and scaled it up to a full sized yoyo. We also caught a Snorlax with it, so it weighs about 10g heavier for some nice and relaxed play and better stability. We also upgraded to outer rings made with titanium. This became my favorite yoyo for chill relaxing play and really brings me back to the 2010s if you decide to swap a flat bearing into it for even tighter binds.These debuted as our mystery yoyo for 105$ shipped which is a steal for titanium ringed yoyos. There are only 55 a grades released to the public, and this will never be made again. Once they're gone, they're gone."

title: Mystery Meat
content: The Mystery Meat was a bimetal descendant of the Beef, sharing the same 6061 aluminum + stainless steel outer rim construction but with a modified H-shape body and wider catch zone. The stainless rim rings provide substantial spin power. Colorways include Red/Gold splash and Green. $109.99 USD.

title: N10 Ceramic
content:
About
N10 Ceramic is a T6-based aluminum yoyo with a ceramic-inspired paint/printing finish, referencing Chinese pottery/tea-set aesthetics across four oriental-themed colorways.

title: N11
content: About the N11The N11 was designed around a concept by Chinese player Yi-cheng Luo (Takuto) — a clean, minimal recess design that avoids decorative cuts in favor of pure performance geometry. Steel weight rings provide added stability and spin retention. A dependable beginner-to-intermediate aluminum throw widely praised for outperforming its low price point. An updated "N11 Upgraded" version followed. Available in multiple colorways including Green/Gold, Black, and Red/Silver.

title: N12 Shark Honor
content: About the N12 Shark HonorThe N12 Shark Honor quickly became MagicYoYo's most recognized and best-selling model globally. Its wing-shaped butterfly profile, sand-blasted finish, and wide 44mm catch zone made it accessible to beginners while remaining capable for competitive play. The 10-ball bearing and recessed silicone pads deliver smooth, consistent unresponsive performance. Praised universally in community reviews for its smooth spin, comfortable feel, and exceptional value. Available in Light Blue, Army Green, Blue with Silver Splash, Deep Blue, Green Acid Wash, Red, Red with Gold, and a Merry Christmas limited edition.

title: N5 Desperado
content: About the N5 DesperadoThe N5 Desperado was one of MagicYoYo's first flagship models, released in 2011 alongside the N6 Magistrate and T5 Overlord. At the time of its release, a precision-machined aluminum yo-yo in the $12–16 price range was almost unheard of — the Desperado helped establish MagicYoYo as a disruptive force in the global market. Its wide profile and comfortable hand feel made it approachable for beginners while still capable enough for advanced 1A string play. Available in Blue, Purple, Red, and Raw (silver).

title: N6 Magistrate
content: About the N6 MagistrateReleased in 2011 alongside the N5 Desperado and T5 Overlord, the N6 Magistrate offered a slightly more compact form factor than the N5 with a wide gap for long spin times. Precision-machined 6061 aluminum with a smooth anodized finish. One of MagicYoYo's original metal flagships and among the first affordable unresponsive metals available internationally. Available in Blue, Gold, Red, Silver, and Purple.

title: N8 Dare to Do
content: About the N8 Dare to DoThe N8 Dare to Do is an undersized aluminum yo-yo machined for nimble, fast 1A string play. Its reduced 47.40mm diameter makes it highly maneuverable while weighted outer rims maintain stable, long spins despite the compact profile. Smooth anodized finish; fully unresponsive — bind required. A solid entry in MagicYoYo's growing N-series lineup of the early 2010s.

title: N9 Floating Cloud
content: About the N9 Floating CloudThe N9 Floating Cloud was MagicYoYo's dedicated hubstack aluminum model. Z-stack style hubstacks allow players to pinch the spinning yo-yo for pinwheel and gyroscopic trick variations. The N9 featured a grind-friendly outer finish and a 10-ball concave bearing for centered string play. A heavier throw at 70g, the added weight provided strong spin stability. Available in bicolor and solid colorways including Black, Green, Gold, Red, and bicolor combinations.

title: Naivete
content: AboutThe Naivete features a machined polycarbonate body with stainless steel rings for incredible power and stability. Blasted for a frosted look and smooth grinding, with mirror-polished rings for visual contrast. Available in Dark Purple/Silver, Pink/Silver, Blue/Silver, Purple/Silver, Pink/Gold, Blue/Gold, and Purple/Gold.

title: Naivete 2
content: AboutThe Naivete 2 features a more aggressive V-shape and is slightly wider than the original, delivering better horizontals, easier catches, and higher overall performance. Competition ready with mirror-polished rings in glitter polycarbonate body. Available in Glitter Pink/Silver Rim, Glitter Pink/Gold Rim, Glitter Black/Black Rim, and Glitter Black/Gold Rim.

title: Nano
content:
From Diverse Animals:

"The Nano is the signature yo-yo of Patrick Condon. It is larger and heavier than most yo-yos on the market, but this mass has been carefully balanced. While not optimal for high speed technical play, the Nano excels with smooth, flowing playstyles.

Like all Diverse Animals yo-yos, the Nano is hand crafted. It is machined from Delrin, a low friction plastic, and sports the Diverse Animals aluminum SPR. The axle and threaded inserts are steel. Because of the handcrafted nature, colors may vary."

title: Nap
content:
History / About
The Nap is a new organic undersized design from Recess, designed by CJ Atkinson — the same designer who co-created Jake Bullock's Dunk family — and featuring artwork by Drew Tetz. The name fits Recess's break-time naming conventions perfectly. The Nap is described by Tyler Severance as a "new take on the classic Recess Vacation profile," and represents a deliberate diversification of Recess's shape catalog beyond their signature organic full-size forms. At 51mm diameter and 50mm width, it is nearly a 1:1 yo-yo — a design where width and diameter are almost equal. As Tyler explains, 1:1 designs require undersized dimensions because a 60mm × 60mm yo-yo would need impossibly thin walls to hit reasonable weight. The 50mm width (widest Recess has ever made) and even weight distribution produce the "floaty" feeling Tyler loves without the dense, brick-like feel that undersized yo-yos can have when forced to use extra mass for spin power. The Jack-o'-lantern colorway features artwork by Eddy Dubell (Instagram: @spawnoftheed).

title: Olympic
content: History / AboutThe Olympic was a one-piece wooden, fixed-axle yo-yo with an Olympic-torch center stamp. The Yo-Yo Museum says National Yo-Yo and Bo-Lo Company of Toronto sold the Olympic and Pro yo-yos from 1968 to 1977, with roughly 2 million Olympics and 3.8 million Pro Tournaments made, and that Elfverson of Sweden manufactured them. It calls the Olympic Canada's equivalent of the Duncan Imperial. It was sold on bubble cards (89 cents CA) or from counter display boxes; the carded version shown carries the distributor line National Yo-Yo and Bo-Lo Co. Ltd., Toronto. Similar versions were later sold by Parker, Canada Games, Playtoy and Irwin Toys.

title: Pro Tournament
content: History / AboutThe Pro Tournament was an Elfverson one-piece wooden yo-yo (the lineage of the Kalmartrissan yo-yo) branded for the Canadian market. The Yo-Yo Museum says two versions were sold: the first by National Yo-Yo Limited of Toronto from the 1960s to about 1978 (and Parker Bros. of Concord, Ontario from about 1978), with differences mostly in graphics and gold-leaf stamps. Version 1 reads Original / Pro / Yo-Yo Top / Tournament / Genuine; version 2 reads Original Genuine / Pro / Yo-Yo Top / Tournament / Spinner. It was turned from maple as a single piece. Original retail price was 79 cents Canadian; a one-off 1969 orange color sample was found at the Kalmartrissan factory in Sweden. The YoYo Wiki describes it as a wooden imperial-shaped yo-yo.

title: Nature in Motion
content: Nature in Motion was Hummingbird's classic wooden model, crafted from natural maple with elegant branding on both sides. Released in 1988, this model showcased the company's commitment to traditional wooden yo-yo manufacturing and natural materials.

title: Nectar
content: AboutNectar is a 75/25 cotton and trilobal polyester blend in the Throw-Yo Threads Responsive family. Crisp disposition and glacial velocity with a slightly coarse feel suit it to fixed axle, 0A, and responsive 1A play. The most colorway-rich string in the responsive lineup, available in Yellow Archangel, Corpse Flower, Alchemilla, Dahlia, Windflower, Silver Ghost, Bleeding Heart, Torch Lily, and Calla Lily alongside monocolor.

title: Nemesis
content: Large SPR with lighter aluminum inset rings. Originally sold for $35.

title: Neo Gaia
content: History / AboutUpdated retail Gaia model documented separately by Rewind.

title: Neo Master Galaxy
content: A third iteration of the wide Master Galaxy platform. Rounded M.O.V.E. body combined with the wide-stance Galaxy series dimensions for smooth, stable play.

title: Neo Solar
content: Evolution of the original Solar and Solar Plus, reworked to maximize spin power. Slightly smaller diameter but wider than the original Solar. Adjustable gap via three spacer configurations providing two gap settings. Described as a "generalist" for various offstring techniques. Used as the design base for the Flawless. Price: $54.99.

title: Neolith
content:
History / About
No brand-authored description available — product page carries placeholder text only. Confirmed as a real, distinct listing (own product handle/URL, separate from Halcyon Soar), but no independent source corroborates its specs.

title: Nessie
content:
History / About
The Nessie is the second release from G Squared, arriving in 2012 as a follow-up to the Albatross. Named after the mythical Loch Ness Monster, the Nessie was described by reviewers as underrated compared to the Albatross despite being a capable player in its own right. Like the Albatross, it came with a One Drop 10-Ball bearing and clear flowable silicone. Both the Albatross and Nessie received AL7 (7075 aluminum) variants under the G2 "AL7 Series" branding that applied to multiple models across the brand's history. The Nessie design has been revisited in 2022 (Nessie reissue) and again in 2024 as the Nessie 24.

title: Nessie 24
content:
History / About
The Nessie 24 is the third generation of G2's beloved Nessie design, originally released in 2012 as their second-ever yo-yo. The "24" suffix indicates a 2024 production run with updated specs and colorways for the modern market. Twelve years after the original, the Nessie design continues to find an audience — testament to the enduring quality of G2's early organic designs.

title: Nessie (Reissue)
content:
History / About
A revisit of G2's classic 2012 second release, brought back for collectors and fans of the original design. The Nessie has proven enduringly popular in the G2 catalog and was later updated again as the Nessie 24 (2024), keeping the design alive across three generations.

title: Netrunner
content:
The following is archived from the Yoyofriends website:

The Story of Netrunner

Netrunner ushers in a new competitive era for yoyofriends and team yoyofriends players. The concept of this yoyo actually started around mid to late 2024. At that time we were trying to have design candidates for the 9th anniversary yoyofriends yoyo. One of the candidates is an ultra competition bimetal that focuses on power, width and stability. Traditionally, an anniversary yoyo for yoyofriends is cheaper compared to our normal releases. We would use simple design queues with a twist for easier machining. So for the overall shape, we just went with a classic V shape profile besides the SS rings.  At that time, we just released our best competition budget monometal yet, the Ultracut. One of the many things we liked about that yoyo is the dimensions.

The wide width and slightly larger diameter really made hitting zoning tricks and long combos easier. So for this bimetal, we made the width and diameter the same as the Ultracut. Next is the material construction, we want to still push the design of this yoyo, experiment with new material options while making the price not super high. 7075 came to mind as we usually do 7068. 7075 has always been a material we want to try and master. We decided this project will be a great opportunity. Finally, the SS ring. This is what makes this project so special. Traditionally we use a wrapped around ring on our highest premium bimetal yoyos, examples of which are the Hummingbird, Peregrine X and tachyon. This time we want to try something new. Utilizing a hollow wrapped around stainless steel ring for the first time ever in our lineup. With all the parameters set, we made our first prototype.

(Picture of Netrunner prototype 1)

(Picture of Netrunner prototype 1 and Ultracut) 

The prototype played very well. It has hit and surpassed just about every single metric of performance we expected. The yoyo is powerful, stable and still fast. The standout is how controllable the yoyo is, especially in horizontals. The yoyo holds itself in the air slightly longer than our traditional bimetals due to the hollow stainless steel rings. Overall we saw a significant improvement in overall comp meta performance over our previous bimetal model. The manufacturer team however found some issues. The weight of the prototype was all over the place, we really want to hit a more consistent weight for production. There are also a lot of vibey prototypes and the yield was not great. The manufacturing team has decided in order to solve this, we will make some slight tweaks on the design, ensuring a better weight consistency and ring fit. We ran into another issue as the cost of making this yoyo will be really high due to its wide body and hollow ring construction. With all these problems we decided to use hypercut as our 9th anniversary yoyo and further refine this project and make it a normal release as our next top competition model. Prototype 2 was then made. 

(Picture of prototype 2)

The prototype 2 arrived and we solved all the problems above. We even increased its weight, doubling down on power. Somehow, increasing the weight slightly did not affect its speed and acceleration. We know from prototype 1 this is going to be one of the best comp yoyo in our lineup, so we made extra for yoyofriends players. James Heder and Stephen Madden switched to this model at PNWR (Pacific NorthWest Regionals). The best way to test a competition yoyo is always on the stage and this yoyo delivered big time. Both James Heder and Stephen Madden made finals with Stephen hitting a near flawless prelim and James getting 7th place in the finals for his first ever 3 min freestyle. The feedback from them was incredible. After this we greenlit this yoyo for production. 

Here are the PNWR performances from Stephen Madden and James Heder using Netrunner at PNWR. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xhXGQ_fHm0E

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MSd0ENgDmiQ

https://youtu.be/tBil3emz538?si=i1XqOQYEVsMMSCmV

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OKDyn4oZhXk

Recently, James Heder used Netrunner and won NER (Northeast Regional yoyo contest) 1A Finals! Further proving the competition readiness of the netrunner.

We also specially made signature colorway for our player Stephen Madden celebrating his years of contributions to team yoyofriend.

For the naming, we decided to use Netrunner, inspired by Cyberpunk 2077 (game) or Cyberpunk Edgerunner (show). Netrunner are cyber augmented hackers, dominating cyberspace. We think using this yoyo feels like hacking in a way for contests due to its sheer capabilities. 

(picture of Netrunner in Cyberpunk 2077) 

(Picture of production Netrunner) 

(Picture of Stephen Madden -Netrunner Sig colorway)

title: Neutron (Ti)
content: About Neutron (Ti)Throw Revolution's titanium flagship. The Neutron represents the absolute peak of yo-yo engineering—a ultra-premium instrument combining titanium's exceptional durability with lightweight spin characteristics for elite-level competition.

title: Adrenaline Rush
content:
History / About

The Adrenaline with Pom rings.

title: NEW ANGLE
content: About the NEW ANGLEThe NEW ANGLE is an undersized 6061 aluminum monometal at 53.52mm diameter — smaller than most of sOMEThING's full-size lineup but described as "mid-sized and powerful." Compact dimensions target players who prefer smaller-feeling throws with strong spin. $64.99 USD. Colorways: Green, Gunmetal.

title: New Breed
content: About the New BreedThe New Breed was designed for Eric Koloski with a wider-than-average profile creating an exceptionally forgiving catch zone for complex string trick sequences. The polycarbonate body with aluminum outer ring delivers the weight distribution of a heavier yo-yo without the full-metal price point. Removable YoYoJam side caps allow cosmetic customization.

title: New Overdrive
content: AboutThe New Overdrive is the 2013 revision of Ryota Ogi's Overdrive signature. Retaining the 59.5mm × 44mm dimensions of the original, the New Overdrive refines the internal profile and weight distribution for contemporary competition play. Ogi's high-speed horizontal and multistyle approach remained the design brief — the update simply brought the geometry in line with advances in competition play between 2010 and 2013.

title: NEWS Free Agent
content:
History / About
NEWS Free Agent (RY-013F) is a no-rim off-string (4A) variant of NEWS Special Agent, a tribute/successor to YoYoJam's Free Agent.

title: NEWS Special Agent
content:
History / About
NEWS Special Agent (RY-013S) is Sturm Panzer's first off-string (4A) yoyo, a tribute/successor to YoYoJam's Special Agent — a homage, not a licensed collaboration like Night Moves 9. Ships with Storybook Vol.13, which includes an "All About YoYoJam 2002-2003" retrospective covering 27+ models.

title: Next Level
content: About the Next LevelThe Next Level combines an aluminum body with stainless steel outer rims in an inverse-round profile, placing dense steel weight at the outermost edge for exceptional rim-weighted spin stability. Mirror caps add a premium aesthetic. It was released as a limited-run premium model without a specific player signature, positioned at the top of YoYoJam's performance lineup.

title: Night Moves 5
content: About the Night Moves 5The Night Moves 5 is a premium limited-edition undersized yo-yo featuring an aluminum body with a nickel-bronze rim finished in 24-karat gold plating. Its stepped response system keeps the string away from the body during play, and the Dif-e-Yo KonKave bearing is included officially licensed. Removable side caps allow minor weight adjustment.

title: Night Moves 6
content: About the Night Moves 6The Night Moves 6 is the signature model of Jun Aramaki, building on the Night Moves 5's aluminum-and-brass formula with increased diameter and weight to match the evolving demands of competitive play. First-run limited editions feature a nickel-coated aluminum body and 24k gold-plated brass rim. A signed card from Aramaki was included with purchases from select retailers.

title: Night Moves 7
content: About the Night Moves 7The Night Moves 7 is the personal signature edition of YoYoJam founder Dale Bell, departing from the full-metal Night Moves tradition by using a POM/Celcon body with gold-plated aluminum rims and a metal-reinforced axle area. Its H-profile body is designed for the rigors of both horizontal and standard play. It represents one of the final premium releases in the Night Moves collector series.

title: Night Moves 9
content:
History / About
Night Moves 9 (WY-009) is an explicit tribute to YoYoJam's Night Moves 5, H3X, and Diamondback 2 shapes, made because YoYoJam never released a "Night Moves 9" of its own. Sturm Panzer's official page states the YoYoJam and Night Moves names are used with Dale Bell's permission, and that the model became YoYoJam-authorized in 2017. Ships with a 22-page "All About Night Moves" YoYoJam-history booklet. Restocked/renewed January 2025.

title: Night Soil
content: AboutNight Soil is a collaboration string produced by Throw-Yo Threads in partnership with Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop and Return Bottoms, created specifically for the Waffle Stomper yo-yo. The blend — 40% rayon, 50% trilobal polyester, 10% Maxi-Lock stretch nylon — produces a slick, brisk, enduring string tuned to the weight and play character of the Waffle Stomper. Released June 3, 2025 as a 36-piece bundled run. Currently out of stock.

title: Nile (Original)
content:
History / About
ILYY’s dive into fullsize high RPM throws. Designed by Frank.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (December 2012) — 10 units, Black/Gold; D56.00mm / W44.00mm / 66.20g. Finish: Soda Blast.

title: Nile2
content:
From ILYY:

"Initially devised as our entry into full-size yoyos with highter RPMs we decided to combine the inner ring design with an outer stainless steel ring. The result is a fun and chill yoyo with loads of spintime. We added our signature rounded hub to the design as well.

The outer dimensions are the same as the original, while the overall weight is reduced by around 2 grams."

First Batch

The first batch of Nile2 yo-yos was released in February of 2025. Only 25 units released, all in a Purple/Violet colorway with a Soda Blast finish.

title: Nimbus
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Nimbus: Shinnosuke Ishizuka signature yoyo.

'Like playing with a cloud'

Shinnosuke has been a valuable part of our team for years, and embodies the style, creativity, and uniqueness that we put into our brand and our yoyos.  It was obvious he was the perfect team member archetype and super deserving of a signature.

Nimbus has a nostalgic feel in the hand and during play that's reminiscent of higher-end models from 2009-2011, offering a nimble, soft handling that feels both easy-going and controllable..  this combined with its modern performance lends itself to effortless movement during your tricks. Nimbus encourages a relaxed approach to yoyo play, allowing for a more enjoyable experience.  The bimetal rings and weight distribution lends itself to Shinnosuke's swift changes in direction and speed during his combos.

To foster even more creativity, four stickers are being included with each design to make each yoyo unique in its own right.  Unfortunately these do cause vibe when applied, so use at your own risk.

This is also our first throw featuring our new 'Cloud Blast'; a new lower grit, fluffy blast that will be featured on our main line throws from now on.

We hope that this yoyo brings you peace and joy whenever you throw it!"

title: Nirand
content:
History / About
Nirand is Duncan's monometal 6061 aluminum signature model for Thailand national champion Garbkamol "Polo" Limangkul, positioned as the successor to his earlier Veylaa signature. It debuted at the 2025 World Yo-Yo Contest in Prague. Spinkult (Sweden) released an exclusive matte-clear "Motion Blur, Spinkult Ed." colorway for $55; the first 50 orders included a Kitty String "First Class" string in Light Grey.

title: Nitro
content:
From One Drop:

"The technical idea behind the Seven Summits revision of the Summit was to take a 6061 aluminum alloy yo-yo, redesign it as 7075 aluminum alloy (heavier metal) yo-yo, but make the final result *lighter* while retaining the same profile shape.  The Seven Summits are well loved.

We thought it would be cool to do the same thing for our recent super affordable release, the Intro.  The redesign is called the Nitro.  Clever letter switch aside, the name is very appropriate because it plays faster.  Coming in at 62.4 grams  (3.6 grams lighter than the Intro) it’s overall weight has been reduced significantly.  The weight distribution redesign, coupled with the more dense alloy, gives it a totally new play, even though it still has the nice comfy organic feel in the hand.

The diameter and the width remain exactly the same but you will notice the cup has a slight raise in it while the Intro had a flat cup.  This is your visual cue to be able to tell which is which at a glance.

The first run is very limited at 80 units."

content:
From Sputnik:

"Our best creation for competitions is finally here! Meet NIX — a high-performance bi-metal yo-yo, named after the goddess of the night. Precision, power, and elegance combined into one masterpiece."

title: NKG2
content:
History / About
NKG2 is an aluminum monometal released November 24, 2025.

title: NoΩstar
content:
From Diverse Animals:

"The NoΩstar is a collaboration between Diverse Animals and Square Wheels. It features a Royale base and replaceable delrin rims."

title: Noah
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

This one has been a long time coming. Organic profile, Side Effects compatible; borrowing some goodness from its Fruitbowl brothers but firmly set on its own path.

We're proud to introduce the Noah.

SPECS

dia 54.3mmwid 48.4mmbase weight with AL Ultra Lights 62.3g , and 65g with Brass Ultra Lightsmaterial 7068 ALincludes AL Ultra Light Side effects, Brass Ultra Light Side effects

The Weatherman Line draws inspiration from – quite obviously – aspects of weather and the wilderness. Nature has always been a personal refuge for me. I’ve found being in the great outdoors helps me clear my mind, and can be incredibly restful. Given my adoration for and years spent in nature, it was instinctive to draw from my experiences in it – in the Nepali Himalayas, Norwegian Alps, and even desertlands of the Midwest in my years in the United States – and connect them to the concept of variability, which is core to the Weatherman Line.

The Khuno is named after the Incan God of the Storm. Its construction as a Side Effects bimetal, which gives its user a wide range of weight and power, pays homage to the spectrum of force in meteorological phenomena.

Noah as a name was a wonderful starting point for our next model. It has obvious ties to the Biblical episode of the Flood, but more directly, its etymological roots gesture towards the notion of rest – which one can experience deeply in nature. Nature can be a terrible force – it is also simultaneously peaceful and restorative.

In mapping out design parameters and descriptors, we wanted to do something that was unreservedly light, and relaxed. Something that mirrored the ability of nature to set someone completely at ease. Going with an organic profile made sense, given our design parameters.

Still, we needed an approach on organics that was clearly distinct from our Fruitbowl designs. The Cloudberry and Goji were designed to still provide power in their rims to balance an otherwise lithe playfeel, but for this project, we weren’t really looking for balance.

We wanted a purer organic shape that moved as easily as the Goji and felt as floaty as the Pomelo, so that’s what we set out to work on – our initial sketches were based on a miniaturised Pomelo with a frame akin to our smallest and zippiest organic, with the added feature of variability through One Drop’s Side Effects system.

We ended up with something fluffier at 54.3mm, just sitting between the physiques of the Cloudberry and Goji, and with a base weight of 62.3g.

As weight distribution goes, there is nearly zero bias towards the rims. The rims are a clean, lipless cup with unbroken curvature.

We wanted to add a bit of centerweight without rehashing the protrusive hub-bump that has been popular in many other recent designs. Keeping consistent with curvature, we ended up with a graduated slope surrounding the Side Effects axle holes, replacing the usual straight-line edges of other Side Effect designs.

This addition is subtle, but we managed to pack on roughly 3g to centerweight while maintaining its gradual, gentle surface.

We’ve also gently reworked our schmoove-response bump to be less aggressive than before. These are micro, under-the-hood changes that might not be immediately obvious to the eye, but they contribute to a smoother ride.

Part of our ongoing tinkering is focused on getting our Side Effects designs as smooth as possible. This included extensive testing with various bearing types, all of which have specifications that can vary on a microscopic level. The construction involves multiple independent, fitted parts, and the tiniest amounts of vibe can emerge from imprecisions in any of them.

Yoyorecreation’s NSK DS Platinum bearings worked well with the Khunos. We managed to source for an alternative concave design, which we internally refer to as Type I’s, which yield a similar smoothness.

These Type I Concaves will be included stock with the Noahs.

They will also be kitted with the new Saturn Pads, which we developed and produced in conjunction with RSO. These pads are made to Shore 30 spec, and provide nice, tight binds.

When Noah prototypes were first posted online, we had someone ask what Side effects felt most “native” to the design. Your mileage may vary, but I’ve most enjoyed the Noah with Aluminium Ultra Lights, since they make full use of its light frame. Aluminium Flats feel great as well. In its native featherweight configuration, the Noah just bobs, weaves and floats through tricks.

It’s a joy to regen and whip – something you might be familiar with if you ever played a Pomelo.

Heavier setups, such as with the Brass Ultra Lights (65g) (or some of my personal favourites in Brass MMCs, 65.9g) grounds the playfeel a bit. Despite the extra weight, the relative distribution keeps those additional grams away from the rims, so you don’t lose its supple feel.

In some ways the Noah feels like our version of the essential blank canvas for organics. It’s capable of a wide spectrum of play, but it’s designed for a certain purist in mind.

Short aside – this “restful” style of play, in my opinion, is wonderfully embodied by Coleman Weimer. On top of being a really kind and insightful human being, he’s been behind many outstanding short film projects that have emerged in 2021, such as We Got This Pt. 5, which features Harrison Lee and Ethan Cheung (link here, if you happen to like incredibly produced yoyo videos.)

The Noah comes with our signature dusty, ceramic-like blast, and includes:- A pair of Saturn Pads- AL Ultra Light Side effects (installed)- Brass Ultra Light Side effects- Zipline String’s Case Study 50s for some out-of-box goodness.

Thank you for getting to the end of this writeup!

We’d love to hear your thoughts, questions, or any reactions at all.

We rigorously hand-tune our Side Effect models to be smooth, but players should expect that some degree of tuning a multi-part model is part of the game.

meta.yya_weight: Base weight with AL Ultra Lights 62.3g , and 65g with Brass Ultra Lights

title: Nobumecha
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"Sengoku went down the path of designing the successor to their flagship Nobunaga with more prototypes by FAR than they had ever made. Taking all physics into account, you have to trade off between features and if you want to make it powerful you have to make it heavier. Likewise if you like light yoyos you have to sacrifice power and stability. Quite the challenge always comes with trade offs.

But in the process, something came to mind as priority. Competition oriented yoyos are not usually beginner friendly. They are less forgiving because they need to obey to nuanced movements, but a begginer may make many unwanted nuances! So in short Nobumecha is a yoyo you can compete with and at same time is great for learning. Doesn't feel like a brick, but it keeps rolling and rolling. You can stack layers and it wont stop, you can practice a few moves without rewinding.

At the end of design, what was supposed to be a nobunaga 2, a Nobunaga with slight adjustments ended up looking and playing and feeling completely different! Still the Nobunaga at its core but with a cybernetic body upgraded feeling! The Nobumecha!"

title: Nobunaga
content:
History / About
Sengoku's very first product, pre-released at the Japan National Yo-Yo Contest in early May 2015 with a wide retail release on May 15, 2015. A bimetal design engineered to play like a monometal, named for warlord Oda Nobunaga.

title: Noctu
content:
From ILYY:

"Back in 2007 when we came close to finishing up the E1NS, we goofed around in CAD and created crazy ‘never-been-done’ shapes. At the time, we thought our yoyo making to be a one-time endeavor. Thus, the designs we created were not focused on DFx aspects at all.

One of these brainchilds was the Noctu. Right after we rendered the first 3D-model, we realized, there was something here. This was too special to be left in a mental drawer. It had to be brought to life.

When the E1NS nuked into the scene and obliterated our wildest expectations, we immediately sought out to awaken the Noctu. This proved itself to be hard, very hard. The design was so bonkers (including the asymmetrical bearing seat), our machining shop struggled long and hard to get the first prototypes machined. In the end, they succeeded and were in business.

Tossing these around, we quickly had a list of improvements collected and were ready for the next improved iteration. However, we soon learned the design still was very challenging to machine and thus went from iteration to iteration.

The delays became so intense that we released more yoyos and new models in between the Noctu prototypes. In the end, we released 10 different batches and all had their quirks and changes.

We always wanted to return to the OG specs, the way we had initially thought Noctu to feel like. That’s what we did with this 2019 release, based on the smaller diameter and the traditional wider wings, the new Noctu is an ode to old school ILYY.

Ready to roam night skies on Halloween 2019.

2020 batch #1 to feature our brand new Lebkuchen (ginger bread) colorway.

2020 batch #2 to feature the Schokolade (chocolate) colorway."
