title: Nocturnal
content:
History / About
Released August 2019, the Nocturnal is a competition-geared monometal suited for any play style. It features a wide full-size frame designed for a maneuverable, fast feel in play. The rounded edges are comfortable in the hand and offer a soft feel on the catch. Easy to handle with ample speed and a light, powerful string presence, the Nocturnal feels equally at home with slow, flowy tricks or the fastest speed combos. One of mowl's most universally praised aluminum models.

title: Noir
content: Signature model for Jakub Dolejš, four-time European Champion and Vice World Champion 2024. The Noir won two EYYC titles for Dolejš. A 7075 aluminum body with large stainless steel rims delivers exceptional spin power, stability, and stopping power for complex competitive combos. Engraved with the noir definition. A cornerstone of the Empathy lineup.

title: Noir Deux
content: The second signature model of Jakub Dolejš, European Champion and Vice World Champion 2024. A hybrid construction pairing a polycarbonate body with stainless steel rims — delivering the power and stability of steel while preserving the light, responsive feel of plastic. Wider than the original Noir for improved string mounting and consistency. Described as fast and effortless. Engraved with the noir definition.

title: Noma.
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re proud to announce the final release of 2024, and the first of our Artist Edition line – the Noma., an ultralight organic designed for featherweight, floaty fun.

Designed by Tsukasa takatsu and Atmos Projects, and powered by One Drop.

SPECSDiameter 52.6mmWidth 46.1mmWeight 59.5gMaterial 7068 al

In October 2023, an idea surfaced in the Atmos group chat about the possibility of working with players and designers in co-creating designs that embodied a unique player or design philosophy – an Artist Edition, of sorts – similar to how some Japanese clothing brands work with artists in developing signature capsules and releases. Multiple exciting names and brands came up in that conversation, but the consensus revolved the most emphatically around Tsukasa Takatsu.

If you don’t know already, Tsukasa Takatsu is a legendary player hailing from Japan, the father of the #thingsthatrepeat trick movement, and is known for his effortlessly creative and intelligent repeater-style tricks that have inspired an entire genre of play. It’s difficult to overstate his impact on modern yoyo culture. Tsukasa is also a tenured member of the One Drop player team, and has produced two signature yoyos with them – the incredibly popular and successful Panorama and Diorama. 

We reached out to Tsukasa – and we were incredibly glad that Tsukasa was as excited to do something together as we were. One Drop also very graciously gave their blessings on this project, which we were incredibly grateful for.

The conversation went quickly towards developing a design concept that would anchor the project. Tsukasa has long enjoyed our organic designs – especially the Noah, Abel and Cephas, and asked to base his design off the Noah, mostly – but melding it with inspirations from a long list of his other favourite yoyos, such as the Wooly Marmot by Caribou Lodge, the 2007 888 by Yoyofactory, the Fern by A-RT, and the Hitman Pro by YoyoJam. We began with an initial specifications ballpark of 50mm-diameter, 42mm-width, and 60g-mass. Tsukasa also requested that the design be Side Effects-compatible – and to be shipped with Aluminum Ultra Lights, his favourite type of SEs.

Our initial reaction to these specs were that this design was turning out to be a lot smaller and lighter than we’ve ever been comfortable with. Our smallest design at that point was the Goji, which came in at 52.5mm, and we had never gone lighter than 61.3g (the Pomelo). For the past few years, we had also been trending towards heavier designs, transitioning away from the ultralight, floaty organic design mold that had been the essence of our early years. At the same time, this felt like the most natural request. The Panorama and Diorama were surprisingly slight and light in play – a perfect match for Tsukasa’s gentle, incredibly controlled style. And for us, it was going back to something incredibly familiar.

We drafted up a first prototype that was north of 52mm in diameter, 46mm in width, and 60.5g in its lightest form. For the most part, we were able to translate the Noah’s weight distribution to the prototype, all while scaling down its size. To begin with, the Noah is an evenly-weighted design – with most of its mass spread out in the center-and-midweight sections. To reduce width overall, we asked Tsukasa if he would prefer us remove the Schmoove-step that is a characteristic feature of the Noah, and go with a wall design more akin to the Butterball – but Tsukasa insisted it remained. These prototypes were sent promptly to Tsukasa for testing. His feedback was that they had “great impressive feel, and very comfortable”, but also felt still  “a little heavy”, by about 1-2g. The spin power was also a little “too strong”, and asked if it could be “powered down”. Tsukasa felt the weight distribution and dimensional proportions were perfect, but wanted something scaled down slightly – in other words, to keep its balance and feel, but go even lighter and gentler.

This feedback was perfect. It’s always incredibly helpful when a player’s tastes are refined and genuinely opinionated – it provides so much clarity of where to go. The further we iterated and heard feedback from Tsukasa, the more clear it became where this design was headed.

During the design process, a comparison to ultralight fishing surfaced, and feels fitting here to describe light play – it’s one thing to go big game hunting, where heavy-duty, high-poundage gear, adrenaline, and physical strength and skill are the focus. Ultralight fishing feels entirely different – the experience is focussed on finesse and precision, technique, and the fact you feel everything – every single turn and twist.

The second prototype was nearly 2g lighter overall, and was designed to have a little less rotational force than its first version. We kept the diameter at 52.6mm to preserve its dimensional proportions, and 7068-AL was also used to make core design parameters achievable. The Schmoove-step was preserved, but slightly altered for smoothness and ease in play. The outcome of these changes were that the prototype played like a baby-sized Noah with its lightness and sensitivity dials turned all the way up. It played floaty, ultralight, and gentle – like a natural extension of the string. 

It feels like a little cloud on a string. 

If you’ve ever had the chance to throw a Panorama or Diorama, you would feel Tsukasa’s tastes and preferences similarly imbued in this one – which, to us, is a perfect reflection of the Artist Edition line, which sole purpose is to spotlight a specific player’s signature feel and play.

The design changes landed perfectly with Tsukasa – he was extremely pleased with the way it played, preferred it heavily over the first prototype, and felt it perfectly fit what he had in mind.

That was all we needed to hear.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oCJo6W7q1rE

Here’s Tsukasa playing a Noma. – if you’ve not read anything up to this point, take three minutes to watch this goodness.

Noma. (々) is a symbol that linguistically functions in Kanji as a repeater – and comes from a simplified form of the character 仝, a version of “same” – which is a perfect homage to Tsukasa’s playstyle, philosophy, and legacy.

The Noma. is not built for the speed player with high-click aspirations, but the type that finds joy in subtlety, finesse, and fine control.

Come enjoy the Noma.

title: Nomad
content: The Nomad is W1LD's first bi-metal designed around a Size D bearing, delivering a distinctive torque profile and tenacious spin that differs meaningfully from the standard Size C models in the lineup. Prominent inner stainless steel rims and a compact 55mm diameter make it versatile across 1A, 3A, and 5A play styles. Features an M3.5 × 10mm axle.

title: Noradrenaline
content: The Noradrenaline is Blaise Becker's bi-metal companion to the Adrenaline, sharing the same small-diameter, wide-body philosophy but using 7075 aluminum and stainless steel rims rather than tri-material construction. The result is a lighter and sharper-feeling competition throw that suits players who prefer the speed and precision of a traditional bi-metal over the unique feel of the tri-material Adrenaline.

title: Not Machine
content:
History / About
Not Machine is Aroundsquare's first-ever yoyo, released in August 2026. Aroundsquare is best known as a maker of begleri and other minimalist skill toys; after years of customers asking when the brand would make a yoyo, founder Matthew Hiebert concluded the real appeal was never high-performance modern throws but the wooden yoyos of childhood — a category almost nobody makes anymore. Not Machine is light, compact, and generously rounded, shaped for comfort in the hand rather than technical trick performance, with wood's natural weight, warmth, and texture standing in for the precision-machined feel of a modern throw.

title: Daji
content: History / AboutPer Yoyo Store Rewind, Daji combines an aluminum alloy body, stainless-steel rims and clear polycarbonate parts. A laser-etched logo shows through the transparent parts, and it makes a clear high-pitched sound on bind. The name and design reference Daji, the nine-tailed fox spirit of the Chinese myth 'Investiture of the Gods'. The gap is set slightly narrow for an easy bind.

title: Flow
content: History / AboutPer Yoyo Store Rewind, Flow is a bi-material yo-yo following on from Swift: metal body with a plastic outer rim, wider than Swift with weight pushed further to the rim. The rim comes in polycarbonate (PC) or POM versions. Rewind's spec table follows the PC version; the POM version weighs about 68.4 g.

title: Moon Monster
content: History / AboutMoon Monster is a plastic Novastage model built from polycarbonate parts, with a hollow translucent detachable cover on the outer rim area and an aluminum finger-spin groove at the center. YoSam's listing says the larger aluminum center spot places more weight inward to improve handling, and that the design was once exhibited at the Tianjin China Art Museum.Four colorways represent four desires per the listing: yellow for money, pink for love, black for emotion, blue for career. The Yoyo Store Rewind listing adds that the included display caps come off easily and are not recommended for play. Specs per YoSam: weight 65.8 g, width 46.5 mm, diameter 58 mm. Sources: YoSam; Yoyo Store Rewind.

title: Nezha
content: History / AboutNezha is a bi-metal yo-yo from Chinese brand Novastage, designed in collaboration with Chinese 1A champion Zhu Hang Feng as his signature model. Per YoSam's listing, it takes its theme from the Nezha character of the Chinese myth 'Investiture of the Gods' (Fengshen Yanyi): the gold stainless-steel ring represents his Universe Ring weapon, and the detachable PC ring represents the Wind Fire Wheels.Specifications listed by YoSam: 6061 aluminum body with stainless-steel rims, gap width 4.55 mm, width 52 mm, diameter 56 mm, total weight 66-68 g with the detachable PC ring. Colorways: black with gold rims, red with gold rims, silver with silver rims. Sources: YoSam product listing; Yoyo Store Rewind (Japan) listing.

title: Swift
content: History / AboutPer Yoyo Store Rewind, Swift is a cost-effective mono-metal from Chinese brand Novastage with a wide body and weight placed toward the rim for strong spin and stability. A finger-spin dimple sits in the center of the body. Rewind lists it at JPY 3,990 in five colorways.

title: Tang Yan
content: History / AboutPer Yoyo Store Rewind, Tang Yan is a wide mono-metal, roughly 50 mm across, with the center of the body thinned and the saved weight moved to the outer metal rim, keeping total weight while raising spin power. Rewind describes it as a high-value model at JPY 3,490.

title: Yang Jian
content: History / AboutPer Yoyo Store Rewind, Yang Jian has a polycarbonate body, stainless-steel rim and large plastic wings fitted over the rim, making a very wide yo-yo with weight gathered slightly inward. It references Yang Jian (Erlang Shen) of 'Investiture of the Gods', known for growing to giant size. The center of the body is designed to accept attachable parts not available at launch, with dimension data for user 3D-printing promised by the brand.

title: Nucleon
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Yoyofriends 7th version yoyo name is Nucleon, its design is based on pure power and stability.It is coming in at over 65g with the classic 7068+SS yoyofriends construction, we made a yoyo that can power through just about any combo you throw at and more. We also kept the width below 44mm to keep the yoyo on any plane of your choice easily. Combining the weight, width, and construction, a nucleon is undoubtedly our most powerful and stable mainstream bimetal yet. After testing from the yoyofriends players, we found that due to its insane stability, it can hold horizontal combo really well, one of the best yoyos in our lineup."

title: Numen
content:
The following story was taken from ILYY.

At ILYY, we do not necessarily follow the path of ever improving performance. Instead, our goal has always been to explore niches we haven’t touched before, regardless of performance. This led us to create yoyos like the Krapfen or the PYBIT, both by no means competition-oriented designs. Some of these considerations even became our standard at ILYY like the 4 mm gap width.Keeping true to this design philosophy of seeking untouched ground regardless of the outcome, there is one design niche we have not covered: a modern competition yoyoBeing a competition-oriented design, it should reside above all other ILYYs in terms of raw capability, the usual limits and ideas left far behind, a true testament to power, stability and maneuverability.

This is the Numen.

All bi-metal ILYYs to this point featured an inner ring keeping the outer appearance of the yoyo undisturbed. While offering very slick and pleasing aesthetics, this is a compromise in terms of rim weight capabilities, as the ring cannot be placed in the outermost region of the body. The Numen’s performance-oriented concept clearly needed outer rings to benefit the most from the bi-metal construction.

In order to stay true to our slick and understatement design philosophy we gave the intersection area small radii to comfort the profile lines to a haptically and optically pleasing conjunction. Furthermore, we went with blasted and electroplated rings to take on the matte aesthetics of the blasted 7068 aluminum body resulting in a beautiful laid-back overall look.

On the inside, Numen also features a carefully designed transition between ring and cup. Aluminum and steel meet in the same beautiful way as on the outer profile rounding off the harmony-driven design concept.

7068 aluminum alloy allows for very thin material thickness down to (or even below) one millimeter. However, the Numen does not go that route. We purposely left the cup walls well beyond this thickness to further strengthen the overall construction and make the Numen more resistant to drops and undesired hits. The massive rims still provide a lot of inertia and give the Numen its immense power and stability.

Aside from the crazy PYBIT, Numen is our widest yoyo to date. It offers the widest catch-zone of all ILYYs. Its concave gap profile is derived from the Golden Abyss and expanded even more to enable fingergrinds like never before. Hitting even the most daring tricks is made possible thanks to the forgiving shape. The rims flatten out to allow for a nice hand feel.Most of our line-up featured a 4 millimeter gap. We consider this gap width enough for most tricks and situations. This gap width also allows for snappy and tight binds of the entire lifetime of the response pads.For the Numen we increased to gap to 4.5 millimeters for maximum string layer capability. The Numen’s flush pad design retains tight binds and overall reliable response of smaller gap width yoyos.

The Numen features shorter bearing seats to allow for tool-less bearing swaps and maintenance. This yoyo is supposed to be played, bearing maintenance should not take away more time than necessary from play. Numen will not require any tools or pliers to access the bearing.

With the Abyss line we delved into the word of fingerspin yoyos using concave cup design. Even though perfect centering is possible with this construction it comes with a few drawbacks. Concave cup designs do not force the finger into the cup center, only really steep shapes may do so which come with other compromises in terms of mass placement. In addition (depending on the center of the cup) concave profiles are less stable to disturbances while fingerspinning.

The Numen solves theses drawbacks by introducing a convex cup design that mimics the concave outer profile. This pushes the finger right into the center area and keeps it there all the time. This strong push to the center allows the Numen to have a more traditional central hub without any dimples, anti-cones etc. Perfect centering is simply not needed with the Numen thanks to its convex inner cup design.

To further increase stability during fingerspins, the central cup features a small step as the transition from the concave profile to the center. These features make the Numen the best fingerspinning yoyo we ever made. Hitting the cup will ensure fingerspins no matter what. The traditional central cup design allows the Numen to use longer axles resulting in longer threads improving their durability. In combination with the shorter seats, risk of stripped threads is reduced to a minimum.

The Numen is without a doubt the best yoyo we ever made. It does everything any ILYY can but it does it a lot better. Longest spins, highest stability, widest catch-zone, best fingerspins, strongest (finger)grinds, easiest maintenance. If you want ‘maximum everything’ from ILYY, the Numen is for you.

Initial Run

The initial run of the Numen was released in February 2024 and was limited to 42 pieces in a Bronze/Black colorway with a Soda Blast finish.

title: Nuur
content: Sputnik x In Hyeok

title: Oasis
content:
From Dressel Designs:

"Oasis joins our vast array of organic and D bearing yoyos and features a very mid school design flavor. Since our first ever release, the assassin, launched all the way back in 2021, we've been clamoring at the idea of releasing another steel yoyo.

There's something special about a well designed stainless steel yoyo, and our team realized we hit the jackpot from the first throw. When done properly, it has a very premium feel in all aspects of play feel and performance without a very steep price tag. With Oasis, we wanted to explore a larger diameter than the assassin without going overboard, and focusing on the most comfortable and enjoyable experience in a yoyo. With this in mind, we set out to design an organic with a wide but not too wide body, and really angled and rounded end curves for a yoyo you will not want to (and don't have to) put down!

We knew from the start we wanted steel since it is the perfect material to bring a yoyo wherever you want, without feeling the guilt of dropping an expensive titanium design. Steel is a very strong material when used properly, but can get expensive and brittle at larger sizes, so we design around a mid sized organic in order to keep the qualities of steel we love and enjoy, as well as the ability to offer a fresh thermocline in relation to other steel yoyos on the market, finding a sweet spot between 53 and 54mm diameter.

In play, the yoyo maneuvers easily, letting its 63.7 grams shine when bouncing and shaking easily between your string layers and trick creations. Our new Hybrid D bearing ensures snappy binds and regens and enhances the play experience of this yoyo all around. It has a very large and easy IRG to hit any thumb or talon grinds you may want, and features a very mindful and flavorful hub design with a drop of water rippling across the center."

title: Obscure
content: AboutThe Obscure is Japan Technology's first inner-rim bimetal design, as opposed to the outer-rim placement used in the Kagerou and Shade. Placing the stainless steel ring on the inner wall produces a distinct weight distribution: a smaller diameter with increased width and added weight vs. outer-rim models, creating a strong presence on the string and precision suited to high-level freestyle. Available in Matte Black/Silver Ring and Matte Red/Silver Ring.

title: Obsession
content:
History / About
After the success of the M and Surveillance H-shape models, mowl changed direction entirely with the Obsession — abandoning the H-shape for a beautiful organic step round profile. A mid-size throw with focus on spin power and competitive play, it was first debuted at 44clash in November 2018. The mid rim weight distribution gives it a light feel on the string with plenty of stability and a level of control that is hard to match. It demonstrated that mowl's design excellence extended beyond H-shaped profiles into organic shapes.

title: Obsession+
content:
History / About
The Obsession+ evolved from the question: "What happens if we make the Obsession bimetal while keeping the same profile?" Released October 24, 2021 at mowl's online store, then at partner stores October 30. The stainless steel rims increase stability significantly while the core comfortable feeling of the original Obsession is preserved. The artwork features hand and brain motifs — an evolution of the original Obsession's hidden characters. The team noted that few mid-sized bimetals existed on the market, making the Obsession+ a notable niche fill. Two "S" shapes are incorporated into the brain design, a nod to the SS (stainless steel) material.

title: Obtuse
content: AboutReleased in April 2024, the Obtuse features center weight reduction while accommodating wider stainless steel rims in a step-straight profile. JT describes it as offering "remarkable ease in navigation and impressive spin times." Available in Gold/Silver Ring, Teal/Black Ring, and Matte Blue/Matte Silver Ring.

title: OC
content:
About
OC is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Octavia
content:
History / About
The second Luftverk release, dropped December 6, 2015. First teased as a photo of the prototype catching rain in Madrid, Spain, it then appeared in a promotional video for the Czech National Yo-Yo Contest. Uses a Step Round body profile — a departure from the Evora’s H-shape — and ships with a premium NSK Micro Platinum DS bearing. The release was split into North American and European time slots to combat the chaos of the Evora selling out in just over three hours. 30 Navy and 30 Bronze units were available, plus 10 special AMS2488 Type II hard-coat units with a full ceramic bearing.

meta.yya_bearing_size: NSK Micro Platinum DS (Size C); full ceramic on AMS2488 version
meta.yya_response: 19mm Large Slim Honey String Pads (adhesiveless, Hungarian-made)

title: Odyssey
content: About the OdysseyThe Odyssey is a collaboration between Yomega and YoYoJam, one of a small number of cross-brand projects YoYoJam undertook. It combines elements of both companies' design traditions and was sold alongside the Firestorm as a sibling collab model from the same partnership. Exact specifications are not widely archived.

title: Official Pro 99
content: HistoryThe Official Pro 99 was Cheerio's competition-grade wooden yo-yo, marketed in the US and Canada from 1950. When Duncan acquired Cheerio in 1954, they continued manufacturing this model under the Duncan brand until approximately 1963.

title: OG Bapehidora
content:
History / About
The OG Bapehidora is a modern yoyo upgrade inspired by the Bapezilla. It features an upgraded inside profile to handle all modern tricks, and inverts several characteristics from its predecessor, reducing weight from 67g to 63g while enhancing performance capabilities.
This yoyo utilizes the One Drop Side Effect System, allowing users to swap components for different weights and aesthetics. The ultralight flat caps keep the yoyo fun and lightweight for players who prefer a floaty feel, though heavier alternatives are available for customization.

title: OhZone
content: OhZone was a distinctive limited-production wooden yo-yo released by Hummingbird in 1992, featuring a vibrant orange finish with black paint-drip design elements. This model represented a departure from traditional natural wood finishes, showcasing Hummingbird's creative design approach.

title: Old-School Ink (Prototype)
content:
About
Old-School Ink was a monthly Project Torsion blend from Throw-Yo Threads, offered only to Patreon subscribers in September 2026. No public retail release has been confirmed.

title: Confluence
content: Old School Throws Confluence is an organic bimetal yo-yo with a 6061 aluminum body and stainless steel perimeter rings. Its cup design draws on the Resto, while its larger proportions recall the Medallion.The FIU collector list records a September 15, 2020 Unknown edition with a reported total of 25; the official listing says 21 were offered publicly. Those details describe the edition, not a confirmed exact base-model launch date. A 4.25 mm gap has been reported by an owner and remains unverified.Sources: Old School Throws product listing; Old School Throws model catalog.

title: Omega
content:
The following is archived from ILYY:

A year the its inception, the Alpha finally receives its counter part – the Omega!

The Omega inherits all characteristics of the Alpha: diameter, width, weight, gap size. It uses the same stainless steel rings. The only difference is the shape.

While Alpha uses a very concave H-shape, Omega sports a complementary organic profile.

title: Omertà
content:
From True Arc:

"Omertà is a 7075 aluminum and brass bi-metal built to feel powerful, stable, and deliberate on the string, while still keeping the clean and intentional design language I wanted for this release.

Thanks to everyone who has followed this project so far. Looking forward to seeing what people think once it lands in players’ hands."

title: Omnitron
content: Peter Pong's second C3 signature, combining design elements from the 2012 Berserker and the 2016 Seiren collaboration. Designed for speed and stability; the titanium axle supports extended sleep times. Machined from 7068 aluminum. Includes stock C3 JP pads developed with Shion Araya. Variants include Omnitron 44CLASH edition and Omnitron Noah (titanium rim version). Price: $119.99.

title: Omnitron Noah
content: History / AboutReworked Omnitron's rounded form with a modern H-profile, ultra-thin 6061 body, and precision titanium rims for extreme weight distribution.

title: edITION
content:
History / About
The edITION is a collaboration between One Drop and modern responsive specialist ed Haponik, built on the Deepest State platform. Where the Deepest State was designed for optimal aluminum responsive play, the edITION is ed Haponik's personal tuning of that formula: specific hardware choices dialed in to his style of stall tricks, flips, and regenerations.
The key departure from the stock Deepest State is the bearing. Ed found the standard One Drop 10 Ball too unresponsive for his preferred style; the edITION ships with One Drop's Greasebucket bearing, pre-lubed for snappy, consistent response. The launch also included a string collaboration with ZipLine — ed's preferred Fluff string is included.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball Greasebucket

title: Gauntlet
content:
History / About
The Gauntlet extended the value-focused mission One Drop pioneered with the Vanguard, offering a $49 starting price in a dramatically different shape: big, wide, and fully organic. Where the Vanguard is mid-sized and angular, the Gauntlet is large-bodied and smooth, with a catch zone that tapers elegantly to the rims.
Early feedback at contests was strong. The Gauntlet is stable, long-spinning, and fast, with a satisfying feel in hand that belies its accessible price. It demonstrated that One Drop's in-house Eugene manufacturing could produce competition-worthy yo-yos without the premium markup of earlier models.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball

title: Rebirth
content:
History / About
The Rebirth is the signature yo-yo of One Drop team player Ryosuke Kawamura, the first player to join the One Drop team from Japan. Ryosuke is a devoted fan of the One Drop classics — the Project and Project 2 — and when asked for his signature design he conceived an updated, modern version of those models.
Back when the Project was released a 50mm diameter was considered standard; today that reads as undersized. The Rebirth brings the diameter up to 53mm to feel more contemporary. The nut-capture axle of the original Projects is replaced with the Side Effect system (ships with Ultra Light Side Effects). A friction-reducing bump at the catch-zone transition widens the string-catching area. The flat rims and Projection Profile of the originals are retained, giving the Rebirth a strong visual and tactile connection to its predecessors.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball

title: Terrarian
content:
History / About
The Terrarian was born from an unlikely partnership: independent game studio Re-Logic, creators of the open-ended 2D sandbox game Terraria, approached One Drop in early 2015 with the idea of adding yo-yos to the game. Over the following months One Drop worked with Re-Logic to upload several classic One Drop models into Terraria as in-game weapons — and then collaborated with Re-Logic head Andrew "Redigit" Spinks to design an original real-world counterpart.
The Terrarian features a wide wing-shaped profile engineered to maximize string-segment catchability. The launch colorways — Crimson, Surface Grass, and others — map directly to biomes players explore in Terraria. It ships with Spike Side Effects.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball

title: Top Deck
content:
History / About
The Top Deck is the signature yo-yo of One Drop team member JT Nickel. The design focused entirely on pure performance: using 7075 aluminum alloy — denser and stronger than 6061 — One Drop applied the same weight-to-rim techniques pioneered on their titanium Citizen to an aluminum body. The result is a thin-walled yo-yo that pushes mass to the rims for maximum stability and spin time.
The shape draws from multiple One Drop classics: a mid-weight step influenced by the Summit, a false-rim visual cue from the Cascade, and an organic catch zone that keeps the play comfortable. Despite 7075 aluminum previously commanding $120+ pricing on models like the Valor and Format:C, the Top Deck launched at $79 — a price point One Drop achieved through continued manufacturing refinements in Eugene, Oregon.
"I wanted the Top Deck to move with ease and grace, similar to the Summit, but with a little more stability, for that extra edge during a session." — JT Nickel

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball

title: Ultra State
content:
History / About
The Ultra State is One Drop's second collaboration with the Stay Gold America project of the Atwood family — the first being the aluminum Deepest State. The goal was identical: build the best possible modern responsive yo-yo. The difference: titanium.
Titanium's higher density versus aluminum creates a weight challenge at large diameters. One Drop's machinist Shawn pushed the walls extremely thin to keep the 56.77mm body at 53.7g bare — 56.2g with aluminum Micro Caps. The thin walls push mass to the rim, producing surprising power and spin time that can feel alarming on a responsive yo-yo. Modern responsive play consultant ed Haponik spent six months testing production versions before launch.
"Having played the Ultra State over the past 5 months, I am convinced that it's the best, lowest-maintenance, and most reliable modern responsive yo-yo to date." — Ed Haponik

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball Greasebucket

title: Vanguard
content:
History / About
The Vanguard represents One Drop's commitment to keeping premium, US-manufactured yo-yos within reach of players at every level. At a starting price of $49 for solid colors, it was One Drop's most affordable all-aluminum model at launch — machined in their Eugene, Oregon workshop with the same exacting tolerances as their high-end releases.
The Vanguard is stable and powerful, with a shape that feels familiar from the first throw. It was designed to work equally well as a first aluminum yo-yo or as a reliable daily throw for experienced players, and it laid the groundwork for the value-focused line that later included the Gauntlet and Top Deck.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel — One Drop 10 Ball

title: Oni
content:
History / About
The full-size counterpart to the oversized Bakemono, sharing the same H-profile scaled down to standard dimensions — described by the maker as a "nimble heavyweight."

title: Onigiri
content:
History / About
Onigiri (SS-005) is a novelty, basic-trick/looping-oriented responsive design shaped like a Japanese rice ball, with a seaweed-wrap-styled body and a red potting cap representing pickled plum. Bindable if the user swaps in a standard Size C bearing.

title: Onigokko
content: AboutThe Onigokko (鬼ごっこ) is Wu Congcong's first signature model from JIGUN, released around 2022. "Onigokko" is the Japanese word for "tag" (the playground game). A bimetal with an aluminum body and stainless steel outer rims, it was designed as a competition throw to Wu Congcong's specs as 2022 China National 1A Champion. Available in Silver, Pink, Red, Blue, Orange, and Acid Wash colorways. Succeeded by Onigokko 3 in 2025.

title: Onigokko 3
content: AboutThe Onigokko 3 is the third iteration of Wu Congcong's Onigokko signature line, released in 2025 at $35. A budget bimetal with stainless steel rims, it is available in ten colorways: Red, Orange, Yellow, Navy, Titanium Color, Tiffany Blue, Sky Blue, Grey, Pink, and Violet. WYYC 2025 limited editions are noted in the packaging.

title: Onomatopoeia
content:
History / About
The Onomatopoeia is Anomaly Yo-Yos’ debut release. An H-shape machined from Grade 5 titanium with a raw blasted finish, it came in well under the typical titanium weight range at 54.7g, producing a lighter, faster character than most titanium throws. The raw blast gives excellent string feel while the H-profile pushes weight to the rim for stability. It was available at the 2019 National Yoyo Contest and had a Cyber Monday sale later that year at $65 shipped.

title: Onslaught
content: AboutThe Onslaught is a co-signature between Iori Yamaki and Ayumu Kasuga — two of Team yoyorecreation's elite 1A players. At 57mm × 46mm × 65.4g, the wing-profile body is 3mm wider than the Draupnir, providing a generous catch zone while the outer stainless steel rims deliver full bi-metal spin performance. Released as a limited edition, the Onslaught represents the combined competitive sensibilities of two players who have each performed at the highest level of the World YoYo Contest.

title: Typo
content:
About the Typo

The Typo is the signature throw of KnotCreators team member Abby Brodsky, developed over roughly two years as a pandemic-era collaboration between Only Pink Yoyos and KnotCreators. The name references Brodsky’s well-known tendency to produce typographical errors in online group chats. Built in 7068 aluminum with a stainless steel inner ring, the Typo is designed for fast, stable, long-spinning technical 1A play — Brodsky describes it as “fast playing when you want it, stable, and long spinning for my tech tricks.” All colorways were named after minerals, a nod to her career as a geologist. The Typo sold out and no restock has been confirmed.

title: OPEN 2025
content: AboutThe OPEN 2025 is "the largest mono-metal AceYo has made to date," featuring an oversized design that delivers easy string hits, rock-solid stability, and extended spin times. The substantial weight and dimensions create significant momentum for a predictable, stable platform. Available in Matte Purple, Matte Green, Matte Red, Shiny Blue, Shiny Purple, and Shiny Gray.

title: Operation Desert Storm
content: Operation Desert Storm was a themed wooden yo-yo variant released by Hummingbird in 1991, reflecting the contemporary geopolitical climate. This limited-production model showcased the company's willingness to create timely, culturally relevant products alongside its core traditional offerings.

title: Optima
content:
About
Optima debuted alongside Gotham as the launch of YYR's Type Face Inspired Series — a line whose shapes riff on classic typefaces. Optima's profile is inspired by the Optima font: simple and refined, resulting in a highly-finished monometal.

AboutThe 543 takes its name from its cube-like proportions — 54mm in both diameter and width. Inspired by the YYR Clash Cube but significantly reworked, it emphasizes long spin time for practicing whippy and slacky elements. The debut release from Only Pink Yoyos, each unit shipped in a magnetic box with a certificate of authenticity, stickers, and Airetic string. Production was limited to 33 units total: 31 numbered 0–30 plus 2 retained by Jordan Blofeld, with the #0/30 edition released exclusively by contest.

title: Oracle
content: AboutReleased May 6, 2016, the Oracle was Radical Seas' exploration of bi-metal construction. Rather than the standard stainless steel ring, Jamelle Kent chose brass and copper as weight ring materials — each offering different density characteristics and a subtly different play feel. The 7075 aluminum body received a 180-mesh beadblast finish.The brass ring version shipped in Emerald, Scuba Blue, Radiant Orchid, Light Blue, and Purple. The copper ring was limited to Midnight Blue, with a small batch featuring contest-winner artwork. A Butter Yellow Team Edition was produced for team distribution only.The Oracle's shape and weight distribution philosophy directly informed the Tempo, Radical Seas' collaboration with 2SickYoYos released later in 2016.

title: Orange
content:
From updn:

"it's the orange!

a big yoyo, approximately the size of a large orange, a little smaller than a small grapefruit. 

It's big, it's weird, but it will make you play different, your experience with using this yoyo will impact your other ones too. This yoyo is big, it will make you do bigger tricks, and will make you appreciate regular, small yoyos, differently.

Concept by myself (Andrew Bergen) and my 20 years of yoyo experience, and neuroticism. Technical design from Jameson Larkins of Throw Spiral.

Anti-Stick recess on the inside to prevent snagging, designed to be lighter than its appearance, giving a feeling like the yoyo nearly levitates on the string.

The yoyo might be dumb, but it is, to quote multiple shocked yoyo players, "surprisingly playable". "

title: Orb Side Effects
content:
Orbs are available in:

Titanium

Orbs are one of 4 different Side Effects to be made in Titanium by Brian Fellhoelter. They are made of Grade 5 Titanium, and 25 sets of each were made.

title: Orbis
content: A collaboration with YOYOFFICER, the Orbis is a refined variant of the original Orbis, 1mm narrower with rounded edges. H-profile. Supports Center Part Unit compatibility. Texture coating for enhanced grip and control.

title: Orbital GTX
content: AboutThe Orbital GTX is the signature bi-metal of Tal Mordoch, a three-time European Yo-Yo Champion. Mordoch and Duncan spent months refining the design after early Orbital prototypes, landing on a 56 mm profile with stainless steel rims that creates "perfect balance between softness and sharpness" — the kind of throw that responds crisply to Mordoch's precise technical play without being punishing to less-experienced hands. The angular silhouette became visually distinctive in the bi-metal market, and the Orbital GTX quickly earned a reputation as one of the finest competition bi-metals in Duncan's history.

title: Orbital GTX 2.0
content: AboutThe Orbital GTX 2.0 incorporates two additional years of Mordoch's competitive feedback. The width was trimmed slightly from 46 mm to 44.54 mm for improved string slack control, and the weight was increased from 63.14 g to 65.4 g by repositioning mass in the rims, resulting in longer spin times while maintaining the yo-yo's characteristic angular handling. The 2.0 was released during a period when Mordoch continued winning European championships, making it a live competition-developed product rather than a static catalog item.

title: Orchid
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"Introducing: the Orchid. One of the main goals of our new Stem system is to open the door to new materials in yo-yo. This is our first release to move in that direction.The Orchid features a full Teflon body in a comfortable and familiar organic profile. If you’ve never used a Teflon yo-yo, there are a few things that make it unique. The material is softer than other plastics like POM, giving it a different feel in the hand, excellent grinds, and a less painful experience if the yo-yo smashes into your hand. It also has a density closer to aluminum than POM, allowing for unique weight distribution while still giving the classic experience of using a plastic yo-yo.Teflon is traditionally a very difficult material to use for yo-yo construction due to its softness and low friction properties. The Stem system is the perfect platform to support the material, and some of the durability issues of older Teflon yo-yos are mitigated by using our new hardware. Please note that due to the ultra-low surface friction of Teflon, your yo-yo may feel like it is continuing to tighten even when the Stem is holding everything securely in place. When assembling and unscrewing these Teflon yo-yos, press the halves together as you tighten/untighten the yo-yo for best results. The Teflon material also may have some slight imperfections in its color, please also note that this is normal and does not affect play. All of these first run Stem yo-yos will come stock with a size D bearing, and they are compatible with other bearing sizes using additional Stem bearing seat kits."

title: Organ
content:
About
Organ pairs a compact aluminum body with plastic outer rims — available in POM or Polycarbonate rim variants — softening the overall character while maintaining stability for a balanced, controlled, fluid play feel.

title: Origin
content: AboutThe Origin was Japan Technology's 18th POM-machined yo-yo, released in 2017. With a pronounced sloping rim and updated H-profile, it was refined to draw out the full potential of POM as a material for string trick play — combining speed and power with the soft texture characteristic of Delrin. JT describes its play feel as "top-class." Suitable for 1A, 3A, and 5A.

title: Ork
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Here's the link: The Ork (A Yo-Yo).

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a yoyo. It goes up and down and sometimes it bites. I can't be held liable if it eats some of your yoyo string. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used: https://amzn.to/4hDD0lg. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole, then the pin, and the other half with glue as well. If you want it to work well, slice it to 54-60 grams weight. 

The Ork face has an actual purpose and functions as the response system, what makes it go up and down. This has a very unique feeling response system, you can feel the teeth on throw and pull."

title: Ork MR85 Version
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: The ORK MR85 Version.

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a redone version of my first publicly shared yo-yo now designed for MR85 bearings. 

It uses different hardware, but I tried to make it as simple to build as possible with readily accessible parts. 

It requires:

2x m3ns or other ~5.4mm wide square nuts

1x m3-0.5 x 20mm grub screw

2x 19mm silicone yoyo pads or flowable silicone. 

1x MR85 bearing

Install the pads first. Then drop a square nut into the nose hole in one half, thread the grub screw in from the inside face, ad the MR85 bearing, drop the second square nut into the other half, and spin it onto the first half. Have fun. "

title: Orochi
content:
From Sengoku:

"After many years I finally came up with an organic design worthy of the brand. The design must be elegant, classic, and have a pure organic feeling. What sets this yoyo apart from the typical Organic yoyo are the measures, weight distribution, and overall comfort in the hand. After experiencing working with many alloys, I came up with wall measurements and general weight distribution that only the Alloy 7068 can only do while withstanding a good amount of punishment.

The rings take the most advantage of the light body to allocate a good chunk of the weight for an extended spinning time and end in a curve for a more roundish side shape and comfortable in hand.

The idea of making an Organic has been bugging me since the beginning. I see that idea as a snake that keeps growing and lurking. There is a legendary massive snake in Japanese folklore named “Orochi.” I dig the name, and when the inspiration finally came, I thought it was a good name and concept for the model. I present you the Orochi!"

title: OS1
content: About the OS1The OS1 (Off-String 1) was YoYoJam's inaugural 4A offstring model, featuring soft rubber shells forming a Butterfly body profile for bounce recovery. Its starburst response and B-size bearing made it an early stepping stone toward the more refined Aquarius.

title: Osmo
content:
History / About

The Osmo is the second release from Wicked YoYos and the first in the brand’s dedicated philanthropic product line. The concept originated at the 2024 NYYL Nationals when Jeff Recker of Neverthirst approached Owen Kroeger with the idea of developing a yoyo aligned with their cause — building wells and bringing clean water to people in need worldwide. Wicked YoYos committed in that moment to creating a line of yo-yos devoted to charitable, humanitarian, and environmental organizations. The Osmo is an organic 6061 aluminum monometal priced accessibly at $45, with $10 from every sale donated directly to Neverthirst.  The goal was to raise $1,000 for Neverthirst through the release. B-grade versions are also available at a lower price point.

title: Osprey
content:
From Featherspin:

"The Osprey: Inspired by the bird that looks elegant from a distance but is actually a hyper-focused murder-seagull with wings. The Osprey yo-yo carries that same chaotic professionalism. Throwback to classic competition form with the talons of modern engineering. It doesn’t just cut through air; it owns it. Every spin feels like a dive in perfect control."

title: Outlier 5
content: AboutThe Outlier 5 stepped up from 6061 to 7075 aluminum for added stiffness and performance, and expanded width to 55mm. It was OFFSET's most powerful wide bi-metal at the time of its release. Brandon Vu used the Outlier 5 to win the Preliminary Stage of the 2024 World YoYo Championship, validating the design at the highest level of competition before the Outlier 6 expanded width further.

title: Outlier 6
content: AboutThe Outlier 6 pushed the Outlier line to 60mm width — the widest of any Outlier at launch — with an angular body profile designed for aggressive competitive play. The overhang stainless steel rims maximize rim weight at the extreme edges of the expanded catch zone. Brandon Vu used it to place 21st worldwide and 2nd in Australia at the 2025 World YoYo Championship.

title: Outlier Limitless
content:
About
Outlier Limitless combines the established Outlier shape with the LIMITLESS platform, adding stainless steel rims to a 7075 aluminium body. Brandon Vu's own competition signature, positioned for fast, high-combo competition play.

title: Outlier Mini
content: AboutThe Outlier Mini is Brandon Vu's personal competition warmup throw. The reduced 41.9mm diameter forces greater landing precision than a full-sized yo-yo — a deliberate training constraint. Brandon's reasoning: if you can land tricks on the Mini, you can land them anywhere. It shares the Outlier bi-metal construction (6061 aluminum body, stainless steel rims) and the same bearing and response setup, compressed into a form that punishes imprecision. Brandon reaches for it before every competitive performance.

title: Outlier
content: AboutThe original Outlier was Brandon Vu's first signature yo-yo and OFFSET's debut aluminum model. Built with a 7068 aluminum body paired with stainless steel rims for extended spin time, it established the Outlier's identity as a wide, competition-ready bi-metal designed around Brandon's fast technical play. The model was later succeeded by the Outlier+ and subsequent numbered generations as the line evolved.

title: Outlier+
content: AboutThe Outlier+ is Brandon Vu's updated signature bi-metal and the model that put OFFSET on the international competition map. Its 50mm catch zone and extreme spin time — claimed at around eleven minutes — were engineered for the fast technical play Brandon uses in competition. Brandon took national and international titles with the Outlier+ in 2023, cementing it as OFFSET's flagship throw of that year. The design evolved from the original Outlier's 7068 body, switching to 6061 aluminum with revised geometry.

title: Outlier Titan
content: AboutThe Outlier Titan is OFFSET's first titanium yo-yo, co-designed by Brandon Vu and Jeffrey Pang (founder of Luftverk). The titanium body paired with stainless steel rims achieves a weight distribution geometry not possible in aluminum. Limited to 50 units, it was announced on October 30, 2024, alongside the Deviant Titan, marking OFFSET's entry into the premium titanium market. The proportions mirror the Outlier+ but the material change produces a distinctly different feel and spin character.

title: Overclock
content: AboutThe Overclock is the signature yoyo for Yiyang Wang (Philip), the Yoyofriends team leader, featuring a distinctive L-shaped inner ring running both vertically and horizontally to create a hybrid V/H shape profile. This unusual ring geometry delivers both power and speed, making it a competition-focused bimetal with a unique inner construction.

title: Overdrive
content: AboutThe Overdrive is the signature of Ryota Ogi, known for high-speed horizontal and multistyle play. The step-straight profile at 59.5mm × 44mm and a light 64g weight made it equally capable in 1A, 3A, and 5A configurations — a rare versatility for a signature model. It was updated as the New Overdrive in 2013. Ogi would later receive the Overdrive Draupnir (~2021), a full bi-metal signature carrying the Overdrive lineage forward.

title: Overdrive Draupnir
content: AboutThe Overdrive Draupnir is the return of Ryota Ogi to the yoyorecreation lineup, blending his original Overdrive signature name with the Draupnir's bi-metal construction. At 58mm × 44mm × 64.5g, it is larger than both the original Overdrive and the Draupnir, with a wing-profile body and outer stainless steel rims. The additional width versus the Draupnir broadens the catch zone for Ogi's high-speed horizontal play. It became a prominent model in the YYR mid-range bi-metal lineup after its release.

title: Overthinker
content: History / AboutDistinct base model with retailer-specific ToyToyToy edition documented separately.

title: Overture
content:
From One Drop:

"An Overture is an introduction and a start to something great.We are deeply honored to begin working with U.S. National Champion Sebastian Brock to bring his dream yo-yo into the world:  The Overture.  Sebby is a legend and has been at the top of the yo-yo competitive scene for more than a decade.  He is also an innovative yo-yo artist with a unique style.  He brings years of experience and perspective so we were thrilled to have the opportunity to build his yo-yo.  

We are  also excited to have Max Naff in the collaboration to bring us the artwork.The approach to the collaboration was to build the yo-yo that Sebby has had in his mind and heart for a long time:  a refinement of the classic organic yo-yo.   Sebby's yo-yoing is noted for plane-pushing and having many layers to the tricks, and as a result he was looking for big (58mm), stable, bead blasted yo-yo with a balanced distribution of weight that is tuned for his style.   It feels good to return to a large retro hub that allows for a little extra center weight, a beefy and reliable 16mm axle and lots of style.Besides being a top competitor, Sebby is well known for creating the The Alternative Freestyle Invitational which generally takes place at the World Yo-Yo Contest.  He had the idea to showcase the art of yo-yoing without the pressure of the point system.   He did this for the love of yo-yoing and inspiring players are all kinds to showcase their talents and style and hopefully inspire future players.Sebby hopes the Overture will inspire your play and he says that it "slays with a soul"."

title: Ovo
content: Undersized organic throwback to the mid to late 2000's.

title: P.Wave
content: Peter Pong's first C3 signature, built with the theme "Aggressive design for aggressive player." Used the Movitation as the base shape, combined with the speed of the Berserker series and the floatiness of the Master Galaxy — a fusion of three C3 designs. Machined from 7075 aluminum, loaded with Center Trac bearing. Became the shape basis for the Accelerator.

title: p3ak (Prototype)
content:
At Design Lab x Caribou Lodge
An announced but unreleased collaboration between At Design Lab and Caribou Lodge (CLYW), positioned as a reimagined/undersized entry in CLYW's Peak lineage (Legacy Peak → P3AK → p3ak). At Design Lab has stated a planned 2027 release with no exact date. No specs (diameter/width/weight/gap/axle/bearing/response) have been published by either brand as of this writing.
Note: this is distinct from CLYW's own standalone "P3AK" model (56.6mm/45mm/68g), which is already a separate released product — do not confuse specs between the two.

title: Pacer
content:
About
The Pacer focuses on sustained power and consistent pacing. Its profile and weight distribution aim for maximum accuracy during long combos, at a budget-friendly price.

title: Zephyr
content:
History / About
The Zephyr is a 3D-printed yo-yo from Pachyderm Yoyos with a 1:1 ratio of 63.6mm diameter to 63.6mm width, weighing 72.75g. The maker promoted it as "the wildest-shaped yoyo ever."
Sold directly through the maker's forum sale thread and Instagram, at $30 plus shipping. The maker notes more colors are available than shown.

title: PAKFA
content:
History / About
PAKFA (WY-008) is named for the Sukhoi PAK FA fighter program. Considered by Sturm Panzer's fans a pure expression of the brand's bimetal x Size-D-bearing x ultralight design formula.

title: PAKFA TYPE-82
content:
History / About
PAKFA TYPE-82 is a factory-production remake of the original PAKFA, with rim weight increased from 31g to 42g at the same overall body weight (body lightened by roughly 11g).

title: PAKFA TYPE-85
content:
History / About
PAKFA TYPE-85 widens the body to 44mm (from 41mm on TYPE-82) to increase rim weight and reduce wobble, and reverts to a standard M4 axle from TYPE-82's experimental M3.5 hex.

title: Palantir
content: The second officially licensed Lord of the Rings yo-yo by MK1. This is a larger, floatier organic with several colorways available.

title: Panorama
content:
This is the signature yo-yo of team member Tsukasa Takatsu from Japan. Here is his description of it:

"There are a lot of excellent yoyos in existence now. 

To us, as players, this is a joyous thing. 

With that said, I realized at some point that yoyos tend to fall into one of two groups:

Yoyos which you never really stop playing with. Without thinking about it, you leave them somewhere handy after a session. You pick them up again the next day, and again the next day. So it goes, day after day for months on end until suddenly… You realize that you’ve used them consistently for years. 

Yoyos which you play with for a few days, then put back in the box. 

What’s the difference between these two kinds of yoyos? 

I’m certainly not saying that the latter yoyos don’t play well (and actually, it’s probably harder to find a bad playing yoyo than it is to find a good one these days). In a lot of cases, these are yoyos which, at first, I have felt are really nice. 

It’s hard to identify, but this distinction was at the forefront of my mind throughout the process of designing the Panorama. My primary objective was to create a yoyo that falls into the former category, a yoyo that is never far from your reach - An authentic yoyo. In order to make the Panorama a reality, it was absolutely essential to capture this. 

High walls for increased control, rims that seem to adapt to your hand on the catch. These are some of the traits of authentic yoyos from which I took inspiration during the Panorama design process. 

However, these things alone do not make an authentic yoyo. After all, sometimes high walls can cause stress, and weight distribution designed to maximize spin time can cause a yoyo to feel out of control. Similarly, nice playing yoyos do not always transcend the era in which they were created. 

Panorama is a yoyo built with all of these things in mind, and in keeping with the sensibilities of the modern competitive scene - like a hybrid of cutting-edge tech found in a well-tuned F1 machine combined with the flavor of a classic car from the 50s.

A yoyo which seems to consistently appear in your hand and thus becomes a part of your lifestyle. It is my hope that the Panorama will become this kind of yoyo for you."

title: Papa Jim’s Imperial
content: History / AboutPapa Jim's yo-yos were handmade wooden models, slightly oversized, with large axles and good balance. The Yo-Yo Museum says the Imperial models were available in maple, oak and mahogany (the exhibit is mahogany), made in Colden, New York, and calls it a very short-lived brand. The Museum exhibit is dated 2002 and was collected in August 2003. YoYo Wiki says Papa Jim's was founded by Jim Hilburger, who toured schools demonstrating the manufacturing process, and that the yo-yos were made in both butterfly and classic shapes.

title: Papercut
content: AboutReleased as Yoyofriends' 8th Anniversary model, the Papercut is the bimetal iteration of the popular Shortcut monometal. The design broadens the outer stainless steel ring by reducing aluminum-to-steel contact while maintaining structural integrity, resulting in a light, fast, and aggressive throw that takes the Shortcut's accessible platform to bimetal performance territory.

title: Par Avion
content:
From One Drop:

"The Par Avion is a very big yo-yo.  The biggest we have ever made. But that’s not where it’s name came from.

It’s not easy trying to describe the subtle differences of how different yo-yos feel in play.  There is some good evidence that some (not all) of how players perceive these differences is subjective.   We have released over 50 different models in our history and it’s clear for each one that some people like it and some don’t.  It’s clear that there are various choices for what people consider to be their favorite One Drop. There is this phenomenon where whatever yo-yo you have been playing will affect how you perceive another one.  It’s probably because your muscles and your feel are all adjusted to a particular yo-yo and so you try a different one and it feels strange - you need time to adapt. This phenomenon shows how even the same person will perceive the same yo-yo in different ways depending on when they throw it.  Finally, it’s difficult to get agreement on the use of terms that are used to describe yo-yo play and a solid definition of what those terms mean. We have a worked with a PhD Physicist (hi, Dirty Birdy) in trying to quantify these terms but it’s a difficult task because there is no universal agreement of when and where the terms apply.

For this reason, we tend to shy away from describing how a yoyo plays in our product descriptions. We do it sometimes and to some degree, but mostly we feel it’s better if players decide for themselves.  

One of the common terms used is “Floaty”.  Clearly, a yo-yo can’t float. So what does “floaty” mean?   Generally it seems that the term refers to the yo-yo having a lightness of feeling but not necessarily that it simply is light on the scale.  It’s likely that the weight distribution plays a big role in creating this feeling. Some have described it as being easy to change the direction of the yo-yo.  And there are other possible meanings.

“Par Avion” means “By Airplane” or “By Air Mail”.  We chose this name because this yo-yo feels floaty to us and we just liked the sound of it too.  Will it feel floaty to you? It may or may not and it will be interesting to see. The Par Avion started it’s design life as us wanting to make the biggest diameter yo-yo we could (as limited by the size of material we can put through our machine) - 62.5mm.  We had also been making a lot of organic yo-yos so we thought it would be cool if there was an angular-ness to it. We weren’t sure how well it would play being so big but so far everyone who tries is really surprised - it plays fantastic. It’s fast, agile, and dare we say it, floaty.  There we go using terms. But man, this yo-yo is surprising.

We were so impressed with the play that we named it for that.  We have only done this twice before: Format:C and Downbeat.

We are looking forward to hearing how you describe the Par Avion in action."

title: Parallel
content:
From Motion:

"This is Parallel Motion.

Parallel is the final installment in a series of Perpetual-inspired yoyos. We give credit to proto team member Hunter Cuniff for his idea to create a "mini" Perpetual. The idea was planted almost immediately after Perpetual prototypes arrived, and it took a long time to finally create it. But it was well worth the wait.

Parallel is Motion's first D bearing yoyo. The D bearing is the perfect size for the undersized specs this yoyo features. While we don't consider this yoyo a "mini" at 52mm diameter, it is definitely undersized. The H shape, incredible boundary-pushing weight distribution (the body weighs only 8.45 grams per half!), and the overall light weight (less than 61g), make this yoyo perform astoundingly for its size.

Undersized yoyos often suffer from being heavy on the string. Not the case here. The yoyo feels natural, like a full-size, and it spins a long time. This is a yoyo you can truly throw in your pocket and, with it, do any trick. Incredible stability, speed, and compactness. It handles 5A, tech tricks, slacks, rejections, whips, all the things, with ease. Our customers have used it in a variety of awesome ways.

Parallel was available for pre-order, as well as Yoyo Expert, Yoyosam, and YoyoLoco retailers."

title: Parlay
content:
From One Drop:

"We have been so blessed to make yo-yos for the last ten years.  A big part of that blessing is the friends we have made and continue to make everyday.  The story of the Parlay started ten years ago at the US National Yo-Yo Contest when we stumbled upon a bunch of rad yo-yoers from Utah after a night of frolicking in the streets.  This was a different time when yo-yos were smaller, had more vibe, were just starting to be unresponsive out of the box,  and we (all of us in the community) were all in the process of creating the craft of modern yo-yo design, building and playing.  Much has been learned and the amazing yo-yos available today reflect this journey.  

We met Aaron Day of Static Co. back then and have remained good friends.  Aaron was visiting us recently and the idea of doing a collaboration came up.   Of course it did because this is all about friends and yo-yoing.  

There is a certain nostalgia that yo-yoers who played in the mid-2000s have for those "imperfect" yo-yos of the time.  The idea that Static brought to the table was to create a yo-yo that seems and feels like it was released in that era but to add the modern touches and luxuries.  The Parlay is smooth as you would expect these days.  It has Side Effects if you ever feel the urge to add some freshness to it.    It has everything we have learned about making yo-yos in it.  But you’ll feel like you just got it at the 2007 US National Yo-Yo Contest.

Here is how Static describes their journey as a yo-yo company that has led to this release.  Hopefully they will be able to parlay this collaboration into bringing more of their vision to our community.

“When we decided to make yoyos, we really didn’t know what we were doing. We mentally mashed some yoyo designs together during sessions in my garage, and sent the designs to a shop in China. They did their thing, and a few weeks later, we had a box full of yoyos.

We found that this method of manufacturing didn’t really suit us. The story of the SGNL, from the time that we signed off on the third prototype of it, to the moment that it was delivered, is a blank to us. This experience made us realize that we very much wanted to be involved in every step of the production of our yoyos going forward. We wanted a process that would allow for more input from us, more thought on our part, more effort. Something that required us to be present. In other words, we wanted to feel like we had actually given of ourselves in order to add to something that we care about.

We had planned to move production to One Drop for a few reasons: 1. They’re our homies. 2. They make the best yoyos in the world. 3. These dudes live and breathe yoyo culture. In this way, we’re on the level.

So, last summer when I visited them, I approached them about producing our next model. They countered with the proposal to collaborate on a design. We didn’t think twice about accepting.

Meet the Parlay.

Designed over a decade, executed in a day.

You might recognize some strategically placed elements from some legendary One Drop yoyos from the past (and maybe the present, for that matter) in its design. That’s probably not a mistake. The Parlay features the now signature One Drop response bump, though the area around the bump is sunken into the yoyo, effectively creating the Response Moat. This gives you the classic high wall feeling that will whip your ass into shape, but also gives you increased spin time by reducing string friction. Some players may balk at the weight of the Parlay, shipping at less than 62g with Flat Caps. Don’t go by the numbers though, man, go by the feeling. Despite its light weight, it spins for centuries, and is deceptively stable. It even has quite a bit of heft, thanks to the masterful touch of the most talented machinist in the industry.

The Parlay is a collaboration in the sincerest sense of that term. Much thought and much love, among other things, went into its design. We had such a great time teaming up with One Drop to create this yo-yo.  The result is unlike anything out right now and we truly hope you will enjoy it.”"

title: PC Hypernova
content:
From Recess:Machined Poly Carbonate Hypernova features a slightly enlarged body to compensate for lack of material density between alumimum versionsA big, fun, floaty (don’t let the weight scare you, plastic plays light!) plastic throw in tons of colors - you will love this YoYo <3Hypernova is a reissue of a timeless Tyler Severance Pro Model. Developed over 3 generations of designs, landing on a perfect shape amalgamating classic YoYo designs into a modern masterpiece. One of the first yoyos capable of effortlessly moving between multiple styles competitively (1A, 3A, 5A), and simultaneously becoming a preference with trick innovators. Combining elements from different shapes (H shape, W Shape, V Shape and Organic), and utilizing an even weight distribution, created an amazing play experience while also giving players an approachable happy medium. You could win Worlds with this YoYo, or go to YoYo Club and have fun with your friends. Going on to win 3 US National Titles, countless Worldwide International Titles, several top 3 World YoYo Contest placements, and creating a generation of classic tricks. It is a certified classic that will continue inspiring generations to come.

The PC Hypernova has three different options for colorways. Printed caps (graphic), rainbow dyed (full body), or hand-painted caps (solid).

title: PC Hypernova
content:
History / About
The PC Hypernova is a machined polycarbonate reissue of Tyler Severance's legendary Hypernova pro model, originally developed through three generations of designs at YoYoFactory. Described by Recess as "a timeless Tyler Severance Pro Model," the Hypernova won 3 US National Titles, multiple Worldwide International titles, several top-3 World Yo-Yo Contest placements, and was used to create a generation of classic tricks. It was one of the first yo-yos capable of competing across multiple styles (1A, 3A, 5A) at the same time. The shape combines elements of H, W, V, and Organic profiles with even weight distribution into a happy medium that can suit competition or casual play. The PC version is slightly larger than the aluminum Hypernova to compensate for polycarbonate's lower density. Available with hand-painted caps (each unique) and rainbow-dyed finishes as premium variants.

title: PC Rumbling
