title: Pelican
content:
About
Pelican is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2018. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Pelican 19
content:
About
Pelican 19 is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2018. This model has been retired. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Pelican (AL7)
content:
History / About
The AL7 Pelican uses 7068 aluminum instead of the standard 7075 because it anodizes and blasts better, at a cost of only about a gram of extra weight versus nearly two grams for straight 7075. G2 notes it "feels great, no thud, just a bit of extra spin but no extra lag." Distribution prioritized Patreon backers before wider release via the G2 Nation Facebook community.

title: Pendant
content:
History / About
The Pendant is a narrow 3D-printed yo-yo from Pachyderm Yoyos, measuring 53mm in diameter and 35.5mm wide at 57.5g.
Sold directly through the maker's forum sale thread and Instagram, at $28 plus shipping. The maker notes more colors are available than shown.

title: Pendulum
content: About PendulumThrow Revolution's bi-metal platform combining aluminum and stainless steel. Engineered for advanced string trick execution with precision weight distribution for extended spin time.

title: Peregrine
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Peregrine is an all-out competition yoyo is based on the input of every yoyofriends player. Every design queue is clean, simple and with one goal in mind, Maximizing performance for competition. Peregrine has a wide catch zone for ease of sting hit, wrapped around stainless steel outer rings and 7068 for extreme weight distribution, and lightweight for speed and acceleration. Peregrine is the pinnacle of competition yoyo that gives full confidence to the player at all times. We chose the name Peregrine because it is one of the highest performing Avian with insane diving speed and agility, which perfectly represents the yoyo."

title: Peregrine Rev. 1
content: AboutThe Peregrine Rev. 1 is a significant evolution of the original Peregrine bimetal, featuring a stainless steel rim weight increase of over 30% — the heaviest SS ring weight in Yoyofriends history at release — while keeping the overall weight increase to just ~1g. This dramatic redistribution enhances power and stability while preserving the original's maneuverability.

title: Peregrine X
content: AboutThe Peregrine X upgrades the legendary Peregrine platform for the modern competitive era, adding width, an expanded catch zone, increased total weight, and over 30% greater stainless steel rim mass. The extra 47.98mm width dramatically increases string landing area, while the heavier rims drive superior stability and extended spin.

title: Perpendicular
content:
From Motion:

"Say hello to our newest edition to the Motion family - Perpendicular (Motion)We are taking a detour from our typical YoYo offerings to venture into the undersized domain. The introduction of parallel was groundbreaking, as it made an undersized YoYo feel indistinguishable from a regular-sized YoYo on the string. The experience that parallel offered caught players off guard. We went back to the drawing board, choosing the D bearing as our preferred option. I strongly believe that designing a YoYo with a specific bearing size in mind allows for tailored optimization. We found inspiration in classic organics, incorporating a unique Motion twist. This YoYo is likely to leave a lasting impression on everyone."

title: Perpetual
content:
From Motion:

"Talk to me about design and play?

The crossroads where aesthetics meet functional performance. The main things I wanted to focus on were power and stability, and we nailed it.

The design shares a V/H hybrid shape that is typically reserved for more “performance oriented” yo-yos. The rounded rim design is there for a mixture of performance, aesthetics, and most of all, comfort. The YoYo is full sized and fits very nicely in your hand.

Visually the cuts and angles are meant to attract your eye from each and every angle, no matter in play or sitting on your shelf you will constantly be drawn to the design.

The unique rim design holds power on the spin. You can feel the power in every throw. Perpetual is nimble and agile enough to change direction with ease. The binds are tight and crisp, and each time the YoYo comes up into your palm you feel the momentum that was still there, realizing you could have extended the trick longer.

Being full sized, Perpetual still retains a “more narrow” design to be able to move through intricate and tighter tricks with ease. The full size also helps maintain power and momentum when you are maneuvering through each toss and trapeze.

Try one for yourself, I don’t think you will be disappointed."

1st Run (Q2 2022)

66 yoyos were made in production, in 4 colorways: 

16 Renaissance Red

16 Terra Amor

17 Infurious Red

15 Glistening Amethyst

*Two "happy accident" polished purple with black rims were also made, but not sold.

2nd Run (Q3 2024):

Shining Citrine

Matte Citrine

Hibiscus (polished)

Dark Side of the Moon

title: Perspective
content:
From One Drop:

"We are so proud and honored to have Jordan Hacherl on our players team. He’s an amazing yo-yoer and even greater person. He was overdue to get a signature model.

When he visited the factory and sat in the designing “hot seat” with The Machinist (Shawn), he proposed an interesting idea: intentionally make a yo-yo with different halves. One half being rounded and curvy and the other half being angular and straight BUT making sure that they both have the exact same basic specs (diameter, width, gap, and weight). Jordan describes the idea and the process this way:

''When David and Shawn approached me for my signature model, I initially wanted to design something more traditional. While thinking about my ideal yoyo, I realized that a unique element of One Drop’s design philosophy is innovation and trying the unconventional. Side effects, M1, the CODE series, 1-to-1, Marquis and Mantis, Fat Tire; their unique approach can be seen throughout many of their models. I wanted to approach this as not just a signature, but a true collaboration and something that would challenge the status quo of yoyo design. Shawn and I sat down and meticulously went over the design, ensuring that the halves would balance at the same center point, that weight would be distributed similarly across the separate designs, and that the width and diameter would be aligned. This ensures Perspective is extremely smooth, does not precess, and maintains balance and harmony out of the visual contrast.The two halves are representative of the earth and sky, mountains and clouds, twin spirits in union, the duology and dichotomy of all things.I hope that as you play with Perspective it encourages you to change the perspective of your tricks and reminds you to challenge the perspective of your everyday experience.'"

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Dominator
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the Dominator as a take-apart yo-yo with a metal balance and wooden axle, shaped like the Duncan Professional, with no silicone filling. It retailed for US$6 and was collected in June 1999.The YoYo Wiki says the Dominator originally used a wooden axle sleeve, later moving to a ball bearing with starbursts and then a size B bearing with foam pads, and was for a time a popular product on YoYoTricks.com.

title: Luminator
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the 1999 Luminator as a take-apart hologram ball-bearing yo-yo marked "Silicone Implanted Self-Balancing Ball Bearing Luminator", shaped like the Duncan Professional and retailing for US$9. Later models included a pad return system. The YoYo Wiki also says it was popularized by YoYoTricks.com tutorials.

title: Originator
content: History / AboutThe YoYo Wiki describes the Peter Fish Originator, also called the Yo 1, as a blue light-up yo-yo with a clutch mechanism.

title: Pamela
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum records the Pamela as a 1996 yo-yo made in Sydney, Australia, by Peter Fish & Company Proprietary Limited. It had a wooden transaxle sleeve over a metal axle, starburst response, a black and glow body of plastic and silicone, and was a take-apart model. Listed dimensions are 57 mm diameter, 31 mm width and 50.69 g. Original retail price was US$7.The museum notes the name was widely believed, though never confirmed, to refer to Pamela Anderson. The YoYo Wiki says the name changed to Silicone Glow after the initial release.

meta.yya_axle: Wooden transaxle sleeve over metal axle

title: Silicone Glow Yo
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum says this model was originally called the Pamela and had the name printed on the side cap, but within about six months the name was removed and this version followed. It is advertised as the world's first silicone-implanted self-balancing glow yo-yo, in which silicone putty fills the cavities so that centrifugal force improves balance. It has a wooden spool with a take-apart metal axle and sold for US$7. The package gives the maker as Peter Fish & Co.The YoYo Wiki lists a 1996 release, a 56 mm diameter, a 30 mm width and a slimline Duncan Professional-like shape.

title: Phantom SS – Prototype V2
content:
History / About
Phantom SS – Prototype V2 is a bimetal prototype released via G2's unannounced "Loadout Tuesday" surprise-drop format, pairing a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel components.

title: Phase
content:
From ILYY:

"In 2012 we played around with a quite unique design for an under to mid-sized yoyo called the Phase. Eventually, we released a run of 30 yoyos in a cool soda blast grey that was unlike any finish we did at the time. After this limited run, no further Phase have been produced.

We decided to give this yoyo another go with slightly updated specs to reflect our design philosophy better. As an homage to the OG these 2023 Phase feature a very chalky blasted finish. We call the finish “Kreide”, German for chalk."

Disclaimer: Please note that this Kreide-finish is not as resistant to scratches as traditional anodization. We recommend to throw the Phase with care when wearing rings or metal watches etc. to prevent undesired marks. The scratch shown here was caused by a titanium ring.

Prototype

The Phase's prototype came out in August 2012 with a run of 10 yo-yos in a titanium colorway with a Candodize finish. The specs for this yo-yo are what were used for the first production run.

1st Run

30 Phases with a grey colorway and Soda Blast finish were made.

2nd Run

11 years after the initial release of the Phase, a new run of 32 yo-yos was released in white with a Kreide finish.

Proto #1

Run 1

Run 2

title: PHASER
content: About the PHASERThe PHASER upgrades the Superfly Remix profile by adding a stainless steel rim to create sOMEThING's first stainless bi-metal. The steel rim "gives its spin an extra boost" while maintaining the same overall weight. Available in 6061 and 7075 aluminum body variants.Hajime Miura used the PHASER to win 3A at the World Yo-Yo Contest in 2014, 2015, and 2016 — three consecutive world titles — making it one of the most accomplished competition models in 3A history. Colorways included Yellow, Red, Black/Gold Rim, Emerald/Rainbow Rim, Black/Black Rim, Splash Green/Grey, Blue, and Pink.

title: Pheasant
content: Developed and designed in collaboration with spingear and players.

title: Pheasant 2023
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Pheasant 2023 is a yoyo inspired by the Japanese players. We interviewed alot of players in Japan and designed accordingly. This yoyo maximizes the ease of use and control in contest situations. It features extreme weight distribution, lightweight for maneuverability, stability and large gap width for multiple string layering. Giving player the most confidence in high stress combo and in contests."

title: Pheasant Monometal
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Pheasant Monometal is our first flagship monometal. Based on the Pheasant 2023, we tweaked the shape by adding more stages and weight to create flow and a splash of fun on top of pure performance. Resulting a yoyo that can not only perform well in contest, but also a great yoyo for everyday use. We truly think this design is a standout for our monometal offerings and proud to call it a flagship."

title: Phenom
content: About the PhenomThe Phenom is Hiroyuki Suzuki's fifth signature model and YoYoJam's most technically advanced bi-metal design, featuring brass weight rings positioned mid-body on an aluminum body rather than at the rim. This unusual placement optimizes spin axis stability for horizontal plane tricks without sacrificing standard play performance. Ships with a Dif-e-Yo KonKave bearing.

title: PHENOM
content: About the PHENOMThe PHENOM carries the name of Hiroyuki Suzuki's legendary YoYoJam-era signature but is a complete redesign built from the ground up. At 46mm wide it is one of the widest 1A models in the sOMEThING lineup, optimized for stability across long combo sequences. Mid-body stainless steel rings provide "extreme stability when performing even the longest combos." $209.99 USD.Colorways: Matte Red with Silver Rings, Matte White with Black Rings, NY Green with Silver Rings (Hiroyuki Edition), Gunmetal with Gold Rings (Yuiga Edition).

title: Phenom T
content: About the Phenom TThe Phenom T replaces the standard Phenom's brass midship rings with titanium for reduced weight with equivalent density, producing a subtly different spin profile. The flat side face without a mirror cap and laser-engraved "PHENOM TITANIUM" logo distinguish it visually from the standard Phenom. It was produced as a limited special run in a blue and silver splash finish.

title: Phenomizm
content: About the PhenomizmThe Phenomizm reproduces the Phenom's innovative midship weight ring design in a polycarbonate body with chrome-plated nickel-bronze rims, making the flagship performance profile accessible without the full-metal price. Like the Phenom, it ships with a licensed Dif-e-Yo KonKave bearing and Solid Spin Axle. Multiple special editions were produced for World and National Championship events.

title: Photon Spirit
content: The Photon Spirit introduced Auldey's innovative spinning cover-stack design — rotating side covers that can be grabbed mid-play. Plastic body with aluminum rim for weight distribution. Supports 1A, 3A, and 5A play. Bind-required for unresponsive sleep.

title: Physix
content: Empathy's first yo-yo and the signature model of Korean player Kim Min Joon. Named after his favorite bowling ball. A compact full-sized bimetal with a slightly rounded V-shape and an organic curve in the catch zone leading up to the stainless steel rim. Kim is known for his hard technical tricks and original style. The 6061 aluminum body paired with stainless steel rims delivers exceptional stability and spin time.

title: Pilgrim
content:
About
Pilgrim is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2022. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Pinecone RE
content: AboutThe Pinecone RE was the flagship model in Huatian's lineup. While much of the market trended toward ever-larger diameters and wider metal yo-yos, the Pinecone RE stuck with a standard size. Its intricately shaped, faceted body conveys an aggressive aesthetic, and players noted the very powerful rotation it generates on the throw.

title: Pinnacle
content: About the PinnacleThe Pinnacle is based on the Prelude's design and includes a counterweight dice for 5A freehand play, making it one of YoYoJam's few purpose-built 5A yo-yos. Its soft Celcon construction is gentle on the hands during extended freehand sessions. It performs equally well as a 1A yo-yo. Championship editions were produced for 2011 Worlds and Nationals.

title: PixelApe
content:
History / About
The PixelApe is co-designed by Ray Smith and MFD team manager Chris Allen (“Dr. Yo-Yo”). The angular gap geometry and open cup were deliberately engineered to encourage new trick design and grind experimentation, rather than simply optimizing for competition specs. 7075 aircraft aluminum provides added strength. The PixelApe is considered one of MFD’s most visually striking throws, frequently showcasing their most elaborate in-house anodizations.

title: PixelApe Helium
content:
History / About
The PixelApe Helium is a lighter, competition-tuned evolution of the PixelApe. Where the original PixelApe used 6061 aluminum, the Helium is machined entirely from 7075 — no 6061 anywhere in the build. At 62.3g it spins, per MonkeyfingeR, like a heavier throw despite the reduced mass. The full performance specification carries through: Tasmanian Tornado bearing and MonkeySNOT silicone response. Designed to be fast and aggressive without sacrificing the angular, visual identity of the PixelApe line.

title: Plactal
content: AboutThe Plactal is the signature model of Kohei Nishimura (2023 Japan National 1A Champion), featuring a three-material construction: polycarbonate body, aluminum core parts, and stainless steel outer rim. The rim shape is inherited from the early Fractal and Fractal JET models. Months of fine-tuning went into the innovative joining technology that bonds these three materials together. Available in Translucent Purple/Matte Gold Ring, Clear/Shiny Black Ring, and an additional Unknown Edition (Black/Black Rings).

title: Plage
content: AboutThe Plage is a hybrid yo-yo with a polycarbonate body and 6061 aluminum outer rims. Wave-inspired engraving gives it a distinctive visual character that JT describes as having a "vacation vibe." The aluminum rims add power and spin stability while the polycarbonate body maintains comfort. Available in Translucent Black/Gold Ring and Translucent Teal/Light Blue Ring.

title: Plasm
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"MK1 YoYos teams up once again with Spinworthy to bring you a fresh take on the beloved RBC—this time in plastic!

The Plasm is a polycarbonate yo-yo built for responsive play. Featuring a translucent, multi-piece construction, it offers a lightweight yet durable design that’s perfect for everyday throwing. Whether you’re working on classic tricks or just want something fun to carry on the go, the Plasm delivers smooth performance with a nostalgic feel. A modern responsive yo-yo designed to go wherever your creativity takes you."

title: Plasma Crash
content: Based on the Hydrogen Crash platform with improved spin time and maneuverability. Maintains a wide profile while being slightly smaller in size. Positioned as a refinement of the wide bi-metal formula. Price: $109.99.

title: Plastic Cheatcode
content: AboutThe Plastic Cheatcode brings the Cheatcode's Auto Orientation Technology — the angled dimple that gyroscopically forces the yo-yo into fingerspin position at any angle of contact — into a polycarbonate body accessible to any budget. Nine prototype iterations refined the performance to deliver the same trick-enabling benefit as the aluminum original. It ships responsive with an included unresponsive bearing upgrade. Co-designed by Brandon Vu and Jeffrey Pang (Luftverk).

title: Plastic Fulvia
content:
History / About
The first major plastic release from Luftverk, the Plastic Fulvia used an “Injection Machined” technique — first injection molded into a large plastic blank, then the profile is fully CNC machined for premium surface quality. Jeffrey credits this release with exponentially expanding Luftverk’s retail presence worldwide. Released in late 2022 just before he relocated from Toronto to Osaka, Japan. The project’s success funded the development of future plastic models and eventually the magnesium Akura.

title: PlasTiC StarFire
content:
History / About
Released August 16, 2025, the PlasTiC StarFire brings the Starfire hubstack shape to PETG plastic, with a flat C-size bearing, 19mm response pads, and a twist-adjustable gap that shifts the throw between responsive and unresponsive play with a quarter- to half-turn.

title: PlasTiC StarFire FR
content:
History / About
Released April 11, 2026, the PlasTiC StarFire FR ("flat-rim") is a capped variant of the PlasTiC StarFire, adding side caps and a silver pinstripe logo. Colorways included matte navy blue, with lavender and blue variants also released in small numbers.

title: Plastic 000 / Triple Zero
content:
History / About
The iconic Triple Zero design in Injection Machined polycarbonate, based directly on the original 2018 titanium model. Like the Plastic Fulvia before it, the blank is first injection molded then fully CNC machined for surface quality beyond standard injection molding. The organic shape retains the floaty, fast feel the Triple Zero is known for at a fraction of the titanium price. Released in early 2023 as the second major plastic entry in the Luftverk lineup.

title: Ace
content:
History / About
Essentially a miniature Cold Fusion GT, the Ace was one of the only miniature aluminum yo-yos Playmaxx produced, using multi-piece aluminum construction with the Brake Pad response system and a ball bearing axle.

title: Ace II
content:
History / About
The second release in Playmaxx's Ace mini-aluminum line, following the same multi-piece construction and Brake Pad response.

title: Albino Bee GT (Prototype)
content:
History / About
A test run of the Turbo Bumble Bee GT molded in undyed, natural "Proyonium" plastic (marketed internally as bulletproof). Only 12 to 15 units were ever assembled and it was never released for sale.

title: Cold Fusion
content:
History / About
Playmaxx's first aluminum yo-yo, launched in October 1998 at a premium price point of roughly $150 and reported to have exceeded sales expectations despite the cost. Regarded as one of the most sought-after aluminum yo-yos of its era.

title: Cold Fusion GT
content:
History / About
A concave butterfly-shaped variant of the Cold Fusion, built for string tricks rather than looping. Released shortly after the original Cold Fusion in late 1998.

title: Cold Fusion Isotope-1
content:
History / About
The first release in Playmaxx's limited-run "Isotope" sub-line, a slimline butterfly-shaped aluminum yo-yo. Approximately 150 units were made.

title: Cold Fusion Isotope-2
content:
History / About
The second and heavier release in the limited "Isotope" sub-line, with fewer than 150 units made.

title: Cold Fusion Nucleus
content:
History / About
A successor to the original Cold Fusion released very late in Playmaxx's independent run, with fewer than 50 units made before Duncan Toys acquired the company's assets in late 2001.

title: Crow’d Fusion Nucleus
content:
History / About
A special edition of the Cold Fusion Nucleus with one anodized red half and one anodized blue half. Only 15 pieces were made, making it among the rarest ProYo collectibles.

title: Killer Bee (Prototype)
content:
History / About
Built on the Turbo Bumble Bee, the Killer Bee was never sold at retail — it was awarded exclusively as a contest prize to winners of ProYo-sponsored competitions, in solid red plastic with special side pogs.

title: Mongoose
content:
History / About
Playmaxx's response to Henry's Viper, the Mongoose shipped as a bare metal core with rubber-ring rims. A patent held by Henrys prevented Playmaxx from legally selling its own rubber shells, so the company produced "String Pilot" shells and gave them away free to fans and beta testers rather than selling them.

title: Nuclear Ace
content:
History / About
A glow-in-the-dark variant of the mini Ace line.

title: ProFire
content:
History / About
Released as a lower-cost alternative to the Turbo Bumble Bee, the ProFire used a two-piece brass transaxle sleeve rather than a ball bearing, paired with the Brake Pad response system. Shipped with a spare string and a spare Brake Pad.

title: ProFire GT
content:
History / About
A butterfly (GT) shaped variant of the ProFire, sharing the same body shape as the ProYo II GT.

title: ProYo
content:
History / About
Patented in 1974 and put into production in 1976, the ProYo was the founding product of the company that became Duncraft, then Duracraft, then Playmaxx in 1988. A rim-weighted, central-spool fixed-axle design with undercuts for string tricks, it was marketed as "copied by many, duplicated by none" and remained in production until it was replaced by the ProYo II in October 1996.

title: ProYo II
content:
History / About
Released in October 1996 to replace the original ProYo, the ProYo II used a patented wood-axle design that allowed for interchangeable side caps ("pogs") and a holographic silver insert seal. Marketed as the "world's longest spinning fixed-axle yo-yo, with tricks inside," it became a top seller internationally, distributed in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Indonesia, Japan, the UK, Poland, Greece, Norway, Sweden, Italy, Finland, Canada, and Denmark.

title: ProYo II GT
content:
History / About
A wing/butterfly-shaped variant of the ProYo II sharing its wood-axle sleeve design, aimed at beginners and string tricks rather than long sleep times. After Duncan Toys acquired Playmaxx in 2001, this model was rebranded and sold as the "ProFly."

title: ProYo III
content:
History / About
The last of the original fixed-axle ProYo line, succeeding the ProYo II as Playmaxx's entry-level model. Overseas distribution was handled by TCL, with more consistent manufacturing quality than earlier runs. Widely used as the base for promotional and custom pog editions.

title: Roadster
content:
History / About
Computer-designed to mimic the ProYo's playing characteristics while excelling as a looping yo-yo, the Roadster is unusually large at 63.5mm — a dimension that originated as a manufacturing error but was kept intentionally. Most units were sold unfinished, with laser-carved graphics on raw wood; a small number were factory-stained or finished. Some units carried the "Flores" name, its rights licensed by Playmaxx as a nod to yo-yo pioneer Pedro Flores. Discontinued when Duncan Toys acquired Playmaxx in 2001.

title: Turbo Bumble Bee
content:
History / About
Playmaxx's best-selling model and its first yo-yo to use the patented "Brake Pad" response system — replaceable cork-like starburst pads. Nicknamed the "Butterbee," it used a stainless steel A-size ball bearing axle, a significant step up from the fixed-axle ProYo line. Renamed simply "Bumblebee" after Duncan Toys acquired Playmaxx in 2001.

title: Turbo Bumble Bee GT
content:
History / About
A butterfly (GT) shaped version of the Turbo Bumble Bee, sharing its Brake Pad response system and ball-bearing axle, for wider string-trick performance.

title: Vid-e-Yo
content:
History / About
A companion product to Playmaxx's "Vid-e-Yo" instructional video (produced with TimeLine Video, winner of a 1998 "Aurora" Platinum Best-of-Show award). Shipped with 10 interchangeable 3-D caps featuring Playmaxx demonstrators YoHans, Ben McPhee, John Higby, and Julius performing tricks, plus a hologram-effect pog.

title: Vid-e-Yo GT
content:
History / About
A butterfly (GT) shaped variant of the Vid-e-Yo, following the original's release.

title: X-Ray Bee
content:
History / About
A limited-edition Turbo Bumble Bee variant produced in translucent "ProYo blue" plastic.

title: please UNBLOCK me – Keiran Edition UNLOCK
content:
About
The "please UNBLOCK me" Keiran Edition is a limited-edition collaboration between "alternatives" and OFFSET based on the UNLOCK platform. The colourway was designed entirely by Keiran Cooper (@krncpr). Severely restricted inventory; released at AP Open 2026 Singapore and PNWR. $140.

title: Plumpy V2 (Prototype)
content:
About
Round-two signature prototype for team member Collin (forum handle Son-of-Morris) — not a formal brand collaboration, just an individual player's signature model. Sold out shortly after release.

title: PNIR
content:
History / About
PNIR is a carved — not injection-molded — plastic model released November 17, 2025, giving it the machining freedom typically reserved for metal yo-yos. It has a recessed center designed for finger-spin tricks such as "DNA."

title: Pocket Gravitation
content: AboutThe Pocket Gravitation is AceYo's smallest mono-metal, designed to fit in a pocket without sacrificing performance. Despite its compact 44mm diameter it handles technical tricks with ease.

title: Beginner
content:
About the Beginner

The Beginner is the entry-level model in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010 at $4.99. A fixed-axle plastic yo-yo in a classic imperial shape, it was designed for learning basic looping tricks and did not disassemble. Available in blue, green, and red, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet and sold through mass-market toy retail channels.

title: Boomerang
content:
About the Boomerang

The Boomerang is the beginner-intermediate model in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010 at $7.99. A plastic yo-yo with a centrifugal clutch mechanism that automatically returns the yo-yo to the hand as spin decreases, the Boomerang was designed to help beginners master tricks without needing to perfect throw tension. Available in blue, green, orange, and yellow, it included a 50/50 poly-cotton string and trick instruction booklet.

title: Creeper
content:
About the Creeper

The Creeper is a novelty yo-yo in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010 at $7.99. A butterfly-shaped take-apart plastic yo-yo made from transparent acrylic, the Creeper contains a real farm-raised spider permanently encased in the body — making each unit visually unique. Available in red, green, and blue acrylic, it was part of Pocket Pros' bug series alongside the Stinger Blonde and Stinger Black. Included a 50/50 poly-cotton string and trick instruction booklet.

title: Dragon
content:
About the Dragon

The Dragon is the intermediate-level model in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010 at $9.99. A plastic looping yo-yo in a modified classic/imperial shape, it featured the brand's proprietary "18K Gold Pro" gold-plated ball bearing for extended spin times. Included Pocket Pros' Slick Six string — a 6-strand, 80/20 poly-cotton blend. Available in black, blue, and green, it was packaged with a trick instruction booklet.

title: Stinger Black
content:
About the Stinger Black

The Stinger Black is a novelty yo-yo in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010. A transparent acrylic take-apart yo-yo with a real farm-raised black scorpion permanently encased in the body, it is the dark-scorpion companion to the Stinger Blonde. It appears in all Pocket Pros product navigation from 2010 onward; no product detail page was archived by the Wayback Machine, leaving colorways and retail price unconfirmed.

title: Stinger Blonde
content:
About the Stinger Blonde

The Stinger Blonde is a novelty yo-yo in the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010 at $7.99. A butterfly-shaped take-apart plastic yo-yo made from transparent acrylic, the Stinger Blonde contains a real farm-raised blonde/light-colored scorpion permanently encased in the body. Available in blue, purple, and red acrylic, it was part of Pocket Pros' bug series alongside the Creeper and Stinger Black. Companion piece to the Stinger Black.

title: Vampire
content:
About the Vampire

The Vampire was part of the original four-model Pocket Pros launch lineup in 2010, alongside the Zombie, Dragon, and Boomerang. It appears consistently in product navigation across archived versions of pocket-pros.com through 2011 and is referenced in the yoyo.fandom.com Pocket Pros article. No product detail page was captured by the Wayback Machine, leaving material, specs, colorways, and price unrecorded.

title: Zombie
content:
About the Zombie

The Zombie is the flagship model of the Pocket Pros lineup, released in 2010. Machined from aircraft-grade aluminum in a slimline butterfly shape, the Zombie was one of the least expensive metal yo-yos available at mass retail at approximately $19.99. It featured reversible silicone brake pads (one flat side, one starburst side), Pocket Pros' Slick Six 6-strand string, and a ball bearing axle for unresponsive string-trick play.

The bearing specification changed across production runs: the 2010 version used a Size C V-Notch ABEC-7 bearing, later versions used the brand's non-standard 18K Gold Pro bearing, and subsequent runs returned to a standard high-performance Size C. Available in silver, candy red, and lime green. The Zombie should not be confused with the Small Minds Zombie, an unrelated earlier model.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (ABEC-7; later runs: 18K Gold Pro / standard Size C)

title: Pocket Watch
content:
About
Pocket Watch is a solid machined brass responsive throw — small enough to disappear in a pocket. Ships with a proprietary MR85 micro-response bearing custom-made for Return Bottoms by the factory, and "String Burn" silicone response pads (Shore 40A). $5 of each sale is donated to Book Trust, a childhood literacy charity.

title: Pocket Watch — Nickel Plated
content:
About
A nickel-plated special edition of the Pocket Watch, limited to 40 units. Same brass-body responsive construction as the standard Naked Brass edition, finished in nickel plating.

title: Polaris
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re kicking off the year with the Polaris – a design that encapsulates fluid power.

SPECSDiameter: 54.9mmWidth: 46.0mmWeight: 67.5gMaterial: titanium

Atmos’ roots lie in organic design, but working on various performance-oriented, high function designs has been such a joy.

While this segment in the market has been saturated, particularly over the past couple of years, we’ve found gaps and niches that make the space a welcome challenger to tinker in. That’s been the raison d’etre of the Weatherman Line – a product line dedicated to experimentation and fresh expression in the high performance yoyo space.

The Weatherman Line currently comprises the Khuno, Ari, Aria, and other designs that are still in the works. The Aria evolved from the Ari, a titanium, Side-Effects and cap-enabled iteration of the Khuno. The Khuno was the first-ever bimetal in history to accept Side Effects, and the Ari remains one of our most beloved designs to date. 

In the Aria we tunneled into a performance focus; we kept the general form factor, but removed the Side Effects components of design for players who treasured play and performance over customizability and modularity. What emerged was a performance-optimized, 57mm-diametqer beast. It had a big frame, and was technically “heavier” than average at 68g – but the Aria was one project where we learned an enormous amount about how to make powerful designs in the high 60+g range feel fluid and nimble, breaking conventions and expectations of how heavy yoyos generally feel sluggish and reluctant. 

The Aria turned out feeling like a muscle car that hummed silently with torque – it had a low-center-of-gravity smoothness of movement, immense stability, and gave players superb control over pace, with the play experience never coming close to being overbearing, or bricky.

We’ve had questions regarding the width of our designs, and why they’re always as wide as they are. Our slimmest design clocks in at 45.6mm, but the rest mostly hang around the 48mm-range. In terms of ergonomics, we make sure they feel nice and full in the hand, though it can feel large for some. Our decisions about the width of our designs are intentional – they allow us the space to do creative things with weight distribution that produces a signature litheness with surprising power. The Aria is a specimen of that formula. 

For our first release of the year, the Polaris is a fresh reimagination of the Aria concept that dials up performance, power and control, but packed into a smaller form factor. We were incredibly inspired by the Chopsticks Gorilla and Toru 0.99 by Yoyorecreation, as well as the Cetus by Turning Point, which we regard as industry-leading examples of designs that have compact frames, but are outsized in performance. 

In conversations with Yuji, Coleman and Vladimir, we got excited to work on a model that embodied that fluidity and power, without a “min-max” approach to weight distribution, or bombastic physical frames.

Going small while increasing power requires some tinkering, as the two aims are not instinctively compatible. Generally, all things held constant, a larger diameter leads to more rotational power. Reducing overall size while stepping up power required a structural overhaul, as well as a shift towards a more extreme diameter-to-width ratio. 

We scrapped the rim design in the Aria, and redesigned it to further optimize it for power. The Aria’s rim was a simple, even extrusion, whereas the Polaris sports an angled, dipped rim that packs a deceptive amount of mass. The Polaris also features a gradual domed hub – which, alongside the heftier rim design, provides a distribution of weight that perfectly balances power with fluidity.

On the surface of the Polaris, we kept the signature cuts and lines that call back to the Khuno, and have been present in the Weatherman Line. It’s extremely comfortable in hand, and it doesn’t feel like you have a traditionally performant model in hand. It’s elegant and minimalist, but extremely functional.

Playwise, it weaves in and out of technical mounts without sacrificing stability and power, and even improving upon the agility and maneuverability of the Aria. It’s just as stable, but has a degree of fluidity that its predecessor lacks.

Polaris is Latin for pole star, which is beautifully evocative of the celestial, and etymologically it also draws from polus, which translates to “end of an axis” – which is an interesting play on design terminology.

Polaris also pays homage to the Weatherman Line in that ari is embedded in its name.

The turn of the year represents many new things – including a refreshed direction in our product design philosophy.

The Polaris typifies that, and we’re incredibly excited to share that with you.

title: Pollen
content: AboutPollen is wound from 100% cotton in the Throw-Yo Threads Responsive family. Grippy disposition, glacial velocity, and coarse feel make it the most traditional responsive string in the lineup — ideal for fixed axle and 0A play where grab and snap response matter. Custom Pollen colorways were bundled with the Return Bottoms Demon's Fun (70-piece run). Available in Yarrow colorway alongside monocolor.

title: Polyberry
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

The Polyberry is a modernised, polycarbonate remake of the Snowberry — a perfect blend of float and fun, while having enough juice to power through any trickset.

SPECS

Diameter 58.4mmWidth 50.3mmWeight 68.5gMaterial Polycarbonate

The Polyberry began with a desire to bring back the Snowberry, but in an improved, modernised way.

The Snowberry was our first ever plastic design, which we released in October 2022. At the time, the Snowberry was our homage to plastic yoyos — a genre that we grew up around, having come into the scene in the early 2000s. The Snowberry knocked our expectations out of the park and has been a staple in our lineup ever since. We have projects that exist best as one-and-done small batches, and then there are designs that deserve a permanent, evergreen spot in the rotation.

Our first plastic Berry definitely fit the mold of the latter, and we’re excited that the Polyberry will take its place today. The Snowberry also sparked a love in us for working with machined plastic. We were so taken by Delrin as a material, and that delight was deepened when we worked with polycarbonate on the Arctica, which later inspired our work on the Canopy PC. Earlier this year, we released Coleman’s signature in the Smoke, which combined both Delrin and polycarbonate in one of our most true, unique and honest designs. Working with these materials has just been such a joy.

We’re exactly three years from releasing the Snowberry, and the Polyberry exists today as our fifth plastic release. The Polyberry doesn’t just reflect much of our experience, learnings and familiarity with the material, but also our evolving personal philosophy with organic design, material choice, and objects of play.

The most immediate aspect of machined polycarbonate is its look and feel. Frosted plastic has a timeless, understated aesthetic — at the same time, it’s an incredibly versatile material. It’s soft enough in the hand and in play, but rigid enough that it yields excellent and predictable results from a manufacturing perspective. This unique balance allows the design process immense flexibility and creativity — working with it often feels like an inviting canvas for experimentation and play.

The capability of plastic designs have also vastly improved over the years. You still wouldn’t opt to compete with one, but when it comes to casual performance, modern plastics have seriously started to punch way above their weight.

A quick note on materials that bears mentioning — polycarbonate designs tend to sound a lot bigger than they actually are. Polycarbonate is roughly 44% the density of 6061 aluminum, so given the relationship between mass, diameter, density and overall spin power, the usual physical measurements can look and feel inflated.

TThe Polyberry is 58.4mm in diameter, 50.3mm in width, and 68.5g in mass, but contrary to what the numbers could imply, it doesn’t play overweight, or clumsy in the least. The Polyberry is one of the most floaty and agile and controlled yoyos we’ve designed — likely even more so than its predecessor.

This is subjective, of course, but the “real feel” of the yoyo is a lot closer to a 64g monometal design, if that comparison makes sense.

How the Polyberry most obviously departs from the Snowberry is the removal of the schmoove step and a vastly thickened rim. These structural changes allowed us to apportion mass more strategically — when the Polyberry gets up to speed, it’s significantly more stable than the Snowberry.

If you’ve tried any of our organics, the playfeel of the Polyberry will feel very familiar. It excels in flow, motion-focused play, and directional shifts. It handles pace and momentum well, feels very controlled, and has a wonderful “hang time” in the air.

It has to be said — the ergonomics are wonderfully friendly, too. The Polyberry sports a very round and bubbly silhouette. It’s extremely friendly in the hand, and is exceedingly soft on the catch.

We’ve used this comparison before, but it feels like catching a baseball with an old, seasoned glove.

We designed the Polyberry as a successor to the Snowberry — and for it exist in our lineup as a casual player’s rotation favourite. It’s the one you bring along for long roadtrips, the one that feels right to bust out on the Subway on the way home, the one you pick up on a late night jam. It’s the one you accidentally nail bangers on, it’s the one you drop a thousand times, the one you gift an old friend at the local meetup.

The polyberry is fun, smooth and light. It’s deceptively capable, and doesn’t take itself too seriously.

We hope you enjoy this one.

title: Polybius
content: AboutThe Polybius is a rim-weighted monometal praised in community reviews for delivering "bimetal performance in a mono." Designed for confident long combos, with rounded rim edges for comfortable catches. A limited-run release available through the OPYOYOS website, continuing Jordan Blofeld's philosophy of high-spec, low-production-volume throws.

title: A4
content: History / AboutPer Polyform, the A4 is named as a representation of a blank page for a fresh start. It is a 6061 aluminum body with a hollow Polyamide 66 nylon ring, and uses the new PF20.6 response pad, developed for a snappier bind than conventional 19mm pads. An extra pair of white silicone pads, a random sticker design and string are included, and a fatter string is recommended. YoYoExpert lists the release as April 2023. Yoyo Store Rewind (Japan) says Polyform was launched by Jeffrey of Luftverk and the A4 is its first release.

title: DEMA
content: History / AboutPer Polyform, the DEMA is the signature yoyo of sponsored player Jacky Le, the result of six months of testing and feedback. It is a 6061 aluminum monometal with cuts on the body that create an illusion of a "pixelated hub", tuned weight distribution, and PF20.6 pads. An extra pair of white silicone pads is included, and part of the proceeds supports Jacky. The Micro-Arc Ceramic finish is slightly abrasive at first and can fray string until broken in. YoYoExpert lists the release as April 2023.

title: POM Draupnir
content: AboutThe POM Draupnir launched the YoYoRecreation AE sub-brand in June 2017, alongside the announcement that AE would deliver cutting-edge designs at more moderate price points than the main YYR line. The model takes the Draupnir's exact shape and outer stainless steel rim construction but replaces the 7075 aluminum body with POM (polyoxymethylene/Delrin) — a denser engineering plastic that produces a distinct feel under the fingers and a weight profile very close to the aluminum version. A Full Black limited edition was available exclusively through the official store.

title: Pomelo
content:
The following is archived from Atmos' website:

This is something we’ve been working on for months and months, and we’re excited to finally introduce the second project in our line-up. Here is the Pomelo.

SPECS

dia 65.3mmwid 54.96mmweight 61.3gmaterial 7068 AL

I’ve always loved oversized throws. I got into yo-yoing in 2006, a time where Duncan’s Hardcore line was still very much the rage. The first bearing yoyo I ever got was the Duncan Throw Monkey, Duncan’s 5A-centric model, and I absolutely loved it. At 63mm in diameter and around 70g, it was quite a handful, but there was a charm to its physical largesse, both in roundness and bounciness of the shape and material. I remembered going through wads of friction stickers on the Throw Monkey, shredding it through the summer.

In time, I found a new favourite in the Freehand Zero — which was Duncan’s premium choice for “performance” plastics at the time; it excelled in ways the Throw Monkey did not, and its design allowed for nimbler and more precise play.

I never forgot, however, the comfort and satisfaction of the way a large, fat throw felt in the hand, or the fun of hitting tricks on a yoyo of such massive proportions. The tactile signature of these “biggies” were unique; sometimes it felt like you were playing 1A and 4A at once.

The Pomelo is a modern love letter to the oversized throws of bygone eras. It is not made for dense tech, or play that abides by the current meta; the Pomelo is made for risky bangers, creative movement tricks, and excels at regens, binds and whip-style tricks, and more artistic and expressive play. It has soul, and is just really, really fun to throw.

The Pomelo is named after one of the largest citrus fruits, and true to form, it is unapologetically large, sitting at 65.3mm in diameter and 55mm in width. (The word pomelo also feels like a portmanteau of pillow and marshmallow, “pi-mallow”, which represents all the characteristics of it being big, but airy and light… but that’s just us being silly.)

In the Pomelo, we adapted the step-and-schmoove response area from the Cloudberry, which allows it to glide smoothly on the string and to take serious layering without snagging. We also adapted our response gap to keep binds tight and predictable, and it shows; we put the Pomelo through a gauntlet of bind tests — low rpms, ghosts, whip-types — and it missed next to none of them. In other words, uncompromising and dependable in the right places, but forgiving where it needs to be.

The most exciting feature of the Pomelo to me, and what distinguishes it from its oversized counterparts, is its light weight. One downside of old-school oversized throws like the Throw Monkey or Flying Panda were that they were flat-out dense, given their rubber-rims and polycarbonate-shell hybrid construction. At only 61.3g, the Pomelo is incredibly featherweight, especially given its large profile, and is svelte on the string.

We maximised the characteristics of 7068 AL, keeping the walls as thin as the material would allow, and also kept rim weight to a minimum. We put a little raised doughnut around the “halo” on the cup to add just a bit of center weight.

The overall mass and how it is distributed gives it an insanely fun playfeel. It is ridiculously floaty and willowy, and its strange how something this large and fat could move so nimbly. It really does feel like a pillow on a string.

The heart of our project in the Cloudberry was in finding a sweet spot between fun and performance; the soul of the Pomelo is similar. While it aces modern tests of playability, it fundamentally pays homage to its old-school forebears — and joins a lineage that lives on in other throws like the 420, Burm, Overture, and Par Avion.

The Pomelo is a delight to me personally, as it takes its cue from the past, but has a seat at the table of modern throwing. We’re hoping it brings you as much joy as it does us.

Thank you for reading this long post, and for all your support so far. Please let me know if you have any thoughts or responses – I would really love to hear them.

·January 2021

·

·

title: Pomodoro
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re adding more organic sauce in our lineup. We’re proud to introduce the Pomodoro.

SPECSDiameter5 5mmWidth 45.2mmWeight 66g (base) 68.7g(heavy)Material 6061 AL

The Pomodoro joins the Cloudberry, Goji, Thunderberry and others in our Fruitbowl design line. It’s one our first organics that doesn’t fall within the ultrawide category, and it also sports a Side Effects hub design that is a first in the field.

This one took some time to get perfect. Some designs are straightforward, and you can tell you really nailed it the first time around. Some others, like the Pomodoro, have a longer, winding route. We’ve been working on this since April 2021 – two years and three prototypes later, we think we’ve finally landed on something special.

The first prototype of the Pomodoro was machined in 2021. This was during a season of wide experimentation – the same period that produced the Goji and Pomelo, so you can imagine the sort of parameters we were happy to toy with. The idea was to produce a model that played like a slimmer, more center-weighted Cloudberry. What resulted was this prototype – it played fairly well and had surprising power for its size, but it ultimately lacked character. It was on par with the Cloudberry in performance, but it didn’t feel special enough in terms of playfeel. A deeper overhaul was clearly necessary, so we shelved it in favor of other projects.

We returned to the prototype in 2022, this time adding significant elements to the design concept. Minor design changes included a different diameter-to-width ratio, and a bit more heft, but the major departure from Prototype I was in pursuing a proof of concept of an embedded Side Effects slot, which would be flushed with a rounded hub. If executed properly, Ultra Light Side Effects would sit entirely flushed with the surface.

All Side Effect designs that currently exist utilize a protruded nipple – not dissimilar to the Khuno, Ari and Noah. While there have been adaptations of this nipple, such as in titanium designs like the Gravity (which we produced alongside our friends at RSO), we believe this is the first design that allows the Side Effect to sit cleanly and fully within the hub.

10 units of Prototype II were made, and we gave a few of them away during our first November Market event. Together with some given to Coleman and Evgeniy as testers, there are about 8 of these in the wild.

It was a big leap from Prototype I, but Prototype II still had some significant faults – it felt anemic, and still did not have enough presence on the string. The rims were also too sharp, and it didn’t have the fullness of in-hand comfort that has come to be a signature of our designs.

We went back to the drawing board and worked on it until early 2023, when we felt ready for a third shot at the design concept. We sent in new blueprints for machining, and what resulted was a rounder, fatter, and more whole version of the Pomodoro.

Prototype III didn’t just sport a fuller and rounder frame throughout, it also played a whole lot better.

We increased the center-mass with a much rounder hub, but balanced that increase with a fuller and thicker rim design for increased spin power.

The protruding nipple contributes nicely to an angular, industrial look – we love how it looks with the Ari – but can be disruptive to an organic, rounded shape. In the Pomodoro we wanted to push design coherence and a purer look in a Side Effects enabled organic.

It also has the narrowest width in our lineup – for reference, the Cloudberry is 48mm wide, while the Pomodoro sits at a relatively normal 45.2mm in width.

In play, the Pomodoro feels close to the Cloudberry if it were condensed into a smaller, more compact frame, and if it were more center-weighted. It’s a touch heavier at 66g (Base Weight), but less reluctant, and has a nice momentum to it.

The Pomodoro is the heaviest entry of our organics, but its weight distribution makes it amenable to directional shifts and quick, nimble rhythmic movements. It has some of that float that many of our designs have, it flows and shifts nimbly, and is incredibly easy to control.

The Base weight is with Aluminum Ultra Lights installed; this weight option is what feels the most natural and “native” to us. For those that enjoy plenty of center-weight, we’ll also have Heavy options that clock a nice, massy 68.7g. They’ll be available in select colorways and come with Brass Ultra Lights installed.

The Pomodoro is not made for the modern meta. It will not DNA or horizontal well if that is your focus. We design some yoyos for tech under the Weatherman line, but this isn’t it. It’s subtle and sensitive; it lets you know when more finesse is required. This is meant for those who enjoy the subtlety of organic goodness.

Note – we hand-tune each Pomodoro for smooth play before we send them out, but as it is with any Side Effects design, players should expect that, should faint vibe occur, some degree of tuning is part of the game.

title: Weasel Gen 2
content:
History / About
The Weasel Gen 2 is Pop! Yoyos' revised production run of their original Weasel, addressing community feedback about the Gen 1's sharp thorn spike. Founded in April 2025 by Ben Seaberg out of the Pacific Northwest, Pop! Yoyos debuted the Weasel Gen 1 in 2025. The Gen 2 debuted at US Nationals in May 2026, featuring a blunted spike for safety and a slightly widened gap for improved power. It sold in two colorways — Lilac Attack and Green Apple — at $75 (A-grade) and $60 (B-grade).

title: Pory Crash
content: C3 × PoryKon collaboration combining PoryKon's 5A philosophy with the Crash series design language. Shape combines elements of the Galaxy Diver and Gamma Crash. Available in both POM (soft feel) and PC (lighter, harder) body variants with stainless steel ring. PORY CRASH R2 released March 2021.

title: Porycrash
content:
About
The Porycrash is the result of C3yoyodesign's expertise in the Crash series (Galaxy Diver, Gamma Crash) combined with PoryKon's deep knowledge of 5A freehand play. The collaboration produced an H-profile bi-material yo-yo engineered for both 1A string play and 5A counterweight play — optimized for stable spin and comfortable aerial catches during freehand trick sequences.
The Porycrash was produced in two material editions: a POM body version and a polycarbonate body version, both with stainless steel rings. Multi-step cuts in the body reduce weight while rounded rim edges ease 5A hand catches when the yo-yo comes back unpredictably through the air. The diameter is 1.9mm wider than C3's Galaxy Diver, with a 1.7mm reduction in width — a geometry shaped by PoryKon's understanding of what makes a yo-yo easier to catch in freehand play. Released July 29, 2020, in six standard colorways. Two special bundled editions paired the Porycrash with a custom PoryKon V counterweight.

title: Positional
content:
History / About
Inspired by the performance and popularity of the Accelerated, the Positional takes that proven design philosophy in a new direction with a D bearing setup and premium 7068 aluminum construction. The Accelerated earned a reputation for its speed, agility, and power while maintaining a compact, competition-ready profile. With the Positional, Motion YoYo revisited those ideas from the ground up, designing a yo-yo specifically around the unique characteristics of a D bearing rather than simply adapting an existing model.
Every element of the Positional was carefully refined to maximize efficiency and performance. The smaller D bearing delivers quick acceleration and a distinct feel on the string, while the surrounding weight distribution has been tuned to maintain stability and minimize unwanted spin loss. It carries over the signature "rim bump" design first introduced on the Accelerated, a feature that has become a recognizable part of Motion YoYo's design language. The result is a yo-yo that feels fast, responsive, and remarkably confident throughout long trick sequences.
Each Positional ships with a string from Big Red Strings.

title: Positron
content: A collaboration between Auldey and Turning Point of Japan. The Positron features a step-round shape with M4x8mm axle. Includes LED unit (randomly colored, not pre-installed). Multiple splash colorways available. Endorsed by Kentaro Kimura, Turning Point founder and 3A specialist.

title: Possum
content: HistoryThe Possum, released October 26, 2024, is a collaborative design between Jeremy Park of ZipLine Strings and designer Terry Orchard. Drawing inspiration from "the button nose and floppy ears of small mammals," the undersized rounded-V profile (48.6mm diameter) was built for pocket carry and everyday use. In 6061 aluminum with a soft bead-blast finish, the Possum lands at 63.1g — light for its diameter. Initial colorways included Speckled Teal, Speckled Brown, and a Half-Swap combination; a second run followed January 17, 2025 in additional options including Ultra Violet and LT Sage Grey. Priced at $65.

title: Potion Strings
content:
Throw-Yo Threads' first strings produced. These strings were made of 100% polyester and came in 3 different varieties:

Filtered Potions

These strings were made of spun polyester and were wound tightly. They did not use pretwisted strands, and could be hard to string up on a yo-yo.

Semi-Filtered Potions

These strings were made of a blend of spun polyester and trilobal polyester and were wound tightly. They did not use pretwisted strands, and could be hard to string up on a yo-yo.

Unfiltered Potions

These strings were made of trilobal polyester and were wound tightly. They did not use pretwisted strands, and could be hard to string up on a yo-yo.

title: Practice Yo-Yo
content: HistoryThe Practice Yo-Yo was Cheerio's basic entry-level model, designed for beginners and casual players. Estimated dimensions: 2.25" diameter × 1.25" depth. Produced throughout the 1950s.

title: PreFluchs
content:
The Fluchs prototype.  From what I’ve seen there were 8 of these made. I’ve seen them in a clear ano, and a half/half silver & red.  These were thinner and heavier than the production Fluchs, and had a larger axle nub.  Hoping to get specs on these.

This is, from what I was told, the prototype that became what we know as the Fluchs.

title: Prelude
content: About the PreludeThe Prelude is one of YoYoJam's lightest models at 56.8 grams, designed for players beginning to explore string tricks before committing to a full-featured yo-yo. A thin C bearing ships installed for tug-responsive play, and the design accepts a standard C bearing for bind conversion. Championship editions were produced for 2011 Worlds, Nationals, and 2012 EYYC events.

title: Prescription
content:
From One Drop:

"Hey there. Doctor B here at your service.

Diagnosis: Need the perfect Yo-YoPrescription: Signature Yo-YoPrognosis: Most Excellent

The Prescription is the yo-yo I see in my head whenever I close my eyes. I've been lucky enough to have thrown thousands of yo-yos over the course of the past 23 years since I started playing when I was a little kid: Wood yo-yos, pioneering bearing yo-yos, and every kind of innovation and breakthrough in between. And when I started throwing for One Drop almost four years ago, I knew that eventually I'd have the opportunity to leave my mark on the community that I love with my very own signature yo-yo.

Give me the curves of the Cascade. Give me the weight and hand-feel of the Project 2. Tweak the weight distribution. Make sure the Projection Profile is juuuuust right. Oh, and Side Effects. Gotta have those.

It's crazy to me that soon, very soon, you're going to be holding in your hands something that is so, so important to me. After all these years, after all those contests and club meetings, after all those videos, and after meeting all of YOU, it's finally here...and I couldn't be happier.

So if the Doctor could make a recommendation, you should call or text up your favorite human beings and invite them over, let them know you have a Prescription on the way, don’t forget to cook or order some food, and spend the evening sharing tricks and catching up. Then, when you wake up in the morning, repeat that process. Get your daily dose of this yo-yo, and I bet you'll start feeling better. Not because you felt bad before, but because sometimes we all know deep inside we deserve more happiness. Will this yo-yo make you happier? Well, all I know is that it makes me happier than I can believe. Your mileage may vary, but I highly doubt it.

During my last trip out to Eugene to visit the One Drop shop, I got to spend a lot of time with Shawn to make sure the yo-yo that we made exactly the yo-yo I wanted. So when we sat down, we turned on some jazz, and I got to watch Shawn work his magic. He’s the Dizzie Gillespie of CNC machines, the Charlie Parker of CAD...and getting the chance to sit down and envision my dream yo-yo with him was one of the best experiences of my life. When we saw the first halves getting finished up, we tested them out and kept working hard to bring you this yo-yo. Each prototype and iteration was better than the last by a large margin, and we ended up with a throw that represents me and my style better than anything I’ve played before.

At the end of the day, the Prescription feels like the Cascade's older, more refined, and obviously more handsome brother. It's got some float paired with mid-weighting, which means it's perfect for complex and intricate movements. It’s stable and surprisingly fast when you push it hard.

And, trust me. They call me the Doctor for a reason. I know just what you need. Side Effects included."

title: Prime8
content:
History / About
The Prime8 is MonkeyfingeR Design’s signature model for Tyler Jorgensen (MFD Team Captain). The name is a play on "primate" and the eight great ape species. The design features two inner thumb grind rings that also serve as weight distribution channels — an uncommon detail that gives the cup a distinctive appearance. Two alloy variants were released simultaneously: the standard 6061 (65g) and a stiffer 7075 (68g). Ships in a custom triangle display box with Ape Hangers string.

title: Prober
content: About the ProberThe Prober was a King Yo Star model referenced in promotional giveaway content (circa 2013) and featured in Josh Yee's February 2015 video "Bet On It." No specifications, price, or colorway information has been publicly documented.

title: Procyon
content: HistoryProject Cosmos' first release captures the early 2010s monometal aesthetic, reimagined for modern daily play. Each unit ships with a center sticker for customization.The Procyon was finalized after four iterations of prototyping, with direct feedback from the local Korean yo-yo community.

title: Progressiver
content: History / About6061 and stainless-steel retail competition design, also sold in a Shibuya-specific color edition.

title: ProJam
content: About the ProJamThe ProJam is YoYoJam's most basic production yo-yo, sold primarily in bulk (minimum 50 units) for school demonstrations, promotional events, and introductory kits at approximately $10 USD retail. Special commemorative side caps were produced for major championship events.

title: Project
content:
One Drop's initial release. Here's the description of the yo-yo, in One Drop's own words:

"The One Drop Project Yo-Yo is designed, manufactured and supported in Eugene, Oregon by a partnership between One Drop Design and Designer/Yo-Yoer Colin Leland. This is the first yo-yo from One Drop and it is set apart by it's high quality craftsmanship, innovative design, and great play. It features a unique hex nut assembly which has the axle threading into a 4mm steel hex nut instead of into the body of the yo-yo. Advantages to this are: 1. If you strip the hex nut (highly unlikely given that it is steel), you just replace it instead of having a dead yo-yo 2. It allows for perfect axle centering, never has to be tuned and creates a more stable and balanced yo-yo 3. It allows for a wide variety of mods (including the FHZ hubstack kit) 4. Easy to take apart and put back together with no parts "explosion" This is the first yo-yo on the market (that we know of) to be soda blasted and clear anodized which gives it a smooth and clean look as well as better grinds! Grinding is also improved by the "Projection Profile" which are the grooves on the inner surface. Pictures just don't do this finish justice! The overall profile is designed to have a heavy rim weight and be comfortable to hold. One Drop spent months in design and testing refining the profile and weight ratios."

Have more information on this product? Shoot us a message from the Contact page!

title: Project 2
content:
From One Drop:

The Project has been evolved to meet the modern standards and features that players have come to expect and the result is the Project 2. Our goal was to maintain the spirit of the original while adding the new refinements.

title: Prologue

Prologue is a bi-metal entry in MagicYoYo's "Hit" competition team line, pairing a 6061 aluminum body with 304 stainless steel rings for rim-weighted stability in horizontal and technical play.

title: Prometheus

History / About
Frank’s entry, a full-size mid-weight powerhouse.

Production Runs

Run #1 (April 2016) — 10 units, Red; D56.00mm / W42.00mm / 65.50g. Bearing: C. Finish: Soda Blast.

title: Prowler
content:
History / About
The Prowler is G2's 100% stainless steel monometal — a full-steel throw in the tradition of the earlier Slingshot (which used a steel body with aluminum rims). At ~155g the raw steel construction provides a uniquely dense, planted feel compared to aluminum. Available in Blackout Blasted and Raw Blasted finishes, both leveraging the natural stainless steel aesthetic. The raw blasted version shows the bare steel surface.

title: PS AUTOSCOPY
content:
History / About
PS AUTOSCOPY is a machined-plastic version of Hajime Miura's Autoscopy, released July 25, 2026, in POM and PC variants with heavier rims than the standard model.

title: Ptarmigan
content:
From Featherspin:

"Inspired by the willow ptarmigan, a bird that survives arctic hellscapes in full winter camo, yelling “AWEBO!” at its foes, ready to square up. Then poses all cute and lively, molding its feathers to party on for the summer.

This yo-yo packs that same chaotic energy: tough enough for the cold, fast enough for the storm, and loud enough to make gravity question its life choices. The Ptarmigan doesn’t just spin, it squawks, struts, and survives."

Colorways

Bird Berries - Purple with pink and silver splashFoliage - Green with yellow splashSummer Plumage - brown with bronze gold, and red splashDeadly Awebo - Blood covered silver.

title: Pulse
content: AboutThe Pulse debuted at the 2007 World Yo-Yo Contest and represented a step up from the Limelight: it added a ball-bearing axle for longer, smoother spins while retaining the light-up internals. Its LEDs shift through multiple color patterns correlated with spin speed, giving players a visual readout of their yo-yo's momentum. The 2018 redesign updated the profile, gap-adjusting washers, and friction sticker response while retaining the Size A bearing to keep the Pulse responsive for looping players.

title: Pun
content: About the PunReleased June 25, 2015, the Pun is Jeremy McKay's ("Mr. Yoyothrower") signature throw for King Yo Star. Named after his fondness for wordplay, it was designed to perform across skill levels — from learners to competition players. Described as "rock stable" with excellent spin retention. McKay filmed over 150 trick tutorials, often featuring this model.

title: Punk
content: AboutJeff Anderson's signature throw designed for 5A freehand and matador tricks. A wide scalloped V-profile in dyeable Delrin with protruding spikes for matador play. Inspired by early 2000s yoyo mod culture and punk rock aesthetics. Includes a spiked counterweight (7.5g, 30mm × 21.8mm). The dyeable Delrin construction encouraged personalization.

title: Pure
content: AboutThe Pure is a machined polycarbonate yo-yo with a frosted look. The center hub is designed for fingerspin tricks. Available in Purple, Pink, Blue, and Pink/Blue.

title: Pure 2
content: AboutThe Pure 2 is a sequel to the original Pure with a wider, more angular profile and beefier rims for power and stability. Features a unique centering cup for fingerspins. Described as "high speed polycarbonate fun." Available in Clear/Silver Hub, Green/Gold Hub, Glitter Pink/Blue Hub, Glitter Pink/Silver Hub, Glitter Black/Gold Hub, and Glitter Black/Black Hub.

title: Pure (Injection Molded)
content: AboutThe injection-molded Pure is AceYo's budget recreation of the machined Pure at an exceptional cost-to-performance ratio. Features a deep rounded bowl for fingerspins, good for DNA trick training. Available in Glitter Blue/Silver Hub, Glitter Yellow/Black Hub, Glitter Gold/Black Hub, Solid Light Purple, Solid Aqua, Solid Pink, and Solid Light Green.

title: Purple Line
content:
About
Purple Line is a MAGICYOYO x iYOYO collaboration model: a big, wide, well-balanced butterfly shape with a polka-dot splash finish.

title: PYBIT
content:
From ILYY:

"If we had to point at the weirdest yoyo we made to date, it would undoubtedly be the PYBIT. Its super bulky can-like shape made it stand out of the organic shapes or standard V-profile swamp of its time.

With it being so extreme and experimental, we only made a handful of these specimens. They became highly sought after by collectors. Voices pleading for a re-run became louder and louder over the years.

Right from the beginning we knew, it cannot simply be a re-run of the exact same design. We wanted something even more unusual than the original design. Keeping the maxim dialed to ‘bonkers’, we thought:

“Why not make a bimetal version, but without adding a second metal?”– “That does not make any sense!”“Perfect!”

Out came the Mango PYBIT!

The new PYBIT for 2021 features a bi-7068 aluminum construction with a slick black body and fruity mango gloss rings for extra mojo. In addition, we widened the catch zone to allow for easier play. For the first time, PYBIT 2021 now features the beloved ILYY-dimple horn."

title: Pynk
content: Pynk is the signature model of Kahli Evans, three-time Australian 1A Champion (2007–2009). Machined from A7068 aluminum — a higher-grade alloy than 7075 — the 59.93mm × 43.76mm step-round profile favors slow, deliberate, extended combo play. Available in rim-engraved and center-engraved variants. Retail $89.99 USD.

title: Pyro III
content: The Pyro III is the third iteration of HSpin's iconic Pyro series and one of the most sought-after collector pieces in the lineup. At 52mm diameter it is radically undersized compared to the original 55mm Pyro. It was the first Pyro to use flowable silicone response and the first to adopt the L-size bearing (ILYY/OXY5 specification) used in the Phoenix. Only 149 units were produced. Considered a highly collectible piece that showcases HSpin's willingness to radically reimagine a beloved model. Price: $135.99 USD.

meta.yya_response: Flowable silicone (first HSpin with this response system)

title: Pyro Light
content: The Pyro Light was HSpin's direct response to community feedback that the original Pyro's 45.5mm width and 71.7g weight were excessive for competition play. HSpin trimmed approximately 6mm from the width and 9.6g from the weight while retaining the flame laser engraving on the profile and matte anodized finish. The result was faster and more maneuverable than the original while preserving its visual identity. Still uses the HSpin D-size bearing system.

title: Pyro OG
content: About the Pyro OGThe Pyro OG is a collaboration between At Design Lab and HSpin (Switzerland), released April 17–18, 2026 — Japanese National YoYo Day — to mark the 20th anniversary of the original HSpin Pyro. The original Pyro, designed by Chris K. and released in December 2005, is widely credited as one of the yo-yos that proved full-metal designs could compete at the highest level, changing the trajectory of competition yo-yo design. At Design Lab initiated the project and produced the re-issue "to the exact original drawings designed by Chris.K in 2005."The only change from the original is the response system: the original pads are no longer manufactured, so updated ring pads (OD 18mm × ID 13mm) are used. Two axle lengths are provided (M3 × 18mm and 16mm) to replicate both the original narrow gap (slim bearing) and a slightly wider modern gap (standard bearing). Vintage Coating finish across all colorways, all named "Original Color" as a deliberate homage. HSpin is not currently in The Yoyo Archive. $120 USD.

title: Pyro X
content: The Pyro X is a modernized reinterpretation of HSpin's iconic Pyro, produced by iYoYo under license from HSpin. Designed in collaboration with Hadrien Bennaceur — a long-time HSpin team member who also worked on the Antipodes. The wide 45.75mm profile and flame-inspired aesthetic are retained from the original Pyro, but the construction uses 7075 aluminum, a modern C-size center track bearing, and contemporary slim pad response. "Feels like Pyro, but plays like 2020." A REWIND-exclusive Blue/Light Blue colorway was produced alongside Blue/Green, Black/Blue, and Blue/Orange variants. At $59.99 it was far more accessible than the original.

title: Qi
content:
From ZGRT:

"(pronounced "chee").

Qi is energy in the very broadest sense possible.

Qi is universal.

Qi embraces all manifestations of energy, from the most material aspects of energy to the most immaterial aspects.

Qi needs to have a balance in order to maintain good flow. If there is an imbalance of qi, energy cannot flow properly.

We started our journey with a remarkable H-shape yoyo because of the amazing properties and performance capabilities this shape can bring when in motion. This time, we wanted to bring another H-shape yoyo into our portfolio with a different style and design.

The Qi contains the typical characteristics of an H-shape yoyo where weight is pushed to the sides and comfortability comes very natural to the hand. For such reasons, we just wanted to enhance such characteristics and have a good weight (energy) distribution.

Let’s begin with the size of the diameter. The Qi could be ambiguously considered either a regular sized or an undersized throw depending on how the players considers it. For us, the Qi is in the maximum limits of what is considered an undersized throw in terms of size, but not in terms of performance.

The Qi plays very powerfully and nimble by properly utilizing the 62 gr. body weight along the thick rims that drive great performance. The centre of gravity of this throw is closer to the rims than the rest of the monometal throws we have designed.

Such factor allows the Qi to compensate the performance factor that a yoyo with a bigger diameter could provide. In a side-by-side comparisson with our Winglet, the Qi is 3 mm smaller in diameter, 2 mm wider and ~3 gr less in weight. The H-shape, altough is more conservative than the Winglet as it can be observed, it has been stylized with several subtle cuts that adds great personality to this throw. The catch zone of the Qi is wide enough to land tricks very easily.

The way the Qi has been machined is absolutely gorgeous. It has a very nice finish and smoothness that your hand will be happy to experience. The cup also has some cuts to aesthetically match the design of the rest of throw. It is also noticeable how we minimized the centre weight and left certain room for finger spinning. Thumb grinding will definitely not be an issue.

The engine and responsive system the Qi comes with are a concave C bearing and pads exclusively formulated for us in order to have a great spinning time and a nice grip. The Qi comes with Alpha line - ZipLine string.

We made this project with the intention to have a performer, handsome and comfortable throw that makes the energy to flow harmoniously.

Wish you a nice Qi entry flow and let nothing hold you down."

title: Quadfour
content:
About
Quadfour is a shrunk-down evolution of YYR's 2010 CLASHcube, keeping its perfectly square 44×44mm profile but swapping the CLASHcube's specialty D-bearing for a standard Size C bearing — trading some of the original's specialized feel for a more relaxed, stable ride. Marketed for tight technical tricks like chopsticks and protrusions.

title: Quail Egg
content:
History / About
The Quail Egg is a compact 3D-printed yo-yo from Pachyderm Yoyos. At 42.7mm in diameter and 66.3mm wide (16.5mm catch zone), it is wider than it is tall, weighing about 62.5g.
Sold directly through the maker's forum sale thread and Instagram, at $27 plus shipping.

title: Quake
content:
History / About
The Quake marked a turning point in G2's design philosophy — the first model explicitly designed to be midsized and fast, responding to community feedback that most new releases were full or oversized. Jacob Gross described it as "the best yoyo I have ever thrown for horizontal." It was also the first G2 to ship with response pads (G-Grips) instead of flowable silicone. Two bearings are included: the BOSS Rage (grooved) and BOSS Wrath (flat), giving players a choice of response feel. The AL7 variant runs approximately 2 grams heavier. The Quake became one of the most beloved G2 designs and later spawned the Aftershock (full-size Quake) as a direct evolution.
