title: QUALIA
content:
About
QUALIA is a 7075 aluminum release from SPUTNIK. No further colorway or story details have been published by the brand as of this writing — specs below are confirmed via SPUTNIK's own forum announcement.

title: Quark
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Get the files here: The Quark, a Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is The Quark, sequel to The Ork and The Dork. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/41RypW. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. If you want it to work well slice it to 54-60 grams weight. 

If you print it and it doesn't come back up add a drop of lube or rub some chapstick on the end of your string and after a couple throws it will work just right. 

Credit to Chris from the Noun Project for the DS9 diagram.  https://thenounproject.com/icon/deep-space-nine-574903/"

title: Queen Bee
content:
From Rifogiate Design:

"I played with yoyos a lot in elementary school and up through junior high until I just kinda…stopped. Over the last several months, however, I’ve uncovered my old collection and rediscovered my love for the hobby. Some of the more modern design philosophies really show a love for the craft and a grasp of physics that truly impresses me as a machinist. That said, my experience is firmly rooted in that earlier era of play and my designs reflect it.

I took a lot of inspiration for this piece from the exterior design from my favorite yoyo, my trusty old Turbo Bumblebee GT, and as such I’ve taken to calling it the “Queen Bee.” It’s a touch heavier than the original, but comes with a much longer spin time to match. I’m not a particularly advanced player by modern standards, to be perfectly honest, but I’ve been putting it through its paces as simple 0A retro yoyo and really enjoying myself. I’ve recently been able to put it into the much more talented hands of more “modern” players, and it turns out that it also plays very well on the string in a way I didn’t think was possible."

title: Quest
content: About the QuestThe Quest is the signature yo-yo of Takeshi Matsuura, the 2012 5A World Champion, featuring a POM Delrin body with a brass midship weight ring for a gentler impact feel during freehand play while maintaining extended spin time. An included lateral cap indicates its 5A design pedigree. The H-profile shape provides the stability needed for Matsuura's complex freehand routines.

title: Square Apart T-Shirt (Black)

title: R1
content:
History / About
The R1 is Roll Out's groundbreaking debut model, produced in an extremely limited run of just 100 units worldwide. This exclusive Italian design represents one of the most limited yo-yo releases in the hobby's history.
Featuring original, extravagant design with high-end aluminum construction, the R1 is highly sought after by collectors for its rarity and design innovation.

title: R2009
content:
History / About
The R2009 (v2) is the second production run of Roll Out's flagship model, building on the original R1 design. This iteration refined the specifications slightly and introduced multiple finish options.
Available in two distinct finishes—shiny blue and black matte—the R2009 brought the exclusive Italian design to a slightly wider collector base while maintaining the brand's commitment to quality and limited production.

title: R2009 Team Edition
content:
History / About
The R2009 Team Edition is a premium variant of the R2009, offering enhanced customization and a distinctive sandblasted finish for collectors and team riders.
This edition featured custom silicone response options and came packaged in either a premium box or plastic case, distinguishing it as a special release within Roll Out's limited production philosophy.

title: R2010
content:
History / About
The R2010 (v3) represents Roll Out's final evolution of their core platform, introducing technical refinements and a striking visual identity through purple anodization and laser-engraved graphics.
This generation featured a reduced gap width and upgraded to a stainless steel ABEC 7 flat bearing, combining improved performance with the brand's signature aesthetic. The purple finish with intricate engraving made it the most visually distinctive model in the R-series lineup.

Per the YoYoExpert new-company announcement (Feb 2021) it ships with a custom brass 'major deduction' coin.

title: Euclase
content: History / AboutThe Euclase was originally released in 2019 and, per YoYoExpert, was so popular it sold out on the first day of its initial China release. It is the basis for the Frosted Euclase, Euclase AL and the Riesenwellen Sailfish.

title: Euclase AL
content: History / AboutEuclase AL is a full 6061 aluminum version of R2FG's popular Euclase, keeping the profile of the original bi-metal with a modified weight distribution. YoYoExpert notes an extreme weight distribution with thick rims. Introduced at YoYoExpert in June 2022.

title: Frosted Euclase
content: History / AboutThe Euclase was released in 2019 and, per YoYoExpert, sold out on its first day in its initial China release. Frosted Euclase is a full-plastic version in machined polycarbonate with a metal finger-spin hub and a matte finish, with a wide competitive profile and thick rims. Introduced at YoYoExpert in July 2021.

title: Garnet
content: History / AboutYoYoExpert states that Garnet Neon was the second round of the Garnet after huge demand for the original release. The original is a wide hybrid with a lightweight machined plastic body and broad stainless-steel rings.

title: Garnet Neon

Colors, inspired by neon city lights, were hand-dyed, and a pair of caps is included as a nod to classic plastic/metal yo-yos. Introduced at YoYoExpert in July 2021.

title: Halberd
content: History / AboutHalberd is a budget metal yo-yo from R2FG introduced at YoYoExpert in February 2021. The company was described as founded in 2017 by a designer who was an early member of Yoyofficer.

title: Ion Cannon
content: History / AboutIon Cannon is a 2A looping yo-yo from R2FG, a yo-yo maker founded in 2017 in Shenzhen, China (the name stands for 'Rotation To Fight Gravity', per YoYoExpert). It was released at YoYoExpert in February 2021 as one of the brand's first products there. YoYoExpert notes the shape is suited to loops and shoot-the-moons, and responsiveness can be tuned with thick bearing lube.

title: Radius 7068
content: History / AboutA stronger-alloy retail revision of Shion Araya's competition Radius.

title: Radius Nexus
content: Shion Araya's second C3 signature, carrying the torch from the original Radius. Switched to 6061 aluminum from 7075, with a sharper straight shape, 1mm larger diameter, and 1g heavier. Araya won the 2016 and 2017 World Yo-Yo Contests with this model. Price: ~$50–$65.

title: Radius Ti
content: History / AboutPremium titanium reinterpretation of Shion Araya's world-championship Radius platform, tuned for spin, durability, and fast combo control.

title: Raijin
content:
From Rewind:

"This is a 7075 aluminum monometal model, featuring the largest catch zone among Sengoku's models (as of this yo-yo's release).

The active width, maximized within the total body width, is ideal for tricks requiring large movements and simple mounts. Despite its sharp appearance, it allows for light and floaty yo-yo play.

It's perfect for one-hand string tricks, and the manufacturer also recommends it for counterweight play."

title: Railgun
content: History / AboutDistinct base model with Shibuya and contest editions documented separately.

title: Flat Earth
content:
History / About
The Flat Earth is a responsive yo-yo released by Rain City Skills (Vancouver, BC) as part of founder Jeremy McKay's ongoing exploration of skill-oriented designs alongside the brand's performance lineup. Released circa 2024 before the company's closure in early 2025, it was designed to encourage fundamental responsive play and looping practice — a nod to the throwback sensibility that defined many of Rain City's specialty releases. Limited quantities were sold through the Rain City Skills online store.

title: Loonie
content: AboutNamed after the Canadian loonie ($1 coin), the Loonie is Rain City's brass micro throw and one of the brand's most consistent sellers. It evolved across multiple editions: the first edition was narrower and less stable; the second widened the catch zone considerably; the third (January 2024) dialed in a balance of width and weight. Features a LEGO-compatible hub. Packaged in a coin purse with a chocolate coin included.Edition 1: 32mm dia / 26mm width / 65.4g. Edition 2: 31.8mm dia / 33.2mm width / 64.1g. Edition 3 (2024): 33.2mm dia / 27.1mm width / 54.8g.

title: Ouroboros
content: AboutLuna Harran's signature model, co-designed with Jordan Blofeld. Wide enough for comfortable 5A freehand catches but nimble enough for 1A string tricks. Named for the ouroboros — the self-eating snake — reflecting the loop of yoyo play. Includes a LEGO snake, keychain, stickers, and pogs. "Sorry grades" (cosmetically blemished) also sold at discount. Price: $69.99.

title: Rebrand
content: AboutRain City's entry-level beginner throw, built on a licensed Magic Yoyo One Third mold. Unusually transparent about the licensing: Jeremy openly credited the source rather than creating original tooling. Wing-shaped, tug-responsive out of the box with the included slim bearing; upgradeable to a full C bearing for unresponsive play. Includes team pogs.

title: SETI
content: AboutThe SETI is Rain City's oversized throw inspired by a satellite dish. Despite its imposing 67.8mm diameter, it plays better than expected. A bell-like resonance in E♭ was discovered during testing and became a selling point. Three engraved themes: Melody to the Stars, Bovine Abductions, and Mars Attacks. LEGO-compatible hub. Includes an alien minifigure.

title: The Gamer
content: AboutIntended as a small catalog entry, the Gamer became Rain City's most iterated flagship. A slimline aluminum design made in partnership with Eternal Throw, it includes both a slim bearing for responsive play and a full Size C bearing for unresponsive. Over its production life it went through three runs of the original aluminum design and spawned the Delrin Gamer and Gamer AL Light variants. Available in over 13 colorways including video-game themes (Samus, Pokémon, Mega Man).

title: Rainbow Pro Model
content: HistoryThe Rainbow Pro Model was manufactured in Sweden by Elfverson from 1958–1964, marked "Made in Sweden" on the box. Part of Cheerio's later outsourced production after Duncan acquisition. Premium wooden construction with multi-color finishes.

title: Rainbowl 303
content:
The following was archived from RSO's website:

Rainbowl 303 is a special edition of the Bowl 303 yo-yo, based on the same CAD. Revered by enthusiasts of the Bowl series for its remarkable heft and density, the 303 has the most predictable movement signature.

Only 35 Rainbowl 303s were made, each an exceptional masterpiece. The electroplating process has resulted in only a select few with an opulent blue hue in the hub, while the remaining ones have a resplendent light green tone. Like the raw batch, the Rainbowl 303s are polished to a gorgeous mirror finish.

title: Rainier
content:
From One Drop:

"The Rainier is the biggest mountain in the Cascade range. 

This yo-yo started as a simple idea: What if we took a Cascade, scaled it up, and shifted all the weight to the rims? We used that as the starting point and then refined the design to end up with what could be argued as our best performing yo-yo to date.

More specifically we scaled up the diameter to 56.4mm and the width scaled up to 48.4mm in keeping the same proportions as the Cascade. The Cascade has a ring of weight down in the cup. We got rid of that and thinned out the profile as much as possible and put all the weight out at the rims. 

In play, it gives you a feeling of confidence because it feels so stable and spins for a long time. However, when you want to speed up or change direction, it feels really nimble. Team member, Lukáš, from Hungary, is going to be using the Rainier as his primary competition yo-yo."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Rainier – Boosted
content:
From One Drop:

"The Rainier started with the idea of scaling up a Cascade and shifting the weight out to the rim and turned into a performance monster. It was one of our first “Dark Side” yo-yos and among our best performing models. It seemed natural to make a Boosted version.

“Boosting” is making a 6061 alloy yo-yo out of 7075 alloy, but changing the design so that the overall weight ends up being lower, even though 7075 is a heavier alloy than 6061. It takes a lot of tweaking to the design to make this happen, but we like to do it in a way that yo-yo looks the same and has the same or similar specs (except for the weight). Given that 7075 is a heavier alloy, if we took the same design of a 6061 yo-yo and produced it in 7075, it would end up about 2.5 grams heavier. We have done this in the past and called it “GZR Edition”. Turns out to be not as interesting as Boosted because the weight distribution is the same so it plays very similarly. Changing the weight distribution is how to make the feel in play change which is why we do Boosted and not GZR when we make a 7075 version of a 6061 model.

The Rainier is optimized for rim weight at essentially the limits of 6061 alloy. We have a hard limit on what we consider the thinnest we can make the body. We can safely go thinner with 7075 alloy which is what we did: thinned out the body and added rim weight while maintaining the same profile shape. The result is a yoyo with considerably more rim weight, but a total weight of about .5 grams less (or about 3 grams less than if we just ran the same design in 7275 - see above). The Boosted Rainier is further into the Dark Side than the original. It’s even more of an extreme design."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Rally
content:
From One Drop:

"Three years in the making: One Drop presents the Rally - a premium performance plastic yoyo made in the U.S.A.

We set out to match the nostalgic feel of plastic with the performance of modern metal while maintaining our high quality standards and "made in the USA" ethos. The result is a wing shaped design based on the CODE 2 featuring a marbleized catch zone for superior grinds. The machined and anodized aluminum rings complete the weight distribution for long spins and the type of performance players have come to expect."

title: RAMI
content:
About
RAMI is Mizuki Takimoto's signature model, positioned as a turning point toward lighter, more agile 3A play. Specs are intentionally downsized versus mainstream 3A yoyos for a lighter swing feel, aimed at improving control on power-transfer-dependent tricks. Widened edge geometry seats the middle finger securely for a confident grip while still throwing cleanly off-hand. Reuses the stainless inner-rim construction proven on YYR's Anomaly model for spin power and durability under 3A-style collisions.

title: Rapid Eagle
content: Launch-year Blazing Teens tie-in yo-yo, featuring a ball bearing with starburst response. Part of the first season of the live-action franchise that transformed yo-yoing across Asia.

title: Rapid
content: About the RapidReleased November 17, 2014, the Rapid was King Yo Star's first bi-metal yoyo, combining a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel weight rings. Designed by Jake Elliott, the 2013 US 5A National Champion, to meet his competition-level 5A standards. The stepped V-profile delivers fast, stable play with long spin times from the SS ring weight distribution. Marketed as "fast and stable" for both 1A and 5A.

title: Rapid Light
content: About the Rapid LightReleased May 20, 2015, the Rapid Light is an all-aluminum mono-metal companion to the bi-metal Rapid — reshaped (not a direct downgrade), with flat rims particularly suited to 5A catches. Lighter on the string than the original Rapid, it was described as a great all-around player at an accessible $55 price point. Promoted by Josh Yee.

title: Raptor
content: AboutThe Raptor marked a pivotal moment in Duncan's history when it was released in 2010 as part of the De-Luxxe series. It was the first Duncan yo-yo to use SG (Silicone Groove) Stickers — precision-machined silicone response that replaced the friction stickers and O-rings Duncan had used for decades — and it launched a new era of competitive-grade production from the brand. The Raptor's simple butterfly shape was a deliberate departure from complex profiles; its undersized 54 mm diameter and deep catch zone made it highly maneuverable. It includes removable side caps and a Candy Dice counterweight for 5A play. The Raptor showed the community that Duncan could produce a world-class unresponsive aluminum yo-yo at a mainstream retail price.

title: Raven Butterfly Cap Sticker
content:
About
Raven Butterfly Cap Sticker is a sticker from Throw-Yo Threads. Thermal-printed sticker sized for Butterfly caps. Types: Holo, White. Price: $1.50-$2.

title: Raven & Skull Sticker
content:
About
Raven & Skull Sticker is a sticker from Throw-Yo Threads. Die-cut matte raven and skull sticker. Price: $3. First a Patreon sticker (June 2026).

title: Raytracer
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"The name Raytracer is based on a computer graphics rendering technique which simulates the physics of light to produce images with precision and accuracy. To make raytacing work, it takes an immense amount of speed and power. This name perfectly fits this yo-yo, stable and fast, landing tricks with both precision and accuracy. Fully utilizing the 7068 material and stainless steel rims, they were able to put weight exactly where it was needed the utmost precision to achieve the best possible performance."

title: RBC
content:
The RBC is a modern responsive yo-yo collaboration between MK1 and Spinworthy Yoyos. It is an aluminum re-imagining of Spinworthy's wooden Blood Cell.

There were two releases. The original December 20th, 2021 release and a August 19th, 2022 release.

YoyoExpert Colorways

There were two exclusive RBC colorways sold by Yoyo Expert.

2nd Run Colorways

The 2nd run of the RBC was done in red, black, and clear. The black version was an official Unknown release that had hidden engravings on the yo-yo

title: RE AUTOSCOPY
content:
History / About
RE AUTOSCOPY is Hajime Miura's updated signature, released November 2, 2025, combining Autoscopy's inner-rim structure with the wide body of the already-archived Liminal Autoscopy.

title: RE:Devil
content:
History / About
The RE:Devil is GWAY Throws’ revisit of their debut model, the Daredevil. Upgrading the alloy from 7068 to 7075 and refining the dimensions, the RE:Devil aims to deliver the same energetic D-bearing character as the original with improved performance headroom. The Copper Sherbert colorway was released as a special edition.

title: Re:Master Galaxy
content: A five-years-later revisit of the original 2012 Master Galaxy, maintaining identical dimensions but with modernized weight distribution. Machined from 7075 aluminum (upgrade from the original's standard alloy) and blasted for a grind-friendly finish. Plays smooth and floaty with enough spin power for any routine; the wide stance delivers an enormous catch zone and extreme stability through complex off-plane tricks. Price: ~$75–$90.

title: RE:MOUNT
content:
About the RE:MOUNT

The RE:MOUNT is the second-generation revision of SPUTNИK’s debut model, the MOUNT. It carries forward the all-around 6061 aluminum monometal character of the original while expanding the profile — a slightly larger diameter (55.8mm vs. 55.2mm) and meaningfully wider gap (50mm vs. 46mm). Released in 2025, it bridges the gap between the casual-friendly MOUNT and the competition-oriented MESA7075.

title: Reagent (Prototype)
content:
About
Reagent was a monthly Project Torsion blend from Throw-Yo Threads, offered only to Patreon subscribers in June 2026. No public retail release has been confirmed.

title: Reaper
content:
History / About
The Reaper was released in 2022 as part of G2's modern era lineup. The design was revisited in 2026 as the Ti Reaper — a full titanium version priced at $325 — making the Reaper another G2 design to receive the premium titanium treatment alongside the Ti Triton and TiShee.

title: Rebellion Acro
content:
History / About
The Rebellion Acro is a 2015 release under YoyoRecreation's Rebellion sub-brand, with a shape based on the YoyoRecreation Acrophobia, scaled up.

title: Rebellion Golyat
content: AboutThe Rebellion Golyat was the debut model of yoyorecreation's Rebellion sub-brand, launched at Japan Nationals 2015. Rebellion was created to offer high-performance designs at more accessible price points through China-based manufacturing. The Golyat is an oversized organic step-round plastic made from polyacetal resin (Delrin/POM), providing a smooth, bounce-resistant catch surface. It debuted alongside several other Rebellion models (Acro, Butcher) at the same event.

title: Rebellion Lilliputian
content:
History / About
The Rebellion Lilliputian is an undersized-diameter yo-yo under YoyoRecreation's Rebellion sub-brand, debuted at the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest.

title: Rebellion Qilin
content:
History / About
The Rebellion Qilin is a 2015 release under YoyoRecreation's Rebellion sub-brand, positioned as a budget-friendly version of the already-archived Sleipnir.

title: Rebellion Start the Riot
content: AboutStart the Riot is Rebellion's first bi-metal model, released in February 2016 as the signature of Yusuke Otsuka. The design uses a 6061 aluminum body — a departure from YYR's main-line preference for 7075 — with a double inner stainless steel ring construction that embeds two ring sets rather than the single outer rim of the Draupnir. This inner ring geometry, similar to that used in models like the CLYW Chief and Avant Garde 2, produces a different spin character than outer-rim bi-metals. Priced at approximately $140 USD, it demonstrated that the Rebellion line could support competition-grade bi-metal construction at sub-main-line pricing.

title: Reboot
content:
From One Drop:

"Our first yo-yo, the Project, released in 2007. It was born in an exciting and experimental time in the yo-yo world and had some unique features like the replaceable axle system and “Projection Profile” grooves. Sixteen years later, thanks to all of you supporting us, we’re still here and still making yo-yos. It’s been quite the ride. 

The Project is a yo-yo we keep revisiting in various ways because it seems like we did something right on that first attempt. In 2008 there was the Markmont Project. A year later in 2009 the Project 2 was released. The next time was the Markmont Next in 2010. It was until 2015 when team member Ryosuke was due for a signature yo-yo and he wanted to modernize the Project. The Rebirth is bigger than the Project and has Side Effects. It became the definitive version of the Project for the last 8 years.

Ryosuke correctly suggested it was time again to do more. The Reboot is here. Looking at the catch zone, it looks identical to a Rebirth. However, there are significant changes: It is made out of 7075 aluminum alloy, is “Boosted” (a 7075 version of a yo-yo that weighs less even though 7075 alloy weighs more than 6061 alloy), and has new beautiful “Projection Profile” grooves in the cup.

The Reboot weighs 3 grams less than the Rebirth coming in at 63.4 grams with Ultra Lights."

title: Reborn
content: AboutThe Reborn is a premium bi-metal using 7068 aluminum for the body paired with stainless steel rims. One of AceYo's flagship alloy designs.

title: Reborn X
content: AboutThe Reborn X is a tri-material construction combining an aluminum body with stainless steel rims and polycarbonate inner rings. Combines the spin power of a bi-metal with the softness and ding protection of polycarbonate. Available in Matte Black/Silver Rim, Matte Black/Rainbow Rim, Matte Silver/Silver Rim, and Matte Silver/Rainbow Rim.

title: Firecracker (Size D)
content:
History / About
The Firecracker (Size D) adapts Recess's slimline aluminum design to a D-bearing configuration. It ships with two bearings: a rubber-shielded flat D bearing pre-installed for responsive play and a grooved unresponsive bearing for string tricks. The same 54mm diameter and 37.8mm slim profile as the C-bearing Firecracker, now with a Size D pad response system matching the wider gap. A versatile daily carry that bridges classic responsive feel and contemporary unresponsive play.

title: First Bass
content:
History / About
A collaboration with Recess yo-yos producing a Jake Bullock branded edition of their First Base responsive plastic model. At $25 it is the most accessible Jake Bullock item ever produced, making the brand reachable to beginners and entry-level players for the first time. The First Base is a well-regarded beginner responsive throw — pairing it with Jake's name is consistent with his long-standing interest in keeping yo-yos accessible; his entire brand launched at $45 when most comparable designs sold for much more. Part of Jake's willingness to engage the full spectrum of the hobby, from beginner collabs to $299 titanium editions.

title: Rectifier
content:
About the Rectifier
The Rectifier is a 7068 aluminum bimetal from Mr. Mazal Top's Yoyos, released in 2022 and reviewed in a YouTube unboxing published July 4, 2022. It continues the brand's focus on high-alloy aluminum bimetal construction at accessible prices, targeting competition-oriented 1A play. The Rectifier represents the brand's third bimetal design, building on the formula established by the Vindicator and Vindication.

title: Reflection
content:
From Edition:

"The Reflection is a personal examination into design traits which have made an impact on the yo-yo's which I pick up.

Design insight and inspiration:Rounded wide rims, inverted catch zone, and a center "button" style hub were all key design aspects I wanted to incorporate. A 47mm width draws inspiration from the SF movement, a key and influential yo-yo. While the 67g weight looks toward the heavier standard set by Japanese designs, paired with a conventional 56mm diameter we have all learned to love. All to say, these specs were not completely random. However unlike most modern throws that pack a ton of ring weight, and min max the weight distribution, I wanted to pull inspiration from some older Turning Point's such as the Anubis. This meant trying to strike a balance between the distribution of center weight and rim weight, opting for more center weight and less ring weight, allowing for the 6061 to help fill the gap of overall rim weight. What was achieved was a less fatiguing play that might be associated to a similar design with a higher "min, max" styled weight bias.

Initial Process:When you start a design you are met with a blank canvas. Originally this design was a bit of a crazy late night idea with titanium rings. After getting a quote for the prototyping cost the decision was made that it would be too expensive to continue as the first prototype made, as well as unfair to those who were offering to help order the run by purchasing the left overs. So a step back had to be taken and a small redesign had to happen, this time using SS rings but staying true to the original ring weight constraint as before.

Manufacturing:Manufacturing is taken care of by FPM. This is primarily because of the lower run count but I am happy to have them working on this project due to their high quality workmanship.

A note:This would not be possible without Alex Hattori who stepped in to assist with the CAD for this yoyo, as well as the 3 other folks who picked up one of the 3 remaining prototypes. Thank you David, Matt and Adrian."

title: Reflex Auto Return
content: AboutThe Reflex pioneered the centrifugal-clutch auto-return yo-yo category, using a spring-loaded clutch mechanism that grabs the string when the yo-yo slows down and snaps it back to the player's hand without any tug. Originally designed to give absolute beginners an immediate win, the Reflex has been continuously refined and re-molded; the current version features a lighter, wider shape and simplified internals. It remains one of the best-selling yo-yos in toy stores worldwide and serves as an entry point for children who might otherwise be frustrated by the skill barrier of a conventional yo-yo.

title: Refractory
content:
History / About
The Refractory is GWAY Throws’ seventh release — a bimetal combining a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims. The design prioritizes maneuverability through difficult string sequences while maintaining the spin endurance needed for extended technical combos. A Chunkeez counterweight option is available for players who want 5A capability.

title: Regulator
content:
History / About
The Regulator is GWAY Throws’ third release, developed over nearly a year in collaboration with Dressel Designs. The design evolved significantly through prototyping, moving from organic origins to its final form — a shape that balances distinctive aesthetics with playability. YoYoLab pads provide consistent response for clean binds.
Colorways included Brown, Fuchsia, Teal, Reaper Robe (Black/White Splash), Joker Toxin (Purple/Green Splash), and Rip City Rush (Red/Silver Splash).

title: Relentless
content: The Relentless is the 4A World Champion signature of Ryan Connolly. Built with a POM (Delrin) body and brass rims for maximum spin power in offstring play, the Relentless features a reinforced 16mm axle for durability under the demands of high-impact 4A competition. Also available with stainless steel rims at approximately 1g lighter. Among the most competition-ready offstring throws in the W1LD lineup.

title: Replicant
content: AboutThe Replicant is the signature throw of Matthew Wallsten, featuring an unusually wide 51mm body paired with hollow stainless steel ring construction to maximize rim weight efficiency. Described by Yoyofriends as one of their highest-performing competition bimetals, it is designed for ultimate competitive performance.

title: Rescue
content:
About
Rescue is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Respawn
content:
About
Respawn is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2019. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Respawn Lite
content:
About
Respawn Lite is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2021. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Respawn X
content:
History / About
The Respawn X was released in late 2024 with Halloween-themed colorways (Hulk Storm, Frankenstein's Monster) suggesting an October release window. The "X" designation may indicate a special or crossover version of a prior Respawn design. Full material specs were not publicly documented at time of research.

title: Reticle
content: The Reticle is a wide tri-material competition throw built on a 7075 aluminum base with POM rings at the center. At 58mm diameter and 55mm width, it is among the widest throws in the W1LD lineup, combining the wide platform of the Wilderness family with a tri-material construction for a distinctive play character.

title: Retro Rocket
content: AboutA 1950s rocket-inspired pocketable throw co-designed with 24K Whips' Daniel Kessler. The Retro Rocket notably replaced Rain City's signature LEGO hub with a fingerspin trainer cup. Three sci-fi colorways: Kessler Run (Star Wars), Redshirt (Star Trek), and DHD (Stargate). Development began early 2018.

title: Dirty Caramel
content:
About
Sequel to the Everyday Caramel! More Ultem yo-yos! These use the Freshly Dirty stem system for the guts. They come with C bearing stems but they will also fit the A and D bearing stems if you acquire some. They come with a half spec C for responsive play, a greased and sealed C for semi responsive, and a grooved dry C for unresponsive play. They come with Hollywood Yo-Yo 40a pads which are great for responsive but might need broken in a little for unresponsive. Comes with swag including a Double Peach Ultem counterweight set, stickers, and custom Throw Yo string.
Colorways: Purple, Green, Orange, Blue. Engraving options: None, Mosquito (hubs only), Full Jeff (hidden Jeff under bearing seat plus mosquito). Price at retail: $77.00.

title: Everyday Caramel
content:
History / About

The Everyday Caramel is a "semi-production" model from Return Bottoms (also operating as Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop) made entirely from Ultem. Swiss-lathe machining differentiates the production units from earlier prototypes. Early runs experienced manufacturing issues and were sold at "trash grade" discounts, being incredibly fragile. The final Everyday Caramel still had some fragility issues with the axle and was never sold as an official production run. Instead, they were packaged in with the Demon's Fun as a freebie.

title: Returner
content:
History / About
Turner Return Tops was founded in 2022 by Bruce Turner in Florida, with a focus on fun, accessible yoyos for the community.
The Returner is tug responsive steez! Feel this fresh jam, a new jive, light and agile. Regen into a flip-flop bebop — fun is just a quick tug away. This return top is tug responsive, meaning there is no need to perform a bind trick to make it return: simply give it a tug while it's spinning. Each Returner includes a Zipline Strings Polyesque string, Turner sticker, and Turner Series #5 Pog, packaged in a custom sponge-lined papercraft Turner Tube.

title: Rev
content:
From One Drop:

"We are blessed to have a unique experience behind the scenes in designing and building a new yo-yo model.  This is a process of REVisions. We usually build the first version of a new model and then begin testing it and each of us ends up with an opinion.  We consider all the ideas, and then typically build one or more revisions and repeat the process until we find “the one”.

It’s really interesting to be able to feel how even relatively small changes can affect how a yo-yo feels and plays.   The word “opinion” above was chosen intentionally because so much of the evaluation is subjective. Obviously if a design has a huge obvious flaw (pulse vibe, doesn’t spin very long, etc) then it objectively needs to be changed and in a specific way.  But typically we don’t have those issues because we have sufficient experience to avoid the big problems.  

The point is that it usually comes down to personal taste.  We end up choosing one of the revs even though all of them are good yo-yos and could be the one released.  If you visit our factory, The Machinist has a special drawer with some of these un-released versions of yo-yos that you could try.

For the Rev, we want to give you this experience.   Over time we will release different revisions of the Rev starting with “Rev 1”.  Each release will be limited to 300 units and will not be made again. We plan on having the CAD cross-sections on the box art.   For the first one, there will be one cross-section. For the second one, there will be two overlapping cross-sections so that you can compare the difference in the design and then compare the difference in play.  

After the first Rev is released, we will then listen to you feedback informally (no votes, surveys or anything official - just message us your thoughts), come up with a new version and that will be Rev 2.  And so on, as long as you all are interested.

The design itself is based on a Top Deck so you’ll notice it has a similar profile shape, but don’t be fooled, the weight distribution and cup are changed radically and it plays like a totally different beast.  If you happen to have a Top Deck, you can get the comparison party started early when you have the first Rev. Like the Top Deck, it’s made of 7075 alloy.

For the first Rev, you’ll notice a single groove in the cup.  This is there to make it clear which version it is. We’ll do something similar on subsequent versions."

title: Rev-1 Dif-Fly
content:
History
In 2022, marking the 20th anniversary of the Dif-Fly's debut, Frank Difeo released the Rev-1 Dif-Fly as an upgraded reimagining of the model that launched Dif-e-Yo as a player brand. The Rev-1 retained the slimline butterfly character of the original while incorporating two decades of refinement in specs, materials, and response. One of Frank's final standard releases before the Dif-Con 1.

title: Rev-1 Over Haul
content:
History
The Rev-1 Over Haul was a complete remake of the 2003 Wide Load concept, built for the 2010 market with updated specs and a dramatically expanded weight customization system. The package included six weighted O-rings: four large (1.6g each) and two small (1.5g each), distributed across three grooves per side — inner, middle, and outer. Players could configure any combination across these positions, fundamentally altering weight distribution and feel in ways no other Dif-e-Yo allowed.
At minimum ring configuration the weight dropped to approximately 64g; at maximum it reached 73g. Priced at $104.99.

title: Rev 2
content:
From One Drop:

"The Rev 2 brings out the first set of tweaks to the Rev as we explore how small changes to a design affect the look and the play.

The first change is to the transition in the catch zone.  In the cross-section art on the box the white line is the Rev 2 and the black line is the Rev 1.   You can see we added material there which has the effect of making the transition more severe and sharp.  Changes to the catch zone (or sometimes called the “profile”) have the biggest impact on how a yo-yo looks.  And you can see this change makes the yo-yo appear much less organic and rounded and much of a wing shape.

The second change is to the cup side.  On the cup side the changes are less visible to the eye, but end up having impact on weight and weight distribution.  In fact, when designing and tweaking yo-yos we commonly use this area to control the final weight.  You can see in the cross section we removed some of the cup and the result is almost two grams of weight loss compared to the Rev 1.  This change will have the most impact on how the yo-yo feels in play. Side note:  we forgot to update the weight on the box art so it shows the Rev 1 weight (65.8 grams), instead of the Rev 1 weight (64.1 grams).  Oops :)

We still used 7075 aluminum alloy and the other specs remain the same.  On future Revs we might look into using a different alloy or changing the specs to a much bigger degree.  We received a ton of excellent suggestions from Rev 1 owners and are excited to continue this project into the future and encourage you to submit your feedback after trying the Rev 2."

title: Revival
content: About the RevivalThe Revival is Grant Johnson's second YoYoJam signature model, combining a POM smooth plastic body with a Synthesis-inspired aluminum metal frame structure. The H-profile design and 56.38mm diameter position it as a versatile competition yo-yo, and the smooth POM body enables comfortable grind tricks. A 2014 WYYC edition was produced.

title: Revolution
content: About the RevolutionThe Revolution is Grant Johnson's signature yo-yo, engineered around a dual-bearing setup that lets players swap between a thin responsive bearing and a Speed Bearing for bind-response play without any additional tools. Its straight body with aluminum rim delivers consistent spin, and the model was produced in championship editions for 2010 Worlds and Nationals.

title: Revolve
content: History / AboutHenson Chan signature looping yo-yo using an internal 5 g 6061 ring to tune rotational behavior.

title: Revora 6061 (Anodized)
content:
History / About
The Revora design in 6061 aircraft-grade aluminum with an anodized finish. Brings the 2025 flagship geometry to a more accessible price point. Currently available at $90 on luftverk.com.

title: Revora 6061 (Raw)
content:
History / About
The Revora design in 6061 aircraft-grade aluminum with a raw, unfinished surface. Brings the 2025 flagship geometry to an accessible price point while showcasing the natural aluminum finish. Currently available at $90 on luftverk.com.

title: Revora (Titanium)
content:
History / About
Luftverk’s 2025 titanium flagship. The name “Revora” is a reimagining of “Evora” — based on the ethos of the 2015 original but completely redesigned for modern performance. The defining feature is a double “nested cup” design with a reverse rake rim just before the hub, producing an aggressive and visually distinctive profile unlike anything in the previous lineup. The classic Luftverk engineering logo on the inner cup combines a vintage feel with the modern aggressive geometry. Available in Raw and Soda Blasted finishes.

title: REX
content: About the REXThe REX is MagicYoYo's ultimate performance flagship. Its body is machined from titanium with walls as thin as 0.5–0.7mm; each half requires over 45 minutes of CNC processing — approximately 15 times longer than a standard aluminum piece. High-density stainless steel rims account for over 55% of the total weight, enabling exceptional spin stability and speed. The aesthetic is inspired by Bauhaus design principles: functional simplicity expressed with visual precision. Designed collaboratively with Yixing Tan. Priced at $469 USD, the REX is MagicYoYo's most expensive production release. Competition-grade by any standard.

title: Rextreme
content: About the RextremeThe Rextreme is the signature model of 2008 4A World Champion Rei Iwakura, inspired by the Big Yo but incorporating midship weight rings and the Solid Spin Axle system. Its polycarbonate/ABS construction with aluminum rim provides bounce recovery while the configurable gap allows fine-tuning for different trick styles. Championship editions were produced for 2011 and 2012 World YoYo Contests.

title: Rextreme 2.0
content: About the Rextreme 2.0The Rextreme 2.0 expands marginally on the original with a larger diameter and width to refine weight distribution for Rei Iwakura's evolving 4A style. Removable suction-cup side caps allow conversion for top-on style spinning tricks. Multiple championship editions and colorways were produced, including World Champion and Supreme Edition variants.

title: Rextreme R
content: Rei Iwakura's signature competition 4A throw with bi-metal construction, combining offstring demands with the stability and spin power of bi-metal design. Price: $114.99.

title: Freyja
content: History / AboutPer the maker (posted on YoYoExpert, Feb 2021), Freyja is the third yoyo from Reykjavik Return Tops, inspired by the Norse goddess. It is an H-shaped 7068 yoyo with organic elements and engravings of a Nordic compass and Freyja's two cats, with an UNKWN variant. Runs were under 30 pieces per colorway. Palli first introduced it in April 2020. Rewind cites a total weight of about 64 g.

title: Mjolnir
content: History / AboutPer the maker (posted on YoYoExpert, July 2020), Mjolnir is the second release from Reykjavik Return Tops and its first bimetal, named after Thor's hammer. It is a heavy bimetal with stainless steel rims and a slightly larger diameter. A 2023 final run was described as mostly the same with slightly increased durability, a redesigned face and about half a gram lighter; that run was the last stock after owner Palli announced in May 2023 the shop would close. The Japanese retailer Rewind lists the body as A7068.

title: Ragnarok
content: History / AboutReykjavik Return Tops is a solo project of Pall Valdimar (Palli), a community member since 2005 and head organizer of the 2017 World Yo-Yo Contest in Iceland. Per the maker (posted on YoYoExpert, Oct 2019), the first release is a 7075 monometal named Ragnarok after the Norse battle that ends the world. It is competition focused with a wide shape and good rim weight. The first run was limited to 99 pieces, 33 each of Blood Red, Sky Blue and Sand.

title: Rhino
content:
From ZGRT:

"One of the metals that we were missing was Titanium and, as previous projects, we wanted to bring something unique in terms of shape and design. 

We chose an H shape for our first titanium yoyo, but we worked very diligently to have a stylized r-H-ino shape. The H shape is known to be powerful and to bring incredible stability into a yoyo. That was a key element to use with titanium because with Ti walls can be thinner than walls using other alloys and weight can be easily pushed to the rims.

The weight distribution of this throw is phenomenal which is a sign of using Titanium properly. When it comes to playability, the Rhino gives enough spin time and stability to perform complicated and technical tricks which were part of the the desired and expected outcomes as we moved almost half of its weight towards the rims. The Rhino also plays very nimble for an H shape yoyo and one of the reasons of that is due to the 64g weight.

This year we have been playing around and enjoying D bearings so much. I can say this is our D-bearing year and what a way to release a Titanium throw using this type of bearing. To my knowledge this might be the second D-bearing Ti throw so far. One of the things we like about D bearings is the capability to bind the yoyo at lower RPM. This feature is very cool as it gives you a little bit of extra time to finish your routine or trick even though the yoyo is at its final spinning time. The dimensions of the pads are exclusively for D-bearing size. They have the same outer diameter as a regular C-bearing size pad, but the inner diameter is 1 mm smaller. This response system assures great bindings in conjunction with the D bearing.

The stylized design of The Rhino was a challenging task to get accomplished. One one hand, we were looking to incorporate as much details as possible to give this throw a rhino personality. This was not an easy task to do. We worked with several manufacturers and the details we wanted on this throw were very challenging for them to machine in Titanium due to the rigidness of this metal. Some manufacturers just could not do it. But we did not give up, we kept trying until we were able to make this happen.

For the finish, we wanted to go just raw to enhance the rhino personality this throw already has.

This project took us several months to design, to prototype, to test and to fine tuning all the details. "

title: Rhinoplasty
content: The Rhinoplasty was an evolution of the original Minute, retaining the unusual A-size bearing but refining the profile with shaved, rounded rims for better hand feel and easier catches. At 50mm diameter it remained firmly in undersized territory. The Blueprint Rhino Pad was developed specifically for this model's response needs.

title: arc
content: AboutThe arc is RiHara's debut model, initially released under the brand's original name, 7yoyodesign. The company rebranded to RiHara after the first arc units shipped. Featuring Zhang Wenlin's signature curves-based, minimalist profile, the arc established the design language that would carry through the brand's entire catalog. Early units with a green logo and silver blasted finish are among the most sought-after pieces in the modern Chinese yo-yo collector community. TopYo later produced a remake of the arc. Full specifications are not publicly documented in surviving sources.

title: arc AIR
content: AboutThe arc AIR is the flagship of RiHara's Light sub-brand, designed to bring Zhang Wenlin's design philosophy to a wider audience at $48.99. A 6061 aluminum monometal with an inverse step round profile, the arc AIR evolved the original arc's V-influenced shape into one featuring "more straight lines" for improved high-speed stability. The attention to detail and quality of construction is maintained from RiHara's top-end work. Distributed exclusively in the West through Rewind. Colorways: Splash Silver/Blue, Splash Silver/Grey, Red.

title: arc AIR 7075
content: AboutThe arc AIR 7075 is the premium material variant of the arc AIR, machined from 7075 aluminum (超々ジュラルミン) and finished with a matte coating. Dimensions are nearly identical to the 6061 version, but the higher-density alloy produces a noticeably harder, more robust feel in the hand and on the string. "Better material and premium quality." Priced at $88.99 through Rewind. Part of the RiHara Light line. Colorway: Black.

title: Black Bird
content: AboutThe Black Bird is a collaboration between TopYo and RiHara designer Zhang Wenlin, bringing RiHara's design aesthetic to an accessible $32 price point. Machined from 7003 aluminum with thick rims and a soft grid finish, the Black Bird is described as "subtle but elegant" — quick on string tricks and exceptionally stable as a daily throw. Available in Blue, Pink, Silver, and Black colorways.

title: ino
content: AboutThe ino is RiHara's flagship and most ambitious model — the brand's first bimetal, conceived in November 2015 and released in 2016 as the centerpiece of the Major Line at $189.99. A 6061 aluminum body paired with a stainless steel rim that wraps from the inner wall all the way to the outer edge, creating a thin inner sheath with a unique weight distribution profile. The construction produces a throw that is "rock-solid yet well-suited for speedy play" — light and fast without sacrificing stability. Distributed exclusively in the West through Rewind. Colorways: Grey, Black.

title: Ring Bearer
content:
The Ring-Bearer™ is an officially licensed Lord of the Rings yo-yo, featuring several designs from the story engraved on different colorways.

From Mark at MK1:

"Back in early '23 I had what I thought was a really straightforward idea to engrave the ring inscription from Lord of the Rings on a bimetal yoyo design that I had been sitting on for a bit. I called up my Dad (a big Tolkien fan and avid reader) to chat about this, and he reminded me of the reality of trademarks - but he also recommended contacting the licensor to ask for permission. Is it really that easy, I thought.

I looked up the best licensing contact for my proposed use and found one for Middle-earth Enterprises. I sent them an email and waited - for many weeks - until I got the response I was hoping for. This was, however, only the beginning of my adventure!

It’s now quite clearly almost 2 years after “early '23” so I’d like to talk about everything that went into this amazing project, the Ring-Bearer.

If you aren’t familiar with the behind-the-scenes of licensed products, there’s a lot that needs to happen. Contracts, insurance, brand assurance, approvals. On top of that, I wanted to make this a big release, with extra colorways, cool box art, a mini-poster - the works. All of this extra stuff will get revealed soon, as I’m waiting for the shipment to arrive.

This will be as far as I can tell the first officially licensed Lord of the Rings yo-yo.

I’d like to also give a huge shout-out to my team & all the other people who helped make this happen, especially Mag who made the packaging artwork and many of the engravings for other colorways."

Ring Bearer™ Colorways

The confirmed colorways are:

The One Ring (Serialized) - Black w/Gold Rims. Numbered. Only 111 were made.

The One Ring (Unlimited) - Black w/Gold Rims.

Vilya - Blue w/Gold Rims - Based off of, the ring that eventually found its way to Elrond.

Narya - Red w/Gold Rims  - First given to Círdan the shipwright, and later, to Gandalf, who carried it during the Third Age.

Nenya - Silver - Given to Galadriel by Celebrimbor

UNSeen - Black - Different Elvish inscription on the yo-yo

Smaug - Red w/Gold Rings - YoYoExpert exclusive with Smaug engraved in the cup

Elfstone - Green w/Siver Rings

Arkenstone - Silver w/Rainbow Rings - The Arkenstone is a big plot point (and a big gemstone) in the Hobbit,

The Box

The boxes for the Ring-Bearer are similar to MK1's hexagonal boxes, but are designed to look like Hobbit Holes:

Check out Mark's article on designing the Ring-Bearer's box.

title: RingMaster
content: About the RingMasterThe RingMaster is the signature model of AJ Kirk, featuring an above-average 58.2mm diameter in an inverse-round body with aluminum alloy rims. Its relatively narrow 39.61mm width despite the large diameter creates a specific weight distribution profile optimized for Kirk's competitive 1A style. The model ships with bind-response configuration via the included thin bearing.

title: RIO
content: AboutThe RIO is Yoyofriends' highest-performing plastic to date, combining a polycarbonate body with a beadblasted 6061 aluminum core and hub for fingerspin capability at a budget price. With expanded 56mm diameter and 48mm width, it delivers enhanced power and stability compared to the AoE, positioning it as a performance plastic competitive with entry-level monometals.

title: RippleDrop
content: From Riforgiate:Meet the RippleDrop:It’s an organic design, also the first yoyo I ever designed/made. I’ve been told it hits a lot of retro feels for an unresponsive design. There haven’t been many people who have had the chance to play with it, but it’s been pretty well received by those who have. It’s primarily been the DXL club in the LA area and Spindox club in the Bay area that have tried it out, though it made an appearance at nationals as well.For anyone who’s been hands on with the first version, this version has a couple minor changes. I’ve made some changes to the response and gap, so this should be an even better version than the first one I cut. The hub is a little thicker to guarantee durability, and there’s a shmoove groove to compensate for the extra mass. I did some tuneup work on the lathe, so the ripple doesn’t have backlash steps in it, and the response pads sit where and how they should. I’ve also swapped to using Modern Yo-yo pads, which has been an upgrade over the original spec imo.I did my best to keep the MMOI and total mass close to the original, so it should feel the same as the first one did.I’ve got 2 versions to go for. They are identical in geometry, though not in function. The titanium was the originally intended design, but at the time I always cut a practice unit from 6061 or 7075 before the titanium to make sure the toolpath was good to go so I could cut down on scrap cost. Turns out that was a happy little accident.The titanium version is around 62g by design. Definitely more of a funsies yoyo than a competition throw with the balance between rim and hub weights, but a solid throw overall.Then there’s the aluminum version:Turns out that this design makes a spectacular featherweight. The extra hub weight gets it spinning pretty well, and the lack of mass in general allows for unreal redirects when going through speed trick routines. I’ve taken to calling it the “1st Law” variant because it really likes to stay in motion. Dunno if the name will stick forever, but I think it’s clever for now.

title: Roadrunner
content: AboutThe Roadrunner is the newest member of the Runner series Duncan developed in the late 2010s, and at 52.97 mm it is the most undersized of the group. Its groove-finish catch zone is machined specifically to facilitate flowing finger and arm grinds, and its wide body relative to its small diameter creates an unusual combination of compactness and stability. Featured in a January 2019 YoYoNews feature and praised for its horizontal trick capability.

title: Roentgen
content:
From Alchemik:

"The Roentgen is the signature model of Tyler Jorgensen! Tyler runs the Tri-Cities yoyo club in Eastern Washington, and in his own words, “The inspiration for the Roentgen comes from a love of competitive style yo-yos that keep that fun-loving spirit. We wanted to make something that was powerful, agile, and durable. It has a great width for practicing those more difficult tricks, and with enough spin time to keep up!”

The Roentgen uses titanium weight rings on a 7068 body, which adds a really special feel compared to many bimetals. I personally have loved testing it as a team member and can’t wait for everyone else to get to experience it too!"

title: Rogue
content: The Rogue was a hybrid/modified yoyo. Starting with an aluminum Small Minds Zombie yo-yo, he cut the rims off then and then installed them onto an Element X body. Similar to the DV8, there was a limited prototype run of Rogues, and the yo-yo was never fully put into production, due to patent issues with YoYoJam. It is estimated that there are around 100 of these that were made.

title: Ronin
content: The Ronin was meant to be sponsored player Ed Haponik's signature yoyo. There were approximately 10 prototypes made. Due to Throw Down shutting down the yoyo never made it to the production stage.

title: ROOC
content: History / AboutShinya Kido signature brother model to Krown, reproducing its profile in a polycarbonate body with stainless rings.

title: Roots
content: Roots was the first Burgeon Yo-Yos model and the foundation of Mike Montgomery’s 2017 maker project. Each was a handmade, one-piece wooden fixed-axle yo-yo intended for responsive play, including modern kickflip and stall-oriented fixed-axle tricks.Work began in January 2017, with orders, samples, giveaways, and custom woodburned versions documented through spring and summer. Exact dimensions, weight, wood species, and launch price have not been recovered.

title: Roozenith
content: AboutThe Roozenith is the A7075 monometal signature of Kohei Nishimura, released in 2026. JT describes it as a "structural reference point" — combining a responsive feel with natural controllability. It inherits nearly identical size, weight, and shape from the Zetica bimetal, allowing players familiar with the Zetica to immediately connect with its character. Available in Shiny Pink.

title: Rope
content: AboutRope is a commission-only ultra-thick specialty string wound from 100% spun polyester, wound past the point any standard string would be called normal. Designed for heavy-duty 0A, fixed axle, or experimental play where regular string can't handle the load. Not sold in the standard shop — must be commissioned directly through Throw-Yo Threads.

title: Rotix
content:
History / About
The Rotix is mowl's first-ever undersized yo-yo, released in 2025. mowl defines their undersized category as 51mm diameter or less. Throughout the design process, the team prioritized adaptability to modern tricks and ease of handling, settling on approximately 45mm width. The Rotix expands mowl's lineup beyond its full-size comfort zone, offering players who prefer compact, nimble throws a genuine mowl option for the first time.

title: Round Fullsize
content:
From #UNBRANDED

"Uncompromising Curves for Your First Round Yoyo

Experience the seamless beauty of uninterrupted curves. This full-size round yoyo combines precise balance engineering with a gentle touch and ample spin time, offering both ease of control and performance.

If you're intrigued by casual round models but not yet ready for the low-spin designs favored by advanced players, this yoyo is crafted for beginner to intermediate players seeking that next step forward.

Recommended for:

・Beginners to intermediates looking to try a round-shaped yoyo

・Players desiring a soft feel with sufficient spin time for practicing tricks

・Those seeking a full-size yoyo that's less demanding than competition models and easy to carry around"

title: Round One
content:
History / About
Released on mowl's 9th anniversary — June 6, 2025 — the Round One is mowl's very first beginner model, a significant departure for a brand known exclusively for premium and competition-oriented products. Announced alongside the opening of mowl's first flagship store, the Round One was positioned as "Supporting Your First Step" — giving new players an entry point into the mowl brand. Available in multiple colors: Red, Blue, Black, Neon Green.

title: Chico Super Deluxe
content: Chico Super Deluxe was a one-piece wooden yo-yo made by Royal Tops Manufacturing Company during the 1950s and 1960s, featuring a decal logo. Chico was the nickname of Royal's founder, Joe Radovan, who wore a sombrero during competitions.

title: King Size Yo-Yo
content: The King Size Yo-Yo was a jumbo, roughly 3-inch-diameter wooden yo-yo made by Royal Manufacturing Company in the 1950s, the largest model Royal Tops MFG. Co. retailed.

title: Royal Special
content: Royal Special was a wooden model featuring a red-and-yellow crown graphic on a blue-and-white decal reading Royal Special, Official Tournament Top.

title: Rozzor
content: The Rozzor was developed in collaboration with Indonesian player Oke Rosgana and was Werrd's third yo-yo. The straight, slightly rounded profile offered a wide catch zone and comfortable 1A, 3A, and 5A play. The 2010 Worlds Edition came packaged in a trophy-display holder that suspended the yo-yo inside and included a belt clip — one of the more memorable packaging concepts of the era. $88.99 USD standard; $99.99 USD Worlds Edition.

title: Rozzor 2
content: The Rozzor 2 was a refined collaboration with Oke Rosgana, trimming 3.8g from the original and narrowing the width to 36.5mm for a more pocketable throw. Jimmy Hat hub posts allowed optional hubstack attachment. $88.99 USD.

title: RSM Side Effects
content:
RSM Side Effects are a unique Side Effect made by One Drop. It is said only 25 were made, and that they've been discontinued due to how hard they are to manufacture. RSM are the heaviest Side Effect ever produced, and spin similar to hub stacks.

Getting your hands on these is tough, and will cost a pretty penny.

title: RTD
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"Handcrafted by our own Alex Morton, these RTDs are the pocket friendly Stem offering that you may have seen around the National and World Yoyo Contests this year. Each one is cut from plates of HDPE plastic, with a surface finish reminiscent of playground equipment.

Note: Due to the construction of the RTD it is only compatible with size C bearings. Each will ship unresponsive but can be set up with a half  spec bearing for responsive play too!"

title: Rumbling
content: AboutThe Rumbling is the signature model of Zhang Suze, a competitive player in JIGUN's roster. A 6061 aluminum body bimetal with stainless steel outer rims, it was priced at $60. Available in Silver with Silver Rims, Red with Black Rims, Purple with Silver Rims, Mint with Silver Rims, and Maroon Tan Acid Wash with Silver Rims. A polycarbonate version, the PC Rumbling, was later released.

title: Russell Beginners
content: History / AboutThe Beginners was Russell's cheapest promotional model, introduced in Australia in 1961 alongside the Championship. Made of tin metal (later transitioning to plastic in final runs), the string was tied directly to the axle, meaning the yo-yo could not sleep — only Gravity Pull was possible. It was used in Coca-Cola campaigns as a low-cost give-away for young children. Manufactured in Hong Kong, it was discontinued around 1978 when the Spinner model took over the budget tier. The tin version is now a prized collector's item.

title: Russell Butterfly
content: History / AboutThe Russell Butterfly was a prize-only model, never available for purchase. It debuted in Japan in 1976 during the first Coca-Cola campaign, with "1976" engraved on the body and rounded caps. Subsequent releases appeared in Hong Kong (1977, Sprite launch) and the Philippines (1979, Sprite launch — with flat-topped sidecaps similar to the Spinner). Its winged/flared shape set it apart visually from Russell's standard slimline and bulge-faced models, though it retained the same fixed axle and starburst response of the broader line.

title: Russell Challenge
content: History / AboutThe Challenge was released exclusively in Japan in 1979 as part of the Coca-Cola campaign surrounding the 1980 Moscow Olympics (which Japan ultimately boycotted). It occupied the mid-tier of the three-model Japan lineup alongside the Super and the premium Special Spin. Its shape — rounded with flat centers — echoed the older Duncan Tournament form rather than the bulge-faced profile Russell was adopting elsewhere at the time.

title: Russell Championship
content: History / AboutThe Championship was Russell's first production model, introduced in Australia in 1961 for Coca-Cola promotions. Its slimline profile and engraved graphics became the template for all Russell promotional models that followed. A redesigned version with bulged faces appeared in Australia from 1981 onward, though most markets outside Australia continued to receive the flat slimline version under the name "Professional." Prize variants include the Gold Medal (awarded at the 1984 Japan Olympics Coca-Cola campaign) and the Ronald McDonald Championship (yellow body with red sides, 1960s McDonald's co-promo).

title: Russell Ellipse
content: History / AboutReleased in 1999 as part of Russell's expanded lineup following the Team High Performance (THP) partnership, the Ellipse reintroduced the slimline shape after the bulge-faced profile had dominated Russell's output for roughly twenty years. The Ellipse mold also served as the base for the Millennium (glitter), Master (red glitter / silver caps), and Galaxy (gold glitter / gold caps) prize variants released in the same period. A documented Ireland release featured clear gold-colored Ellipse-based Galaxy and Master variants.

title: Russell Fast Eddy Shooter
content: History / AboutThe Fast Eddy Shooter was produced by Russell for "Fast Eddy" Eddy McDonald, a Canadian yo-yo performer and founder of Touch the Sky Inc. It used the Imperial/looper body shape with glitter plastic and was regarded by contemporary reviewers as one of Russell's better-performing looping yo-yos. The face carried text reading "The 'Fast Eddy' Shooter / Fast Eddy McDonald / RUSSELL," with the reverse reading "Touch the Sky Inc." Available in red and clear sparkle colorways, it retailed for approximately $7–$10 USD. An example is held at The Strong National Museum of Play (Object ID: 108.2943).

title: Russell Galaxy
content: History / AboutThe Galaxy was a prize-only yo-yo never sold commercially, awarded at Russell's Coca-Cola promotional contests across multiple decades. Its defining characteristic was glitter integrated directly into the plastic during manufacturing, giving the body a starry visual effect. Early versions used the same mold as the Challenge or Professional; some variants combined gold paint with glitter. A 1999 version based on the Ellipse mold featured a clear gold-colored glitter body with gold chrome sidecaps and was released in Ireland.

title: Russell Millennium
content: History / AboutReleased in 1999 to mark the turn of the millennium, the Millennium was a glitter-bodied special edition built on the Ellipse mold. It was part of the broader Ellipse family of prize and special-edition variants produced during Russell's 1998–1999 THP expansion period. The glitter plastic body — similar in construction to the Galaxy prize variant — gave it a distinctive appearance compared to the standard Ellipse.

title: Russell Professional
content: History / AboutThe Professional is the direct evolution of the Championship, progressively rebranded from the mid-1970s as Russell standardized its global lineup. It became the backbone of Russell's Coca-Cola promotions across 95 countries, making it arguably the most widely distributed yo-yo model in history. The two-tone opaque plastic body with white inner sections and starburst response was manufactured first in the Philippines, then Korea. Post-1998 versions produced with the THP partnership used translucent colored plastic with rings around the sidecaps. In addition to Coca-Cola, the Professional was produced for McDonald's, Volkswagen, Shell, Go Fly A Kite, YoYoGuy.com, and Daft Punk across different eras.

title: Russell Special Spin
content: History / AboutIntroduced in Japan in 1979 for the Coca-Cola Moscow Olympics campaign, the Special Spin was Russell's most technically advanced model. Its steel axle with a concave center kept the string centered in the gap during play — a significant engineering departure from the standard fixed wooden axle used on every other Russell model. Russell marketed it as spinning "two and a half times longer" than conventional yo-yos. The design was finalized in 1981 when it became available outside Japan, with a documented Australian Coca-Cola release that year.

title: Russell Spinner
content: History / AboutIntroduced in South Africa in 1976 as a budget model for the Coca-Cola line, the Spinner was the first Russell yo-yo to feature the flat bulged sidecap profile that became the brand's signature aesthetic. Prior models used the older slimline shape derived from the original D.R.I. mold. The Spinner replaced the Beginners at the entry-level tier. During the Philippines' 1979 Sprite launch, some Spinner units were incorrectly labeled "Butterfly."

title: Russell Super
content: History / AboutIntroduced in 1970 as a premium model above the Championship, the Super's defining feature was its transparent (clear) plastic body — the higher-density material gave it more weight and longer spin times than the opaque Championship. It became one of Russell's most widely distributed models across Coca-Cola global campaigns through the 1970s–1990s, with documented runs for Coke, Fanta, Sprite, and US regional variants including "Coke is it! in Utah." After the 1998 THP partnership, updated versions used opaque colored plastic. The Hyper Russell Super, released through Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line in Japan, was a lightweight successor variant.

title: Russell Super Edition (Daft Punk)
content: History / AboutIn 2015, French electronic duo Daft Punk partnered with Russell Promotions to produce an official branded yo-yo using Russell's vintage 1980s mold. Marketed with a retro advertising campaign using the tagline "Strings of Fury," it pre-ordered in June 2015 and shipped in July. The yo-yo was sold for $30 AUD exclusively through Daft Punk's official regional online stores in Australia, the UK, and Europe. It stands as one of the more unexpected licensed applications of the Russell brand in its later years. Daft Punk disbanded in 2021.

title: Russell Yo-2K
content: History / AboutThe Yo-2K was a Y2K era commemorative model distributed in the United States by Go Fly A Kite, Inc. under their GO-YO branding. An example with an orange glitter body is documented at The Strong National Museum of Play (Google Arts & Culture / The Strong archive). The Strong's catalog dates it to "1980," which is almost certainly a mold-date error; contemporary context places it firmly in the 1999–2000 period. Collab partner Go Fly A Kite, Inc. is not currently in the archive.

title: Sa
content:
About
Sa is Shota Saga's signature model — a “new casual” design pairing a machined polycarbonate body with stainless steel rims for a balance between effortless maneuverability and surprising spin power.

title: Saber Crash
content: A unique addition to the Crash series featuring an inner stainless steel ring that protrudes outward, distributing weight across the width for enhanced stability and control. Signature variants include Jun Aramaki edition. Price: $99–$110.

title: Saboteur
content:
History / About
The Saboteur is GWAY Throws’ second release, again developed in partnership with Anomaly Yo-Yo’s. The design leans into high-walled organic shaping, evoking classic yoyo aesthetics while delivering full modern unresponsive performance. Interior cuts reduce string friction during play, and matador spikes in the cup add versatility. The bubble-shaped contours keep handling comfortable.
Colorways included Silver, Gray, Pink/Blue Fade, Red/Orange Fade, and Smoke (Black/Silver).

title: Sagane
content:
Sagane Protoype 01

The first Sagane prototype was released in September of 2024, with a limited amount sold via a 1-month pre-order window prior to release.

title: Sago
content:
From TRT:

"We’re proud to present to you our first foray into performance oriented bimetal engineering, designed for float, speed, and fun!

This is the Sago.

Each cup is a mere 9.5g of 7068 aluminum, adorned with a 21.5g stainless steel ring. The overall weight is kept slightly lower than what most would consider the norm. Sago weighs in at only 65.1g to maintain an easily maneuverable and incredibly wild flow. When you’re ready to move, just say go.

FPM’s PinkPads provide satisfyingly snappy binds inside of the 4.4mm response gap while still allowing for ample string layering, and a 12mm axle ensures endurance.

Each Sago comes with a @ziplinestrings ZS.AIR string, TRT sticker, and pog. All packaged in a hand stamped box."

Colorways

The Sago comes in four colorways: Citrus Splash, Florida Bay Fade, Clear w/Rainbow Rims, and an Unknown colorway.

Unknown Sago Colorway

The Unknown colorway for the Sago comes with a few extra goodies.

What's in the Box

Each Sago comes in a hand-stamped, numbered box, making every piece feel special. Included with the yo-yo is a Zipline ZS Air 100% nylon string, a TRT sticker, and a TRT Series #4 POG, with special variations for the Unknown Edition.

title: Saint Eel
content:
History / About
The world deserves a brutal mini yoyo. We deliver it. This time, they are finished by vibratory grinding in two steps. The first being ceramic pellets followed by walnut shells. This gives the outside of the halves a smooth polish-like appearance while the inside keeps its machining looks.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (May 2009) — 9 units, Raw; D41.10mm / W30.85mm / 68.00g. Bearing: D.
Proto #2 (July 2009) — 25 units, Raw; D41.10mm / W30.85mm / 59.00g. Finish: Ceramic Blast.
Proto #3 (December 2009) — 22 units, Raw; D41.10mm / W30.85mm / 65.00g.
Run #1 (March 2010) — 110 units, Raw; D42.10mm / W31.00mm / 61.50g. Finish: E-Polished.
Proto #4 (May 2011) — 9 units, Raw; D42.10mm / W31.00mm / 62.00g. Finish: Satin.
Run #2 (July 2011) — 135 units, Raw; D42.10mm / W31.00mm / 62.00g. Finish: Satin.
Run #3 (December 2012) — 30 units, Raw; D42.10mm / W31.00mm / 62.00g. Finish: Walnut Polished.

title: Sakura (Original)
content:
History / About
Raytsh is at it again. His third design is a mid-sized, fully rimweighted powerhouse – Sakura.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (June 2010) — 5 units, Silver; D52.00mm / W41.00mm / 65.30g. Finish: Candodize.
Proto #2 (October 2010) — 8 units, Purple; D52.00mm / W41.00mm / 65.30g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (November 2010) — 99 units, Purple; D52.00mm / W41.00mm / 65.30g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Special #1 (April 2011) — 20 units, Orange/Green; D52.00mm / W41.00mm / 65.30g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Special #2 (December 2011) — 8 units, Red/Black; D52.00mm / W41.00mm / 65.30g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.
Run #2 (February 2013) — 25 per colorway (Hair Band, Broken Heart, Light Dusk, Cobalt, Dark Dusk, Melon); D52.00mm / W41.25mm / 62.80 + 2.90g. Bearing: C. Finish: Pyramatte.

title: Sakura SE
content:
From One Drop:

"We are proud to announce a collaboration with I Love YoYo that has been in the works for quite a while. We decided to make a Side Effect version of the ILLY Sakura.

We added Side Effects to this beautiful 52mm diameter curvy H-shaped yoyo by ILYY. The Side Effects are the same shape as the hub in the original. This collaboration is similar to when we did the Wooly MarkMont with CLYW in that we only released a limited number and won't make any more.

There was about 200 available in 6 different colorways sold direct from the One Drop online store on Monday February 25th at 11am PST."
