title: Samothrace
content: History / AboutPremium C3 retail model using a strong 7075 body and stainless rims in compact dimensions.

title: Samurai
content:
From Rewind Worldwide:

"Brought to you by the maker named for the era of the Samurai warrior, the Samurai is a bimetal string trick yo-yo with a rare M-profile.

This is a bimetal throw unlike the others that came before. Sengoku has mixed the themes and concepts of its other yo-yos to come together in this new M-profile. The stainless steel ring looks like both an outer and inner rim at the same time. Strangely the benefits of both seem to be present in the Samurai.

The secret is in the inertia moving toward the axis of revolution, and not just the "spin" itself. This shift in focus means that the Samurai keeps its posture upright and true, maintaining incredible stability to the very end of its sleep. This benefit is immediately apparent at the first throw, and makes for unbelievably steady horizontal play.

Sengoku is very enthusiastic about their latest design, stating that this development may uproot the contest scene when they see what it can do. Not just a bimetal design, the Samurai represents a new era and understanding of the physics of yo-yo. After throwing it ourselves, we think they may be right."

title: Samurai Armadillo
content:
From Sengoku:

"This is a powerful, midsize, and wide yo-yo. The ridges make rejections and grinds a joy, while minimizing string friction with the walls.

The performance is there, it gets the job done just as well as any other wide bimetal.

It just does it in a way that stands out.

A true distillation of Sengoku’s core philosophy."

title: Sandevistan
content: History / AboutMagnesium design whose face and large diameter later influenced Zillion.

title: Satinav
content: History / AboutLeo Chan signature experience that informed the later Vanitas Spectre; uses a 6061 body and titanium rims.

title: Satyr
content: AboutReleased in June 2019, the Satyr was the last documented release from Radical Seas. Limited to just 60 pieces under the "Heaven's Gate" edition name — a reference to the late-1990s UFO group, whose name is engraved on the rim — the Satyr placed weight firmly at the rims for strong spin power while retaining enough profile curve for a comfortable catch zone. The silky finish was praised by players for its grind performance.Available in Purple. A small number of units received QC reports of light vibe, but the Satyr drew strong overall praise for its fast, agile character and high stability.

title: Savage
content: AboutThe Savage is the signature of Ayumu Kasuga, released in July 2024. Its defining feature is an ultra-wide 50mm catch zone — one of the broadest in the YYR catalog — paired with a tri-material construction: a 7075 aluminum body combined with stainless steel weight rings and POM (polyoxymethylene) wing inserts. The 56mm × 50mm × 68g spec makes it both wide and substantial, tuned for Kasuga's competition style. A mono-metal variant (Little Savage) and a premium version (Savage 55) with different wing materials were also released.

title: Schneider
content:
History / About
Schneider is a straight-profile bimetal built on an OEM chassis credited to "YOYO Laboratory" as their "ELAN."

title: Schneider Blade Attack Mode
content:
History / About
Schneider Blade Attack Mode depicts the storyline's in-manga "Blade Attack Mode" transformation. Unusually, the storyline concept was designed first and the hardware built second, the reverse of most models in the line.

title: Schneider MK-II
content:
History / About
Schneider MK-II was Sturm Panzer's first stainless-rim bimetal, bundled with buyer's choice of Storybook Vol.3 or Vol.6. Cited by the maker as one of the hardest models to manufacture due to variable rotational balance.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size D (CP-06 D9 on later lots)

title: Scintillator
content: Simpson Wong's first signature after 25 years in the yo-yo community, combining several of his favorite C3 models into a budget-friendly competition-ready monometal. Features an exaggerated H-shape with a distinctive flat fingerspin hub (not rounded) designed to minimize skin contact and extend spin duration. Wider than typical yet narrower than the Galaxy Diver. DNA trick-optimized. Multiple splash and solid colorways. Price: $45–$50.

title: Scorpion King
content: About the Scorpion KingThe Scorpion King was the heaviest model in King Yo Star's 2011 debut lineup at 72.3 g, and at 59.51 mm diameter the largest. Its H-shaped profile was designed for hopping tricks and Influent-style freestyle, providing great spin and stability. Marketed as a "tough beast" for high-impact performance play.

title: Scrub
content:
From Turner Return Tops:

"We’re proud to present our latest top, the Scrub! A performance packed soft H shape that’ll give you what you want from a modern mono-metal design. Stability, spin time, snappy response, a profile for snug finger grinds, and fat lips for inner ring grinds. Scrub even boasts an M4x12mm axle that ensures a smooth spin, even after taking a beating. Those TRT nipples aren’t just for show, you know!"

Known as the "Wide Isthmus" during development, the Scrub boasts performance unlike any other TRT throw.

title: Sea Monkey
content:
History / About
The Sea Monkey is a collaboration between MonkeyfingeR Design and YoYo WorkShop (YYWS). The project began in 2016 and took years to finalize, bringing together design elements from both companies. Released September 2019.

title: Secret Slim
content:
Jake Bullock's Secret Slim is exactly what it sounds like, a Slim Dunk with something hidden. Tucked completely beneath the Delrin rims are stainless steel rings you can't see, giving this organic-feeling throw a backbone of stability and power that belies its slim profile.

The result is a yoyo that plays with the familiar, comfortable DNA of the Slim Dunk, but carries noticeably more authority on the string. The colored Delrin does the visual heavy lifting, keeping the whole package looking clean and understated while the steel does its quiet work inside.

title: Ashigaru
content:
History / About
The Ashigaru takes its name from the foot soldiers (ashigaru) of Japan's Sengoku period — indicating its role as the accessible entry point to Sengoku's line. The monometal aluminum body features thick rims for stability and spin power while the overall weight is kept light at 63.8g. A simple, beautifully executed design at $65, the Ashigaru delivers a fast, lightweight feel with a comfortable shape suitable for players stepping up from beginner throws.

title: Masachibi
content:
History / About
The Masachibi is a smaller, more powerful evolution of the Masamini. Where mini yo-yos typically sacrifice spin power and stability, the Masachibi addresses those limitations with oversized stainless steel inner rims that dramatically increase rotational mass despite the compact 36mm diameter body. At 60g in a 36×34mm profile, it delivers full competition performance in a pocket-carry form factor optimized for accuracy practice and refined technique.

title: Masamune
content:
History / About
The Masamune was Sengoku's second release, announced November 2015 at $228 USD. Named after the legendary Japanese swordsmith Masamune, it used a then-novel material called Alumigo Hard — a high-tech alloy described as comparable to or better than steel in strength while remaining more machinable and affordable than titanium. The stainless steel rings were installed using nitrogen cooling and weigh more than 50% of the aluminum body weight, creating extreme rim weighting in a 55mm diameter profile.

title: Answer
content: Answer is a YoYoPalace bimetal yo-yo now listed by Spinkult under SENSE, the successor name for YoYoPalace. Its 7075 aluminum body has stainless steel rings. This record covers the Answer model; Journey is a separate yo-yo in the Answer Series.The FIU collector list records a December 14, 2020 Unknown edition with a reported quantity of 30. This is edition information, not a confirmed base-model launch day.Source: Spinkult Answer listing.

title: A-Mono2
content:
About

title: Anti Mono

About
Anti Mono pairs an A6061 core with a polycarbonate rim.

title: Anti Mono Mini

About
Anti Mono Mini is a miniature version of the Anti Mono line. Colorway: Pink/Blue Polycarbonate.

title: Anti Mono2
content:
About
Anti Mono2 is the second-generation successor to Anti Mono, an A6061 body with a plastic rim.

title: Code
content:
About
Code was YoYoPalace's (SENSE's predecessor brand) first release, designed by founders Yiwen Li and Jiale Tong starting November 2019.

title: Code 2
content:
About
Code 2 is the second-generation, entry-level step-up model in the Code line.

title: Code 3
content:
About
Code 3 is the third-generation release in the Code line. Colorway: Matt Splash (pink/blue/red).

title: Extra Sensory
content:
About
Extra Sensory is a wide-profile bi-metal model, notable for a width that exceeds its diameter. Colorway: Shiny Fade (Blue/Silver).

title: Fake Two-Pieces
content:
About
Fake Two-Pieces uses a dual-finish treatment to create the illusion of a two-piece build despite being a mono-metal.

title: Liberado
content:
About
Liberado is a bi-metal evolution of the earlier Libre model. Colorway: Splash (Black/Blue/Gold).

title: Libre
content:
About
Libre is Jihoo Lee's 5A signature model, a bi-metal build in A7075 with a stainless rim. Lee later moved on to sponsorship by C3yoyodesign.

title: Libre 6061
content:
About
Libre 6061 is a lower-cost bi-metal variant of the Libre, using an A6061 body with a stainless rim.

title: Login
content:
About
Login is SENSE's first "cap yoyo," a mono-metal A6061 body with a removable plastic cap for adjustable play feel. Colorway: Light Green (W1LD).

title: Mimic
content:
About
Mimic was the last release under the YoYoPalace name, positioned as the bridge to the SENSE rebrand ("YYP's last farewell, SENSE's first greeting").

title: Mono Stage
content:
About
Mono Stage is the mono-metal version of Next Stage, also a Quoc Anh signature model.

title: Next Journey
content:
About
Next Journey is Ahmad Kharisma's signature model, an evolution of the earlier "Journey" release.

title: Next Stage
content:
About
Next Stage is Quoc Anh's 5A signature model, a bi-metal build with a stainless rim.

title: Next Stage 6061
content:
About
Next Stage 6061 is a lower-cost bi-metal variant of Next Stage, an A6061 body with a stainless rim.

title: Senti Metal
content:
About
Senti Metal is a flagship bi-metal model (A6061 body/cap with a stainless rim), notable for shell sections under 1mm thick.

title: SenTI-Vessel
content:
About
SenTI-Vessel is a titanium, non-competitive leisure design with a "mug body" shape. "Year of the Horse" gold-logo colorway.

title: Twinsense
content:
About
Twinsense is the signature model of twin yoyo players Qin Ruiwen and Qin Ruian. Colorway: Pink.

title: Ur-Journey
content:
About
Ur-Journey is Ahmad Kharisma's signature model and the first outer-rim bi-metal build in the Journey line.

title: Sentinel JP
content: The Sentinel JP is the second-generation Mark Allen signature, replacing the original's spiked hub with a smooth cupped hub inspired by the Irony JP. Weight was stripped from the center and redistributed to the rims for a modern performance profile. MagicStep™ geometry on the catch zone reduces string rejections. Available in Gold anodized finish. $89.99 USD.

title: Sericin
content: AboutSericin is a 100% spun silk string — no blending agent, no modifier — from the Throw-Yo Threads Luxury tier. Launched April 6, 2026, it is the most premium string in the catalog, priced per individual string due to material cost. Docile disposition and brisk velocity with an enduring shelf life. Available in Orpiment and Rose Madder colorways.

title: Serum
content: AboutSerum is wound from 100% Maxi-Lock stretch nylon, producing a plush, very soft feel with moderate velocity and shelf life. One of the most colorway-rich strings in the Throw-Yo Threads catalog, Serum is available in Litmus, Scheele's, Biliverdin, Auripigment, Ceruse, Eosine, Mauveine, and Minium alongside monocolor.

title: Set Sail
content: AboutThe Set Sail was Radical Seas' first production yo-yo, released in February 2015. Designed by Jamelle Kent, it introduced the brand's philosophy of precision over complexity. The oversized H-shape profile delivers long spin times and strong stability while remaining more agile than its 58mm diameter suggests.Each colorway was produced in extremely limited quantities — some runs as few as 20 pieces — making the Set Sail a sought-after collector piece almost immediately. Sold through YoYoExpert at $85 USD.

title: Seven Summits
content:
From One Drop:

"The original Summit came from the meeting of the minds and hearts of CLYW? and One Drop Yo-Yos?. As documented in the video, it was a short but intense beginning to one of the most popular models released by either company. Nearly two years later they are still just as loved and we continue to produce them.

To continue this journey we knew we wanted to make the Summit in 7075 alloy. Since this is the Summit, we knew it had to be different and took inspiration based on that 7075 is part of "Seven Series Aluminum". It became obvious: we need to do the Seven Summits.

The Seven Summits? are the tallest mountains on each of the 7 continents. Climbing to the summit of all seven (let alone even one) is an incredible human feat known as the "Seven Summits".

We are going to create the Seven Summits of yo-yo by offering seven different runs of 7075 Summits - each run limited to 50 yo-yos and named after each of the actual seven mountains. Each run will be released separately over a period of months starting with Kilimanjaro in Africa.

And here is another cool part. 7075 weighs more (is more dense) than the usual 6061 so you would expect the Seven Summits to weigh more. However, we re-designed the weight distribution so the resulting total weight of the yo-yo is lighter! Whoa. Heavier metal, lighter yo-yo, but still looks the same (and has the same width and diameter).

You will know it's a Seven Summit because it will have a mountain name engraved on it. But more than that you will know because it plays different from the original while still maintaining the same essence.

Everest - Asia 

Kilimanjaro - Africa - Black base with gold and blue splash

McKinley - North America

Aconcagua - South America

Elbrus - Europe

Vinson - Antarctica

Kosciuszko - Australia"

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)
meta.yya_weight: 60.85g (63.35g with aluminium Ultra Light Side Effects)

title: Seventh Heaven
content: AboutThe Seventh Heaven was released at the 2015 World YoYo Contest to mark yoyorecreation's seventh anniversary — the number seven woven throughout its identity, from the name to the price. Built from titanium on a shape and size inspired by the Sleipnir, it is the second YYR titanium model after the 2013 Dazzler. The ¥77,777 price (~$635 USD at the time) and extremely limited production run made it an immediate collector's item. It was released alongside the Valkyrie bi-metal, offering the full spectrum of YYR construction in a single Worlds release.

title: BD
content: BD is an SF Yoyos retail yo-yo offered through a surprise preorder associated with Blind Date and birthday marketing. The model has multiple engraved designs and mixed-half variants documented by owners; these are variants of one model.Sources: 2023 preorder and owner discussion; SF production and shipping updates.

title: Bliss
content:
History / About
The Bliss is the signature model of SF Yoyos team member Paul Harness, released in 2018. Its H-profile and thick stainless steel rim deliver a play characteristic distinctly different from earlier SF designs. At 63.9 grams it is among SF's lightest throws, yet the rim weight provides strong stability.

title: Bliss CS
content:
History / About
The Bliss CS is Connor Seals' personal variant of the SF Yoyos Bliss, released in 2019. The CS version features a slightly tighter gap for snappier returns, optimized for regeneration tricks. At 65.1 grams it is 1.2 grams heavier than the standard Bliss, providing additional stability.

title: Cadence
content:
History / About
The Cadence is the signature model of Keiran Cooper, NER champion and SF Yoyos team stalwart, released in 2018. Its wide 46.51mm body and step-straight profile were designed to feel lightweight and fast on the string. The high bump around the response area minimizes string contact during play. The Cadence became one of SF's most recognized models.

title: Cadence ES
content:
History / About
The Cadence ES is a revised version of Keiran Cooper's signature Cadence, released in 2019 following his European Open championship win. The update redistributes weight toward the rim for increased spin time and stability while maintaining the wide-body feel of the original. Laser engraving was used as a tool for fine-tuning weight distribution — an approach Cooper described as "messing with functional benefits of laser engraving."

title: Ceasefire
content:
History / About
The Ceasefire is a unique dual-signature model from SF Yoyos, released in 2019. Designed as a collaboration between rival players Alec Jones and Collin Ellingson, the yoyo was conceived as a creative truce between two distinct playing styles. The bimetal construction achieves what SF called an "unusual combination of light and stable," with a stainless steel inner rim seated in a 7075 aluminum body.

title: DK
content:
History / About
The DK is a collaboration between SF Yoyos and A-RT (Alternate Return Tops), released in 2018. The design was inspired by a doorknob profile — a deliberately unusual shape that prioritizes aesthetic expression over competitive performance. Its hollow aluminum construction keeps weight to just 62.8 grams. Multiple anodized colorways were produced including silver, pink, black, and gold blast.

title: Motive
content:
History / About
The Motive is the signature model of Connor Seals, released by SF Yoyos in 2019. Based on the platform of the SF Statement, the Motive features a thicker stainless steel inner rim and beautiful curves designed to sit comfortably in the hand. The name reflects a philosophy of supporting players regardless of their goals or skill level.

title: Motive Beta
content:
History / About
The Motive Beta is the pre-production variant of Connor Seals' SF Yoyos signature, released in 2019 ahead of the standard Motive. It differs with a slightly wider body (45.83mm vs 45.95mm) and a heavier weight (64.6g vs 64.3g) due to the thicker stainless steel rim. Limited production run sold through Rewind Japan.

title: Movement
content:
History / About
The Movement is Tony Šec's second signature model with SF Yoyos, released in 2020. Where the Statement featured midship weighting and a bimetal construction, the Movement is an all-aluminum design in 7075 with a wider 47.36mm body and rounded edges throughout. It was Šec's final SF Yoyos signature before the brand wound down operations.

title: PLSTC
content:
History / About
The PLSTC is SF Yoyos' first full plastic model, released in 2019 at just $19.99. Its design combines elements from the Cadence and Statement into a polycarbonate body, delivering what the brand called "a soft catch but powerful spin." The throw ships with two bearings — a standard center-track and a slim bearing for tug-response play. A REWIND Shibuya exclusive clear colorway featured a logo designed by store manager 44nollie.

title: SF
content:
History / About
The SF is SF Yoyos' founding model, released in 2016. Its step-round profile and narrow 41.92mm width set the template for the brand's identity, earning a reputation as a smooth, controllable throw despite modest dimensions. The brand emerged in the latter half of 2016 and quickly built a following through social media, player sponsorships, and accessible pricing.

title: SF SS
content:
History / About
The SF SS (Stainless Steel) is the bimetal successor to SF Yoyos' debut model, released in 2017. It retains the distinctive step-round profile of the original SF but adds a stainless steel rim for extended sleep times and the ability to execute longer trick combinations.

title: SStatemment
content:
History / About
The SStatemment (intentional double-letter styling) is SF Yoyos' bimetal evolution of the Statement, released in 2019. While sharing nearly identical dimensions with the Statement, the SStatemment integrates a stainless steel inner rim into a refined H-profile curve set. The brand described it as offering "ungodly stability with light power."

title: Statement
content:
History / About
The Statement is the signature model of Slovak player Tony Šec, released by SF Yoyos in 2019. The profile features a subtle inverse S-curve with midship weighting, creating what the brand described as "loads of spin" combined with "a soft handshake" feel. Its 7075 aluminum body is paired with a stainless steel rim for stability. The Statement became the foundation for subsequent SF models including the Motive and Movement.

title: Shade
content: AboutThe Shade is JT's competition-geared bimetal, with adjusted weight distribution, shape, and size compared to the Kagerou. JT describes it as delivering "reliable stability through combos, instant power, easily maneuverable." Available in a Light Blue Niigata Edition colorway, Black/Matte Silver Rims, Pink/Black Rings, and Silver/Gold Rims.

title: SHADOW × INERTIA – Xavier Ng Edition
content:
About
The SHADOW × INERTIA - Xavier Ng Edition is a collaboration between "alternatives" and OFFSET. The colourway was designed entirely by Xavier Ng. Limited to 30 pieces. Specifications are identical to the standard INERTIA. $70.

title: Shawn Exploder
content: AboutThe Shawn Exploder is a 7075 aluminum yo-yo designed by Doctor Popular as a signature model for yo-yo photographer Shawn Garcia — Doc Pop's first photographer signature collaboration. The design is intentionally optimized for Garcia's distinctive "exploded" photography technique: V-shaped wedge geometry and stepped inner walls maximize the contrast and visual separation between string layers in photographs while simultaneously reducing string friction during play.Each unit shipped with an acrylic display stand with artwork, a microfiber lens cloth, and a silkscreened carrying pouch. Available in Blue and Yellow colorways at $75.A Moon Rock White edition was released in 2022 in 7068 aluminum (60.4g, slightly lighter), featuring One Drop's Moon Rock anodize, a cloth bag, and a 10-pack of white/gold PopString. The Moon Rock edition was priced at $100.

title: Shell
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"Good Life YoYos proudly unveils the next evolutionary leap in collaboration with Dressel Designs – introducing Shell, a yoyo that seamlessly merges vibrant aesthetics with functionality. Crafted with a focus on enjoyment, Shell offers a laid-back, full-feeling throw that not only excels in style but also delivers on tricks.

This yoyo is meticulously engineered to engage your senses, featuring a machined polycarbonate shell seamlessly integrated with aluminum and precision press-fit onto the body. Good Life YoYos design goal was simply to make a yoyo with a Polycarbonate outer layer, when they played the prototypes they found it was a drastically different experience than expected – crisper Regens, enhanced comfort in hand, and overall performance that surpassed expectations. It was a revelation, confirming that they had found the perfect design.

The collaboration between Good Life YoYos and Dressel Designs marks an exciting fusion of their respective aesthetics and design philosophies. Get ready to showcase your tricks with flair and experience the essence of Shell – where style meets substance!"

title: Shenzhou Assault
content: About the AssaultThe Shenzhou Assault was the flagship metal model in Shenzhou's first international hobbyist yo-yo release, circa 2011. CNC-machined from aluminum alloy and anodized in a solid orange finish, the Assault featured clear hubstacks, a grooved shieldless bearing, and a silicone O-ring response system. It was sold internationally through Amazon and eBay alongside the Battle Axe and BlitzFire as part of Shenzhou's entry into the overseas yo-yo market. The Assault was produced in a single orange colorway.

title: Shenzhou Avenger
content: About the AvengerThe Shenzhou Avenger (Fùchóuzhě) is an aluminum alloy yo-yo from Shenzhou's domestic Chinese retail line, introduced circa 2018 and continued through the 2021 catalog under product number 201234. Like the companion Destroyer, it is sold through Chinese retail channels and toy fairs as part of Shenzhou's broader yo-yo portfolio. Specific play specifications are not published by the manufacturer.

title: Shenzhou Battle Axe
content: About the Battle AxeThe Shenzhou Battle Axe was part of the trio of metal yo-yos Shenzhou released for the international market circa 2011, alongside the Assault and BlitzFire. Machined from aluminum alloy and finished in blue anodizing, the Battle Axe was distinguished from its siblings by its black hubstacks rather than clear. It shared the same grooved shieldless bearing and silicone O-ring response system. Like the other models in the line, it was available in a single colorway and distributed through Amazon and eBay.

title: Shenzhou BlitzFire
content: About the BlitzFireThe Shenzhou BlitzFire rounded out the three metal models in Shenzhou's 2011 international hobbyist lineup. Machined from aluminum alloy with a red and blue bicolor anodized finish and clear hubstacks, the BlitzFire shared the grooved shieldless bearing and silicone O-ring response of the Assault and Battle Axe. It was notable for shipping with two spare strings and two spare silicone pads — the most complete package in the line. Distributed through Amazon and eBay in a single bicolor colorway.

title: Shenzhou Crystal
content: About the CrystalThe Shenzhou Crystal was one of two plastic models in Shenzhou's 2011 international yo-yo release, alongside the Professional. Molded from clear polycarbonate with a rainbow iridescent coating, the Crystal did not feature hubstacks — distinguishing it from its companion plastic model. It used a grooved shieldless bearing and silicone O-ring response, and shipped with two spare strings and two spare silicone pads. Available in a single clear/rainbow colorway through Amazon and eBay.

title: Shenzhou Destroyer
content: About the DestroyerThe Shenzhou Destroyer (Huǐmièzhě) is an aluminum alloy yo-yo from Shenzhou's domestic Chinese retail line, introduced circa 2018 and continued through the 2021 catalog under product number 201235. A companion model to the Avenger, it is sold through Chinese retail channels and toy fairs. Specific play specifications are not published by the manufacturer.

title: Shenzhou Nuclear Elements
content: About the Nuclear ElementsThe Shenzhou Nuclear Elements is an undersized aluminum yo-yo produced circa 2016 as part of Shenzhou's mid-decade retail line. It features a concave H-profile body with free-spinning hubstacks on both halves — a design closely paralleling YoYoFactory's 888 — fitted with a Size C Konkave (KK) bearing and press-fit silicone response pads. At 71g for a 50mm diameter, the Nuclear Elements is notably dense for its size. Documented by YoYo Museum collector Rick Brough as an "economical Chinese brand of aluminum yo-yo," it was sold in display-box packaging.

title: Shenzhou Professional
content: About the ProfessionalThe Shenzhou Professional was the second plastic model in Shenzhou's 2011 international yo-yo lineup. Molded from black polycarbonate and fitted with clear hubstacks, the Professional shared the grooved shieldless bearing and silicone O-ring response system of the metal models in the line. It shipped with two spare strings and two spare silicone pads. Contemporary forum users noted responsiveness issues after the response pads wore in — a common characteristic of this era’s pad-equipped plastic yo-yos. Available in black only through Amazon and eBay.

title: Shenzhou Speed Soldier
content: About the Speed SoldierThe Shenzhou Speed Soldier is an undersized ABS plastic yo-yo produced circa 2016 alongside the metal Nuclear Elements. Despite its plastic construction, the Speed Soldier uses a Size C Konkave (KK) shieldless bearing and press-fit silicone response pads. At 68g for a 50mm diameter across a 41mm-wide body, it is unusually heavy for a plastic yo-yo of this size. Documented by the YoYo Museum, it was sold in display-box packaging as part of Shenzhou's mid-decade retail line.

title: Shenzhou YO Huan
content: About the YO HuanThe Shenzhou YO Huan ("YO Fantasy") is a consumer yo-yo from Shenzhou's domestic retail catalog, product number 201227, introduced in 2021. Part of a trio alongside the YO Xuan and YO Ji, it is sold through Chinese retail channels and toy fairs. Material and play specifications are not published by the manufacturer.

title: Shenzhou YO Ji
content: About the YO JiThe Shenzhou YO Ji ("YO Trace") is a consumer yo-yo from Shenzhou's domestic retail catalog, product number 201228, introduced in 2021. Part of a trio alongside the YO Xuan and YO Huan, it is sold through Chinese retail channels and toy fairs. Material and play specifications are not published by the manufacturer.

title: Shenzhou YO Xuan
content: About the YO XuanThe Shenzhou YO Xuan ("YO Dazzle") is a consumer yo-yo from Shenzhou's domestic retail catalog, product number 201212. First appearing in 2017 and continuing through the 2021 catalog revision, the YO Xuan is sold through Chinese retail channels and toy fairs as part of Shenzhou's recurring yo-yo product line. Material and play specifications are not published by the manufacturer.

title: Shine
content: AboutThe Shine is Drake Bogataj's signature Yoyofriends bimetal, designed for competition and everyday play with a focus on responsive binds, powerful regens, and horizontal tricks. The V/H hybrid shape delivers maneuverability alongside the power expected from a stainless steel bimetal, reflecting Bogataj's dynamic play style.

title: Shingen
content:
From YoYoExpert:

"The Shingen, named after the Samurai leader Takeda Shingen, is the first yoyo made out of 7175 alloy, a mixture of magnesium, zinc, copper and aluminum.

The yoyo industry standard is 6061 aluminum. A less common, and more premium option 7075, which has superior strength to weight, can be machined thinner, and is even a little harder to ding.

The 7175 alloy is a step above this. Its strength and rigidity are both superior, once again allowing for more extreme weight distributions. The Shingen makes full use of these properties to maximize rim weight. Add an extra large stainless steel set of rims, and you’ve got some serious angular momentum!"

title: Shinobi
content:
From Rewind Worldwide:

"A rare tri-metal M-shape yo-yo!

Taking the M-shape body profile of the Sengoku Samurai, this variation enters the stage with even more design consideration for weight distribution through its use of three different metals for its construction. Shinobi wraps its aluminum body with both steel and brass weight rings, which combine with its unusual profile for a truly unique playfeel!

The inner rim provides additional balance and stability, while the thin outer rim gives additional power that gives the Shinobi a slightly more fierce spin than the Samurai. With the added weight and power boost, the Shinobi is ready for exceptionally long combos and horizontal tricks. It holds its planes very well, with lots of control without losing its posture. This means the Shinobi isn't just ready for long combos, but it's ready to help you push the entire genre of trick to the next level. Take your role in the evolution of trick design!

This level of power and performance is immediately apparent; you'll notice the difference at first throw and catch. Sharp, hard, and tight, are all words that come to mind. The limits of metal yo-yos are there for you to push further!"

title: Dolphin
content: Dolphin is a model in Shinwoo's yo-yo catalog. No further description available.

title: Dolphin (Old)
content: A new undersized offering from Shinwoo, the full metal Dolphin. After the release of the oversized GrandYo, Shinwoo has brought out the small guns. The Dolphin is the undersized counter point to the GrandYo. The unusual outer hub shape isn't just for looks, it's form follows its function. At 50mm, the Dolphin is indeed slightly undersized, making it great for intricate between-finger string tricks. But undersized yo-yos are generally known for lacking serious power and stability, which makes players who want to practice speedy or horizontal play. To prove this stereotype wrong, the Dolphin has both a low edge and an inverse round shape, to minimize sleep loss, and its thick rim gives it both power and stability you wouldn't expect. The axle protruding from the side shows just how much weight has been shaved off the center hub to provide this kind of performance. Just like the GrandYo

title: Fire Loop
content: Shinwoo's standard looping yo-yo now comes loaded with a Fire Circuit to light up the stage at your next performance. This is Shinwoo's Loop, outfitted with a Fire Circuit LED board. Whereas the SW301 only has a red LED on board, the Fire Loop is multi-colored, giving you a beautiful brush to paint the stage or just impress your friends. There are some other options out there for LED yo-yos, including Duncan's Pulse and Limelight, but with the different colors and abilities available, you have more choices to find the model that suits your needs best. The Fire Loop performs beautifully for inside loops and around-the-worlds, leaving an eye-catching trail of light behind it. Of course, even simple tricks like throw down and forward pass are enough to turn heads. With some practice, double looping will look even more impressive as you paint twin ovals in the dark. If string tricks are

title: Fire Phantom
content: In place of the metal weight, the Phantom now sports a LED light system! *This product does not have a package The Phantom may be Shinwoo's definitive plastic string trick yo-yo, and now it's available with its own impressive lighting system. Pre-loaded with Shinwoo's own "Fire Circuit" multi-color LED kit, the Fire Phantom is Korea's answer to the Duncan Pulse. The ease of use is unchanged from the original Phantom, but now your performances will brighten up any space. Despite its light weight the Phantom spins furiously. The circuit is activated by the spin of the yo-yo, making switches unnecessary. Just pick it up and give it a throw for a yo-yo fireworks show. As this yo-yo is based on the Phantom 2, use either Shinwoo's Response Pads or Shinwoo's Silicone Rings .

title: Fire Techno
content: There aren't many LED yo-yos out there for string play, making the Fire Techno a glimmering diamond in the dark. Perfect for performances with the lights turned down. This is the Shinwoo's Techno, loaded with a Fire Circuit LED board. Whereas the SW301 only has a red LED on board, the Fire Techno is multi-colored, giving you a beautiful brush to paint the stage or just impress your friends. There are some other options out there for LED yo-yos, including Duncan's Pulse and Limelight, but with the different colors and abilities available, you have more choices to find the model that suits your needs best. The Fire Techno has a clear body, making the yo-yo's movement itself the brush with which you draw your light strokes. It performs beautifully for brain twisters, and eli hops. Of course, even simple tricks like throw down and forward pass are enough to turn heads. There aren't many LED

title: GrandYo
content: An unusual addition to Shinwoo's lineup, the GrandYo is an oversized full metal yo-yo. Up until now, the only full metal yo-yos in Shinwoo's lineup were the Zen series, which all came in with a 54mm diameter and 40mm width, varying only in their body shapes. The Zens provide excellent cost-performance, and now the GrandYo stands to show a whole new potential from our friends in Korea. Firstly, the GrandYo has grown to a 58mm diameter and 42.5mm width, making it big enough to spill out of small hands a bit. Its large size gives it impressive spin and makes it easy to mount on the string, making it a spectacular throw. Just a light toss will give you enough spin to pull off some impressive combos, with time to spare. Since it's so cheap for a full metal yo-yo, the GrandYo makes a great "first metal" model for players looking to level up. There's just something about the feel of a metal

title: Griffin Wing 1
content: In recent years, the Shinwoo Griffin Wing has earned for itself a place in the hearts of off string players the world over. Years since the development of the ZanNavi, it finally gets an off string treatment in the form of the Griffin Wing. The beautiful clear colored wings are made from rubber, and it's loaded with the same RSS Spacer that comes in the ZanNavi 2. Just by flipping the spacer around, you can adjust the gap to suit your playing style. At 80 grams, it's not a lightweight by any stretch of the imagination, but for off string yo-yos this is an ideal size and weight for stability and spinning power. Removing the side caps will drop the total weight down to 73 grams. Surprisingly, this actually increases spinning power by moving the center of weight outwards towards the wings, so if you weren't satisfied with the Griffin Wing's spin and weight, you can remedy this quite

title: Griffin Wing 2
content: The highly valued Griffin Wing gets an update with a new response system. Years since the development of the ZanNavi, it finally gets an off string treatment in the form of the Griffin Wing. The beautiful clear colored wings are made from rubber, and it's loaded with the same RSS Spacer that comes in the ZanNavi 2. Just by flipping the spacer around, you can adjust the gap to suit your playing style. At 80 grams, it's not a lightweight by any stretch of the imagination, but for off string yo-yos this is an ideal size and weight for stability and spinning power. Removing the side caps will drop the total weight down to 73 grams. Surprisingly, this actually increases spinning power by moving the center of weight outwards towards the wings, so if you weren't satisfied with the Griffin Wing's spin and weight, you can remedy this quite easily. Naoto Okada used this yo-yo to claim the 4A

title: Loop
content: *This product does not have a package Shinwoo's representative looping yo-yo, great for beginners and those looking to give looping a try. This is Shinwoo's model for general looping practice, with the most straightforward name possible. It has a raider shape with a ball bearing, with a starburst response system. The overall settings are very close to the Yomega Raider, and for a low price that gets you practicing quickly. You aren't likely to find a looping yo-yo with these capabilities for a comparable price. To add further value to your purchase, Shinwoo has included the RSS spacers for a more customizable feel. By flipping over one or both of the spacers so the larger step is facing the bearing, you can increase the gap for less responsive play when you are ready for it. For maintenance, use looping oil for your bearing (sold separately). For beginners, we recommend using the

title: Loop 2
content: Loop 2 is a model in Shinwoo's yo-yo catalog. No further description available.

title: Phantom 1
content: *This product does not have a package It looks so plain, but its ordinary exterior hides its impressive potential. The legendary round shape makes a comeback with some new improvements for string tricks. Inside the plastic body is a metal rim, bringing the total weight up to an average 65 grams for impressive spin. The response pads are very durable, hardly ever requiring replacement. Whether you're looking for a fun yo-yo to throw around casually, or a serious contest model, the Phantom can suit your needs. An homage to the Duncan Freehand's round body, the Phantom feels familiar and comfortable in the hand, and is sure to please fans of that body type. With its similar size and weight, it's as if you can step up the potential of the Freehand without the use of mods. For players looking for the next step in the low-cost, high-quality plastic market, this is the yo-yo for you. Comes

title: Phantom 2
content: *This product does not have a package The next step up from the Phantom 1, the Phantom 2 boasts a reversible response system, Shinwoo's RSS Spacer and a weight boost. The legendary round shape makes a comeback with some new improvements for string tricks. Inside the plastic body is a metal rim, slightly heavier than that of the Phantom 1, for even more spin. The response pads are very durable, hardly ever requiring replacement. Whether you're looking for a fun yo-yo to throw around casually, or a serious contest model, the Phantom can suit your needs. An homage to the Duncan Freehand's round body, the Phantom feels familiar and comfortable in the hand, and is sure to please fans of that body type. With its similar size and weight, it's as if you can step up the potential of the Freehand without the use of mods. For players looking for the next step in the low-cost, high-quality plastic

title: Phantom Pro
content: *This product does not have a package The Phantom 2 with an even heavier body and a dry large bearing. Click here for the regular Phantom 2

title: ProWing 1A
content: A model change for the ProWing, now available in 1A flavor. The ProWing 1A is the new baby brother of the splendid delrin off string ProWing 4A. As the name indicates, the ProWing 1A takes the general design of the ProWing 4A and scales it down and revises it to suit string tricks. The ProWing's central hub area is practically unchanged, so only the body shape is different from its bigger brother. The delrin still gives a smooth-as-silk texture we've all come to love. Sized down, with a thicker outer rim for greater spin and stability, the ProWing 1A also has a low edge and inverse round shape for greatly improved string play. Of course, the gap has been widened for a bind-required response, and the 1A now sports a curved bearing for top performance out the box. The axle has been modified to fit the inner diameter of the bearing exactly. There may be a bit of wobble during play, but if

title: ProWing 4A
content: Shinwoo's first all-plastic body off string yo-yo. When you think of Shinwoo's off string yo-yo, surely you imagine the Griffin Wing, which was famously used by Naoto Okada in 2009 to win the 4A world championship. The ProWing 4A is designed to surpass the potential of the Griffin Wing, in a body made entirely from plastic. Despite the fact that it's machined from delrin, the ProWing 4A is shockingly cheap. You can feel the smoothness of the design through the string as you play with it. The ProWing 4A is loaded with the same proprietary response system used in Shinwoo's high end Zen series, and it works surprisingly well for off string play; even when the yo-yo's spin weakens, it will still return to your hand and bind tightly. Another special facet of this design is the body size. ProWing 4A is a little smaller than other off string yo-yos, which makes it supremely easy to control,

title: SW101 Tire Yo-Yo
content: A low-cost plastic yo-yo in the shape of a car tire/wheel. Is it a wheel or a yo-yo? The center axle has a plastic spool (not a fixed axle), so this cheap budget yo-yo sleeps like a top class yo-yo. If the yo-yo doesn't respond to your satisfaction, simply wrap the string 2-4 times around the plastic spool. This yo-yo does not come apart.

title: SW301
content: Auto-return AND lights, the SW301 is a simple yo-yo that combines two useful functions. Auto-return makes the yo-yo return to your hand when it starts to slow down, and the LEDs keep it lit up while the yo-yo spins, making this a fun and easy yo-yo to toss around casually. While many auto-return or light-up models tend to have the gimmick only loaded on one side, it causes unbalance. The SW301 has the auto-return function on one side, and Shinwoo's Fire Circuit on the other, giving both functions and keeping the yo-yo better balanced (one side is 29 grams, the other is 27). Thanks to this and its functions, it's easy to recommend to beginners; making even easy tricks look impressive with its lights. Although the lights are only on one side of the yo-yo, the body is clear, so you can see it from any angle. The red LED is very bright, making it easy to stand out in a crowd. The weight

title: Techno
content: *This product does not have a package Shinwoo's Techno can easily be seen in the hands of a beginner or professional player. Maximum performance for a minimum cost. The Techno has a traditional round shape, with a low edge to make it easier to hit difficult string tricks. It is loaded with a ball bearing and an inner weight behind the side cap, giving it both stability and spinning power. Thanks to Shinwoo's original response system, almost no maintenance is required, letting you concentrate on your practice instead of taking care of your yo-yo. If the yo-yo's response weakens, you can apply a little bit of oil to the bearing. Some models have loose side caps, which may cause some instability during play. The silver version has a plastic body with a metal coat; it is not a full metal body. For a light-up version of the Techno, check out the Fire Techno.

title: Techno 2
content: An upgrade from the original Techo, the Techno 2 has a new body shape to stave off sleep loss to extremes. *This product does not have a package The Techno 2 is an improvement on the original design with a new shape to take over the reigns from the Phantom to be Shinwoo's new flagship string trick yo-yo. To put it bluntly, this is the ultimate beginner's yo-yo. The price, weight, stability, and ease with which it handles tricks is unmatched. From simple basic tricks to more advanced barrel rolls and even more complicated moves. We especially want to see the old Hyper Yo-Yo Boomers get ahold of this model. Old tricks that used to be a real challenge are much easier now, you can feel just how far yo-yos have come in the past decade. If the yo-yo stops responding properly, you can just replace the Shinwoo response pad. You shouldn't need to replace it often, thanks to its durable materials

title: ZanNavi2
content: *This product does not have a package ZanNavi is the new multi-style offering from Shinwoo, using its new original response system. This is Shinwoo's representative multi-style yo-yo. The outer rim is made from durable rubber, ready for rough play. It can even be used as an undersized off string yo-yo. Its body is between a normal off string and 1A yo-yo in size, but it has a wide catch zone which is effective for both styles of play. The response system is incredibly durable, reducing maintenance to just replacing strings. The loaded RSS spacer allows you to regulate the gap just by flipping it around, so you can find the best setting for you. The ZanNavi2 is a long-lasting model accommodating a wide array of styles of play. It's ready to keep you spinning for years to come. Comes with a rubber ball, one RSS spacer, and one string.

content: *This product does not have a package The next development in the ZanNavi line, incorporating Shinwoo's reversible response system. This is Shinwoo's representative multi-style yo-yo. The outer rim is made from durable rubber, ready for rough play. It can even be used as an undersized off string yo-yo. Its body is between a normal off string and 1A yo-yo in size, but it has a wide catch zone which is effective for both styles of play. title: ZanNavi3 Heavy
content: *This product does not have a package The multi-style ZanNavi3 puts on some weight. This is a heavy version of the ZanNavi3, for the discerning multi-style yo-yo player. The rubber wings are harder and have a slick look, similar to plastic for a different visual appeal from the original. Add a little oil to improve the response for beginners, or keep the oil-less setting for more advanced players. Comes with all the same goodies as the ZanNavi3, for all your yo-yoing needs. Click here for the regular ZanNavi3

title: Zen 1
content: *This product does not have a package Shinwoo's first full metal yo-yo conceals its impressive abilities with a low price. The now-famous ZanNavi and Griffin Wing designs get a full metal release. The price is low, but at 65 grams, the Zen 1 provides plenty of weight to prove its worth. If you wish, you can increase the weight by installing rubber weights on the sides, pushing the weight up to 67 grams. The Zen 1 uses Shinwoo's reversible response pads, with a corrugated starburst pattern on one side (the default setting) and a flat underside, giving you the option to choose a setting that's right for you. The small body is well suited for intricate string tricks, with its eye-catching tapered straight shape. With its customizable feel, there are so many possibilities with this yo-yo. This is Shinwoo's masterpiece. Comes loaded with reversible response pads and a single string. *Due to

title: Zen 1 Rebuilt
content: The original Zen 1 gets an overhaul with a wide gap, and the sharp body shape gives way to sexy curves. *This product does not have a package The classic Zen 1 gets a wide, curved renewal with the Zen 1 Rebuilt. A total departure from the sharp edges of the original Zen 1, the Rebuilt features a round wing shape. The shape almost seems to match up with the Zen 4 and 6, and is similar to Turning Point's Positron, or the YoYoJoker Uroboros. Even the flat standard bearing has been switched out for a 10-ball rounded one, bringing out the full potential of this yo-yo. The yo-yo has almost a soft feeling during play, and has stability that is sure to please everyone. You might wonder why Shinwoo is making such a radical change to an old classic, but with the first throw you'll find yourself nodding in approval. If you're looking for the reason the Zen series is such a beloved lineup, look no

title: Zen 2
content: Zen 2 *This product does not have a package

title: Zen 3
content: Low price and high quality is the name of the game with Shinwoo's Zen. the Zen 3 is Korean maker Shinwoo's third full metal release, in the pursuit for the ultimate metal yo-yo at the lowest possible price. Known for acheiving this with with other materials, Shinwoo is now applying their expertise to a full metal body. The round stepped body gives a spin you wouldn't expect in this price range. The response system is the same as the ZanNavi3, Phantom 2 and Griffin Wing 2, Shinwoo's own reversible response pads, with a corrugated starburst pattern on one side (the default setting) and a flat underside, giving you the option to choose a setting that's right for you. Because of the ease of configuration, this is a good model for newcomers to the full metal market and aren't quite sure yet what settings work best for them. Give all the settings a try, just to see what works best for you.

title: Zen 4
content: Its simple design makes the Zen 4 easy to handle and easy to love. *This product does not have a package This is the 4th model from Shinwoo's low price/high quality Zen series. This model has forgone any fancy gimmicks or unique body shapes for a simple but effective approach. It uses the same response pads as the Zen 1, 2 and 3, giving you the option of which side to use for adjustable response. It is also loaded with a rounded 10-ball bearing for maximum potential out the box. Its round body features a very low edge, for even less sleep loss than you'd expect. The shape somehow combines the soft feeling of a round body with the sharpness of a straight shape. For those who don't care for the feeling from an H-profile, you should give the Zen a try: it won't hurt your wallet. Coms with two reversible replacement response pads and a string to get you started. Due to the manufacturing

title: Zen 5
content: The Zen 5 sports a pronounced inverse round shape that looks like a capitol "U" Shinwoo's Zen series sits in a very small niche amongst the many full metal yo-yos out there, as it provides high performance for very reasonable prices, making the Zens an excellent value. The secret to its success is the heavy outer rim and inverse round shape. This gives the Zen a great amount of spin and keeps string loss to a minimum. To improve on this, the Zen 5 even sports a 10-ball bearing for smoother play and top performance right out the box. Despite its extreme shape, the Zen 5 fits surprisingly well in your hand, giving more an interesting sensation than anything else. With its great performance and low price, it's hard not to include the Zen 5 in your competition arsenal. *There may be some unevenness or smudging in the anodizing or printing on the yo-yo.

title: Zen 6
content: You'll slowly find yourself falling for the unique shape of the Zen 6. With a polygonal shape similar to hspin's Cut, the Zen 6 isn't just a uniquely shaped yo-yo; it's a tough model designed to give you impressive sleep times. Slightly heavier than the Zen 4 and 5, the Zen 6 also incorporates a super low edge, giving you the kind of spin and stability you wouldn't expect in this price range. You'll quickly realize the true value of the Zen 6 as you link trick after trick with just one throw! The Zen 6 comes fitted with a concave 10-ball bearing, ensuring that the specs are maxed out right from the box. Despite carrying the same name, each member of the Zen series is a unique and amazing yo-yo; it seems like the only thing they have in common is their great cost-performance. There may be some markings on the body; this is due to the manufacturing process, and has no effect on play.

title: Zen Star 1
content: Zen Star 1 is part of Shinwoo's Zen line of full-metal yo-yos, originally listed on the Korean maker's own site, swyoyo.com.

title: Zen Star 2
content: Zen Star 2 is part of Shinwoo's Zen line of full-metal yo-yos, originally listed on the Korean maker's own site, swyoyo.com.

title: Shiou Messaijin (L.O.E.P!!)
content:
History / About
Shiou Messaijin (獅凰滅砕陣!!, SY-010) references the storyline's Leo Sniper MK-II + Eclipse Ogre team-up finishing move, billed as the culmination of the brand's Size-D-bearing design philosophy. Yoyo performance duo SPINATION (Tommy & Soul) appear in the storybook as cast/performers for this volume — this is a storybook casting credit, not a confirmed product design or commercial collaboration.

title: Shogun
content:
History / About
Billed as the first trimetal design to utilize a cobalt-chromium alloy — a material-science first for the brand, pairing a 7068 aluminum body with a stainless steel midship and cobalt-chromium inner rim.

title: Shortcut
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"After experimenting with new materials and the pinnacle of manufacturing with the Mg cloudstrike and Tiss hummingbird. We are going back to earth with a budget yoyo offering. We want to bring the same yoyofriends quality and performance to everyone.

Shortcut is a yoyo that is great for any level of play. Plenty of power for learning new tricks and combos. Fun and floaty for more advanced player perfecting their craft. Stability that can handle any type of horizontals. Shortcut is meant to be played by everyone.

Usually yoyofriends have less cuts and simplistic lines, however we challenged ourselves this time to have multiple cuts on the yoyo design. This brings out a new kind of aesthetic in our lineup.We named the yoyo shortcut because we believe this yoyo is a shortcut to a higher level of yoyoing for people due to its price, performance and good old fashioned yoyofriends quality. A perfect path to our higher end offerings and showcase what yoyofriends are capable of to all players."

title: Shortcut (2024)
content: AboutThe 2024 Shortcut is a revised edition of the popular original, upgrading from a 7mm axle and Center Track bearing to an 8mm axle and standard concave bearing for improved spin performance and longevity. Specs are otherwise identical to the original, but the hardware refresh makes it a better daily player. Available in an expanded colorway range.

title: Show Pony
content: AboutThe Show Pony is the evolved form of Rain City's original Showgirl design, redesigned by Justin Scott Larson to be slightly wider, larger in diameter, and about 3g lighter. The changes made it faster and more stable while retaining the O-shape feel. Features a LEGO-compatible hub. Performing arts-themed colorways include circus, musical theatre, flow arts, magic, and dance.

title: Showgirl
content: AboutThe Showgirl was Rain City's original organic-shaped throw, designed by a Facebook friend of Jeremy's. Only 150 units were produced before the design was retired in favor of the Show Pony redesign, which made the shape wider, slightly larger, and about 3g lighter.

title: Shuriken
content:
The Shuriken was Throw Down's second aluminum yo-yo. It was an undersized yoyo. The gap was very large for it's size, so they shipped with thick Dif-E-Yo pads. According to the YoYoWiki, "the yo-yo was coated in manganese phosphate and then clear coated." 168 Shuriken's were in the production run. The prototypes had longer spikes.

title: Happo
content: History / AboutHappo is Shuriken's first bi-metal and performance-oriented design, per the YoYoSam listing. It pairs a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims in an H/V-shape profile aimed at power, stability and agility, with a weight distribution that lets it accelerate easily without losing stability. The name comes from the Happo shuriken, an eight-pointed shuriken used by various ninja families of Iga Province. Each yo-yo ships with an extra pair of RSO landing pads (Type 50). YoYoStoreRewind (Japan) also calls it Shuriken's first bi-metal, with a sharp straight shape designed for ease of control; it notes the pad opening is narrower than on other yo-yos, so some slim-size pads fit less easily.

title: Juji
content: History / AboutJuji is a wide-rim mono-metal from Shuriken Yoyos. Per the maker's description relayed by YoYoSam, wide rims usually come with a narrow catch zone, so Juji widens the overall body to give a decently wide catch zone and disperse impact force on return. It weighs 61.75 g, with a wall thickness of about 1 mm in 7068 aluminum and the remaining weight placed in the rims. Japanese retailer YoYoStoreRewind describes it as an oversized (58 mm) flat-rim yo-yo that is chunky in the hand but lightweight, with a narrower effective width than its looks suggest. The logo is a small cross-shuriken artwork on one side. Shuriken's Roppo announcement calls Juji the first of its monometals (oversized and chunky), followed by the slimline Senban.

title: Roppo
content: History / AboutRoppo is described as Shuriken's first performance-focused mono-metal design after the oversized Juji and the slimline Senban. It has a V-shaped profile, weighs 65.3 g and is 46.8 mm wide, and is described as handling a wide range of tricks with decent stability and maneuverability. The name comes from the Roppo shuriken, a six-pointed hira-shuriken. A subtle logo is engraved near the hub. Diego Berini has his own signature colorway with his logo engraved near the hub. YoYoExpert lists it as designed in Hong Kong and released June 2023.

title: Senban
content: History / AboutSenban is described in the YoYoSam listing as the second release by Shuriken Yoyos. It is a slimline unresponsive yo-yo intended as a pocketable everyday-carry model; at 37 mm wide it is meant for practicing control and precision for modern tricks. It stays under 60 g while the 7068 aluminum alloy supplies rim weight for spin power. The name comes from the Senban shuriken (a four-pointed ninja star commonly used by practitioners of Togakure-ryu ninjutsu), and a logo of that star is engraved on the outer rim. It has a matte finish and uses a center track bearing.

title: Shutsujin
content: The Shutsujin is a unique model in W1LD's lineup — a full metal body with polycarbonate side caps oriented toward casual and entertainment play. The PC caps create a hollow feeling that transmits throw movement through the arm, giving the Shutsujin a tactile play experience unlike any other W1LD model. Designed for no-stress casual play without competition pressure.

title: SHY
content: The SHY is the signature model of W1LD team member Hanyang Shen. An H-profile bi-metal with large stainless steel rims for powerful extended spin, the SHY's butterfly logo symbolizes growth and player development. Wide and powerful, with a 48mm trapeze catch zone for easy landing on complex string elements.

title: Shy Ti
content: The Shy Ti is the titanium monometal version of Hanyang Shen's SHY series. At 65g, it is the lightest of the three SHY variants. A short 6mm axle reduces center mass while maintaining the wide, powerful spin character of the platform. Machined from TC4 Grade 5 titanium.

title: Shyness
content: The Shyness is the monometal version of Hanyang Shen's SHY, maintaining the same wide body and H-profile in 6061 aluminum for a slightly lighter and more approachable play feel. Designed to make the SHY platform accessible to players who are still learning to bind, the Shyness retains the powerful spin of its bi-metal sibling at a fraction of the price.

title: Waffle Stomper
content:
History / About
The Waffle Stomper is a novelty yo-yo created by Audrey (AudreySickburn) in collaboration with Seth McNeeley, originating from a running joke in a player profile thread on the YoYoExpert forums. Despite its absurdist origins, players found it genuinely enjoyable to throw. Audrey subsequently released the design as open source on Printables.com, making it freely available for 3D printing by the community. A Titanium Waffle Stomper (Richie Kretzschmar's signature version) was later announced as a separate model in prototype development. A Waffle Stomper-themed shirt collaboration with Throw-Yo Threads was also released in June 2025. Each retail unit ships with a special counterweight.

title: Sigtyr
content: AboutThe Sigtyr occupies the same 57mm × 43mm footprint as the Draupnir but uses broader, more protruding stainless steel rims that add approximately 2g of rim weight (to ~65.5g). The result is a yo-yo tuned for maximum spin time and stability — more than the already-formidable Draupnir — for players who prioritize those qualities over the Draupnir's slightly lighter, more agile feel. Named for a Valkyrie from Norse mythology, consistent with YYR's naming tradition.

title: Silhouette
content:
From One Drop:

"To join the very affordable Intro, we wanted to offer a Side Effect yo-yo that is also sensitive to the economics of the times.  We present: The Silhouette. The play is airy, stable and fast and has a definitive feel in the hand unlike anything we’ve done before.  If you hold it with your eyes closed you’ll know what it is. Here we embrace concave arcs in the catch zone and sport the traditional Side Effect hub in the cup - offering adjustability, durability and the ability to customize at a bargain.

Those of you who were around in the mid 2000’s may notice that we were inspired by a yo-yo made by our friends at I Love Yo-Yo: The Noctu.  It was released in 2009 and it was completely unique. It’s shape is cool and extreme and can hurt when catching it if you get sloppy. We have one in our collection, we consider it a true gem and a treasure from a different era."

title: Silverback King
content:
History / About
The Silverback King is a collaboration between MonkeyfingeR Design and King Yo Star — the first offstring (4A) model from either brand. Four prototype stages preceded release. The Delrin construction keeps it durable through impacts while three finish colors (White, Blue, Orange) show off the material’s natural translucency. Ships with a throw glove, spare pads, three stickers, two Monkey Hanger strings, and two bearings (grooved 10-ball C pre-installed, standard 8-ball C spare). Designed to be accessible to beginners while meeting competition-level expectations.

title: Silvia XP50
content:
History / About
The undersized member of the Silvia series, released alongside the XP54 in early 2018 to directly compare how diameter affects performance and feel. At 50mm it is zippy and pocket-friendly, feeling surprisingly dense and punchy for its size — a small throw with serious spin power. “XP” stands for Experimentation, and “50” identifies the diameter variant. Both models weigh the same 65.5g, making the diameter difference the only variable, by design.

title: Silvia XP54
content:
History / About
The full-size member of the Silvia series, released alongside the XP50 in early 2018. At 54mm it is more competition-oriented than its sibling — wider catch zone, more forgiving on long combos, and more stability for technical play. Both models are identical in weight at 65.5g, making the diameter the sole variable. Together they served as a real-world experiment in how size changes the character of the same design.

title: Sincerity
content: AboutThe Sincerity is described as "one of the finest releases" from AceYo — floaty with an elegant look and feel. Premium 7075 aluminum combined with polished stainless steel rings delivers extreme speeds and spin times for the longest combos. Available in Silver/Gold Ring and Black/Gold Ring.

title: Sinew
content:
About
Sinew is a Performance-line string from Throw-Yo Threads built for durability rather than speed. It blends Trilobal Poly and Bonded Nylon in roughly equal parts, each spun as a separate cord and then combined. The Trilobal's impulse to run is reined in by the nylon, giving a slower, more deliberate feel without becoming Responsive. Expect a stiff break-in period of an hour or two, after which it settles and holds its state for a very long time; it was tested for months on an MR-85 responsive bearing. It debuted as Patreon Project Torsion blend #6 (May 2026) before its public launch on June 4, 2026.

title: Siren
content: AboutThe Siren was a small-batch organic release from Radical Seas, introduced in 2017. Its compact 52mm profile and finger spin hub marked a departure from the brand's oversized H-shape debut, and it sold out quickly after announcement. The demand generated by the original Siren directly led to the wider-production Siren V2 in 2018.The body dimensions of the original Siren are shared with the V2 — the profile and size remained unchanged between versions, with development focused on refining the finger spin hub.

title: Siren V2
content: AboutThe Siren V2 arrived in August 2018 as a broader-production follow-up to the sold-out original Siren. The body dimensions and organic profile remained identical, but the finger spin hub was redesigned for improved performance. Priced accessibly compared to earlier Radical Seas releases, the V2 was positioned as an everyday player — smooth, compact, and well-suited to trick development.Available in Blue and Pink at approximately $50–$85 USD depending on market.

title: SIX
content: AboutThe SIX is Takahiro Iizuka's second signature model, following the Messiah. At 48mm diameter it is 1mm smaller than the already-undersized Messiah, and 42mm wide — one of the smallest-diameter competition metals ever produced by yoyorecreation. The reduction was intentional: Iizuka's hyper-complex technical style benefits from a smaller, faster instrument, and the SIX pushes that concept to its furthest expression. The Messiah 666 (2023) would later merge the DNA of both Iizuka signatures into a bi-metal.

title: Sixth Sense
content:
History / About
The Sixth Sense is Fallen44’s flagship fixed-axle model and the foundation of the brand’s catalog. Hand-turned by Kevin Markie in Charlotte, North Carolina, each piece is made from exotic hardwood and features Fallen44’s proprietary Vortex Response System — spiral cuts around the wooden axle that regulate return without a conventional bearing or silicone pad. The high-wall design facilitates stalls and grinds while keeping the overall profile comfortable and lightweight.
The Sixth Sense has been released in a wide range of wood species and horror-themed laser-etched art editions — including Redrum (red/black spectra birch ply), Scary Tree, Haunted House, Witch, Pumpkin and Ghosts, Planchette, Werewolf, Zombie, Oogieboogie, Jack o’ Lantern, Jason Friday the 13th, Bad Luck Kitty, Fvck Love, Canarywood Crow, Purpleheart, Zebrawood, Olivewood, Kingwood, and Shedua — with stainless steel cap variants available on select wood editions. Each piece is hand-made to order.

title: SK
content:
From One Drop:

"SF + OD = SK

Some new weird company is an anonymous mystery and you're a natural born detective. After some digging and interrogation, you finally figure it out.  Why not join forces and salsa dance with the enigma?

It's that feeling all the time."
