title: SKF Plastic
content: History / AboutSKF (Svenska Kullagerfabriken) of Gothenburg, Sweden is a bearing maker, not a toy company. According to the Yo-Yo Museum, in the mid-1980s it introduced plastic and wooden yo-yos with miniature SKF ball-bearing axles, sold only in Europe. The yo-yo may have been made by Wigart AB of Helsingborg, Sweden, and bears 'ROYO' imprinted in red on the reverse. It was never patented, and the Museum suggests it was a company novelty or advertising item. YoYo Wiki credits SKF with the first ball-bearing axle yo-yos (1984), with a large bearing, narrow gap and riveted halves.The plastic version has flat rims with a hockey-puck profile and hollowed inner faces. A hollow brass axle tube rivets the two halves together over a pre-installed bearing, so it does not come apart. Variations include a bagged version with a header card and a solid SKF-blue band with yellow lettering, versions imprinted with gas station brands, and plain SKF imprints. The Museum exhibit is dated 1984 to 1986.

title: SKF Wheels
content: History / AboutYoYo Wiki lists three SKF yo-yos: Plastic, Wheels and Wooden. The company, Svenska Kullagerfabriken of Gothenburg, Sweden, produced bearing-axle yo-yos in the mid-1980s. No description, specifications or photographs of the Wheels model were found in the sources checked.

title: SKF Wooden
content: History / AboutSKF (Svenska Kullagerfabriken) of Gothenburg, Sweden is a bearing maker, not a toy company. According to the Yo-Yo Museum, in the mid-1980s it introduced plastic and wooden yo-yos with miniature SKF ball-bearing axles, sold only in Europe. The yo-yo may have been made by Wigart AB of Helsingborg, Sweden, and bears 'ROYO' imprinted in red on the reverse. It was never patented, and the Museum suggests it was a company novelty or advertising item. YoYo Wiki credits SKF with the first ball-bearing axle yo-yos (1984), with a large bearing, narrow gap and riveted halves.The wooden version was painted in solid colors and sold in a display box, according to the Museum. It is hollowed out like the plastic version but, unlike it, is a take-apart model.

title: Skyfish
content:
About
Skyfish is Ryuichi Nakamura's first YYR signature model. Positioned as the lightest yoyo in YYR's high-end lineup at 63.5g, it's built for a fast, agile feel. A wide, straight V-shape profile opens the catch zone, while thick, bumped-out stainless steel rims push weight to the rim for spin power without sacrificing lightness.

title: SKYVA
content: About the SKYVAThe SKYVA was designed by Jeffrey Pang, founder of Luftverk Titanium Supply Co., in collaboration with MagicYoYo. It features dual finger spin cups: a primary cup for initial finger spin entry and a secondary cup for locking tricks in place — a then-novel approach to finger spin mechanics. The seamless, injection-mark-free polycarbonate body provides a clean, premium feel unusual for a plastic at this price point. Response is handled by the LuftPAD, developed by Luftverk specifically for this model. The SKYVA became one of MagicYoYo's most celebrated collaborative designs and remained in production for years. Available in Pastel Pink, Pastel Green, Pastel Blue, Clear, Translucent Yellow, Translucent Red, and Translucent Orange.

title: SL1000
content:
History / About
The SL1000 is a purpose-built competition bimetal using 7068 aluminum for its lightweight, rigid body paired with stainless steel rims for maximal rim weighting. The "SL" in the name references the slimmer, more aggressive competition profile. Colorways include "Blackout" and "First Blood," both in a clean military aesthetic consistent with G2's modern naming conventions.

title: Slam Dunk
content:
History / About
The Slam Dunk continues the naming wordplay of the family and brings stainless steel rims to the Dunk profile for the first time, producing significantly greater rim weighting, stability, and spin time versus the monometal originals. Released in 2021, it represents Jake's entry into bimetal territory using the shape that started his brand. The archive section covering the Slam Dunk was not fully accessible at research time — Jake's own archive begins the heading but the content loads dynamically. Further details and colorway documentation are available at jakebullockart.com/yoyo-archive. Secondary market listings describe it as a bimetal and confirm the orange/black colorway among others.

title: Slap Jr
content:
History / About
Slap Jr emerged from a single offhand comment. Randy Shreeves — Jake's oldest friend and, in Jake's words, his "yo-yo life partner" — visited, tried the Slappa SS, loved it, and mentioned it would be cool at the diameter of the Anti-Yo Bapezilla, their shared longtime favorite. That was enough. Jake and Jameson Larkins developed prototypes within months, shrinking the diameter from ~58mm to 52mm. To keep meaningful weight at the smaller size, Jameson fattened the stainless steel rims substantially — producing an extraordinary and possibly unique engineering outcome: the rims now outweigh the entire aluminum body and guts combined. It is, as Jake puts it, "literally majority rim weight, and it shows when you throw it." The 7075 aluminum body (an upgrade from the Slappa SS's 6061) keeps the body light enough for this rim-dominated weight distribution to work. The Trevor Boice and Randy Shreeves signature editions carry the same specs with custom colorways and artwork specific to each player — fittingly, Randy's edition honors the friend whose offhand comment started the whole project.

title: Slappa
content:
History / About
The Slappa is Jake's collaboration with yo-yo designer Jameson Larkins, released in 2022. The design brief was deceptively hard: create a pocketable slimline that played like a real, powerful yo-yo rather than a novelty. The counterintuitive solution was a larger-than-typical diameter (~58mm) combined with a very narrow width (~36mm). The large diameter generates centrifugal force without requiring rim weighting, and the narrow width keeps weight down and the profile pocket-friendly. It succeeded on both counts and cleared the way for an expanded slimline family. The Slappa SS followed as a bimetal version, inspiring the Slap Jr when Randy Shreeves suggested going even smaller. A nickel-plated Slappa variant was produced at the same time as the Nicky Slim (nickel Slim Dunk), both batched together at the nickel plating shop.

title: Slappa SS
content:
History / About
The Slappa SS is the bimetal evolution of the Slappa, again designed with Jameson Larkins. Taking the exact same geometry as the monometal original, it adds stainless steel rims that transform the already powerful slimline into something with exceptional stability and spin time. The design was inspired by the H-Spin Good & Evil, one of Jake's childhood favorites — a similarly bold bimetal slimline that influenced how he thought about weight placement in a narrow form factor. The Slappa SS directly led to the Slap Jr: when longtime friend Randy Shreeves visited, tried the Slappa SS, and offhandedly mentioned it would be cool at Bapezilla-size, Jake and Jameson had prototypes within months.

title: SLASHER 2026
content: About the SLASHER 2026The SLASHER 2026 updates the 2016 original with a 5mm wider body while maintaining virtually the same diameter and weight. The expanded width improves hit rates on string trick elements and adds confidence in rail-based and hop-based combos. "Responsive touch" for reliable trajectory tracking. Outer stainless steel rim construction is retained from the original. $179.99 USD.Colorways: Matte Midnight Navy, Silver.

title: SLASHER
content: About the SLASHERThe SLASHER was sOMEThING's first bi-metal design to position the weight ring at the outer edge of the body rather than the inner rim — a departure from the ANGLAM's inner-rim titanium approach. The outer stainless steel ring maximizes the rim-weighting effect, pushing spin time and gyroscopic stability to a new level within the sOMEThING lineup.

title: SLCK-YWET
content: The SLCK-YWET was a Yoyoexpert.com exclusive.

meta.yya_response: Quad-Fist Response (2 Concentric O-Rings on each side)

title: Sleipnir
content: AboutThe Sleipnir is yoyorecreation's defining model, carrying the signature of Shinya Kido — multiple World 1A Champion and brother of company founder Kengo Kido. Named for Odin's eight-legged horse in Norse mythology, the Sleipnir introduced a step-straight profile that became influential across the industry. Its 57mm diameter and 65g weight established a benchmark for competition feel that persisted for years.The design was revisited in 2014 with rounded step edges and updated engravings. Limited editions include a Christopher Chia signature run and an undersized gold edition at 66% of standard size. The Sleipnir remains in production and is widely considered one of the most important yo-yos in modern competitive history.

title: Slim Dunk
content:
History / About
Jake describes the Slim Dunk as "being a band coming off a surprise hit debut album." He had zero plans for a second yo-yo when the Dunk took off. The concept arrived during a fly-fishing trip in northern Pennsylvania: chatting with Drew Tetz from a cabin toilet, Jake got the suggestion to "chop shop" the Dunk — remove the inner bump and slim it to the width of a Duncan Freehand. He loved it instantly, texted CJ Atkinson from that same toilet mid-poop, and got an immediate yes. CJ suggested the name Slim Dunk on the spot. Jake laughs that it took him weeks to realize "Slim" was a play on "Slam" as well. Having learned from the Dunk's two-run sellout, he ordered 600 pieces at once — still his largest single run ever. The tiffany blue prototype arrived June 30, 2020, and was immediately approved with zero changes. Jake regrets not running that colorway for production, thinking at the time it was important to keep prototypes visually distinct, which he now calls "stupid." The main drop on August 17 featured 20 distinct colorways including culturally referential names: Bape (Light Green/Light Blue), Halloween (Black/Orange), Ninja Turtle (Light Green/Brown), Fluch (Pink/Black), Eetsit (Brown/Silver), Redbull (Light Blue/Silver), Pyro (Red/Orange). Jake attempted to ship every Slim Dunk disassembled inside recycled bubble mailers as an environmental gesture — removing the axle, wrapping each half separately, shipping flat. His partner Mikhaila helped with every order. He later acknowledged this had a net zero environmental impact once global air freight was factored in, but finds it funny to look back on. The Nature Series colorways (October 2020) were intended to be more ambitious — a tortoiseshell acid wash, a CJ-inspired colorway for his wrestling persona "The Whisper," and a camo pattern. The factory delivered three basic two-color splashes instead. Jake pivoted, grouping them as Earth, Water, and Fire. They were the first and last splash-anodized Dunks ever released publicly. The Whisper Edition was eventually executed properly: raw Slim Dunks sent to a USA anodizing shop, blasted and anodized to a dark blue/gunmetal with laser engraving, celebrating CJ's 4-year wrestling anniversary. The Nicky Slim (nickel plated) was a quiet release of leftover raw Slims sent to the nickel shop alongside Slappas, appearing about 18 months after the original drop.

title: Slingshot
content:
History / About
The Slingshot uses a reversed bimetal construction — a stainless steel body with 6061 aluminum rims. This is the inverse of the typical bimetal where aluminum forms the body and heavier metals form the rims. The result is a significantly different weight distribution and play feel compared to standard bimetals: the heavier material is distributed throughout the body rather than concentrated at the rim, giving the Slingshot a more planted, connected feel on the string rather than the floaty-yet-stable character of conventional bimetals.

title: SlipStream
content: AboutThe SlipStream is a full-sized stainless steel model inspired by the Damascus FS, offering the unique weight character of steel construction at a lower price point than Damascus. Its classic V-shape profile and steel weight distribution deliver fast, stable, and linear play with minimized air resistance.

title: Sliver
content:
From MK1:

"In the world of yoyo companies, new alliances and collaborations appear as if overnight, but the real work happens over months and sometimes years beforehand. This yoyo is the product of such a collaboration, between @throwspiral and @mk1yoyos.

The “Sliver” was created out of the need to make a better performance slimline that challenges the player without limiting them. We carefully chose which aesthetics to bring in to the design, including an expansive flat cup and the signature Spiral rim groove in the face, and a faceted inverse round shape in the profile to reduce string drag. The slim form factor makes the Sliver an exceptional daily companion.

Sliver creature art by Sheyenne Smith. Box layout and design by Evelyn “Vote Checkbox”."

title: Bounce
content: History / AboutPer YoYoExpert (Nov 2018), the Bounce is the first budget model from Smashing, a full-size yoyo with a wide profile and thick rims, recommended for 1A and 3A. Released 2 November 2018.

title: Float
content: History / AboutPer Smashing (posted on YoYoExpert, Oct 2018), the Float was made with the Scales yoyo podcast, with 100 percent of proceeds going to send Andrew Bergen to the 2018 World Yo-Yo Contest in Shanghai and to sponsor other players. Jordan Blofeld designed it to Bergen's specification. Released 12 October 2018; restocked December 2018.

title: Interlagos
content: History / AboutThe Interlagos is a Smashing YoYo Company model, reviewed by Nate on the YoYoExpert forum in September 2017 and listed among Smashing's yoyos by Jordan Blofeld in 2018. Specs not found.

title: Kubrick
content: History / AboutPer YoYoExpert, the Kubrick was a prototype that remained unrealized during Smashing's active period. Jordan of OPYOYOS conceived three designs and a team vote chose the Kubrick. Its goal was a satisfying experience for its size rather than top performance. Raf, a team member who loves cinema, inspired the name from Stanley Kubrick's wide-lens style. It was released through YoYoExpert in October 2023 as a 7075 aluminum yoyo.

title: Monocle
content: History / AboutThe Monocle is a Smashing YoYo Company model. Founder Jordan Blofeld listed it among the company's yoyos in a November 2018 YoYoExpert forum post, and it was reviewed by Nate in September 2017. A SLVRANDBLK-colorway Monocle appeared in a May 2016 for-sale thread, which conflicts with YoYoNews calling Poppet (July 2016) the first release. Specs not found.

title: Pip
content: History / AboutThe Pip is a Smashing YoYo Company model listed among its yoyos by Jordan Blofeld in a 2018 YoYoExpert forum post. Specs and release date not found.

title: Poppet
content: History / AboutPer YoYoNews (Steve Brown, 5 July 2016), the Smashing YoYo Company is the brainchild of UK collector and player Jordan Blofeld, possibly the first UK-based yoyo company. Poppet was its first release, manufactured in China with an ethically run small engineering shop, and went on sale Sunday 17 July 2016. Specs: 54 mm diameter, 42 mm width, 64 g, 4.45 mm gap, 19mm slim pads, 7075 aluminium. Price was 65 GBP for solid colors and 70 GBP for fades and splashes.

title: Spectacle
content: History / AboutThe Spectacle is a Smashing YoYo Company model that Jordan Blofeld included in a photo list of the company's yoyos in a November 2018 YoYoExpert forum post. No further details found.

title: Titanium Float
content: History / AboutPer Smashing (posted on YoYoExpert, March 2019), the Titanium Float is a limited release with the same size and weight as the original Float, redesigned for titanium with a slightly convex flat cup area. It released 9 March 2019 as a Smashing x Scales project.

title: Smoke
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re so excited to present the third instalment of our Monogram Line, the Smoke — our signature model for Coleman Weimer.

Crafted from Delrin and polycarbonate, the Smoke is full of old school organic goodness, and carefully machined to perfection.

This Design Journal was written by Coleman Weimer.

SPECS

Diameter 55.1mmWidth 46.0mmWeight 66.0gMaterial Delrin & Polycarbonate

The Smoke came out of a meeting of practical and philosophical concerns related to my tendency to play yo-yo for the feeling of it over a predetermined result. I tend toward play without a plan and wanted my signature model to embrace its status as a toy and support a free-flow, feeling-based style of play.

A practical intention we decided on early was to design a delrin signature model that owns its status as being "just a toy." I have always prioritized carrying yo-yos that look welcoming over intimidating. I prefer a friendlier shape. This, paired with my prioritization of how a trick feels more than its technicality led to this classically comfortable design — with mileage to handle both long and short string-length trick structures and both slow and fast play.

Smoke reacts to some movement with resistance and other movement with leniency. Hops and redirects are rounded out by the heavier mass of the yo-yo. But, similar to Tyler Vienneau's Yokel, the Smoke is pliant when string is pulled in opposing directions, keeping the player on their toes and holding them to a certain level of accountability.

These dynamics were accentuated by narrowing the width of the yo-yo and adding Cephas-inspired flush polycarbonate caps. Inspired by the elegance of the Snowberry and Crucial Delrin models, I wanted a heavier delrin body to round-off rigid play, while also reminding myself to follow what the yo-yo itself is doing.

Smoke was designed to support an approach to play I have been developing for a few years, inspired by my favorite poet, William Stafford. Smoke as a physical phenomena has a thick presence but also an unpredictable levity and freedom to it. William Stafford once described his poetry writing process as being likened to "smoke's way", which always finds an opening, a way out.

When I play yo-yo, I also find the yo-yo, like words in a poem, presents its own momentum and direction. When I'm receptive the yo-yo leads the dance, meandering through the string, eventually finding it's way out of a sequence. Even if the sequence has been done a million times, the execution always can change. Often the trick begins and ends not by my intent but by some unpredictable sense of pull the yo-yo and string suggest. Smoke facilitates play without agenda, and I am thrilled to get this yo-yo into people's hands.

The Smoke was first designed in May 2023, and went through four prototypes before we landed on what we felt was perfect. While the Smoke is intentionally designed to be as minimal as possible, there are about a dozen under-the-hood design innovations (adapted from previous projects such as the Snowberry and Arctica) that are hidden from the eye, but help it perform as smoothly as it does.

Smokes will be available in White, Black, White/Black, and Black/Clear.

title: Smol
content:
History / About
Atmos Projects’ first release of 2026 and inaugural 1:1 design (diameter-to-width ratio). This is Vladimir Glazkov’s second signature model, following the Hamr. The designers describe it as “playful, light, and inspiring,” engineered for casual play rather than pure performance.
The H-shaped design concentrates over 70% of mass in the rims, enabling sustained spin and quick acceleration despite its compact footprint. According to the creators, “it plays like a mid-sized yoyo” with stability comparable to larger models while maintaining exceptional agility in technical tricks. The design reflects influences from miniature models by YoyoRecreation and A-RT.

title: Smoothie
content: About the SmoothieReleased November 3, 2017, the Smoothie was Kris Toledo's signature model and Crucial's first bi-metal design. Developed collaboratively between Toledo and Crucial founder Paul Yath, the design uses stainless steel rings to push approximately 30% of the total weight to the rims, maximizing stability and spin time. Despite weighing just under 65 grams, YoYoExpert noted it delivers "a beautiful presence on the string," playing fast and stable through extended combos. It features one of Crucial's softest grind finishes and simple engraving. A restock at a lower price point followed in February 2018.

title: Smothers Brothers
content: The Smothers Brothers yo-yo was a branded variant produced during the 1980s as part of Hummingbird's expansion into licensed and co-branded products. This model capitalized on the Smothers Brothers' cultural prominence and represented the company's success in securing major entertainment and retail partnerships.

title: Snack
content:
History / About
The Snack is Recess's first venture into the undersized category — a small, pocketable organic aluminum throw priced at $55. The Snack took Recess's organic design philosophy and shrunk it into a compact package, appealing to players who prefer smaller, nimbler throws for technical tricks. The "Little League" later revisited the undersized concept with modernized dimensions and a shape influenced by the Dressel Designs 5050.

title: Snapdragon
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Snapdragon is our first yo-yo to utilize the new Stem system. It features a 6061 aluminum construction and a large H profile that can accommodate most any play style. All of the first run Stem yo-yos will come stock with a size D bearing, and they are compatible with other bearing sizes using additional Stem bearing seat kits..."

title: Snowangel
content:
History / About

The Snowangel is the third release from Wicked YoYos and the first signature model in the lineup, designed for team player Angel Orozco. The design was specifically engineered to support Orozco’s extensive body tricks — the exceptional 52.75mm width (among the widest in any modern yo-yo) makes it ideal for the body-wrapping, arm-pass, and whip-style tricks central to his play. At 65.9g in 7075 aluminum, it has the mass to keep spinning through complex body trick sequences. The Snowangel was announced and pre-hyped on Instagram before its launch, with the logo designed by artist @kaigamarine. Released in three colorways: Angel Blue, Pink, and Yellow.

title: Snowberry
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

We’re proud to introduce the Snowberry – it’s plastic fantastic.

SPECS

Dia 56.4mmWidth 50.5mmWeight 65.6gMaterial Delrin

Most of our design journals pay a degree of homage to the lineage that precedes it, but a look back in history never made more sense than for the Snowberry. At risk of sentimentality, the significance of our first plastic design lies in the very roots of what we now do at Atmos Projects.

I came into the scene around 2006, a time where design sensibilities were starkly different from what they are now. I was always taken by the design leaders of the era, such as Caribou Lodge, One Drop, and Yoyofactory, but I got started on a steady diet of ball-bearinged plastics – I began throwing in high school with a Duncan Throw Monkey, moved on shortly to the Freehand Zero, and then eventually throws from other brands such as the now-defunct, but eternally amazing Yoyojam. The Patriot, Journey and Lyn Fury featured regularly in my rotations. Another fun fact was that I mainly played 5A for years before I transitioned to 1A, deciding it was what the cool kids did – but my taste for wide and round shapes that were suited for 5A play was forged in those years.

These plastics were perfect for the time. They could take the hits that came with perfecting counterweight tricks, and you didn’t ever have to feel precious with them. And they played so satisfyingly.

In 2007, Paul Yath released the Milk under his brand, Crucial. I never got to own one myself, but took every chance to play with one that belonged to a friend. It shifted my perception of plastics considerably; the machined delrin felt like an altogether different material from injection molded polycarbonate – softer, denser, more refined, and incredibly smooth to the touch. Years later, the One Drop Cabal was released, and again, I was fascinated by what I imagined was a Delrin reincarnation of the Markmont Classic. This time I managed to get my hands on one. 

Sometime last year I doubled down on this Delrin exploration, and managed to acquire a Crucial Cream and Yoyopalace (now Sense) Sphere. In my book they are such joyful designs that are severely underrated.

All that to say – there’s an enormous nostalgic significance that sets the context for our first plastic design.

Sometime in 2021, I started toying with the idea of making a delrin yoyo. The reasons for not doing that as a small boutique gig like ourselves are myriad and endless. But I was keen to try, even if it meant the project ended with a couple of prototypes of a design that didn’t make sense for a larger production.

I began with the Cloudberry’s shape as a reference; this was the most instinctive starting point, given its big, round shape that isn’t identical to but reminiscent of the Milk and the Patriot. It was also a natural progression of our exploration of materials in the Berry line – two monometals (in the Cloudberry and Thunderberry), then bimetal (in the Stormberry), and now a fully delrin iteration. It features very similar features, such as the schmoove-step.

The diameter was kept to 56.4mm, which is consistent throughout the Berries, but we increased the width to 50mm. The idea was to keep the weight distribution similar to the Berry series, and the playfeel in the same zippy, floaty and light-stable range. 

One thing we were insistent on was maintaining a fully plastic exterior. Modern machined plastic designs generally have an exposed metal insert in the hub, which are at times adapted to aid tricks like finger spinning. But what was entirely arresting about the Crucial Milk was its pure white structure. ditto with the cream and the sphere. We felt a metal nub in the hub would be a distraction, a visual disruption to an otherwise full and uninterrupted surface.

In later prototypes, we configured the spacer inserts to sit embedded within the delrin hub, and then be concealed by a small machined delrin cap, which features the “halo” groove signature to the Fruitbowl series. We worked with our machinist to experiment with multiple spacer constructions, and finally settled on one.

(L-R; early prototypes to final production version)

Initial prototypes came in, which made for a very exciting day. Prototype I was a wobblefest. Prototype II had a small, unobtrusive metal nub; it played more solid and was slightly smoother on string; Prototype III was full-delrin, was degrees floatier and lighter, but had a bit of vibe. I sent Prototype II and III to Coleman and Evgeniy. I preferred Prototype III, but wanted to triangulate my own thoughts with their feedback. After some play, their responses leaned towards the fully-delrin version. Evgeniy referred to it as the “monolith proto”, which I thought was cool, and mentally I referred to it as that from then on.

Coleman put the Snowberry through its paces in his own singular way, with flowy, relaxed combos that feel more like an art form than anything.

https://player.vimeo.com/video/710986144?h=e5318ce48c&app_id=122963

To fix the slight vibe, we adjusted the hub and spacer construction again for tighter and more secure fit against the delrin body, and they came out playing great. The production version also has a bit more weight – plastic designs have a tiny bit of variance weight-wise, but the Snowberry sits around 65.6g.

It’s very slick on the string, and has the classic Atmos lightness of feel. it has the same fluffy-oomph of the Cloudberry, but is even softer.

It’s an unapologetically wide and fatty organic, it’s very stable for a plastic, and spins long enough for a modern trickset. It won’t beat a new bimetal at sleep length if you’re counting seconds, but if you’re genuinely thinking about trick capability – have you seen what Evgeniy has done with it?

https://player.vimeo.com/video/761468776?h=9188a26ea3&app_id=122963

The modern market can feel like an arms race sometimes. This is a wholly positive thing – variety and availability of quality designs are great, and it’s never been a better time to be a player. Saturation generally breeds innovation and creativity.

In a crowded space, the ones I’ve personally found inspiring have a quietly oddball quality to them; the CLYW Arctic Circle 2, the A-RT 420, a-rt x sf dk, and the RSO Spaceship ES sit amongst our favorites; and amongst those we produce, the Noah, Abel, Fruitloop and Goji. It’s not a stretch to say all these designs are an imperfect fit for the median player who looks for least error, but in play they just make me go, oh.

The Snowberry sits in that pocket for us; it recaptures feelings of uniqueness and nostalgia, and also an excitement of old.

The Snowberry is a plastic yoyo — it’s plastic fantastic. It’s a thank-you note to its plastic forebears that kickstarted many yoyo journeys. It spins incredibly well, it feels slick and smooth on the string. It can take a tumble, it’s soft in the hand, it’s the one you chuck in your bagpack and bring on a hike, it’s the one you pull out to teach your younger cousin how to yoyo. it’s one for all seasons.

It feels familiar, like throwing snowballs in January.

title: Loop Spinner
content:
About
The Loop Spinner is the debut yo-yo from Sōchí Company, designed as the signature model for Asia Pacific 2A Champion Yi Cheng Hao. Constructed from polycarbonate with a fixed gap and interchangeable metal spacers, it targets the competitive 2A market with consistent snap return and longer spin times than most loopers. The removable cap system allows quick colorway customization, and the model ships ready for competition straight out of the box. Colorways include WYYC 2023 Edition, Orange/White Cap, Black/Clear Cap, and Clear Red.

title: Loop Spinner LED
content:
About
The Loop Spinner LED is a variant of Sōchí's signature 2A throw with a factory-installed LED light kit affixed to one side. The kit adds approximately 5 grams over the standard model, adjusting the feel for players who prefer a slightly heavier looper. Available in nine translucent and clear colorways, the illuminated yo-yo produces visible trails during competition freestyles under stage lighting. The LED assembly is self-contained and does not interfere with the core polycarbonate construction or fixed-gap system.

title: Method
content:
About
The Method is a collaborative release from Unparalleled and Sōchí Company, designed as the signature everyday throw for Korean player Park Junsang. Machined from 7068 aluminum in an H-profile, it serves as a casual counterpart to Park's competition-level bimetal Seiji — same geometry, same player DNA, none of the pressure. Released in Green, Aqua, Olive, and an Aqua/Green Fade WYYC edition, the Method retailed at $44.99 and reflects Sochi's strategy of bringing accessible competition geometry to the broader community.

title: Socius
content: History / About6061/stainless retail model tuned for Shion Araya's competition play.

title: Solaris
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

Say hello to the Solaris – the aluminum reimagination of our flagship titanium model, the Polaris.

SPECSDiameter 55.1mmWidth 48.9mmWeight 66.8gMaterial 6061 al

In January, we released the Polaris – a new flagship titanium model that was designed to optimize for fluid power, a specific type of playfeel that combines agility and smooth motion, with enough stability and power for any modern trickset. In other words, a model that had everything on spin power and stability that you could want, but was still amenable to a player’s touch and control.

The result of the Polaris was a model that had a very, very comfortable heft – and as subjective and controversial as the term is, the Polaris plays somewhat floaty despite its weight. The Polaris quickly became an internal favorite – and while there’s some obvious and natural bias there, if we had to restart our entire Weatherman Design Line from scratch, the one model we’d keep as our brand cornerstone would actually be the Polaris.

By virtue of the experimental nature of the Weatherman Line, many of the designs that sit under that umbrella naturally fit the category of one-and-dones – the Khuno is a perfect example of that. It was a valuable proof of concept as the world’s first Side Effects-enabled bimetal – as a case study in weight distribution, it showed modular adjustment of mass could yield interesting and educational results for those that tinker. But beyond that, we were unconvinced that the model needed to live on in a sustained way.

Quite conversely, the Polaris does not sit within that category. After the Polaris was released to the general public, the conversation quickly evolved into reimagining its essential features into an aluminum counterpart that could exist as a mainstay in our design lineup – an accessible, simplified design that best represented Atmos’ design ethos and philosophies – perhaps what the newly released Butterball has been to our body of work in the organic space.

We set off to work, using the Polaris as our keystone, and sketched out a draft of our first prototype. The most immediate physical changes are a +0.9mm increase in width, a +0.2mm increase in diameter, and a reduction of mass by 0.7g. The thought here was to decrease overall mass while redistributing the balance across a larger form factor, which would lead to lighter, more powerful play. Something really valuable we’ve learned by working on projects such as the Ekta, Cloudberry and Polaris is using diameter and width adjustments as an effective substitute for mass – and by consequence, how to make heavier yoyos play a lot lighter than their numbers would suggest.

The Ekta sits at 67.3g on paper, but it feels more like a 65-66g design in play; the same could be said of the Polaris. The gap between measured specification and a player’s experience is the space we have enjoying operating in, and is where a lot of the magic happens.

The first prototype we made turned out to be about 75% of what we were hoping and expecting it to be. The Solaris felt nice, full and comfortable in the hand, and the subtle cuts and minimalist lines came out really nicely. It doesn’t feel indulgently large – the 48.9mm in width feels very natural and proportionate to its form factor.

Playwise, however, it felt slightly lacking – even in conversations with the team, it was difficult to really put a finger on what was missing. It’s in moments like this that we hard work to find the vocabulary for experience – and it was particularly difficult to do here. It had a certain hollowness to its play, and just felt very middle of the road. For many of its good traits – such as power and stability – it lacked the same fullness in playfeel that was embodied by the Polaris.

When it comes to prototypes like these, that sit in the 75%-90% zone of completeness, the most essential tweaks are almost always under-the-hood. They don’t lie in diameter and width adjustments – what helps the most is a light touch.

We went into our CAD archives and pulled out various blueprints, and studied alterations in weight distribution we’ve made through quite nearly a hundred prototyping rounds in the past – and finally zoned in on a specific fix via mass redistribution, while keeping overall mass unchanged. We also threw in a few more quality-of-life adjustments, such as rounding off the angle close to the response step, which ensures a smoother play experience, and softened a few lines across the silhouette of the body.

With the Solaris, you feel its weight on initial throw – but once it gets into motion, it feels a lot more like a 64-65g design – it runs across your string with ease.

This is entirely subjective, of course, but beyond the Polaris as a design reference – we personally feel the Solaris shares some qualities with the Cloudberry. It has a fullness about it – it doesn’t feel overly airy or frail – it has some genuine punch. It’s powerful and spins for days, and you really feel this when it returns to hand… We’re always surprised by how much spin there is left even after a longer, technical trick.

It takes after the Polaris in playfeel entirely. It’s a stretch to say it plays light, but it has a really easy and amenable cadence and rhythm. While it has all the technical capability you could ask for, we suspect this might most appeal to rhythmic, flow-centric playstyles.

The name Solaris pays homage not only to Polaris, which is its design forebear, but also the Weatherman Line. It etymologically references the sun – a large, floating body of great gravity – and keeps with our tradition of using natural terminology under the Weatherman umbrella. On a lighter note, we’ll eventually run out of names that have “ari” embedded in them – but today is not that day.

The Solaris is part of our effort at Atmos Projects to develop simplified, minimalist flagships in our design lines. The first of that initiative is the Butterball – which was released a few months ago, and is likely the best received organic we’ve released – and we’ve put forth quite a number.

The Solaris serves that same purpose for our W-shaped models, and we can’t wait to hear what you think.

title: Solid
content:
History / About
From the first second I threw our DR3I titanium prototype I fell in love with its dimensions. The slightly undersized diameter combined with the slim profile and light weight is such a nice combination. It feels sturdy, reliable and isn’t prone to tilt, it just feels solid. This inspired us to delve deeper into this and create a yoyo which oozes these values. What is more down-to-earth than a good ol’ mono-metal aluminum yoyo?
No fancy shape experiments – just a robust and slick organic shape. No dimples, plateaus, grooves, lips – just material where it’s needed. No super short axles that get lost in the infinity of space time. No special bearing or pad sizes, the industry standard shall do. No splash, dots, spray, sparkle, wash, fade with rainbow colours – straight up grey. This is our new yoyo: Solid. It doesn’t fuck around.

title: Solstice (Prototype)
content:
About
Solstice is a G Squared Yoyos bimetal prototype with a 6061 body and stainless steel rims, G19 pads, and a G2 Ripper bearing.

title: Solvent
content: AboutSolvent is wound from 100% spun polyester in the Throw-Yo Threads Performance family. Normal disposition, moderate velocity, and moderate shelf life offer a no-frills performance string with a slightly coarser feel. Available in monocolor only.

title: Somersault
content: AboutThe Somersault is Yoyofriends' first foray into 4A off-string yo-yos, directed by Tony Sung. The extra-wide 65mm body and middle inner rim–focused weight distribution improve landing consistency for banger tricks, while the POM construction provides smooth grind performance ideal for whip combos.

title: BB
content: History / AboutBB is the first slim-line (narrow) yo-yo from Somewhere Designed Yoyos. It returns to the old-school slim yo-yo with a lowered edge and adjusted shape so it sits on the string easily despite the narrow width. It is barrel-polished.

title: Somewhere
content: History / AboutSomewhere is the first release of Somewhere Designed Yoyos, a mono-metal of about 60.7 g that combines light weight with stable spin. The brand concept is that "everything is designed somewhere," and the debut model carries the brand name as a flagship and a wish to become a classic. Some colorways are barrel-polished (Bronze is a direct-shop exclusive) while Orange is polished.

title: System Corp.
content: History / AboutSystem Corp. is an H-profile yo-yo with grooves cut into the rim and a sandblasted surface, weighing 63 g. The name draws on Mallsoft, a vaporwave subgenre, and on the idea that building yo-yo tricks is itself creating a system. The initial throw feels slightly heavy but the low actual weight makes long sessions less tiring.

title: Sorbet
content: About the SorbetThe Sorbet is a collaboration between Crucial and Paragon Yoyos, a Southern California brand led by Eric Ngu — a longtime Crucial team member. Designed as a complement to The Milky, the Sorbet features a clear polycarbonate body with aluminum weight rings for a lightweight feel paired with stability and strong spin power. YoYoExpert describes it as having "a sharper, more performance-driven profile geared toward high-pressure play" that "plays light and quick on the string, yet powerful and steady through long combos." It represents Crucial's hybrid design language extended into a collaborative format.

title: Southpaw Leo Sniper
content:
History / About
Southpaw Leo Sniper is internally identical to the Leo Sniper MK-II, finished in electroless-nickel plating (plated at a Fukui factory) for a left-handed-headgear character tie-in nicknamed "Southpaw."

title: Southside
content: Signature model for young Czech player Maty Držmíšek. A robust, broader bimetal with substantial stainless steel rings. The organic shape balances competition performance with comfortable casual play. The Matte Cream colorway was designed in collaboration with fellow Czech team member Kryštof Nosek.

title: Sovereign
content:
From One Drop:

"The Sovereign is our first all titanium yo-yo. The design takes advantage of the strength of titanium by allowing most of the weight to be placed at the rim. You'll also notice that it is a more curvy shape than we have done in the past.

The first 50 are numbered and released with some special things. It came with special packaging, custom Intentus string from yoyoGstring, and a black Novus to hold the extra parts."

title: Spaceship
content:
History / About
Spaceship is a sci-fi-narrative titanium release ("Nactaria" fiction) and precursor to RSO's later Starship model. Packaged in a CNC-machined delrin capsule with a USB drive containing a custom font/alien-language key. Concept and art by Jason Week. 40 units, raw titanium only.

title: Spartans Spin
content:
History / About
The Spartans Spin is a 7068+SS bimetal with likely Ohio State University team connections — the "Spartans" name and "Team Edition" colorway suggest an institutional collaboration or tribute. Michigan State University's teams are the Spartans; alternatively this could reference a yo-yo team. Full background not documented in available sources. Uses the same 7068+SS construction as the SL1000 and Loadout SR.

title: Speedaholic
content: C3's second plastic yo-yo after the Alpha Crash, the Speedaholic became a landmark budget throw. Developed with input from the C3 competition team who acted as test pilots, its organic polycarbonate shape is wider than the Alpha Crash for improved stability. Proved a sub-$15 plastic could compete with metals costing multiples more, making it one of the most celebrated value yo-yos ever produced.Evolved into the Speedaholic XX (2020) and further variants. First look published on YoYoNews August 6, 2013. Price: $10–$15.

title: Speedaholic FX
content: Based on the Speedaholic XX, the FX adds machined precision polycarbonate body paired with an aluminum alloy rim (not stainless steel) for fingerspin specialization. The aluminum rim provides pleasant lightness and fine control while significantly improving fingerspin duration. Positioned between the standard XX and the MAX bi-metal. Multiple colorways including signature editions. Price: $60–$70.

title: Speedaholic MAX
content: The bi-metal evolution of the Speedaholic XX, applying stainless steel rims to the successful Speedaholic XX polycarbonate platform. The 2022 version introduced a hollow structure between the stainless steel rim and body for enhanced weight distribution. Price: ~$55–$70.

title: Speedaholic MN
content: History / AboutTranslates the XX/MAX H-profile and fingerspin cup into an affordable 6061 monometal.

title: Speedaholic XF
content: History / AboutApril Fools concept made retail: an FX-derived hybrid with fixed flat caps and extra metal hubs, intentionally removing conventional fingerspin capability.

title: Speedaholic XX
content: The groundbreaking sequel to the original Speedaholic, the XX made a massive impact with its H-shape profile, thick rims for great power and spin, and an updated cup designed for fingerspins. Helped fuel the wider community's fingerspin trend. Machined from polycarbonate (unresponsive), available in a massive range of colorways including signature editions for Yamato, Naoto, Sora, and others.A Responsive Edition was also released for beginners. A "New Generation" version with redesigned automatic-locking hubs and deeper fingerspin spots released 2025. Price: $30–$38.

title: Speedaholic XX New Generation
content: Major update to the XX line with redesigned hubs featuring automatic locking systems and deeper fingerspin spots. New thumb grind area. Suitable for beginners learning binding through professionals practicing daily. Price: $30–$38.

title: Speeder
content: About the SpeederThe Speeder established Hiroyuki "Mickey" Suzuki as a dominant force in competitive 1A play and became YoYoJam's top-selling model during the mid-2000s. Its straight body profile minimizes sleep loss, and the heavy brass rim delivers spin power and stability. The hybrid starburst/O-ring response provided a balance between bind reliability and extended play.

title: Speeder 2
content: About the Speeder 2The Speeder 2 updates the original Speeder with Triton-grade polycarbonate for increased durability and smoother spins. At 63.8 grams it is notably lighter than its predecessor, enabling faster play that suits Hiroyuki Suzuki's speed-focused competitive style. The brass rim weight retention ensures competitive spin times. Championship editions were produced for the 2011 World YoYo Contest.

title: SPEEDER REVIVAL
content: About the SPEEDER REVIVALThe SPEEDER REVIVAL revisits Hiroyuki Suzuki's classic YoYoJam-era Speeder signature, this time produced under sOMEThING. The original's hybrid plastic + metal construction is retained but upgraded: brass inserts are replaced with broader 6061 aluminum rims for more balanced weight distribution and enhanced spin power. Rounded V-shape profile. $89.99 USD.Colorways: Hot Pink with Hot Pink Rings, Yellow with Yellow Rings.

title: SpeedMaker
content: About the SpeedMakerThe SpeedMaker reproduces the Speeder's successful profile in a pure POM plastic body, making Hiroyuki Suzuki's design accessible at a lower price point. Without metal rims it is notably lighter, but the adjustable gap and hybrid response system retain the Speeder's characteristic play. It served as an entry point for many players into advanced string trick yo-yos.

title: Spider Man
content: About the Spider ManThe Spider Man is the undersized model in King Yo Star's 2011 debut lineup, measuring just 48.14 mm in diameter while maintaining an H-profile for a wide catch zone. Thick rims generate substantial spin time. Designed for quick, intricate string tricks. Features a sharp spider logo motif.

title: Spike-Fly
content:
History
The Spike-Fly was a made-to-order multi-style variant of the Dif-Fly, produced around 2003–2004. Frank Difeo extended the axle section to accommodate YoYoJam spin top bearing tips on both sides of the yo-yo. With tips pressed in, the Spike-Fly could function as a spin top for 2A looping play; with tips removed, it reverted to standard 1A string play. Fitting rubber O-rings on the rims enabled 4A offstring use.
The Spike-Fly was never a standard production model — each unit was made specifically to customer order, making it one of the rarest Dif-e-Yo configurations.

title: Spike Side Effects
content:
Spikes are available in:

Aluminum: Multiple Colors

Brass

Titanium

Spikes are one of 4 different Side Effects to be made in Titanium by Brian Fellhoelter. They are made of Grade 5 Titanium, and 25 sets of each were made.

title: Spin Drifter
content: AboutReleased in February 2021, the Spin Drifter features spinning sidecaps mounted on ball-bearing hubs that rotate independently of the yo-yo body. It can be used as a conventional yo-yo, as a spinning top when the sidecaps are engaged, or as an interlocking stacker challenge where the sidecaps lock together with other Spin Drifters. The transaxle provides extended spin times suitable for beginner string tricks, and the take-apart design makes it easy to re-string.

title: SpinFaktor
content: About the SpinFaktorThe SpinFaktor was YoYoJam's first composite yo-yo, featuring a plastic body with aluminum weight rings developed with input from Linda Sengpiel and Bill de Boisblanc. Nine of the top fifteen players at the 2001 World YoYo Contest used SpinFaktor series yo-yos, including all top six. Its rubber O-rings were attached to the outside of the rims for protection rather than response.

title: SpinFaktor X
content: About the SpinFaktor XThe SpinFaktor X (SFX) is the 10th anniversary reimagining of YoYoJam's original breakthrough model, preserving the composite plastic-and-aluminum-rim construction while upgrading to a modern silicone pad response system. The adjustable gap accommodates both beginners and advanced players. Championship colorways were released alongside the standard run.

title: SpinGadget
content:
About
Launched in December 2021, the SpinGadget is SpinGear's most significant original product and has become the brand's flagship beginner model. It uses a plastic transaxle bearing housed in a polycarbonate body, making it highly durable, very affordable (¥990–¥1,650), and easy to untangle — the body disassembles for quick string removal. The responsive design makes it ideal for beginners learning fundamental throws.
The SpinGadget spawned a large family of variants and sub-models:

SpinGadget Illustrated Model — same specs with custom limited-edition artwork (Sakura, Step1 Revival, Looping Star designs). ¥1,650–¥2,200.
SpinGadget SL — lighter, slimmer variant. ¥1,430.
SpinGadget POM/PC — hybrid model with POM or polycarbonate body and aluminum parts; 56.8mm, 41.2mm wide, 53.5g, D-size bearing. ¥6,600.
SpinGadget Big — oversized variant. ¥8,800.
SpinGadget Wooden — wood-bodied variant. ¥1,500.
SpinGadget Yuzuki Yukari Nagi — character collab edition (Vocaloid). ¥1,870.

title: SpinGadget OS
content:
About
The SpinGadget OS (Off-String) is SpinGear's dedicated 4A yoyo, applying the SpinGadget design language to off-string play. At 71.4mm diameter and 81.4g it is substantially larger and heavier than the standard SpinGadget, suited to the catch-and-throw mechanics of 4A freestyle. Made from POM with a D-size bearing.

title: LoopingStar
content:
About
The LoopingStar is SpinGear's entry-level looping yoyo, drawing on the brand's experience developing the Step 1, Starburst, and SpinGadget. It uses a nylon transaxle (rather than the K-size ball bearing of the Starburst) for a more budget-friendly price point (¥990–¥1,090). Popular colorways include glow-in-the-dark, Clear Glitter, Yellow Glitter/Clear, Yellow/Black, Red/Black, and Clear/Blue.
The LoopingStar body served as the base for the Guilty Gear -STRIVE- Bridget Yo-Yo collaboration with Arc System Works.

title: SpinGear Starburst
content:
About
SpinGear's dedicated 2A looping yoyo, made from polycarbonate with a starburst response system. Designed specifically for two-handed looping tricks. At 52.9g and 58.5mm diameter, it sits in a comfortable size range for looping play. Available in a wide variety of colorway combinations including glow-in-the-dark and two-color options.

title: SpinGear Step 1
content:
About
SpinGear's introductory beginner yoyo, designed to teach fundamental skills including Gravity Pull, Forward Pass, and Man on the Flying Trapeze. The convex body shape is similar to a Yomega Raider. Notable for its manga-illustrated side caps, which give it a distinct Japanese aesthetic. Available in red and blue.
A companion Step 1 Pro variant was also released, aimed at 2A looping practice: 58.5mm diameter, 35.7mm width, 52.8g, K-size bearing, starburst response. The Pro version came in Red Glitter, Clear/Red, Clear, Black, and Clear Yellow colorways.

title: SpinGear Step 2
content:
About
SpinGear's intermediate offering, bridging the gap between the beginner Step 1 and full metal competition throws. The H-profile body provides a comfortable catch zone for string trick play. Originally shipped with a C-size bearing; redesigned in 2023 with a D-size bearing to reduce string tangling during brain twister-style moves. Responsive (no-bind) design. Available in polycarbonate or POM.

title: SpinGear Step 3 Metal Wing
content:
About
The Step 3 Metal Wing is SpinGear's introductory aluminum yoyo, designed for old-school responsive play (looping and string tricks) while offering a clear upgrade path — swapping the bearing, pad, and axle allows conversion to unresponsive string-trick play. Available in two bearing configurations: a C-size version and a D-size version, each with its own colorway set.
The C-size variant (standard) offers a wider colorway range including Oliver Green, Dark Blue, Matte Silver, Pink, Red, Black/Gold, Copper, and Blue. The D-size variant is available in Blue and Red. The premium Black/Gold colorway commands a higher price point.

title: SpinGear Wooden Yo-Yo
content:
About
SpinGear's original wooden yoyo represents the brand's most entry-level offering — a classic fixed-axle design intended for young players and beginners learning basic up-down play. Two sub-variants exist: a larger model (58mm diameter, 52mm wide, 70g) bearing the SpinGear logo, and a smaller JOYC logo variant (57mm diameter, 32mm wide, 45g). Both are made from natural wood, which means color and grain vary between individual units. No bearing or response pad — purely fixed-axle play.

title: SpinJammer
content: About the SpinJammerThe SpinJammer was Dale Bell's first production yo-yo, developed at his injection molding company Advanced Air International. Its puck-like profile with faint Butterfly curves was superseded within a year by the DragonJam.

title: Blade
content:
History / About
A significant design step up from the Trilogy; production was outsourced to China to cut cost.

title: Eclipse
content:
History / About
Featured a modular brass-and-rubber weight-ring system and used Duncan friction stickers under license from Duncan Toys. A "Solar Eclipse" glow-in-the-dark variant was also produced. Discontinued in September 2004 due to side-cap production issues, the final run was limited to 250 units. Basis for the Doctor Popular signature "Hesitator."

meta.yya_response: Duncan friction stickers over starburst (used under license from Duncan Toys)

title: Firefly
content:
History / About
A 71-piece limited release: a glow-in-the-dark, LED light-up TigerShark variant.

title: Great White Shark
content:
History / About
A widened, heavier TigerShark variant ("GWS") built for low-responsive tricks. V1 used a starburst response; V2 switched to Duncan friction stickers.

title: Hesitator
content:
History / About
A signature series for yo-yo player Doctor Popular, derived from the Eclipse but using lighter aluminum weight rings instead of brass. Hand-painted with custom pog art; of 55 made, 15 were destroyed for quality control, leaving only 40 distributed.

title: Manta-Ray
content:
History / About
A fixed-axle butterfly yo-yo, popular as a canvas for custom/advertising pog art (including a Smokey Bear 60th-anniversary edition and regional contest editions). Upgradable to TigerShark specs via a bearing kit.

title: Oliver’s Comet
content:
History / About
A signature series for founder and world champion Dale Oliver; a glow-in-the-dark Tornado variant with a battery-powered LED light-up system.

title: Revolver
content:
History / About
Used the Eclipse-derived bearing system with weight adjustable via O-rings/snap rings under the pogs.

title: Space Monkey
content:
History / About
The company's first bi-metal model. Positively reviewed at release, including a note from reviewer Dylan Kowalski that it plays well for 5A.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C / Size C- (two bearings included: responsive + unresponsive)

title: Spin Wizard
content:
History / About
An Americanized rebadge of Abbe Toys' (Australia) "Black Mamba" (originally sold under the Yo-Matic name); Spintastics distributed it in North America but did not design or manufacture it.

title: Spintega Special
content:
History / About
Signature yo-yo for Matt Harlow, 2001 World Yo-Yo Champion, a glow-in-the-dark, Tornado-based looper. Reportedly later re-released under the name "Riot."

title: Technic
content:
History / About
Designed by former Duncan pro and U.S. National Grand Master Dale Oliver, the Technic was first sold in summer 1995 and became the basis for Spintastics Skill Toys, Inc., formally founded the following year. Originally sold as the "Technic Terminator" before the name was shortened for legal reasons. Still praised as a looping/beginner yo-yo.

title: TigerShark
content:
History / About
Spintastics' best-selling model. Joel Zink won the 1A division at the 1999 World Yo-Yo Contest using a TigerShark. Basis for the later Great White Shark variant.

title: Torch
content:
History / About
A clear-bodied Tornado 2 variant fitted with a battery-powered LED light-up system.

title: Tornado
content:
History / About
The ball-bearing counterpart to the fixed-axle Technic, originally sold as the "Terminator Tornado." Later discontinued and replaced by the Tornado 2.

title: Tornado 2
content:
History / About
Successor to the Tornado, made heavier via internal metal snap rings.

title: Spintastics Tornado Full Glow
content: AboutThe Spintastics Tornado Full Glow is a special-edition collaboration between Spintastics and Twisted Stringz. Based on the classic Tornado design originally created by World Yo-Yo Champion Dale Oliver, this version features a fully glow-in-the-dark body and caps, upgraded with a Twisted Stringz Trifecta bearing for improved responsiveness and looping performance. The take-apart ABS construction allows for bearing and string replacement. Designed for classic looping tricks: Loop the Loop, Shoot the Moon, Rock the Baby, UFO, and Milk the Cow.

title: Torus
content:
History / About
A step-round companion to the Blade with a wider profile; also made in China.

title: Trilogy
content:
History / About
The company's first all-aluminum model, featuring metal "hub spinner" hubstacks and a Duncan MoMentuM-style screw axle system. Widely regarded by players as a commercial and design misstep, vibration, weight distribution, and hub-spinner build quality were common complaints, and the company reportedly dismissed player criticism on YoYoNation forums at the time. Released in gold, blue, black, and cranberry.

title: Bowtie
content: History / AboutThe Bowtie is a 6061 aluminum yoyo from Canadian brand Spintek, listed at more than 100 mm wide. Spintek describes it as a novelty yoyo that makes technical string tricks a challenge but makes hops and whips comically easy. It ships unresponsive, requires a bind, and comes in a pouch rather than a box because of its width. YoYoExpert lists its release as July 2025.

title: Crosshair
content: History / AboutThe Crosshair is a Spintek fingerspin yoyo with an aggressive H-shape and a dimple that locks the finger in place, with white engravings. Per Spintek it ships responsive with an unresponsive bearing kit included, aimed at beginners learning fingerspin tricks. YoYoExpert lists the material as 6061 aluminum and the release as July 2025.

meta.yya_response: Responsive out of box; unresponsive bearing kit included; slim pad 19mm

title: Metal Skyva 2
content: History / AboutSpintek, in collaboration with MagicYoYo, describes the Metal Skyva 2 as a completely new experimental design with an H shape and a very wide profile. It has a deeper fingerspin dimple to address "aimless wandering", a lighter weight distribution, and removable Delrin caps that can be swapped between Metal Skyva 2 colors using compressed air through the axle hole. It is a 6061 aluminum body with Delrin caps and ships unresponsive.

title: R1 Pro
content: History / AboutThe R1 Pro is a Spintek yoyo made from hardcoat 6061 anodized aluminum. Per Spintek it ships responsive for beginners, with larger rubber pads for reliable return, and an included unresponsive bearing converts it to an unresponsive yoyo. YoYoExpert lists its release as July 2025.

meta.yya_response: Responsive; unresponsive bearing kit included; slim pad 19mm

title: Revlo
content: History / AboutSpintek says the Revlo is based on the discontinued Polyform A4 and was developed by its North American team members as a performance "organic" yoyo. Each yoyo has a unique splash pattern. It ships responsive with an unresponsive bearing kit included. The material is 6061 aluminum.

meta.yya_response: Responsive; unresponsive bearing kit included; slim pad 19mm

title: Skyva 2
content: History / AboutSpintek describes the Skyva 2 as the plastic Skyva redesigned for 2025 in collaboration with MagicYoYo. Per Spintek, replacing the brass bearing seat nut with aluminum moved over 3 grams to the rims for longer spin time, the profile is slightly wider, and a new "NanoBlast" finish developed by Spintek gives a soft-touch feel. Material is injection polycarbonate. Spintek says the changes keep the character of the original Skyva.

title: Ballsy
content:
About
The Ballsy is Spinworthy's largest fixed-axle design, measuring 60mm in diameter and 38.5mm wide — substantially larger than the rest of the wooden line. The extra size and width make it well-suited for longer string play, flipping tricks, and players who want more presence on the string. Wood options span standard and exotic hardwoods as well as Spectraply laminated birch; Hickory versions top out around 73g. Hand-turned in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Bloodcell
content:
About
The Bloodcell is Spinworthy's wooden original for the shape later adapted in metal as the MK1 x Spinworthy RBC. Glen drew the design from the organic form of a red blood cell — rounder and more comfortable in hand than the sharper Harbinger profile. Subtle dimples on both faces enable clean pull-starts and finger-spin capability. Available in Zebrawood (47–51g) and Maple (51–52g), with special runs in Tasmanian Blackwood and Purpleheart. Hand-turned in Adelaide, finished with natural oils. The all-metal RBC version (already imported) is the responsive unresponsive aluminum counterpart.

title: Boon
content:
About
The Boon is a slightly smaller and more curved fixed-axle than the Harbinger, prioritizing comfortable hand feel and a forgiving catch zone over maximum diameter or spin time. At 56.5mm diameter, it sits noticeably compact for the genre. Standard wood options include Sugar Maple, White Oak, Merbau, Spotted Gum, Jarrah, Karri, and Hickory; exotic options include Purpleheart, Wenge, Tea Tree, Tiger Oak, and Sheoak. Weights range from roughly 46g to 64g depending on species. Hand-turned and finished with natural oils in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Burley
content:
About
The Burley is Spinworthy's undersized fixed-axle, turned exclusively from Gidgee — a dense and exceptionally hard Australian hardwood selected specifically because its hardness can withstand the stress of a smaller-diameter throw. At 45mm diameter, it is notably compact for fixed-axle play. The single wood choice (no alternatives) keeps the production focused and consistent. Priced at $70 shipped. Hand-turned in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Button
content:
About
The Button is a classic butterfly-shaped fixed-axle with a distinctive feature: a pattern of drilled holes in both faces. The holes serve three purposes simultaneously — improved weight distribution that allows denser woods to be used without excess weight, easier knot picking during play, and a distinctive aesthetic. Available across the widest wood selection in the Spinworthy line, including White Oak, Purpleheart, Zebrawood, Spectraply (laminated birch), Australian Sheoak, Walnut, Wenge, and Spotted Gum — resulting in weights ranging from approximately 34g (Walnut) to 54g (Purpleheart). Hand-turned and finished in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Harbinger
content:
About
The Harbinger is Spinworthy's inaugural model and the starting point for the brand's hand-turned fixed-axle catalog. Turned in Adelaide, South Australia by Glen (Glenacius_K), the butterfly profile features curved rims and tapered inner walls optimized for stalling, flipping, and looping on a cotton or polyester string. Available in Merbau (branded "Merbau Unicorn") and Myrtle Beech ("Myrtle Beech Lion"). Finished with natural citrus and tung oils. Not designed to be disassembled. A later revision (Harbinger 2) expanded the diameter and added more wood species.

title: Harbinger 2
content:
About
The Harbinger 2 is Spinworthy's improved take on the original Harbinger, expanding the diameter to 59mm for longer spin times and adding a tuned inner wall with recessed response for more precise play. Four hardwood options are offered, each producing a meaningfully different throw: Australian Sheoak (54–57g) for a balanced feel, American Hickory (65–67g) for power, American Walnut (46–48g) for a lighter option, and Purpleheart (70–71g) as the heavyweight choice. Hand-turned and finished with natural citrus and tung oils in Adelaide, South Australia. Not take-apart.

title: John Smith
content:
About
The John Smith is Glen's deliberately straightforward fixed-axle — described as "an absolute basic, classic butterfly" designed as a streamlined, accessible entry into the Spinworthy line. Full logo engraving on one face. Available in the widest range of woods in the catalog: Purpleheart, Spotted Gum, Maple, Walnut, Zebrawood, Hickory, Red Gum, Radiata Pine, and Australian Blackwood. Heavier woods like Purpleheart can reach 60g or more. Hand-turned in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: KNack
content:
About
The KNack is Spinworthy's signature model for fixed-axle player Kyle Nations. Glen worked directly with Nations to dial in every aspect of the design — gap width, inner wall taper, axle diameter, wood species selection, and subtle face concavity — specifically around Nations's smooth, creative trick style emphasizing quick response and reliable regeneration. The European Beech version (~49g) plays with a softer feel against the string; the White Oak version (~55g) provides more feedback and resistance — described by Nations as "business end vs. casual end." The Tasmanian Blackwood edition (48g) occupies a unique middle ground. Face dimples aid pull-starts.

title: KNack XL
content:
About
The KNack XL is an oversized variant of the Kyle Nations signature KNack, produced in limited quantities by Spinworthy. Two sub-variants are documented: a 63mm version at 46g (Dandelion wood) and a 65mm version at 56g (Blue), sold through the YoYoExpert forum BST and directly. The expanded diameter increases string contact area and extends sleep times relative to the standard KNack. Availability was extremely limited.

title: Scone
content:
About
The Scone is an unresponsive yo-yo from Spinworthy with an organic shape, described as light and floaty in character. It is slightly larger (55.5mm) and lighter (60g) than the Stout sibling, trading the Stout's planted, solid feel for a more effortless, floating play quality. Made in Australia. Standard ball bearing and silicone pad response for bind-return operation. Exact material not confirmed in published sources — likely POM or polycarbonate construction consistent with the Stout.

title: Skinflint
content:
About
The Skinflint is Spinworthy's budget-tier fixed-axle, designed to put a capable wooden throw in more hands at a lower cost. It uses a single wood type — Merbau — and offers no weight selection: buyers receive whatever weight the lathe produces. At $35 shipped versus $50 for other Spinworthy models, it plays comparably to the rest of the line without the premium wood or weight-control options. Hand-turned in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Steadfast
content:
About
The Steadfast is a production model from Spinworthy sold through YoYoExpert as a listed product (since delisted). Secondary market sales describe it as "dead smooth and spins forever" — consistent with an unresponsive 1A metal construction. A prototype version preceded production, with the two differing in gap specification. Raw anodized finish. Resale prices on the YoYoExpert BST ranged from $60 to $90. Very limited public documentation; full specifications were not published.

title: Stout
content:
About
The Stout is Spinworthy's first venture into unresponsive yo-yo design, departing from the all-wood fixed-axle format entirely. Machined from POM (polyoxymethylene / Delrin) in Australia, the wide 46mm body targets modern 1A string trick play. The material choice gives it a quiet, smooth feel distinctly different from aluminum. A compact 53mm diameter combined with significant width creates a solid, planted playing character. Standard silicone pad response and ball bearing for bind-return operation.

title: Survivalist
content:
About
The Survivalist is Spinworthy's experiment with non-wood polymer construction. The original version was machined from UHMWPE (ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene) but was discontinued after the plastic axles failed under hard throws and the material proved difficult to glue reliably. A revised version in transparent polycarbonate with a solid 1/4-inch aluminum axle was planned and produced in limited numbers — Glen described it as playing "really nicely when together." Extremely limited production. Made in Adelaide, South Australia.

title: Urchin
content:
About
The Urchin is a fixed-axle model from Spinworthy, confirmed available in Walnut and referenced in the Spinworthy Appreciation Thread on the YoYoExpert forums. Published specifications are limited. Hand-turned in Adelaide, South Australia by Glen (Glenacius_K).

title: Woodsman
content:
History / About
The Woodsman is one of Spinworthy's foundational fixed-axle wooden yo-yos. Founded by Glen in Australia, Spinworthy builds yo-yos with an emphasis on responsive play and natural materials. The Woodsman draws on classic wooden yo-yo traditions while meeting the demands of modern fixed-axle trick play.

title: Split Decision
content: The Split Decision introduced Werrd's interchangeable Donut rim system. The aluminum body ships with one of three Delrin rim profiles: Johnny 5 (traditional H-shape for longer spin), Anti-Superstar (H-shape with flatter outer rims for stability), or Speed Donut (angular butterfly, lightest and fastest). Rims must be hand-matched and balanced due to variance in Delrin manufacturing. The large rim option enabled offstring play. Each set ships as one body plus one rim type; rims are sold separately to mix and match.

title: Spore
content: AboutSpore is wound from 100% cotton-wrapped polyester in the Throw-Yo Threads Responsive family. Grippy disposition with slow velocity and an enduring shelf life — it sits between pure cotton and full synthetic, offering more durability than Pollen with the same grip-forward character. Available in the Substrate colorway.

title: Spright
content: AboutOPYOYOS's lightest release, the Spright is a bimetal weighing just 55g, praised for exceptional stability and spin time relative to its weight. The distinctive steel rims appear iridescent ("rainbow") in certain light. Blasted finish for grinding. Comes with Airetic nylon string.

title: Sprint
content: A 3D-printed, fixed-axle yo-yo designed and manufactured by Ardeus. The Sprint is one of four of Ardeus' initial line-up, sold through the YoYoExpert Forums.

title: Sprout
content:
History / About
Turner Return Tops was founded in 2022 by Bruce Turner, a lifelong yoyo enthusiast based in Florida who rediscovered the hobby in 2016 and later learned CAD and manufacturing through Mark Dierh's tutorials and QC work with Mk1 Yoyos. TRT's goal is to create fun, accessible yoyos for the community.
Sprout is a small, unresponsive top, very small! This lil' nugget packs a punch with 72% of its total weight in the rims, its fresh sprung spring spin time for days. Your tricks will be smokin' with this teeny tiny bud. This is the miniaturized version of Turner Return Tops' popular competition model, the Sago. Each Sprout includes a Zipline Strings Polyesque string, Turner sticker, and Turner Series #5 Pog, packaged in a custom sponge-lined papercraft Turner Tube.

title: Sprout (Prototype)
content: Sprout was a Burgeon Yo-Yos follow-up concept documented in a May 2017 project update, which described a new prototype received from a machinist. No public retail release has been confirmed.The prototype’s material, play style, dimensions, weight, response, bearing, axle, color, and intended price remain unknown. The unnamed machinist is treated as a fabrication vendor rather than a collaborator.

title: Sputnik
content: AboutThe Sputnik brings bi-metal construction to a compact 52mm diameter, using inner stainless steel rings at the lips rather than outer rim rings — the same placement strategy as the earlier Laser. The 52mm footprint gives it a smaller, faster feel compared to the Draupnir's 57mm, making it a natural choice for players who prefer undersized competition throws with bi-metal performance. A limited 66g variant was released on April 4, 2015, Japan Yo-Yo Day.

title: Spyglass
content:
The Spyglass was MK1's 8th yo-yo, releasing on June 24th, 2022 with a second run on January 27th, 2023.

Below is a video MK1 produced about the Spyglass and its development.

https://youtu.be/fjU1yv1Urq0?si=d9UZAOt8EGDp9WWv

Prototype

The Spyglass prototype was orange/black. There was an earlier clear w/rainbow rims prototype that we cannot find a picture of.
