title: Addict
content: AboutThe Addict was SPYY's second commercially released yo-yo and its first to use a Size C large bearing, then an emerging standard for unresponsive play. Released in December 2006, the first run came in deep red anodize; a subsequent run was bead-blasted green. The Addict used recessed .555 Dif Pad response and had a slightly undersized feel despite its approximate 54mm diameter. It was the foundation for the later Addiction design.

title: Addiction
content: AboutThe Addiction refined the Addict's design with a larger gap, grooves machined to accept flowable silicone response, and a distinctive skull motif in the cloudy anodize. Running from approximately 2009 to 2013, it was one of SPYY's most enduring models. The Addiction required a bind return and featured a 43.32mm width that gave it a noticeably wider catch zone than its predecessor. Its CBC slim pad response and silicone compatibility made it easy to maintain with widely available materials.

title: Addiction WYYC 2011
content: AboutThe Addiction WYYC 2011 was a special edition of the Addiction produced for the 2011 World Yo-Yo Contest held in Orlando, Florida. Sold exclusively at the contest, it featured a slight weight increase over the standard Addiction and came equipped with a CBC Center Trac bearing. Its dimensions matched the standard Addiction closely, making it a direct competition-ready variant. Only a limited number were available at the event.

title: Amplifier
content: AboutThe Amplifier was described by SPYY founder Steve Buffel as "the ultimate example of optimized weight distribution and mass centralization" in the company's catalog. At 56.5mm diameter — the same as the later TYY-01 titanium — and 42mm width, it used a smooth anodized finish and was available in three colorways: Green Flash, Icy Blue, and Plasma Burn. Its 4.25mm gap and stainless dry bearing reflected SPYY's mature approach to competition-grade design in their final years of production.

title: Dynamo
content: AboutThe Dynamo was Nate Sutter's first signature model with SPYY, designed for repeater tricks, horizontal play, and extended combo sequences. At 55.03mm diameter and 44.05mm width, it had a wider body-to-diameter ratio than other SPYY Pro series models. The bead-blasted aluminum body was engraved with alternating animal motifs — fox and hare on one set of halves, pelican and crane on another — making it one of SPYY's most artistically distinctive releases. The Dynamo marked a significant moment for Sutter as a sponsored player receiving his first signature yo-yo.

title: eH (2012)
content: AboutThe eH was a collaboration between SPYY and wood yo-yo maker TMBR (Tim Byrd), designed as a fixed-axle signature yo-yo for Ed Haponik. The first edition was released in December 2012 and used TMBR's signature Reversible Woodthread Axle system — allowing the player to adjust the yo-yo's profile between Imperial, Butterfly, or Pagoda shapes by flipping the axle. It was a limited run, and its success established an annual December release tradition for the eH series that continued through 2016.

title: eH (2014)
content: AboutThe 2014 edition of the SPYY × TMBR eH was released in December 2014 in collaboration with YoYoExpert as distribution partner. Made from white oak — chosen for its denser, less porous grain compared to red oak — it used the same TMBR Reversible Woodthread Axle system as the original. Approximately 120 pieces were produced. Ed Haponik's initials appeared on both sides of the yo-yo.

title: eH (2015)
content: AboutThe 2015 edition of the SPYY × TMBR eH was released in December 2015 via YoYoExpert. Approximately 96 pieces were produced. The design was simplified from the 2014 edition, with Ed Haponik's initials appearing on one side only. The TMBR Reversible Woodthread Axle system remained, preserving the adjustable profile between Imperial, Butterfly, and Pagoda shapes.

title: eH (2016)
content: AboutThe 2016 edition of the SPYY × TMBR eH was the most diverse in the series' history, offering three standard wood options — Wenge, Bubinga, and Zebrano — at $85 each, plus two ultra-limited pieces in Ebony available only via raffle at $200 each. It was released on December 19, 2016 at 8 PM EST via YoYoExpert, and represents the final known release from SPYY in any form. As with all eH editions, it featured the TMBR Reversible Woodthread Axle system for adjustable play profile.

title: El Ranchero
content: AboutThe El Ranchero succeeded the Pistolero with an expanded full-size 55mm diameter and a shift to Size C bearing and CBC slim pad response. At 4g heavier than its predecessor and with the same Western design heritage, it retained the Pistolero's rim artwork aesthetic while benefiting from the wider platform of a full-size body. The El Ranchero was one of SPYY's final releases before the company closed in July 2013.

title: Flying V
content: AboutThe Flying V was Ed Haponik's signature yo-yo for SPYY, designed around his background in both fixed-axle and modern string trick play. Its defining characteristic was an extremely narrow 32.92mm width despite a full 55.9mm diameter — giving it a profile unlike anything else in SPYY's lineup. It shipped with a thin C bearing installed, producing tug-return behavior reminiscent of classic yo-yos, but included a standard Size C bearing that players could swap in for unresponsive play. The blend of old-school feel and modern metal construction made it one of SPYY's most distinctive releases.

title: Galactic Goose
content: AboutThe Galactic Goose was a collaboration between SPYY and fellow Canadian company CLYW (Caribou Lodge Yo-yo Works), two of Canada's most celebrated boutique yo-yo makers working together for the first time. The collaboration drew on Canadian identity — the "galactic goose" name referencing both a Canadian goose constellation and the cross-company heritage — with maple leaf constellation artwork by Brazilian players Sid Seed and Rodrigo Pires. The yo-yo itself featured an unusual round stepped H-profile at 53.06mm diameter and 39.75mm width, using CLYW's pad response system. Its packaging extended the constellation theme with a Canadian goose star map.

title: Orbitron 5000
content: AboutThe Orbitron 5000 was a deliberate departure from SPYY's angular competition designs, featuring a wide, rounded profile with old-school aesthetic sensibilities. Pre-released at the 2012 World Yo-Yo Contest with a limited public run after contest sell-through, it became a collectible piece from SPYY's final years. Its 47.5mm width made it one of the wider yo-yos in the SPYY lineup, and string contact with the inner walls played a significant role in tilt control during play — a characteristic unusual for a high-end metal yo-yo of its era.

title: Pistolero
content: AboutThe Pistolero brought Western gunslinger aesthetics to SPYY's lineup, its flat rims engraved with "Wild Bill" imagery and its body shaped to evoke a Colt .45 revolver. At 52mm diameter it sat in the mid-size range, and like the Radian Super Light, its body halves featured machined holes to reduce weight and shift mass to the rims. It used a Japanese EZO 5×11×5mm ultra-precision bearing and a silicone/sticker recessed response. Machined from 6061-T6 aluminum in Canada.

title: Pistolero 2
content: AboutThe Pistolero 2 evolved the Western-themed aesthetic of the original with more ornate calligraphic logo work and laser-etched hearts and spades patterns on the outer rim. At 52.14mm diameter and 41.94mm width, its dimensions were nearly identical to the original, though it switched to an H-Spin D-size bearing. SPYY described the design as "somewhat classic, somewhat retro." Released around 2010–2011.

title: Pro
content: AboutThe Pro was SPYY's flagship competition model for 2010, designed with extreme rim weighting achieved through a dramatically reduced center nub and all mass pushed to the outer rims. Its short, stout body at 54mm diameter and 44mm width gave it a distinctive silhouette among SPYY's lineup. Like the Stryker, each unit received a unique splash colorway. The Pro's weight distribution was intended to maximize spin time and recovery for complex competition freestyle routines.

title: Punchline
content: AboutThe Punchline was Guy Wright's signature yo-yo for SPYY, designed in collaboration with illustrator Paul Escolar whose comic book artwork was laser-engraved into the body. Wright shaped the outer rims specifically for smooth arm and hand grinding, giving the Punchline a rounded profile optimized for his grind-heavy playing style. At 52.5mm diameter and 43mm width, it occupied a comfortable mid-size position. The Punchline was followed by the heavier Punchline Repeater in 2011.

title: Punchline Repeater
content: AboutThe Punchline Repeater was a refined version of Guy Wright's original Punchline signature, adding 2.5g of weight while preserving the identical shape and dimensions. The added mass was intended to improve spin stability and recovery for Wright's repeater-heavy competition style. It shipped with a stainless dry bearing and bead-blasted anodized finish, accepting flowable silicone response. The Repeater superseded the original Punchline as Wright's primary competition weapon.

title: Pure
content: AboutThe Pure was Jonathan Robinson's signature yo-yo for SPYY, released in 2009. Its most distinctive feature was flush-mounted aluminum side caps — a visual element unique in the SPYY lineup at the time. The Pure came in several editions: the standard run, a Bay Area Classic exclusive VSOP version with a polished blasted finish and gold pad-printed logo, an extremely limited 24-karat Gold Pure (collector item), and the XO Pure with a Dif-E-Yo KonKave bearing. All versions used a D-size bearing and recessed pad response.

title: Radian
content: AboutThe original Radian was SPYY's first commercially available yo-yo, sold in limited quantity via eBay in early 2006. Machined in Canada from 6061-T6 aluminum, it used a D-size EZO bearing and recessed Dif Pad response. Exact diameter, width, and weight figures were never formally published; the model served primarily as a proof of concept for Steve Buffel's manufacturing capabilities and directly informed the refined Radian Mk II released later that year.

title: Radian Gen 2
content: AboutThe Radian Gen 2 brought the long-running Radian series into the modern era with a Size C large bearing and CBC slim response pads, replacing the earlier D-size EZO and Dif Pad configuration. Released in 2011 with a splash anodized finish, it retained the Radian's core dimensions while offering improved compatibility with widely available bearings and response pads. The Gen 2 was the final chapter of the Radian series before SPYY closed in 2013.

title: Radian Mk II
content: AboutThe Radian Mk II was the finalized, production-ready successor to the original Radian prototype, and became SPYY's best-selling early model. Released in 2006 at $75 USD, it was machined in Calgary from 6061-T6 aluminum and featured a D-size EZO high-speed chrome steel bearing and recessed Dif Pad response. Its 54mm diameter and 40mm width made it a comfortable full-size player that established the SPYY house feel: solid, precise, and distinctly Canadian-made.

title: Radian Mk III
content: AboutThe Radian Mk III advanced the Radian line with a wider gap, "diamond drag" engravings machined into the rims for improved thumb and finger grinds, and a Full Metal Jacket nickel-plated finish. Released around 2007–2008, it used the same D-size EZO bearing as its predecessors and maintained the Radian's characteristic 54mm diameter and 40mm width profile while pushing performance forward with the wider gap and refined surface treatments.

title: Radian Super Light
content: AboutThe Radian Super Light shared the exact shape of the Radian Mk II but with material machined out of the body in the form of drilled holes, reducing weight by approximately four grams. The result was a noticeably faster player with the same familiar Radian profile. It shipped with thin lube in the EZO bearing and used a deep recessed double Dif Pad response. The raw satin aluminum finish gave it a distinctive look among the otherwise smooth Radian line.

title: Revenger
content: AboutThe Revenger held the distinction of being SPYY's widest model ever produced, with a 48mm width that SPYY described as providing an "aggressive, visually dominating profile" and a monstrous catch zone. At 53.85mm diameter and 66g, it was one of the final models released in SPYY's last era before closure in July 2013. The Revenger used recessed silicone response and a Size C bearing, with a 4.25mm gap consistent with the company's late-era designs.

title: Ronin
content: AboutThe Ronin was Ed Haponik's second signature model for SPYY — a heavyweight full-size design at 68.5g with a multi-step profile that balanced solid play with Haponik's preference for deliberate, controlled throws. The bead-blasted finish carried laser-engraved artwork including a Hokusai-inspired wave and the kanji character for "Ronin" (浪人), referencing a masterless samurai. The Ronin used a large 4.25mm gap and accepted flowable silicone response. It was one of the most visually striking releases in SPYY's catalog.

title: Skyy Chaser
content: AboutThe Skyy Chaser was SPYY's first model to break the 50mm diameter barrier, coming in at 49.5mm while offering a wider gap and more rim weight than the Spyder. It was released in two distinct variants sold simultaneously: a Size C stainless bearing version (dry) and a Size D stainless bearing version (light lube). Both versions used CBC slim pad response. The dual-variant approach allowed players to choose their preferred bearing size without buying a separate model.

title: Solaris
content: AboutThe Solaris was SPYY's most competition-focused model to date at release in 2011, combining a step-straight and H-profile hybrid geometry with a transparent side hub that revealed the axle and reduced center mass. At 56.07mm diameter it was one of the larger SPYY designs, and SPYY stated it offered "the greatest spin times and stability" in their catalog at time of release. The bead-blasted, splash anodized finish and large 4.25mm gap made it a serious performance tool for competitive players.

title: Speed Freak
content: AboutThe Speed Freak was built for one purpose: raw speed. Its V-profile with low edges and an inverse-round step near the bearing seat concentrated mass away from the rims to minimize rotational inertia and maximize acceleration. At 63.5g it was the lightest model SPYY had released to that point. The bead-blasted orange/red two-tone finish gave it a striking look. SPYY acknowledged the design trade-off openly, describing it as built for speed at the cost of stability.

title: Spyder
content: AboutThe Spyder was SPYY's foray into undersized design, debuting at the 2007 World Yo-Yo Contest. At 49.5mm diameter, it was compact, but SPYY gave it a 41.5mm width — unusually wide for a sub-50mm yo-yo — to maintain a large catch zone. It used a Size D Japanese EZO bearing and recessed Dif Pad response. The Spyder was released in black and in a "Super Hero Edition" red/blue colorway. It remained the company's undersized flagship until the Spyder 2 in 2012.

title: Spyder 2
content: AboutThe Spyder 2 updated SPYY's undersized design with a Size C large bearing, replacing the original's D-size EZO. The body was reworked with more dramatically reduced edges and a double-stepped outer rim profile designed to catch the thumb or finger during grinds. At 66.3g it was slightly heavier than the original Spyder while maintaining the same sub-50mm diameter. It was available in both A-grade and Star Grade (premium cosmetics) versions.

title: Stryker
content: AboutThe Stryker debuted at the 2010 Canadian National Yo-Yo Championship and was designed as a sharp H-profile undersized competition model. Coming in below 50mm at 49.49mm diameter, it had an aggressive geometry with a 4.5mm gap and CBC Center Trac bearing. The two-tone black/silver splash anodize made each unit cosmetically unique. The Stryker was one of SPYY's most competition-focused models, with extended sleep time and stability for its size.

title: Supra
content: AboutThe Supra was an undersized competition model conceived as a successor to the Pro, bringing that model's rim-weighted approach to a 51mm frame. Named after the Toyota Supra, it came in an acid wash / splash anodized finish and featured a 4.5mm gap — one of the widest in SPYY's catalog at the time. At 67.5g, its weight was pushed heavily toward the outer rims for maximum spin time and gyroscopic stability. The Supra was one of SPYY's most technically deliberate designs of 2010.

title: TYY-01
content: AboutThe TYY-01 was SPYY's return from retirement and the company's only titanium yo-yo. Released on November 8, 2015 via spyy.bigcartel.com, it was limited to approximately 150–165 pieces at $300 USD / $400 CAD with shipping included. Steve Buffel applied the same aerospace-grade machining precision to titanium that had defined SPYY's aluminum work, producing an H-shaped profile at 56.5mm diameter and 41mm width. The TYY-01 used a Dif-E-Yo KonKave bearing and CBC 19mm slim pads, with a 316 stainless steel axle to avoid galling the titanium threads.

title: Square Apart Pack
content:
About
The Square Apart Pack bundles both halves of Quocrea's Square Apart hybrid 5A counterweight — one polycarbonate (Clear or Clear Black) and one POM (Solid White or Solid Black) — so a player can use the QA (Quoc Axis) Lock System to swap between them on the same body.

title: Square Apart – PC
content:
About
Square Apart is the first release in Quocrea's Stand Apart Series: a hybrid-construction 5A counterweight built around the QA (Quoc Axis) Lock System, a threaded interface that lets a player swap between polycarbonate and POM halves on the same body to change weight and tug response without buying a whole new counterweight. Each half is CNC-machined in a two-step process, with the bearing seat built directly into the structure.
This listing is the polycarbonate (PC) half, sold in Clear and Clear Black colorways.

title: Square Apart – POM
content:
About
Square Apart is the first release in Quocrea's Stand Apart Series: a hybrid-construction 5A counterweight built around the QA (Quoc Axis) Lock System, a threaded interface that lets a player swap between polycarbonate and POM halves on the same body to change weight and tug response without buying a whole new counterweight. Each half is CNC-machined in a two-step process, with the bearing seat built directly into the structure.
This listing is the POM half, sold in Solid White and Solid Black colorways.

title: Nomad
content:
History / About
The Nomad is the signature model of Shane Lubecker for Square Wheels Yoyo Company, released on July 10, 2014. It was the brand's fourth and one of its final production models. Used in player videos by Lubecker alongside Chandler Steele and featured in multiple player edits, the Nomad represented the brand's evolution toward signature-model programming before Square Wheels quietly wound down operations circa 2015. Also used by sponsored players Spencer Walker and Robbie Graham.

title: Rex
content:
History / About
The Rex is Square Wheels Yoyo Company's oversized D-bearing throw, released in 2013. The brand positioned it as "the D-bearing yoyo that plays like a C," challenging the common assumption that D-bearing models offer inferior performance. At 57mm diameter and 68 grams it is significantly larger than the Royale and Rockefeller, delivering tight binds and snappy regenerations. Featured in videos by Spencer Walker and Owen Ekblad.

meta.yya_response: Square Wheels D-Pad or flowable silicone

title: Rockefeller
content:
History / About
The Rockefeller is Square Wheels Yoyo Company's competition-focused model, released in 2013. Where the Royale was positioned as an everyday throw, the Rockefeller was built for serious play, earning praise for its "incredible regenerations" and extended sleep times. At $135 it was a premium offering. Players described it as playing heavier than its 66.4 grams suggest, with solid stability. Multiple colorways were produced including Ice Caps, Borealis, and PNWR/CalStates editions, some with soda-blasted finishes for grinding.

title: Royale
content:
History / About
The Royale was Square Wheels Yoyo Company's debut model, released in 2013 from Kansas City. Designed as an accessible everyday throw emphasizing "personality, performance and practicality," it introduced the brand's aesthetic identity through striking anodized colorways. Square Wheels was known for groundbreaking anodization work, and the Royale was the vehicle through which the brand built its early community following. A fixed-axle variant called "Royale w/ Cheese" was also produced.

meta.yya_response: Square Wheels C-Pad or flowable silicone

title: SR-71
content: About the SR-71The SR-71 is the signature yo-yo of Nathan Crissey, designed as a successor to the Sirius with a straight Butterfly profile and heavy aluminum rim for extended sleep times. It ships with a thin bearing for standard play convertible to bind response with an included Speed Bearing. Multiple championship-edition colorways were produced for 2010 Worlds and Nationals events.

title: SSJ GOD MODE
content:
History / About
The SSJ GOD MODE is Enso’s ultimate ultra-wide competition throw, drawing inspiration from Levi White and reviving the company’s original “UI” design concept from their inaugural titanium release. Rather than titanium, the SSJ GOD MODE uses 7075 aluminum to maintain thin walls while achieving competitive performance.
The name references a powerful anime transformation, reflecting the designers’ belief that “this is one of our strongest yo-yos today.” It excels at horizontal combos and banger transitions, suited for all trick styles. Available in SSJ Blue, Dragon Fruit, Zuno Force, and Gilgamesh colorways.

title: Stainless Steel KOI
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"We continue to explore, and master the design and usage of different types of materials. Establishing a foundation for us for our future releases with more options on materials. We choose the SS Koi to be our first ever full stainless steel yoyo. Stainless steel has a very high density, surpassing aluminum and even titanium. Making a full stainless steel yoyo requires very thin walls and very precise manufacturing. We decided to utilize the design of Koi for its organic shape and its use case even when it's slightly undersized due to the nature of stainless steel.

SS KOI yoyo became our first ever D-bearing yoyo. The D bearing is smaller than the standard C bearing, increasing the power and spin speed of the yoyo, which solidifies the performance of the SS koi and our performance-driven culture. SS Koi feels powerful, stable, yet flowy, organic and undersized, perfectly blending performance, fun, and specialty."

title: Star-Chaser
content:
History / About
Star-Chaser (SS-003) follows the YoYoJam PHENOM shape, positioned as an "EDC" (every-day-carry) throw rather than a pure competition tool. Originally released in A6061 (2021), later upgraded to A7075 (date unconfirmed, likely 2022-2023) with mixable half-body colorways (up to 15 combinations).

title: Stardust
content: AboutThe Stardust was the first yo-yo ever produced by 44re:creation (later renamed yoyorecreation), released in 2008 by founder Kengo Kido. The first production run used a titanium-threaded axle to prevent stripping — an issue that had plagued the initial batch and was corrected before wide release. A second run included a licensed KonKave bearing. Compact at 52mm and light at 65g, it established the brand's preference for precision over spectacle.

title: Stardust 2
content: AboutThe Stardust 2 retains the original Stardust's 52mm diameter but reduces mass in the axle area to push weight outward toward the rims, improving spin time and stability while keeping the compact feel that defined the original. It represents an incremental but meaningful refinement rather than a redesign — the core shape and dimensions are preserved while the weight distribution is optimized.

title: Starfire
content:
History / About
The Starfire is TimCor Productions' original yo-yo, an aluminum hubstacked model teased in 2008 and sold to the community around 2009. Its narrow profile, reminiscent of a YoYoFactory Coldfusion GT, suited it to string tricks. It shipped in royal blue anodize with orange silicone O-ring response installed and spare neoprene O-rings included, and used YoYoFactory-brand hubstack hardware.

title: Starfire (2018 Reissue)
content:
History / About
Announced September 14, 2018, this is a metal reissue of the original Starfire, retaining the hubstacked narrow profile but with modern machining and updated anodized and bead-blasted finish options, including a rose-gold/black "Splash" colorway and a blasted blue-with-black-hubstacks colorway.

title: StarFire FReedom
content:
History / About
Released July 4, 2026, the StarFire FReedom is a capped plastic Starfire in a "Betsy Ross" American-flag colorway, limited to just four pieces.

title: StarFire (May the 4th Edition)
content:
History / About
Released May 4, 2026 ("May the 4th"), this Star Wars-themed capped Starfire run shipped in "Evil Lord" and "Best Friends for Life" colorways.

title: Stargazer
content: AboutThe Stargazer arrived in 2009 as the direct successor to the Stardust, sharing its predecessor's 7075 aluminum construction but bumping the diameter to 54mm for a more substantial feel. A 2009 revision updated the shape to step-straight, widened the gap by 1mm, and dropped the weight by 2g, producing the version most players encountered. The Stargazer also had a separate 3A-optimized variant (StarGeyser) developed later for Minato Furuta.

title: Starship
content:
The following was archived from RSO's website:

TWO NEW MINIS

The RSO family will welcome a new mini member in March 2022 - a boy!

The second mini addition to the RSO family is STARSHIP, an undersized version of SPACESHIP. Coincidentally, my wife was pregnant with our first child while I was working on SPACESHIP. Because this release is close to the End Titanium release, I am making it one of the lowest-priced RSO titanium yo-yos to date for the benefit of the hardcore RSO collectors.

STARSHIP is the only yo-yo remaining in the RSO inventory, as future projects have been put on hold in anticipation of my second son’s arrival in the coming month. I am aiming to fulfill all STARSHIP orders by mid-February 2022.

This STARSHIP run will be the last SPACESHIP iteration. No other versions in any other form or color will be made.

Not much has been said about the design process behind the STARSHIP / SPACESHIP in my previous write up, so I will chronicle my prototyping journey here.

ORIGINS

There is a long story behind how I finally arrived at STARSHIP, which is based on one of the prototype CADs of the SPACESHIP.

Like most of the other RSO yo-yos, the prototyping process of SPACESHIP was rather arduous. Being new to CAD drawings and struggling with the sluggish Fusion 360 made things worse. It was during the design process of SPACESHIP that I eventually caved in and subscribed to AutoCAD, which made designing yo-yos more efficient, enjoyable and rewarding.

SPACESHIP was only put into production after 3 rounds of prototypes. The whole process took a surprisingly short 4-5 months.

The first prototype was a 50mm, C bearing, titanium yo-yo. The run was unusually sizable for an RSO prototype, consisting of 8 yo-yos (I typically only do 3 yo-yos for each prototype). The prototypes were machined by Magic YoYo and sold in a private Facebook Messenger group consisting of individuals from a yo-yo forum in October 2018. The prototype had an engraving by Jason Week, which was similar to the one on the production SPACESHIP. They loved the prototype. I was ready to put the yo-yo into production but changed my mind at the last minute.

Note that STARSHIP is machined from a revised CAD of this first prototype, with some ugly machine lines removed.

C bearing SPACESHIP prototype by MagicYoYo.

50mm SPACESHIP prototype run, consisting of 8 yo-yos.

Despite the positive response from the owners of the first prototype, a second, larger prototype with a 54mm diameter was made. My thinking at that time was that a mid-sized yo-yo would be more well-received than an undersized one. An Instagram poll I created confirmed this.

An Instagram poll which showed people wanted the 54mm version more than the 50mm one.

The second prototype was unique in its own right. It had a more “solid” playfeel because it had more rim weight, as well as a D bearing instead of a C bearing. But, to be completely honest, I didn’t like how it played. It was machined by YoYoEmpire, which was (at that time) the only machinist who had readily available D bearing pads that could be installed in OEM yo-yos. Today, you can recognize D bearing yo-yos made by YoYoEmpire from the white pads with a smaller outer diameter of 18mm, depicted in the picture below.

The D bearing yo-yo landscape has changed in recent years, with the usage of the ubiquitous wider 19mm outer diameter D bearing pad specification popularised by Freshly Dirty. D bearing RSO yo-yos like the aluminium Bowl Mini, stainless steel Bowl Mini and TiRAMiSU come with Landing Pads of this pad specification.

D bearing 54mm SPACESHIP prototype by YoYoEmpire, with their white, 18mm outer diameter D bearing pads.

I went back to Magic YoYo for the third and final prototype - a C bearing 54mm version. I changed the weight distribution slightly and shifted some weight from the rim to the yo-yo center (notice the chunkier rims on the D bearing 54mm prototype in the picture below). The changes resulted in a yo-yo with a more desirable floaty playfeel. Apart from being about 2g heavier, the final prototype was essentially identical to the production SPACESHIP. The process from prototype to production was lightning quick because Magic YoYo had designated a CNC machine specifically for SPACESHIP. The final prototype was machined, polished, assembled, shipped to me, CAD amended (with 2g less), and production completed within a week.

50mm SPACESHIP prototype (left), 54mm SPACESHIP production model (centre) and 54mm D bearing SPACESHIP (right).

Those who owned both the first SPACESHIP prototype and the production SPACESHIP preferred the former. Since then, there have been calls for RSO to do a run of the first SPACESHIP prototype. Years later, the STARSHIP is born.

A WELL KNOWN BUTTERFLY SHAPE

SPACESHIP / STARSHIP is a reinterpretation of the classic butterfly shape made by other prominent companies in the past.

The pioneer of this shape was YoYoFactory with the FAST 401k, an aluminum 56mm small bearing yo-yo in 2005. It had adjustable knobs on both hubs. By twisting the knobs, the player could adjust how much the starburst grooves would jut out from the response area, altering the yo-yo’s responsiveness. The FAST 401k was a novel design and remains highly coveted by collectors today.

Fast forward to 2017, A-RT made an oversized 63mm large bearing version of the 401k aptly named the 420. Essentially a “FAST 401k Max / Plus”, it had almost identical catch zones, but was devoid of the adjustable knobs.

YoYoFactory FAST 401k (2005).

A-RT 420 (2017).

RecRev made a yo-yo called the Bad Rep in the interim period, an undersized hubstacks enabled yo-yo with a larger bearing. It had a steeper catch zone than the FAST 401k / 420, with a smoother transition from the pad groove to the rim. The Bad Rep is the only yo-yo out of the few I have mentioned in this write-up that I have never owned or thrown.

SPACESHIP’s catch zone mirrors that of Bad Rep's, with a smooth arc from the pad groove to the rim. Being undersized like Bad Rep, SPACESHIP has a bigger width-to-diameter ratio and visually different proportions than the FAST 410k / 420. The rims of SPACESHIP are also sharper than the others. SPACESHIP is the only titanium yo-yo of the lot.

RecRev Bad Rep (2007).

SPACESHIP (2019).

COMPARISON WITH SPACESHIP

STARSHIP is only 0.5g lighter than SPACESHIP - this weight difference is insignificant. However, if you were to blindfold yourself and do tricks with both yo-yos, STARSHIP feels paradoxically “heavier” as the weight is concentrated in a smaller package. An example of what you would feel would be throwing a CLYW Peak, then throwing a Wooly Marmot 1 (essentially a condensed version of the Peak) after. Weight distribution wise, both yo-yos are similar, but this is irrelevant as both yo-yos are of different diameters. STARSHIP and SPACESHIP are completely different yo-yos, and it would be worthwhile to own both of them.

For those who own the first SPACESHIP prototype, STARSHIP is identical except that some machine lines have been perfected and smoothened out. If you already own the first prototype, the only reason that would justify getting STARSHIP is its brand new engraving and package, which is, like SPACESHIP, by Jason Week. More on this later.

A NEW CNC MACHINED CANISTER

The first SPACESHIP prototype was the first RSO yo-yo that came with a CNC machined canister, which costs almost as much to make as an aluminium yo-yo. The black canisters were engraved with the words “SPACESHIP PROTOTYPE” in the alien language I created together with Jason Week, and had the number of the yo-yo carved on the side of the canister. Since then, I have included a delrin canister for the production SPACESHIP (in black and white), Doombot (in red), SPACESHIP ES (in blue) and most recently Droid (in black).

For STARSHIP, the canister is machined out of polycarbonate, the same material that is used to make many yo-yos on the market today and the one used to machine the custom caps and rings for Gravity. In addition, the canister is translucent, which showcases the silhouette of the yo-yo within.

The number of each yo-yo is engraved on the base of each canister.

ART BY JASON WEEK

The STARSHIP art, like SPACESHIP, is by Jason Week.

The story behind the SPACESHIP was an impending invasion of Earth by an alien species called the Nactaria, with SPACESHIPS sent to Earth by another alien species called the Eljasek to protect the human race. Since then, the human race has successfully fended off the Nactarians and have brought the battle to the Nactarians. The STARSHIP artwork shows human STARSHIPS travelling towards the Nactarian planet.

Will the human race emerge victorious?

WHAT’S IN THE PACKAGE

CNC MACHINED POLYCARBONATE CANISTER WITH NUMBER ENGRAVING

STARSHIP MISSION EMBROIDERED PATCH

SPACE PATTERN PROTECTIVE CLOTH

A PAIR OF 19MM CYAN TYPE 50 LANDING PADS RESPONSE

ORANGE STRING

title: Static (Prototype)
content:
About
Static (v0.5.0) is Motion's all-7068-aluminum mono-metal V-shape design, marked "Prototyped" only on the brand's timeline — no retail-release evidence found.

title: SGNL
content:
History / About
The SGNL is Static Co.'s debut standalone metal model, released in 2020. Founded by Aaron Day of Utah, Static Co. built its identity around precision machining and a nostalgic mid-school aesthetic. The SGNL's compact 54.43mm diameter and V/H hybrid profile were designed to play fast and smooth. Available in four colorways (Blue, Green, Red, Orange), it established Static Co.'s manufacturing voice beyond the One Drop Parlay collaboration.

title: Sudo
content:
History / About
The Sudo is a collaboration between Static Co. and One Drop Design, released in 2019. It serves as the premium metal successor to the Parlay collaboration, retaining the Side Effects axle system and the characteristic undercuts around the response pads. Built from 7075 aluminum rather than the Parlay's 6061, the Sudo delivers extended spin times while maintaining the organic feel that defined the earlier collab.

title: Wave
content:
History / About
The Wave is the signature model of Brian Cosky for Static Co., released in 2022. Designed in collaboration with Patrick Dressel, the Wave features a "fun, slim, highwall organic" profile with a deep-dish inner rim flat and added rim weight for extended spin. Despite its narrow 41mm width, the full 54.8mm diameter gives it a satisfying presence on the string. Available in six colorways through Static Co. and YoYoExpert.

title: Stealth Ogre 66
content:
History / About
Stealth Ogre 66 is an extreme miniaturization of the original Stealth Ogre concept, extending the "66%" micro-yoyo format. Sturm Panzer's own page credits distribution/collaboration with Spin Gear (a Japanese yoyo retailer/manufacturer) and 66percent (a micro-yoyo brand), and names Mitsumi Seisakusho as the manufacturer — the manufacturing credit is first-party only. Also released as Eclipse Ogre L66/R66 colorway variants. Neither Spin Gear nor 66percent currently has its own archive entry.

title: Stellar IX
content: History / AboutSora Ishikawa signature evolution of IX; used to win the 2023 World 5A title and later revised in axle/weight distribution in 2024.

title: Stelvia XP589
content:
History / About
The largest titanium yo-yo Luftverk has ever produced — an experiment in giving a titanium throw the proportions of a plastic. Developed simultaneously with the plastic Stelvia XSP as a head-to-head material comparison in nearly identical geometry. At almost 59mm with ultra-thin walls, the XP589 achieves an average weight despite its size. The thin titanium body creates an unusual playing experience: incredibly floaty for its diameter, and the string resonating against the walls produces audible ringing during slack and bind tricks. Only 40 units produced globally including retail. Numbered and signed by Jeffrey Pang.

title: Stelvia XSP (Plastic)
content:
History / About
The plastic counterpart to the Stelvia XP589 titanium, developed simultaneously as a head-to-head material comparison in nearly identical geometry. Nearly the same diameter, width, and shape as the titanium version, yet completely different in character — lighter, more forgiving, and with a softer feel in hand. The project was one of Luftverk’s most deliberate experiments in how material choice transforms play experience within the same design.

title: Stem System
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"The Stem system is a piece of new axle and bearing seat hardware that can support a wide variety of yo-yo designs. It’s made up of two different pieces. 

1. The Stem

The Stem is the primary piece that holds the yo-yo together, while also centering and aligning the body of the yo-yo so that it’s able to spin smoothly.  It features a cone shaped body that can center itself in a variety of hole sizes and a knurled outer knob to allow for a tight grip when tightening your yo-yo together. 

2. The bearing seat

The second component is what supports your bearing and response pad while the yo-yo is assembled. Different bearing seat pieces can be purchased for use in all Stem yo-yos, depending on what size bearing you want to use...

Setting up your Stem yo-yo is easy. Simply insert the Stem into the yo-yo half, then press the bearing seat down over it until you feel the O-ring hold it in place. Then, you can begin screwing the yo-yo together. If you feel the Stem start to rotate freely in the middle of your yo-yo, you can either hold the Stem by the textured outer edge while tightening, or press the halves together in your hands as you turn. The same techniques can be used when unscrewing your Stem yo-yo if the halves start to spin freely. "

Stem System yo-yo ship with D bearings currently, but kits for C and A bearings are available to purchase from Freshly Dirty.

For those wishing to 3D print yo-yos to work with the Stem System, Freshly Dirty has a template available from grabcad.com.

Stem System A Bearing Kit

Stem System C Bearing Kit

Stem System D Bearing

title: Stepround Fullsize
content:
From #UNBRANDED:

"A full-size Step Round yo-yo that pursues a standard balance within the #UNBRANDED lineup.

The body is as thin as possible, while the rim is as thick as possible. With an aggressive design comparable to titanium yo-yos, it achieves an otherworldly balance that combines the maneuverability of a monometal yo-yo with the spinning power of a bimetal yo-yo."

#UNBRANDED Stat Block

title: Stepround Undersize
content:
From #UNBRANDED

"You’ve started to fluidly connect your own combos with a full-size yo-yo. Yo-yoing is fun. You want to keep it with you more often. If only it fit in your pocket… The desire for an undersize yo-yo naturally grows from that feeling.

However, when you actually throw a smaller yo-yo, your usual tricks don’t feel the same. The spin is insufficient, mounts are unstable, and binds don’t snap back. You haven’t changed, but just by switching yo-yos, that “flow” disappears. Eventually, you go back to full-size, and the smaller yo-yo ends up sitting on the shelf.

STEPROUND UNDERSIZE was designed to change that experience.

We took the high rotational efficiency of the “Step-Round Shape” established with the STEPROUND FULLSIZE and brought it directly to the undersize format.

Small yo-yos inevitably lose spinning power. Traditionally, the only way to compensate was to make the rims heavier, resulting in “heavy yet sluggish” undersize yo-yos that still wouldn’t spin long enough."

title: Stepstraight Fullsize
content:
From #UNBRANDED:

"Control your flow. Feel your progress.

Ever feel like you’re practicing, but you’re not sure if you’re actually improving? The STEPSTRAIGHT FULLSIZE is the smart, reliable partner designed to turn that vague uncertainty into solid confidence.

With its exquisite floaty feel and incredible control, it faithfully responds to your every intention. The joy of being in total control is what helps you truly feel your skills grow.

Thanks to the STEPSTRAIGHT shape, which effectively distributes weight to the rim, it ensures plenty of stability and spin time. The result It’s surprisingly nimble on the string, yet you can feel the reassuring presence of its solid, powerful spin.

This isn’t just about performance; it’s a model designed to remind you of the pure fun and sense of achievement that comes from getting better.

Perfect for players who:

・Want to truly feel their progress, from beginner to intermediate.

・Are looking for a faithful, smart partner, not an uncontrollable beast.

・Prefer a slightly smaller, highly controllable full-size throw."

Second Run

A second run of the Stepstraight Fullsize came out on January 1, 2026. This release is similar to the first, but it shaves a gram off the weight and redistributes it. The weight of this release is 63.5g.

title: Still Rollin
content:
From One Drop:

"We are so proud to have Talia Jamison on our team. She’s an amazing person and an incredible yo-yoer so of course she deserves a signature yo-yo! Here is what Talia says about the Still Rollin:

'I’m sure everyone has played a game that lasted way longer than they expected. A childhood memory of playing cards, tag, hide and seek, or dice and the fun that seemed to never end. That to me perfectly describes the Still Rollin - the fun that seems to never end.

When I worked with Shawn on the design, he was able to perfectly capture the elements I have always most enjoyed in a yoyo: a soft shape which fits comfortably in the hand, that isn’t just fun for the casual throw, but can hold up on stage during competition. I wanted Side Effects to give you a way to personalize its weight and aesthetic, and a yoyo that can confidently spin for my longer combos. With its slightly smaller size, the Still Rollin allows for more mobility during tech combos while maintaining stability and a great catch zone for lacerations and slacks. One Drop never fails to make the best yoyos on the market, and Still Rollin is no exception. 

Just like when it was Nana’s turn to roll the dice, well into my longest combos, this yoyo is ‘Still Rollin’'."

title: Stormberry
content:
The following is archived from Atmos’ website:

This design release was intended for the beginning of 2022, as an intermission to what we're building in the Weatherman Line, but here we are. Our final release of 2021, and — at least for us — a nostalgic callback to where we began.

This is the Stormberry.

SPECSdia 56.4mmwid 48.9mmweight 63.9gmaterial 7068 AL / SS

Our first design, the Cloudberry, was designed in early 2020 to be our dream organic. A nice, comfortable, and even fat profile that played light yet powerful, so it could stand up to the rigours of modern play whilst retaining its organic soul. The Thunderberry was released later as a heavier variant that sported a bit more torque and heft, and departed slightly from its lighter, floatier origins. Now, the Stormberry – the third and possibly final installation of the Berries – takes another step towards that design aspiration of light power.

We’ve been working on the Stormberry since late 2020, and just about a year on, we’re happy to finally share this with you.

There is considerable weight behind the opinion that a bimetal construction defeats the purpose of an organic. From a purist’s perspective, I can understand that view, as organics generally embody a type of play that doesn’t necessarily emphasise spin power, stability, or clinical precision – and leans towards, perhaps, what some might find the more artistic, rhythmic, or experimental. The A-RT Grail, One Drop Markmont Classic, and CLYW Peak are amongst many other of these classical organics that I feel embody that purism. In my opinion, our yet-unreleased design, the Noah, would find its place amongst these.

That purism isn’t something we’re attempting to dispute – with the Stormberry, we just pulled on a thread of inspiration and we really enjoyed where we ended up with that.

The original Cloudberry playfeel was actually partially inspired by CLYW’s Akita, Mark Mangarin’s signature return top, despite it possessing a very different frame. I was captured by the way it felt on the string, and I thought it represented the best of CLYW’s storied history and more modern directions. It was an extremely comfortable design, and it was also celebrated for being competition-capable. Given the Akita’s long-held place in our sandbox of references, it felt natural that we’d one day create an iteration of the Berry that paid homage to it.

To get the Stormberry lighter and still yet more powerful, we wanted to lose some mass in the mid-areas, pack on some muscle at the rims, all the while reducing its overall weight. Our vision of the Stormberry necessitated that it came in leaner than its two Berry brothers.

The Cloudberry comes in at 64g, and is relatively evenly weighted. The Thunderberry is about a gram more at 64.9g, with the extra meat applied onto the rims. For the Stormberry, we reduced its walls to its minimal viable thickness, which gave us room for nice, thick stainless steel rims without having to inflate its weight. It comes in at 63.9g, which makes it the lightest of the Berries, but also the most powerful.

Clocking that weight is significant, given it sports a full frame of 56.4mm (d) and 48.9mm (w).

It’s external profile looks nearly identical to its Berry brothers, but it’s got an entirely new engine under the hood. Anyone who has thrown a Cloudberry or Thunderberry would find the Stormberry familiar in-hand, and might be pleasantly surprised at the additional torque it has without sacrificing any manoeuvrability. It moves and feels even lighter than its weight might suggest.

In any conversation on bimetal organics, special mention must also be made to Damian Puckett’s Duality. I came across the design earlier in the year and picked one up from him directly in September, and loved it almost immediately. It’s difficult not to love Damian’s designs. The resounding sentiment surrounding the Duality is that it is a competition return top disguised as an organic. It definitely plays that way – It comes in at 64g, but has more torque than that spec implies – and elicits our highest recommendations.

The Stormberry project began as a third-act to our Berry series within the Fruitbowl Line, and we ended up with what we feel might be the final installation in our light power organic designs. There are no plans to extend it further, given our sense that this might be it, possibly the furthest we can push it – the Berry with the most juice.

Quick notes on kit:

The Stormberry comes fitted with these clear-grey response pads that came with our earlier models. The Cloudberries, Pomelos and Gojis come with these. They are slightly harder than our own Saturn Pads, and require some break-in time before they become fully grippy. The Stormberry has a wider gap width, and plays its best when its response pads have been given some love.

The Stormberry also comes with Zipline String’s Case Study 50s. They are premium in quality, last long, and are incredibly comfortable. Our models are now designed with this particular string type in mind, so we very literally cannot recommend it more as an ideal pairing.

If you’ve stayed with us till the end of this long post – and the end of this crazy year, too – thank you. Genuinely. 2021 has been a ride, and we’re grateful we’re still in this process of making things that bring joy through play. The love you consistently show us gives us that little extra to keep going.

·

title: Strand
content: AboutThe Strand combines a 6061 aluminum body with large rim-heavy polycarbonate caps and a deep fingerspin hub for competition and fingerspin trick capability. Wide at 49mm for a generous catch zone, the steep aluminum wall drives stability while the PC outer caps keep weight accessible and enable DNA-style fingerspins.

Watanabe selected the KonKave bearing and SG Sticker response for its performance in European competition conditions, and the Strix was his weapon of choice when he claimed the 2013 EYYC 1A title. It remains a sought-after signature collector piece.

title: Sugar Glider
content:
From One Drop:

"The Sugar Glider can be best understood with some background story on the Cascade.

We released the Cascade in July of 2012.

Prototype #1 was known internally as “The Wing”.   It was certainly really different for the time and there was disagreement about how to proceed because we didn’t know it was good enough to release.  Some team members were showing it off at Pacific Northwest Regionals that year and some really took a liking to it. For some reason that no one can remember they started calling it the “Glider King” and the name stuck.   We initially decided to scrap the project entirely, but then chose to make a big revision and see what happened.

Prototype #2 was known internally as known “The Glider” and it had changed considerably from the first version.

Prototype #3 had some small tweaks and refinements suggested by Markmont and this is what was released as the Cascade.

Because the Glider King was well loved and lost to history as a cool early prototype, we decided we might be able finish this yo-yo as it was intended and came up with the Sugar Glider. The profile shape and the overall size are pretty similar to the original but with some important changes:

*We added some Projection Profile grooves on the lower part of the catch zone*We removed Side Effects to put in an almost flat hub*Weight distribution change to improve the spin time and feel

Solid colors starting at $49!"

title: Summit
content:
From One Drop:

"We had a crazy idea. Have the guys from CLYW come visit the One Drop shop and design/manufacture a brand new collaboration yoyo from scratch all the while filming the whole process.

The result: 'the Summit'. The name really speaks for itself as this is a melding of a CLYW Avalanche and a One Drop Cascade. The name also refers to how this was a meeting of the minds.

Then we had an even crazier idea: release a small run at Cal States the following weekend! We weren't sure if this was even possible, as neither of us have ever made a yo-yo from scratch so quickly, but we were up for the challenge and wanted to try!

Over the course of 4 days we created what we think is one of the best yo-yos on the market today.Day 1: DesignDay 2: Make a Prototype, while Jason Week works on ArtworkDay 3: Manufacture a Small Run and have Evan from Toxic Strings anodize them overnightDay 4: Laser Engrave/Assemble/Package

We had team members from both companies on site including Jensen, Zach, Charles, Paul, Andrew, Jordan and JT to help with the design and testing on the spot. The first version played really well, but everyone agreed that it needed a little bit more weight, so a 2nd revision was done. Round 2 of prototyping yielded the final version and we all loved it!

Charles made a documentary, which shows the full process of these amazing days that we spent together to create the Summit. It also includes footage of Cal States where we sold the first run, and how both One Drop and CLYW team members rocked the stage with it."

title: Summit 2
content: From One Drop:13 years ago we had a crazy idea: have the wonderful people of Caribou Lodge visit the One Drop factory to design and manufacture a new collaboration yo-yo from scratch, film the whole process, and release it that weekend at a contest. The Summit yo-yo came into existence in just one hectic week and the documentary endures as a snapshot of both collaboration and a “How It’s Made” for modern metal yo-yos. It has become a document of a special time in yo-yoing and it’s wild to see us all looking so young. Oh, how time flies.Last year, One Drop approached Caribou Lodge with a simple message: we’re better together. From there it didn’t take long for the idea of a Summit 2 to take shape. The basic idea was the same: design and manufacture a collaboration yo-yo in a few days, film the process and drop them at a contest that weekend. We quickly remembered that the time frame and goal for this idea are absolutely reckless and worried if we could pull it off again, now that we’re all older and need more sleep. Lucky for us, coffee came through! We knew we couldn’t repeat the magic of the first Summit. But this new adventure brought together folks from the first project and a slew of new faces, and is once again a reflection of a specific moment in yo-yo history. The experience of the first Summit served as a playbook, but 13 years on we created some new magic. The Summit 2 experience and resulting yo-yo, while building on the past, has it’s own character and story.There will be a new documentary, but it will be released later because (good) editing takes time. While we wait, here is the short version:With Steve and the Caribou team in Eugene, we started the process at a coffee shop on Monday morning discussing ideas for the design. We decided we wanted to capture the energy in the room, so no work was done in advance. Starting at square one with the simple question “responsive or unresponsive?” we talked through all kinds of ideas and ended up on a Side Effect Chief/Leaf. The profile would be Caribou Lodge and the cup would be One Drop: a perfect melding of the two brands that nodded to the original Summit while moving forward with a very different look and feel.We went back to the One Drop factory and with Shawn at CAD controls surrounded by team players, the design was ironed out. Once the CAD was finalized, Shawn went to work and by that evening we had a raw prototype in players’ hands. Shawn’s years of experience and skill is why it was possible for this to happen so fast, and the electricity in the room when we realized we’d have prototypes on Day One was incredible. Testing began and everyone loved it but there was some discussion about adding a little weight. Because of the time frame, we decided to produce the initial, lighter version for the weekend release at the Pacific Northwest Regional Yo-Yo Contest. It played great and tweaking the weight for production would be simple. We decided to call this initial version the “First Draft” and we released 80 of them at PNWR in a cool unique blue color done by local anodizer BT. The willingness of BT to have all of us show up at their shop and anodize these in two hours was legendary. There is some amazing footage of this that will be in the documentary. The box and engraving art were once again created for us by the incredible Jason Week. We asked Jason to play with the idea of doubling the original Summit concept and he gave us something that perfectly called back to the original while moving forward with new spirit and energy.For production, nearly everyone agreed on adding 1 gram of weight but no one could agree on Side Effects. So each player who was present for the Summit 2 experience will eventually get their own “Player Edition” model with their color and Side Effects of choice. This final production version has the additional 1 gram of weight and we all agree it’s exactly what we hoped for. This project has already been more than we could dream and we are excited to share this first step into a new future of collaboration between One Drop and Caribou Lodge.

title: Sunbird
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"We created the Sunbird to give people a more accessible and affordable option while still keeping the feel and performance everyone loved in the Hummingbird. We started with the basic Hummingbird competitive v-shape profile and tweaked the weight distribution to maximize the performance in an all aluminum form. Right from the first throw you'll notice the same light and powerful feel on the string that the Hummingbird is known for. It has great stability and spin power, and if you're looking for speed you're really in luck! The Sunbird is fast, maybe the fastest yo-yo that we has released so far!"

title: Sunset Trajectory NXG
content: About the Sunset Trajectory NXGThe Sunset Trajectory NXG combines a small bearing with O-ring response in a plastic body with an adjustable gap mechanism — users tighten or loosen the halves to dial in responsiveness. Its paper cap inserts are customizable, and the O-rings are described as exceptionally durable. It became a beloved classic among 2A players.

title: Sunwing
content: AboutThe Sunwing uses the classic Yoyofriends 7068+SS bimetal formula with rings pushed to the extreme outer edge of the side profile for maximum power and stability, while retaining the brand's characteristic flow and technical capability. A pure competition bimetal in the Sunbird lineage.

title: Super Emperor
content: The Super Emperor launched Auldey's yo-yo line in 1999 as a clone of the Bandai/Duncan Hyper Imperial. Made from cheaper plastic (~11g lighter than original), it featured a starburst response and was designed for 2A (looping) play.

title: Super Scintillator
content: TThis is the signature model from C3 media producer, Simpson Wong Wai Sheuk. It features an aluminum body with a stainless steel outer rim followed by a polycarbonate rim.
