title: Super Scintillator Reverse
content: A reverse-geometry variant of the Super Scintillator tri-material design. Simpson Wong's signature line. Price: $115–$125.

title: Super Scintillator Universe
content: History / AboutRetail Universe revision expands the Scintillator concept to an 84 mm width and 60 mm diameter, making it physically distinct from the base model.

title: Super SpinFaKtor
content: About the Super SpinFaKtorThe Super SpinFaKtor's extremely narrow width and slim gap make it ideal for intricate string passing tricks and technical 1A play emphasizing string manipulation over speed. It uses a smaller B-size bearing with a four-hole response system. YoYoJam describes it as a "true classic" rooted in the string trick tradition.

title: Super Yo-Yo Speed Russell
content: History / AboutThe Speed Russell occupied the elementary tier of Bandai's Super Yo-Yo line, one step above the Auto-Return model. It also used a disableable auto-return clutch system similar to the Yomega Brain, but was constructed with slightly higher quality materials. Its winged shape was designed for beginner to intermediate players discovering the hobby through the Chousoku Spinner anime. Distributed across Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia in anime character colorways.

title: Super Yo-Yo Super Russell
content: History / AboutReleased as part of Bandai's Super Yo-Yo product line — a regional localization of the Chousoku Spinner (Super Yo-Yo) anime — the Super Russell was the entry-level junior model in the series. It featured a rounded body with clear sidecaps over printed character pog inserts, and a removable wooden axle held in place by two rubber washers. The sharp gap edges made it unsuitable for sleeping or string tricks. Distributed across Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia in multiple character colorways from the anime.

title: Super Yo-Yo Super Russell Auto-Return
content: History / AboutThe Auto-Return variant of the Super Russell replaced the fixed wooden axle with a two-clutch auto-return mechanism modeled after the Yomega Brain, allowing the yo-yo to return automatically to the hand when spin speed dropped. The clutch could be disabled by removing a rubber O-ring. The winged shape and lightweight construction made it suitable for beginners. Like all Super Yo-Yo line products it was distributed by Bandai across Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia in anime character colorways.

title: Super Yo-Yo Ultra Russell
content: History / AboutThe Ultra Russell was the mid-tier intermediate model in Bandai's Super Yo-Yo line. It used a replaceable wooden axle sleeve held by two small rubber rings, with starburst response on the sidewalls compensating for the lack of wooden response on the axle faces. It was positioned above the Auto-Return and Speed Russell models and aimed at players who had graduated from auto-return. Like all models in the line it was released in anime character colorways across Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia.

title: Supercell React
content:
About
Supercell React is an alternate-weighting version of the original Supercell offstring model. Based on the Supercell's shape, weight distribution was redesigned to prioritize maneuverability for regeneration-type tricks — built to respond to the subtle nuances of feeling required during regeneration.

title: SUPERFLY
content: About the SUPERFLYReleased alongside the ANGLAM at sOMEThING's 2012 launch, the SUPERFLY is the brand's pure 7075 monometal offering. Its H-shaped inverse round profile is built for speed and agility, making it a sharper, lighter counterpart to the rim-weighted ANGLAM. Ships with an Addict Bearing and sOMEThING neon string.

title: SUPERFLY (3rd Gen)
content: About the SUPERFLY (3rd Gen)The third-generation SUPERFLY is "more powerful and lighter" than its predecessors. Width is kept under 43mm for sharp acceleration and rapid trick execution. The compact dimensions prioritize speed without sacrificing spin power, making it a competition-focused monometal for players who prefer a quick, agile feel. $87.99 USD. Colorway: Dark Red.

title: SUPERFLY REMIX
content: About the SUPERFLY REMIXThe SUPERFLY REMIX crosses the shape characteristics of the Superfly with the ANGLE, sOMEThING's predecessor model. The inverse round body uses 6061 aluminum and targets players who want middle-size dimensions with vigorous spin and strong maneuverability. Available in Splash Silver/Green, Splash Silver/Pink, Turquoise, Dark Blue, Splash Pink/Green, and Splash Gold/Black.

title: SUPERFLY REMIX 7075
content: About the SUPERFLY REMIX 7075The SUPERFLY REMIX 7075 upgrades the Superfly Remix's body material from 6061 to 7075 aluminum. sOMEThING notes the material change "creates a noticeable difference in the way it plays," with the harder alloy adding a firmer feel. Available in Silver, Red, Gold, and Gunmetallic.

title: Boomerang
content: AboutThe Boomerang was SuperYo’s auto-return transaxle yo-yo, positioned as a competitor to the Yomega Brain. The original version used a brass sleeve axle, making it notably smoother and longer-spinning than the Brain. A later revision switched to a plastic sleeve, bringing performance roughly in line with the Brain.The Boomerang was later produced in NED Show branded editions as the character assembly program grew to become the company’s primary focus.

title: Cosmic Spin
content: AboutThe Cosmic Spin was a NED Show branded edition of the Renegade, released in 2014 as the final known SuperYo product. The NED Show was founder Arne Dixon’s educational character-building assembly program for K–6 schools, built around the acronym NED: Never give up, Encourage others, Do your best. The yo-yo featured NED messaging on one half and came in a glow-in-the-dark colorway, sold exclusively through NED Show school assembly events.

title: Cruiser
content: AboutThe Cruiser was SuperYo’s debut product, launched in 1994 alongside the company itself. Designed for school performance demonstrations by founder Arne Dixon, it featured a butterfly/concave profile and fixed brass axle with starburst response. It was priced at $5 USD and came in translucent red with a gold foil stamp; a glow-in-the-dark variant sold for $6.Two versions exist: the first uses the spelling “yoyo” (no hyphen) and came in translucent red; the second, collected circa 1997, uses the hyphenated “yo-yo” spelling and came in solid purple. Mechanics are identical between versions.

title: Invader
content: AboutReleased in 1999 at $15 USD, the Invader was marketed as the only glow-in-the-dark ball-bearing yo-yo on the market at the time. It featured a modified/imperial profile with starburst response and bearing axle. Construction was similar to the Renegade but in an imperial rather than butterfly shape.

title: Nitro
content: AboutThe Nitro was released in 1999 at $15 USD as part of the same IntelliGap product line as the Typhoon. It featured a modified profile with rim weighting and SuperYo’s patented IntelliGap system, which allowed the string gap to be adjusted by twisting the halves without releasing any small parts. Described as a "long spin Power Band design" with a "lightning fast ball bearing system."

title: Renegade
content: AboutLaunched in 1997, the Renegade was marketed as the world’s first shape-changing ball-bearing yo-yo. Building on the concept of the Triple Play fixed-axle model, it added a bearing axle and retained the three switchable profiles — Imperial, Butterfly, and Pagoda — via a twist-apart take-apart design. With starburst response that wore smooth with play, the Renegade became capable of sleeping long enough for advanced string tricks, making it one of the most versatile and popular yo-yos of the late-1990s boom.The first production run featured hex-shaped bolt heads and came only in basic black. A version 2 redesign circa 2000 replaced the hex bolt heads with star-shaped bolt heads and a larger, stronger axle assembly. Version 2 was produced in a wide range of colorways including solids, clears, marbles, glows, and glow marbles through the 2000s.

title: Samurai
content: AboutThe Samurai was SuperYo’s flagship premium model, released in 1999 at $130–$180 USD. CNC-machined from aluminum to a diamond finish with halves toleranced to ±0.0005″, it featured a SatinGlide ceramic bearing — one of the first production yo-yos to ship with a ceramic bearing. The redesigned IntelliGap axle was described as "2.1.0" construction: two halves, one bearing, zero loose parts.The first run was limited to 1,000 units, each with Samurai markings and an individual serial number. At release, the Samurai held a documented sleep record of twelve minutes and two seconds, competing directly with the ProYo Cold Fusion and Tom Kuhn SB-2 at the top end of the performance market.

title: Sonic Spin
content: AboutThe Sonic Spin was a modified-profile, rim-weighted ball-bearing yo-yo released in 1996, priced at $15 USD. The original version featured a Supersonic Transport (SST) airplane silhouette graphic. When British Airways and Air France retired the Concorde in 2003, SuperYo updated the graphic to a stylized globe/atom design — this revised version is sometimes designated the SS II Sonic Spin.Later packaging noted the IntelliGap adjustable gap system. Dimensions: 61mm diameter, 28mm width, 58g weight.

title: Spinboss
content: AboutReleased in 1997, the Spinboss featured a heat-sensitive plastic body that changed color based on the warmth of the player’s hands — a mood-ring effect applied to a yo-yo. Like the Triple Play, it offered three reconfigurable shapes: Imperial, Butterfly, and Camel. Priced at $10 USD.String came pre-wrapped three times for beginners; removing wraps increased the difficulty and sleep time. Red caps with blue body was the standard colorway.

title: Triple Play
content: AboutThe Triple Play was SuperYo’s first shape-changing yo-yo, released circa 1994–1996. Its three-position recessed starburst response and take-apart design allowed players to configure it as an Imperial, Butterfly, or Pagoda profile — a concept that would later be refined into the ball-bearing Renegade. Made in USA.

title: Turbo Tread
content: AboutReleased in 1999 at $7 USD, the Turbo Tread was a novelty transaxle yo-yo designed to look like a treaded car tire with a chromed hubcap. The take-apart design used a wooden sleeve transaxle, comparable in construction to ProYo models. The "SY" initials appeared on the face alongside the tire tread detailing. Standard colorway was black body with chrome hubs.

title: Typhoon
content: AboutReleased in 1999 at $15 USD, the Typhoon was a landmark product: the first production yo-yo to feature a plastic ball bearing. Designed jointly by Arne Dixon and engineer Don Heaverlo, it used SuperYo’s patented IntelliGap adjustable gap system — the gap could be increased or decreased by twisting the halves without releasing any loose parts. Marketed as requiring no lubrication.The plastic bearing was a genuine engineering innovation at the time, predating the widespread adoption of SPEC and C-size metal bearings in budget yo-yos.

title: Wildcat
content: AboutThe Wildcat was a lower-cost fixed wooden-axle yo-yo produced by SuperYo circa 1999, serving as a more accessible companion to the IntelliGap bearing models. It featured a butterfly (winged) profile with starburst response. No longer in production. Confirmed colorways include black; others are unknown.

title: Surge
content: About the SurgeThe Surge is positioned as the natural upgrade from the Classic, shipping with silicone response pads and bind-response configuration for players transitioning from tug-return to advanced play. At 70.7 grams it is notably heavy for an all-plastic yo-yo, contributing to strong gyroscopic stability. A championship edition was produced for the 2013 World YoYo Contest.

title: Surveil
content:
History / About
Released in 2018 as the polycarbonate sibling of the Surveillance bimetal, the Surveil reimagines the design with a PC body while preserving the stainless steel rims for maximum rim weight and spin power. Compared to its bimetal brother, the Surveil has a very light and speedy feeling without sacrificing control. The plastic body has a special finish resembling blast-coating that reduces friction for grinds and reduces sleep loss when the string contacts the body. The shape differs from the Surveillance — the light body demanded different proportions to make the most of the rim weighting. Note: uses special proprietary shims available only from mowl; losing them makes reassembly difficult.

title: Surveillance
content:
History / About
The Surveillance is the second mowl release (2017) and the signature model of Daiki Tanaka. Developed as a direct counterpoint to the monometal M, it features an angular H-profile incorporating straight-shape elements — optimized for Tanaka's signature horizontal and grinding tricks. At 66.6 grams it is one of the heavier bimetals of its era, but the power and stability at even the lowest spin is remarkable. The stainless steel rims provide serious rim weighting and precision. The artwork features an all-seeing eye motif and a side profile of mowl's spirit animal engraved on the side. Daiki Tanaka used it to take 2nd place at the 2017 44Festival and 6th place at the 2017 Asia Pacific contest. Has been reissued in multiple colorways and remains in the lineup.

title: Surveillance HPF
content:
History / About
The Surveillance HPF is the signature bimetal model for 3A legend Hank Freeman — three-time consecutive World 3A Champion (2011-2013). Modeled after Freeman's previous signature, the Oscillator by 44RPM, the key change was moving from an inner rim to an outer rim design, dramatically shifting weight distribution and feel. The large outer stainless steel rims give the HPF impressive power and stability while the lighter overall weight keeps it fast and agile with excellent control. Designed as a 3A powerhouse but optimized for 1A and 5A as well, making it one of the most versatile models in the mowl lineup. The Driftline (2025) is its successor in the mowl line.

title: Surveillance Max
content:
History / About
The Surveillance Max takes the beloved Surveillance design and upgrades it with a 7075 aluminum body and repositioned stainless steel rims for a more modern performance profile. Released in January 2023 alongside the Heterogeneity Ti. The use of 7075 instead of 6061 allows for a lighter body with equivalent strength, enabling better weight distribution to the stainless steel rims. The result is a more competition-focused version of the Surveillance with improved stability and spin time over the original.

title: SUS 001 G2 FD Generator
content: About the SUS 001 G2 FD GeneratorThe G2 FD is a signature edition of the G2 Generator developed for Fumiaki Daito, known as "MC Fumin" — a Japanese yo-yo player and freestyle MC who finished 5th at the national 1A championship. Daito's preference for a wider catch zone and more outer-edge weight led to a ~2mm width increase to 48.46mm with adjusted rim mass distribution versus the standard G2.

title: SUS 001 G2 Generator
content: About the SUS 001 G2 GeneratorThe G2 Generator is a full redevelopment of the original SUS 001 built around A7003 aluminum and a hollow stainless steel rim. The hollow construction delivers more rim mass at the same total weight, boosting spin power without exceeding 65g. The step-round profile and widened 46mm catch zone — 2mm wider than the G1 — targets horizontal tricks and chopstick combinations.

title: SUS 001 G3 Generator
content: About the SUS 001 G3 GeneratorThe G3 Generator is the lightest version of the Generator line at 63.8g, down 1g from the G2. Midship rim placement — moving mass toward center compared to the G2's outer rim — produces a different spin character suited to versatile play. A curved bearing replaces the Center Track found in earlier iterations.

title: SUS 001 Generator
content: About the SUS 001 GeneratorThe Generator was SUS YOYO MECHANICS' debut original design, released in early 2018 as a prize in Yo-Yo Store REWIND's New Year Lucky Bag. Slightly undersized at 55mm with a 44mm catch zone, it was built for stability and long-spin performance. The stainless steel rim concentrates weight at the outer edge without sacrificing the compact feel that defines the SUS design philosophy.

title: SUS 002 Transmission
content: About the SUS 002 TransmissionThe SUS 002 Transmission is a full-aluminum monometal built around the undersized yo-yo concept SUS developed from studying the 2014 Trick-Motion bimetal. At 52.5mm diameter with a 47mm wide body, the Transmission amplifies feedback from each trick element — string contact and bearing load communicate with more sensitivity than standard-sized designs. The name references automotive transmission, extending the mechanical engineering philosophy of the brand.

title: SUS 003 G2 Transmission Cross Ratio
content: About the SUS 003 G2 Transmission Cross RatioThe G2 Cross Ratio refines the original SUS 003 with the "Control Edge" redesign — a revised rim profile that narrows overall width by ~1mm to 46.2mm while maintaining the close-ratio power delivery. Released in Matte Pink/Gold Rim colorway.

title: SUS 003 Transmission Cross Ratio
content: About the SUS 003 Transmission Cross RatioThe Transmission Cross Ratio takes the SUS 002's undersized philosophy into bimetal territory. At 51.94mm diameter with 76% of total weight in the stainless steel rim, the yo-yo generates spin power far beyond what its compact size suggests. The "close-ratio" name references automotive gear theory — optimized power delivery across a narrow range. Colorways follow a custom automotive paint theme.

title: SUS 004 IGNIS
content: About the SUS 004 IGNISThe SUS 004 IGNIS is the fourth SUS original — a bimetal designed as the competition signature for Ryosuke Ito, a Japanese 3A specialist. At 53.94mm, it sits at the compact end of competitive sizing to thread through the dense string configurations of complex 3A combinations. The 46mm width ensures reliable catches on shortened string paths typical of 3A play. Released in Purple/Silver Rim.

title: Act
content: About the ActThe Act was SUS YOYO MECHANICS' first dedicated 3A design, created for Yo-Yo Store REWIND instructor Shotaro Matsuda. Where the Trial uses an inner rim, the Act uses an outer stainless rim — placing maximum weight at the outer edge for longer spin times across the demanding multi-yoyo sequences of 3A. At 56.97mm diameter and 42mm width, it provides a slightly larger catch zone than the Trial while remaining narrow enough for 3A string management.

title: Act 2
content: About the Act 2The Act 2 is a full redesign of Shotaro Matsuda's signature 3A bimetal. Diameter trimmed from 56.97mm to 56.85mm and weight reduced 0.3g. The most significant change is the narrowed gap which improves bind reliability — critical when handling two yo-yos simultaneously in 3A competition.

title: Act 3
content: About the Act 3The Act 3 is the third signature bimetal in Shotaro Matsuda's series developed by SUS YOYO MECHANICS for Yo-Yo Store REWIND. Building on refinements made in the Act 2, the Act 3 continues the competition-focused 3A design language of the series.

title: ExtenTion
content: About the ExtenTionThe ExtenTion is a full titanium yo-yo developed by SUS YOYO MECHANICS for Yo-Yo Store REWIND's New Year Lucky Bag. At 50.25mm wide — an exceptional catch zone for titanium — and only 64.8g, it demonstrates the strength-to-weight potential of titanium construction. Available exclusively through REWIND Lucky Bag programs.

title: Melfore
content: About the MelforeThe Melfore is a three-way collaboration between Yo-Yo Store REWIND, SUS YOYO MECHANICS, and Chinese player Yi Chenghao. It marks SUS's first foray into 2A looping design and incorporates Yi Chenghao's proprietary "Windball" response technology. Released as the signature model of REWIND instructor Yuki Takami.

title: Newt
content: About the NewtThe Newt applies the Viper Remix's aluminum-and-TPU hybrid construction to a 1A string-trick context. The aluminum body provides competition-grade performance while replaceable TPU wing inserts absorb knocks during practice. At 63.67mm diameter and 66g, it occupies standard competition sizing while offering the durability advantage of the hybrid design.

title: SUS Transmission High Gear
content: About the SUS Transmission High GearThe Transmission High Gear carries the undersized H-profile formula of the SUS 002 Transmission into a full titanium build. The material change delivers higher rigidity at the same mass, producing crisper feedback and longer spin times. At 52.94mm diameter and 66.5g in titanium, the High Gear is the premium expression of the Transmission design language.

title: Trial
content: About the TrialThe Trial is a competition bimetal developed by SUS YOYO MECHANICS for Yo-Yo Store REWIND instructor Yuki Takami. Unlike conventional outer-rim bimetals, the Trial uses an inner-rim stainless steel construction that positions the added mass closer to the axle, producing a different spin character suited to 3A pair play. The rounded rim profile accommodates the hand-contact demands of 3A combinations.

title: Viper Remix
content: About the Viper RemixThe Viper Remix is an off-string yo-yo developed in collaboration between Yo-Yo Store REWIND and SUS YOYO MECHANICS, with approval from Henrys — the German manufacturer behind the original Viper off-string design. An A7003 aluminum hub pairs with replaceable TPU polymer wings that absorb impact on drops, reducing breakage risk on hard surfaces. Multiple colorway editions have been released since 2022.

title: Sushi
content:
The following is archived from RSO's website:

SUSHIHOLIC

I am not a sushi connoisseur but definitely a sushiholic. Like most of you, I would be more than satisfied with a simple pre-packaged sushi roll from the supermarket! My love for sushi stems from my fondness for Japan. In 2015, I proposed to my then-girlfriend on top of the Tokyo Skytree and attended the World Yo-Yo Contest. Fast forward to 2019, with a 6-month old toddler in tow, our little family toured the beautiful cities of Kyoto and Osaka. I am definitely going back to Japan when travel restrictions ease.

A sushi chef inside Sushi Dai.

A long queue outside Sushi Dai.

Inside the Tsukiji market, which has since relocated.

Japanese sushi chefs' love and respect for sushi preparation are awe-inspiring. Often lauded for their culinary excellence, they are immensely passionate about their craft and spend years honing their skills. You would easily find a delicious sushi meal in any random restaurant in Japan.

I have adopted a similar mindset for all RSO releases so far. RSO yo-yos are prototyped extensively, and the journey is comprehensively documented. Considerable time is also spent on the story, artwork, engraving, accessories and packaging for each release. These add production costs to each yo-yo, but RSO has been able to keep its prices similar to (if not lower than) many companies who mainly sell bare-bones titanium yo-yos today.

For an RSO yo-yo named Sushi, the intricate details had to be absolutely perfect.

My then-fiance (now wife) in Sushi Zanmai.

LET’S ROLL

Production Sushi yo-yo.

Since the release of Gravity, I have been brainstorming for unique shapes that differ from the primarily organic RSO lineup. One of the most coveted RSO yo-yos is the titanium Bowl: Japan Edition, which had a ramen theme. Naturally, making a second yo-yo inspired by another Japanese food staple was always on the cards.

This may sound ridiculous, but I went to great lengths to ensure that the yo-yo halves would look like they were cut from a sushi roll. The pieces form a cylinder when lined up together.

Forming a Sushi roll with Sushi halves.

Why did I choose disc Side Effects (SE) for Sushi?

Disc SE are the only ones suitable for Sushi, as any other SE would reveal the hub and make the yo-yo look… “un-sushi-like”. A piece of sushi does not have a nipple in the center. Note that while disc SE fit the overall Sushi look, the same cannot be said for most other yo-yos (particularly V-shaped ones like Droid).

Moreover, it has been a long time since One Drop released a yo-yo that ships with disc SE. A yo-yo equipped with disc SE would have a novelty factor and would have some appeal.

The disc SE are one of the heaviest SE available at 7.2g and only come in aluminium. One Drop does not make them in brass for obvious reasons. Even with disc SE installed, the shipping weight of Sushi is a very delectable 63.7g, due to the relatively low base weight of the yo-yo halves. With aluminium ultralight SE (2.5g) installed, Sushi weighs a mere 59.0g.

Having a palatable weight is a fundamental requirement for any yo-yo. Caps play an essential role in weight variation and changing the playfeel of the yo-yo, in addition to their ancillary function of improving the yo-yo’s aesthetics. I did not want Sushi to weigh a hernia inducing 70g with the caps installed. With aluminium ultralight SE and the heaviest caps available installed, Sushi only weighs 64.6g.

Sushi is not a rim-weighted yo-yo, less so than Gravity. I designed Gravity to closely match the Freehand 1’s weight (65.8g) with aluminium ultralight SE, and the Freehand Zero caps (2.7g each) installed. Sushi had to weigh less to avoid a “heavy” playfeel. Each half of Sushi is almost 1g lighter than a Gravity half.

The magical thing about disc SE is that because they are so heavy and have a much broader profile, swapping them out for another SE changes the yo-yo’s playfeel significantly more than other SE types.

With the included disc SE, Sushi plays unhurried, controlled and steady, just like an omakase meal you would have at a top tier Michelin starred sushi restaurant. I would describe the playfeel as “floaty”.

However, suppose you want a quick sushi fix; simply swap out the disc SE for aluminium ultralight SE (not included). Sushi weighs a mere 59.0g in this configuration and plays zippy and light, and is bound to instantly satisfy your sushi cravings.

Don’t be fooled by Sushi’s squarish shape - it is pretty comfortable to hold. Despite its reasonably high walls, it has a generous gap and handles multiple string layers effortlessly. It is also one of the more stable RSO throws so far. Without having to consciously try to ensure that the yo-yo does not tilt, you can be fully focused on the gastronomic experience.

DANCE TO A DIFFERENT TUNA

The Sushi shape might look simple, but it is one of the yo-yos I spent the most time prototyping after Doombot and Droid. My insistence on retaining the cylindrical shape was the root of all the problems.

52mm 6061 aluminium Sushi prototype with a hollow construct.

Sushi started out as a 52 mm diameter aluminum yo-yo with a hollow construct. My initial plan was anodize the caps in different colors to match typical sushi ingredients (for example, yellow for tamago, pink for sashimi and orange for uni). I could do a fairly large run and price them low so that more people would be able to own an RSO.

The caps were CNC machined out of 6061 aluminium, and measured 1 mm at their thinnest portions. They were also made marginally bigger than the cap grooves, allowing them to be pressed fit into the yo-yo firmly.

The aluminium prototype failed miserably. The yo-yo was smooth if assembled without the caps, but installing the caps would introduce intolerable pulse vibe. It was the most vibey prototype since I started making yo-yos. The problem was that the caps were too thin and had warped during the machining or press-fit process. This prototype plays extremely floaty.

Spaceship (left), a 54 mm diameter yo-yo, next to the aluminium Sushi prototype (right), a 52 mm diameter yo-yo. Photo by Shimon Osada (@shimoff_2).

The solution seemed simple initially - just make the caps thicker! However, I could not remove enough weight from the yo-yo body to redistribute to the caps after countless attempts. In addition, the inherent cylindrical shape of the yo-yo necessitated a significant amount of material at the yo-yo’s rims since the rims extend outwards to span almost the entire width of the yo-yo. Conversely, a V-shaped yo-yo with similar dimensions would take up less weight (if you find it hard to visualize this, just compare the volumes of a cylinder and a cone).

Sushi was only possible with a titanium SE design, which allowed for retention of a similar aesthetic with caps installed. As much as I love how yo-yos play in titanium more than aluminium, there was a lot of inertia to take this route because the small size of the market for such a peculiar shape. Would anyone buy a titanium yo-yo with a squarish shape? I decided to bite the bullet anyway, ultimately making a small run of 62 yo-yos.

52mm titanium Sushi prototype. Note the different engraving from the production version.

The titanium prototype had one thing I did not like - its size. It felt large in the hand at 52 mm, and… wait for it… it was not small enough to look like a convincing piece of sushi (you must be tired of my obsession with making the yo-yo look exactly like a piece of sushi by now). The 52 mm diameter also made the disc SE look relatively small and not “fill” the hub.

Ideally, I would have liked the yo-yo diameter to be 50 mm. However, I wanted to make the accessories backwards compatible with Gravity and was constrained by the 48 mm diameter of the Freehand Zero caps. Sufficient material is needed at the cap groove for the yo-yo to be machinable. I eventually settled for a 50.5 mm diameter for the production version of Sushi, with the thickness of the cap groove measuring a safe 1.25 mm.

Before I put Sushi into production, a final prototype with a 50.5 mm diameter was made.

From left to right: 52 mm titanium prototype, 50.5 mm production version, 52 mm aluminium prototype.

TASTES BETTER, TOGETHER

I spared no effort in creating the complete package for Sushi.

Like Gravity, Sushi comes with a set of rings and caps, allowing for weight variation. Due to the collaborative nature of the Gravity project and associated cost constraints, a full set of custom CNC machined polycarbonate rings was only included with the Lunar Edition Gravity. This time, the full set is included with every Sushi, at a lower price compared to Gravity.

The components included with Sushi are as follows:

Yo-yo body, 53.7g

RSO CLYW Slim / G-grip Sized Landing Pads and Yoyorecreation NSK platinum double straight C Bearing, 2.3g

Aluminium disc One Drop SE, 7.2g

Pair of rubber cylindrical weight rings, 3.6g

Pair of custom polycarbonate thin rings, 2.8 g

Pair of custom polycarbonate thick rings, 4.4g

Pair of custom polycarbonate caps, 5.6g

Pair of FHZ caps, 5.4g

From left to right, custom CNC machined thin weight ring (1.4g), thick ring (2.2g) and cap (2.8g)

The polycarbonate rings and caps were custom CNC machined to achieve a perfect fit. They have a slightly different design compared to the ones included with Gravity. The hole in the center of the thick rings measures about an inch, which is a hair wider than the disc SE and allows the SE to pass through.

The weight rings, weighing 1.8g each, sit just underneath the caps. Sushi uses the same rubber weight rings as Gravity and the titanium Silver Bullet.

Thin polycarbonate weight ring, weighing 1.4g each.

Thick polycarbonate weight ring, weighing 2.2g each.

Polycarbonate cap, weighing 2.8g each.

Three pairs of meticulously designed stickers were produced. They fit perfectly on the included polycarbonate caps to make your yo-yo look exactly like a piece of sushi.

Blank Freehand Zero caps, weighing 2.7g each.

FEAST YOUR EYES

The artwork is by RSO’s resident artist, ATILA.

The cover star is a sumo wrestler inspired by one of my favorite Street Fighter characters of all time, E-Honda.

For the side flaps, I referenced a few scenes which depict the sushi-making process from the movie Jiro Dreams of Sushi. Despite being in his late nineties, its chef Jiro Ono is still involved in the restaurant’s daily operations.

Special thanks to RSO’s long time friends, Yuuki Yoneno (@ynnyuux) and Shimon Osada (@shimoff_2), who helped with the Japanese banners in the background.

Sushi includes a redesigned cap removal tool. The new tool is longer, which allows the caps to be removed easily.

The enamel pin features a hangiri, a traditional tub used to mix sushi rice.

The certificate of authenticity features an oroshigane, used for grating wasabi.

WHAT’S IN THE BOX

A PAIR OF POLYCARBONATE CAPS

A PAIR OF THICK POLYCARBONATE RINGS

A PAIR OF THIN POLYCARBONATE RINGS

A PAIR OF DUNCAN FREEHAND ZERO CAPS

A PAIR OF RUBBER WEIGHT RINGS

NEW IMPROVED CAP REMOVAL TOOL

OROSHIGANE Certificate of AUTHENTICITY

HANGIRI ENAMEL PIN

RICE PRINT PROTECTIVE CLOTH

CLYW SLIM / G-GRIP SIZE WHITE TYPE 50 RSO LANDING PADS

GREEN STRING

title: Sushi – Japan Edition
content:
History / About
Sushi - Japan Edition is the first production run to reach the "originally envisioned" 50mm diameter for the Sushi platform, after six years of prototyping. Two colorways: Otoro (Ti40A titanium alloy, bluefin-tuna marbling engraving, green Side Effects, 25 units, $329.99) and Uni (Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy, sea-urchin-lobe engraving, orange Side Effects, 17 units, $379.99). Includes Tokyo sushi-pilgrimage documentary photography and an enamel pin. One Drop supplies the Micro Cap Side Effects hardware as a component partner.
