A collaboration with CLYW producing a titanium version of the iconic CLYW Peak — one of the most historically significant yo-yo shapes in the hobby. Released around 2020 and primarily distributed through Luftverk’s personal archive rather than a standard retail drop. Production run details were not widely publicized, making this one of the rarer Luftverk collaborations. The Peak profile holds deep cultural significance in the yoyo community as the model that helped launch CLYW and defined an era of play.

title: Titanium Pelican 2
content:
History / About
The Ti Pelican 2 is a 2025 full titanium release, revisiting a Pelican design that originally appeared in G2's 2018 lineup as a 6061 aluminum model. The jump from 6061 to titanium represents G2's most dramatic material upgrade for any single design in their catalog. Listed at $299+ based on comparable G2 titanium releases.

title: Titanium Respawn
content:
About
Titanium Respawn is a titanium yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos, released 2024. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Titanium Sunbird
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"The Titanium Sunbird follows the tradition of the hummingbird yoyo series, with high speed, acceleration, and power. It features a 0.5mm thin wall, a lot of rim weight, some of the never before seen titanium colorways, all made possible by our incredible manufacturing prowess. We hope the Ti Sunbird will enhance your titanium yoyo experience."

title: Titanium Triton
content:
History / About
The Titanium Triton brings G2's foundational 2013 design into premium titanium construction. A rare and collectible piece — secondary market listings note the V1 prototype is blasted raw titanium. The Ti Triton follows in the tradition of the TiShee (Ti Banshee, 2019) as G2's premium titanium offerings. Jacob Gross signed each unit.

title: TiWing
content:
Overview
The TiWing is a TISS (titanium inner shell with stainless steel rings) from Damian Puckett, produced circa 2023 in an extremely limited quantity. Described by secondary market sellers as very rare. Secondary market trades documented at approximately $185. Full specifications have not been published.

title: TM
content:
About
TM is the signature model of Mizuki Takimoto, 2019 Japan National 3A champion. Its cross-sectional silhouette traces Takimoto's initials “T” and “M” into the profile shape — a concept-first design that Takimoto nonetheless competed with and won the North Japan regional tournament using.

title: Arne
content:
History / About
The Arne is one of tmbr.'s later production models. Handmade in Canada from quality hardwood, the Arne continues tmbr.'s mission of producing premium fixed-axle wooden yo-yos for the modern revival community.

title: Baldwin
content:
About
The Baldwin is TMBR's smaller-diameter butterfly model, offering a different feel from the larger Irving and Fremont. Its profile includes an interior step that makes it particularly well-suited to stall techniques and regenerations. Distinctive "Dado Cap" inlays on the faces serve both a decorative and functional purpose — they provide a visual indicator of spin speed for stall timing.
The original (2012–2013) used a fixed wooden axle. A 2015 redesign introduced the Woodthread Axle System, allowing reversibility between butterfly and imperial configurations and gap adjustment. The model continued in production with periodic restock announcements through approximately 2020.

title: Bassline
content:
History / About
The Bassline is part of tmbr.'s mature lineup, offering a lower-profile shape that sits comfortably in the hand and plays smoothly on the string. Like all tmbr. products it is handmade in Canada.

title: Carlson
content:
About
The Carlson is one of TMBR's later-era production models, available in multiple wood species including ash, maple, and oak. A compact variant called the Carlson CS was also produced — a slightly smaller Carlson in oak. Secondary market activity places Carlson sales primarily between 2018 and 2020.

title: Citizen
content:
History / About
The Citizen is a mid-lineup model from tmbr., positioned as an accessible everyday fixed-axle throw. Handmade in Canada from quality hardwood, it embodies tmbr.'s philosophy of producing well-crafted wooden yo-yos for the modern fixed-axle revival community.

title: Codington
content:
History / About
The Codington is a model from tmbr.'s expanded catalog. Handmade in Canada, it offers the quality all-wood construction that tmbr. is known for in the fixed-axle revival community.

title: Daytripper
content:
History / About
The Daytripper is a core production model from tmbr., designed as a comfortable companion for extended fixed-axle sessions. Its name reflects tmbr.'s ethos of building yo-yos meant to be played daily rather than displayed. Handmade in Canada from quality hardwood.

title: deHcade
content:
About
The deHcade is both Ed Haponik's tenth anniversary signature yoyo and TMBR's last model before the company closed circa 2023. Released December 21, 2021 at 8 PM EST, the initial drop of 40 pieces sold out in under a minute.
The name "deHcade" fuses "decade" with Ed's signature "H" — commemorating ten years (2012–2021) of the eH annual signature line. The design pulls from across the eH history: red oak and raised gap profile echo the original 2012 eH; the Woodthread Axle System derives from the 2014–2017 "eHra." A raised hub shifts weight away from the rim, improving flip tricks and stall-regenerations. Engraved with the phrase "throw grace, catch joy." Additional production runs followed the initial drop.

title: eH
content:
About
The eH is Ed Haponik's annual signature yoyo — a collaboration between TMBR (manufacturing), SPYY (design), and pro player Ed Haponik. The name "eH" combines Ed's initials: lowercase "e" and uppercase "H." The line ran as a holiday limited release each year from 2012 to 2016, with "20-eHteen" in 2018, and concluded with the deHcade in December 2021 (documented separately).
The eH was born from Ed's "#365yoyotricks" project — a year of performing tricks exclusively on fixed-axle yoyos — and TMBR manufactured the first two prototypes for that project. The design became TMBR's most collectible line.
Annual Releases

2012 (1st): Red oak body, walnut peg axle. ~40 pieces. $35. Two original prototypes preceded the production run.
2013 (2nd): ~61mm × 35.6mm, 55g. White oak (denser than 2012's red oak). Take-apart wooden peg. Darker engravings. ~$35–$50.
2014 (3rd): White oak. First year with Woodthread Axle System — reversible butterfly/imperial/pagoda configurations. Described as "entirely new beast" vs earlier versions.
2015 (4th): ~61mm × 35.6mm, 55g. White oak, tight grain, hand-carved Woodthread axle. 96 pieces. ~$75. Includes signed note from Ed Haponik. One side engraved "eH" logo, other plain.
2016 (5th): 4 exotic woods — Wenge, Bubinga, Zebrano, Ebony (only 2 Ebony, raffle only). Standard woods $85; Ebony $200.
20-eHteen (2018): Released 2018; sold via eBay for $80–$145 on secondary market.

title: Fremont
content:
About
The Fremont (sometimes spelled "Freemont" in early TMBR marketing) is a classic butterfly-shaped counterpart to the Irving, offering a high-wall profile particularly suited to looping tricks, regenerations, and stalls. Named after another Portland neighborhood, it shares the Irving's oversized diameter and philosophy but in a rounder, wider form.
The original November 2011 release used a simple fixed walnut peg axle. A 2015 revision introduced the Woodthread Axle System for adjustable gap and take-apart convenience. A 2020 production run continued the model into TMBR's later era. Available in maple (standard), cherry, and oak.

title: Irving
content:
About
The Irving is the yoyo that launched TMBR in September 2011 and established the company's reputation for fixed-axle throws capable of modern string trick play. Named after a Portland neighborhood, it features a flat-rimmed body profile with a tapered string gap and a through-hole on one side for knot tying. Slightly oversized at 59mm for extended spin time. The original production used a simple walnut peg axle; a take-apart version followed shortly after.
Limited-edition runs were produced in exotic woods including zebrawood, purpleheart, and padauk. A 2019 production run was released alongside the Morrow. The Irving remained in the catalog as TMBR's flagship model throughout the company's lifespan.

title: Irving Pro
content:
About
The Irving Pro is a redesign of TMBR's founding Irving model with a noticeably wider profile (34.58mm vs 28mm) optimized for string tricks. The added width improves string layering and catch-zone geometry. Take-apart design gives string access and allows axle replacement. Some players added Duncan silicone response pads to the Irving Pro to increase the response spectrum. Maple body with walnut axle, consistent with TMBR's standard construction.

title: Jack
content:
History / About
The Jack is the debut model from tmbr., Canada's boutique fixed-axle wood yo-yo company founded by Colin Leland. Hand-turned from quality hardwood, the Jack introduced tmbr.'s signature all-wood construction philosophy to the fixed-axle revival community. It remains a benchmark for traditional wooden yo-yo play.

title: Lincoln
content:
About
The Lincoln is TMBR's flat-pack, self-assembly yoyo — similar in concept to 44RPM's Flat Pack series. Players receive the components and assemble the yoyo themselves before play. YoYoExpert posted assembly instructions alongside the release. Limited documentation is available; the model appears to have been a limited run in TMBR's 2015–2016 era.

title: LoveJoy
content:
About
The LoveJoy is described by TMBR as "the yoyo that brings modern string tricks to fixed axle." Its wider body (34.925mm) and tapered gap with chamfered edges are designed to maximize string catch and layering, allowing string trick sequences that would otherwise require a bearing yoyo. Rounded rims improve knuckle comfort. One of TMBR's later catalog additions, appearing in restock announcements from 2016 through approximately 2019.

title: Morrison
content:
About
The Morrison is one of TMBR's early 2012 production models. Limited documentation is available compared to the Irving and Fremont lines. Consistent with TMBR's construction approach: hand-turned wood body, fixed wooden axle, designed for fixed-axle string play. Named in keeping with TMBR's Portland-neighborhood naming conventions.

title: Morrow
content:
About
The Morrow was released in 2019 alongside an updated production run of the Irving. It features a round, comfortable V-shaped gap and smooth rounded rims designed to minimize knuckle impact during finger stalls. Described as stable on flip tricks and stall-regenerations, and smooth on regenerations. Combines comfort and performance in a later-era TMBR package.

title: Moxon
content:
About
The Moxon was announced alongside the Sullivan as part of a "Two Innovative New TMBR Yo-Yos" release circa 2014. It is a smaller and lighter yoyo than TMBR's other models, designed specifically to take advantage of the Woodthread Axle System's reversible configuration. Where the Sullivan's reversal changes feel dramatically, the Moxon's smaller halves give each orientation a distinct play personality suitable for both string tricks and looping.
The Moxon's most distinctive feature is its packaging: it ships in the original wood plank it was cut from, making each unit's origins visible and tangible.

title: Ply
content:
History / About
The Ply from tmbr. uses laminated hardwood layers (plywood) to create a visually distinctive yo-yo with consistent grain direction and predictable weight. Part of tmbr.'s commitment to exploring different wood construction techniques, the Ply appeals to fixed-axle enthusiasts who appreciate material variety in their wooden throws.

title: Scout
content:
History / About
The Scout is designed as a compact, lighter option within the tmbr. family, catering to players who prefer a smaller-diameter feel for stalls and classic fixed-axle maneuvers. Like all tmbr. products, it is handmade in Canada from quality hardwood.

title: Stave
content:
History / About
Named for the staves used in barrel construction, the tmbr. Stave uses a segmented wood assembly that gives it a distinct look and structural character. Part of tmbr.'s ongoing exploration of wood construction techniques.

title: Sullivan
content:
About
The Sullivan is one of TMBR's most technically ambitious designs: a yoyo with zero metal components. The body, axle, and all internal threading are wood, using TMBR's Woodthread Axle System. The reversible halves allow three profile configurations — butterfly (string tricks), imperial (looping), and a "pagoda" orientation described as novelty only. Announced alongside the Moxon in a "Two Innovative New TMBR Yo-Yos" announcement circa 2014.
The 100% wood construction makes the Sullivan unique in the yoyo market. Response and play feel are governed entirely by gap geometry and wood friction.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Fixed axle — Woodthread Axle System (all wood)

title: This-A-Way / That-A-Way
content:
About
The This-A-Way / That-A-Way (marketed as both names depending on configuration) is TMBR's dedicated dual-purpose design. Each half tapers differently: one face at 3/16" depth, the other at 3/32". Assembled with the deeper taper inward creates the slim "This-A-Way" looping profile; reversed creates the wider "That-A-Way" string-trick profile. One yoyo, two fundamentally different play styles.
Available in two finish levels and three wood species:

Standard: $39.99 — 180-grit sanded, unfinished, envelope packaging
Deluxe: $49.99 — 220-grit, oil/varnish finish, stamped lettering, plank packaging

Wood options: maple, oak, cherry. Uses the Woodthread 416 walnut axle system. Gap is adjustable at 2.65mm.

title: Turner
content:
About
The Turner is TMBR's larger, heavier fixed-axle alternative to the Baldwin, designed for improved stability and longer spin time. It shares the organic rounded profile of the Baldwin but at increased diameter (~57mm) and weight (58g). The gap is described as "tall and straight" with a small cutaway that gives a similar feel and trapeze catch to the Baldwin while adding stability. Take-apart design allows string access.
Walnut axle and cap are standard; exotic wood axle and cap options were offered for customization.

title: wood•z
content:
About
The wood•z (with a bullet-point separator) is a collaboration between TMBR (design and manufacture) and ZipLine Strings, a string maker based in Nampa, Idaho. TMBR built the yoyo; ZipLine packaged, branded, and distributed it. The design takes inspiration from the Duncan Pro-Z profile and the aesthetic of TMBR's own This-A-Way/That-A-Way.
At 55.79mm diameter and 41.05g, the wood•z is smaller and lighter than most TMBR models — designed as a casual EDC (everyday carry) throw rather than a performance-focused piece. Each comes with a commemorative button, sticker, and a length of ZipLine's signature [kot-n] cotton string. ZipLine recommends 100% cotton string for best response.
B-grade units were sold via ZipLine Strings's BigCartel store.

title: TMNT
content: TMNT was a licensed variant produced by Hummingbird in partnership with the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise during the height of the property's popularity in the early 1990s. This branded wooden yo-yo represented Hummingbird's success in securing major entertainment licenses and expanding beyond traditional yo-yo enthusiast markets into mainstream retail.

title: Toasted Burger
content:
History / About
Toasted Burger is a gold-electroplated-titanium variant of RSO's original Burger, limited to 25 units. "Return toppings" (lettuce/tomato accessories) were sold separately to preserve the plating. One Drop supplies the Side Effects hardware (Aluminium Dome), a component partnership rather than a full co-branded release — consistent with how the archive's existing Burger entry treats One Drop.

meta.yya_bearing_size: YoyoRecreation NSK Platinum Double Straight C
meta.yya_weight: 61.5g (with One Drop Aluminium Dome Side Effects)

title: Fat Cat
content: AboutThe Fat Cat is Tom Kuhn's most substantial aluminum yo-yo, heavier than the Tom Cat for longer spin times. Inspired by a jazz motif ("The FAT ONE"), it uses the same adjustable gap system and Turbo Disc response as the SB-2, in a butterfly profile. Vacuum-machined from aircraft aluminum to a hand-polished mirror finish. Every unit is individually numbered and dated, limited to 500 per production run.A 2024 edition (Fat Cat Unresponsive / "Fat Cat +") added a Size C bearing option for unresponsive play. Weight is configurable via rubber weight rings (59.53–68.04g depending on configuration).

meta.yya_bearing_size: Tom Kuhn Size I; Size C available (2024)

title: Lightning
content: AboutThe Lightning is a budget fixed-axle looping yo-yo produced by BC YoYo (Brad Countryman / What's Next Mfg.) under the Tom Kuhn brand umbrella. Its rainbow laminate cross-section reveals concentric rings of colored wood veneer. A classic looper at an entry-level price point. ~$9.99.

title: No Jive
content:
History / About
Tom Kuhn produced this custom No Jive exclusively for Yoyoguy.com, the retail arm of Infinite Illusions. Like all No Jive models, it is machined from northern hard maple and features the classic three-configuration axle system first introduced in 1977. The Infinite Illusions branding made it a collectible item for fans of both Tom Kuhn woodcraft and the Yoyoguy store.

title: No Jive 3-in-1
content: AboutThe No Jive 3-in-1 is one of the most historically significant yo-yos ever made. Patented in 1978 (U.S. Patent #4,127,950), it was the world's first take-apart modular wooden yo-yo, and a version of it has been in continuous production for nearly 50 years. The name came from a newsboy on Dr. Kuhn's porch: "No jive, you made that?" The three configurations — Imperial ("Classic"), Butterfly ("Flying Camel"), and Pagoda — are achieved by reversing the two halves without any tools.Made from Northern hard maple with a steel rod through a birch wood sleeve for the fixed axle. The body has been produced in natural maple, painted, laser-engraved, laminated (exotic wood cross-sections from 2001), and airbrushed versions across countless special editions over nearly five decades.Notable EditionsSan Francisco Woodies (1977): Earliest branded versions — Cliff House, Seal Rocks, Fisherman's Wharf, Cable Car, Golden Gate Bridge, Maple Leaf.Mandala series (1977+): Laser-carved geometric designs — Filigree, Snowflake, Starburst, Celtic Mandala (2000, designed by Matt Carter), Quatle Mandala (2002). The 1980 Smithsonian Jeweled Starburst Mandala, adorned by jeweler Sydney Mobell, sold for $10,000 and was donated to the Smithsonian Institution.Flying Camel (1977–1998): Butterfly-orientation carved versions; last run 1998.Celebrity/retail editions: Neiman Marcus No-Jive (c.1979), Abercrombie No-Jive (c.1987), Smothers Brothers "Smo Bro" (1980s, laser-carved signatures of Tommy and Dick Smothers; also Smothers Fine Wines edition), Olympic / Aspen No-Jive (1984), Datachecker/DTS.Anniversary editions: 10th Anniversary Diamond No-Jive (1987), 15th Anniversary (1992), 20th Anniversary Painted No-Jives (1997), 25th Anniversary No-Jive (2003), Big Yo 25th No-Jive (2004, oversized), Batik (2007, Indonesian art-inspired), 50th Anniversary (2026, dual-sided laser engraving).Current production (No Jive 3 body, 2007+): Maple Leaf, Mandala 6, and others. Available at tomkuhn.com and authorized retailers.

meta.yya_response: Fixed Axle (wood sleeve on steel rod)

title: Pocket Rocket
content: AboutThe Pocket Rocket is Tom Kuhn's miniature aluminum yo-yo, launched in 1999. At just 38mm in diameter it is the smallest yo-yo in the lineup. The first Tom Kuhn model to include the Turbo Disc response system, which went on to be used across all subsequent models. Every unit is individually serialized. Marketed as "Small is beautiful."Available in polished silver aluminum and multiple anodized "Light Elements" colorways. Ships with 4 Turbo Disc pads, extra string, pouch, and instruction booklet.

title: RD-1
content: AboutThe RD-1 (Recreational Device 1) is a laminated hard maple butterfly yo-yo with metal hub assemblies and removable rim weight rings for distribution adjustment. Unlike the Sleep Machine and Roller Woody, the RD-1's gap is not adjustable — it is fixed and tug-responsive, making it well-suited for beginners and intermediate players. Ships with 5 strings and an instruction booklet. Retailed at $29.99.

meta.yya_response: Turbo Disc Pad (fixed gap — tug responsive)

title: Redline
content: AboutThe Redline was designed to bring Tom Kuhn's bearing yo-yo technology to an affordable $10 price point. Features a speedometer/tachymeter gauge graphic on a black and silver painted maple body. A "Wood Rocks" variant was produced in 2005 to salute 35 years of Dr. Kuhn's dental practice. Simple, functional, and inexpensive — a gateway into the Tom Kuhn lineup.

title: Roller Woody
content: AboutThe Roller Woody is the Imperial-shaped sister model to the Sleep Machine, released simultaneously in 1992. One of the first wooden ball-bearing yo-yos ever produced. Uses the same Tom Kuhn Size I bearing, Turbo Disc response, and adjustable gap as the Sleep Machine, in a classic rounded Imperial profile. "Spins up to 10x longer than a standard fixed axle."Colorways include Natural, Black, and Blue. Rainbow laminate cross-section versions were introduced in 2001. Ongoing production by BC YoYo.

title: SBX 3-in-1
content: AboutThe SBX 3-in-1 brings the modular "3-in-1" philosophy of the No Jive into the metal era. A gold anodized aircraft aluminum yo-yo that converts between Responsive, Unresponsive, and Looping play modes by swapping the included axles, bearings, and spacers. Classic SB-2 styling updated for modern play. Limited to 500 units. Also available in a "Tangerine Yo-Yo Set" bundle with a complementary fixed-axle Tangerine wooden yo-yo.

title: Silver Bullet
content: AboutThe Silver Bullet (sometimes called SB-1) is recognized as the first full-metal yo-yo ever produced. Released in 1984 by Dr. Tom Kuhn, it uses the same take-apart construction as the No Jive but in aircraft-grade aluminum, with the characteristic bullet-shaped hub nubs on each half that give the line its name. A fixed wooden axle sleeve is retained from the No Jive design.Production ran from 1984 to 1991, with the first run reaching only approximately 60 units before quality review. Optional weight rings were available. A rare anodized variant (50 units, clear anodize) exists. In 2012, 50 standalone Silver Bullets were produced as part of a collector's Silver Bullet Series Set.The Silver Bullet is considered an artifact of yoyo history: every full-metal yo-yo that followed owes something to this design. The SB-1 is held at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C.

title: Silver Bullet 2
content: AboutThe Silver Bullet 2 (SB-2) is one of the most significant yo-yos in history: the first commercially produced ball-bearing metal yo-yo. Released in November 1990, it achieved 14,300 RPM and 100 mph rim speed as measured by U.S. National Grand Master Dale Oliver in 1991. It was individually numbered and sold with a collector's box, tuning tool, 5-string pack, velvet storage bag, and rubber weights.NASA astronauts flew the SB-2 aboard a Space Shuttle, validating its physics beyond Earth's atmosphere. The Turbo Disc response system was developed alongside the SB-2. The adjustable gap (3.2–4.2 mm) was a breakthrough for customizing string response.Multiple anodized colorways were produced: Blue, Red, Gold, Silver, Purple Splash, Bronze Splash, and the "Infrared" edition. Production was initially by Tom Kuhn directly; from 1999 onward via Brad Countryman's What's Next Mfg. / BC YoYo. The SB-2 remains in production and is considered the ancestor of every modern bearing yo-yo.

title: Silver Bullet 3
content: AboutThe Silver Bullet 3 (SB-3) features a unique "Click Adjust" ratchet twist gap system — unique among all Tom Kuhn metal yo-yos. Machined from highly polished aircraft aluminum. Initially produced in a run of about 15 units; a 100-unit production run in 2012 yielded 50 standalone units and 50 included in the Silver Bullet Series Set (with SB-1 and SB-2), priced at $699.99 for the complete set.

meta.yya_response: Turbo Disc Pad / Click Adjust ratchet gap

title: Silver Bullet 4
content: AboutThe Silver Bullet 4 (SB-4) marks a significant turn in Tom Kuhn history: the first competition-grade throw, the first butterfly-shape Silver Bullet, and the first Tom Kuhn to use a standard large Size C bearing for unresponsive play. Designed and produced in collaboration with Chico YoYo Company (CYYC), with CBC Slim Pads for silicone pad response — departing from Tom Kuhn's proprietary Turbo Disc system.Available in Classic Silver (polished raw aluminum) and Cobalt Blue Mandala (tomkuhn.com exclusive). Retailed through YoYoExpert. ~$145–$150.

title: Silver Bullet Titanium
content: AboutThe Silver Bullet Titanium is a collaboration between Tom Kuhn and Round Spinning Objects (RSO), released August 15, 2020. A titanium take on the iconic Silver Bullet profile, with the original Silver Bullet font engraving. Sold through YoYoExpert and the RSO store; sold out rapidly. A collector's piece celebrating the Silver Bullet legacy in the most premium material.Factory default is responsive play via a slim bearing. Alternate configurations are possible with included components: two custom machined bearing blanks, shorter axles, and two black rubber weight rings (1.8g each) to expand weight to 64.6g. Total weight with rings: 64.6g.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Slim bearing (responsive factory default); Size C compatible

title: Sleep Machine
content: AboutThe Sleep Machine debuted in 1992 alongside the Roller Woody as one of the first wooden ball-bearing yo-yos. In a single jump it beat the previous wooden yo-yo sleep record by a factor of 10. The butterfly-shaped hard maple body uses the same Tom Kuhn Size I bearing and Turbo Disc response as the SB-2, with an adjustable gap screw. The interior is engraved with string-winding instructions.Colorways include Natural maple, Black, and White/Blue. Laminated versions with exotic wood cross-sections were introduced in 2001. A "Solarflare" special edition was also produced. Ongoing production by BC YoYo.

title: TK60
content: AboutThe TK60 was produced in a very limited run to commemorate Dr. Thomas Kuhn's 60th birthday in 2003. Machined from walnut wood in an Imperial profile with hollow sides and removable metal weight rings — the same concept later reused for the RD-2 production model. Among the rarest Tom Kuhn wooden yo-yos.

title: Tom Cat
content: AboutThe Tom Cat is Tom Kuhn's aluminum butterfly yo-yo, released in 2001. Built on the same size and profile as the SB-2 but in butterfly shape, it uses the same adjustable gap system and Turbo Disc response. Removable power rings allow weight customization. A jazz-inspired design character.Special editions include: "Acid-wash talisman" colorway (limited to 500 serialized units), "Tom Cat & The Rose," gold unresponsive version, and a special-edition responsive configuration. Ships with 5 strings, 8 Turbo Disc pads, 2 power rings, laser holster, gap adjustment keychain, and instruction booklet.

title: Turbo-Yo
content: AboutThe Turbo-Yo is the pre-production bearing prototype that preceded the Silver Bullet 2, produced in September 1990. Only 39 units were made. At $100 apiece, it came with spare bearings, adjusting screws, optional weight rings, cotton strings, and a string gap tool.During testing, Dr. Kuhn himself performed 102 consecutive Around the Worlds with a rubber-ring-equipped Turbo-Yo. The design was refined into the Silver Bullet 2 just two months later. The Turbo-Yo is the zero-to-one moment for all bearing metal yo-yos: the first time a ball bearing was fitted to an all-metal throw in any form.

title: Tomato Soup
content:
Interested in 3D-printed yo-yo? Grab the files here: Tomato Soup, the YoYo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a fixed axle (no bearing) octagonal yoyo. It has been designed to be printable in one piece with no assembly required, just need a yoyo string. 

Inside the gap, not visible from the outside are 6 holes that serve as the yoyo's response system (what makes it go back up the string when you tug)

The dimple is there for pull starts and other tricks. 

Recommended to print it in as thin a layer lines as possible (.05, .07 etc) in order to not wear down strings and have best playability. Ideal weight varies person to person but I found 56 grams to be idea, so slice accordingly with extra perimeters."

title: Tomo
content:
History / About
Tomo (とも, Japanese for "friend/buddy") is the sole yo-yo model ever released by ikimono, launched in August 2024 as the brand's first product after more than a year of prototyping. It's an undersized W-shape/inverted monometal in 7075 aluminum with machined acrylic accent rings, marketed as a comforting, casual everyday throw rather than a competition design. Ikimono followed the standard release with a limited engraved collaboration edition and a discounted "b-grade" batch of cosmetic seconds in September 2024, both of which sold out. The brand has since gone on hiatus and its website is offline.

title: Tomo (Unknown Edition)
content:
History / About
A limited collaboration edition of ikimono's Tomo, produced with Unknown — the yo-yo scene engraving/apparel brand founded by six-time National Yo-Yo Champion Bryan Figueroa. Same base shape and dimensions as the standard Tomo, finished in black satin/matte blast with engraved artwork on both halves and a hidden engraving under the acrylic rings on one side, reading "The only one who can sympathize with you and understand you is you." The edition sold out within about an hour of release and now trades well above retail among collectors.

title: Pocketmate No. 19 “D-51 Yo-Yo”
content: History / AboutThe D-51 Yo-Yo is listed as Tomy Pocketmate No. 19 (1975) among the yo-yos Tomy released. No further details could be verified.

title: Pocketmate No. 20 “Racing Yo-Yo”
content: History / AboutThe Racing Yo-Yo is listed as Tomy Pocketmate No. 20 (1975) among the yo-yos Tomy released. No further details could be verified.

title: Screw Ball
content: History / AboutThe Screw Ball was an auto-return yo-yo produced by Abbe Toys and distributed by Tomy exclusively in Japan during the late-1990s yo-yo boom. It was the Japanese version of the Australian Yo-Matic Black Mamba. It uses a centrifugal cam system for returning to the hand, with a three-star transaxle sleeve. The version described is clear with holographic gold decals.

title: Screw Ball Mini
content: History / AboutThe Screw Ball Mini was produced by Abbe Toys and distributed by Tomy in Japan in 1998 as the miniature version of the Screw Ball. At 50 g it is heavy for its size thanks to metal disks on the inner surfaces. It was designed by Takahiko Hasegawa (Taka), who tested mini yo-yos of 34 to 42 mm during prototyping and concluded 38 mm (plus or minus 1 mm) was the optimal minimum diameter. Unlike the Screw Ball it cannot auto-return; the clutch inside one half is for show. Hironori Mii used it for the hardest challenge of Team Off-String. A limited Famitsu edition was also released.

title: Screw Ball Mini (Famitsu Bros. Special Limited Edition)
content: History / AboutA limited promotional edition of the Screw Ball Mini given out in the video game magazine Monthly Famitsu Bros., featuring the likeness of Necky the Fox, the cartoon mascot created by manga artist Susumu Matsushita.

title: Toonie
content: AboutThe Toonie follows the brass Loonie in Rain City's Canadian coin micro series, but steps up to a bi-metal construction: an aluminum body with a stainless steel rim ring for improved stability. Named after the Canadian $2 coin (the "toonie"). Includes LEGO fingerspin cups and arrives in a leather wallet.

title: Annihilation
content: AboutThe Annihilation is the bimetal signature model for Lin Junyi, 2018 CYCC Luyu Regional Champion and 2021 Online World Championships finalist. Machined from 7068 aluminum — a harder, denser alloy — with stainless steel rims, the Annihilation is wide at 47.4mm and focused on high-speed braking control and maximum stability. Despite its competition specifications, the weight feels heavier on the string than the numbers suggest.

title: Annihilation Mono
content: AboutThe Annihilation Mono is the monometal counterpart to Lin Junyi's bimetal Annihilation. Machined from 7003 aluminum at the same 56mm × 47.4mm dimensions, the monometal version comes in at a notably heavy 68.8g — designed to deliver the braking performance and on-string feel that Lin Junyi's high-speed playing style demands at an accessible price point.

title: Aura
content: AboutThe Aura is part of Top Yo's high-end series, delivering a bimetal-style visual aesthetic through polished raw aluminum ring accents on an anodized 7003 body. The S-shaped step-round profile at 54.6mm × 45mm places weight clearly at the outer edge for a powerful feel. Released in Japan in 2021 and later reaching US market distribution.

title: Bizarre
content: AboutThe Bizarre is the signature model for Top Yo team member Sun Yuqi. A high-end bimetal featuring a 7068 aluminum body with stainless steel outer rims and a POM (polyoxymethylene) inner ring, the tri-material construction is engineered for high-speed combos and horizontal play. The 54.6mm diameter with 44mm width keeps it nimble despite the aggressive specifications.

title: Black Bird
content: AboutThe Black Bird is an aesthetic collaboration between Top Yo and designer Zhang Wenlin through the Rihara brand. Designed with elegance and daily use in mind, the 7003 aluminum monometal at 54.6mm × 43.8mm is described as "quick on string tricks and exceptionally stable." Available in Blue, Pink, Silver, and Black.

title: Block
content: AboutThe Block is a modular 6061 aluminum yo-yo built around interchangeable "block" parts that allow players to customize the configuration. The slim 32.3mm width and 53g weight make it one of the lightest and narrowest throws in the Top Yo catalog. Ships in a base configuration that can be modified with additional parts. Available in Silver, Orange, Red, Green, Blue, and Gray.

title: Cheapskate
content: AboutThe Cheapskate is the signature model of Song Zihao, 2019 China National 3A Champion. Designed as a bimetal optimized for 3A (two-handed) play, the 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims provides the stability and maneuverability needed for dual-string looping tricks at the highest level. Despite its competition pedigree, it also excels at 1A and 5A. Multiple run colorways include acid wash and splash finishes.

title: Clos-SUS S
content: AboutReleased as a limited edition for World YoYo Contest 2023, the Clos-SUS S upgrades the Colos-SUS to bimetal construction. SUS Yoyo Mechanics redesigned the body for a 7003 aluminum frame with stainless steel rims, shaving approximately 1.5 grams and adding 2mm of width compared to the Colossus S. The curved surface Size C bearing offers refined centering for competition play.

title: Cloud
content: AboutReleased in July 2021, the Cloud is a Delrin (POM) competition yo-yo offering solid unresponsive performance at a budget price. The 56mm × 43mm dimensions follow standard competition sizing. A straightforward design without finger spin dimple or novelty features, the Cloud aims to deliver the smooth, consistent play associated with Delrin plastic at an accessible price.

title: Colos-SUS
content: AboutThe Colos-SUS is a collaboration between Top Yo and Japanese design studio SUS Yoyo Mechanics, originally prototyped at Japan Nationals 2019 and debuted officially at Japan Nationals 2021. SUS redesigned the Colossus to push weight to the extreme limits of what thin aluminum walls allow, retaining the familiar Colossus character while dramatically improving rim-weighted performance.

title: Colossus
content: AboutThe Colossus was Top Yo's first flagship model, released in 2015 as an introduction to their mission of "top-grade yo-yos for professional players." The step-round profile at 52.95mm diameter delivers an undersized feel with reliable spin and stability. Available in polished and anodized finishes with a wide variety of splash colorways.

title: Colossus 8
content: AboutThe Colossus 8 evolves the series with a notably wide 47mm body width, the broadest in the Colossus line. Machined from 6061 aluminum with a glossy face and blasted sides, it delivers a distinctive tactile contrast. The unresponsive setup with Size C bearing follows competition-standard configuration for the modern era of the Colossus line.

title: Colossus III
content: AboutThe Colossus III arrived in 2017 as the third entry in Top Yo's budget flagship series. Constructed from 7003 aluminum with a smooth matte finish, the step-round H-profile at 54.02mm provides tighter spin control and improved string response over earlier generations. The 5-cut bearing improves centering for consistent unresponsive play.

title: Colossus IV
content: AboutThe Colossus IV expanded the series to a full 55mm diameter. Top Yo incorporated weight distribution cues from the Silenus and Mojo into the redesigned side face, improving stability and spin time. The profile sandblast finish gives a premium feel at the budget price point. A finger spin dimple was introduced in the cup.

title: Colossus S
content: AboutThe Colossus S brings bimetal construction to the long-running Colossus series. A 7003 aluminum body is paired with stainless steel rims, concentrating weight at the outer edge for increased spin time and stability. The diameter is slightly larger than the Colossus VI at 56mm, while a slim profile keeps maneuverability high. Available in rim-contrast colorways with silver rings.

title: Colossus V
content: AboutThe Colossus V refined the fourth generation's formula with a finer sandblast texture on the semi-blasted body and a glossy response area. A large circular TopYo logo laser engraving decorates the cup. The classic nipple axle nub styling returns alongside modern design elements for one of the most well-regarded budget competition throws in the series.

title: Colossus VI
content: AboutReleased in 2021, the Colossus VI was the widest Colossus at the time of its release at 44.02mm. The deeper center cup enables finger spin capability. Top Yo switched to a carbon steel M4 × 8mm axle for improved thread durability. The sandblast profile with glossy response area continues the series' signature look. A Chi Gaoyun signature colorway in dark green was among the special editions.

title: Colossus VI MAX
content: AboutReleased in early 2022, the Colossus VI MAX is the larger-diameter variant of the Colossus VI, expanding the diameter to 56.6mm while keeping the same step-round profile and weight. The sandblast profile finish and 7003 aluminum construction carry over from the VI, giving players who prefer a full-size feel access to the Colossus DNA.

title: Colossus VII
content: AboutThe Colossus VII iterates on the sixth generation with a slightly larger diameter and heavier weight, delivering enhanced power, longer spin time, and improved stability for competition. Available in signature colorways for Team TopYo members Fang Xiaofeng and Lin Junyi, cementing the Colossus line's role as the platform for team riders.

title: Dominator
content: AboutThe Dominator is another signature model for Lin Junyi, featuring ultra-thin 7003 aluminum walls with electroplated stainless steel outer rings. The combination delivers a fast feel on the string with powerful, long-running spin. The sandblast surface and understated copper or gold rim finishes give it a premium aesthetic. Lin Junyi won the 2018 CYCC Luyu Regional Championship.

title: Dynamax
content: AboutThe Dynamax is the signature 4A off-string model for Dax Zhe Chen, machined from POM (polyoxymethylene) for the combination of durability and precision that off-string play demands. At 79.33mm diameter and 79.5g, it is large and stable in the air. Top Yo describes it as having "exquisite weight that does not blow away" — critical for consistent returns in competition 4A.

title: Encores
content: AboutThe Encores is the bimetal signature model for Top Yo team member Chi Gaoyun. Positioned as an entry-level bimetal at $69.99, it features a 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims, a flat cup with bold laser engraving, and a comfortable hand feel. Available in Dark Gray and Hot Pink colorways. Chi Gaoyun also has a signature Colossus VI colorway in dark green.

title: Faceless
content: AboutThe Faceless is a collaboration between Top Yo and Expectmake, designed as a modular polycarbonate yo-yo with interchangeable center parts for custom color combinations. The 58mm diameter PC body includes a finger spin dimple in the cup. Available in clear two-tone combinations — each half a different translucent color — making customization part of the experience.

title: Frozen
content: AboutThe Frozen is a limited premium bimetal notable for its signature snowflake cutout design in the cup, filled with a polycarbonate inlay that creates a striking visual effect. The 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims at 55.81mm × 43.31mm delivers high-end competition performance. Released in a single Black/Rose Gold colorway, it became one of Top Yo's most collectible pieces.

title: Frozen II
content: AboutThe Frozen II is a sequel collaboration between Top Yo and Expectmake, advancing the original Frozen's premium aesthetic into a tri-material hollow structure combining A606 aluminum, stainless steel, and polycarbonate. Each of the four colorways features a unique milling pattern on the cup, making every version visually and structurally distinct. The result is a high-end collectible competition throw.

title: Impulse
content: AboutThe Impulse is Top Yo's sharp V-shape speed monometal, machined from 7003 aluminum with a sandblast-and-gloss finish. The aggressive step-straight V-profile at 56mm × 43mm is designed to glide through string tricks with minimal resistance. Excellent speed and stability made it a popular competition option at its $31.99 price point.

title: Impulse II
content: AboutThe Impulse II refines the first-generation Impulse V-shape with hub-area updates that improve spin power and stability without altering the core speed-focused character. The 5-cut Size C bearing enhances string centering, and silicone pad response provides clean, reliable binds. Dozens of colorways were produced across anodized and smooth-blasted finishes.

title: Impulse New Generation
content: AboutThe Impulse New Generation advances the Impulse line with a larger 56.7mm diameter, a sharper V-profile, and a wider 45.4mm body. Top Yo marketed it as the "new king of speed" in the Impulse series — lighter at 64.5g with a wider gap to accommodate the more aggressive trick repertoire of modern 1A play.

title: Marshmallow
content: AboutThe Marshmallow is Top Yo's POM 4A off-string model. The CNC-machined polyoxymethylene body features an inverse round S-shape profile at 71.61mm diameter — compact for a 4A throw — with gentle curves designed to minimize sleep loss during trick transitions and off-axis returns. The M4 × 12mm axle and 5-cut Size C bearing provide reliable 4A performance at $39.99.

title: Mojo
content: AboutThe Mojo is Top Yo's flagship injection-molded plastic, produced from a high-precision CNC mold. Metal hardware is fitted directly into the plastic body for consistency across units. A centering Size C bearing and finger spin dimple bring modern performance to the plastic price point. Top Yo claims it plays as smooth as their metal offerings at $13.99.

title: Mojo POM
content: AboutThe Mojo POM is a CNC-machined polyoxymethylene (POM/Delrin) version of the Mojo, stepping up from injection-molded plastic to a precision-machined premium plastic. The H-profile at 57.19mm × 47.3mm is slightly larger than the injection Mojo, with a 5-cut Size C bearing and a M4 × 10mm axle. A single black colorway keeps the focus on performance.

title: Neo Classic WYYC2023
content: AboutThe Neo Classic was designed by SUS Yoyo Mechanics specifically for World YoYo Contest Japan 2023. The step-round profile prioritizes outer-edge weight concentration for a combination of gentle feel and powerful spin. A curved surface Size C bearing and 7003 aluminum matte construction round out a premium collaboration piece. Limited to the WYYC2023 event.

title: Neo Classic WYYC2024
content: AboutThe Neo Classic WYYC2024 is an updated limited edition of the Neo Classic collaboration between Top Yo and SUS Yoyo Mechanics, released for World YoYo Contest 2024. The diameter is slightly expanded compared to the 2023 version while maintaining the same powerful step-round profile and outer-edge weighting philosophy.

title: Noema
content: AboutThe Noema is the updated signature model for Song Zihao, evolving from the Cheapskate with a wider 48.4mm body and a refined step-round H-profile. The bimetal construction pairs 7003 aluminum with stainless steel rims for improved stability and weight distribution. Released in understated matte finishes and a glossy light pink colorway.

title: Null
content: AboutThe Null is a collaboration between Top Yo and July YoYo, notable as Top Yo's first yo-yo machined entirely from 7068 aluminum — a harder, denser alloy than the 7003 used across most of their lineup. The H-profile at 56.47mm × 46.04mm is wider than the July YoYo collab Reality. The M4 × 8mm axle and curved surface Size C bearing provide precise unresponsive performance.

title: Origin
content: AboutThe Origin is Top Yo's retro-inspired organic/round profile monometal. The smooth round shape at 56mm × 40.6mm fuses classic yo-yo silhouettes with modern unresponsive performance. The flat hub and 67g weight provide a stable, deliberate feel distinct from Top Yo's more angular speed-oriented shapes. Available in green, red, silver, gunmetal grey, and blue.

title: Overlap 7068
content: AboutThe Overlap 7068 is a collaboration between Top Yo and July YoYo, machined from 7068 aluminum with a full sandblast finish. At 56.92mm diameter and 45mm width, it is slightly smaller than the Null collab while sharing the same 7068 alloy construction. Available in silver, matte blue, matte gold, and gradient colorways.

title: Patronum
content: AboutThe Patronum is the monometal companion to Liang Lu's bimetal Patronus. Sharing the same H-profile design philosophy, the Patronum is machined from 7003 aluminum at a slightly larger diameter and width. The M4 × 10mm axle and 5-cut Size C bearing provide reliable unresponsive performance. Colorways include Midnight Blue, Tiffany Blue, Sakura Pink, and the multi-tone Yucci finish.

title: Patronus
content: AboutThe Patronus is the bimetal signature model for Top Yo team member Liang Lu. The 7003 aluminum body is paired with stainless steel rims finished in a striking rainbow anodization, making it as visually distinctive as it is performant. Top Yo describes it as "magically beautiful and powerful." The companion monometal version is the Patronum.

title: Photon
content: AboutThe Photon is Top Yo's undersized all-aluminum bimetal, pairing a 7003 aluminum body with harder 7075 aluminum rims. Rather than the added weight of stainless steel, the 7075 rims prioritize durability over mass concentration, resulting in a stable axis that maintains integrity as spin decreases — a nod to classic undersized yo-yos. At 49.87mm it is significantly smaller than Top Yo's standard lineup.

title: Raiser
content: AboutThe Raiser was one of Top Yo's first bimetal offerings, pairing a 6061 aluminum V-profile body with stainless steel rings. At 56mm × 43mm and 64.6g, the lighter-than-average weight for a bimetal contributes to its nimble, fast character. Available in blue and white finishes.

title: Raiser 2.0
content: AboutThe Raiser 2.0 is the signature model for Korean player Seo Jungmin. The bimetal design places 6061 aluminum paired with stainless steel rings inside the cup rather than at the outer rim — concentrating weight toward the center for a fast, maneuverable character rather than maximum spin time. The stepped profile at 55.95mm × 44.45mm prioritizes control and speed.

title: Reality
content: AboutThe Reality is a bimetal collaboration between Top Yo and July YoYo. After both teams evaluated the finished design, neither wanted to stop throwing it — hence the name. A 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims at 56.4mm × 44.4mm delivers balanced performance. Available in six rim-contrast colorways including rainbow, gold, and silver ring finishes.

title: Refraction
content: AboutThe Refraction takes a unique approach to bimetal construction: a polycarbonate/ABS body paired with a heavy 18.5g stainless steel rim. The lightweight PC body keeps overall weight at 63.8g while the massive rim concentrates spin at the outer edge. Top Yo noted its ability to deliver fast, tight binds even after extended combo strings. Available in five clear-body finishes with colored rims.

title: Robusta
content: AboutThe Robusta is a collaboration between Top Yo and YOYO BARISTA. Its defining feature is an innovative "through-structured" single stainless steel ring that penetrates the 7003 aluminum body and is visible from both sides — a unique structural approach to rim weighting. The concentrated weight distribution and 56mm × 44.6mm profile result in a premium competition bimetal.

title: Selene
content: AboutThe Selene is a full-size competition monometal released in 2024. The wide profile slopes into the gap with substantial rim weighting, making it particularly well-suited for horizontal play and hop tricks. A Center Trac Size C bearing provides consistent string centering. Available in an extensive range of swirl, galaxy, solid, and surprise colorways.

title: Silenus
content: AboutThe Silenus departs from Top Yo's speed-focused V-shapes with a wide stepped profile at 55mm × 46.5mm, emphasizing comfort in hand over raw performance metrics. At 67.5g it is one of the heavier entries in the lineup, concentrating mass at the rims via the stepped design for extended spin time. The sandblast finish with polished ring accent gives it a premium look at a budget price.

title: The Top
content: AboutThe Top is Top Yo's current flagship bimetal, representing a return-to-basics approach with an ultra-wide 47.45mm profile. The 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims includes a "bumped response area" — a subtle engineering detail that reduces spin loss at the response pads during bind. At 57.29mm × 47.45mm it is one of the largest throws in the Top Yo catalog.

title: Time Jacker
content: AboutThe Time Jacker is the bimetal signature model for Su Jia Peng of Team Top Yo. The wide 47.29mm H-profile pairs a 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel rims and a 5-cut Size C bearing for centered, consistent unresponsive play. At 64.3g it is relatively light for a bimetal, contributing to the fast, maneuverable feel Su Jia Peng designed it for.

title: The Top EX
content: AboutThe Top EX ("EX" = extreme ultimate) challenges conventional bimetal design by using an oversized stainless steel rim on a lightweight 7003 aluminum inner structure. Rather than the typical approach of adding SS rim weight at the expense of total feel, the design achieves strong rim weighting while maintaining an agile, non-heavy character at 64.5g. The H-profile at 55.69mm × 42.17mm maintains a narrower, more maneuverable width.

title: T.R.Y.
content: AboutT.R.Y. stands for Top Yo Round Yo-yo. Machined from 7068 aluminum, the harder and denser alloy allows for thinner walls and more precise weight placement in the step-round profile. The "low edges" design — described as a step-round with no actual steps — creates a smooth, gradual arc that emphasizes stability for high-difficulty trick sequences.

title: T.S.
content: AboutT.S. stands for Top Steel. Top Yo's most ambitious engineering project, the T.S. is constructed entirely from stainless steel with walls measuring just 0.6mm thick — a machining feat that achieves full competition size and weight from a single material. The ultra-thin walls are necessary to bring stainless steel down to competition-legal weight without sacrificing the diameter or width expected from a modern 1A throw.

title: Turbine
content: AboutThe Turbine is the signature model for Wang Weichuan, featuring a wide 45.22mm undercut-sided H-profile machined from 7003 aluminum. Released in 2017, the 56.53mm diameter and 67.8g weight make it one of the heavier monometal offerings in the Top Yo lineup, optimized for powerful, controlled play. A limited 30-unit black collab edition with the brand UNKNOWN was produced alongside the standard splash runs.

title: TopYo × 44CLASH (44FESTIVAL)
content:
About
The TopYo × 44CLASH is the collaboration produced for the 2019 44FESTIVAL — a variant of the annual 44CLASH event held August 24–25, 2019 in Japan. Produced in partnership with TopYo of China. Full specifications were not published in available sources at time of import.

title: Null
content:
About
The Null is a collaboration between TopYo and July YoYo, and TopYo's first full-metal yo-yo. Machined from 7068 aluminum in an H-profile at 56.47mm diameter, it became one of the most widely recommended first-metal throws in the community, praised for competition-ready performance at a sub-$40 price point. Wider than the companion Reality with repositioned step cuts for improved string play. Available in Type:Fire (Red), Type:Water (Light Blue), and Type:Grass (Green), plus solid and splash variants. Released April 2022.

title: Overlap (7068)
content:
About
The Overlap is a collaboration between TopYo of Taiwan and July YoYo, machined from premium 7068 aluminum alloy with a full sandblast finish. TopYo provided the design and manufacturing; July YoYo brought it to the Chinese and global market. The 57mm H-profile at 65.1g delivers stable, controlled play with a textured grip surface. Available in Silver, Matte Blue, Matte Gold, Glaze Silver Pink Blue, and Energy Silver Gray Mint colorways. Retailed at $34.99 and sold out.

title: Reality
content:
About
The Reality is a bimetal collaboration between TopYo and July YoYo, originally developed by TopYo specifically for July YoYo's Chinese market. Impressed by the result, TopYo released it as a full collaboration. The 7003 aluminum body with stainless steel ring produces a bimetal narrower in profile than the companion Null. Available in Red/Silver Ring, Silver/Black Ring, Blue/Rainbow Ring, Pink/Gold Ring, Red/Gold Ring, and Black/Gold Ring. Retailed at $79.99 and sold out.

title: Tornado
content: The Tornado features a distinctive cover-cap that wraps around the rim and sides like an extended Z-stack, enabling hand-catching while the yo-yo is spinning. Plastic body with steel rim weighting. Available for 1A, 3A, and 5A play.

title: Torque
content: AboutThe Torque was designed with direct input from top Team Duncan players, featuring a stepped V-shape with angled edges for stable, powerful spins and a wide catch zone optimized for modern technical play. The inner ring is machined for fingerspin capability, giving the Torque a dual function as both a competition string-trick throw and a fingerspin platform. Its rim-focused weight distribution maximizes spin time, and the KonKave bearing keeps the string centered during complex multi-layer tricks.

title: Hazmat
content:
History / About
The Hazmat was the first yoyo from Toxic Strings, designed by owner Evan Evans and machined by One Drop Yo-Yos. Released in March 2012, the Hazmat features a full-sized hybrid H/V-shape profile, a deep cup with a slight inner-grinding ring, and Side Effect axle compatibility. It shipped in black, deep orange, and 50/50 split colorways, with black aluminum spike Side Effects. A portion of Toxic Strings proceeds supported medical expenses for Evan's son Trevan, who was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes — the same cause later served by the One Drop x Toxic Strings T1.

title: TOY
content:
History / About
The TOY (the name is written in all caps, suggesting it may be an acronym) is G2's most premium release to date at $335 — surpassing even the Ti Reaper. A full titanium model, it was released in January 2026 in two colorways: the standard TOY and the TOY Rainbow. The ironic name — calling G2's most expensive, most premium model a "TOY" — is consistent with Jacob Gross's sense of humor and the brand's self-aware "Functional Art" tagline.

title: Chicago Fair HEP (Baseball)
content: History / AboutToy Tinkers (also known as the Tinker Toy Company), based in Evanston, Illinois, entered the yo-yo market in the mid-1950s with its Toy-O-Ball series, a rewinding metal reel housed in a round plastic shell and made as baseballs, basketballs and footballs. The YoYo Wiki notes the balls looked very similar to the HEP Magic String Balls sold in the same period, and that it is unclear whether Toy Tinkers produced the HEP line or the reverse. The wiki describes the Toy-O-Balls as the first auto-returning yo-yo balls produced. The model "Chicago Fair HEP (Baseball)" is one of six Toy Tinkers yo-yo balls listed on the wiki's manufacturer page; the wiki has no separate entry or specifications for it.
