title: The Thing (with Doc Pop)
content: History / AboutPer the YoYoSam listing, The 'Thing' is a delrin yo-yo made in collaboration with yo-yo figure Doctor Popular, designed for portability and performance. It has a lightweight design and titanium guts at the center, can be played responsive and, with a bearing switch, unresponsive. The 2023 version is a black body with purple hubs. Toybania's Stoopid is described as an aluminum re-imagining of The Thing, with the same specs and profile.

title: TP-2
content: About the TP-2The refined successor to the original Turning Point throw, designed and machined in Japan but produced in China for accessible pricing. Undersized at 50mm diameter but wider than average, creating a large effective catch zone that belies the compact diameter. The TP-2 later spawned bimetal (Counter-Jet) and titanium (Absinthe) variants.

title: TP-3
content: About the TP-3The third generation of the brand-name Turning Point series. Slightly lighter and with a larger diameter than the TP-2, offering improved control and presence. Compact and well-balanced, inheriting the TP-2's horsepower and stability lineage. The bimetal Point Breaker was derived from this body.

title: Absinthe
content: About the AbsintheThe first titanium version of Turning Point's TP-2 design. The Absinthe takes the TP-2's undersized diameter and wide catch zone and renders it in full titanium for dramatically extended spin and power. The titanium body provides endless spin capability despite the compact dimensions, making it one of Turning Point's most powerful performers relative to its size.

title: Absinthe 2
content:
About
The Absinthe 2 is the second generation of Turning Point's acclaimed Absinthe, machined from titanium. Building on the original Absinthe's reputation as a premier competition-grade titanium yo-yo, the Absinthe 2 refines the profile and surface geometry. Turning Point's titanium production sets the standard for Japanese precision manufacturing, and the Absinthe 2 exemplifies the brand's commitment to pushing the limits of premium construction.

title: Acanthus
content: About the AcanthusMatsuura's mid-size 5A-focused signature model. The H-profile design at 54mm diameter and 46mm width is optimized for counterweight compatibility, offering exceptional sleeping power and maneuverability during 5A play. Mid-size and step-round shape prioritizes control and responsiveness for the demands of counterweight string tricks. The Acanthus S bimetal followed in 2023.

title: Acanthus S
content: About the Acanthus SThe bimetal upgrade to the Acanthus, adding stainless steel outer rims to the 5A-optimized mid-size shape. Retains the Acanthus's excellent counterweight operability while boosting spin power and stability through the rim weight. The "S" designation follows Turning Point's convention for bimetal upgrades.

title: Alnilam
content: About the AlnilamA magnesium-body bimetal based on the shape of Matsuura's Colony. The magnesium body with stainless steel rim delivers "floaty and stretched-out sleep" characteristics. Enhanced stability throughout play with impressive sleep power for trick execution. Part of Turning Point's expanding magnesium series.

title: Anubis
content: About the AnubisBased on the Basilisk body form and expanded with a full outer stainless steel rim for an oversized bimetal. Despite the 58mm diameter the Anubis plays with the agility of a smaller yo-yo. Powerful and stable spin, comfortable to catch, and capable of sustaining long freestyles. A team signature shared across Turning Point's most decorated players: Takeshi Matsuura, Tomoya Kurita, and Takuma Inoue. An Awoken Anubis variant (68.3g, Kentaro Kimura's personal rework) was also released.

title: Anubis II
content: About the Anubis IIThe second generation Anubis with a slightly wider H-profile body (44mm versus 42.84mm on the original). Maintains similar diameter and weight while the added width enhances control and stability. M4×12mm axle. Consistent power without stalling and reliable performance across all string trick styles.

title: ASTer
content: About the ASTerKashiwaya's second signature and Turning Point's tri-metal design — three materials (aluminum, stainless, titanium) in one throw. Despite 70.1g weight, the titanium outer rim's positioning creates exceptional maneuverability and acceleration, prioritizing responsiveness over raw spin power compared to the MSG. The tri-metal construction produces a notably different feel from any two-material model.

title: Bacchus
content: About the BacchusThe "final form" of Shingo Terada's Doska signature line. Features hollow-body construction giving it a floaty yet balanced feel at 66.8g. The round body shape provides comfortable hand feel during 5A counterweight play. Comes with an autograph photo card. A Premium Bacchus colorway and a Candy Dice Pro Bacchus (with counterweight) were also released.

title: Basilisk
content: About the BasiliskDescribed as the Prominence's heavyweight sibling, the Basilisk features an oversized profile with a thick outer rim profile that extends spin time well beyond typical aluminum monometals. A competition-grade freestyle support tool intended to underpin extended, complex routines. Designed by Kentaro Kimura for Shinji Saito's training. Also released in a Basilisk Light variant at 66.4g for players preferring a lighter feel.

title: Boom Bap
content: About the Boom BapJun Aramaki's third Turning Point signature and the monometal counterpart to the Mortal bimetal. Compact at 48.8mm with substantial rim thickness overcoming typical undersized limitations of lacking spin power. Designed for chopstick-style tricks that pass between fingers. Comes with a Jun Aramaki signed photo card.

title: BU2R
content: About the BU2RA highly limited collector's release distributed exclusively at the 2014 World Yo-Yo Contest in Prague, in collaboration with crystal manufacturer Preciosa and Budweiser Urban Projects. Based on the Leviathan 5 shape with 126 Preciosa crystals set into the rims and hubs. Only approximately 100 units were produced, making it one of the rarest Turning Point models.

title: Collapsar
content: About the CollapsarJason Liu's second signature and one of Turning Point's heaviest models at 76.6g. The titanium rim paired with aluminum body creates extreme centripetal force for power and stability that enables the most difficult combos. The super-heavy weight requires adjustment but rewards players with exceptional rotational performance.

title: Colony
content: About the ColonyMatsuura's third signature model, used at the 2016 World Yo-Yo Contest in Cleveland where he won his seventh 5A World Championship. The Colony is effectively an outer-rim bimetal evolution of the Palpitation — same size and shape but with a heavier steel outer ring that fundamentally changes weight distribution, extending sleep time and boosting stability for long, complex trick sequences. The deep rim design provides maximum power in the narrowest possible body.

title: Colony 2
content: About the Colony 2The second generation of Matsuura's Colony signature. A slight weight increase from the original Colony's 66.3g to 66.7g enhances performance without compromising speed or agility. H-profile shape with M4×12mm axle (versus M4×15mm on the original). A refined evolution of one of Turning Point's most beloved competition designs.

title: Colony ST
content:
About
The Colony ST is a bimetal evolution of Turning Point's Colony series, adding stainless steel weight rings to the 7075 aluminum body. The "ST" designation signals its steel-ringed construction. Following the Colony and Colony 2, the Colony ST pushes the series' performance ceiling with bimetal rim-weighting for enhanced stability and spin time in high-level competition play.

title: Counter-Jet
content:
About
The Counter-Jet is a bimetal yo-yo from Turning Point combining aluminum and steel for competition-oriented performance. Its name evokes high-velocity dynamics, and its construction prioritizes the kind of spin force and rim-weight balance demanded at the World Yo-Yo Championship level. A later addition to Turning Point's bimetal lineup, the Counter-Jet continues the brand's tradition of precision engineering for serious competitors.

title: Derivative
content: About the DerivativeThe third magnesium model from Turning Point and the first full-size magnesium throw, following the oversized Radix and mid-size Mgska. The Derivative brings magnesium performance to a standard competition-size diameter, delivering a familiar full-size feel with the characteristic magnesium lightness and response. An aluminum monometal version, the Derive, was released in 2024.

title: Derive
content: About the DeriveThe aluminum monometal version of the magnesium Derivative. H-profile shape bringing the Derivative's proven geometry to an accessible aluminum price point. Designed as an all-purpose reference model intended to become a standard Turning Point throw.

title: Diaspora
content: About the DiasporaThe second full titanium model from Turning Point and Shinji Saito's titanium signature. A mid-size design specifically tailored to Saito's performance style. The titanium construction provides impressive power in a compact, nimble package. Ships with both stainless steel and titanium axle options. A Grade 5 titanium successor, the Diaspora Grade 5, was released in 2026.

title: Diaspora Grade 5
content: About the Diaspora Grade 5The Grade 5 titanium successor to the original Diaspora. Grade 5 titanium is significantly harder and more difficult to machine. Designed specifically for Saito's intricate trick style, providing control and spin power at the highest level in a slightly more compact, agile mid-size format than the original Diaspora.

title: Doska
content: About the DoskaShingo Terada's first signature model at Turning Point. A compact mid-size monometal at only 62.1g, optimized for casual carry and daily practice rather than maximum competition power. The Doska spawned the Another Doska variant with modified weight distribution and eventually the refined Bacchus. Terada is a 2001 X-Division World Champion and Rewind Shibuya store manager.

title: Ensemble
content: About the EnsembleJun Aramaki's first Turning Point signature, co-designed by Kentaro Kimura. A unique hybrid using an aluminum body with POM (Delrin) plastic rim weights, which deadens the impact sound while still providing power and stability similar to full metal models. The Ensemble was also included in a limited anniversary box set in 2019.

title: Entangle 2
content: About the Entangle 2The second generation of Kurita's narrow-width, large-diameter signature. Slightly heavier than the original Entangle, offering enhanced power and stability while maintaining the slim profile optimized for threading between strings in 3A play. The "long, vertical shape" is designed specifically for intricate 3A string combinations.

title: Gachiska
content: About the GachiskaShingo Terada's magnesium bimetal signature, a stainless-steel-rimmed version of the Doska shape in magnesium. Dead-stock units from Terada's personal stock. The combination of magnesium body and steel rims creates an unusually light overall weight (64.5g) with strong rim-weighted spin.

title: Haast
content: About the HaastJason Liu Zichen's first Turning Point signature. An oversized yo-yo at 58mm with a distinctively multi-stepped, inverse polygonal profile unlike anything else in the Turning Point catalog. Despite its large diameter the weight distribution creates a surprisingly fast and maneuverable feel. Designed for Liu's high-speed combination style, which earned him the 2016 China National 1A Championship.

title: Hades
content:
About
The Hades is a heavyweight bimetal from Turning Point, weighing approximately 80g — well above the typical 65g competition norm. Named after the Greek god of the underworld, it is one of Turning Point's most unusual designs, built to explore the extremes of rim-weighted mass distribution. The substantial weight produces an unusually powerful, persistent spin, making the Hades a curiosity and a collector's piece within Turning Point's diverse catalog.

title: Hinemosu
content: About the HinemosuMatsuura's titanium-rim signature, combining the Colony and Mustang shape lineage with titanium rings on an aluminum body. Titanium is lighter than stainless steel, so Turning Point made the rings wider and thicker to achieve the desired rim weight. The slim 42mm width enables intricate string tricks and tech combos. Produces a significantly different feel from the steel-rim Colony.

title: Hinemosu 2
content: About the Hinemosu 2The second-generation Hinemosu with significantly enlarged titanium rims — greater weight ratio than the original, pushing more mass toward the periphery. Emphasizes tenacity, stability, and controllability while maintaining every last bit of sleep time even under the load of extended trick combinations. A power upgrade while maintaining the slim width.

title: Houska
content: About the HouskaThe Houska series was Turning Point's first budget-oriented offering, designed in Japan and produced in China. The Houska Dry variant (2014) shaved weight from the heavier original through completely redistributed mass, making it faster and more agile while maintaining long spin times. The organic shape echoes the Leviathan series with distinct cuts and angles. A 2016 revised production run brought the weight down to 65.1g.

title: Isotope
content: About the IsotopeThe Isotope is a Positron with a stainless steel weight ring, combining Turning Point's flagship shape language with bimetal power. Released alongside the Isotope 1.03 variant (which has a slightly higher weight ratio), the Isotope represents a significant evolution from pure monometal to bimetal design at Turning Point. Multiple aurora and blast colorways were produced across several runs.

title: Isotope 2
content: About the Isotope 2The updated Isotope based on the Positron 2 shape. This was the yo-yo Takeshi Matsuura used to win the 1A division at the 2014 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest and to place 2nd at the 2014 World Championships behind Gentry Stein, cementing its competition pedigree. Multiple new colorways were released throughout 2014.

title: Kiwi
content: About the KiwiJason Liu's third Turning Point signature and the monometal version of the Collapsar's concept. A super-heavyweight monometal at 76.3g, preventing string blowouts during powerful combos. Despite the extreme weight it offers surprising maneuverability and smooth response. One of the heaviest non-titanium yo-yos in the Turning Point lineup.

title: Lachesis
content:
About
The Lachesis is a monometal yo-yo from Turning Point, named after Lachesis, the Fate of Greek mythology who measures the thread of life — a thematic fit for a brand that treats manufacturing as craft. Machined from aluminum, the Lachesis embodies Turning Point's philosophy of disciplined geometry and exacting tolerances. It sits within the brand's extensive catalog of monometal competition models.

title: Leviathan
content: About the LeviathanThe yo-yo that launched Turning Point internationally. The Leviathan pioneered the low-edge, wide-body step-round shape, redistributing weight toward the rims for improved stability and spin time with minimal sleep loss. Machined by hand by local Japanese craftsmen, it set the standard for boutique Japanese competitive yo-yos and its influence can be felt across the entire industry.

title: Leviathan 2
content: About the Leviathan 2The first full revision of the Leviathan, updated with a marginally narrower gap and slightly reduced weight compared to the original, shifting mass outward for enhanced stability. Maintains the step-round profile and Japanese craftsman-machined construction. Multiple color runs were released over several years.

title: Leviathan 3
content: About the Leviathan 3Refined from the Leviathan 2 with a lower edge profile and a more polygonal outer silhouette. The reduced gap trapeze width minimizes sleep loss further. The third Leviathan represents the peak of the monometal Leviathan form before the series moved to bimetal construction.

title: Leviathan 4
content: About the Leviathan 4The Leviathan series' first bimetal, pairing a 7075 aluminum body with a brass inner rim weight. The denser brass shifts weight distribution dramatically compared to the Leviathan 3, producing exceptional stability and longer spin without changing the overall mass. A landmark release that proved bimetal construction's advantages at Turning Point. A pre-production Leviathan 4β run of approximately 30 units was used by Shinji Saito at the 2013 East Japan Contest.

title: Leviathan 5
content: About the Leviathan 5A deliberate return to monometal construction for the Leviathan series, designed to replicate the feel of the Leviathan 4 Light without a weight ring. Turning Point engineered the weight distribution through careful shaping to deliver a lightweight, rim-heavy feel in a pure aluminum body. Widely considered a masterwork of monometal design.

title: Leviathan 5 (2015 restock)
content: About the Leviathan 5 (2015)A new production run of the Leviathan 5 released in 2015 alongside the Leviathan 6, featuring new colorways not available in the original 2014 release. Identical specs to the original Leviathan 5.

title: Leviathan 6
content: About the Leviathan 6Based on the Leviathan 5, this bimetal version adds a stainless steel inner rim weight while maintaining near-identical dimensions. The denser stainless steel fundamentally changes the play feel despite the minimal weight difference, delivering the Leviathan 5's shape with significantly more rim-weighted power and spin stability.

title: Leviathan 7
content: About the Leviathan 7Turning Point's first bimetal with an outer rim weight configuration, a significant design shift from the inner rim of the Leviathan 6. Same body shape as Leviathans 5 and 6 but the outer placement of the stainless steel rim changes weight distribution without altering total mass, producing a noticeably different and more aggressive playfeel. A pivotal release in Turning Point's bimetal evolution.

title: Loop Phase One
content: About the Loop Phase OneTurning Point's first looping yo-yo and first 3D-printed model. Designed slightly wider than conventional loop yo-yos for enhanced stability during Around the World and sleep-based looping tricks. The starburst response system combined with the wider width creates longer sleep times than typical looping throws.

title: Lop Nur
content: About the Lop NurJason Liu's fifth Turning Point signature and the heaviest aluminum monometal in the catalog at 77g. Exceptionally wide at 51mm, maximizing string landing visibility and catchability for high-difficulty maneuvers. The extreme weight provides stability for dynamic trick combinations while the wide body ensures reliable string hits.

title: Maxbet
content: About the MaxbetDesigned by Kentaro Kimura as his ultimate 3A yo-yo. The Maxbet features a low edge and large body with a multi-step profile that minimizes sleep loss, accommodates extreme string quantity in the gap, and provides perfect weight and balance for 3A stability. The design later influenced the Solenoid.

title: MGB
content: About the MGBThe bimetal version of Ishihara's MIID-Y signature. The stainless steel rim adds significant spin power and stability to the undersized wide-body design optimized for 5A counterweight play. Available with signed photo card.

title: Mgska
content: About the MgskaTurning Point's first full magnesium yo-yo and a tribute to Shingo Terada. Based on the shape of the Majiska, the Mgska uses magnesium for an entirely new feel. The protective coating patinas from skin oils — normal wear, recommended to wipe dry after use. A collector's piece and technical milestone for the brand.

title: MIID-Y
content: About the MIID-YHiroyasu Ishihara's first signature model, modeled after the TP-2's profile but slightly enlarged. An undersized wide-body optimized for 5A counterweight play with a rim weight profile that provides stability unusual for the compact size. Features center-lock titanium axle and optional side caps.

title: Misfit
content: About the MisfitThe original Misfit, Kentaro Mannen (BB26)'s debut signature model. A lightweight adult casual throw at 62.5g with a wide 46.7mm body designed for effortless daily swinging. Features a dry finish (サラサラ加工) for grip. The Misfit Air bimetal followed later in 2022.

title: Misfit Air
content: About the Misfit AirThe bimetal upgrade to the Misfit, adding a stainless steel inner rim while maintaining the casual, fluffy "adult toy" feel concept. A bimetal designed to feel relaxed and effortless rather than competition-aggressive, distinguishing it from the rest of the Turning Point lineup. Floaty yet with improved spin power and stability from the bimetal construction.

title: Mortal
content: About the MortalJun Aramaki's second Turning Point signature and a complete design departure from the Ensemble. An undersized bimetal at 48.68mm inspired by the Mini Mo-Trix series, with a wide stainless steel rim providing powerful rotation despite the compact form. Designed for chopstick-style tricks that pass between fingers. The Boom Bap (2025) is its monometal successor.

title: MSG
content: About the MSGYuta Kashiwaya's first signature. A "super heavyweight" at 70g, the MSG delivers outrageously powerful and tight returns. Based on a fusion of the Anubis size with the structure of the BGM model. Despite the extreme weight, the bimetal design maintains top-class competition performance. The tri-metal ASTer (2022) is its follow-up.

title: Mustang
content: About the MustangThe titanium monometal version of the Colony. Combining the Colony's proven design with titanium construction gives the Mustang impressive stability and extended sleep time, providing a competitive edge for intricate trick sequences. Released alongside the Mustang ES (approximately 3g heavier at 68.5g) for players preferring more power. A Grade 5 titanium successor, the Mustang Grade 5, was released in 2022.

title: Mustang Grade 5
content: About the Mustang Grade 5An upgrade to the original Mustang using Grade 5 titanium, which is significantly harder and more difficult to machine than standard titanium. Side face design draws from the Mustang ES with adjusted weight balance. Maintains "strong and long-time sleep" performance with enhanced maneuverability described as ease in directional changes. Re-released in new limited colorways in 2024.

title: Mustang U
content: About the Mustang UThe ultimate Mustang — a titanium body paired with stainless steel rims for a bimetal titanium construction. Delivers "ferocious rotational force" with quick, smooth response despite exceeding 66g. The top of Turning Point's Mustang line, combining titanium durability with bimetal power characteristics.

title: Naja
content: About the NajaZannix Wong's first Turning Point signature. An unconventional titanium model weighing nearly 70g — exceptionally heavy for a titanium throw. The inward-curving rim design creates distinctive weight distribution enhancing stability and power for extended combos. A follow-up, the Yaz (2025), features reduced diameter and increased width for improved controllability.

title: One Way Ticket
content: About the One Way TicketJason Liu's fourth Turning Point signature and third in the heavy-titanium line following the Collapsar and Kiwi. A full titanium super-heavyweight at 76.3g, offering "overwhelming weight and stability" for the most powerful advanced string trick performance.

title: Palpitation
content: About the PalpitationTakeshi Matsuura's first signature model at Turning Point, developed following his 2014 Japan National 1A title win. The Palpitation was Matsuura's primary competition throw and the foundation of a signature line that grew to include the Colony, St. Elmo, Mustang, Hinemosu, Acanthus, and St. Tempest. A full-size bimetal blending power with precise balance for complex 1A and 5A string tricks.

title: Palpitation ES
content: About the Palpitation ESA derivative of the original Palpitation with a new shape and refined side-face geometry for dramatically improved stability. The narrow 42mm width combined with the ES shape changes produces overwhelmingly powerful spin — described as "top class among bimetals." Available at Western retailers in early 2024.

title: Paranoid
content: About the ParanoidShinji Saito's first signature model with Turning Point. Mid-size at 52.5mm, the Paranoid combines the tight turning of an undersized yo-yo with the powerful spin of a full-size competition throw. Designed to facilitate top-on and finger-balance tricks alongside traditional string trick performance. The first release showcasing Turning Point's capability with player-focused mid-size designs.

title: Point Breaker
content: About the Point BreakerThe bimetal evolution of the Turning Point 3, adding stainless steel rims to the TP-3's undersized wide-body design. Spin strength that rivals full-sized models despite the compact 52mm diameter. Wide profile ensures effortless control for threading tight gaps and precise string hits.

title: Positron
content: About the PositronThe Positron merges characteristics of the Maxbet and Leviathan to minimize sleep loss. A full-size competition yo-yo optimized for hop tricks like Eli Hops and whole-body movements. Marcus Koh (Singapore) placed 2nd at the 2011 Asia Pacific Championship and went on to win the 2011 1A World Championship using the Positron, bringing Turning Point to global prominence. A special Marcus Koh Edition with his name engraved was released in 2011.

title: Positron 2
content: About the Positron 2The successor to the original Positron, with refined weight distribution for improved spinning power and sleep times. The Isotope 2 bimetal was derived from the Positron 2 shape. Takeshi Matsuura used the Isotope 2 (based on this body) to win the 1A division at the 2014 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest. Multiple color restocks ran through 2014–2015.

title: Prominence
content: About the ProminenceTakuma Inoue's first signature model at Turning Point. The Prominence features an inverse-round shape built from straight lines giving it a polygonal profile. A large axle bump area facilitates "Top On" finger-balance tricks and other specialized techniques. Inoue won the 2011 Japan National Championship and placed in the top tier at multiple World Championships using Turning Point models.

title: Radix
content: About the RadixTurning Point's second magnesium yo-yo and the first oversized magnesium model. Despite the metal construction it delivers the agility of a plastic yo-yo — exceptionally light-feeling for its size. High friction with strings means it rewards precise players who keep string off the body. A landmark in Turning Point's magnesium series.

title: Shake
content: About the ShakeMatsuura's second signature model and his first mid-size design. The Shake shaves 2mm off the diameter compared to the Palpitation, placing it firmly in the mid-size class. Produced to high tolerance in China while maintaining full Japanese design oversight, making it Turning Point's most accessible price-point model at launch. Dense and stable for its compact size.

title: Shot Glass
content:
About
The Shot Glass is a miniature yo-yo from Turning Point machined entirely from stainless steel, small enough to literally fit inside a standard shot glass. A curiosity and collector's piece, it demonstrates Turning Point's machining capability at the extreme end of miniaturization. Despite its tiny dimensions it is a functional yo-yo, and its stainless steel construction gives it a satisfying heft relative to its size.

title: Solenoid
content: About the SolenoidThe Solenoid combines the profile of the Positron with design elements from the Maxbet, adding a new step close to the center. A heavier spin and greater stability than the Positron make it ideal for those who want the power of the Maxbet in a competition 1A form. Kentaro Kimura named it his personal throw of choice for general play.

title: Soul
content: About the SoulChan Man Fai's titanium signature. The Soul takes the Leviathan as a design reference at 43.5mm width, emphasizing weight balance over raw mass. At 65g it plays lighter than the weight suggests while maintaining exceptional spin stability. Ships with both a lightweight titanium axle and a spare stainless steel axle.

title: St. Elmo
content: About the St. ElmoA monometal version of Matsuura's bimetal Palpitation. The St. Elmo retains the Palpitation's size and step-round shape but strips the steel rim, producing a lighter, more agile feel while maintaining the same competitive stability. Approximately 1g lighter than the Palpitation. Became one of Turning Point's longest-running and best-selling models due to its accessible price point and competition-proven shape.

title: St. Tempest
content: About the St. TempestA wide-body evolution of the St. Elmo. Based on the St. Elmo's proven shape but with a boldly expanded 48.92mm width — more than 6mm wider — making string mounting significantly easier during dynamic tricks. The extra width enables players to attempt bolder, more ambitious combinations while maintaining the powerful spin that defines the St. Elmo line.

title: Superstar (Turning Point × YoYoFactory)
content: About the Superstar (Turning Point × YoYoFactory)A collaboration between YoYoFactory and Turning Point commemorating YoYoFactory's 20th anniversary. The original Superstar was actually designed by Kentaro Kimura during a formative period in his career, making this a homecoming of sorts. Hub stack compatible. Powerful, stable, with well-balanced weight distribution.

title: Untangle
content: About the UntangleThe bimetal successor to Kurita's monometal Entangle. Adds a stainless steel rim to the Entangle's narrow-width, large-diameter profile, delivering bimetal power while maintaining the slim silhouette designed for threading between strings in 3A play. The bimetal construction also reduces the collision noise typical of monometal contact during 3A play.

title: Yaz
content: About the YazZannix Wong's second Turning Point signature and successor to the Naja. Features a reduced diameter and increased width compared to the Naja, improving controllability and string mounting ease while maintaining the heavyweight titanium approach. At 72.3g it carries the same heavyweight philosophy as the Naja with fundamentally different proportions.

title: Ziz
content: About the ZizRyo Enomoto's signature model. Combining A6061 with a titanium rim for a distinct "straightforward playfeel" without the gravitational sensation of stainless steel models. The compact 52.9mm form enables detailed trick execution while the titanium rim provides solid, secure spin. Everyday carry size ideal for high-level technical string tricks.

title: Tranquility
content:
About
The Tranquility is a capped organic yo-yo built for fun. Where many Yoyofriends projects focus on competition and performance, this one is purely about non-competition characteristics. Its profile and shape draw on the Koi, one of the brand's most popular yo-yos for its organic feel.

title: Transcend
content: About the TranscendThe Transcend is the signature model of Tessa Piccillo, the 2014 Women's World Yo-Yo Champion, making it one of the few female-player signature yo-yos produced during YoYoJam's history. The step-rounded aluminum body at 56.0mm diameter provides a wide catch zone suitable for Piccillo's flowing competition style. It was one of the final significant model releases before the company's December 2015 closure.

title: Traveler
content: A wooden, three-piece, fixed axle yo-yo with flat rims. Made from walnut.

title: TRE 2K13
content: The TRE 2K13 is Eric Tran-Ton's signature model. "TRE" is Eric's team nickname. Tran-Ton placed 4th at the 2013 WYYC — the highest finish by a US competitor that year — using horizontal-heavy freestyles that the TRE was designed to excel at. The consistent drop from rim to bearing creates an optimal catch zone, and the 7075 construction keeps the weight where it counts for horizontal stability.

title: Trekker
content:
From ZGRT:

"The Trekker is the newest throw we are adding to our slim line family. This project took a while to be completed as we went back and forth with different approaches and multiple prototypes. This project took a couple of years from initial prototyping to launch date.

This time we wanted to bring a larger diameter and more pocketable slim throw with a lighter weight.  With the use of 7075 aluminum we achieved having thin walls in certain areas and push out more weight towards the outer diameter to compensate the thin width and cap seat of the Trekker.

Like El MiJo, the Trekker has a hub-system, but now the hubs themselves are completely removable and replaceable. The bearing remains sitting on the body of the throw as most of the throws.

Early prototypes measured 55.1 mm diameter, clocked in at 55 g, and stretched to 29 mm wide. Our mission was to get smaller and lighter without sacrificing playability. In the final build, the Trekker grew 3 mm in diameter, shed 5 g in weight, slimmed down 6 mm in width, and gained a fully rounded profile that fits perfectly in your hand. The ultra-fine blasted finish feels incredible under the hands.

Inside, inverted walls taper from a narrow 2.3 mm at the gap out to 5.9 mm at the catch zone, making tricky binds a breeze and landings more forgiving. 

This throw is designed to play with fixed (blank) and responsive bearing with the capability to play with unresponsive bearing if you want to.  The Trekker is a light-carry, all-day companion built to spark creativity and elevate your tricks."

title: Tres Leches
content: About the Tres LechesAnnounced in August 2010 alongside the Heavy Cream and Half & Half, the Tres Leches was the third and final yo-yo in Crucial's Milk series. Where the original Milk featured an organic, rounded profile, the Tres Leches adopted an H-profile shape that placed more of the Delrin mass on the rims — delivering enhanced stability and spin time while retaining the precision machining Crucial was known for. It represented the evolution of the Milk concept toward a more competition-oriented geometry.

title: Tri-B
content:
History / About
The Tri-B is MonkeyfingeR Design’s first throw built collaboratively by the full team. "Tri" references the three design lineages synthesized in the geometry: the Ape-X, the Caesar, and the Gelada 2. It was the first MFD throw to ship with the REvolution bearing — a 10-ball composite with ceramic balls and a steel cage, introduced here as MFD’s house bearing. Two alloy variants were produced simultaneously: a standard 6061 version and a stiffer, competition-oriented A5/7075 variant.

title: Triarch
content:
History / About
The Triarch represents mowl's refined vision of tri-material performance — combining 6061 aluminum, stainless steel rims, and polycarbonate wings in a single design. The concept traces back to early experiments derived from the Surveillance platform that eventually took on a distinct identity separate from both Surveillance and Narcissist. Rather than being tailored to a single player's signature preference, Triarch was engineered as a versatile, competition-focused model built to suit a wide range of advanced players. The profile moves away from the sharper H-shape of Surveillance in favor of a more controlled, less aggressive H outline. The steel rings are positioned internally (midship), and the overall width was increased to enhance string presence and modern performance capability. Triarch's defining strength is its balance — powerful yet composed, stable yet agile.

title: TRICKLAB HARD MODE
content:
History / About
TRICKLAB HARD MODE is a narrower variant within Hiro Irifune's Tricklab series, released November 21, 2025.

title: TRICKLAB RESPONSIVE
content:
History / About
TRICKLAB RESPONSIVE is a responsive, pull-back yo-yo in Hiro Irifune's Tricklab line. It saw two releases: an early machined lot on October 28, 2025 in 6 clear colorways, and a standard mass-production mold version on March 12, 2026 in Clear Color only, sold as a pre-production item without packaging.

title: Tricklab Standard
content:
About
Tricklab Standard supports Hiro Irifune's “Tricklab” project, where he shares yoyo trick ideas and concepts with the community. It brings a more traditional, organic shape to the Tricklab series — powerful spin and rock-solid stability aimed at a comfortable daily throw.

title: Trickster
content: The Trickster was Hummingbird's flagship competitive model, featuring multi-layer laminated construction with dyed wood veneers. Available in both imperial and butterfly shapes, the Trickster became the signature model for accomplished players including Dale Myrberg, Jennifer Baybrook, and Dennis McBride during the mid-1980s competitive circuit.Known for smooth wood construction and elegant aesthetics, the Trickster represented the height of Hummingbird's handcrafted approach to yo-yo design.

title: Trident
content: About TridentThe Trident is a precision bi-metal yo-yo combining 6061 aluminum and stainless steel. At 55.89mm diameter and 65.3g, it delivers the spin stability and trick responsiveness needed for high-level string tricks.

title: Trigger
content: About the TriggerThe Trigger is Johnnie DelValle's eighth signature series yo-yo, featuring a step-round body machined from Delrin plastic as thin as structurally possible to maximize the metal rim's proportion of total mass. The H-profile-adjacent design provides a wide catch zone while concentrating weight at the rims for spin stability. The smooth Delrin body excels at finger and thumb grinds.

title: Trion Crash
content: History / About6061, stainless-steel, and plastic construction established the three-functional-material approach later used by Super Scintillator.

title: Triple Double
content:
History / About
The Triple Double is the signature model of Joe Wilson, Virginia State Champion and Recess team member. Priced at $40 it was one of Recess's most accessible aluminum models. The name reflects Joe's 5A background — a "triple double" being a basketball stat, fitting Recess's sports-break naming theme, and a nod to Joe's interest in combining complex 1A/5A elements. It plays light but binds heavy, sitting between the full-size Joyride and the undersized Snack in character.

title: Triple Double x OhYesYo / Zeekio Quiz
content:
History / About
A collaboration between Recess and Zeekio producing an all-stainless-steel yo-yo. The 100% steel construction gives it a unique heft and resonance compared to standard aluminum throws. Ships responsive but plays excellently unresponsive, giving it dual-use appeal across beginner and advanced players. Sold with a pouch — one of the few Recess releases to include a carrying case.

title: 000 / Triple Zero 2024 (Titanium)
content:
History / About
A 10th anniversary re-release of the original titanium Triple Zero, available December 12, 2024. Updated weight distribution and a more comfortable edge bring it up to modern trick standards while preserving the ultra-minimalist design language. Manufacturing quality improved markedly over the 2018 original — glass smooth finish, fine satin brush, no tool marks or unscrew issues. Jeffrey described this run as “miles better” than the first. Released alongside the experimental 000D mini variant. Only 50 numbered units.

title: 000 / Triple Zero 6061
content:
History / About
The Triple Zero design reimagined in 6061 aircraft-grade aluminum. Prototyped specifically to capture the floaty, fun feel of the titanium and plastic versions while making the iconic design accessible at a lower price point. The 2025 run introduced three new colorways. Continues the tradition of translating the Triple Zero’s design language across materials — titanium to plastic to aluminum — for different audiences and play contexts.

title: 000D / Triple Zero D-Bearing Mini (2024)
content:
History / About
An experimental mini variant of the Triple Zero released alongside the 2024 titanium reissue on December 12, 2024. Uses a D-size bearing instead of the standard C, exploring how bearing size and the resulting change in diameter alter the character of the iconic Triple Zero design. At 49.2mm it is one of the smallest titanium throws Luftverk has produced. Only 50 numbered units globally.

title: 000 / Fulvia Monometal (Raw Aluminum / Ti-7068 Series)
content:
History / About
The 000 and Fulvia designs were simultaneously reimagined in new materials and released together. The raw aluminum has a beautiful rainbow effect from a slow machining pass — similar to the RSP finish on early Evora releases. The 000 version has an additional stepped sheen from the CNC toolpath that creates a rainbow illusion on the surface, a purely aesthetic byproduct of the machining process. Initial release was 40 raw units of each design.

title: 000 / Triple Zero Hybrid
content:
History / About
The Triple Zero design continues into hybrid material territory — extending the lineage from titanium (2018) to plastic (2023) to aluminum (2024) into a new hybrid construction. Specific material composition not fully documented at time of this research. Currently available at $70 on luftverk.com.

title: 000 / Triple Zero (Original Titanium)
content:
History / About
The defining model of the Luftverk lineup, conceived in 2017 and released in 2018. The Triple Zero was one of the first “ultra minimalist” organic yo-yos of its era — a completely uninterrupted organic curve from hub to rim with no steps, no V-shape, no interruptions. It became a flagship not just for Luftverk but for the organic yo-yo movement as a whole, with its design language eventually carried through to plastic and aluminum variants. Known for a floaty, fast feel on the string that remains unique in titanium.

title: 000 / Triple Zero Ti-7068 Bimetal
content:
History / About
The iconic Triple Zero design reimagined as a bimetal, released around 2022. Uses 7068 aluminum with a titanium ring that is fully embedded and sandwiched inside the outer lip — an extremely rare inner-rim construction. Unlike most bimetals where the ring sits exposed on the rim, here it is completely hidden inside the body. This preserves the clean minimalist aesthetic of the original while adding stability. Per Luftverk, the risk of ring separation is virtually zero due to the construction method. Maintains the floaty, organic feel the 000 is famous for.

title: Triplet
content: AboutThe Triplet is the 3A signature of Yasuki Tachibana, who also used the Laser at the 2013 World YoYo Contest. The 57mm diameter matches the Sleipnir and Draupnir, but the 40mm width — nearly as narrow as the Fragment — is deliberately chosen for 3A pair formation stability. The 70g weight adds momentum for 3A's unique demands. Triplet players benefit from the extra heft when managing two throws simultaneously.

title: Triton
content:
History / About
The Triton is G2's third release and their first of 2013, arriving after the brand won New Manufacturer of the Year at the end of 2012. Reviewer Brett Grimes (High Speed YoYo) described the Triton as a "night and day difference" from the Albatross despite visual similarities — the profile retains the Albatross rim curve but adds Project 2-style grooves and a more industrial cup with a sharper inner rim cut. At 66.7g it has more heft than its predecessors, contributing to what reviewers called "rock solid" stability. The Triton is especially suited for flowing, artistic tricks and longer combo play.

title: Tropic Alien
content:
History / About
The Tropic Alien is the signature model of Zafran Aqil, two-time Malaysian National Champion and Recess team member. The curved H-shape profile gives it a comfortable feel in hand and powerful string presence. What makes the Tropic Alien stand out beyond specs is the story behind its artwork: Zafran worked with his friend Diane Tahir to design an alien character named "Mamood," depicted wearing a sarung (traditional Malay garment) and an Asian farming hat. Zafran's stated desire was to bring his culture wherever his passion for yo-yoing takes him. Reviewers noted the organic/V-shape hybrid character makes it an excellent all-rounder — competitive-level stability and spin time in a shape that also excels at creative content.

title: Troupe
content: AboutThe Troupe is JT's premium offstring released in 2025, built on the Cirrus shape with added rim weight for significantly improved stability. Released simultaneously in two material configurations: the PC variant pairs a polycarbonate body with a stainless steel rim (78.2g), while the POM variant uses a POM body with 6061 aluminum rings (77.0g) for a softer, more controlled feel. Both share the same profile and inner dimensions.

title: TRUENO
content: AboutTRUENO is the second signature model of Bryan Figueroa, featuring an extra-wide POM profile and a distinctive double ring cup design. Entry-friendly for players still developing catch consistency, but competition-capable for advanced technique. Available as the TRUENO Light in translucent polycarbonate with a black hub, and in Blue with a Blue Hub.

title: Trvth (Original)
content:
History / About
Dominik loves his SB2 so much, so we decided to work on a classic shape yoyo, a tribute to Tom Kuhn’s classic. We finally came up with nothing but the Trvth.

Production Runs

Proto #1 — 9 units, Black; D54.00mm / W26.00mm / 66.00g. Finish: Candodize.
Proto #2 (June 2011) — 10 units, Black; D54.40mm / W28.50mm / 66.60g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (February 2012) — 12 units, Black; D54.40mm / W28.50mm / 66.60g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #2 (September 2014) — 30 units, Titanium; D54.40mm / W28.50mm / 66.60g. Finish: Candodize.

title: Trvth2
content:
The following is archived from ILYY:

The Trvth came to life as a tribute to the legendary SB-2 by Tom Kuhn. Being one of the few ILYYs with engravings it struck a nerve for ILYY fans and collectors.

For this 2025 re-invention, we went all out in terms of performance. The Trvth2 features massive stainless steel weight rings that carry 66.6% of the body weight, making the Trvth2 the most rim-weighted ILYY ever, it is relentless.

Also new for this era is an old school death metal inspired “side b” engraving of fleshy darkness by none other than the great Mark Riddik and a box that has seen the undead.

A note about optical imperfections

The Trvth2 batch has slight optical imperfections in the form of black spots around the response area and in the cup.

These are fairly subdued thanks to the black anodizing and bold engraving. We decided against trashing the batch and having them remade since we dislike the thought of scrapping perfectly fine yoyos. Instead, we will offer them at a €20 discount. These imperfections are only cosmetic and do not affect play. The spots are also barely visible without closely inspecting them. We even think they go nicely with the gnarly undead theme of the yoyo.

title: Tsunami
content:
History / About
The Tsunami was released in 2023 as part of G2's growing modern catalog. The AL7 Tsunami, using a 7068 aluminum body with stainless steel rims, became a popular bimetal option for players wanting G2 competition performance at a competitive price. It received a "Totality" solar eclipse colorway in 2024 alongside several other G2 models.

title: Tundra
content:
History / About
A collaboration between Luftverk and CLYW, the Tundra blends the design languages of both companies into a single titanium release. The catch zone was inspired by the CLYW Chief and original Yeti; the step near the pad mirrors the Borealis; and the response uses CLYW’s beloved Snow Tire pads. Originally planned for 150 units, 90 had to be destroyed due to anodization issues — leaving only 55 total. First available at the 2016 World Yo-Yo Contest in Cleveland before an online release on August 5th. Each came in exquisite packaging with a hand-stained wood inlay cut by Drew Tetz and custom grey-on-grey patches.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Center Trac (Size C); full ceramic on AMS2488 version

title: Turduccen
content: AboutReleased November 30, 2023, the Turduccen is Rain City's tri-metal flagship and the apex of the Ducc family. A 7068 aluminum body combined with stainless steel and brass rings delivers "stable with a bit of float." Named after turducken and the base Ducc model. Arrived in elaborate nesting packaging: handcrafted yoga-chicken bag inside a duck coin purse inside a turkey fabric bag. Price: $135.

title: Burning Hammer
content: History / AboutPer Turnbuckle (as posted on YoYoExpert), Burning Hammer is the second release, named for Kenta Kobashi's super finisher that he performed only seven times. It takes design cues from modern yoyos in a 6061 aluminum body. Released August 2022.

title: Tiger Driver
content: History / AboutPer Turnbuckle (as posted on YoYoExpert), Tiger Driver is the first of the Four Pillars, named for the Four Pillars of Heaven wrestlers of All Japan Pro Wrestling: Mitsuharu Misawa, Kenta Kobashi, Akira Toue and Toshiaki Kawada. It is an organic shape with modern elements, a slightly thinner than standard gap and a balance of rim and center weight aimed at stable regens. Released April 2022.

title: Goemon
content: History / AboutGoemon is the first looping model officially released under the Turning Center brand, a lathe-machining workshop known for making yo-yos for Turning Point and Japan Technology. It was developed over more than three years and its prototype won the Mods division in 2013. The Delrin body, anodized aluminum side rings and aluminum spacers are all machined, giving a smoother feel than molded plastic. The caps are made of Hakone yosegi-zaiku, traditional marquetry. Parts such as bearing and axle use standards easily available in Japan to ease repair. The name refers to the folk hero Ishikawa Goemon.

title: Behemoth 2018
content:
About
The Behemoth 2018 (44CLASH Edition) is the collaboration between Turning Point and 44CLASH for the event's 10th anniversary in 2018. A modified Leviathan design fitted with hubstacks, the Behemoth's H-profile accommodates a custom center axis for the hubstack system while maintaining the high spin power and rim weight that characterizes Turning Point's engineering approach. The 6061 aluminum body at 70.3g delivers significant momentum during play.

title: Turtle
content:
From Turner Return Tops:

"It’s been a while. How’ve you been? We’ve been busy.

We’re pleased to announce our next major release, the Turtle is here!!!

The first of six colorways this release is classic clear, the master, the rat!

4 pieces of precision machined 7068 aluminum have been fitted together to form each of these terrestial terrapin terrors.

Light and fun, this return top will truly test your meddle. It feels wide in the hand, but the catch is narrow and requires attention to detail. This turtle is ready for training with precision control.

This is also our first release to come in our new standard #turnertube packaging. A custom papercraft tube lined with 3 separate pieces of sponge to ensure your top arrives in the same condition we packaged it in! This package also features our TRT logo cut window in the top for your viewing pleasures."

title: Glow Kevlar String
content: AboutThe Glow Kevlar String combines the ultra-durable Kevlar construction of Twisted Stringz's Premium Kevlar line with the glow-in-the-dark treatment from the Luminous-X. The result is the most performance-oriented stage string in the lineup — long-lasting and bright under UV or darkness. Sold individually at $2.49. Available colorways: Chartreuse, Blonde, Jaded Lemon, and KGB.

title: Premium Kevlar String
content: AboutThe Premium Kevlar String is Twisted Stringz's most durable offering, constructed from Kevlar fiber. Kevlar's inherent yellow coloring forms the base of the string; colorway names (Jaded Lemon, KGB, Blonde) reflect accent thread variations over that yellow base. Positioned as the most long-lasting string in the lineup and sold individually at $1.99 — a reflection of the material cost and handmade construction. Suited for all play styles and particularly favored by players who want to go long sessions without a string change.

title: Luminous-X Glow String
content: AboutThe Luminous-X is Twisted Stringz's glow-in-the-dark performance string. Made from polyester with glow treatment, it plays comparably to Type E — soft, ready-to-play, minimal break-in — while delivering brighter glow performance than competing glow strings on the market at the time. Available in seven named colorways: Acid Wash, Blue Grass, Coven, Electric Strawberry, Sunshine, Envy, and Peach. Sold in 5-packs at $8.99. The Luminous-X proved the glow category didn't have to sacrifice playability for stage performance.

title: Mini String
content: AboutMini String is a handmade polyester string engineered specifically for micro and mini yo-yos with narrow gaps. Standard-length strings are too thick for the tiny bearings in yo-yos like the YoYoFactory Mighty Flea, making a purpose-built thin string essential. Twisted Stringz Mini String fills that niche with handmade quality in a thinner construction, available in 5-packs at $7.99. Colorways include Blue, Green, and Yellow. Not compatible with standard-size yo-yos.

title: Polyester String — Extra Thick
content: AboutThe Polyester Extra Thick is the heaviest string in Twisted Stringz's commercial bulk line, designed for maximum string presence in the gap. Ideal for 4A (off-string) play, 5A (freehand), and wide-gap 1A setups where extra string mass improves plane control and trick definition. Available in Blue, Green, Orange, Pink, White, and Yellow. Sold in 10-packs ($6.99) and 100-packs ($22.99); the 100-pack includes a string cutter. Length is 60 inches.

title: Polyester String — Regular
content: AboutThe Polyester Regular is the entry point of Twisted Stringz's commercial bulk line, which succeeded the handmade premium types as the brand's retail-facing product. Made from 100% polyester at normal thickness, these strings break in quickly, last well, and perform reliably at slacks and whips. Available in Blue, Green, Orange, Pink, White, and Yellow. Sold in 10-packs ($5.99) and 100-packs ($22.99). The 60-inch length allows players to cut to preference. Distributed through Zeekio and YoYoSam.

title: Polyester String — Thick
content: AboutThe Polyester Thick is the mid-tier offering in Twisted Stringz's commercial bulk line, running the same 100% polyester at increased thickness for more string mass in the gap. Favored by players who prefer more tactile feedback on the string or who run wide-gap throws. Available in Blue, Green, Orange, Pink, White, and Yellow. Sold in 10-packs ($6.99) and 100-packs ($22.99); the 100-pack includes a string cutter. Length is 60 inches.

title: Project-X
content: AboutProject-X is the flagship offering of the Twisted Stringz handmade lineup, positioned at the top of the type hierarchy. The name reflects its origins as an experimental prototype that proved to be the best-received string Jenn produced. Community members consistently cite it as their preferred type, praising its whip performance and exceptional durability above all other types in the line. Specific material and thickness details are not documented in surviving sources. Production appears to have been limited and the type was discontinued along with the broader handmade line around 2014.

title: Trifecta Bearing
content: AboutThe Trifecta Bearing is the signature hardware product from Twisted Stringz, introduced around 2012 alongside the premium string line. A Size C (.250×.500×.187 inch) 10-ball ABEC 7 stainless steel bearing, the Trifecta features a dual-curved inner groove that functions as a hybrid between a KonKave-style centering curve and a deep recessed channel. This profile keeps the string centered during play while providing a deeper pocket than a standard KonKave, reducing string-on-wall contact. It became one of the most widely adopted aftermarket upgrade bearings of the early 2010s unresponsive era and is still sold through Zeekio. Shipped in the Aftermath Apocalypse (Zeekio × Twisted Stringz collab) and Spintastics Tornado Full Glow as the included bearing.

title: Type A
content: AboutType A is the original Twisted Stringz handmade string, made from 100% nylon. It ships stiff out of the package and requires a 20–30 minute break-in — stretch the string, throw hard binds, and let it loosen up. Once broken in, it transforms into one of the most consistent tension-holders in the handmade lineup, excelling at slack tricks, whips, and advanced moves like behind-the-head vanishes. Longest-lasting type in the premium line; experienced players favor it for extended sessions without constant readjustment.

title: Type A-1
content: AboutType A-1 is a polyester-nylon blend iteration of the Type A formula. It retains the excellent tension-holding properties that made Type A a community favorite but with a noticeably softer, smoother texture that reduces string burn and requires less break-in time. Suitable for both beginners and advanced players. Lasts approximately 1.5–2 weeks with consistent play. An accessible entry point into the premium handmade line without sacrificing performance.

title: Type B
content: AboutType B is the thick, soft-play string in the Twisted Stringz handmade lineup. Constructed from polyester with a fat, bouncy build, it excels at whips, lacerations, and suicides, and is particularly well-suited for wide-gap yo-yos, including those running KonKave-style bearings. The primary recommendation is for 4A (off-string) and 5A (freehand) players, though wide-gap 1A setups benefit as well. Not recommended for narrow-gap unresponsive setups — the extra bulk can cause sag and snap-back issues.

title: Type C
content: AboutType C is the all-around workhorse of the Twisted Stringz handmade line. Hand-twisted from medium-weight polyester, it performs well across slack tricks, whips, and general technical play. The balance of thickness and tension retention makes it the most approachable type for players who want premium handmade quality without specializing in a specific style. Sold in 10-packs; confirmed colorways include Chupacabra and Nessie, following the lineup's cryptid-inspired naming theme.

title: Type E
content: AboutType E is the most accessible string in the Twisted Stringz handmade lineup. Made from 100% polyester, it plays well right out of the package with minimal break-in required — unlike the nylon-based Type A. Performance is comparable to standard commercial polyester strings, elevated by the handmade construction. Type E became the internal benchmark for the Luminous-X glow line, which was described as playing comparably to Type E. A solid daily-carry choice for players who rotate strings frequently.

title: Two Bits
content: AboutThe Two Bits is Rain City's micro-micro: a stainless steel yoyo roughly the size of a US quarter, the smallest in the Canadian coin micro series. Arrives in a coin purse with pogs and a 10-pack of thin string. Released June 2022.

title: Two Fat Ladies
content: The Two Fat Ladies was Werrd's first yo-yo, released in 2006. Named after the bingo call "N 88 – Two Fat Ladies," it introduced the Beefcake bearing setup — two stacked Size C bearings — which centers the string without requiring a concave bearing. The rounded butterfly profile made it a comfortable everyday and competition throw capable of 1A, 3A, and 5A play.

title: Tyrant
content:
From Alchemik:

"Introducing: the Tyrant, a tribute to the legendary Chronos with a daring twist. Crafted from solid titanium and equipped with D bearings, this high-performance yoyo embodies precision engineering and timeless elegance.

The Tyrant pays homage to its predecessor while forging its own path, boasting extended spin times and unparalleled durability. With the blessing of the SoSerious Yoyos, Alchemik Yoyos has seamlessly blended tradition with innovation, creating a yoyo that stands at the pinnacle of excellence."

title: Ultima BTM
content:
History / About
Released July 25, 2019, the Ultima BTM was built after Jeffrey returned to Toronto. Aesthetically close to the Fulvia but with a concave profile that fundamentally changes how it feels — the curve hugs the middle finger during catch and throw, and locks finger grinds more firmly. A unique TiAlN (Titanium Aluminum Nitrate) PVD coating gives the finish a deep blue haze that photographs poorly but looks stunning in hand. The BTM variant uses titanium rings matched and pressed by Jeffrey himself using a Delrin negative to ensure no warpage — a quality-control process he developed after issues during the Fulvia BTM-R production.

title: Ultimate Eagle
content: AboutThe Ultimate Eagle is JT's stainless steel-ringed Delrin offstring released in 2014. Originally debuted as a limited contest exclusive at the 2014 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest, the production version was redesigned with a smaller diameter (70mm) and increased width (56.2mm) compared to the contest prototype. The blue colorway was machined from solid colored Delrin. Available in White, Green, Black, and Blue.

title: Ultra Lights Side Effects
content:
Ultra Lights are currently available in:

Aluminum: Multiple Colors

Brass

title: Ultracut
content: AboutThe Ultracut is Yoyofriends' answer to the ultimate budget competition monometal, offering a wide-body 6061 design with a 50mm catch zone and heavy rim weighting. At 58mm diameter and 50mm width, it provides an unusually large landing area for its price tier, designed to handle any trick in any situation on a budget.

title: Umbra
content:
From MK1:

"Inspired by other wide yoyos that paved the way (such as the CLASHcube, Superwide, Atlas, etc), the Umbra is a super wide, super lightweight, and all-around super fun yoyo that is 100% sure to give you a smile*.

*We are legally required to say that the Umbra may or may not give you a smile."

The first run of Umbras were released in blue and a pink/purple fade.

The 2nd Run

The second run of the Umbra began selling on June 16th, 2021, with several new colorways.

title: Unbound
content: The Unbound is W1LD's first inner-rim bi-metal, inspired by the Boundless offstring. Unlike conventional bi-metals where the weight rims sit at the outermost edge, the Unbound's stainless steel rims are positioned on the interior of the yo-yo, delivering a balanced weight distribution with a hollow, airy play feel. Precision meets power in an unconventional configuration.

title: Underdog
content: First released in 2005, the Underdog 1 was a modified version of a Freehand 1. It was an aluminum bodied yo-yo with one side deeply recessed. You could fit 5 stacked friction stickers in the recess, allowing you to customize the amount of response you wanted. It was also one of the first yo-yos to have an inner lip on the rim for thumb grinds. It had a Teflon hard coat finish.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size A Bearing w/ Duncan Spacers/O-Ring for an Adjustable Gap

title: Underdog 2
content:
The Underdog 2 was created in 2018 and was never sold publicly. It was a modern styled yoyo, very different from the original Underdog. These were only sold to friends and family. They came in grey hardcoat ($70) and red hardcoat ($80). Matt had said the red was "very limited".

Photo from Matt Schmidt

title: Unicorn
content:
From MK1:

"Is it a yoyo? Or a spintop?

The Unicorn is a cap-compatible bimetal that looks unassuming before being adorned with its “horns”, which transform it into a unique palm-spinning toy that still plays like a traditional unresponsive yo-yo.

The core idea behind the Unicorn was to make something that crossed the line between yoyo and spin-top, making it ideal for palm-spins, walk-the-dog-sideways, and other fun ideas that aren’t always practical with other yo-yos.

MK1 YoYos dug through the history of yo-yo/top combinations, sometimes playfully called “terror tops”, and came away with a shape & size that took those ideas into a more unresponsive direction.

The Unicorn features removable caps, allowing you to customize your yoyo like never before. These caps are cross-compatible with most Duncan-sized (48mm) yoyo caps."

The Unicorn had three different releases:

Early release at the 2023 US National Yoyo Contest in Mesa, Arizona.

First retail release of 120 units on August 5th, 2023.

Second retail release of 240 units on February 16th, 2024.

Production Colorways

Unknown Edition

Caps
