title: Affinity
content: The Affinity is Unity yoyos' first release: a 64g stable, floaty, all-around forgiving mono-metal machined from 7075 aluminum. Each comes with a Zipline x Sochi Alphaline string, collectible box, and sticker with art by Carter Tanney. A 5A edition ships with a matching titanium chainmail counterweight by Dustin Gunter.

title: Universal Gravitation
content: AboutThe Universal Gravitation is a premium bi-metal upgrade of the Gravitation line, using 7075 aluminum for the body and stainless steel rings placed closer to the center for enhanced stability and control for long, intricate combos. Available with brass or silver rings in Blue/Brass, Green/Brass, Green/Black/Gold with Silver rings, Black/Pink/Silver with Silver rings, and Clear.

title: Unleashed
content: About the UnleashedThe Unleashed is the signature 2A looping model of National Champion Joseph Harris and marks a significant departure in YoYoJam's looping philosophy: the first looper to use starburst response instead of the traditional O-ring system. Both shim inserts and body twisting allow gap adjustment. Championship editions were produced for the 2011–2014 World YoYo Contests.

title: Abduction
content:
About the Abduction
The Abduction is Elliot Ogawa's signature throw for UNPRLD, released around 2019. An oversized 7075 aluminum monometal at 58.01mm diameter, it stands out in the catalog for its wide diameter relative to its width, shaped to suit Ogawa's playing style.

title: Anion
content:
About the Anion
The Anion is a 6061 aluminum monometal released by UNPRLD in 2024 as the counterpart to the Ion bimetal. The pair shares design DNA but diverges in construction — where the Ion adds stainless steel rim weights, the Anion stays full aluminum for a different weight distribution and playing feel.

title: Antidote
content:
About the Antidote
The Antidote is a plastic yo-yo produced in collaboration with Top Yo and released at the 2019 World Yo-Yo Contest. Based on the shape of UNPRLD's Corruption monometal, the Antidote was the brand's first full plastic model and its first collaboration with Top Yo.

title: Asteria
content:
About the Asteria
The Asteria is Tsukasa Asahara's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2026. A 7075 aluminum bimetal with stainless steel rims at midship placement — following the approach used in the Novalis — it is designed around Asahara's specific competition preferences.

title: Beach
content:
About the Beach
The Beach is an oversized polycarbonate throw from UNPRLD, released in 2026. At 70.87mm diameter it falls into off-string size territory, though the brand presents it for casual string-trick and freestyle play. It represents a departure from UNPRLD's typical precision-machined metal competition lineup.

title: Clarity
content:
About the Clarity
The Clarity is UNPRLD's first 4A (off-string) yo-yo, released in 2025. A departure from the brand's 1A-focused catalog, it uses a polycarbonate body with stainless steel rim weights — construction suited to the durability and weight requirements of off-string play. At 69.37mm diameter and 78.1g, it meets standard 4A competition specifications.

title: Coglite
content:
About the Coglite
The Coglite is Colin Beckford's third signature for UNPRLD, released in 2021 as a lighter reimagining of the Cognition. Featuring a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rim rings, the Coglite shaves weight from the original formula while maintaining the bimetal rim construction that defined Beckford's earlier UNPRLD signatures.

title: Cognition
content:
About the Cognition
The Cognition is Colin Beckford's first signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2018. Built on a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rim rings, it launched what became one of the most prolific player/brand series in the catalog — Beckford went on to design the Coglite, Recognition, Notion, Recognition Redux, and Cognizance for the brand. The Cognition is discontinued.

title: Cognizance
content:
About the Cognizance
The Cognizance is Colin Beckford's sixth signature model for UNPRLD, released in 2026. A tri-material construction using 6061 aluminum, stainless steel rims, and polycarbonate outer elements, it continues the naming thread of Beckford's Cognition-series signatures. At 51.12mm wide it is the widest Beckford UNPRLD signature to date.

title: Constellation
content:
About the Constellation
The Constellation is Daniel Kim's third throw for UNPRLD and his second bimetal signature (distinct from the tri-material Distortion), released in 2026. A 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rim weights, it offers a more conventional bimetal construction compared to Kim's tri-material work of the previous year.

title: Corruption
content:
About the Corruption
The Corruption is a 7075 aluminum monometal designed by UNPRLD founder Tyler Hsieh and released in the brand's founding year. Compact and competition-ready, its shape later served as the basis for the Antidote, a plastic collaboration with Top Yo released at the 2019 World Yo-Yo Contest. The Corruption represents the monometal side of UNPRLD's early catalog alongside the bimetal Flash and Ignition.

title: Devotion
content:
About the Devotion
The Devotion is a 7075 aluminum bimetal released by UNPRLD in 2024, featuring a step-round profile with stainless steel rim weights. It joins a dense 2024 catalog that includes the Domination UL, Hash, Nation, and Recognition Redux.

title: Distortion
content:
About the Distortion
The Distortion is Daniel Kim's second signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2025. It uses a tri-material construction: 6061 aluminum body, stainless steel rims, and polycarbonate outer elements — combining three materials to tune weight distribution and playing feel beyond two-material bimetals. One of several tri-material designs UNPRLD introduced in its 2025–2026 lineup.

title: Domination UL
content:
About the Domination UL
The Domination UL (Ultra Light) is Nate Dailey's first signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2024. A 6061 aluminum H-profile monometal at 62.2g, it is among the lightest throws in the UNPRLD catalog. The UL suffix signals its weight-optimized construction for players who prefer a lighter feel on string. Dailey's second signature, the Nation bimetal, was released in the same year.

title: Elevation
content:
About the Elevation
The Elevation is Patrick Canny's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2020. A 7075 aluminum monometal, it joins the Nostalgia and Elimination as part of the brand's 2020 catalog expansion.

title: Elimination
content:
About the Elimination
The Elimination is UNPRLD's second collaboration with Top Yo, released around 2020. Built on an A7003 aluminum body with a double-rim stainless steel construction, it carries the largest diameter (58.89mm) of any UNPRLD release. A follow-up to the 2019 Antidote plastic collab, the Elimination is a full bimetal designed for competition play.

title: Flash
content:
About the Flash
The Flash was UNPRLD's first yo-yo and Yuki Nishisako's debut signature model, released in 2016. Constructed with a 6061 aluminum body and stainless steel rim weights, it established the bimetal-forward direction the brand would pursue across its full catalog. As both a founder's statement and a signature throw, the Flash set the precision-machined standard that defined UNPRLD's early identity.

title: Flashback
content:
About the Flashback
The Flashback is Yuki Nishisako's second signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2018 as a follow-up to the original Flash. Moving from a 6061 to a 7075 aluminum body, the Flashback refined the bimetal formula with updated geometry while retaining the stainless steel rim construction of its predecessor.

title: Hash
content:
About the Hash
The Hash is Tetsuto Kato's signature throw for UNPRLD, first released in 2024 with an updated run in 2025. It uses a 7075 aluminum body with 6061 aluminum hollow caps in a step-round construction — an approach that concentrates weight differently than a conventional solid profile. The design reflects Kato's specific feel preferences not achievable with standard monometal construction.

title: Ignition
content:
About the Ignition
Released in 2016 as Eric Tranton's first signature throw for UNPRLD, the Ignition is a bimetal built on a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rim weights. Part of the brand's inaugural lineup alongside the Flash, it reflects UNPRLD's early focus on performance-grade bimetal designs for sponsored players.

title: Informel
content:
About the Informel
The Informel is In Hyeok Choi's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2022. A 7075 aluminum monometal, it joined a busy UNPRLD year that also produced the Seiji and Motif.

title: Ion
content:
About the Ion
The Ion is a 6061 aluminum bimetal released by UNPRLD with an updated run in 2025, paired conceptually with the Anion monometal. The addition of stainless steel rim weights over the Anion's baseline geometry provides increased rim mass and a distinctly different playing feel from its monometal sibling.

title: Metal Capsule
content:
About the Metal Capsule
The Metal Capsule is a collaboration between UNPRLD and designer dt, released in 2025. Its wide H-profile — 59.29mm wide at a 54.35mm diameter — takes visual and structural inspiration from capsule toy (gachapon) design. A 6061 aluminum monometal, it is among the widest throws in the UNPRLD catalog by width-to-diameter ratio.

title: Method
content:
About the Method
The Method is Park Junsang's second throw for UNPRLD, released around 2023 in collaboration with Japanese brand Sochi Company. A 6061 aluminum monometal, it takes a lighter approach compared to Junsang's bimetal first signature, the Seiji.

title: Motif
content:
About the Motif
The Motif is Daniel Kim's first signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2022. It uses a hybrid construction: a 7075 aluminum main body combined with a 6061 aluminum cap — a stepped design that produces a specific weight distribution not achievable with a single alloy. The Motif preceded Kim's Distortion and Constellation by several years.

title: Nation
content:
About the Nation
The Nation is Nate Dailey's second signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2024 alongside the Domination UL. A 6061 aluminum bimetal with stainless steel rim weights, it contrasts with the same-year Domination UL — where that model prioritizes low weight in a full monometal, the Nation adds rim mass for a different playing character.

title: Nostalgia
content:
About the Nostalgia
The Nostalgia is Shuyun Tang's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2020. A bimetal featuring a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rim weights, it is part of the brand's 2020 lineup alongside the Elevation and Elimination.

title: Notion
content:
About the Notion
The Notion is Colin Beckford's fourth signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2023. It uses a POM (polyoxymethylene/Delrin) body with stainless steel rim weights — a hybrid construction that gives the throw different weight feel and response character compared to Beckford's aluminum-body UNPRLD signatures.

title: Novalis
content:
About the Novalis
The Novalis is a bimetal released by UNPRLD around 2024. It uses a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rings positioned at the midship rather than the outer rim — a placement that produces a different spin axis weight distribution compared to conventional rim-weighted bimetals. The name references the 18th-century German Romantic poet.

title: Oblivion
content:
About the Oblivion
The Oblivion is Chandler Steele's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2025. Like the same-year Distortion and later Cognizance, it uses a tri-material construction combining 6061 aluminum, stainless steel, and polycarbonate rims — part of UNPRLD's expanding use of three-material design for precise weight targeting.

title: Patience
content:
About the Patience
The Patience is Aidan Cioch's signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2025. A 7075 aluminum monometal, it offers a full-aluminum alternative in a 2025 lineup that otherwise leans heavily toward tri-material and bimetal construction.

title: Recognition
content:
About the Recognition
The Recognition is Colin Beckford's second signature model for UNPRLD, released in 2019. Departing from the bimetal Cognition, the Recognition is a full 7075 aluminum monometal — lighter and differently shaped for a distinct playing character. It was later updated as the Recognition Redux in 2024.

title: Recognition Redux
content:
About the Recognition Redux
The Recognition Redux is an updated reimagining of Colin Beckford's 2019 Recognition monometal for UNPRLD, released in 2024. It grows the original formula — wider at 47.12mm vs. the original's 45.79mm — while maintaining full 7075 aluminum construction. The Redux is Beckford's fifth distinct model for the brand.

title: Reduction
content:
About the Reduction
Released in 2019, the Reduction is a compact 6061 aluminum monometal in the UNPRLD catalog. At 53.76mm diameter it is one of the smaller throws the brand has produced, offering a distinct feel from the bimetal-heavy lineup surrounding it.

title: Seiji
content:
About the Seiji
The Seiji is Park Junsang's first signature throw for UNPRLD, released in 2022. Constructed from a 7068 aluminum alloy body — a high-strength alloy less common in production throws — with stainless steel rim weights, the Seiji is one of the few UNPRLD models to use 7068 as its body material. Junsang's second UNPRLD signature, the Tenacity, followed in 2025.

title: SU 01
content:
About the SU 01
The SU 01 is a bimetal produced in collaboration between sOMEThING and UNPRLD, released around 2020. The name condenses the two brands' initials — S from sOMEThING, U from UNPRLD. Built on a 7075 aluminum body with stainless steel rim weights, the SU 01 merges the design sensibilities of both brands into a single competition-focused throw. Also known as SU:1.

title: Sublation
content:
About the Sublation
The Sublation is a collaboration between Japanese brand Aufheben and UNPRLD, released in 2022. A 7075 aluminum monometal, the name references the Hegelian concept of Aufhebung — negation-and-preservation — nodding to both brands' identities. It is UNPRLD's collaboration with Aufheben, outside its primary collab partners Top Yo and sOMEThING.

title: Tenacity
content:
About the Tenacity
The Tenacity is Park Junsang's second signature for UNPRLD, released in 2025. A 7075 aluminum bimetal with stainless steel rim weights, it is wider (48.26mm) and heavier (68.1g) than Junsang's first signature, the Seiji — reflecting an evolution in spec preference from the 2022 design.

title: Apollo
content: About the ApolloThe Apollo is Unspoken Project's third release and the signature model of team rider Alexis JV. It launched November 16, 2017 at 8 PM EST through YoYoExpert. Machined from 7075 aluminum — a step up in strength and density from 6061 — the Apollo was engineered to be simultaneously light, fast, and stable.The design features slightly scalloped rims that bring a portion of the rim weight inward toward the center, aiding in maneuverability without sacrificing the stability that comes from rim-heavy distribution. The result is a throw that excels at speed-oriented 1A play while remaining comfortable for grinding. Two colorways were offered at launch: Turquoise and Cherry Fade, both with minimal engraving and a smooth grind-friendly finish.The Apollo was designed with two material variants — a version with stainless steel accents (63g) and a brass-accented version (64g) — though the primary release was the monometal 7075 aluminum body.

title: Artemis
content: About the ArtemisThe Artemis is Unspoken Project's first bimetal yoyo and their most competition-focused design at the time of release. It debuted in January 2020 through YoYoExpert, positioned as a more powerful and stable counterpart to the Apollo.Where the Apollo balanced rim weight with center mass for maneuverability, the Artemis pushes the profile wider and adopts a more angular shape to maximize speed and on-plane stability. Inner stainless steel rings add rotational mass at the periphery, delivering the extended spin times demanded by complex modern 1A sequences. Despite its power, the Artemis retains enough maneuverability for off-plane and horizontal play.The Artemis was well received and received subsequent colorway restocks, including pink and gold runs. It remains Unspoken's flagship bimetal.

title: Decoy
content: About the DecoyThe Decoy is a bimetal collaboration between 2SickYoYos and Unspoken Project, released October 31, 2018 through YoYoExpert. The project was over six months in the making, beginning in January 2018, and sought to merge the signature design philosophies of both companies into a single throw.2SickYoYos's contribution was their proven sandwiched bimetal ring construction — stainless steel rings bonded within the aluminum body — a method that had appeared on all their previous bimetal models but always with flat rims. For the Decoy, Unspoken introduced a faceted rim treatment, a design element seen on the Paradox and Murmur, creating an angled edge that is distinctive visually and provides a different grind surface character.The profile is a clean V-shape with smoothed edges for comfort, an inner lip characteristic of 2Sick designs, a simple dome hub, and concentric stepped lines in the cup. Weight is distributed heavily to the rims, producing a powerful and stable spin while maintaining the overall lightweight feel 2Sick is known for.

title: Murmur
content: About the MurmurThe Murmur arrived in early 2018 as Unspoken Project's most accessible release to date. Following the competition-oriented Apollo, the goal for the Murmur was a yoyo that felt balanced and free-flowing, easier on the wallet, and suited to relaxed daily play rather than stage performance.The design adopts an organic profile — a domed hub with a subtle border, smooth catch zone, and gently curved wall — that gives the Murmur a pleasant, nimble character on the string. At 54.20mm diameter and 63.2g, it sits in familiar mid-size territory. The faceted rim detail (seen later echoed in the 2Sick x Unspoken Decoy collaboration) adds visual distinctiveness to the otherwise clean silhouette.The Murmur rewards a controlled, deliberate touch; its organic profile means it will tip off-axis if thrown carelessly. Multiple colorway runs were produced, and a later restock run featured a collaboration with YoYoFactory.

title: Mystic
content: About the MysticThe Mystic launched September 5, 2020 at 8 PM EDT through YoYoExpert. Machined from 7068 aluminum — the same high-strength alloy used in the original Riddle — the Mystic represents the natural progression of Unspoken's monometal line, drawing a direct lineage from the Riddle while advancing the design language.Where earlier Unspoken throws used H-shapes and organic profiles, the Mystic adopts a V-shape, trading the horizontal stability of an H for greater agility and longer spin times through a more aerodynamic cross-section. Heavier rims increase stability and spin power, while a touch of center weight provides a balanced, responsive string feel that doesn't feel like a pure rim-heavy competition machine.At 55mm diameter and 63.7g, the Mystic slots comfortably into the mid-size competition category. Its design was described at launch as a yoyo capable of handling any trick in a player's bag.

title: Paradox
content: About the ParadoxThe Paradox was conceived alongside the Riddle as one of Justin Bui's earliest CAD designs, and was brought to production after the Riddle sold out in early 2017. Where the Riddle was mid-sized and H-shaped, the Paradox pushed in the opposite direction: a small-diameter throw with chunky rims and a simple cup, intended to be genuinely light and floaty rather than the dense-feeling compact yoyos common at the time.At 52mm diameter and just 58g, the Paradox achieved a distinctly airy character on the string — quick-moving and responsive to directional changes without sacrificing spin time. The straightforward cup and rounded profile make it approachable, and the rim-heavy weight distribution keeps it stable despite its reduced size and mass.The Paradox was released in April 2017 through Unspoken's Big Cartel store. A later collaboration colorway with Skully was also produced.

title: Riddle
content: About the RiddleThe Riddle is the inaugural release from Unspoken Project, designed primarily by Justin Bui and refined with the help of Noah Burrows and Alexis JV. It launched on March 17, 2017 at 5 PM PST exclusively through the Unspoken Project Big Cartel store, following a limited prototype run the previous month.The brief was simple: a mid-sized H-shape with enough rim weight to be stable and long-spinning, but light enough at 63.5g to stay nimble. The resulting design features a scalloped catchzone and a profile that sits between competition powerhouse and everyday player. The Riddle is machined from 7068 aluminum — a higher-strength alloy than the standard 6061 — giving it improved durability and allowing for tighter tolerances on the rims.The Riddle sold out quickly and its revenue funded the production run of Unspoken's second release, the Paradox.

title: Untitled 67
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"Untitled 67. A love letter to the process.

Iteration is where the most fun parts of running a yo-yo brand happen. The feeling of throwing a new prototype for the first time, assembling something unique for the first time ever off the 3D printer, or a doodle on your daily carry to make it truly your own. The creative side of yo-yo extends to more than just tricks.

We love making new yo-yos. Freshly Dirty has never been about money, instead your support over these last 9 years has only allowed us to keep iterating and taking more risks. Untitled is all about trying new things and doing what brings joy.

We made a heavyweight counterpart to this yo-yo called the 74. We hope that experiencing both designs will allow players and collectors to get a taste of the process of iteration that we so deeply enjoy.

The “67” engraving is a reminder of the iteration that goes into making anything that is great. We scribble weights on yo-yos when rapidly trying new designs or tweaks to the shape, and something as simple as a number can represent an enormous amount of thought, attention to detail, and love.

Thank you for 9 years of support and for loving this process as much as we do."

title: Untitled 74
content:
From Freshly Dirty:

"Untitled 74. A love letter to the process.

Iteration is where the most fun parts of running a yo-yo brand happen. The feeling of throwing a new prototype for the first time, assembling something unique for the first time ever off the 3D printer, or a doodle on your daily carry to make it truly your own. The creative side of yo-yo extends to more than just tricks.

We love making new yo-yos. Freshly Dirty has never been about money, instead your support over these last 9 years has only allowed us to keep iterating and taking more risks. Untitled is all about trying new things and doing what brings joy.

We made a 74 gram bimetal with big brass rings. It’s oversized, H shaped, and insanely stable. It will help you push into new territory in your 1A. It will make demanding 5A combos immune to tilt or going off plane. But most of all it is a monster of a 3A yo-yo.

The “74” engraving is a reminder of the iteration that goes into making anything that is great. We scribble weights on yo-yos when rapidly trying new designs or tweaks to the shape, and something as simple as a number can represent an enormous amount of thought, attention to detail, and love.

Thank you for 9 years of support and for loving this process as much as we do."

title: UPHEAVAL EXPANSION+
content:
History / About
UPHEAVAL EXPANSION+ is Ryuichi Nakamura's heavier follow-up to his existing Upheaval Expansion signature, released June 21, 2026. YYR describes the increased weight as making it feel like "a completely different product" from the base Expansion.

title: Upshift
content: The Upshift is the signature model of W1LD team member Nam DongHun. An H-profile bi-metal using 7075 aluminum and stainless steel rims, the Upshift is designed for powerful, competition-ready 1A performance at 66.5g with wide proportions for maximum string control.

title: Uragment
content: AboutThe Uragment takes its name from "ura," the Japanese word for "behind" or "reverse" — reflecting its status as the prototype variant of the Fragment. The two models share the same D-bearing specification and compact 40mm width, but differ in rim shape: the Fragment has a curved outer rim while the Uragment features a flattened, straight-cut rim that shifts the mass distribution slightly. Released as a retail product in 2013 after the Fragment had established its form.

title: USS Enterprise NCC-YOYO-D
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: USS Enterprise NCC-YOYO-D

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Factory:

"Space: the final frontier. These are the voyages of the yoyo Enterprise. Its five-year mission: to explore strange new skill toys; to seek out new throws and new tricks; to boldly yo where no man has yo'd before. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/41RypW. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. Print at 100% infill or it may not work. If you print it and it doesn't come back up add a drop of lube or rub some chapstick on the end of your string and after a couple throws it will work just right. 

There are two stand models, I would start with the smaller model and use it unless you yours doesn't fit, then print out the larger one. 

It also functions as a mediocre spin top if you get bored with yoyoing."

title: Utopia
content: AboutThe Utopia features a dual stainless steel ring design for a strong presence on string, great stability, and excellent spin time. Combines premium 7075 aluminum with two sets of stainless rings. Available in Silver/Gold Rings.

title: V-tour (Prototype)
content:
History / About
The V-tour is BigBoi Yoyo's first full yo-yo release, a collaboration with manufacturer Spintastics Yoyos. Designer Nicholas Privett announced the throw on August 23, 2026, describing it as "our first step as a community back in the direction of aggressive V shaped yo-yos in the competitive world" and noting roughly 18 months of development. As of this writing the yo-yo is in production but has not yet had a public retail release, and it does not yet appear on Spintastics' official catalog.

title: V1
content:
About
V1 is a comfortable full-size yoyo with notably heavy rim weight for long sleep times, finished with a signature acid-wash treatment.

title: V10 Finger Spin
content:
About
V10 is a dual-mode responsive/unresponsive finger-spin yoyo with a concave hub, matte-blasted for grip.

title: V11 Fingerota
content: About the V11 FingerotaThe V11 Fingerota is a bi-material yo-yo pairing a polycarbonate hub cap specifically engineered for finger spin entry with a 6061 aluminum body. The PC cap's small size and low friction surface allows the spinning yo-yo to lock onto a fingertip during finger spin tricks. At 50mm wide, the catch zone is exceptionally generous. Hollow interior optimizes weight distribution. A "Newly" updated variant followed with minor improvements.

title: V12 Topioneer
content: About the V12 TopioneerThe V12 Topioneer is MagicYoYo's most feature-loaded finger spin platform, offering both a yo-yo dimple for fingertip spinning and a dedicated hook finger spin design. Wide 48–50mm profile for generous string catch zone. Ships with both responsive and unresponsive bearings, plus tools, 10 replacement strings, and a carrying case. A comprehensive learning and progression package.

title: V13 Deepspin
content: About the V13 DeepspinThe V13 Deepspin is MagicYoYo's most technically complex finger spin platform. Its tri-material construction pairs a CNC-machined aluminum alloy body with dual polycarbonate outer rings and a PC grooved cap. Tapered finger spin dimples combined with the innovative PC outer rim architecture focus weight for stability while reducing rim mass for smooth finger spin entry. One of the most engineered finger spin designs in MagicYoYo's catalog.

title: V15 SpinTrace
content:
About
V15 SpinTrace has a deep finger-spin hub and wide profile, sold as a dual-purpose beginner-to-pro model.

title: V3
content: About the V3The V3 is one of MagicYoYo's most successful and widely purchased models globally. Its super smooth sand-blasted finish resists scratching and fading, and it ships with both a slim responsive bearing and a KK unresponsive upgrade bearing — covering the full beginner-to-intermediate learning arc in one package. Balanced and stable, suited for high-speed 1A tricks. Available in Aqua, Black, Black with Pink and Aqua Splash, and Green. Extra axle included.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Slim (responsive stock) + Size C KK upgrade

title: V4
content:
About
V4 is a high-speed unresponsive yoyo, CNC lathe-turned, sold with a spinning string as an Amazon-exclusive collaboration release.

title: V6 Locus
content: About the V6 LocusThe V6 Locus builds on the V3's successful formula, adding a polycarbonate finger spin cap and a concave inner ring for finger support during fingerspin tricks. Ships with both responsive and unresponsive bearings. Positioned for beginners through competitive players wanting finger spin capability in an affordable aluminum package. A V6S (upgraded) version followed. Includes 5 replacement strings, tool, and glove.

title: V6S Locus
content:
About
V6S Locus is a sandblast-finished upgrade of MagicYoYo's V6 Locus, sold as its own SKU with a swappable responsive/unresponsive bearing setup.

title: V8
content:
About
V8 is an aluminum butterfly-shaped yoyo with a responsive flat bearing convertible to an unresponsive U-bearing. Predecessor to the previously catalogued V8S Trickseeker, still sold as its own model.

title: V8S Trickseeker
content: About the V8S TrickseekerThe V8S Trickseeker is a wide 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a specially designed finger spin hub for DNA and other finger spin techniques. Ships with both responsive and unresponsive bearings for progressive skill development. Includes 5 strings, upgrade bearing, bearing tool, and a glove. Successor to the V8 with improved hub geometry.

title: Vacation
content:
History / About
The Vacation is the second bimetal from Recess, released in 2016 as a companion to the Weekend. Where the Weekend had a soft, controlled playfeel, the Vacation has a harder, more crisp character with an emphasis on speed and power. The stainless steel rings are fitted seamlessly at the very outer rim for maximum rim weighting. A stepped H-profile provides a comfortable hand feel, the outer lip enables thumb grinds, and the cup is fingerspin-ready. Recess positioned the Weekend and Vacation as intentional counterpoints to each other — both capable, but approaching performance differently so players could understand their own preferences by comparison. Featured in Recess promo content shot in Singapore with Ahmad Kharisma and Daniel Flaherty, and in California with Daniel.

title: Valhalla
content:
History / About
The Valhalla debuted as a Patreon-exclusive before its first public/production release on September 30, 2021 (Pacific Fade colorway), which added an updated spike — slightly longer and sharper, closer to the Banshee spike, more usable for matador play — versus the earlier Patreon version. An AL6 (6061-body) version followed in March 2022, described as "a good bit faster" on the string due to increased rim-weight percentage versus the original 7068 body (difference of ~0.6g).

title: Valhalla Brass
content:
About
Valhalla Brass is a 6061 aluminum with Brass rims yo-yo from G2 Squared Yoyos. Sourced from the community-maintained g2releases.info release tracker; specs and colorway history below are as documented there and have not been cross-checked against an official G2 spec sheet.

title: Valkyrie
content: AboutThe Valkyrie was released at the 2015 World YoYo Contest alongside the Seventh Heaven titanium, offering a bi-metal option at a more accessible price point for the Worlds audience. At 55.5mm × 43.5mm and 67g, it sits between the compact Sputnik and the flagship Draupnir — a deliberate middle ground designed to appeal to players not yet committed to the Draupnir's specific feel. It was later redesigned in a subsequent run.

title: Valor
content:
From One Drop:

"When we approached Vilmos about making a signature yo-yo, his original goal was to make an all around competition throw with a straight forward design. He was going for pure performance that has excellent play demands. Vilmos came to visit One Drop from Hungary and we sat down with him and worked out the design.

In more detail, he asked for a simple and comfortable V shape with small undercut rims and lots of rim weight for long spin times made out of 7075 aluminum. For the play, he wanted it capable of handling all kinds of trick styles including fast technical, horizontal and finger spins. If you watch Vilmos compete you will see what a complete player he is and he needed a yo-yo that would keep up with him.

We added a small circular bump in the hub area to make finger spins possible both inside and outside of the circle. The rest of the hub is as flat as possible to minimize center weight. For some reason, some consider the tap-through axle a "budget" feature, but the use of it here improves performance and quality. Usually on a flat hub yo-yo, a very short axle is used meaning there are less threads which increases the chances of stripping or the yo-yo coming apart. The tap-through axle feature allows the performance of a flat hub yo-yo with the assurance and quality of a longer axle and more threads.

For horizontal play there is nice bump coming out of the guts as well as a nice open wide catch zone to lower string friction so spin times and stability remain constant.

On the last day of the design process, Vilmos came up with the "Triple Grooves" in the catch zone and inside the hub as a unique styling element. It is an new take on our classic "Projection Profile" first seen on the original Project and it looks amazing.

The dictionary defines Valor as "strength of mind or spirit that enables a person to encounter danger with firmness". For Vilmos, the Valor will allow him to encounter his yo-yo challenges with firmness and resolve because of the unique design, high quality dense aluminum and the incredible play."

title: Valve
content:
History / About
We are expanding our lineup of low priced yoyos. The Void was the first one in that category. Now we follow up with Valve and Verve. Both yoyos feature a similar shape and design elements, the Valve being the choice for fans of full size entertainment.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (October 2011) — Green; D54.00mm / W42.00mm / 65.50g. Finish: Candodize.
Run #1 (November 2011) — 85 units, Green/Titanium; D54.00mm / W42.00mm / 65.50g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.

title: Vamos
content: AboutThe Vamos is AceYo's first offstring (4A) yo-yo. Smooth and sturdy POM construction makes it suitable for both learning offstring basics and performing advanced offstring on stage. Available in Black.

title: Vamos 2
content: AboutThe Vamos 2 is an updated version of AceYo's offstring yo-yo with a slightly wider, more forgiving gap for the most outrageous offstring tricks. Same sturdy POM for durability. Available in White and Red.

title: Vandal
content: AboutThe Vandal is JIGUN's budget entry-level competition throw, priced at $20. Machined from aluminum to standard competition specifications, it was produced in a wide range of colorways including Raw, Pink, Dark Green, Light Blue, Purple, Gray Blue, Green, Tiffany Blue, Black, and Colorful. Limited WYYC (World Yo-Yo Contest) colorways — Blue/Silver Splash, Green WYYC, and Purple WYYC — were produced for tournament presence. A Vandal AP Edition was later released for the AP Yo-Yo Open 2026 in AP Green and AP Grayish Purple colorways.

title: Vanitas
content: Leo Chan Matsumoto's first signature bi-metal for C3yoyodesign. Extra-wide profile designed for fingerspins and horizontal play. Signature: Leo Chan Matsumoto. Price: $100–$120.

title: Vanitas 7075 Phase 1
content: History / AboutPhysical Vanitas revision pairing a stronger 7075 body with stainless rims for wider, heavier competition performance.

title: Vanitas Phase WALAO
content: History / AboutLeo Chan signature expansion of Vanitas using 7075, stainless steel, and POM at 57 mm width.

title: Vanitas Spectre
content: History / AboutCombines Vanitas speed with Satinav experience; extensive prototyping shifted more mass into large stainless rims for stability and endurance.

title: Vapor
content: AboutVapor combines trilobal polyester and Maxi-Lock stretch nylon in a 50/50 blend for a normal-disposition comfort string with moderate velocity and lasting shelf life. The trilobal poly adds subtle brightness while keeping the overall feel very soft. Available in Pink Bismuth, Fulminating Gold, Argon, Methylene Blue, Silver Nitrate, and Gentian Violet colorways alongside monocolor.

title: VaporMotion
content:
About
VaporMotion is a hybrid PC/aluminum yoyo: a polycarbonate inner body wrapped in a 6061 aluminum outer cowl, with aluminum fingerspin caps. Developed as a collaboration between C3yoyodesign and MagicYoYo.

title: Variant
content: AboutThe Variant was OFFSET's first product — a high-performance plastic conceived after founder Brandon Vu noticed a gap in the market: plastics were either slow and stable or fast and unstable, never both. After prototyping began in 2017 with Jeffrey Pang (Luftverk founder) at MagicYoYo's factory, the design went through roughly four revisions before landing on something that could genuinely compete with metals. It launched alongside OFFSET in 2020 and became the brand's entry point for players who wanted competition-grade performance without the aluminum price tag.

title: Nova Pro
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the Nova Pro as a ball-bearing yo-yo with seven LED dots (five in a row and two opposite each other, near the perimeter on the face). The lights produce up to 32 light patterns depending on skill level, as indicated on the package. It has a fixed gap and starburst response, and the museum notes it may have an associated patent. The exhibit is dated 1999.

title: Variflex Pro
content: History / AboutVariflex, a mass-market sporting goods company founded in 1977 by Raymond H. Losi, teamed with Team Losi to have two yo-yos produced and an instructional video made (YoYo Wiki). The Yo-Yo Museum records the single yo-yo, labeled "Variflex - Precision ABEC-1 Ball Bearing", as identical except for the bearing to the Team Losi Grim Sleeper and Da Bomb, with an adjustable twist gap and starburst response. The YoYo Wiki says the Variflex Pro came in two shapes.A Competition Yo-Yo Kit was also sold with a clear-body yo-yo labeled "Hi-Tech Ball Bearing - Variflex - Variable String Gap", two extra strings, two weight rings and a pouch; it retailed for US$12 (Yo-Yo Museum). Steve Brown also recorded a Variflex instructional video in 1999.

title: X-Games
content: History / AboutThe Yo-Yo Museum describes the X Games model as a hybrid between a butterfly and an imperial shape with an ABEC-3 bearing. It came with a miniature skateboard with grip tape, removable wheels, metal trucks, tools and spare wheels, and was considered Variflex's top-of-the-line model (collected September 1999).Steve Brown says he developed the Hybrid Bomb shape for Team Losi, which was passed to Variflex for the X-Games yo-yo (Yo-Yo Museum Team Losi profile). The YoYo Wiki notes it was half-way between modified and butterfly shapes.

title: Verge
content:
About
The Verge is an ultra-wide string-trick yo-yo combining a metal body with POM wings, over 60mm wide. The width significantly raises the success rate of mounts in 1A play, and the wide effective gap makes fundamental movements like mounts and hops far more reliable. Positioned for players who perform on stage or want extra stability.

title: Verve
content:
History / About
We are expanding our lineup of low priced yoyos. The Void was the first one in that category. Now we follow up with Valve and Verve. Both yoyos feature a similar shape and design elements, the Verve being the choice for fans of the undersized experience.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (October 2011) — 6 units, Green; D50.00mm / W35.50mm / 62.00g. Bearing: L. Finish: Candodize.

title: Vexed
content: About the VexedThe Vexed is the signature yo-yo of YoYoJam co-founder and Grand Master Bill de Boisblanc, featuring an inverse-round body with ridged brass weight rims for an unusual tactile profile. Its relatively light 64.6 gram weight in an undersized format suits de Boisblanc's technical playing style. The model is constructed from upgraded "Titan" plastic for enhanced durability.

title: VHS
content:
From YoyoExpert:

"The VHS is an organic shaped D bearing yoyo. However it didn't start out its life this way. FD initially wanted to produce the VHS with titanium, however after testing titanium prototypes they realized that they could keep the same extreme rim weight of the yoyo while switching to a much more affordable material, 7068 aluminum.

The results speak for themselves.  Although it's got a classic, unassuming shape, this yoyo's performance is not to be underestimated. FD hopes you love throwing it as much as they've loved the process of bringing it to life."

title: Victorious Fighting Buddha
content: AboutThe Victorious Fighting Buddha "pushes the very limit of hybrid polycarbonate yo-yo" with four-material construction: a frosted polycarbonate body, stainless steel outer ring, 7075 aluminum inner ring, and titanium alloy hub. The most materially complex model in the AceYo lineup. Available in Clear/Silver Ring.

title: Vigilancia
content:
History / About
The Vigilancia was designed to get as close to the Surveillance bimetal feel as possible in a full aluminum monometal model. The original concept behind the Surveillance was a bimetal that was easy to control while retaining bimetal spin power. After several prototypes, mowl achieved impressive spin times for a monometal without sacrificing controllability. Rather than just a cheaper version of the Surveillance, the Vigilancia is described as an evolution — a modern reimagining of what made the original great, now accessible in aluminum.

title: Vigilante
content: About the VigilanteThe Vigilante is the signature model of Mikhail Tulabut, using a distinctive thick hexagonal outer rim profile that generates momentum efficiently despite the yo-yo's angular design and light weight. At 51.48mm it is undersized, suited to Tulabut's precise, technical play style. The step-straight body shape offers a traditional feel with modern response.

title: Vindication
content:
About the Vindication
The Vindication is the second yoyo from Mr. Mazal Top's Yoyos, announced via Instagram in 2021 and sold through the brand's BigCartel store. Continuing the design language of the Vindicator, it uses 7068 aluminum with stainless steel rings and a V-shaped profile tuned for high-speed 1A performance. Like its predecessor, the Vindication was praised in community reviews as a strong performer at its price point — underappreciated despite playing above its class. The model received a dedicated YouTube unboxing and review around 2022.

title: Vindicator
content:
About the Vindicator
The Vindicator is the debut yoyo from Mr. Mazal Top's Yoyos, released in 2020 via the brand's BigCartel store. Built from 7068 aluminum with stainless steel weight rings, it features a V-shaped profile optimized for speed-oriented 1A combo play. Early community reception praised it as a capable performer at its affordable price point, with reviewers noting it was significantly undervalued relative to its playing quality. The Vindicator established the brand's identity as a source for high-alloy bimetal performance at accessible prices.

title: Virtuoso
content:
From One Drop:

"It’s always intriguing to make a signature yo-yo.  We always invite the player to contribute as much as possible to the design so that this important moment for them is the best it can be.  A good measure of success is if the yo-yo is a reflection of the person. Ethan Cheung is a player on our team who is focused on competitive yo-yoing, but he doesn’t sacrifice any artistry in this pursuit.  This rare combination makes Ethan stand out.

If you watch Ethan Cheung’s performance at Worlds 2018 in Shanghai you will notice precision, artistry, clarity, mastery.   If you look at his signature yo-yo, the Virtuoso, you will notice the same characteristics. The 7075 aluminum alloy design is very focused towards function as a hard core competitive yo-yo with all the performance you would expect.  If you look closely, you’ll also see the artistry with the clean flowing lines, the minimalist cup, the light bead blast, and the beautiful “projection profile” on the face of the rim giving a small nod to our first yo-yo, the Project.

Ethan explains his thought process on designing his signature yo-yo:

'At a glance, the design is reminiscent of the Format:C: which was the yoyo that allowed me to push my own boundaries and place 10th at Worlds in Iceland. But if you look more closely, you’ll notice the grooves on the rim - a tribute to the original Project and the roots of One Drop. For this signature model, I wanted a yoyo that would allow me to explore more styles of movement, that complements any style of play thrown at it. It is this balance of comfort and performance, of minimalism and detail, that makes us proud to present: the Virtuoso.'"

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Viscera Butterfly Cap Sticker
content:
About
Viscera Butterfly Cap Sticker is a sticker from Throw-Yo Threads. Thermal-printed sticker sized for Butterfly caps. Types: Holo, White. Price: $1.50-$2.

title: Vision
content: Vision was a wooden yo-yo model produced by Hummingbird in the late 1980s. While detailed specifications and production history are limited, this model was part of Hummingbird's diverse product line during the company's peak years.

title: Vision Trickster
content: Vision Trickster was a variant within Hummingbird's Vision product line, combining elements from the popular Trickster competitive model. This variant represented the company's efforts to offer multiple performance levels to different player demographics.

title: Viszilla
content:
Anti-Yo's Story:

"Six years ago Anti-Yo released the Bapezilla with the idea that you can build a story around a brand and broadcast it through the yoyo world, taking everything about that brand and rolling it into one simple skill-toy. Six years later the image of the hottest brands coming out of Japan are different, the tone is different, the image is simpler. The story is the same, the image and brand inspiration is different. Inspired by the newest and brightest, we bring you the Viszilla."

title: Void
content:
History / About
Up until now, we made premium priced yoyos with premium quality. But now we thought, why not make a premium yoyo for a less premium price? Said and done. The Void was born. Simple shape, a new horn (hello matador) and superb playability. We want only the best just like you! 2011 version brings a bigger horn for easier matador handling.

Production Runs

Run #1 (March 2010) — 40 units, Silver; D52.25mm / W41.10mm / 65.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #2 (June 2010) — 120 units, Blue/Gold; D52.25mm / W41.10mm / 67.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #3 (May 2011) — 110 units, Red/Blue; D52.25mm / W41.10mm / 66.20g. Finish: Candodize.
Special #2 (July 2011) — 26 units, Black; D52.25mm / W41.10mm / 66.20g. Finish: Candodize.
Special #1 (August 2011) — 10 units, Gold; D52.25mm / W41.10mm / 67.00g. Finish: Chroma.

title: 1Sx Zebra
content: History / AboutThe 1Sx Zebra is an undersize Vosun yo-yo with a fixed gap and silicone pads (Vosun official site). Colors: Blue, Gold, Matte Silver, Red.

title: 5S Crawler2
content: History / AboutYo-Yo Store Rewind describes the Crawler2 as the second Crawler, about 2g lighter than the first. The first version had a heavy feel; the Crawler2 keeps strong spin but with less arm fatigue. The shape looks classic, but Rewind says the edges, rim and performance show Vosun's manufacturing skill.

title: 8S Vanquish
content: History / AboutYo-Yo Store Rewind describes the 8S Vanquish as a standard step-round full-metal yo-yo that stands out for sleep power and playability among Vosun's low-priced metals, with a taller bump outside the pad diameter to reduce sleep loss and small dimples in the faces for finger spins. Rewind links a promo video featuring Alexey Pavlov.

title: DRIVE
content: History / AboutDrive is a hybrid aluminum and polycarbonate yo-yo with a size C bearing (responsive or unresponsive) and slim 19mm OD pads, per the Vosun official site.

title: EMiSSARY
content: History / AboutEmissary combines a 6061 aluminum body with SUS304 stainless rings, using a size C KK Premium bearing and slim 19mm OD pads (Vosun official site).

title: Eragon2
content: History / AboutEragon2 is the second version of the Eragon bimetal series, using a wing-shape bearing seat, per the Vosun official site.

title: Eragon3
content: History / AboutEragon3 is the third version of the Eragon bimetal series, using three materials. The brand site says it is wider and sharper for fast competition tricks, designed by Team Vosun player KUN of Beijing, who has taught many young players. KUN is a Kamen Rider fan, which is why the series is named Eragon.

title: Geats
content: History / AboutGeats is a bimetal with a 6061 aluminum body and SUS304 rings (Vosun official site) and the base for the later Geats9, Geats CG and Unrival.

title: Geats CG
content: History / AboutGeats CG ("CG" stands for Creation God, per the brand) is a super-wide, big yo-yo based on the Geats9 with over-rim weight, aimed at speed combos and horizontal tricks. Body is aluminum 7075 with SUS304 rings.

title: Geats9
content: History / AboutThe brand site describes Geats9 as a monometal max-wide version based on the Geats, especially friendly to horizontal tricks.

title: Gravity Escape
content: History / AboutGravity Escape pairs an Al-7068 body with a plated steel ring (Vosun official site) and uses a round-grooved bearing.

title: HæLi
content: History / AboutHæLi is a titanium (TC4) yo-yo with a wing-shape bearing seat and M4x8mm axle. The Vosun official site tags it with TiGeekr and lists colors fading splash, Pink, raw and stone.

title: INSECTS AWAKEN
content: History / AboutInsects Awaken is the signature design of Team Vosun player ZIKUO, described by the brand as a top-10 player in the China 1A professional division with several regional titles. It is a 6061 aluminum and SUS304 bimetal.

title: KSTAR
content: History / AboutKSTAR uses a gold-plated brass ring on its body and a U-type bearing seat with an M4x8mm axle, per the Vosun official site.

title: Leopard Beyond
content: History / AboutLeopard Beyond is a bimetal continuation of the Leopard line (Vosun official site), with a C-grooved bearing and 10mm SUS304 axle.

title: O1-EZSPiN
content: History / AboutThe brand says EZSPiN revisits the earlier 7S Eztrik design by Eren, which got good market feedback; "EZ" means easy. The original prototype was based on two other successful designs, the V6 Petrichor and 8S Vanquish, with the front design updated from the Petrichor and weight shifted to the outer ring for longer spin time; the side shape updates the Vanquish with greater width in the A-zone.

title: O2 Aten
content: History / AboutAten (also Aton, Egyptian jtn) is the disk of the sun in ancient Egyptian mythology. The brand says the O2-Aten design uses broken lines and a larger catch zone. The first run included five splashed and three solid colors with a dual polishing ring. The brand tags it WYYC2018.

title: O3-Artura
content: History / AboutO3-Artura is a monometal design with a polishing ring, in Al 6061-T6 (Vosun official site). Later variants include Super Artura and Artura Arena.

title: Surges
content: History / AboutPer Yo-Yo Store Rewind, Surges is Vosun's first looping model and an OEM of the Blitzball 2.0, the yo-yo of 2A champion Yi Chenghao. Printing, accessories and the initial parts differ from the Blitzball 2.0, and parts and caps are shared between the two. The initial spacers are double-sided gold and no adjustment shims are included.The brand site calls it the first plastic looping yo-yo by Vosun, dated 2022.10.10, with a precision injection-molded polycarbonate body, an anodized aluminum spacer, stainless steel axle and ball bearing, and a Starburst response. The white-string version ships with a very thin Yi Chenghao string and oil is recommended for the axle and string.

title: TASTiC
content: History / AboutTASTiC is a titanium (TC4) yo-yo with a Center Trac bearing and 10mm SUS304 axle (Vosun official site).

title: TiCKET
content: History / AboutTiCKET is a titanium TC4 yo-yo with a size C KK bearing and slim 19mm OD pads (Vosun official site).

title: TiTOS
content: History / AboutThe brand site describes TiTOS as the latest small-quantity titanium release, made with TiGeekr, with hand-made splash colors it says are unique in the titanium yo-yo market.

title: Trinity
content: History / AboutYo-Yo Store Rewind calls the Trinity a rare plastic model from Vosun, reasonably priced and usable for learning binds or intermediate string tricks. Swapping to a size C- bearing and 8mm axle converts it to responsive. It has a large diameter within the full-size range and a wide trend shape, with a finger-spin spot (the crack in the center spot is a product feature). The brand site later issued a 2024 Trinity update and a Trinity Super.

title: U1 TiPS
content: History / AboutU1-TiPS is Vosun's full-titanium full-size model; Yo-Yo Store Rewind says the name stands for Titanium Premium YoyoS and that it sits at the high end of the Vosun line. Compared to the mid-size TiMe, it is full-size with a taller bump and a "high wall" rather than the low edge typical of full metals, which Rewind says leaves room for the string to contact and improves control.Bearing is a V-cave or Center Trac, and side-face hubs are either cone or round type, assigned at random (Rewind).

title: U2 Leopard
content: History / AboutThe U2 Leopard is the signature design of Vosun team member and Canadian champion Terrance Wang (Vosun official site). A later version, Leopard EX, was made lighter after Wang used the original in the WYYC 2018 semi-final.

title: U2 Leopard EX
content: History / AboutThe Leopard EX updates the Leopard, Terrance Wang's signature, after he suggested a slightly lighter version for high-speed play following WYYC 2018. Yo-Yo Store Rewind describes a full-size light-feeling bimetal with a thin, widened stainless-steel rim that increases effective width, and says it is the culmination of the Leopard line, following the original Leopard released a year earlier.

title: U3 Sparkle
content: History / AboutThe U3 Sparkle is a titanium (Gr5 / TC4) yo-yo with a V-shaped size C bearing seat and an 8mm SUS304 axle, per the Vosun official site.

title: U4 KiSA
content: History / AboutThe U4 KiSA is tagged as a bimetal on the Vosun official site, with a Center Trac bearing and 10mm SUS304 axle.

title: Uncia
content: History / AboutAccording to the brand site, Uncia is based on the first Leopard with updated details, designed for expert players who also like responsive tricks. A fixed bearing and axle design lets the user switch between unresponsive and responsive with an extra slim bearing and axle.

title: Unrival
content: History / AboutUnrival is a wide aluminum yo-yo in the Geats family per the Vosun official site, with a size C KK bearing and slim 19mm OD pads.

title: V1 TiMe
content: History / AboutThe V1 TiMe was the first Vosun yo-yo made with a titanium body. The brand site says the name combines "Ti" (titanium, the luxury body material) and "Me" (individual character, also read as "Mi", meaning fun and the craftsman spirit in Chinese).Yo-Yo Store Rewind describes it as a mid-size yo-yo with a slightly wider body than usual, giving a full-size mounting feel while staying agile, with a shape close to the Vanquish. A Premium Edition had the outer rim polished to a mirror finish. Some units shipped with a Center Trac bearing instead of the grooved bearing.

title: V2 Koreyoshi
content: History / AboutThe V2 Koreyoshi followed the TiMe as Vosun's second titanium yo-yo. The brand site says "Koreyoshi" comes from the Japanese "これよし" ("this is a good item") and that Vosun wanted it to be a top series. The polished ring was produced at a watch factory that makes luxury watches; the brand notes that titanium heats up easily during machining, and that most yo-yos on sale at the time were left raw.The brand site says a simple style collection watch was released alongside the V2.

title: V3 TipowerX
content: History / AboutThe V3 TipowerX is a bimetal from the V series with an AL7075 body and a titanium ring, using a V-shaped bearing seat and an 8mm SUS304 axle, according to the Vosun official site.

title: V4 Vortex
content: History / AboutThe V4 Vortex is a simple step-straight full-metal yo-yo. Yo-Yo Store Rewind positions it as a step-up model into full metal, with a slightly wide mid-size body. The rim area is left raw without anodizing, so it is not a bimetal.Specs from the Vosun official site.

title: V5 Space Cookie
content: History / AboutThe V5 Space Cookie is the signature design of Vosun team member and UK champion Jakub Wawrzyniak (known as Kombo), per the Vosun official site.

title: V6 Petrichor
content: History / AboutThe brand site describes the V6 series as a high-end simple design by Team Vosun, with an aluminum 7075 body for higher-grade performance. The page states "Design in: Turkey, Made in: China". Rewind notes the Petrichor served as one basis for the later EZSPiN.

title: V7 Duang
content: History / AboutThe V7 Duang is described by the brand as the first bimetal from Vosun, with a brass ring finished in 24K gold plating. Yo-Yo Store Rewind adds that brass has a higher density than stainless steel, giving an inner-ring bimetal mid-size yo-yo unusually strong spin power for its price.

title: V8 Offstring
content: History / AboutThe V8 Offstring is Vosun's first offstring yo-yo, machined from Delrin (POM). Yo-Yo Store Rewind notes its unusually low-edge shape with a deep recess, which reduces sleep loss and gives strong spin retention when the spin weakens. The gap is wide, so thicker string is recommended. Two package designs were shipped at random.The brand lists gap widths of 3.0mm and 2.4mm (the latter marked "NEW").

title: V8x Fighter
content: History / AboutThe V8x Fighter is the second Vosun offstring, released four years after the V8. The brand site says Vosun discussed the design with its team and with 4A players at WYYC, and chose a CNC-cut hexagonal Delrin axle seat paired with a metal screw so the sides stay tight when hit on the floor.Yo-Yo Store Rewind describes an H profile close to the V8 but wider, with a thick ring-weight-like rim on the side faces for mid-ship weight distribution, and notes the 92g weight gives a solid feel in offstring play.

title: V9 Galsang
content: History / AboutThe V9 Galsang is tagged as a bimetal by the Vosun official site, with a grooved bearing and 10mm SUS304 axle. The page gives specifications and colors only; ring material is not stated.

title: VTWO
content:
From One Drop:

"Hi there! Vilmos here. I couldn't be more happy and proud to introduce the VTWO. It took us two years and two summer trips to Eugene to see it to its completion.

The VTWO, continues the line of the Vilmos Zoltan Kiss signature series. As with the Valor, I was dedicated to be as personally involved in the design process as the first time.

The Valor was designed to excel in competition yo-yoing and it hit the mark based on the feedback we received. For the VTWO, I wanted to raise the bar even higher in terms of performance, quality and making sure that the design was distinct and iconic.

I love straight lines, flat surfaces and minimalistic design so the V-shape was a no brainer. Using the advantages of 7075 aluminum we were able to make the body ultra thin and maximize the rim weight for more power, more performance. The wide open catch zone is great for maximum control and easy maneuverability. The surface is bead blasted to elevate the design and performance.

To keep it simple and elegant I aimed for a flat hub and decided to go with two grooves in the catch zone to complete the design and give a nod to the Valor's "Triple Grooves" feature.

To further my personal journey in making the VTWO I wanted the art to stand out as much as the yo-yo. To achieve this we collaborated with Portland based comic book artist and writer Leila del Duca."

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Cromo
content: History / AboutThe Cromo is a chrome-colored version of the Vulto Saga, released alongside the standard model. The Yo-Yo Museum describes it as a 'chromed' edition of Vulto's popular high-performance yo-yo; because it is plastic, the finish is not true chrome. The Museum exhibit is a boxed example dated 2004 with an adjustable (spacer) gap and a weight of 60 g.

title: Glitch
content: History / AboutThe Glitch is an undersized, all-metal yo-yo from Vulto of Brazil. According to Yo-Yo Store Rewind, it was developed with input from Vulto owner Mario Troise, Edy Kauan, Iklodi Tamas, designer Caie Perez, and US players Doc Pop and Justin Weber. It uses a short axle with a light center and heavier rims, and ships with a bearing machined with a curved (concave) surface, packaged in a metal case bearing the Glitch and Vulto logos. Yo-Yo Store Rewind first stocked it in January 2013 as its first Vulto import.

title: Saga
content: History / AboutThe Saga is a ball-bearing plastic yo-yo made in Brazil by Vulto and designed by Brazilian yo-yo designer Mario Troise. According to the Yo-Yo Museum, the Saga line was the first professional yo-yo line to come exclusively from South America. It has a fixed gap, a starburst response system and a large C-size bearing. YoYo Wiki compares its shape to the Duncan Freehand 2, with steeper sides and more pointed rims, and places its weight between a Freehand 2 and a YoYoJam Patriot. The Yo-Yo Museum dates its exhibit examples to 2002 (bubble-carded) and summer 2005 (marbled colors); the line was produced in many colors and with many different logo sides. A special marbled edition for Dave's Skilltoys, limited to 36 pieces with a logo by artist Oke Rosgana, is also documented by the Museum.

title: Vulture
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"Vulture is yoyofriends' newest inner ring bimetal. Vulture features a classic composition of 7068 and stainless steel in a V/H shape that focuses on power, stability and flow. The stainless steel ring weight of Vulture is around 16g, a 50%+ increase from our previous inner ring release. Vulture pushes the limit of performance and weight distribution for an inner ring bimetal. The name is inspired by the striking look of the bird and the classic spiderman villain, which signifies power, strength. maneuverability and precision!

We apologize for the delayed release of the koi and vulture. When we released the exclusive green+black acidwash vulture on 5/10, we found out a couple are not dead smooth and fell short of the high yoyofriends standards. We immediately checked the entire stock from the yoyofriends store and asked yoyoexpert, yoyosam to test their stock ( Huge thanks to yoyoexpert and yoyosam ). They said vast majority, almost all of them are dead smooth and only very few have slight finger nail vibe that is barely noticeable. We were glad this run is OK, however we strive for being the best of the best in terms of quality. After internal discussion, we decided to have a 15% discount across all vulture worldwide this run. We thank you for the support on this run of koi and vulture. We will be better in the future. Once again thanks you all for the support."

title: Walter
content:
Walter began around 2010 with multiple prototypes designed. The final Walter was released in May 2013, they were $120. Using the Wayback Machine, it appears there were 7 Walter designs prior to the final Walter.

Chris from CLYW helped with the CAD work, finance and orchestration of the project. One drop did the machining. Sonny from Anti-yo had them blasted and hard coated.

There were100 Walters sold, numbered 00-99 in a black Type III Hardcoat, and a handful of Walters in Blue, Red, Gray and several half swap combinations.

Walter Prototype #?

Blue/Black & Grey/Black half swaps
