title: Warthog
content:
History / About
The Warthog was released in 2017, continuing the animal-naming theme G2 adopted alongside their creature names. The Throwers Swirl colorway appears on the secondary market. Full specifications were not available in accessible sources at time of research — additional documentation may be available at gsquaredyoyos.com or the G2 archive.

title: Wasabi
content:
History / About
Wasabi is part of the signature project. Designed to fit crackout’s style. Now sporting our new unblasted guts for maximum smoothness and less strink breaking.

Production Runs

Proto #1 (June 2008) — 20 units, Green. Finish: CandyBlast.
Proto #1 Engraved (July 2008) — 2 units, Green engraved. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #1 (August 2008) — 110 units, Green; D48.95mm / W38.40mm / 62.00g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Pre-Production #1 (March 2009) — 30 units, Clear; D50.30mm / W40.00mm / 63.60g. Finish: CandyBlast.
Run #2 (July 2009) — 120 units, Green; D50.50mm / W40.00mm / 66.60g. Finish: CandyBlast.

title: C130
content: C130 is a dual-use metal yo-yo built with a concave finger-spin cup for finger spins, weighing 65.3g at 57mm diameter.

title: Count
content: Count is a bi-metal yo-yo with a 6061 aluminum body and stainless steel rings, marketed as an unresponsive model for advanced string-trick players. Ships with case, glove, and extra strings.

title: M18
content: M18 is a dual-mode (responsive/unresponsive) metal yo-yo with a butterfly-shaped profile, sold with a full accessory kit of strings, bearing, and case.

title: R8
content: R8 is a dual-mode (responsive/unresponsive) metal yo-yo marketed for beginners, children, and advanced trick performance.

title: TC4 Aviation Titanium
content: TC4 Aviation Titanium is Watieoboo's flagship model, machined from aircraft-grade TC4 titanium alloy for a non-responsive, competition-grade throw. Priced well above the brand's usual budget aluminum lineup.

title: W07
content: W07 is a dual-mode metal yo-yo marketed for beginners through advanced players, switchable between responsive and unresponsive play.

title: W09
content: W09 is a dual-mode metal yo-yo forged from 6061 aerospace-grade aluminum, switchable between a responsive bearing for beginners and a non-responsive bearing for advanced players.

title: W21
content: W21 is a forged aluminum alloy yo-yo with a responsive mode for beginners and a non-responsive mode for freestyle and competition play, plus a center finger-spin groove.

title: Weasel
content:
From Pop!

"From the depths of my mind and through the help of Mark of Mk1 fame comes the Weasel! A refined balance of fun and competitive mindsets, I am proud to have this as my first foray into the scene of yoyo design! Despite its high mass, the Weasel is extremely easy to maneuver without sacrificing power."

title: Weekend
content:
History / About
The Weekend launched alongside the Joyride and First Base at the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest, making Recess an immediately credible brand across all price tiers. The Weekend uses a 7075 aluminum body with outer stainless steel rims — both materials chosen for strength and durability. Contrary to what the materials might suggest, the Weekend has a surprisingly soft play feel. The stainless rims provide serious rim weighting and improved spin, but the 7075 body keeps overall weight measured and the spin smooth. In Colin Beckford's 2015 Buyer's Guide, the Weekend rated 9.5/10 — best overall quality and speed. The Vacation (2016) served as its spiritual sibling, offering a harder, more crisp feel as a direct counterpoint.

The 86400 (read "Eighty-Six Thousand Four Hundred," for the number of seconds in a day) completed Werrd's Time Series alongside Hour and Minute. Its aggressive step-cut profile, bead-blasted 6061-T6 aluminum, and wider stance than the Hour generated excellent spin time at a competition-appropriate price point. A HACHIROKU limited version was restocked in June 2014. Ships with Blueprint Poly Type 6 string.

title: Beef
content: The Beef was Werrd's first bimetal design, pairing a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel outer rim rings. The steel rings deliver significantly more spin power than full-aluminum throws of comparable size. The flat rim profile kept the weight evenly distributed at the outer edges. An updated 2011 version trimmed approximately one gram while retaining the same construction. Hub posts allow optional hubstack attachment. $103–$109.99 USD.

title: Hour
content: The Hour was part of Werrd's Time Series (alongside Minute and 86400) and was their first 7075 aluminum throw at an accessible $69.99 price point. The tall, narrow step-straight profile centered weight for strong, stable spin. Artwork was inspired by London's Big Ben clock tower. Colorways: Black/Silver, Aqua/Silver, Purple/Silver, Green/Silver, Red/Silver. The 2K13 revision followed in 2013 with subtle width, response, and axle improvements.

title: Irony
content: The Irony was designed by Andrew Bergen and became Werrd's flagship competition model. Its H-shape with flared, angled rims was originally an aesthetic choice, but the design proved to dramatically improve horizontal and off-axis trick performance — a discovery that influenced competition yo-yo design broadly. The GBA ("Guilty By Association") revision added weight to the rims, softened the catch zone edges, and introduced a hardcoat finish. Colorways include Black/Gold splash, Silver, Blue/Silver splash, Gold, Black/Pink splash, Green, and Red/Yellow splash. $109.99 USD.

title: Minute
content: The original Minute was Werrd's first undersized offering — a compact 49mm throw with the unusual choice of an A-size (Duncan) bearing, giving it a tighter response and narrower gap than contemporaries. Its sharp, angular step-straight halves created a distinctive silhouette. This version predated the 2013 C-bearing Minute redesign. Original retail price $70 USD.

title: Minute (2013)
content: The 2013 Minute was a comprehensive redesign of the original A-bearing Minute, switching to a Size C bearing and significantly widening the profile to 42.7mm for rim-focused weight distribution unusual in undersized throws. Released at a WYYC 2013 midnight drop at $40 USD, it retailed at $49.99 afterward. The soda-blast finish aided grinding. Part of Werrd's Time Series alongside Hour and 86400. Colorways: Deep Red, Aqua, Champagne Gold, Light Green.

title: Pacquiao
content: Named after boxer Manny Pacquiao — a champion in the lightest weight classes — the Pacquiao was Werrd's answer to hand fatigue and impact. At 49.4g for a full aluminum throw, it reduces the physical toll of extended practice sessions. The round body carries Pacman-themed styling. Colorways include Blue, Green, and Green/Gold. $88.99 USD.

title: Poo
content: The Poo is Keith "Skip" Mitton's signature model. Despite its 56mm diameter, the slim 36.59mm width and 62.2g weight produce an exceptionally nimble, fast throw. The thin H-shape with rounder rims than contemporaries gave rise to the model name. Light and quick, it suited Mitton's dynamic play style. Colorways include Blue, Green/Yellow splash, and Purple/Silver splash. $88.99 USD.

title: Sentinel
content: The Sentinel is Mark Allen's signature model and was Werrd's largest yo-yo at the time of release. Machined from 7075 aluminum, the 61.79mm × 45.48mm H-profile provides a generous catch zone and a powerful, stable spin. The rounded outer rims reduce impact on the fingers during catches. The original version featured a spiked hub. Available in Raw, Red, Blue, Green, Black, Nickel, and Gold anodized finishes. $119.99 USD.

title: XXXXL
content: The XXXXL (Quadruple Extra Large) was Werrd's second release. The name derives from its four-bearing configuration: two Beefcaked Size C bearings in the center plus two YYF-licensed Jimmy Hat hubstack bearings. Available in both a smooth standard edition and a blasted Groovy edition for grinding. A Green Tea Edition colorway was also produced. $119.99 USD retail.

title: Werther’s Yo-Riginal
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yoyo? Grab the files here: Werther's Yo-Riginal Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"I thought to myself that a Werther's Original candy would make for some good yo-yo pull starts if it wasn't so tiny. 

This uses a 5mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/42dpFui. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole, then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. If you want it to work well slice it to 54-60 grams weight. 

If your yo-yo doesn't come back up when you tug please add a drop of lubricant to the end of the string and massage it in, or rub the string with some chapstick. "

title: Wheels
content: AboutThe Wheels yo-yo is a classic Butterfly-shaped beginner throw with automotive-themed sidecap graphics. Its 2016 redesign replaced the older fixed axle with a plastic transaxle sleeve — the same diameter as a standard C-bearing — and added a take-apart design with bearing seats that let players swap in a standard ball bearing for significantly longer spin times. This modular approach makes the Wheels an unusually versatile entry-level yo-yo, capable of transitioning from a simple responsive looper to a string-trick platform with a single bearing upgrade.

title: Free Wheeling Tournament
content: History / AboutWhirl-E-Gig was a small 1950s yo-yo brand; the term "Whirl-E-Gig" was used in place of "yo-yo" in the years when Duncan owned the trademark on the word. The Free Wheeling Tournament is the only model the YoYo Wiki lists for the company. The Yo-Yo Museum describes it as a plastic yo-yo with no inner plastic shell and a ribbed inner surface, with a wooden axle and fixed string, noting it could easily be converted to a slip string. The seal reads "Free Wheeling Plastic Whirl-E-Gig Tournament, Made in U.S.A., Pat. Pend." The museum dates its example to 1955 and gives an estimated value of $110; the wiki records a highest auction price of $158.

title: Whole Milk
content: About the Whole MilkReleased April 7, 2017, the Whole Milk was Crucial's first metal yo-yo in over four years, building on the Fresh Milk's design language and translating it into aluminum. Made in the USA by Paul Yath, it features a comfortable rounded wing-shape profile, a unique stepped cup design, and heavy rim weighting for stability and spin time. YoYoExpert described it as playing "fast and maneuverable." A second "Ghost Engraving" run — the Rainbow Sorbet colorway with minimal engraving — was released in October 2017; the reduced engraving was designed to lower friction during fingerspin tricks.

title: Wide Load
content:
History
The Wide Load was a 55-unit numbered collector model released in late 2002 or early 2003. It represented Frank Difeo's most elaborately accessorized yo-yo to date: every unit shipped with three sets of rubber weight rings (two black sets in thick and thin gauges, one red/black set), five sets of interchangeable pogs (yellow, orange, and fluorescent laminated paper; clear lexan; black anodized aluminum with laser engraving), a branded display stand, and a combination tool.
At full weight with all pogs and rings installed, the Wide Load reached approximately 72g — the heaviest standard Dif-e-Yo configuration. The design later served as the foundation for the Rev-1 Over Haul (2010).

title: Wide Sport
content:
History
The Wide Sport combined the wide string gap architecture of the Wide Load collector model with the slimline silhouette of the Sportster. The result was the widest player-grade model in the Dif-e-Yo lineup at the time of its release. Weight was fully adjustable through the included O-ring system, reaching up to 73.5g at maximum configuration — one of the heaviest standard Dif-e-Yo configurations available to players.

title: Wild Child x AntiYo Plush Doll
Wild-Trio
content: The Wild-Trio is W1LD's first tri-material yo-yo, featuring a polycarbonate center double-rim that runs through the entire body with a stainless steel outer rim placed much wider than on the w!ld. Displayed by Yang Chen during the 2023 World Yo-Yo Championships Final, the Wild-Trio introduced the PC plus stainless steel structure that would be refined in later models such as the Adrenaline.

title: Wilder
content: The Wilder is W1LD's 2024 flagship competition bi-metal, building on the Wilderness 7075 platform with stainless steel rims for refined weight distribution and enhanced spin power. A strong performer for horizontal tricks, the Wilder strikes a balance between control and speed at the highest competitive level.

title: Wilderness 59.9
content: The Wilderness 59.9 pushes the Wilderness family to its extreme with an ultra-wide 7075 monometal featuring a near-square aspect ratio — 59.9mm diameter and 59.9mm width. The latest and most oversized addition to the Wilderness line, designed for players who want maximum catch zone and spin power.

title: Wilderness 7075
content: The Wilderness 7075 is W1LD's first monometal and one of the widest competition throws in the market at over 52mm wide. Machined from 7075 aluminum, its thick construction delivers power, stability, and an enormous catch zone. All three W1LD team members competed with the Wilderness 7075 at the 2023 World Yo-Yo Championships.

title: Wilderness PC
content: The Wilderness PC is a full polycarbonate version of the Wilderness shape with a 6061 aluminum hub, making it W1LD's most affordable and beginner-accessible model. Wide and forgiving with the same oversized proportions as the flagship Wilderness, the PC variant delivers a casual play experience at the lowest price in the lineup.

title: Wilderness PR
content: The Wilderness PR is a hybrid model built on the Wilderness platform with a 6061 aluminum body and large polycarbonate rims. Positioned between plastic and full-metal construction, it captures strings easily and delivers more performance than a pure plastic at a more casual, approachable character than a full metal. A bridge model for players stepping up from plastic.

title: WildificaTion
content:
History / About
Premium limited-quantity release combining a 7075 aluminum body with ultra-wide titanium rims for unresponsive, luxury-tier play. Positioned by a third-party retailer as the newest entry in W1LD's annual flagship line (Wilderness 7075 2023 -> Wilder 2024 -> Wildify 2025 -> WildificaTion) — this succession claim is not brand-confirmed.

title: Wildify
content: The Wildify is W1LD founder Yang Chen's 2025 flagship model, built on the Wilderness 7075 platform with large stainless steel rims added for bimetal weight distribution. Combining the overwhelming 52mm width of the Wilderness with the spin power of a bi-metal, the Wildify excels at fast combination play and horizontal techniques.

title: Wildless
content: The Wildless is W1LD's entry-level monometal, delivering a crisp and powerful feel at an accessible price. Some colorways feature polished rims that mimic the visual aesthetic of a bi-metal design. Available in a wide range of seasonal colorways, the Wildless opened W1LD's lineup to a broader audience without sacrificing the brand's competition-oriented character.

title: Wildless2
content: The Wildless2 is the second generation of W1LD's budget-friendly monometal, refining the original's proportions with a slightly smaller diameter and a silhouette that draws closer to the flagship Wilderness. High performance at an accessible price, with splash colorways available at a slight premium.

title: Crop Circle
content:
History / About
The Crop Circle is a fixed-axle wooden yo-yo from Wildwood Yoyos, designed specifically for 0a-style play. Its profile combines a butterfly shape with a pull-start dimple integrated into the face of each half, making it easy to start and return. Like all Wildwood throws, it is handturned by Eric Newlin from hardwood stock and fitted with a 5/16" non-separating hickory wood axle and an 8-hole friction response system.

title: Crop Circle Jr.
content:
History / About
The Crop Circle Jr. is a reduced-scale fixed-axle version of Wildwood Yoyos' Crop Circle, handturned by Eric Newlin. Community members who own multiple Crop Circles describe the Jr. as the smoothest-playing variant in the lineup — snappy off the hand and floaty through tricks. Like all Wildwood fixed-axle designs, it features a hickory wood axle in a non-separating body and an 8-hole friction response system.

title: Druid
content:
History / About
The Druid is Wildwood Yoyos' take on modern responsive play — a handturned wood yo-yo fitted with an MR85 bearing, MK1 × Spinworthy RBC response pads, and a pull-start dimple system. Made by Eric Newlin in small batches, each Druid ships with a custom spacer kit, a sanded natural finish, and Zipline Strings CS118 poly/nylon blend. The Druid sits at the intersection of fixed-axle feel and modern responsive performance.

title: Gnomad
content:
History / About
The Gnomad is one of Wildwood Yoyos' flagship fixed-axle designs. Handturned by Eric Newlin, it features a tapered butterfly profile, unique gnome engravings laser-etched on each side, and a 5/16" hickory wood axle that is a single non-screw-apart unit. Response is handled by an 8-hole friction system worked directly into the wood. Weighing in around 45–48g and measuring approximately 60×32mm, the Gnomad is sized for comfortable all-day 0a street and trick play.

title: Windoundary
content: History / AboutJacob Cheng Hongye signature designed for controlled outdoor 5A and 1A play; name combines wind and boundary.

title: Windrunner
content: AboutThe Windrunner was designed as Duncan's accessible full-metal entry point for players interested in unresponsive yo-yos for the first time. Its distinctive double-rim design — a secondary outer rim machined into the catch zone — pushes weight toward the edges for enhanced stability and spin time. Priced between the Metal Drifter and the competition-grade De-Luxxe line, the Windrunner fills a market gap for players who want metal performance without paying competition prices.

title: Windrunner 7068
content: AboutThe Windrunner 7068 is a fan-driven upgrade to the original Windrunner, made after Duncan spent nearly two years collecting community suggestions. The result maintained the original's geometry almost exactly but switched the aluminum alloy from 6061 to the harder, more durable 7068 grade and extended the axle length to reduce the risk of stripping — a common complaint on the original model. The double-rim design and all performance specs remain identical; the upgrade is entirely about long-term durability for players who throw heavily.

title: Winglet
content:
From ZGRT:

"This project came to life in early 2020 after being inspired from the aerodynamics of planes' and birds’ wings. Winglets are made to reduce the air flow and maintain the maximum lift of an object in motion.

The result was an extreme H-shaped profile throw with a smooth finish that is easy to catch and that performs extraordinary finger grinds. Your hand will also notice the ergonomic design of this return top.

We wanted this throw to play lightly and bring kinetics into the mix for a long spin time.

The Winglet will help you in learning new tricks and in improving your technical skills due to its stability and fun design. It also has the capability to easily perform thumb grinds and once you lock into its finger spin hub, you will absolutely love it!"

title: Winglet SE
content:
From ZGRT:

"We wanted to make The Winglet more robust by utilizing 7068 aluminum as its construction material. This particular alloy, known for its exceptional strength and durability, is approximately two times harder than traditional aluminum alloys commonly used in aerospace applications. The increased hardness of 7068 aluminum not only contributes to a higher resistance to deformation and wear but also allows for the design of more intricate and lightweight structures without compromising integrity.

In addition to its impressive hardness, 7068 aluminum boasts a greater density compared to standard aluminum alloys. This increased density results in a more robust and resilient Winglet."

title: Wingweaver
content:
Overview
The Wingweaver is Damian Puckett's debut bimetal, released October 14, 2022 alongside the Fusion collaboration with Dressel Designs. Puckett's fascination with W/wing-shaped yo-yos drove the concept: maximize width without sacrificing stability or spin time.
Available with two ring options — stainless steel for a lighter feel and brass for more pronounced rim weight — the Wingweaver offered buyers a rare choice of weight distribution at the time of purchase. Both versions shared the same aluminum 7068 body geometry; only the ring material differed.

title: Winning Bird
content: History / AboutOne of C3's early unreleased-blueprint concepts later brought to retail; its proportions informed Master Galaxy.

title: Wisteria
content:
Overview
The Wisteria is Damian Puckett's signature shape — previously released as a bimetal, titanium, and TISS — brought to a broader audience in July 2024 as a 7068 aluminum mono-metal. At 58mm diameter it skews large by contemporary standards, reflecting Puckett's established preference for full-size throws.
The mono-metal version uses 7068 aluminum (the same alloy as the Wingweaver's body) to deliver competitive performance without the bimetal price. Launched in four colorways: Red/Yellow Acid Wash, Blue/Green Fade, Blue/Pink Acid Wash, and Purple/Orange Fade.

title: Wisteria (Bimetal)
content:
Overview
The Wisteria Bimetal is the original release of Damian Puckett's signature shape, predating the titanium, TISS, and mono-metal versions. The Wisteria became Puckett's most recognized design and spawned multiple material variants. Full specifications for the bimetal version have not been published.

title: Wisteria (Titanium)
content:
Overview
The Wisteria Titanium is a limited-run titanium version of Damian Puckett's signature shape, produced circa 2023. Full specifications have not been published.

title: Wisteria (TISS)
content:
Overview
The Wisteria TISS (Titanium Inner Shell with Stainless Steel rings) is a premium variant of Damian Puckett's signature shape, produced circa 2023. Full specifications have not been published.

title: w!ld
content: The w!ld is the flagship signature model of W1LD founder Yang Chen, a three-time China National Champion. Debuting at the 2023 World Yo-Yo Championships, where all three W1LD team members competed in the 1A division, the w!ld features exceptionally wide stainless steel rims on a 6061 body designed to balance wildness and elegance. Released in seasonal limited colorways inspired by the four seasons.

title: Wolf
content:
History / About
The Wolf is the signature model of Daniel Ickler (Zammy), a specialist in Moebius-style yo-yoing. Jacob Gross reached out to Zammy in late 2015 to develop a collaborative signature; the project was confirmed via a teaser post simply reading "G2 x Z, get ready..." Sammy requested a baby of the One Drop Code 1 and Code 2 with a double rim. Jacob had a 3D model drafted in under two weeks. The Wolf is a full-sized H-shape with a double rim feature — designed to be "solid as a rock equally to being floaty as a feather." It was meant to sit between "casual" and "competition," serving either role. Multiple runs were produced between November 2016 and January 2020 when it was retired. The DireWolf (oversized variant) and AL7 Wolf (7075, 3 limited runs) were notable special editions.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (BOSS or BOSS Rage, swappable)

title: Amarok
content:
About the Amarok
The Amarok is the debut yo-yo from Wolf Yoyo Works, released in mid-2019. It holds the distinction of being the first yo-yo ever to use PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene, or Teflon) fingerspin cups. By bonding Teflon bowls to an anodized aluminium body, founder Jack Eastwood achieved a design that combined the stability and spin time of a metal yo-yo with the dramatically reduced fingertip friction that PTFE provides — enabling longer, more controlled fingerspin tricks.
The shape was refined through a series of 3D-printed prototypes before moving to production, a process Eastwood estimated reduced development costs by roughly 9,900% compared to commissioning manufacturer prototypes. Manufacturing tolerances were held to 0.0002" to ensure vibration-free play at high RPM.
The Amarok shipped in six color combinations: three anodized aluminum colorways (body) paired with either black or white PTFE cups. This pairing approach doubled the perceived variety without adding significant per-unit production cost.

title: Wolty
content: AboutThe Wolty is JT's beginner-oriented offstring, released in 2015. Built on Kamui design adjustments and shaped as an H-profile, it was engineered for improved balance and catch-zone comfort at an accessible price point. In May 2016, a POM version was released with a distinctive texture engineered to improve winding and sliding performance.

title: Wooden Bullet
content:
Interested in 3D-printing this yo-yo? Grab the files here: Wooden Bullet Yo-Yo

From Sickburn Yo-Yo Workshop:

"This is a reimagining of the classic Silver Bullet yoyo as a fixed axle. Show here 3d printed in Prusament Linden Tree wood filament. 

It uses a 4mm x 20mm stainless steel shelf pin as the axle. These are the ones I used. https://amzn.to/4jaDzUQ. I recommend a tiny drop of super glue in the axle hole then the pin, then the other half with glue as well. Print this one at 100% infill. 

The six shooter holes act as the response to make this one go back up."

title: Wooden Crossed Flags Tournament
content: AboutThe Wooden Crossed Flags Tournament is the last wooden yo-yo in Duncan's production history, originally manufactured from 1960 to 1965 in such quantities that new-old-stock was still being sold into the early 1970s. Its design traces directly to Duncan's pre-plastic tournament models of the 1930s–1950s, and the crossed flags graphic on the face was a symbol of the national competition circuit Duncan ran through the mid-20th century. The current reproduction is packaged in a clear display box with a facsimile of the original 1955 Duncan Trick Book, making it both a functional yo-yo and a collectible piece of American toy history.

title: Wooden Monarch
content:
About
The Wooden Monarch is a hand-turned fixed-axle yo-yo crafted by Tom Holmes in Santa Barbara, California. Holmes began making yo-yos in 1988 and started selling them publicly in 1990 at Santa Barbara art shows and selected galleries. Each yo-yo was produced individually on a lathe from boards milled to 5/8" thickness, with a beeswax finish applied to the final piece.
Holmes selected dense tropical and domestic hardwoods known for their stability and visual character: African ebony, cocobolo rosewood (including two-tone ebony and cocobolo striped variants), purpleheart, Brazilian tulipwood, teak, cherry, African wenge, and white oak. Many editions featured vintage coins inlaid flush into the yo-yo faces — Indian head pennies in the cocobolo rosewood variant and mercury dimes in the purpleheart and white oak variants — making each piece a functional collector's item.
Wooden Monarch yo-yos carry a fixed wooden axle with no bearing, relying on friction and the player's string tension for response — the classic fixed-axle mechanism that predates modern bearing yo-yos. Their dense hardwood construction made them notably heavier than typical plastic yo-yos of the era.
World yo-yo champion Bunny Martin used Wooden Monarch yo-yos in his one-handed string-trick performances. Holmes sold exclusively through Santa Barbara art shows and galleries — never through retail chains or online stores — keeping production volumes low throughout the brand's active years.

title: Wooly MarkMont
content:
From One Drop:

"The Wooly Markmont is the first collaboration between CLYW and One Drop. This return top was inspired by the art work of Frank Bradley, where he submitted an illustration of One Drop team member Mark Montgomery as a Wooly Marmot.

After seeing this image it just made sense to us to combine the Markmont Next axle system with the Wooly Marmot ... and Nickel plate it! The return top also has an improved Wooly Marmot design with slightly angled gap walls for less string friction and a bit more rim weight.

This collaboration is a true union of both company's strengths and will hopefully bring together future projects between One Drop and CLYW."

title: Workhorse
content:
https://youtu.be/-jY86_k9S04?si=1fN6rh_27woeQXZv

The Workhorse is a collaboration between G Squared Yoyos and the Yoyo Boomers Club. Here's a bit of info from Cody, head of the YYBC:

The original design team = MattC, Yodaddyo, Pun1sh3R, and Mr. Jake.

Truth be told, we didn't have a lot of input to the design. Most of the conversation was about deciding which way we should lean on the design. G2 Respawn already leaned toward Responsive 1A. So the initial thought was making a 0A yoyo.

There was a concern about making a yoyo that was good at most things but not designed to be the best at one thing. So being good at both 1A responsive and 0A became its design goal. Counterintuitive to the way things have previously been done.

The other issue at the time: What does Modern Responsive Mean? There were a lot of theories and opinions. So, another goal of this design is to set an Example and Definition. A purposefully designed Ball ball-bearing yoyo that plays two different styles well. One yoyo that can seamlessly work in both areas.

Another part of the design was geared around the “Tinkerer”. Tunability was important. We gave a nod to old school with the ability to add weight rings. You can increase the spinning mass of the throw by adding 1 to 10 grams worth of weights with rings.

Response was also considered. Standard 5mm Bearing, 4mm Bearing, and finally the ability to run it as a “Post Modern Responsive” with a bearing blank.

Billpo provided the original Art Concepts. JSERR did a lot of the final tweaking of the digital designs.

This project was heavily supported and inspired by many members of the club. Ideas were thrown out, discussed, and implemented. A Club Community Project.

v.1 Stats;54 Grams55mm Diameter32mm WideD BearingG2 Respawn Pads

v.2/Production Stats ;53 Grams55mm Diameter32mm WideD BearingG2 Respawn Pads.

The biggest change between v.1 and v.2 was the Redistribution of weight. The size remained the same, but even taking some material out, where the material was shifted made a big impact."

What Comes in the Box

Workhorse Strings

Each Workhorse came with a Throw-Yo Threads Elixir string made to match its colorway. The following lists each Workhorse and its string:

Throw-Yo Threads founder, Rob, had this to say about the color choices:

Monobath Chroma

"The first-ever Throw-Yo string was a Monobath Potion, a white and black 100% spun poly string. Monobath Chroma pays homage to that string, but as a 100% trilobal poly Elixir made of black and silver threads. Perfect for the Founders Edition Workhorse."

Amalthea

"Amalthea Elixirs, named after The Last Unicorn, will come with the Unicorn Workhorse. It’s a tricolor string with purple, pink, and black, with the purple coming through a bit heavier than the other two threads."

Woody Wagon Stain

"How could we have a Workhorse without a Woody Wagon Stain string? The Workhorse V1 had 100% spun poly Woody Wagon Stain. The V2 has a spun/trilobal blend. The G2 Off-Road colorway will come with a 100% trilobal Woody Wagon Stain string."

Booster

"Made for the G2 Gotham colorway, Booster Elixirs are blue and yellow, just like an annoying hero who shows up in Gotham from time to time. Skeets not included."

Visco

"Visco Elixirs are a mix of green and steel, emulating a firework fuse. Very fitting for the Cherry Bomb colorway Workhorse. The closeup doesn’t do it justice. It looks like a fuse when you string up a yo-yo! It also kinda fits since this is a Yoyo BOOMERS Club throw."

title: World Class
content: AboutThe World Class was released at the 2023 World Yo-Yo Contest as a distinctive slim mono-metal with a Size A bearing — a profile that bridges the gap between traditional looping yo-yos and modern unresponsive string play. Its hollow flat cap design and H-profile deliver a unique play feel: the narrow width forces precision on string placement while the metal body provides the spin time needed for longer sequences. Its Worlds-launch context positions it as a collector piece for 2023 competition attendees.

title: Wraith
content:
History / About
The Wraith is a 2024 bimetal using a 6061 aluminum body with stainless steel rims — a straightforward but well-executed competition configuration. It also received an AL7 Wraith upgrade using a 7068 aluminum body (lighter, stronger) with SS rims for a more modern performance profile. The Wraith has become one of G2's most consistently released models alongside the Loadout, receiving frequent new colorways across 2024–2026.

title: Wyvern
content:
From One Drop:

"The Wyvern is the signature yo-yo for long time team member and employee Andrew Daugherty. Because of the unique situation of Andrew being our only employee and a team member, his role in his signature yo-yo was much more involved than normal.  He designed it, machined it, assembled it and did the box art.  His many years of experience in the factory gives him a unique perspective and the result reflects this.  For example, the Wyvern has the classic One Drop flat rims.  

In his own words:

'The Wyvern as a whole is an amalgamation of yo-yos, games, and art that I hold near and dear to me. This yoyo takes inspiration from some of my all time favorite onedrops: the OG Project, the Summit, and the Sugar Glider. This combination has given it great hand-feel, floaty play, and also great spin times. The box art features one of my original characters, in the style of Yoshitaka Amano as an homage to one of my favorite game series, who’s been bestowed the fiery powers of the wyvern and brandishing it for all to see.'"

meta.yya_bearing_size: Large (C) stainless steel (One Drop 10 Ball Bearing)

title: Wyvern – Boosted
content:
From One Drop:

"Team member Andrew Daugherty was also a long time employee (the longest) at One Drop. If you bought a yo-yo from us in the last 12 years, it’s likely Andrew helped make it. If you came to our shop to take a tour you probably met him. His impact here and to the yo-yo community is substantial. We miss having him here on the daily, but we are blessed to be friends and to have him on our team. 

The Wyvern is his signature yo-yo and it was made from 6061 alloy aluminum. Whenever a yo-yo is made from 6061 alloy that gives us the possible opportunity to make a Boosted version.

“Boosting” is making a 6061 alloy yo-yo out of 7075 alloy, but changing the design so that the overall weight ends up being lower even though 7075 is a heavier alloy than 6061. It takes a lot of tweaking to the design to make this happen, but we like to do it in a way that yo-yo looks the same and has the same or similar specs (except for the weight).

The boosted Wyvern was the last yo-yo that Andrew helped build, leaving us all with this final gift including the box art of the original and now the Boosted version. It sits at 63.5 grams overall weight (2 grams lighter than the Wyvern) and you can definitely feel that in play - it’s faster and has MORE spin inertia than the original. It has a small but distinctive change to the look of the hub so you can easily tell if it’s a Boosted version. The rest of the changes you can’t see are on the inside: weight shifted out towards the rim with a thinner wall (7075 is stronger and allows for a thinner wall). It’s always interesting to throw two yo-yos that feel the same in the hand, but feel vastly different in play."

title: X-Con Professional
content: About the X-Con ProfessionalThe X-Con Professional refines the X-ConVict formula with brass weight rims and the Solid Spin Axle system, delivering improved spin stability in DelValle's signature undersized format. It includes a Speed Bearing for players advancing to bind-response play. The compact 50.8mm diameter reflects DelValle's preference for precise, controlled string work.

title: X-ConVict
content: About the X-ConVictThe X-ConVict evolved DelValle's signature yo-yo line with a slightly refined rim geometry and dual O-ring response system. It maintained the undersized profile that DelValle favored for grinding tricks while updating the construction for YoYoJam's mid-2000s lineup. The model bridges the Hitman and the later Hitman Professional in the DelValle signature series.

title: Ixion’s Wheel
content: History / AboutIxion's Wheel is listed with the Xcalibur as the yo-yos produced by X-Yo. No specifications, year or description could be verified from available sources.

title: Xcalibur
content: History / AboutThe Xcalibur was the first yo-yo produced by X-Yo, a Korean manufacturer specializing in high-end metal yo-yos. It has a smooth anodized aluminum body.

title: X01 Titanium
content:
About
X01 is an advanced full-size bi-metal competition yoyo with a titanium body and stainless steel rim, sold at MagicYoYo's premium tier.

title: X03 Titanium
content:
About
X03 is an ultra-wide, full-titanium mono-metal competition yoyo with a 0.7mm inner wall thickness, sold at MagicYoYo's premium tier.

title: Xbone Chip
content:
History
The Xbone Chip was the mid-generation model in Dif-e-Yo's compact Bone Chip lineage, produced around 2009–2010. At 52.5mm diameter and 34.7mm width, it was undersized relative to the standard Dif-e-Yo format but capable of full unresponsive 1A string play. Smooth dry-finish surface. It bridged the original Bone Chip (a rare 2005 collector piece) and the XS Bone Chip (2011) — a continuous evolution in undersized Dif-e-Yo performance design. Priced at $89.99.

title: Aware
content: AboutThe Aware is XCube's competition-oriented H-profile with a completely concaved curved face, creating a striking aesthetic distinct from flat-faced H-profiles. Designed for speedy play, it maintains a satisfying weight feel despite its lighter construction. The deep response groove is designed for flowable silicone, which XCube strongly recommends over the stock pads to avoid snag issues common to the H-shape gap. Available in splash and gradient colorways including a team edition with a four-color fade. Team member support colorways feature silver base with pink and orange gradients.

meta.yya_response: XCube silicone pads (flowable silicone strongly recommended)

title: La Goutte
content: AboutLa Goutte ("The Drop") is XCube's competition-oriented release, designed by Alexandre Valin for technical players. Its sides feature machined ripple waves resembling pond ripples, paired with a frog logo and Graou string included in the packaging. Praised for achieving the feel of a heavier yo-yo at under 64 grams. Limited to 200 units total, each individually numbered. Available in both blasted (grind-friendly) and polished finishes across light blue, pink, purple, and gold colorways. Promoted by Russian player Maxim Lopin.

title: Stampede
content: AboutThe Stampede is XCube's second model, wider than the Steamroller with a rounded ultra-wide catch zone resembling a dumbbell in cross-section. Its silky smooth finish is excellent for grinds. Despite its extreme size it remains light enough for controlled play, and the unusual Size L bearing (6×13×5mm, from ILYY/OXY5 compatibility) gives it a distinctive spin character. Each unit is individually serial numbered with "xXx" engravings. Available in orange, red, purple, black, and silver finishes.

title: Steamroller
content: AboutThe Steamroller is XCube's debut product and one of the most visually distinctive yo-yos from the French boutique scene. Despite a sub-50mm diameter, its extreme width matches — almost exceeding — its height, creating the cross-section of a literal steamroller. A cartoonish laser-engraved run-over cat on the side became one of the brand's signature visual elements. Each unit is individually serial numbered. The sharp exterior edges require cautious play but contribute to the distinctive rim-weighted feel. Includes one extra bearing. Available in light blue, red, purple, pink, and green anodized finishes.

meta.yya_response: XCube silicone pads (red flowable silicone stock)

title: Teh Yo
content: AboutTeh Yo is the XCube signature model for Matthieu Marechale, owner of Graou String and prominent member of the French yo-yo scene. Described as "what happens when the classic and the modern have a child," the slim tall inverse-round profile revives old-school aesthetics with contemporary unresponsive performance. The inverse-round shape minimizes sleep loss and supports horizontal play via the included concave bearing. A 35mm trapeze width makes it narrower than most competition throws of its era, lending it an old-school character. Each unit is individually serial numbered. Includes Graou string in packaging.

title: The Seed
content: AboutThe Seed is XCube's final known commercial release, a signature model for Italian player Riccardo "Blanchard" Fraolini developed collaboratively with the Rspecial crew after over a year of prototyping. Described by the brand as "a kind of big La Goutte, with a strong Zeus feeling," it is the largest-diameter XCube ever produced at 58.65mm and features the widest gap in the lineup at 5mm. Despite its 67.8g weight it plays light and floaty on string. The ceramic flat bearing is standard, with a concave bearing included. Custom anodizing by Morapio in acid-wash and splash colorways. Fraolini left the XCube team shortly after release in March 2014, marking the end of the brand's active era.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Size C (flat ceramic stock; concave included)

title: ZeuS
content: AboutZeuS is a super-wide limited edition (100 units) from XCube with a deep incut inner wing step that gives the cross-section a lightning bolt profile, referencing the Greek god Zeus. Weight is concentrated at three distinct points per half for exceptional stability. Despite its extreme width, the ZeuS is described as "wide without being heavy, with a super long spin." Each unit is individually numbered, with a lightning bolt laser engraving on the side. Available in splash and solid colorways in black, red, green, and blue. A collector's piece given its 100-unit run.

title: Xenon
content: AboutThe Xenon is the first signature yo-yo for OFFSET team rider Xavier Ng (multiple Singapore National Champion). Its rounded, organic body shape was designed with comfort in mind for face-adjacent trick styles. Polished rims give a bi-metal visual treatment without the bi-metal price. Xavier used the final prototype to win the 2024 Singapore Nationals before the model went into production. A second collection released in early 2025 refined the gap width and expanded colorways.

title: Xenon Prime
content: AboutThe Xenon Prime is Xavier Ng's tri-material signature, released in 2025. The construction layers 6061 aluminum body, stainless steel inner rims for spin and stability, and POM (Delrin) outer rims that absorb impact and protect against string cuts during Xavier's riskiest trick sequences. At 60mm width it is the widest Xenon. Xavier used it to place 5th globally and win Singapore Nationals for the fourth time, making him the most decorated Singapore national champion in yo-yo history at the time of release.

title: Xenon Supreme
content:
About
Xenon Supreme is Xavier Ng's signature model in the LIMITLESS line, designed to reduce string interference through extended horizontal combinations while remaining usable in vertical play. Combines a 7075 aluminium body with stainless steel and polycarbonate rim components.

title: XIN
content: AboutThe XIN is a machined POM (Delrin) yo-yo with stainless steel rings embedded into the profile, creating a strong feeling of power in a lightweight body. Delivers impressive spin duration with speedy play comparable to full metal. Available in Yellow/Silver Ring, Pink/Black Ring, Pink/Silver Ring, Yellow/Rainbow Ring, Yellow/Black Ring, and Pink/Rainbow Ring.

title: XL Ti Koi
content:
From Yoyofriends:

"XL Ti Koi is an oversized titanium that focuses on fun and what is possible. This yoyo is to challenge what is possible with the titanium material and what is possible with an oversized yoyo."

2023 Halloween Edition

From Yoyofriends:

"To celebrate Halloween, we made extra special and super limited Halloween Version of the XL Ti Koi."

title: XLR8
content: About the XLR8The XLR8 reverses the typical YoYoJam construction formula by using an aluminum alloy body with Delrin plastic rims, concentrating dense metal weight toward the center rather than the edges. This produces a distinct spin character compared to rim-weighted designs. The concave side caps facilitate top-on style spinning tricks. It was premiered at the 2013 World YoYo Contest.

title: XS Bone Chip
content:
History
The XS Bone Chip was the final evolution of Dif-e-Yo's compact Bone Chip lineage, released in 2011. A new step between the bearing seat and pad area significantly increased the effective gap width relative to the overall body size — giving the XS Bone Chip near full-size gap performance in a 52.83mm package. The 6g heavier body compared to the Xbone Chip improved spin stability and enabled longer combo chains. Smooth matte finish. Priced at $89.99.

title: Y Factor
content:
From One Drop:

"In preparing to evolve our line and move on to different things like an oversized yo-yo, we feel we need a new undersized competition level performer at a decent price ($75) that takes all of our experience and knowledge into consideration. We want to eliminate any X factors (unknowns) so we're focusing on what we do know (the Y factors). The result is our new yo-yo, the Y Factor. It is a synthesis of all of our previous work, current knowledge, and player preferences. In keeping with features we know work well, the Y Factor is very agile due to the new profile, features a newly designed thumb grind lip, and comes with our proven bearing and response system. The Y Factor has the grooves from the original Project. Also, it has the round-nut axle system that has been proven out on M1s and Dingos. The Y Factor will come standard with our new Pyramatte (tm) finish in a wide variety of rich standard colors as well as special editions."

title: Y01 Node
content: About the Y01 NodeThe Y01 Node is an aerodynamic-shaped 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a wide 5mm gap for complex layered string trick execution. The KK concave bearing keeps the string centered through intricate multi-layer combos. Comfortable grip and smooth finish. Available in Black/Golden, Red, and other colorways. Discontinued (last retail: $14.99).

title: Y02 Aurora
content: About the Y02 AuroraThe Y02 Aurora is a 6061 aluminum yo-yo with polycarbonate side caps housing multi-colored LED chip boards. As the yo-yo spins, the LEDs cycle through Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, and Blue. Includes an Allen hex key for cap removal and battery replacement, plus 4 replaceable button batteries. Available in multiple colorways with matching LED colors. Both solid and multi-color LED variants were released.

title: Y03 Hertz
content: About the Y03 HertzThe Y03 Hertz was designed by Xinyu Zhang, an experienced player and Official Team MagicYoYo member. Its streamlined V-shaped profile minimizes string friction during tricks for smoother play, and the three-dimensional front design with distinct cuts expands space for intricate trick execution. Lightweight at 63.5g for speed-oriented play. Bead-blasted matte finish. A VIP Edition was available at selected retailers.

title: Y04 Border
content: About the Y04 BorderThe Y04 Border is one of MagicYoYo's widest aluminum throws, with a 52mm width that creates an extremely generous string catch zone for trick landing assistance. An oversized 58mm diameter wing body facilitates binding and trick execution across 1A, 3A, and 5A styles. Ships with a structured zipper case for storage and transport — unusual at this price point.

title: Yelets
content:
From One Drop:

"We set out to create a Side Effect yoyo that was pocket friendly and budget friendly without sacrificing performance. The result is the Yelets.

The Yelets blends the modern aspects of Side Effects with the classic attributes of affordability, performance, and simplicity continuing the tradition established by the Project, M1, and CafeRacer. We want to take the lead in bringing back smaller yoyos and we felt that 52mm was the perfect diameter. It is bigger than what is traditionally thought of as "undersized" (for example, the M1 is 50mm) to retain the performance of a big yoyo but small enough to give you confidence with chop sticks or tight tech tricks.

Once we had the specs perfect, we came up with a crazy idea for the name. We decided to map the diameter and width to latitude and longitude by plugging the numbers into Google Maps to see where it would end up. The result was a small city in Russia called Yelets.

The suggested retail price is $85 for solid colors making this the first Side Effect yoyo at this price."

title: Yes, Absolutely The End
content:
While not technically an Anti-Yo, it is still part of Anti-Yo history.  The END was a small run of modified eetsits.  There were only 22 made, and 17 sold on August 7, 2006.  Retail price was $150.  Here is the story from one of the creators, DocPop. 

"Wednesday, August 02, 2006

The End is Nigh...

It all started with The End.

Last night Len, the laser engraver, dropped of the yo-yos and Phil and I will spend most of this week getting these babies fully put together and shipping the pre-orders.

Now that I have a pic online, let me explain a little bit about The End. It all started while working with Kiya and Sonny, I asked them for an exclusive batch of unpainted raw Eetsits to use for a special run. Of course nothing is ever as simple as that. So Phil Cox and myself started working together as "Yes, Absolutely." and recruited our good friend Nick Corea to help modify these raw eetsits into even better devices. First we sank the bearing well in, to prevent the slipping string problem, then we removed some in surface to keep the yo-yo from being to narrow, then added groves for the silicone, then we added Shmoove Rings.

Now, this is kind of different, the Shmoove Rings are the two recessed circles on the inside of the yo-yo. It's a new concept, I've never been a fan of concave bearings, but I can understand why someone would want something to reduce the friction of the string rubbing the side of the yo-yo. So I thought, why not just remove more of the inside surface? So using these rings, we've managed to reduce the inside surface that could rub against the string by about %50, but it doesn't affect the wind or throw or anything.

Once the yo-yos were finished, we had them anodized. We wanted these yo-yos to have a classic and unique color, it's hard to describe exactly what they are.. Orange/bronze/yellow/oil-ish? I like 'em, whatever color they are.

Then, with a lot of help from Nick, I took the halves to Len for the Laser Engraving process. The yo-yos were engraved on several places; the outer ring, the inside well, numbered on the posts and even writing on the inside. The inside writing, which says "Shmoove" is a subtle touch that gives the silicone more of a surface to grip on and is partially visible through the clear silicone.

Each yo-yo comes with a concave bearing and a handmade The End yo-yo holster by me. They play great and only 22 will be made. Of those, only 17 will be sold.

I'm expecting the yo-yos to ship by next monday, they retail for $150, if you are interested in getting your hands on an End by Yes, Absolutely. please email me for paypal instructions.

posted by Doc Pop at 4:11 PM"
