title: YG.RMX 11%
content: About the YG.RMX 11%The YG.RMX 11% is a tri-material evolution of the YUIGA for Yuiga Suzuki. A polycarbonate ring is placed along the outer edge of the stainless steel rim, creating a three-material construction. "Quicker and more agile" than the original YUIGA, with a lighter, faster response and sharp maneuverability. $199.99 USD. Colorway: Matte Silver / Blue.

title: YG.RMX 13%
content: About the YG.RMX 13%The YG.RMX 13% is the heavier sibling of the YG.RMX 11%, swapping polycarbonate for POM (Delrin) as the outer ring material. The POM ring delivers a "stronger and more planted feel in play" with softer feel and increased stability and momentum versus the 11%. $199.99 USD. Colorway: Silver / Blue.

title: Aries
content:
About
The Aries is the signature bimetal for Jeong Yong-chan, featuring a construction approach unique in the YJYOYO lineup: stainless steel is sandwiched between two aluminum rim components rather than applied as an outer ring. This distributes the heavy material across a broader area, resulting in a smooth, soft playfeel unusual for a bimetal. The wide 48.04mm step-straight body emphasizes catch zone generosity. Available in Purple/Gold. Retails at $129.99.

title: Atomic Fire
content:
About
The Atomic Fire was YJYOYO Club's first serious attempt at a competition-grade 3D-printed yo-yo, developed during a period of aluminum supply shortages that made metal production impractical. The improved hub system requires no removal tool to access the bearing. A bundled 3D-printer shim system allows gap width adjustment for personalized string feel. At 70.9g and 64.4mm in diameter, it prioritizes stability and spin power over nimbleness. Retails at approximately $15.99.

title: Bell
content:
About
The Bell is an unusual entry in the YJYOYO Club catalog — designed explicitly as a "digital detox tool" rather than a performance throw. The narrow 25.85mm width and classic round-profile geometry discourage complex string work, making it a casual carry item for fidgeting, spinning, and simple tricks. Precision-machined aluminum with 3D-printed internal weight distribution components. Available in Champagne Gold. Retails at $29.99.

title: Big Picture
content:
About
The Big Picture is YJYOYO Club's stage performance throw — designed for maximum audience visibility with a 68.81mm diameter and 55.14mm width that dominate the field of view during performances. The 6061 aluminum body is paired with POM plastic sidecaps that enable fingerspin tricks on the flat cap surface. Despite its massive dimensions, construction targets the lightest possible weight at 74.5g — a significant challenge at this scale. Discontinued.

title: Big Picture 2.0
content:
About
Big Picture 2.0 upgrades the original stage throw with a 7075 aluminum body for greater strength at extreme dimensions, polycarbonate wings replacing the original POM caps, and a reinforced M5×10mm axle to handle the structural stresses of a 69mm yo-yo. The prominent fingerspin hub makes fingerspin tricks more accessible for performance use. At 74.4g and 69.37mm diameter, it maintains the audience-visibility priority of the original in a more durable package. Available in Green/Black rims. Retails at $109.99.

title: Chimera
content:
About
The Chimera is YJYOYO Club's monometal spin on the Vegamonte bimetal concept. Because a single-material construction cannot concentrate weight at the rim as effectively as dual metals, the design compensates by going oversized at 58.95mm diameter — pushing mass further out while keeping the overall weight at 65.1g. An unusually short M4×8mm axle further reduces center weight, mimicking bimetal-like weight distribution within a single-material build. Despite the size, it plays light. Retails at $53.99.

title: Chimera 2023
content:
About
The Chimera 2023 is the third generation of YJYOYO Club's oversized monometal, maintaining the same shape and short-axle weight distribution philosophy of the original while improving the bearing lock ring thickness and overall structural durability. Maintaining the original's 58.98mm diameter and step-round shape. YJYOYO recommends pairing it with fat K-string for optimal play feel. Available in Blue. Retails at $53.99.

title: Easy Trick
content:
About
The Easy Trick is YJYOYO Club's entry-level 3D-printed yo-yo, designed to evoke the classic round ball shape of 1980s and 90s yo-yos — the era of Coca-Cola promotional models and early butterfly designs — while fitting it with a modern slim-C bearing for practical sleep times. The result is a beginner-friendly responsive yo-yo that feels familiar to returning throwers and accessible to first-timers.

title: Easy Trick Metal
content:
About
The Easy Trick Metal translates YJYOYO Club's 3D-printed Easy Trick Retro design into machined 6061 aluminum. The classic round profile is preserved, but the denser material delivers improved spin times and a more substantial feel in hand. Targeted at beginners ready to step up from plastic while keeping the familiar responsive setup. Available in Blue. Priced at $47.99.

title: Easy Trick Retro
content:
About
The Easy Trick Retro is a refined iteration of YJYOYO Club's classic round beginner model, with improved impact resistance for players prone to floor drops. The 3D-printed construction is designed to withstand the knocks of early learning. Available in multiple colorways including seasonal Christmas and camouflage editions.

title: Fuzzy
content:
About
The Fuzzy is a comfort-first monometal from YJYOYO Club, designed to minimize fatigue across extended play sessions. Rounded edges reduce the abrasive feel of repeated catches, and the vibration-reduction technology pioneered in the Nova-Eve is carried into the Fuzzy for a smooth, vibe-free play experience. The 54.98mm step-round profile sits at 66.1g. Available in Gray. Retails at $53.99.

title: Galaxy Time
content:
About
The Galaxy Time is a bimetal evolution of the Time Slip, developed in direct response to fan requests. The rim slope was redesigned from the monometal Time Slip to improve string movement and slip feel in bimetal format, and the balance was completely reconfigured to extract maximum efficiency from the stainless steel rim weighting. At 63.4g, it is one of the lighter YJYOYO bimetals, prioritizing speed and maneuverability.

title: Geni
content:
About
The Geni is YJYOYO Club's compact H-profile metal at 47.88mm diameter, pitched as a pocket-friendly full-metal with capabilities beyond its size. The fingerspin spot enables fingerspin tricks, and the pull-start and DNA trick compatibility expand its trick vocabulary for advanced players. Available in Red. Retails at $29.99.

title: Holly 5
content:
About
The Holly 5 is YJYOYO Club's flagship entry-level metal yo-yo and the best-selling model in their domestic Korean catalog with over 50,000 units sold. Machined from 6061 aluminum at a compact 53.95mm diameter, it accommodates all hand sizes while delivering performance that comfortably exceeds typical beginner-metal expectations. The step-round profile with center-track bearing provides consistent string centering for trick learning. Retails at approximately $27.99.

title: Holly 5 High-end
content:
About
The Holly 5 High-end is a precision-upgraded variant of YJYOYO Club's best-selling Holly 5, machined to the same tolerances as their flagship high-end models. The gap is tuned slightly wider than the standard Holly 5 for improved string movement and playability. Same base specifications, elevated execution.

title: Holly 6
content:
About
The Holly 6 is the most recent evolution of YJYOYO Club's Holly entry-metal line, transitioning from the step-round profile of the Holly 5 to a wider H-profile at 46.22mm width — approximately 4.5mm broader than its predecessor. The Tilt Pad system narrows the gap near the response pads while widening toward the bearing, preventing accidental string catches and unintended returns during unresponsive play. Still positioned and priced as an accessible beginner metal. Retails at approximately $29.99.

title: Lapaz
content:
About
The Lapaz is YJYOYO Club's step-up from the Holly 5, designed for intermediate players making their first move toward competitive metal performance. Featuring the P-TERA rim technology and Zephyros gap system, the 55mm step-round body delivers a soft feel and tenacious sleep time despite being mid-range priced. The forgiving geometry rewards consistent technique without punishing slight misalignment. Available in a pink/orange gradient colorway. Retails at approximately $40.99.

title: LM
content:
About
The LM (Lumen) is the signature monometal for YJYOYO Club speed specialist Nam Dong-hun, and serves as the single-material counterpart to his bimetal Radiance. The step-round profile at 55.97mm diameter incorporates the Tilt Pad system — the gap narrows at the response pad and widens toward the bearing — accommodating thick strings and preventing unexpected returns during high-speed sequences. Available in Ice Blue. Retails at $59.99.

title: Megamont
content:
About
The Megamont is the signature bimetal for YJYOYO Club Japan rider Yasutaka Maeda, built on the Sword Master platform but redesigned with YJYOYO's "Future Structure" — a proprietary bimetal rim geometry described as groundbreaking — that provides more maneuverability than the Sword Master while preserving its powerful spin characteristics. The Tilt Pad system prevents accidental string catches at speed. Available in Volcano Red and Ocean Blue colorways. Retails at $129.99.

title: Miniries
content:
About
The Miniries is a scaled-down version of the Monories, reducing the oversized double-rim step-round geometry by approximately 10% to a 54.95mm diameter. Rather than competing on spin power, it prioritizes a soft, floaty play feel described by YJYOYO as "fluffy." Despite being smaller, it is slightly heavier than the Monories at 67.6g. Available in Blue. Retails at $53.99.

title: Monories
content:
About
The Monories is a monometal interpretation of the Aries bimetal, scaling the double-rim design up significantly in diameter while using a flat-cup profile to shift weight toward center-mid. Despite its large oversized dimensions, the construction yields a floaty, smooth feel with more agility than the size suggests. Discontinued from active retail.

title: Nova-Eve
content:
About
The Nova-Eve is YJYOYO Club's zero-vibration monometal project — every unit is individually tested for vibe before shipping, and those failing quality thresholds are rejected. The wide 46.94mm body in 6061 aluminum at 54.98mm diameter prioritizes smooth, dead-still play feel. The vibration-reduction engineering from the Nova-Eve was subsequently incorporated into the Fuzzy. Positioned as a competition-focused monometal for players who want the cleanest possible play experience. Retails at $53.99.

title: Paranoia
content:
About
The Paranoia is the 2A signature model of YJYOYO Club founder Yoon Jong Ki, machined from POM (polyacetal) — a material prized in looping for its durability and smooth snap action. The floating bearing seat boosts sleep time approximately 1.5× over traditional loopers. The replaceable starburst response system uses interchangeable PVC spacers in four gap widths (Pink 1.85mm / Red 1.90mm / Blue 1.96mm / Black 2.00mm), allowing precise gap tuning without replacing the yo-yo. Widely regarded as one of the highest-quality 2A loopers on the market.

title: Paranoia 3D
content:
About
The Paranoia 3D is a 3D-printed looping yo-yo from YJYOYO Club, sharing the Paranoia name but intended as an accessible entry point for 2A practice rather than a replacement for the high-end POM model. Adjustable shims allow basic gap customization. Compatible with YJYOYO's broader 3D-printed parts ecosystem. At 50.7g, it is lighter than the production Paranoia models.

title: Paranoia PC
content:
About
The Paranoia PC is the polycarbonate evolution of Yoon Jong Ki's signature Paranoia looper. It retains the replaceable starburst response concept of the original but upgrades to super-duralumin gap spacers for improved durability and feel. The cap design is secured against accidental separation during loops. Multiple colorways offered. At 51.2g — 0.6g lighter than the POM original — it maintains the delicate weight balance essential for controlled looping play.

title: Pebble
content:
About
The Pebble is a pocket-sized 6061 monometal from YJYOYO Club at just 47.98mm in diameter — compact enough for on-the-go practice while maintaining a competitive 66.1g weight for stability. The smooth texture finish and step-round profile prioritize comfortable hand feel during extended sessions. Retails at $34.99.

title: Ptera
content:
About
The Ptera is a signature monometal for YJYOYO Club players Lee Min Seo and Park Gyu Min, built around an unusually thick outer rim design that concentrates mass at the extreme edge of the 57.92mm step-round body. The result is spin time and stability competitive with bimetal designs despite single-material construction. Team rider Lee Min Seo reportedly abandoned bimetals entirely after the Ptera, using it for all competitive purposes. Available in Gloss Black. Retails at $49.99.

title: Radiance
content:
About
The Radiance is the bimetal signature for YJYOYO Club speed specialist Nam Dong-hun. The step-round profile at 55.03mm incorporates the Tilt Pad system — a gap geometry that narrows toward the response pad and widens toward the bearing — preventing unexpected string catches during high-speed play while accommodating thick competition strings. The double-rim construction also increases durability for throw-intensive practice. Available in Warm Beige/Matte Silver and Glossy Purple/Matte Silver rim colorways. Retails at $109.99.

title: Radiance 7075
content:
About
The Radiance 7075 is a material upgrade of Nam Dong-hun's signature Radiance, replacing the 6061 aluminum body with 7075 super-hard duralumin. The harder material delivers a "hard and sharp feeling" compared to the original's softer 6061 character, and the slightly reduced weight to 66.3g improves speed for horizontal-axis tricks. The Tilt Pad and double-rim construction carry over from the original Radiance. Retails at $129.99.

title: Rimsert
content:
About
The Rimsert is a structural hybrid — stainless steel rim inserts sandwiched between polycarbonate body layers. The approach delivers bimetal-level spin power and rim weighting while the polycarbonate construction provides far greater resistance to cracking and ding damage than aluminum. The step-round profile sits at 56.91mm diameter and 46.08mm width. Designed for players who practice intensively and drop frequently. Retails at $109.99.

title: Roll Machine
content:
About
The Roll Machine is a bimetal designed specifically for the rail combo style dominant in Korean 1A competition — sequences involving repeated string-to-hand contact that can bleed spin if the yo-yo's rim catches. The sharp edge profile of the stainless steel rims minimizes this friction, allowing players to maintain speed through extended rail combinations. The lollipop fade colorway and no-blast finish give it a distinctive gloss appearance. Retails at $109.99.

title: Rolly
content:
About
The Rolly is YJYOYO Club's 2025 entry-level metal, designed to ease the transition to unresponsive play by providing a stronger return snap than typical metals — making binds more accessible for intermediate players still building binding muscle memory. The H-profile at 54mm diameter and 48.4mm width gives a wide catch zone. Tilt Pad response system. Available in Red. Retails at $29.99.

title: Saber Trick
content:
About
The Saber Trick is YJYOYO Club's homage to the classic 1990s Saber Raider, 3D-printed with a straight profile that mimics the original's geometry while housing a full-size Size C bearing for dramatically longer spin times. Excel at classic tricks like "Reach for the Moon" and other traditional string-skipping maneuvers. Available in multiple colorways. Retails at approximately $13.99.

title: Saber Trick (Japan Member)
content:
About
The Saber Trick Japan Member is a special edition of YJYOYO Club's Saber Trick 3D-printed retro model, produced for the brand's Japan team members. Specs are nearly identical to the original but with a slight 1.5g weight reduction to 58.0g.

title: Saber Trick Pro
content:
About
The Saber Trick Pro scales up the Saber Trick concept to a competition-spec H-profile format. At 63.51mm diameter and 48.1mm width, it is substantially larger than the entry-level Saber Trick, offering a 43mm trapeze width and bind-required operation. Despite the oversized dimensions, noise-reduction improvements over standard 3D-print designs give it a cleaner feel. Lighter overall feel than the Atomic Fire with strong sleep power. Retails at approximately $15.99.

title: SE Proto 01
content:
About
The SE Proto 01 is a commercially released development prototype for Nam Dong-hun's signature bimetal work, based on the Chimera monometal platform reduced to 55mm diameter and rebuilt as a bimetal. The result is a powerful, weighted feel distinct from the final Radiance — heavier on the hand with a sense of substantial mass during play. Sold as a limited development item for players interested in the engineering iteration process behind the Radiance.

title: Segamonte
content:
About
The Segamonte is a collaborative design between YJYOYO Club Japan rider Yasutaka Maeda and Korean 1A champion Park Woo-chan — a lighter, faster evolution of the Vegamonte. The "se" prefix reflects a Korean size-reduction concept: the 65.5g Segamonte is approximately 1.5g lighter than the Vegamonte, with a refined step-round geometry emphasizing "light inside, heavy outside" weight distribution. Fine blast finish. Available in a fade with fine blast finish. Retails at $109.99.

title: Seoul
content:
About
The Seoul was produced to commemorate an international yo-yo tournament held in Seoul. Machined from 7075 aluminum with an M5×10mm reinforced axle, it incorporates the Big Picture's prominent fingerspin hub into a standard-sized 56.95mm body — making fingerspin tricks highly accessible at competition dimensions. Designed primarily for DNA trick applications alongside standard string play. Tilt Pad response. Retails at $84.99.

title: Spinell
content:
About
The Spinell is YJYOYO Club's entry-level unresponsive plastic — a polycarbonate body sized at 57.51mm with a fingerspin spot machined into the side face. It serves as a low-cost bind-return practice model for players stepping from responsive to unresponsive operation. Available in Blue, White, and Pink. Retails at approximately $17.99. Also released under the name "Spinel" in some markets.

title: Steel Pot
content:
About
The Steel Pot is a compact bimetal at just 53.97mm diameter, with stainless steel rims constituting approximately 80% of the 66.2g total weight — an extreme rim-to-body weight ratio that concentrates rotational force at the outer edge. Despite the 54mm form factor, the 46mm width makes it well-suited for chopstick and complex string configurations. The Tilt Pad system and rounded step-straight profile round out the design. Available in Raw Silver/Matte Black, Matte Black/Polished Silver, and Raw Silver/Polished Silver. Retails at $104.99.

title: Steel Pot 2
content:
About
The Steel Pot 2 is a second-generation refinement of the Steel Pot compact bimetal. It sheds 0.6g to 65.6g and gains 1.05mm in width to 47.05mm, improving controllability and competitive playability while maintaining the compact 53.94mm diameter. The sloped response area prevents unexpected returns. Available in Matte Blue. Retails at $114.99.

title: Sword Master
content:
About
The Sword Master departs from YJYOYO Club's typical curved-rim bimetal geometry with an extended flat stainless steel rim that runs straight rather than curving inward. This produces a massive concentration of outer mass and extraordinary spin power, at the cost of slightly increased weight — 68.4g makes it one of the heaviest YJYOYO bimetals. The 56.07mm step-round at 46.20mm width provides a strong platform for control-focused play styles. Available in Matte Burgundy/Black rim and Glossy Purple/Raw rim colorways. Retails at $134.99.

title: Tang
content:
About
The Tang is the signature monometal for YJYOYO Club instructor Kim Jun Ho, who works as a yoyo academy teacher. Designed for daily use in instructional contexts, the H-profile with double-rim aesthetics and dome hubs delivers a nimble, responsive feel without sacrificing durability. The smooth matte finish and Tilt Pad response suit extended daily practice. Available in Gunmetal. Retails at $53.99.

title: The Future
content:
About
The Future is a three-material hybrid from YJYOYO Club: a 6061 aluminum body provides the core structure, stainless steel rims add spin power, and POM wings extend the catch zone and provide a uniquely soft return snap unlike pure metal designs. The wide 50.44mm width at step-straight profile prioritizes string catch success. Design inspired by ancient metalworking aesthetics. Available in Black with gold accents. Retails at $109.99.

title: The Metal of the Future
content:
About
The Metal of the Future is the all-metal evolution of The Future, replacing the POM wings with matching aluminum to create a unified construction. While the tri-material The Future emphasized softness and catch forgiveness via POM, the Metal of the Future targets a "new feeling of strength and softness" from pure metal. The slightly tighter 58.83mm body and 50.71mm width maintain the original's characteristic wide catch zone. Available in Red/Yellow. Retails at $124.99.

title: Time Slip
content:
About
The Time Slip was developed in direct response to requests from YJYOYO Club academy students who wanted longer sleep times for mastering complex trick combinations. The solution is an H-profile with unusually thick rims for a monometal — concentrating weight at the outer edge to generate spin power comparable to entry bimetals without the price premium. The 55.94mm body with low edges minimizes string interference. Available in Sky Blue Dragon, Galaxy Forest, Year of the Blue Dragon, Black Dragon, and Matte Aviator Red colorways. Retails between $36.99 and $41.99.

title: Trefoil
content:
About
The Trefoil is described by YJYOYO Club as their most technically challenging manufacturing project to date. Designed for picture trick specialist Kim Yeong Min, the 7075 aluminum body enables ultra-thin walls that bring total weight to just 63.1g despite the 53.93mm H-profile. The hollow stainless steel rims concentrate mass at the extreme outer edge while reducing rim bulk — producing a throw that YJYOYO describes as "light and easy to handle, yet as stable as a heavier throw." Available in Silver. Retails at $119.99.

title: Vegamonte
content:
About
The Vegamonte is a bimetal with an unusual dual-rim structure: stainless steel is applied at both the inner and outer rim positions, rather than the single outer rim typical of bimetal designs. This creates a weight distribution that sits between the extreme outer focus of a standard bimetal and the centered feel of a monometal. The 58.99mm step-round at 67.1g emphasizes stability and smooth, controlled play over raw spin duration. Available in Glossy Red.

title: Z-Project
content:
About
The Z-Project is Park Woo-chan's affordable signature monometal, conceived as an accessible alternative to the Zephyros for YJYOYO Club academy students. The slightly oversized 56.86mm step-round geometry mimics the Zephyros feel at a reduced price point. Despite the "heavy but feels light" quality of the 66.1g construction, the design improves hook and slack success rates through its generous catch zone. Priced at approximately $45.

title: Zephyros
content:
About
The Zephyros is YJYOYO Club's 2020 flagship and Park Woo-chan's primary competition throw for the 2020 World Championships. The three-material construction stacks a POM ring between the 6061 aluminum body and the stainless steel outer rim, physically pushing the heavy rim further from the center than a standard bimetal construction allows — maximizing rim-weight efficiency while keeping total weight at 65.7g despite the 59.07mm oversized diameter. Represents the peak of YJYOYO Club's manufacturing technology at that time.

title: Zephyros 7075
content:
About
The Zephyros 7075 represents five years of refinement on Park Woo-chan's Zephyros flagship line — upgrading the body from 6061 to 7075 super-hard aluminum while reducing total weight to 64.8g. The oversized 58.97mm form factor carries the Zephyros's proven catch zone and stability, now with a double-rim structure and Tilt Pad system. Multiple limited drops released through 2024 and 2025 in colorways including Matte Blue, Glossy Dark Navy/Gold rings, and Matte Black/Raw Silver rings. Retails at $134.99.

title: Zephyros Double
content:
About
The Zephyros Double is Park Woo-chan's bimetal signature, featuring both outer and inner stainless steel rims on a 6061 aluminum body. The outer rim drives spin power while the inner rim brings mass toward the center — a deliberate compromise between extreme rim weighting and centered control that YJYOYO describes as a "natural extension of the arm." The 55.84mm step-round at 66g delivers fast snap and easy spin-up. Available in Black/Silver and Black/Black rim colorways.

title: YO! JACK
content: YO! JACK was a Halloween-themed wooden yo-yo variant released by Hummingbird as part of its seasonal product line. This themed release demonstrated the company's efforts to create novelty and seasonal offerings alongside its traditional models during the final years of operation.

title: Yo-Spin
content:
About
Yo-Spin combines the spinning power of a gyroscope with the freestyle play of a yo-yo: slip a ring onto a finger, launch the spinning disc on an ultra-stretchy elastic cord, and perform tricks blending yo-yo and fidget-spinner motion. Built-in ball bearing for smooth, long-lasting spins. Compact and lightweight, designed for indoor and outdoor solo play.

title: Yo-Yo Man
content: The Yo-Yo Man was Hummingbird's popular retail model, produced from the early 1980s with a four-year production run. Available in both generic and retailer-branded variants, this model represented Hummingbird's first major commercial success, catching the attention of major retailers including L.L. Bean, Eddie Bauer, and Land's End.

title: Airbus
content: AboutYoku's offstring-specific model. The large, durable POM construction handles the impacts of 4A play well, with a solid wide shape suited to toss-and-catch tricks. Described as smooth and durable, with the 2018 version refining an earlier design.ColorwaysWhite, Yellow.

title: Blast
content: AboutCreated with input from professional players Liang Lu and Gao Min, featured in the 2015 "疾风 Blast Wind" promotional video. The Blast was designed specifically for competitive speed play. Stainless steel rim placement enhances stability during rapid trick sequences, while the concave bearing supports extended spin duration from lighter throws. A capable all-around competition bimetal at an accessible price.ColorwaysBlue/Pink, Green/Yellow, Yellow/Purple, Rainbow; Orange/Pink/Blue, Blue/Pink, Green/Purple, Green/Silver.

title: Burne
content: AboutYoku's plastic entry-level unresponsive model. Basic construction with a DNA-trick-capable design, offering an affordable on-ramp to bind-style play. The standard plastic material gives an unusual texture compared to premium aluminum models. Minor vibe noted in some units. A practice throw or budget pick for learners transitioning to unresponsive play.ColorwaysPink, Yellow, Clear, Orange, Blue.

title: Euler
content: AboutKenTech's debut model, designed by Ken Luo (2015 PNWR 3A champion), distributed by Yoku YoYo Design. A compact bimetal that delivers surprising rotational power despite modest dimensions. The straight-body silhouette with rounded rim edges offers comfortable catches, and the stainless steel rim placement maximizes spin stability. In 2015, this throw made a significant impact on the competitive scene before temporarily disappearing.ColorwaysBlack, Acid Wash (Blue/Yellow), Light Blue, Navy, Pink, Brown, Yellow.

title: Euler ReProduct
content: AboutA refined reissue of the original KenTech Euler design, with Yoku YoYo Design as official distributor. Described as having an improved design over the 2015 original. Features splash colorways exclusive to this re-release, including Yellow/Black/Purple, Orange/Blue/Black, Purple/Silver, Light Blue/Yellow, and Black/Black Rim.

title: Euler Ti
content: AboutYoku's premium flagship model in collaboration with KenTech and 2018 Asia Pacific 2A champion Yi Chenghao. The Euler Ti uses a titanium and stainless steel (TiSS) bimetal construction, offering a carefully refined balance between agility and spin time. Comes in a premium presentation box.Note: SpinGear's auto-translated product listing may describe the body material inaccurately. The ¥45,000 price point and KenTech's own description confirm this as a TiSS model (titanium body + stainless steel rims).ColorwaysRaw, Blue, Purple.

title: Friend
content: AboutYoku's accessible full-size aluminum monometal, designed for intermediate players and above. Positioned as "a full-size high-performance metal throw at an affordable price point," the Friend is unresponsive and requires a bind return. A capable everyday player that punches above its price.ColorwaysPurple Specs, Blue Splash, Pink Splash, Cherry Blossom, Black/Silver Splash, Bronze Splash, Blue.

title: Loop Infinity
content: AboutDeveloped under the guidance of 2018 Asia Pacific 2A champion Yi Chenghao, the Loop Infinity is a budget looping model designed to deliver contest-level performance from the factory. The fixed gap with metal spacers and starburst response set slightly taller than the spacer height creates a light, easy play feel. Suitable for beginners through advanced competition-level wrap tricks and combos without gap adjustment.ColorwaysAqua, Yellow, Clear, Christmas, Green, Purple, Pink, Black, Blue, Light Red, Red.

title: Mars
content: Yoku's foundational monometal aluminum model. Available primarily as a B-grade outlet at SpinGear, indicating minor cosmetic imperfections with full performance intact. Colorways include Black/Blue, Black/Pink, Black/Yellow, Blue/Silver, Pink/Silver, Red/Yellow, and Yellow/Green.

title: Polymer
content: AboutYoku's wide-profile bimetal competition model. The straight-based shape with substantial rim weight delivers solid spin performance while keeping overall weight manageable. The wide body relative to diameter provides extra stability for freestyle play. Positioned as a competition-grade throw at the higher end of Yoku's lineup.ColorwaysBlue/Blue, Red/Blue, Silver/Black, Black/Black.

title: POM Storm
content: AboutA POM/stainless steel bi-material variant of the Storm3 silhouette, with a slightly narrower width. The POM body gives a lighter subjective feel than its 66.5g weight suggests, and an unusual tactile texture compared to aluminum models. Pocket-friendly and solid for casual or practice play.ColorwaysBlack/Black Rim, Red/Black Rim, White/Black Rim, White/Gold Rim.

title: Storm3
content: AboutA budget-accessible bimetal with direct lines and striking color combinations. The Storm3 offers a softer, more forgiving feel than typical bimetal models, prioritizing playability over raw performance. Subtle inverse rim rounding aids spin performance while maintaining a clean flat aesthetic. A strong entry point into bimetal play.ColorwaysSilver/Blue/Black, Silver/Black Rim, Silver/Pink/Purple, Red/Black Rim, Black/Black Rim, Green/Black Rim.

title: Super Storm
content: AboutA high-performance bimetal with a wide, extreme outer-edge rim placement for maximum rotational power. The Super Storm's design emphasizes spin endurance and comeback power even at low velocity, making it well suited for long freestyle runs. Strong visual impact from the large stainless rim profile.ColorwaysBlue/Yellow, Black/Red/Green, Black/Green/Purple, Black/Pink/Blue.

title: Topos
content: AboutA lightweight bimetal designed around "hard-hitting rotation." Despite lower weight than most competitors, the Topos delivers heavier-feeling spin performance through precise rim placement. Strong throw tension and responsive regeneration make it a capable competition model. Described as a "big size Euler" — a wider, full-competition take on the Euler's compact silhouette.ColorwaysRed/Pink Fade, Silver/Rainbow Rim, Gold, Orange/Silver/Blue, Black/Blue/Silver.

title: Alpha Wing
content: The Alpha Wing is a fixed-axle yo-yo with a butterfly profile, notable as Yomega's first fixed-axle design in many years at its 2015 release. Fixed-axle play requires different technique than bearing designs — stall tricks, regenerations, and old-school body tricks that depend on friction rather than free-spinning. The polycarbonate body and starburst response system suit both casual play and serious fixed-axle practice, and the butterfly profile accommodates string tricks not possible on a classic barrel-shape fixed axle.

title: Blazer
content: The Blazer was Yomega's flagship aluminum performance yo-yo in 2007, featuring a distinctive rubber peg response system with adjustable hole positioning. The approximately $90 MSRP placed it in the enthusiast tier, and the aluminum construction provided the spin stability demanded by intermediate and advanced 1A players. The rubber peg system offered a different feel from pad or silicone responses of the era.

title: Brain
content: The Yomega Brain, introduced in 1984 and protected by U.S. Patent #4,332,102, was the toy industry's first centrifugal-clutch auto-return yo-yo. When the yo-yo's spin slows below a threshold, the clutch engages and automatically winds the string, returning it to the player's hand. The Brain became one of the best-selling yo-yos in history and established Yomega as a household name worldwide. It remains in production today and serves as the definitive entry point for beginner players.

title: Crossfire
content:
History / About
Released in 2005, the Crossfire was a significant departure for Yomega. The wide H-shaped profile and large C-bearing made it the first Yomega yo-yo capable of unresponsive bind-return play when the bearing is cleaned. The soft rubber response pad and reversible bearing spacer system allow gap-width adjustment. Adding response oil converts it to a responsive setup suitable for foundational tricks.

title: Dash
content: The Dash shares the Maverick's 52.3mm diameter and overall shape but is set up for unresponsive play, requiring a bind to return. The 2013 edition was the first explicitly unresponsive version, using silicone return pads and a Size C bearing. At 67g with a 4.24mm gap width, the Dash provides the stability needed for learning advanced string tricks while keeping the accessible price point of Yomega's aluminum entry tier.

title: Fireball
content: Originally called the "Outrageous Yo" at launch, the Fireball was renamed and refined by 1992. It was the first commercially available yo-yo with a plastic transaxle (Delrin spool bearing), replacing the fixed axle and dramatically extending spin time. The Fireball allowed players to learn string tricks that were impossible on fixed-axle designs and defined a generation of intermediate play. It remains one of the best-selling yo-yos ever made and continues in production.

title: Fireball Saber Wing
content: The Fireball Saber Wing applies the classic Fireball transaxle bearing system to a V-shaped wing profile, widening the gap for string trick play while retaining the responsive transaxle return. At 58.80mm diameter and 49g it is notably lighter than the original Fireball, making it maneuverable for tricks requiring quick movement. Introduced in the 2026 Yomega lineup, the Fireball Saber Wing bridges the intermediate and performance tiers for players who want transaxle responsiveness in a modern wing shape.

title: Firestorm
content: The Firestorm is a butterfly-profile transaxle yo-yo that became one of Yomega's most widely distributed products through the McDonald's Happy Meal promotion in 1999–2000. Its 57.2mm diameter and 54g weight made it comfortable for younger players, and the transaxle bearing provided enough spin time for introductory string tricks. The Happy Meal promotion introduced the Firestorm to millions of children worldwide at the height of the late-1990s yo-yo boom. YoYoJam collaborated on a limited version in 2014.

title: Glide
content: The Glide was released in Fall 2012 as Yomega's top-tier unresponsive aluminum, positioned above the Dash and Maverick as a competition-ready option. At 42.8mm width and 68–69g, the Glide's dimensions favor stability and long spin times suitable for complex 1A freestyles. The silicone pad response and Size C bearing configuration provide the snappy bind returns expected by experienced players. The Glide represented Yomega's commitment to re-entering the performance competition market.

title: Glide XP
content: The Glide XP takes the Glide's H-shape and anodized 6061 aluminum construction into a smaller form factor — 52.30mm diameter versus the Glide's 55.70mm — while maintaining the same switchable responsive/unresponsive configuration. At 66–67g with a C-size concave bearing for responsive and standard C for unresponsive, the Glide XP suits players who prefer a compact yo-yo for faster movement without sacrificing spin stability. Ships in a metal tin gift box with full hardware kit.

title: Groov
content: The Groov is a round-profile 6061 aluminum yo-yo with a Size C bearing and silicone pad response that can be set up for either responsive or unresponsive play by swapping the bearing. At 52.3mm × 38.1mm and 67.5g it shares a body footprint with the Maverick and Dash but introduces a more rounded, traditional profile. The Groov is part of Yomega's effort to offer a complete metal progression path for players at all skill levels.

title: Groov II
content: The Groov II is the successor to the Groov, retaining its round profile and adjustable responsive/unresponsive configuration in updated aircraft-grade aluminum. Yomega's continued investment in round-profile designs reflects the renewed community interest in classic yo-yo shapes and old-school aesthetics alongside modern precision machining. The Groov II targets players who want the feel of a traditional round profile with the performance of a current production aluminum.

title: Gyrex
content: The Gyrex is a non-responsive wing-shaped polycarbonate yo-yo sharing the Power Spin Ultra's 56.80mm × 48.40mm dimensions and roller bearing mechanism, but set up exclusively for unresponsive play requiring a bind return. At 64.90g with a 4mm gap, the Gyrex provides the stability needed for advanced string combinations in a lightweight polycarbonate body. Ships with two strings. Introduced alongside the Power Spin Ultra as a new Pro-level plastic in the 2026 Yomega catalog, with the Gyrex branding featured prominently on the catalog back cover.

title: Hyper Warp
content:
History / About
Released in 1999 by Yomega and Bandai as part of the Hyper Yo-Yo line, the Hyper Warp features a modified body shape with a ball bearing system derived from the Raider, plus starburst response. The slightly heavier weight profile produces stable looping performance. Yomega's competitive response to the ProYo Turbo Bumble Bee and Spintastics Tornado.

title: HyperWarp Heavy Wing
content: The HyperWarp Heavy Wing combined a polycarbonate butterfly body with metal rim weight rings, increasing spin time through improved angular momentum. Its mini ball bearing and double starburst response made it suited to responsive 1A string play. The model evolved from earlier HyperWarp designs and represented Yomega's more serious intermediate performance tier before the company moved into dedicated aluminum designs.

title: HyperWarp Wing
content:
History / About
The HyperWarp Wing is a weighted butterfly-shape variant of the Hyper Warp, created for string trick play. It packs more rim weight than the Saber Raider and introduces Yomega's updated spacer system for smoother, longer throws. The removable cap system with internally accessible screws allows players to add additional weight.

title: Magnetar
content: The Magnetar features Yomega's roller bearing with the bearing bonded directly to the axle — eliminating the loose bearing that beginners often lose. Its V-shaped body at 59mm diameter and 57g produces reliable spin times for responsive play, and the 2.80mm gap keeps string tension consistent during looping and basic tricks. The Magnetar ships in multi-wave color collections and remains in Yomega's current active lineup.

title: Maverick
content: Introduced in March 2012, the Maverick is Yomega's entry-point into aluminum yo-yos, featuring a 6061 aluminum body with anodized finish and rubber return pads. At 52.3mm diameter and 60g, it fits the hand of players moving beyond plastic designs without committing to a high-end unresponsive. The Maverick's responsive setup with Size C bearing makes it forgiving while still providing the spin stability and quality feel of machined aluminum.

title: Metallic Missile
content: The Metallic Missile was one of Yomega's first aluminum yo-yos, featuring a polished body with rubber rim weight rings and a proprietary "Sandman" bearing. Measuring 59mm in diameter and weighing 55g, it launched at approximately $130 MSRP — positioning it as a premium enthusiast product. The Metallic Missile exemplified Yomega's 1998 push into high-end aluminum designs alongside the Wing Force.

title: Ooch-Yo
content:
History / About
Released in 2011, the Ooch-Yo is the plastic signature series yo-yo of Brett "Ooch" Outchcunis. Described as a "reformed version from full metal" — a plastic body with aluminum alloy weight rings built into the rims, making it a step down in price from Ooch's full-metal Ooch Smoov/Groov series while maintaining competitive-level performance. The large C-bearing creates a wide gap that transitions into bind-return territory.

title: Power Brain XP
content: The Power Brain XP adds Yomega's "Smart Switch" to the classic Brain clutch mechanism, allowing players to toggle the centrifugal auto-return on or off. With auto-return off, the XP functions as a standard responsive transaxle yo-yo for practicing string tricks. This dual-mode feature makes the Power Brain XP an effective bridge yo-yo, serving beginners who want auto-return and letting them switch to manual return as their skills develop.

title: Power Spin
content:
History / About
The Power Spin is a plastic transaxle yo-yo released by Yomega in the mid-1990s. Its modified body shape — similar to the high-end Tom Kuhn SB-2 — places the primary mass towards the rims for faster inertia and increased rim speed. Uses the same Delrin transaxle as the Fireball but in the modified profile. Licensed to Bandai and released in Japan as the Hyper Impulse. A butterfly variant, the Power Spin Wing, was also released exclusively in a Deluxe Pack.

title: Power Spin Ultra
content: The Power Spin Ultra is a wing-shaped polycarbonate yo-yo using Yomega's roller bearing in a wide-gap design suited to modern 1A string tricks and finger-spin play. At 56.80mm × 48.40mm and 64.90g, it is notably wide for a polycarbonate model, providing the platform needed for finger spin landings. The bearing can be swapped between responsive and non-responsive configurations. Each unit ships with a bag, glove, six strings, two axles, two bearings, and a bearing key. Introduced as a new Pro-level plastic in the 2026 catalog.

title: Power Spin Wing
content:
History / About
The Power Spin Wing is the flared-body butterfly version of the Power Spin, adapted for string trick play. Released in the late 1990s, it came exclusively in a Deluxe Pack that included a yo-yo holster and extra string, making it relatively rare. Retains the Power Spin's Delrin transaxle and starburst response.

title: Pro X2
content: The Pro X2 is an H-shaped 6061 aluminum yo-yo designed to cover both responsive and unresponsive play styles using included hardware. Two axle lengths and two bearing types — a C-size concave for responsive and a standard C-size for unresponsive — let players configure the yo-yo for their current skill level without buying a second product. At 57.69mm diameter and 66–67g with a 3.175mm responsive gap or 4.75mm unresponsive gap, the Pro X2 spans the intermediate-to-advanced performance range. Each color ships in a metal tin gift box.

title: Pro X3
content: The Pro X3 is the widest model in Yomega's Pro X line, with a 59.46mm diameter and up to 50.85mm width in its unresponsive configuration. Like its siblings the Pro X2 and Glide XP, it ships with two axles and two C-size bearings — a concave for responsive play (2.97mm gap) and standard for unresponsive (4.55mm gap). At 64.90–65.20g in 6061 anodized aluminum it targets advanced players who want a large, stable platform for complex 1A combinations. Introduced in the 2026 Yomega catalog as a new Pro-level addition.

title: Prodigy
content: The Prodigy was developed in collaboration with One Drop YoYos and designed with input from Yomega team player Daniel Dietz, debuting at the 2013 US Nationals. It is one of the few Yomega models to use One Drop's Flow Groove silicone response and a KonKave bearing from Dif-e-Yo, reflecting the technical priorities of One Drop's manufacturing. At 55.44mm × 44.17mm and 65.4g, the blast-finished aluminum body includes finger-spin dimples in the cup — an early example of this feature appearing on production yo-yos.

title: Raider
content: Released in 1991, the Yomega Raider was the first consumer yo-yo to use a micro ball bearing, enabling longer spin times and more consistent looping performance than any previous design. With its narrow gap and starburst response, the Raider became the standard looping yo-yo for serious 2A players and was used by multiple world champions including Jennifer Baybrook and Shinji Saito. The Raider's design has remained largely unchanged, a testament to how well it was conceived from the start.

title: Raider EX
content: Released on March 31, 2008, the Raider EX refines the legendary Raider with a modified axle design while retaining the same micro ball bearing that made the original a staple of 2A competition. Included spacers allow players to fine-tune the gap for different looping preferences. The Raider EX weighs 53.6g at 58.75mm diameter and remains the preferred looping yo-yo for a large portion of competitive 2A players worldwide.

title: RB II
content:
History / About
The RB II by Yomega is a plastic ball-bearing yo-yo released in the late 1990s. It combines the capless, rim-weighted modified body of the Power Spin with the long-spinning roller bearing of the Raider. Lighter than the Raider for improved control and faster spin, the RB II was marketed as capable of exceeding 10,000 RPM. A transitional model bridging the gap between transaxle looping yo-yos and full ball-bearing string trick yo-yos.

title: Saber Raider
content: The Saber Raider brings the Raider's roller bearing looping performance into a V-shaped (wing) body, widening the profile compared to the classic Raider while retaining its long-spin bearing mechanism. At 58.80mm × 39.60mm and 51g it is noticeably lighter than the Raider, making it more agile for looping sequences. Introduced in the 2026 Yomega catalog as a new addition to the Level 3 lineup.

title: Saber Wing Brain
content:
History / About
Released in 1998, the Saber Wing Brain combines the beloved auto-return centrifugal clutch of the original Brain with the flared butterfly wing body shape of the Saber Wing line. The wing profile makes mounting string tricks significantly easier while the clutch ensures the yo-yo always returns to the thrower's hand. The overseas adaptation of the Japanese Hyper Yo-Yo Stealth Brain from 1997.

title: Saber Wing Fireball
content:
History / About
Released in 1997, the Saber Wing Fireball is a variant of the classic Yomega Fireball redesigned with a flared "Saber Wing" butterfly body shape. The wing profile dramatically improves string-catching ease, making this an ideal entry point for transitioning from looping to string tricks. Retains the Fireball's teflon transaxle sleeve and starburst response. Also released in Japan that year as the Stealth Fire in the Bandai Hyper Yo-Yo line.

title: Spectrum
content: The Spectrum features internal LEDs embedded in the yo-yo body that activate during spin, creating a light-trail effect in low-light conditions. Despite the added electronic components, it maintains a 58.4mm diameter and 62g weight suitable for responsive 1A play. The plastic transaxle bearing provides a comfortable spin time for intermediate tricks. The Spectrum is part of Yomega's current lineup and appeals to players who want both performance and visual flair.

title: Stealth Brain
content: The Stealth Brain was produced for Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line in Japan, launched in October 1997. It features the same centrifugal clutch auto-return mechanism as the Brain in a refined body shape aimed at the mass Japanese toy market during the late-1990s yo-yo craze. Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line became a cultural phenomenon in Japan, and the Stealth Brain was among its flagship products. The North American equivalent was later released as the Saber Wing Brain.

title: Stealth Fire
content: Released in September 1997 as part of Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line, the Stealth Fire is a wing-shaped transaxle yo-yo designed for string tricks. It shares the Fireball's nylon transaxle bearing mechanism but in a wider butterfly profile suited to intermediate play. Like the other Hyper Yo-Yo models, it was a Japan-market exclusive produced through the Bandai partnership and fueled by the late-1990s yo-yo craze. The North American equivalent was the Saber Wing Fireball.

title: Stealth Raider
content: The Stealth Raider was released in December 1997 through Bandai's Hyper Yo-Yo line. It uses a ball-bearing transaxle in a flared wing body shape, bridging the gap between the looping Raider and the string-trick-oriented Stealth Fire. The Stealth Raider evolved from the Stealth Fire's design and added a bearing for longer spin times, making it versatile for both trick styles. The North American equivalent was the Saber Raider.

title: Wing Force
content: The Wing Force was Yomega's first aluminum butterfly yo-yo, released in 1998 at approximately $40 MSRP — making quality metal performance accessible to consumers who couldn't afford the limited high-end competition metals of the era. The Wing Force went through multiple response iterations over its production run, moving from reverse starburst to concentric rings to SPR-style spacers. It represented Yomega's push into the enthusiast performance segment during the late-1990s boom years.

title: X-Brain
content: The X-Brain combined the Brain's centrifugal clutch auto-return mechanism with a butterfly (wing) profile, making it accessible for both beginner looping and introductory string tricks. The wider gap accommodated the string during tricks while still snapping back when spin slowed. The X-Brain was featured in the McDonald's Happy Meal yo-yo promotion in 1999–2000 and introduced millions of children to butterfly-style yo-yos.

title: X-Brain Wing
content: The X-Brain Wing carries Yomega's centrifugal auto-return clutch into a V-shaped wing body, updating the classic X-Brain concept for modern preferences. At 58.80mm × 39.60mm and 58g, it is slightly wider than the original X-Brain, giving more string clearance for intermediate tricks while still snapping back to the hand automatically when spin slows. Introduced in the 2026 Yomega catalog as a new addition to the Level 1 beginner lineup.

title: Xodus II
content: The Xodus II succeeded the original 2003 Xodus with thicker walls and more durable rubber rim construction. At 67mm in diameter it was notably larger than most yo-yos of its era, and the rubber rims provided both weight distribution and protection against dings. The Size A roller bearing offers responsive play with substantial spin time for its class. The Xodus II remains in Yomega's active lineup as an oversized intermediate option.

title: Yonami Code
content: AboutA triple signature throw designed with Ashley Thompson, Bailey Main, and Jake Leach. The modified H-shape maximizes stability while the LEGO-compatible hub stays true to Rain City's identity. Video game-themed colorways reference the Gamer heritage. Includes stickers, collectible pogs, string, and maple candy. Plays both responsive and unresponsive with included bearings.
