title: Chen Long
content: AboutThe Chen Long is YoyoFormula's entry into affordable bimetal competition throws. The sloped H-profile creates a wide catch zone and rounded rims for comfortable catches, while the stainless steel outer rings maximize rim weight for long spin times and stability. At 56mm × 47mm and 66.2g it targets competitive players seeking bimetal performance without a premium price tag. Available in Bright Silver and Black.

title: D1 Angel
content: AboutThe D1 Angel is YoyoFormula's intermediate POM yo-yo, featuring a modified organic profile at 55.7mm × 48.5mm for easy catches and comfortable play. Extra rim weight machined near the outer edges boosts spin time and stability. The distinctive colored aluminum hub is available in five variants — gold, green, blue, red, and purple — providing visual contrast to the white POM body. Positioned as a step up from YoyoFormula's polycarbonate beginner models.

title: D2
content: AboutThe D2 is a polycarbonate yo-yo built around a metal concave fingerspin hub for balanced, long-spinning finger spins. The soft V-shape at 56.1mm × 43.6mm provides power and stability for learning string tricks, while the fingerspin hub opens up an additional genre of modern play. A V2 revision reduced weight by 5g and increased the hub size for improved fingerspin performance.

title: D2 Angela
content: AboutThe D2 Angela is YoyoFormula's compact 4A off-string model, machined from durable Delrin POM. At 66mm diameter it sits on the smaller end of the off-string spectrum, providing a nimble feel for players who prefer tighter, more maneuverable 4A play compared to larger off-string throws. Distributed primarily via Southeast Asian retailers.

title: D3 Dragon Ball
content: AboutThe D3 Dragon Ball is YoyoFormula's entry-level 2A looping yo-yo. The polycarbonate body features aluminum bearing spacers for consistent response geometry, and the K-bearing plus starburst response combination delivers snappy, durable loops right out of the box without modification. A broad selection of eleven colorways makes it approachable for two-handed looping at any skill level.

title: D6
content: AboutThe D6 is YoyoFormula's flagship beginner polycarbonate yo-yo. Spinning caps allow pull-start practice for complete beginners, while outer weight rings extend spin time for learning the basics. The responsive setup provides snappy, reliable returns. Available in a translucent blue body with swappable colored caps — gold, green, blue, purple, and silver — making it a customizable first yo-yo.

title: Empire
content: AboutThe Empire is a mid-sized monometal with a heavily rim-weighted organic design and wide catch zone that minimizes string drag. At 56mm × 43mm and 67.1g, it targets competitive players seeking capable mono-metal performance at an accessible price. Released in a raw unfinished aluminum finish, the Empire emphasizes function over aesthetic flair.

title: F0
content: AboutThe F0 is YoyoFormula's first product and primary entry-level aluminum yo-yo. The classic V-shape profile features soft, rounded edges for comfortable play, and the standard Size C bearing socket allows players to swap in a full-size bearing when they are ready to convert to unresponsive string trick play. Offered in solid and splash finishes at an accessible price point.

title: F0S
content: AboutThe F0S is an updated version of the F0 with increased width and a slightly heavier feel. The soft blasted finish provides a smooth surface texture, and the rounded V-shape delivers comfortable, controlled returns for players learning to throw. As with the F0, the standard Size C socket allows conversion to unresponsive play.

title: F0S23
content: AboutThe F0S23 is the 2023 revision of the F0S entry-level aluminum, featuring increased width and reduced weight compared to its predecessor for a lighter, floatier feel on the string. The soft blasted finish supports grinds, and the extra responsive bearing included in the box allows players to start responsive before upgrading. The rounded V-shape remains accessible for beginners and intermediates alike.

title: F3S-2
content: AboutThe F3S-2 is YoyoFormula's flagship LED yo-yo — an ultrawide POM construction with two USB-rechargeable LED circuit boards. At 84g and 69mm in both diameter and width, the extreme dimensions maximize trick visibility and string exposure during light-up performances. The rechargeable USB system replaces battery-dependent LED designs. Comes with a USB charger, extra strings, and a counterweight. Replacement LED circuit boards are sold separately.

title: F7 LED
content: AboutThe F7 LED adapts the F7's ultrawide geometry into a clear polycarbonate shell housing two USB-rechargeable LED boards. The transparent PC body creates a striking visual effect as the LEDs illuminate through the translucent material. At 52.4mm × 54.1mm and 69.6g, the wide profile facilitates trick execution while the integrated LEDs provide a light show in low-light environments.

title: F7 Pro
content: AboutThe F7 Pro is one of YoyoFormula's widest throws, measuring over 55mm across. The POM plastic body features stainless steel inner rings for added rim weight, improving momentum and spin time despite the ultrawide profile. Despite its extreme dimensions, the F7 Pro is described as comfortable in the hand, and the POM construction offers durability and a distinct feel compared to metal alternatives. Available in three color combinations with a contrasting blue aluminum hub.

title: F7 SS
content: AboutThe F7 SS is a companion to the F7 Pro sharing the same ultrawide POM-plus-stainless-steel construction but with different dimensional tuning. The stainless steel inner rings in the cup boost rim momentum while the POM shell provides impact resistance. Released in a single white colorway, the F7 SS targets competition-focused players seeking the F7's width and weight distribution in a cleaner aesthetic.

title: F8 Perfect Pegasus
content: AboutThe F8 Perfect Pegasus features a classic rounded V-shape with heavy rim weighting and a flat minimalist cup designed to maximize spin momentum. At 55.6mm × 44.5mm and 66.8g, it sits in the mid-size sweet spot for competition 1A play. Marketed as "competition ready," the F8 delivers strong string presence and power at a budget mono-metal price. Available in gold, red, matte blue, matte silver, and splash finishes.

title: F9 Savior
content: AboutThe F9 Savior is YoyoFormula's first undersized yo-yo, measuring just 49.5mm diameter — well below the competition standard of ~55mm. Machined from premium 7075 aluminum alloy, the compact body features thick rims that concentrate mass at the outer edge for stability and spin time despite the small footprint. Designed for players who prefer nimble, responsive-feeling throws for intricate string transitions and on-the-go play.

title: Infinity Blitz Ball
content: AboutThe Infinity Blitz Ball is a signature 2A looping yo-yo developed with Yi ChengHao, the 2018 Asia Pacific Champion in the 2A division. Designed to deliver stable, durable loops at a budget price point, the Infinity Blitz Ball makes competitive looping accessible to beginners and intermediates. It is one of the most colorway-diverse products in the YoyoFormula lineup, available in over twenty options ranging from solid colors to translucent finishes.

title: J1
content: AboutThe J1 is YoyoFormula's entry-level responsive aluminum, machined from 6061 alloy with anodized finishes and unique laser-engraved rim patterns for each colorway. Five "elemental" colorways — Earth, Metal, Water, Fire, and Wood — each carry distinct engraving motifs. The slim responsive bearing can be swapped for a standard Size C for unresponsive play, making the J1 a two-stage learning yo-yo.

title: J1 7075
content: AboutThe J1 7075 upgrades the J1S concept to premium 7075 aluminum alloy for increased strength and durability in the same compact body. At 54.5mm × 43.5mm and 67.5g, it is nearly identical in dimensions to the J1S but with the tighter tolerances and smoother finish characteristic of the harder 7075 alloy. Silicone pad response provides reliable unresponsive play at a budget entry price for 7075-grade performance.

title: J1S
content: AboutThe J1S is a compact redesign of the J1, reducing diameter by 3.6mm while increasing weight for improved spin time in a more manageable form factor. Glossy anodized finish with decorative laser-engraved rims and a string-centering bearing make it suitable for unresponsive string trick play. The five colorways — Gold, Green, Blue, Red, and Purple — mirror the J1's color scheme.

title: J2
content: AboutThe J2 is YoyoFormula's entry-level unresponsive monometal, featuring multicolored glossy anodizing and laser-engraved accents that give it a bimetal-like appearance at a budget price. Classic wide body, rim-weighted design, and a string-centering bearing optimize spin time for learning string tricks. Available in three vibrant multicolor finishes — Pink, Yellow, and Orange.

title: J2S
content: AboutThe J2S is a compact revision of the J2, reducing diameter by 1mm while maintaining the same weight for increased density and stability on the string. Polished splash anodizing — Blue with Pink Splash and Green with Orange Splash — gives it a premium visual character. The slightly smaller form factor makes it feel more nimble than the J2 while retaining strong spin and catch zone.

title: J3
content: AboutThe J3 is YoyoFormula's standard-size 4A off-string yo-yo, machined from POM plastic with a double-rim design and deep center cup for improved balance and durability on drops. The standard version at 68.8g provides stability and momentum for controlled 4A play, while the "Lite" variant at 61.8g caters to players preferring a faster, more maneuverable off-string experience. Available in six colors.

title: Loop Blitzball
content: AboutThe Loop Blitzball is the successor to the Infinity Blitz Ball, co-signed by Yi ChengHao with a redesigned mold and adjusted weight distribution. The side spout was removed for improved durability, and the K-bearing plus starburst combination was retained for consistent loop performance. A 2025 production run introduced a new mold derived from the Wind Ball looper with modified starburst response geometry for refined loop timing. Distributed via Spingear Japan and yoyoformula.com.

title: Metal Globe
content: AboutThe Metal Globe is YoyoFormula's premium 2A looper, featuring a capless clear polycarbonate body with aluminum inner rings for rim-focused weight distribution. The transparent construction provides an unobstructed view of string wrapping around the bearing during loops — a feature unavailable on most opaque loopers. Designed for snappy responsive returns at any 2A skill level. Available in three clear/silver and clear/gold color combinations.

title: Bi-mom
content:
Bi-mom, also written Bimom, is a YoYoFREAKS model described by collectors as an organic bimetal yo-yo. The Unknown collectors’ ledger documents an edition in March 2018. Owner discussions distinguish it from the original aluminum Your Mom.

Documentation notes

Released production identity is collector-documented: the Unknown ledger lists March 2, 2018 and ten edition pieces, and independent owner discussions identify the bimetal model. Original retail announcement, exact initial base-model launch date, total production, all numerical specifications, bearing, response, axle, exact metals/alloys and formal play-style classification remain unverified. The 2018 year records documented edition availability rather than a proven first base-model launch. Do not transfer original Your Mom specifications. No clean image found. No collaborating company established.

title: Freak
content: Freak is a 2019 mono-metal yo-yo from YoYoFREAKS and a SuperFreak derivative. The 6061 aluminum design has a fingerspin cup and more central weighting. The brand described a run of 100 individually numbered yo-yos across ten colorways.

title: Hashtag
content:
Hashtag, styled as #, is a compact bimetal yo-yo in the YoYoFREAKS Hundred Series. Its 41.9 mm diameter and 38.85 mm width make it nearly as wide as it is tall. The brand-store record documents a C bearing and 19 mm CBC response pads.

Documentation notes

Brand-store page confirms bimetal construction but not exact alloys; a contemporary owner review reports an aluminum body and internal stainless-steel rings. Those material details remain owner-reported/unverified and are not assigned as material taxonomy. Exact initial launch day, gap, axle and play-style classification remain unverified. 2017 retail availability is confirmed by the store/review. May 17, 2017 and ten pieces refer to the FIU edition. Brand image host fails TLS; no clean image found. No collaborating company established.

title: Pound
content:
Pound is a bimetal model in the YoYoFREAKS Hundred Series. A contemporary October 2017 review identifies it as the third series model and describes a recessed fingerspin dimple. The brand later used its shape as the basis for the Delrin Sharp.

Documentation notes

Public retail release in 2017 is supported by the October 4, 2017 unboxing/review, which reports the model sold out. Diameter, width, weight, gap, axle, bearing, response, exact metals/alloys, formal play-style classification, launch price and exact initial launch day remain unverified. Do not copy Sharp specifications: Sharp is a different Delrin model. The collector ledger records August 8, 2017 and ten pieces for the Unknown edition, not the base model launch or total production. Brand-store source text was verified through the search index; its live host fails TLS. No clean image found. No company collaborator established.

title: SuperFreak
content:
SuperFreak is a Johnnie Delvalle YoYoFREAKS design with a fingerspin cup and rim-focused weighting. The brand-store record lists a 57 mm diameter, 66.5 g weight and 4.50 mm gap, with a C bearing and 19 mm CBC-sized response pads. Retail availability is documented in 2018.

Documentation notes

Brand-store specifications and September 4, 2018 retail review independently checked in indexed primary text; live host fails TLS. Width, axle, exact metals/alloys, launch price, formal play-style classification and exact initial launch day remain unverified. A contemporary owner describes bimetal construction, but exact materials are not assigned as taxonomy. The FIU ledger’s June 23, 2018 SF entry is probably SuperFreak, supported by brand photo filenames yyf-sf and an owner sale naming an Unknown Super Freak. This alias and its exact edition-date mapping remain inferred/unverified; do not treat as an established match for public article linking. No clean image found. No collaborating company established.

title: Your Mom
content:
Your Mom is Johnnie Delvalle’s first YoYoFREAKS Hundred Series yo-yo. The 6061 aluminum model was offered as an unresponsive string-trick design with a matte finish and a Buddha Dimple bearing. The brand-store record gives a January 25, 2017 release.

Documentation notes

Brand product page specifies 67.9 g; its prose rounds this to 68 g. Specifications and release were independently checked against indexed brand-store text; the live host now fails TLS verification. Axle length remains unverified. The FIU list’s ten-piece Unknown edition is an edition count, not total model production. No clean image found; brand images fail TLS. Buddha is a component vendor, not a collaborating company.

title: Recoil
content:
History / About
Introducing the Yoyofriends Recoil — the widest yo-yo in the lineup. Recoil features an outer stainless-steel ring construction with a V/W profile inspired by the cut series. High SS ring weight and overall weight make Recoil the most powerful and daring Yoyofriends yo-yo yet. If you want absolute performance, catchzone, and power, Recoil is the answer.

title: Alliance
content: About the AllianceThe Alliance represents a unique collaboration between two of YoYoJam's top 4A players — 2011 World Champion Ben Conde and 2005 World Champion John Narum — translating their offstring sensibilities into an oversized full-metal 1A design. At 61.76mm in diameter it is among the largest full-metal yo-yos produced by YoYoJam, yet its aluminum construction keeps it at a competitive 63.7 grams.

title: Classic
content: About the ClassicThe Classic is YoYoJam's most affordable entry-level yo-yo and one of the few yo-yos manufactured in the United States. It ships with a narrow bearing and rubber O-rings for fully responsive play suited to beginners, and can be upgraded to a wide Speed Bearing and silicone pads for unresponsive bind play at very low cost. Its low-edge body shape provides stability, making it the recommended first yo-yo for many learners.

title: Night Moves
content:
History / About
Released in 2002, the Night Moves was the first signature series yo-yo from YoYoJam founder and owner Dale Bell. A composite construction yo-yo developed for serious string play, it featured stainless steel weight rings for enhanced rim weighting — innovations that would define the Night Moves lineage for over a decade. Features a C-bearing, starburst response, and adjustable gap.

title: Night Moves 2
content:
History / About
The Night Moves 2, released in 2003, was the second version of Dale Bell's signature series. It introduced a new O-ring response system in place of the starburst used on the original, and the body was redesigned and slightly widened. Early production runs had some balance and vibration issues that were corrected in later releases.

title: Night Moves 3
content:
History / About
Released in 2004, the Night Moves 3 was a landmark yo-yo: the first production yo-yo to use titanium weight rings. Designer Dale Bell slimmed the profile compared to earlier versions while incorporating titanium rings for extreme rim weighting. The body uses clear plastic with embedded glitter, and the underside of the side caps are painted — giving the yo-yo a distinctive glow effect under stage lighting.

title: Night Moves 4
content:
History / About
Released in 2006 as a Worlds Special Release, the Night Moves 4 introduced a three-layer construction: plastic inner body, aluminum layer, and a nickel-bronze outer rim — the most complex layering in the Night Moves series to that point. The iconic hot rod side-cap graphic carries over from earlier models. Features O-ring response and a large C-bearing.

title: Night Moves One
content:
History / About
Released in 2004 as a special limited re-issue of the original Night Moves, the Night Moves One retained the same starburst response and molding as the original while featuring new side caps and an enyo plastic body. Only 100 units were produced, making this a sought-after collectible in the YoYoJam lineage.

title: Patriot
content:
History / About
To celebrate New Year's 2004, YoYoJam produced an exclusive run of the Patriot for Infinite Illusions using their Enyo plastic formulation. Unlike the standard red, white, and blue colorways, this special edition uses a pearlescent Enyo plastic with suspended glitter particles that shift between blues, greens, and oranges. The YoYoJam Patriot holds historical significance as the first production yo-yo to feature a size "C" ball bearing, which became the modern standard for unresponsive play.

title: SFX
content:
History / About
Released in 2010 to commemorate the original SpinFaKtor's tenth anniversary, the SFX (SpinFaKtorX) takes a new direction: instead of outer metal rings, it places an aluminum alloy weight ring in the midship position for a balance between control and stability. The new Solid Spin Axle system improves reliability. Available with both a standard bearing (responsive) and an included Speed bearing (unresponsive).

title: SpinFaktor HG
content:
History / About
Released on April 15, 2005, the SpinFaktor HG (Heavy Gravity) was YoYoJam's first yo-yo to use a denser composite plastic — saturated with metal powder — to add rim weight instead of traditional aluminum rings. This created a mid-price-point model between the budget all-plastic range and the premium metal-rimmed line. It became the last yo-yo to carry the SpinFaktor name until the SFX in 2010.

title: SpinFaktor HG XTra
content:
History / About
Released in fall 2005 as a limited test run of approximately 80 units, the SpinFaktor HG XTra shares the same mold as the standard HG but is considerably heavier, using an extra-dense concentration of the Heavy Gravity composite material. The extreme 80g weight made it a curio and collector's item, representing the limits of what the HG plastic formulation could achieve.

title: Sunset Trajectory
content:
History / About
The Sunset Trajectory is the dual signature series yo-yo of YoYoJam team members Dave Geigle and Bill de Boisblanc. It became the standard looping model in YoYoJam's lineup, featuring double O-ring response, a ball bearing axle, and adjustable gap. Used competitively by players such as Yoshi Mikamoto and Joseph Harris, it is considered one of the most popular looping yo-yos of the 2000s. It was later replaced by the updated Sunset Trajectory NXG.

title: Titan
content:
History / About
Released in 2012, the YoYoJam Titan is a premium bi-metal yo-yo featuring a duralumin (aluminum alloy) body with a corrosion-resistant titanium rim weight — a material combination rarely seen outside of ultra-premium releases. Ships in a beautiful wooden jewelry box lined with silk. YYJ O-ring silicone response and a large C-bearing provide competitive-level performance. Retailed at $194.99.

title: Titan Gold
content:
History / About
Released in 2004, the Titan Gold is one of the rarest and most valuable yo-yos YoYoJam ever produced. Only ten numbered production units were made (plus a handful of prototypes), each featuring 22-karat gold weight rings around the rims. Custom versions featured sapphire inlays on the side caps. Despite its artistic opulence, the Titan Gold is fully functional — fitted with a large C-bearing, rubber O-ring response, and adjustable gap. Estimated collector value exceeds $1,000.

title: Aluminium
content: The Aluminium was the first yo-yo produced by Brazilian manufacturer Yoyojoca, introduced exclusively at the 2004 Brazilian National Championships. It marked the launch of the brand's all-aluminium G-series line.

title: G-Seven
content: The G-Seven was the seventh and final known model in Yoyojoca's G-series, completing the Brazilian manufacturer's all-aluminium line of 1A yo-yos.

title: G-Six
content: The G-Six was the sixth iteration of Yoyojoca's G-series, part of the Brazilian brand's all-aluminium run of 1A yo-yos.

title: G4
content: The G4 was the fourth iteration of Yoyojoca's G-series, part of the Brazilian brand's ongoing run of all-aluminium 1A yo-yos.

title: GIII
content: The GIII was the third model in Yoyojoca's all-aluminium G-series, continuing the Brazilian brand's progression in domestic yo-yo manufacturing.

title: GV
content: The GV was the fifth iteration of Yoyojoca's G-series, continuing the Brazilian manufacturer's line of all-aluminium 1A yo-yos.

title: Alternative
content: History / AboutThe Alternative is the fourth EX-System model and can serve as a large 1A yo-yo or a small offstring yo-yo. Rewind sold two types: the 1A type uses a size C bearing response unit and Lock Crest for an oversize Delrin feel similar to the Elements, and the 4A (offstring) type is set up for offstring with a gap tuned for it and size D bearing. Weight rings (sold separately) can be added. Looping lube can make it responsive.

title: Cocytus
content: History / AboutRewind describes the third YoYoJoker release as the maker's first undersize, with a thick rim and a very wide body and trapeze width, yet stable. An H-profile step has a bank that makes rejection tricks easier. A concave bearing is standard. Per the maker, "Cocytus" is the river of lamentation at the bottom of hell where traitors are frozen in ice, which the dense, rounded, sharp body suggested.

title: D-Strider
content: History / AboutThe D-Strider changes the Strider from size C to size D bearing for more spin, keeping the same edge height. Rewind describes this version as a limited edition (100 pieces) made in collaboration with HSpin, the originator of the size D bearing, with the Fire pattern of HSpin's Pyro engraved on a clear anodized silver "Pyro Ghost" color. yoyo.fandom lists it as a collaboration with HSpin.

title: DoubleJoker
content: History / AboutThe DoubleJoker was the first release from YoYoJoker, the brand started by Daisuke Shimada, whose record includes the 2002 World X division title and three straight 3A World titles (2003-2005), a total of four consecutive world championships. Yo-Yo Store Rewind describes it as the "first release" from the brand, with an inward-scooped rim that keeps control while moving weight outward, and an inverse-round profile that reduces sleep loss.A pair of small side caps sit tight against the body, a nod to Shimada's roots in the YoYoJam sponsor team, known for foil-stamped caps. Rewind notes the maker called it "heretical" (the brand's stated theme) yet suited as a new standard. yoyo.fandom lists a gold-leaf cap print, silicone Joker Pad response and a Dif-e-Yo KonKave C-bearing.Limited editions include 2010 Japan Nationals colors (pink; blue/pink half), a 2010 Worlds edition (red/blue half bodies) and a nickel-plated version.

title: DoubleJoker (2012)
content: History / AboutYo-Yo Store Rewind describes the renewed DoubleJoker as a completely new yo-yo: larger, with more spin power and stability, at an average 66g. A new "Slider Edge" of Delrin sits in the center of the body, giving a soft plastic feel inside a metal yo-yo, better slip and longer sleeps with the inverse-round shape. The logo changed from plastic caps to laser engraving, the outer rim is rounder, and a Dif-e-Yo concave bearing and a 64 titanium axle are standard. Luminous ring weights fit without length adjustment.Colors are listed as metal body / Delrin part color. Only the nickel/black version is 63.2g. yoyo.fandom lists this as the 2012 DoubleJoker with 55mm x 42mm, 65.8g standard weight, KonKave C-bearing and 19.6mm pads.

title: DoubleJoker LF
content: History / AboutLF stands for Light-weight Full-size. Per Yo-Yo Store Rewind it is lighter and larger than the original DoubleJoker, with a thick rim and wide pads for strong spin. It adds the Core Axle shared with the Luminous and Strider, and the response surface is tapered (higher on the inside, deeper on the outside) for a firm return with better slip. yoyo.fandom lists it as a 2011 variant with a KonKave bearing.

title: Elements
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Elements as YoYoJoker's first oversize and first Delrin yo-yo, 64mm in diameter, with a very light design for its size. Inverse-round profile with an extremely low edge and weight pushed to the perimeter. The face and response unit are duralumin for rigidity and are removable.

title: Eternity
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Eternity as the model used by Kazuki Okada, a Rewind staff member who won the West Japan 1A division in 2007, 2009 and 2010 and placed second at the nationals in 2009 and 2010, and who serves as JYYF head judge. It is slightly heavy to steady the trajectory and extend spin, an inverse-round close to the DoubleJoker with added weight on the rounded wings and a very low edge.The bearing lock has a diagonal cut so the bearing can be removed more easily while the locks still seat tightly, as with the Luminous Core Axle. Dif-e-Yo concave bearing and titanium axle are standard.

title: Exceed
content: History / AboutThe Exceed is the first yo-yo of the EX-System, YoYoJoker's customizable line introduced in 2013. Each EX yo-yo is built from an EX Body, an EX Response Unit and an EX Lock Crest plus a bearing; parts interchange between EX models. The Exceed is lightweight, full-size and uses a size C bearing, emphasizing ease of control and a soft Delrin feel. Swapping in the Perceptor response unit gives a size D Exceed. yoyo.fandom lists a white or black body with colored Lock Crests.

title: ILLmina
content: History / AboutThe ILLmina is a collaboration between YoYoJoker and Yaneura Works (known for leather "Armor Holder" yo-yo holders). It is based on the Luminous, with a leather ring instead of the acrylic ring, a nickel-plated body and adjusted ring seat. Rewind says it was limited to 100 pieces, concept being a luxury yo-yo that looks good to non-players, shipped in a black spindle case. Weight varies due to the leather ring. yoyo.fandom lists it as a collaborative model with Yaneura Works.

title: Luminous
content: History / AboutRewind says this full model change replaced the 2011 Luminous. It has an H profile mixing straight and round lines and is slightly heavier for stability, with weight pulled inward by the acrylic ring. Titanium axle and Dif-e-Yo concave bearing are standard. The acrylic ring is machined individually to reduce wobble. Weight varies from 67g to 68g by ring. The maker states the polished raw finish makes the ring shine.

title: Luminous (2011)
content: History / AboutRewind describes the original Luminous as an all-round model with standard size and weight, based on the DoubleJoker shape. Its debut feature was the Core Axle, which fills gaps between bearing, axle and body, and a neon acrylic ring in the rim that reacts to blacklight. A Dif-e-Yo concave bearing is standard. The maker warns of slight wobble from the acrylic ring structure.

title: Perceptor
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Perceptor as the second EX-System model: a heavy wide mid-size body, 55mm x 48mm, with a size D bearing. Despite the shape tending to disperse weight, the bearing size and rim thickness preserve spin. Swapping in the Exceed response unit gives a size C Perceptor.

title: Satellite
content: History / AboutThe Satellite is YoYoJoker's first offstring yo-yo: a metal center body with Delrin outer rims. Rewind says thin Delrin halves are sandwiched by response-integrated spacers, with a gap between metal and Delrin that absorbs impact when dropped. It has an M4x10mm 64 titanium axle. It was sold as a metal offstring prototype on Rewind in autumn 2011 before the retail release.yoyo.fandom adds: prototype 2011 (84.7g, 78.83mm x 51.37mm, Joker Pad wide response), retail summer 2012 with 19.6mm pads, aluminum body with Delrin shells, blue body with white shells.

title: Skyscraper
content: History / AboutThe Skyscraper is the third EX-System release and an offstring model. The maker's description, quoted by Rewind, notes a large 75mm x 54mm body with flat sides to take hologram stickers, weight between the rim and center, and an offstring response unit with a slightly higher edge and narrow gap. It uses a large-diameter size C bearing, so a normal size C response unit makes it a large string-play model. Broken parts can be replaced. A size D bearing version followed in 2014 (80.3g, Joker Pad small).

title: Stigma
content: History / AboutThe Stigma is a hexagonal EX-System yo-yo. Rewind says it breaks from earlier EX models, and that body and Lock Crest can be positioned freely to align the sides. The Delrin body has chamfered corners. yoyo.fandom lists a 2014 release with an Imperial-like profile and CBC large slim pads. A black/black collaboration with Yaneura Works exists.

title: Stinger
content: History / AboutPer Rewind the Stinger is a casual plastic bind yo-yo, suited to stepping up to binds or for those who already use full metals. Its shape recalls the DoubleJoker. At nearly 60g it is light, and the maker, Daisuke Shimada, has used it in 3A demonstrations. yoyo.fandom lists a May 2016 release, 60.9g, concave C-bearing and Large Slim Joker Pads.

title: Stratos
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Stratos as an extremely inverse-round full-size yo-yo with the step removed and a smooth curve, close to a straight shape. It was first sold in limited form at the second yo-style Kyushu on 2010-10-31 (black/orange half bodies). A Dif-e-Yo concave bearing is initially installed. A charity "Pray/Play for Japan" laser-engraved outlet edition was sold after the 2011 Tohoku earthquake, with proceeds pledged to the Japanese Red Cross.The Stratos and the Stratos Another share diameter, width, weight, edge height and cross-section, so halves can be swapped.

title: Stratos Another
content: History / AboutRewind says it matches the Stratos in diameter, width, weight, edge height and cross-section; only the weight distribution differs, producing a typical H profile with more spin power. The two can be mixed left and right without wobble, since the inner line of one equals the outer line of the other.

title: Stratos Mirage
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Mirage as the "third Stratos," built by recombining Stratos and Stratos Another halves into an asymmetric yo-yo that still spins true, because the inner line of each half equals the outer line of the other.

title: Strider
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Strider as a full-metal yo-yo the maker positions for speed play, sized to suit any style. It uses YoYoJoker's original Core Axle, which raises rigidity between body and bearing. A low-edge, wide body and stability beyond its light-looking weight make it suited to 1A. The model currently on sale has a wing-shaped outer rim like the Cocytus and a gentler round shape than earlier ones.

title: Trancer
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Trancer as the fifth EX-System model, a 58mm yo-yo of about 60g, far lighter than others of its size, with shape design intended to keep stability and control at speed. A size D version was also sold (58.7g).

title: Uroboros
content: History / AboutYo-Yo Store Rewind calls the Uroboros the contrast to the angular DoubleJoker: a mid-size round body with the string-contact edge cut away. The "round plus inverse-round" shape makes string contact a point instead of a surface, reducing sleep loss while keeping spin. Foil-stamped caps carry over, with cap color varying by yo-yo color. A 2010 Worlds edition (red/blue half) and a nickel-plated version also exist.

title: Vortex
content: History / AboutRewind describes the 2015 Vortex as an updated version of YoYoJoker's looping model, about 2g lighter. Setup is nearly unnecessary beyond string length thanks to an original duralumin spacer that integrates with the body, giving appropriate return, long sleep and rigidity so the slit resists forming a V shape. It is a Starburst model, but the maker exceptionally recommends K string (poly 100). Rewind sold special artwork versions (chococot, 2015 Worlds logo, Spination, YOYO SPACE AS Ver.) and a not-for-sale version.

title: Vortex (Original)
content: History / AboutRewind describes the first Vortex as YoYoJoker's first looping yo-yo, developed from research with looping players. It is based on the body of the Kohyo Co. "Professional Yo-Yo" with an original duralumin spacer, set up with a size K (Mighty Free size) bearing like the Loop 900. Only string length needs adjusting.

title: Luminous
content:
About
The Luminous (44CLASH × KIKSTYO Edition) is one of the rarest items in the 44CLASH catalog — a triple collaboration between Japanese yo-yo manufacturer YoYoJoker, 44CLASH, and Japanese streetwear brand KIKSTYO. All three brand logos are laser-engraved on the inverse-round aluminum body. Acrylic rings on the throw may introduce minor wobble at speed. Retailed at $249.99 USD and was produced in extremely limited numbers.

title: Xross Road
content: History / AboutRewind describes the Xross Road as the model of Ken Takabayashi, 2012 East Japan Block A 3A champion. Designed by Shimada, it targets 3A stability with a small, fast size D bearing, the first in the YoYoJoker line, combined with the inverse-round friction reduction. Rewind says it also suits 1A and has a heavy-feeling throw.

title: 3Deep
content: History / About3Deep is a 3D-printed yo-yo designed as a tribute to the OneDrop metal yo-yo Deep State, a modern-responsive model. According to maker Hideki Touhou, he liked the Deep State so much that he wrote to OneDrop directly and obtained permission both to use the SideEffect axle system and to make and sell the homage. It can be played bind or responsive, and Rewind describes its feel as reminiscent of the Coca-Cola yo-yo and older Hyper Yo-Yo models: a classic feel rather than one specialised for tricks.Two print methods were sold: an FDM (fused deposition) version printed in two colors in a yin-yang colorway, and a DLP (resin) version with slightly adjusted weight balance. The DLP resin yellows under prolonged UV exposure. Units from 2024 have a stronger axle area. On the maker site the original FDM spec is listed as 56.8 mm diameter, 30.0 mm width (25.0 mm effective), 40-45 g depending on color and material, YYF slim pad response and a C-size bearing.

title: Hacchi
content: History / AboutHacchi is a honeycomb-pattern yo-yo 3D-printed in PLA on a home 3D printer. The maker's page gives the concept as something people who have never touched a 3D-printed object can easily pick up, a shape hard to make by molding or machining, and a yo-yo for learning the basics. After building Loop Yin-Yang and ThreeDimension, maker Hideki Touhou says he shifted away from high-performance yo-yos toward ones that are fun to hold and look at, and the honeycomb idea came first. The name comes from the main character of a famous Japanese anime. He states Hacchi is the yo-yo that symbolizes YOYOMAKER, and he keeps remaking it in new materials and colors (rainbow, glow, wood, bamboo, bronze filaments) to test printing conditions.

title: Loop Yin-Yang (Prototype)
content: History / AboutLoop Yin-Yang (LoopYin-Yang) was an early YOYOMAKER experiment: could a 3D-printed looping yo-yo be made to play properly, and could a taiji (yin-yang) symbol be reproduced as an object. It was inspired by the Fodera Monarch Yin-Yang electric bass, whose top combines white ash and ebony. The video features double-handle looping player Shunsuke Kawakami.It won an award of excellence at the 2014 MODS contest. It was printed by powder-sintering (SLS). According to the maker, weight/density design problems and prototype costs have kept the project from moving past the second prototype.

title: Pop Loop
content: History / AboutPop Loop (POPLOOP) is YOYOMAKER's first looping yo-yo and is notable for its 80 mm diameter, whereas typical looping yo-yos are under 60 mm. It originated when off-string player and Samurai Rock Orchestra performer Tsubasa Onishi, 2004 and 2010 4A world champion, asked whether a large looping yo-yo could be made to stand out on big stages.After many prototypes the body was balanced for light weight and rigidity, given a very slight round profile, a large-diameter C-size bearing and a fine starburst printed by resin (stereolithography) and built in. Weight is an average of about 50 g, so the feel is closer to a normal looping yo-yo than the size suggests. The maker says it feels quite different from regular loopers and does not recommend it to competition players with an established style. A thicker K string is recommended; the yo-yo ships with a normal K string and a shim for gap adjustment. Print data is available via QR code; polycarbonate or PETG can be used for a stiffer body.

title: Zaguri
content: History / AboutZaguri is a 3D-printed wide-style bind yo-yo from YOYOMAKER, the Japanese 3D-printing brand run by Hideki Touhou. Rewind describes it as a 3D-printed model that has reached practical playability, with a light feel that gets up to speed with little force and a double-rim structure that secures power despite the low weight.The maker states that Zaguri is a string-trick yo-yo. The name comes from the Japanese word for the counterbore machining used to fit electronic parts into electric guitars and basses; here it refers to a recess cut inside the inner rim, a shape that is difficult or troublesome with injection molding or machining. It ships in a 3D-printed box package, and buyers receive a QR-code link to download the print data and print their own in ABS or PETG. Weight varies by about +/-1 g because it is made on a fused-deposition (FDM) printer, and layer lines are part of the product.

title: Zaguri Heavy
content: History / AboutZaguri Heavy is a heavier version of YOYOMAKER's 3D-printed string-trick yo-yo Zaguri. According to the maker comment relayed by Rewind, it uses exactly the same print data as the earlier Zaguri, but switching the material to PETG increases the weight. The sticky material gives a stronger rotation than the sharper-feeling PLA original.The included box package is 3D-printed in cork-filled filament, giving a wood-like texture in plastic; the maker warns not to apply strong force to the cork package because it can crack. Weight varies about +/-2 g between units because of FDM printing, and finishing is done by hand, so machining and layer marks are part of the specification.

title: 3Points
content: History / About3Points is a signature model of Kenichi Nakamura, known as Nakamura-Meijin, a central figure of Japan's late-1990s yo-yo boom. It was conceived as a cellphone-strap sized yo-yo that can really be played. The diameter is 31.4 mm after pi (3.14), which gives the name. The first production run included a yo-yo holder strap handmade by Nakamura himself and, per the Yo-Yo Wiki, a replacement rhinestone axle.

title: Agonist
content: History / AboutThe Agonist is the bimetal version of the Checkmate. Compared with the earlier version the materials changed: the body is A6061, the axle is titanium and the rim is stainless steel. Before machining, a stainless rim is bonded to the aluminum body by a special method, so the seam between rim and body is almost invisible, and the bonded construction makes the rim less likely to come loose after impacts or drops. The weight is concentrated efficiently at the outer edge.

title: Agonist 1.0
content: History / AboutAgonist 1.0 keeps the dissimilar-metal joining of the Agonist and fine-tunes other parts to match the feel Hideo Ishida wanted, hence the name. It was built with particular attention to 5A play, which he said made it hard to go back to other yo-yos. Because the rim is bonded, it resists coming loose in impacts and drops and is usable in 1A, 3A and 5A. The store copy links the 2015 WYYC 5A final performance by Ishida.

title: Agonist (Original Version)
content: History / AboutThe original Agonist is the bimetal version of the Checkmate. The body is aluminum for durability and lightness, and the inner rim is brass for its high density. It uses a different method from the Remate to raise spin power. It was designed at the same size as the Checkmate to Hideo Ishida's preference that 5A looks best at that size.

title: Antagonist
content: History / AboutAntagonist is the POM version of the Agonist and yoyomonster.'s first machined POM model. It derives from the Checkmate and is described as the counterpart to the Agonist. The material gives a light, soft feel that metal cannot, and the weight is set for 5A (counterweight) play, making it suitable for players starting counterweight. It shipped with Hideo Ishida's supervised custom pad type 1. A point-sticker promotion (15 points for a gold-plated Crook, 2014-2016) was included with some units.

title: Astrology
content: History / AboutAstrology follows Material as the second Playmonster. series model. It has average weight, middle size and a step-straight shape, a first for a company known for multi-stepped designs, with a size C bearing and slim pads for broad parts compatibility.

title: Basileus
content: History / AboutBasileus means king in Greek. It has yoyomonster.'s polygonal multi-stepped shape in a nearly full-size duralumin body. The area near the bearing is inverse round, and with a low edge the maker says it emphasizes lasting spin power over sleep length. Weight is 66 g by the maker's description.

title: Checkmate
content: History / AboutCheckmate is the first signature model of Hideo Ishida, who won the 5A division at the Kyushu contest five years running from 2007 to 2011. yoyomonster. describes its three-step stepped-straight profile as the "Mix Straight" shape. It is designed for the counterweight (5A) style but also suits 1A and 3A. A chessboard-inspired graphic is its visual signature, and it shipped with a Dif-e-Yo concave bearing installed. Purple, pink and light blue bodies have a pearl-skin finish; the Raw silver version sold at the time of the store listing is a mirror-polished "super mirror" version.

title: Checkmate (7075)
content: History / AboutThis is the Checkmate body made in A7075 (extra-super duralumin). The change in material alters the feel of the yo-yo compared with the original. Like the original, it is built around Hideo Ishida's first signature model with the Mix Straight profile and chessboard pattern, and it shipped with a Dif-e-Yo concave bearing.

title: Crook
content: History / AboutCrook is the third Playmonster. series model and yoyomonster.'s first looping yo-yo, made with input from 2A players. It feels slightly heavier than other loopers, which the maker says brings stability and sleep power, and it suits wrap and around tricks. Compared with the old Crook the shape is slightly rounder and the cap spec changed. The maker notes the bearing and spacer should be cleaned and oil added before use.

title: Crook (Kumamon)
content: History / AboutThis yo-yo is a collaboration with Kumamon, Kumamoto prefecture's mascot, and is an official Kumamon item. It is based on the beginner Signal: the body is the same as the Crook but the internal spacer and bearing thicknesses differ, widening the gap for simple string tricks. Despite the name it does not use Crook internals. The Crook Upgrade Kit converts it to Crook specification.

title: Crook (Original)
content: History / AboutThis is the original version of the Crook, the first looping model from yoyomonster. and third in the Playmonster. series. It was made with feedback from 2A players and has a somewhat heavy feel for stability.

title: Crook (Team Member Edition)
content: History / AboutA special version of the Crook printed with the members of the yoyomonster. team. Otherwise it is the Crook looping model.

title: Crook (Yo-Style x MC Kobacchi)
content: History / AboutA special edition of the Crook produced with Yo-Style and MC Kobacchi.

title: Dragon Rouge
content: History / AboutDragon Rouge is the first yoyomonster. product, a full-metal yo-yo made in Japan after consultation with metalworking specialists and input from top players including world champions. Its multi-stepped H-profile fits the hand, and it has a narrow body suited to light, quick play. It shipped with a low edge and a concave bearing, a bearing remover and a yo-yo case, and each unit is serial-numbered. The store notes Hideo Ishida won the 2010 Kyushu contest 5A division with it.

title: Dragon Rouge 3G
content: History / AboutDragon Rouge 3G reissues the original with the same grippable size and shape but 3 g more weight and a rebalanced weight distribution. The pad size changed to the wider broad size, which raises spin power. The earlier pink and red colors returned, with new blue and green.

title: Dual
content: History / AboutAfter multi-step shapes like the Dragon Rouge and Checkmate, Dual is yoyomonster.'s first nearly pure straight butterfly. The name means two things into one. The area around the bearing is the thinnest in the lineup and weight is placed between the outer rim and the bearing area, intended to work like YoYoJam's mid-ship weight to reduce wobble in combos and aid speed. It ships with Yoyo Joker Joker Pad Ring Type 50. Red and yellow versions shipped with Dif-e-Yo concave bearings.

title: Dystopia
content: History / AboutDystopia is described as representative of the Playmonster. series: a full-metal yo-yo with angled stacked straight surfaces, developed over more than a year and a half. The store describes it as a high-performance all-rounder at an affordable price. Splash silver and pink bodies have a blasted surface.

title: Fenrir
content: History / AboutFenrir is the second yoyomonster. model, following Dragon Rouge with the multi-step shape the company called its concept. It is slightly larger than the Dragon Rouge and considerably heavier, adding stability. Hideo Ishida placed third at the 2010 national contest with it, showing it works for 5A as well as 1A. It uses the maker's own pads, hardness 40 as shipped. Orange and pink versions shipped with Dif-e-Yo concave bearings.

title: Konig
content: History / AboutKonig is built from the Checkmate shape and the weight distribution of the Dual. At 63.5 g it is meant to be stable despite being light, quick to move without overshooting. The Basileus is the same design in duralumin and 2 g heavier.

title: Material
content: History / AboutMaterial is the first in yoyomonster.'s low-priced Playmonster. line and the first in the lineup made in a Hong Kong factory. Its shape, size and weight are close to the Checkmate. It is aimed at players stepping up from plastic yo-yos. A point-sticker promotion for a gold-plated Crook ran 2014-2016.

title: Noah
content: History / AboutNoah is a mono-metal yo-yo in the lineage of the Checkmate. The Mix Straight sections are rounded for a smooth feel; the maker describes a softness it calls kindness. It is the signature model of Tsukasa Ryu.

title: Quickmate
content: History / AboutQuickmate keeps the Checkmate body shape and changes only the weight, one gram lighter. yoyomonster. says the lighter weight gives acceleration the Checkmate lacks, making speed play easier with less effort.

title: Quickmate 2.0
content: History / AboutQuickmate 2.0 revises the design around the axle to lengthen sleep time while keeping the feel of the original Quickmate. The store copy notes that long-time Quickmate users should find the change seamless.

title: Refrain
content: History / AboutRefrain is the light-up version of the Signal, with blue (center), green and red LEDs and multiple blink patterns while spinning. The LED board adds weight. Fitting the Crook upgrade kit turns it into a looping light-up yo-yo.

title: Remate (Original)
content: History / AboutRemate is Hideo Ishida's third signature model, a redesign of the Checkmate with a new logo. The main difference is a larger diameter at the same width, for stronger spin. The longest straight section of the Mix Straight profile became an inverse round to reduce sleep loss, helping horizontal combo tricks that Ishida favors.

title: Remate (7075)
content: History / AboutThis version of the Remate uses A7075 extra-super duralumin. The shape is the same enlarged-diameter Checkmate redesign with the longest straight section made inverse round. The store notes Naoya Takeuchi used the Remate (7075) in the 2015 EJA 5A final.

title: Reset
content: History / AboutReset is a beginner string trick model in a balanced wing shape. It ships with a surface-processed (concave) bearing for a bind setup, which keeps the string centered and lengthens spin time. A point-sticker promotion for a gold-plated Crook ran 2014-2016.

title: Sfida
content: History / AboutSfida is the signature model of Naoya Takeuchi, 2015 Asia 5A champion. Unlike the polygonal multi-step shapes common at yoyomonster., it has a rounded profile. Takeuchi used it to win the 5A division at the 2015 Asia contest. Its size sits between full and middle size.

title: Signal
content: History / AboutSignaL refines the Crook looping model for beginners, with a looping shape and ball bearing. Swapping internal parts relative to the Crook makes it usable for basic string tricks as well as looping. A point-sticker promotion for a gold-plated Crook ran 2014-2016.

title: YoyoRecreation Aeronaut
content:
History / About
The Aeronaut, released in 2013, was YoyoRecreation's second off-string yo-yo after Maestro.

title: YoyoRecreation C-NINE
content:
History / About
The C-NINE, originally developed under the name "Cloud," is Atsushi Nakamura's signature, released December 2015. A prototype of the model was used by Takumi Yasumoto to take 2nd place at the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest 4A division.

title: YoyoRecreation Negator
content:
History / About
The Negator is a 2A/looping model first released in Delrin in 2014, then re-released in 2015 in polycarbonate with a redesigned profile. Per community record it was commercially unsuccessful — it reportedly didn't loop or hop well for its price point — and was discontinued. Included here for archive completeness.

title: YoyoRecreation Third Impact (Prototype)
content:
History / About
The Third Impact, from 2010, is the signature of Kengo Kido, YoyoRecreation's own founder. Only one prototype run of this model was ever made — it never had a confirmed public retail release.

title: YoyoRecreation Triad
content:
History / About
The Triad debuted at Japan Nationals in 2014 and was updated for the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest (weight raised from 64.9g to 69g, price dropped from ¥7,800 to ¥6,480, engraving redesigned). It was briefly pulled from YoYoExpert for infringing YoYoJam's Central Rim Weight patent, returning to sale in 2015 after YYR obtained licensing from YoYoJam.

title: 1Up
content: AboutThe 1Up is a re-release of the WEDGE, a yo-yo that held the DNA (fingerspin) World Record twice. Thick polycarbonate rims provide unusually high rim weight for a plastic, enabling extended spin times and exceptional stability typically found only in metals. Its wide profile suits 3A (two-handed) play, and the Center Trac bearing keeps the string centered for consistent fingerspin technique. Available in Clear/Silver Hub, Galaxy/Purple Hub, and Fire/Orange Hub colorways at $19.99.

title: Arcade
content: AboutThe Arcade was the first yo-yo released under the Throwback Skill Toys manufacturing label, announced November 2019. It features a comfortable organic shape with a slightly smaller diameter than standard, prioritizing accessibility and feel while maintaining quality manufacturing. The stainless steel axle, VIP bearing, and blasted finish give it a premium construction at a $27.99–$32.99 price point. Available in a wide range of colorways including Black Silver, Cinnamon, Blue Lagoon, Galaxy, Starry Night, Fire, and numerous acid wash and splash variants.

title: Atlas
content: AboutThe Atlas was designed by YoYoFactory as an exceptionally wide aluminum combining speed, stability, and control. Jake Elliott used it to win the 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest. At 54.35mm wide — approximately 25% wider than a standard throw — it features a U-shaped cup for comfortable 5A thumb cradles and a dimpled inner cup for fingerspins. Its exceptional stability and wide catch zone made it a favorite for both 5A and 1A technical play. Released in a wide range of colorways including splash, acid wash, fade, and a dedicated YoTricks Edition.

title: Canon
content: AboutThe Canon was designed by 2015 5A World Champion Jake Elliott after a year of input from top 3A and 5A players, released February 2016 in collaboration with YoYoFactory and Throwback Skill Toys. Its optimized gap width eases binding on the short strings used in 3A/5A play. The stepped response area and reinforced walls tolerate the repeated impacts inherent in off-string and counterweight styles. Every Canon ships bundled with the UltraWeight — a machined Delrin counterweight sized specifically for 5A play. Available in mint and various splash colorways at $44.99.

title: Civility
content: AboutThe original Civility was YoYoTricks.com's first premium metal yo-yo, funded via Kickstarter in January 2013 in collaboration with designer Colin Leland (known for OneDrop and TMBR work). The campaign raised over $23,000 against a $3,500 goal — more than six times its target. Production delays pushed delivery to early 2014. Machined from 6061 aluminum with a bead-blasted finish, the Civility was designed for unresponsive 1A play at an accessible $75 price point for a premium machined throw.

title: Civility v2
content: AboutIn 2021 the Civility was reimagined as a bimetal in collaboration with renowned designer Mark Diehr of MK1 YoYos, with manufacturing by FPM. Stainless steel rings provide extra rim weight for extended spin times and stability. Features a redesigned fingerspin bowl matching the Solstice series and a soft matte bead-blasted finish optimized for grinds. Available in colorways including Red/Black Rings, Blue/Black Rings, Green/Silver Rings, Black/Rainbow Rings, Pink Purple Fade/Silver Rings, and Green Silver Fade/Black Rings at $74.99.

title: Fizz
content: AboutThe Fizz is YoYoTricks.com's entry-level yo-yo for absolute beginners, featuring the proprietary F.A.S.T. (Fully Active Starburst Technology) response system — internal teeth moulded into the body that require no pad replacement. Durable polycarbonate construction and a lightweight profile reduce hand fatigue. The Fizz is prominently featured in YoYoTricks.com's beginner tutorial videos across YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok, and is the first yo-yo recommended in the Level Up! curriculum. Available in blue, green, dark cherry, pink, purple, root beer, American edition, black, and secret agent (black/white) colorways.

title: Match
content: AboutThe Match is YoYoTricks.com's premium 2A looping yo-yo, designed as the upgrade path from the Oracle. Its defining feature is a Size B bearing — larger than the standard Size A used in most loopers — enabling longer sleep times while maintaining the consistent response essential for looping. Translucent colorway options allow players to watch the spin through the body. Available in multiple translucent and opaque colorways including aqua/black, red/black, yellow/black, and lemon lime at $15.99.

title: Oracle
content: AboutThe Oracle is YoYoTricks.com's dedicated 2A (two-handed looping) beginner yo-yo, developed in partnership with YoYoFactory. Its defining feature is the pre-set, slightly wide gap that removes all setup guesswork for beginners learning looping. Soft celcon plastic reduces impact during repeated practice loops. Described by YoYoTricks.com as "at the center of our strategy for teaching you how to yoyo." Available in red, purple, blue, green, and white.

title: Origen
content: AboutThe Origen is an aluminum yo-yo inspired by the Luminator — the yo-yo that launched YoYoTricks.com back in 2009. Designed by MK1 YoYos' Mark Diehr under the Throwback Skill Toys label, it features an organic flared shape with a tiny bearing and wide response pads that produce smooth, consistently responsive play even at slow throw speeds. The result bridges the gap between fixed-axle and modern responsive styles, offering old-school feel with machined-aluminum precision. Available in red, blue, and black at $19.99.

title: Sage
content: AboutThe redesigned Sage maintains the original's beginner-friendly character but upgrades to a larger, more durable polycarbonate body and a redesigned cap with a dedicated fingerspin area for DNA tricks. At 58.2mm diameter it is slightly larger than the Sage Classic for more powerful spins. Ships responsive with a Half SPEC bearing and upgrades to the VIP bearing for unresponsive play. Available in colorways including Red/Blue Caps, Galaxy, Fire, Edge Glow Yellow/Black Caps, Translucent Blue/Black Caps, Recon, and Black/Rayon Vert Cap.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Half SPEC (Size C; upgradeable to VIP bearing)

title: Sage Classic
content: AboutThe Sage Classic was designed in 2013 as a beginner-oriented remake based on the YoYoFactory Protostar profile — a shape that won the 2010 World Yo-Yo Championship in 1A. Built by YoYoFactory to YoYoTricks.com's specifications, it ships with a thin Half SPEC bearing for responsive play with 30–45 second sleep times and is upgradeable to a full Size C bearing for unresponsive play. YoYoFactory retired their own competing product (the ONEstar) in late 2015, recognizing the Sage as the superior implementation of the profile. Available in blue, red, black, sakura, midnight, green, and winter (white) colorways.

meta.yya_bearing_size: Half SPEC (Size C; upgradeable to full Size C)

title: Spire
content: AboutThe Spire is YoYoTricks.com's 4A (offstring) yo-yo, co-designed with iYoYo under the Throwback Skill Toys label. It shares the profile of the iCEBREAKER, which won the 2018 US National Yo-Yo Contest. Machined polycarbonate provides durability for the impacts inherent in offstring play, while an inner lip in the cup prevents thumb-grinding slip during thumb catches. Available in clear and black body versions with blue, mint, black, purple, and red hub color options.

title: Summer Solstice
content: AboutThe Summer Solstice is the power-focused half of a complementary pair with the Winter Solstice, both released in June 2020 by Throwback Skill Toys. Its thicker, wider rims deliver extra rim weight for longer, more powerful spins, while the wide profile suits horizontal tricks. A blasted finish enables grinds, and the fingerspin hub supports DNA play. The Summer Solstice and Winter Solstice are designed as "sister" throws: the Summer for power, the Winter for speed. Available in Red Orange Fade, Punk Galaxy, Galaxy, Blue Lagoon, Steel Breeze, Fire, Pink Orange Fade, Black Rainbow Splash, and acid wash/half-swap variants.

title: Winter Solstice
content: AboutThe Winter Solstice is the speed-focused companion to the Summer Solstice, released simultaneously in June 2020 by Throwback Skill Toys. Its balanced weight profile makes it lighter-feeling and faster than the Summer Solstice while sharing the same dimensions. A blasted finish suits grinds and a fingerspin hub supports DNA play. The Winter Solstice completes the complementary Summer/Winter pairing — Summer for power, Winter for control and speed. Available in YoTricks Edition, Gold, Black, Pink, Blue Aqua Fade, Silver Rainbow Splash, and various acid wash and half-swap colorways.

title: YUIGA
content: About the YUIGAThe YUIGA is the debut signature model for Yuiga Suzuki, designed for expressive and dynamic competitive play. At 49mm wide it was the widest 1A model in the sOMEThING lineup at the time of release. The 6061 aluminum body paired with stainless steel rims delivers a "firm, controlled feel" for precision across complex combos. $189.99 USD.Colorways: Matte Navy, Matte Black.

title: Yukichi The Big Money
content:
History / About
Yukichi The Big Money (諭吉 ザ・ビッグマネー) commemorates the retirement of Japan's ¥10,000 banknote portrait of Fukuzawa Yukichi (in circulation 1984-2024), adapting the YUKIKO (RY-007) face curve into a thicker monometal shape. Portrait artwork credited to Atelier Umiyury (a real illustration studio); base design by regular designer "Sususu"/Usukino.

title: YUKIKO
content:
History / About
YUKIKO (RY-007) is a multi-material hostess "business card" concept yoyo with a laser-engraved butterfly signature. Sturm Panzer explicitly states this is not a Duncan Butterfly homage. Renewed in April 2020.

title: YWET
content:
Pre-Production YWET

First YWET was a non side-effect yoyo machined in 2008. Due to a machining error these were never officially released. Most were polished raw, but there were some anodized red/yellow with the YWET logo engraved on them. There were 8 of these done in hardcoat black, and a few plated in copper.

Production Side Effect YWET

There were also a number of alternate colors produced for the SE YWET, all in limited quantities. I have seen them in grey/gold, gold, grey and black.

AaronW YWET's

Aaron received five of the original raw YWET's from Sonny in 2015.  Later he purchased two more from Trevlor on Instagram. Sonny then sent 6 more original YWET's to AaronW. One was blasted and finished half gold/half blue. The bearing posts on this one were cut down. This allowed the halves to be screwed together without shims, it made for a 3.6mm gap and was fully responsive. The other 5 were all polished and given away to friends. The following are the end results.

This YWET was polished, then anodized in clear to protect it.  1 of 1.  Anodized by "Adventures in Anodizing."

This YWET was bead blasted, then anodized half red/half gold.  No engravings. 1 of 1.  Anodized by "Adventures in Anodizing."

These were bead blasted, and then finished half clear/half red.  2 of these were made.  1 has glued in spacers and has been traded a few times.  Anodized by "Adventures in Anodizing."

This one was was bead blasted and anodized half gunmetal grey/half gold. 1 of 1.  Anodized by Gruntbull.

The last two are currently polished and raw aluminum.  Will eventually be anodized.

Blue/Gold 3.5mm Gap

Recess YWETs

Danny Edition - Powdercoat

From the Recess Intl. website:
"My brother, Danny Severance, was and is one of my biggest inspirations not only in YoYoing but also in life. Anyone who met him would probably say something of a similar effect.
2 years ago he decided to take his own life. As much as it pains me and all of his family/friends and the people he touched, we all know he’s in a better place and wouldn’t want us wallowing in sorrow.
So instead, I’ve made some YoYos in his honor. If you ever got to meet Danny or see some video of him throwing earlier on, you would know how partial he was to a Purple Freehand Zero with plain white caps. A clean look inspired by Seth Peterson and so many of his idols who threw Freehands before him.
This is an original Anti-Yo YWET powder coated in his favorite color way. As you may know these YoYos weren’t sold to the public due to a bearing seat machining error. This is fixed with a simple shim to adjust the gap of you YoYo, and all pieces are hand tested to perfection before shipping. Shims will be glued into place.
They’ll be funding a team who will be walking the “Out of the Darkness” overnight fundraiser, with all proceeds being used in the fight for suicide prevention.
YoYos will be released on Friday April 1st (8 PM EST) (editor note: 2016), and be shipped in mid April after powder coating is completed. Price will be $70."
15 of these yoyos were sold April 1, 2016.
If you'd like to donate to a worthy cause, please visit: http://purpleyoyo.org/

Danny Edition YWET Anodized

On November 9th, 2018, Recess released an additional 20 YWETs anodized by Gruntbull to look like Danny Severance's Freehand Zero. Similar to the powdercoated YWET, shims were hand glued in. They sold for $110 each, with a portion of the proceeds going towards the same suicide prevention charity.

Paul Escolar Anodized Edition YWET

On July 3rd, 2019, Recess released a quantity of YWETs featuring the artwork of Paul Escolar in his signature color scheme, teal and blue. They retailed for $150 and came with a print signed by Paul Escolar.

Paul Escolar Powdercoat Edition YWET

Recess released 20 YWETs featuring the artwork of Paul Escolar in a two-tone powdercoat. They retailed for $140 and came with a print signed by Paul Escolar and stickers.

Nickel Plated and Black Hardcoat YWET's

Static Co YWETs

In November 2019, Static Co. released the YWETs they received from Sonny in three different variants: black nickel plated, copper plated, and Gruntbull anodized (“Mega Shock”, half haggard gold, and half rainy sky blue). The name “Optimally Geared” comes from the parts the yo-yo shipped with: a pair of .015″ spacers installed (making the gap around 4mm), a pair of .02″ spacers as they were determined to also provide a solid experience, and a YoYoRecreation Dual Straight bearing.

meta.yya_response: Quad-Fist Response (2 Concentric O-Rings on each side)

title: YWET – Blasted Edition
content:
After a number of years of teased info, the YWET was released at US Nationals September 30, 2011 through Bird In Hand, in downtown Chico, CA.  The first release was limited to 35 (?) yoyos.  These differed from the full release in that they had a heavily blasted finish, that gave the yoyo a chalky finish.  These were also the first yoyos that were machined by One Drop and featured One Drop's side effect system.  These first run YWET's had hand carved hearts in their side effects.

Retail Price: $135

Possibly a prototype blasted YWET. This once came from Sonny's personal collection. It has a heavier blast that the released version of these did, and has double YWET bubbles on the blue side.

meta.yya_response: Quad-Fist Response (2 Concentric O-Rings on each side)

title: YWETi
content:
History / About
YWETi is a homage to the classic Anti-Yo YWET ("Yo-Yos Will Eat Themselves"), designed with Anti-Yo co-founder Sonny Patrick. Art by ATILA. 38 A-grade units across Blue, Rose Gold, Gunmetal Grey (hard coat), and Raw finishes, plus 20 B-grade "OG" Blue/Orange units.

meta.yya_response: 19mm Type 50 pads or Quad Fist rubber rings

title: YWETi Side Effects Edition
content:
History / About
The YWETi Side Effects Edition was RSO's first titanium yoyo built for One Drop Side Effects hardware, made with Anti-Yo's Sonny Patrick. MK I (Sept 2020, 37 units, raw) was followed by a refined MK II (weight shaved from the SE nipple and added to the inner rims), and the Soaking Ywet colorway (May 2021, 19 units, purple/yellow cracked-coat anodizing, on the MK II CAD). RSO has described this as its last collaboration with Sonny Patrick before moving to independent designs in 2022.

meta.yya_bearing_size: YoyoRecreation NSK Platinum Double Straight C
